Input: Pre- CV19 visit. I'm happy to report this is still a 4-star venue. You should be aware that TF is not large so during their busy periods they will be jammed. One thing that I don't like is their seating, but it's a small price to pay to truly wonderful tortillas 

Be aware that they have rotating taps so ask your server if they have any small batches available. We have been here a number of times and there always seems to be a local or CA-based specialty beer available. But I'm not here for the beer I'm here for quaff down some of their righteous tortillas. 

Onto the food. Homemade tortillas you bet! I went with barbacoa and a pork option. I could have gone for a third but beer, chips, and amazing sauces had filled my panza to satisfaction. 

Not sure if this is still happening but be aware of the no parking signs for the lot next door. If you park there you are booted immediately and your only recourse is to pay up there to have the boot removed.

Input: I can only reiterate what others have said, and what I've told my friends for a long time.  Besides the Alamo Drafthouse locations, this is by far the best theater in the Austin area.  The DLP projection and digital sound is exceptional.

I've seen lots of movies here over the last two years primarily because the Galaxy hosts a large amount of free screenings for movies.  I get a chance to go to many of these screenings which I thoroughly enjoy when they are held here.  The seats are comfortable with a lot of leg room.  The arms for the seats can move up and out of the way if you need the extra room.  I haven't tried the DBOX setup yet, but I've heard that can be rather enjoyable as well (although the price can really set you back a bit).

The only problem is location. For whatever reason (and I'm sure there are many), this part of town has really started to fall apart.  There was a time that the Lincoln Village Shopping Center and Highland Mall were fine places to shop, etc.  Now, not so much.  I'm surprised there were only a couple of mentions of vehicle break-ins in earlier reviews since I've seen my fair share of people walk out of the theater to broken glass on the side of their vehicle.   As with anything else, at night, park as close to the theater as you can preferably under a light and keep any valuables hidden or take them with you.  Common sense, sure, but break-ins still continue to be a problem in the parking lot of this theater.

Input: Oh, Kendall Square. You don't offer much in the way of culture or entertainment, but when you do restaurants you do them well. Hungry Mother. EVOO. And The Helmand.

I can't speak on the authenticity as the only other time I've had Afghan cuisine was during a food festival in my high school world issues class from an Afghani classmate. It was delicious, but it didn't make me an expert. But I'm going to assume the food is pretty authentic considering The Helmand is owned by Hamid Karzai's brother.

In any case, it's just delicious. My friend and I split the Kaddo to start. Fried pumpkin with yogurt garlic sauce and seasoned ground beef. Oh God, it was like the UN was invited to my mouth and everyone brought beer! So many diverse flavors and textures. Incredible! 

For entrees, this is the place to go if you love lamb. There are so many lamb dishes to choose from. After agonizing for an embarrassingly long time, I finally settled on the Khorma Challow. Leg of lamb sauteed with onions, tomatoes, garlic, green beans, and potatoes, with challow rice. Hello, UN party no. 2! Oh, you brought strippers this time? That's nice! My god, this dish was delicious. The lamb was so tender and flavorful and the melding of all those vegetables created the most heavenly stew to mix with rice. My friend had the Chapendaz and raved about how delicious it still was after being microwaved and eaten again the next day. 

They have a really great wine list and the waiters are good at suggesting pairings. The restaurant is beautifully decorated with rugs, blue glassware and various other almost kitschy touches that make the room colorful and lively without being too sleek or modern.

Come here so your food senses can experience the equivalent of a raging kegger with the coolest people in the world. There's nothing like The Helmand.

Input: Kiva is expensive but has some amazing treats! Almost everything is organic and they have plenty of milk alternatives and options for those with food allergies. 

The atmosphere is clean but not super homey. They did recently added cushions to the seats so it's easier to sit for longer periods of time, which is nice because sometimes it takes a while for your food to be ready. 

I absolutely love their Habibi bowl (who knew kale could taste so wonderful!) and green smoothies. The acai bowls are amazing too, but Moberi (a few blocks away) makes them twice as big for the same price. 

Overall they have a great selection and I always recommend it to friends. The biggest thing they could work on is customer service. Just asking "how's your day going?" before taking my order would be nice. I had a few months where I was at Kiva twice a week and always ordered the same thing, but none of the staff asked my name or seemed to remember me. Way different vibe than the staff at Dragonfly (a block away) who have my name and drink memorized and always greet me with a smile. Just a thought!

Input: My date decided to surprise me with a booked reservation to this restaurant. It has been on my to try list for a number of years but for some reason, I always ended up somewhere else. Good thing he placed a reservation because the place was packed soon after 6pm.

Service was fantastic. Our server was very on top of keeping the dinner flow going and our drinks were never empty.

Input: Overall, a very good experience. So yes, the wait on a Friday was about an hour, but we expected that.  We found seats at the bar & the bar staff were all very friendly & attentive. Even when one of the bartenders forgot two of our drinks, she was very apologetic & quickly made the drinks.

Once seated we had Kelsey(?). While she was clearly having a busy night, she was attentive, friendly, & helpful with the menu.  Our party of 4 included 2 guys who like to "interact" with the server, so she definitely handled their obnoxiousness well.  We also somehow received a comp'ed margarita & martini from the bar, so that was an extra perk.

The food:  Here is really the only area where I dropped one star.  Here's a breakdown of what the table ordered & their comments:

Calamari & Zuccini:  "Good, but a little cold"; "nothing special"
Queso:  "Runny", "needs to be hotter" (temperature hot), "the chips are a little odd".  Would suggest the option of adding sausage or ground beef as well.
Mushroom Pizza:  "very good, I would order this again!"
Ribeye:  "the wood firing was tasty, as were the potatoes"
Lamb Chops:  "they were pretty good, but the potatoes and asparagus were great"
Carnivore Pizza:  they forgot the requested jalapenos & egg, but.... "excellent! I would come back just for this pizza", "crispy, hot, cheesy, just the right balance of toppings."  This was what I personally ordered.  The two aforementioned guys took slices as well, so this part of the review is balanced by 3 out of 4 people at our table.
Gelato: I shared the Trio with my husband & we chose: Creamcicle, Pistachio & Stracciatella (which is basically chocolate chip).  They were all very, very good & we ate all of it.  Our friends had the cheesecake & cobbler & there were zero complaints there as well.

We live about 15/20 mins away, so we probably won't be making this a regular stop just due to the commute down 620, BUT as I told my husband in the car on the way home, if someone asked about Napa Flats, I would definitely agree to go or recommend it.

Overall, a great dinner!  I would go back & tell other friends to do so as well.

Input: Right off the bat I want to note that the above hours for the RPAC are their hours while students are in classes.  The weeks between quarters and during holidays are not usually as accomodating.

But wow, this gym is awesome. I was a student during the days of Larkins, the old fitness building, then I remember when the first phase of the RPAC opened up. It was beautiful, especially when you compared it to Larkins - it was decrepit, smelly, cold and it was like a maze in there sometimes.  I always felt like I could get lost somewhere down there and no one would ever find me because my cell phone got no reception in there at all.  *shudders*  Working out at Larkins was like punishing yourself for wanting to get off your butt and work out.

Then along comes the RPAC, all bright, shiny and new, and it made you actually want to work out. People who never worked out a day in their lives were suddenly coming up with excuses to go to the gym. And there were other reasons to go there besides exercise.  There was the Courtside Cafe: right inside the door you could have a seat at this little cafe and eat snacks and sandwiches, like their peanut butter and banana with granola sandwich.  That thing was huge, yummy, and so filling that I got 3 meals out of it.

There was also the Juice Bar, where you could get smoothies, coffee, teas, etc.  There was also a little shop downstairs where you could buy Powerbars and things like that.  

If you felt like getting semi-active, you could change into your bathing suit and hit the recreational pool. Seriously, free awesome swimming pool on campus. Greatest thing ever. There was a little part of the pool that looked like a hot tub but wasn't, unfortunately.  And half the pool was roped off for those who wanted to swim laps.  But it was big enough to go and play around.  

The locker rooms were also nice, had plenty of space, but you had to pay to use the lockers.  I really liked the private bathrooms.  They have like two or three of them, close to where the pool is, and if you're lucky enough to snag one, you have a whole bathroom (that you lock) to yourself. This includes a toilet, sink, shower and sitting area.

There was also a daycare center in there so people could leave their kids in there to play and watch cartoons while they did their thing. I should also mention that there were 2 gyms where you could play basketball and volleyball and stuff like that. I remember that while I was there, and not too long after the RPAC opened, the gym on the lower floor flooded and was shut down for a while because they had to redo it. But I'm sure it's back to normal by now.

I loved the second floor cardio area and used to live on the EFX machines and the treadmills.  There was a whole canyon of them downstairs, but that was too crowded for my taste.  Plus I liked the upstairs because you could see out the glass walls to the outside and it was so bright and cheery up there from all the sunshine coming through.  They had TVs mounted from the ceiling in front of the exercise equipment so you had something to look at, but the sound wasn't very loud and you couldn't hear the TV. They usually had the TVs playing mtvU - the college MTV channel.  I always just brought my iPod and listened to that.

There was usually plenty of machines to go around, but sometimes you had to wait.  I can't really say when the busy hours were, but I remember them being something around noon and 5-6 pm during the weekdays.  I tried to go at odd times and hardly ever had a problem getting right on a machine.

There was a huge weight room downstairs, but I never went there to work out, although I would have liked to.  It was usually full of guys who looked like they were taking lifting weights too seriously, and I didn't really want to go in there and show off that lifting 50 pounds with my weak lady arms is a struggle for me. Just a bit intimidating.

There were all kinds of classrooms in the RPAC, and I had a few classes in there, like Women's Self Defense. I know that they also hosted martial arts and yoga classes.  

I almost forgot to mention the running track upstairs.  That was awesome. It was at the highest point in the buidling, and when you were up there looking over the railing you could see down through the RPAC. It is such a pretty building.

Too bad I only got to use it for part of my college career.  Back then my loans were paying for my reduced membership. But now that I'm out of school?  I don't think I'm even eligible to join, but even if I was, I can't afford it.  It's so expensive, but I think you have to be a staff member or grad student or something to purchase a membership outside of undergrad school.  That sucks, because I would love to work out here again. If you are able to get a membership, try it out. It's the best gym I've ever worked out in and I miss it!

Input: * * * Heavenly food, but space too close for comfort * * *
On my first visit today, I took a friend for his birthday. He had the moussaka, and I had a flatbread with lamb, spinach and shiitake. We shared some hummus and an almond rose cake. The food was perfection: fresh, flavorful, delicate. I appreciated the moderate portions (no supersizing here) and the beautiful flavors.
My only issue was space. The lounge seating there is lovely, but quite small. We went at 1:30 PM on a Friday and it was packed. My friend and I had to squeeze on a bench and share a tiny round table. When the corner spot next to us (with a slightly larger table) opened up, we transferred, only to be given the evil eye and get trapped in the corner by the family of four and a half -- two grandparents, two mommies and small child -- who took our previous, minuscule spot. Clearly they had been waiting for the corner spot, but sadly we didn't realize it until it was too late and awkward to do anything about it. 
What a bummer: I wanted to savor my food slowly but had to rush because we were squished too close for comfort.
Moral of the story: Skip the lunchtime rush.  If you're a party of 1-3 and you want to savor your food without feeling rushed, come mid-morning or mid-afternoon. And if you're a large group, order TAKE OUT or consider other options -- at least until the restaurant has better seating!

The service was attentive throughout the evening, with constant water refills (both iced and hot for our teapots) and smiles to make sure that everything was going well.

An ex girlfriend of mine, who was a strict vegan, often declared that Udipi and Vatica (in Marietta / East Cobb) were her two favorite strict / pure vegetarian restaurants in ATL (that also just happened to be Indian Restaurants).

My friend and I started off with a potato fritter appetizer that came with mint sauce and some other kind of sauce. It was awesome; especially the mint sauce.

He and I both got curry dishes, both come with rice. He got a spinach curry whereas I got a spicy tofu curry. We decided to split our entrees. Both were good but I think I liked his spinach dish a little better; however, my tofu curry was decidedly spicier. My friend, who can't take the spice heat levels that I can, was not able to eat too much of the tofu dish I ordered. Both come with a yogurt dipping sauce which is fantastic. 

We also ordered garlic nan which was soaked in melted ghee (some kind of Indian / Pakistani yogurt butter I think); again fantastic.

A little bit on the pricy side for what we got ($12-$13 dollar range each) but all in all a great dinner.

Input: Based on the mixed reviews I read, I wasn't sure if I'd enjoy it but I was pleasantly surprised. Like everything else, there are usually discounts available (I found a 20% off coupon online).

The first room of the tour, your tour guide, dressed in authentic garb, introduces himself and introduces you to the owner of the ship via video. The next room is the shipyard and the following is the ticket office. Then you get to experience the inside of the ship from the artifacts, a recreation of the grand staircase, even the cargo hold.

Now when you are checked in for the tour, you are given a paper ticket with the name and information of a passenger on the ship. Once you make your way through the boiler room and brave the freezing temperatures of the deck and captains bridge, you find yourself in the memorial room. There you will look up on the walls and find your characters name; my character, despite being second class and female, perished when the ship sank.

Next you get to the room with an actual iceberg! The iceberg is 31 degrees and they have you hold your hand there for 10 seconds. It was freezing and was pretty painful; I can only imagine floating in water that cold for 40 minutes (although most didn't last that long). They even had a huge portion of the ship available to see in the final room.

Although I came in with low expectations, the tour guide really brought the tour to life with colorful stories and even some cheesy jokes. If you need something to do near international drive to kill an hour, it might be worth your while.

Input: If Yelp had half-stars, this would be a 3.5 review, but since I am hopelessly in love with Levenger's paper products, I'm rounding up. And yes, I am a no-fooling Levenger addict; I absolutely live through my Circa. (I lost the previous Circa a couple of years ago and literally could not function or collect my wits for days; not only was my life in that thing, not only were various business notes in that thing, MY REMODEL SKETCHES WERE IN THAT THING. Still not okay. Still not okay. *deep breath*) 

Where was I? Oh yeah, about to enter the temple of Levenger, after buying online for years (and reading the catalog aspirationally in college, because a certain type of person regards fancy pens as The Key To Everything, and sadly I was that person). Anyway, in I went to select my movin'-on-up fancy pen to go with my aforementioned life-encompassing Circa.

The store was okay -- you know, okay. It's possible I expected too much (whatever in the previous two paragraphs gave you that idea?). The store is tidy and easy to navigate; the paper refills I was seeking were handy, and the samples set out for examination were good samples and nice to examine in person. Lots of emphasis on the leather goods and the desk accoutrements, which aren't for me, but someone's buying those too. 

The pen section -- the goal of the visit -- was where the experience slumped just a little. Not the pens themselves; this ends with me choosing a very nice fountain pen that I use daily. The buying experience itself, though, was a little bumpy. I liked the pens I was shown and didn't necessarily feel upsell pressure, but I wish I'd gotten more information on both other pens that might be appealing (seriously, I *announce* that I'm here to spend like a drunken pen-loving sailor and you show me three pens?) and a little more data on the one I eventually chose. (When I said something about buying another nib for it down the line, that would have been a good time to mention that Levenger doesn't offer swappable nibs on this model. Just sayin'.) 

It was okay. I still like my pen. I still live in, through, and for my Circa. I still buy Levenger products...online. Glad I went in. Not frantic to go back.

Input: It gives me great pleasure, more of which than I should probably admit, to inform others of when I have found a deal. Usually, it starts with my quoting a price and then rattling off what I believe to be the vast amount of value (in goods and/or services) that I received for this price. Sometimes, it's a lunch special, other times a sale and, at the most amazing times, it's just how things always are at a particular place.

Enter Berry Freeze. For $2.98, I was able to scarf down a generous portion of frozen yogurt with a multitude of toppings--all of which, I got to concoct myself! For just $2.98, I filled my size small cup with mostly chocolate yogurt and a dash of pomegranate and topped it off with chocolate sprinkles, an oreo, a piece of milky way, a piece of twix, vanilla syrup and a swirl of chocolate syrup, too. For $2.98, I got to feel like a kid again.

Worth noting is the ability to create your own flavors by adding as much or as little of each type of yogurt available, not to mention the vast choices in topping, from fruit pebbles and a chocolate bars, to fresh fruits and nuts.  Worth pointing out as potential downfalls are the yogurt's actual lack of tartness and it's mildly grainy texture. However, paired with a DIY service style and low, low price tag, these are smaller points you'll hardly notice. Especially if you go a little nuts on the toppings.

Input: I wanted to write a review mainly because I don't think the overall rating reflects the establishment. I think they are still working out some of the kitchen/service kinks (according to other reviews, not our experience) but hopefully they will get more consistent as they are open longer. My advice to management is to stick with what you are doing but focus on consistency in food prep and emphasize a bit more on the attentiveness and welcomeness of staff.   Definitely worth a visit if you live in the area.

During a busy time, this market is a nightmare for someone who is claustrophobic. I can say this because I am not claustrophobic and it makes me feel that way when the place is packed at weekday lunch time.

Do I do all my shopping here? No. Do I enjoy stopping by once and a while for a urban shopping experience? Yes.

Input: I love Honey Bubble. The tea is delicious-- admittedly, a bit sweet at times, so ask for VERY light honey (I get 2 pumps) unless you want a very dessert-y tea. I've never tried the gelato, because I always think it looks a bit freezer burnt, but I've had the macarons from Alon's which are delicious. The space itself is cleverly designed, and the staff is mostly friendly. I love that they're open relatively late.

I do think it's a bit pricey for bubble tea-- at $5 for a large, I can't justify going as often as I'd like. And parking can be a nightmare, depending on the time-- they have the spaces slanted, which means if you pull in on a crowded night you're going to have a hell of a time backing out, especially with crazy Ponce traffic.

A side note-- I think it's a little tacky that the owner (or at least, SOMEONE with a Honey Bubble sticker on their car) parks in the tiny front parking lot. It's already super tiny-- why not reserve those spots for customers? I also wish they were able to give out samples of the more unique teas. I'd love to try some, but since they've plastered "NO REFUNDS ONCE YOU'VE TAKEN A SIP" everywhere, I'm worried I'll be stuck with something terrible. I get the need for those signs, really, I just wish there was some way to try a few things out.

Despite all those negatives, however, they're still my favorite (and only) bubble tea spot.

Input: I am so sick of hearing about Brian D.'s picky pizza eating experience. Who loses a star just for being cut in squares? Just ask for it in pie cut! Just sayin'. Anyways...

I love coming to Terita's. The pizza is great! Sometimes the cooking is a little inconsistent. For example, we ordered on a Monday night and had a very crispy bottom with a centimeter of crispy edges, and then the next night the pizza was more flimsy and didn't have much crisp. Many people I'm sure would complain about darker edges, but I loved it that was so I was a little disappointed that it didn't turn out that way the second time around. The dough is thin with a slight airy thickness, a good quality sauce, and thin, greasy pepperonis that curl up and have some spice to them. The cheese is a good quality, but isn't a strong flavor. We also ordered garlic bread with cheese, and that was good too. It has plenty of cheese and plenty of garlic butter. 

My only issue is that you are required to bring your coupon in. Unfortunately, my printer is out of ink, so I couldn't print out the coupon and they require you to physically bring in the coupon to get the $1.25 off, even if you mention it on the phone.  This situation makes me slightly irritated because the area I live in has at least 15 other pizza shops that are super close, but yet I am driving 20 minutes to pick up my pizza at Terita's, and the least they could do is to make it easiest on the customer so that way they are likely to order again, because I'm not sure when I'll be getting ink, since I don't print often. If I know Terita's is less likely to accommodate me for my coupon, I'm more inclined to order from someplace that I don't have to hassle with physically bringing a coupon.

Input: A lot of people will quickly crap all over this place.  "Ohhh its a chain, ohhh its in the Landmark center, ohhh I was not hugged enough as a child".  Seriously, this place is fantastic and I will guide you through the process as I have eaten at the LH S-house dozens of time. I mean really, I practically paid the electric bill for a couple of years with my patronage.
First, sit in the bar.  The atmosphere is better and the service is better, too.  The people behind the bar are quite competent.  
Second, the wine list is decent and they have plenty of beers, but I highly recommend the margarita list.  LH serves their margs in lame plastic shakers so you can "pour your own".  It seems stupid at first, until you realize that that 1 margarita really = about 2.5.  That = yay in my book.  Get the Perfect Margarita, it is all top shelf stuff, with a twist of orange.
Make sure you ask for bread.  They serve fresh, hot whole wheat loafs with some whipped butter = 2X yay.  
Third, don't order any appetizers, as they all come off of the Sysco food service truck.    
Longhorn, now owned by Darden, was part of the Rare Hospitality Group, which owns the Capital Grille, etc. Hint, hint, order steak at the Longhorn.  These guys know how to broil steak and grill fish, that's it.  Fourth. my suggestion: go right to the steaks.  I get the Flo's filet, 7oz. with blue cheese melted on top, side of either brandied apples or grilled asparagus (get the asparagus in warm weather).  Ask for a side of horseradish, too.  By now, you will be in heaven... the effect of the margarita is kicking in, the steak and blue cheese are melding together and the grilled asparagus are topping things off just right.  
Fifth, if you have the cojones, huevos, etc, order the Chocolate Stampede for desert.  It is delicious, but you need at least two people to eat it.
Longhorn is in the Landmark Center and is great for Red Sox pre-game, pre- and post-movie at the AMC, parents weekend, or just a night out to get a high quality steak at a very decent price.

Input: I've visited a good number of game bars in other cities and play games all the time. With that competition in mind, I still really liked this place. One of the things that you'll either love or hate here is that you play a $5 cover to enter and play as many games as you like. For me, I like that--it made me feel like I wasn't obligated to buy a drink. Usually I want a drink anyways, but I have friends who don't drink and don't know what to do at board game bars that get by on drink orders alone.

The game library here was big, probably not as big as some of the places I've seen in Seattle and Vancouver, but helpfully coded and easy to navigate. The bartenders also were helpful with starting instructions if needed.

One thing I will give them major credit for is that we started out at a large table with another group on half of it. That group left, so it was just the two of us at an 8-top. They needed the table for a big group and asked us if we could move to a 2-top. No problem at all, but on top of that--they comped us a free dessert, which ended up being a tasty bread pudding.

The only reason why I'm knocking them down from 5 stars is because my cocktail didn't really seem to be a cocktail. I ordered the elder sage. As I watched the bartender make it, he didn't seem to be doing much of anything...and then sure enough, I ended up with what seemed to be whiskey on the rocks. I like whiskey, but please don't call that a cocktail.

Input: My fiance and I just moved to the Southwest area, and we ran across this place in search of a good meal after a day of lawn work. I ordered a Jackfruit smoothie, and it was quite delicious. There were real chunks of jackfruit in the smoothie and did not taste like they added too much sugar.

We had the spring rolls to start, and they were very good. I could eat a few orders of these as a meal. The lettuce served with the rolls was a little on the older/thinner side, but this did not seem to detract from the taste at all.

I had some Pho, and I found it very good and authentic. The jalapenos given on the side were so potent that just putting 3 of them into the soup made the soup nice and spicy. The flank and meatballs in the soup were good quality meat and did not have any chunks of fat in the meat. Probably one of the best steak meats I have had in pho ever.

My fiance had some pad thai dish, and it was just as good as any other place we've been to. She orders the same exact dish at ever thai place so she's become somewhat of an expert on this dish. She liked the sauce, but there wasn't quite enough of it for the dish. Doubling the sauce put into this dish should solve the issues with this, and we will definitely ask for this next time.

All in all, I'm glad we found a good place near home, and we will definitely be visiting again. I've read some other readers reviews, and it really seems like the menu is hit and miss. There are quite a few different things on the menu, and I think it may benefit them to either cut things out of the menu or work to improve the dishes which are not up to par. I have a feeling there are more gems in their menu, and I intend to find them. We didn't try to ask the waitress for recommendations,  but this could be a good course of action for future visits.

Input: Went for the Weekend Buffet. The item count is a little less than some other Indian buffets, but they make up for it in Quality. Overall, I wish the curries had a little more spice, but perhaps they'd watered it down to make it palatable for a larger demographic. The Service was friendly, fast and helpful  : 

Let me preface everything by saying - If you want good Mango Lassi, go here, Best in Austin ! 

1. Naan (Bread) : Standard Fare. A little too crispy for my liking, but otherwise ok.
2. Papad : Not the one with the peppercorns (Which has more Zing), but these were cooked in oil ! Which is Good ! Most other places microwave it, which reduces the crispiness.
3. Idli : Below average, too soft and mushy, ideally, should be dry and airy.
4. Vada : A little Small and thin , but the taste was ok.
5. Puri : Below Average, it was just too hard, possibly from sitting too long on the little  burner, not sure.
6. Chana Masala : Good, decent amount of spice, could've used a little more.
7. Mixed Veg. Curry : Better than most Indian buffets which make this curry into a cream-fest.
8. Palak Paneer : Same comment as the Mixed Veg. Decidedly better than the average Indian buffet, could've used a touch more seasoning though.
9. Dal Curry : Average. A little too lacking in spice for my taste.
10. White Rice : Standard Far.
11. Dum Chicken Biryani : This was the highlight of the buffet. Well Seasoned, Tender chicken, really good !
12. Chicken Curry : Same issue as with the other curries - low on spice, but the chicken was well cooked and tender.
13. Fish Curry : I dont eat seafood, so this will have to go unreviewed ! :)
14. French/Green Bean Dish : Another one which was hit out of the park. You dont normally find this in Indian buffets, it's a dry dish made using french beans which have been sliced, and cooked with some spices and coconut, REALLY good.
15. Chaat : Another item you dont normally see in the weekend buffets, the Chaat table had the Papri Chaat and the Pani Puri. The little Chili+Garlic dish that went into the papri chaat was an original !
16. Sambar : Ok.
17. Desserts: The desserts consisted of Shahi Tukda (Crustless Bread, Fried and Soaked in Custard), which was different and good. The second dessert was Dudhi Halwa - like the Carrot Halwa made from Grated Bottle Gourd. It was as it should be - sinful and tasty !

The Lunch Buffet also comes with a Masala Dosa,  The Dosa suffered from the same fate of the idli - just not cooked enough, needed to be done just another minute more, and the masala was watered down as well.

Overall, I'd go again, because the Chaat, Desserts, Biryani and Lassi are not only different from the standard buffet fare, they're worth the trip.

Input: Somewhat under the radar on the pizza landscape, but House Pizzeria is a little jewel on Airport with a diverse menu and chill vibe.  

As self-proclaimed pizza junkies, my friend and I polished off one pie each.  This is one of the only significant drawbacks of House Pizzeria: the pies are smaller than your standard pizzeria, frustratingly teetering between too much for one person and not enough for two.  The special (The Subterranean) was unique blend of potato, fontina cheese, fresh basil, mushrooms, and plenty of carmelized onion that gave the pizza a distinctly sweet flavor.  Though not a traditional offering, it was flavorful, even if a little overpoweringly sweet.

The pepperoni pizza was fairly straightforward, but it was saturated - literally dripping - in oil.  Holding up a slice to let the oil drip off may or may not be your thing, but it seemed a little excessive.

Though our two pizzas were fairly average, House merits four stars based on variables and potential.  They have some good beers on tap, the specials are great, and the place itself is relatively nice (great jukebox for indie fans, clean, mineral water served). Input: Dinner here last night-YELP comments about the wings sold us on trying and we were going to take in a band at the Tilly down the street so this was an easy place to go to.

Atmosphere-definite family style-lodge look with both booths and open seating tables for big groups.  Se scored a two top right by the fireplace which was nice on a chilly evening, upstairs in the dining area.  Theres a "Den" downstairs at the front door.  No carpeting and a large room accents the noise...you wouldn't call this intimate dining.

Our servers (plural) were very efficient-the main waitress actually asked the bartender what single malt they poured for me, when none of the bourbons I requested were available..so I have to say the bar is not well stocked...but it is a blew pub so I guess I should be happy they had anything.

Appetizer of chicken wings came out very fast, but 8 wings for $10 and change seemed a bit steep.  They were, however, quite tasty but not stupendous.  I'll go back for a to go order only because the only other option out here is BW3.  FOTM still rules in the River City for wings.

A nicely sized side salad for $3. was a surprise but the bleu cheese dressing was fairly tasteless.  From a bottle perhaps, if it's house made, they need to be a little more generous with the cheese.

My date and I split a plate of baby back ribs with mac and cole slaw and fries and that was a good thing because it was a huge serving.  The ribs were excellent with a tasty sauce on them.  Fall of the bone tender.  This got the 4th star for what would have been a 3 star review.

The small portions of mac salad and coleslaw were perfectly sized, a good crunchy tangy aside to the  fairly sweet BBQ sauce.  Fries were large but seemed to be frozen french fries from Sysco.  

Neither of us had the beer so no comments on that.

Attentive waitstaff for a busy Saturday night.  

We'll probably go back again-the menu had a lot of standard American meals-Meat Loaf, Salmon, etc but the only vegetarian option was the ever present gardenburger and a hummus and veggie plate for lunch.  This isn't a vegetarians place at all.  Since I'm a 99% vegetarian, I'll take my i% with great ribs thank you.

I have lived in Korea, and I have experienced amazing food there, to include here in America too.  One of my favorite places that I have been, was in Valpraiso, FL, and the restaurant is called Suns Korean Restaurant.  I should post a review for them one day soon.  Another few others close by to that restaurant in Fort Walton Beach are called Korea House and Okki Dokki.  Simply the best Korean Restaurants that I've ever experienced stateside!  If you haven't tried those places yet, you must!  If I could give them 10 stars, I would!

Input: Two words you only need to know, ham bao. And another two, bola bola. 

I've tried the restaurant. It's a standard Chinese restaurant. I don't think I need to elaborate "standard". It's as standard as they come. But for the sake of those who want to ask exactly what I had, I had century egg or preserved duck egg congee with chinese donuts. If you haven't tried it, then I suggest you do before you die. Who knows, it might be your soul food, in comparable to having a soul mate. They're non-existent, as far as my loveless life is concerned, but I'm sure soul food exists. I think the south has already proved, otherwise. 

Back to the ham baos. When I turned 19, I turned to Canada. There's a lot to explore in Vancouver than overstimulating your normal 19 year old overactive alky junkie appetite. There's lansones and rambutan which I try to courageously smuggle into the US but decides to inhale everything by the time I get to the border, and there's the ham bao. Here's how good the ham bao is, no one in Seattle can top it. I'm talking circa 2002 here, cos I moved to San Diego after and I'm sure every Chinese or Filipino bakery have sought every possible way to get New Town's secret ingredient since then. Everyone's neighbor's mum would ask if I can get them 10 dozens each. That's the downside of telling everyone you're going to Canada, but the border patrols are used to it by now.

Input: I'm not usually one to review hotels, but this hotel was a special case.
My family drove down to Orlando for a brief Christmas vacation. We checked in the night before Christmas eve and checked out Christmas Day.

Once we pulled up to the front of the hotel, we had so much trouble with parking. We had no idea where to go. The receptionist suggested we pull up in the back, since our room was closer that way. However, when we got to the back, that lot was filled with a Clemson bus, which I believe was staying there for their bowl game. My "suspicions" were affirmed when we saw all the Clemson banners and posters flying everywhere. Good thing I remembered to leave my FSU hoodie at home.

The atrium/lobby is HUGE. It is often used for conferences and conventions, as there are large conference rooms, auditoriums and ballrooms. There is a Starbucks located conveniently in the lobby, as well, but the prices charged have about a 25% premium over the usual Starbucks (the closest one is located about 1-2 miles away).

I believe this is noted in several other reviews, but if you pay the resort fee ($20 a night), you receive quite a few perks such as parking, TWO free water bottles (usually $3.25, I believe), free Wi-fi (good for up to six devices at one time), free shuttles to and from Disney parks and other amenities that will be listed out for you. Instead of paying for each item individually, it is a much better deal to pay the discounted flat amount.

Our room had 2 queen size beds, a couch (not sleepable), a mini-fridge, and a large TV (I can't recall the measurements, but it is more than enough). There are many available TV channels to watch. The beds are comfortable with plush comforters and pillows. There are many outlets for anyone charging their phones or tablets by the beds, which is a requirement for me.

Overall, my stay here was quite pleasant and conveniently located to many restaurant chains, International Drive and SeaWorld. I would highly recommend to any traveler with any group size!

Input: You have to try this place!

I went here with a couple of friends the other night, and I am so glad I did.  They only opened about a month ago, and I came here because my friends from Chicago happened have a TravelZoo deal from here.

We were greeted by one of the owners, and he was one of the friendliest people I've ever met.  We met Calvin later, who was also very nice.

I'm not sure how fusiony it is, but it doesn't matter because the food was really good. For appetizers we had:
- Duck rolls- basically a duck egg roll.  It was a little on the sweet side for me, but my party seemed to like it.
- Basil rolls- nice and fresh.  There was a slightly sour taste to it that was really good
- Calamari- this was ok- I liked that they had little bits of battered and friend onion in there too.
-  Cream of broccoli with truffle oil (on the house):  They gave us a little thank-you-for-trying-this-place soup.  The soup was not too greasy and the truffle oil was so yummy.

For dinner: 
- Green curry (with beef jerky)- not sure what this beef jerky thing was, but it was delicious.  It was nice soft on the side and chewy on the outside. The green curry was very well made and was my favorite thing there.  If only I could swim in their green curry with my mouth opened...
- Fried chicken with lobster mac:  Chicken breast was tender and well fried.  Lobster mac was ok.
- Crispy beef-  Yum.  You have to try this.  A little crispy on the outside and nice slightly sweet sauce.
- Thai meat meatloaf (not a typo):  Nice seasoning and served with mashed potatoes.  Very good.

For dessert- caramel Fuji apple crusted with Georgia Pecans.  Mmm.. Thinking about it makes me so happy.  The combination was phenomenal.  I don't really like desserts, but I could eat this thing a thousand times over.

The prices are not too terrible.  Entrees were about 12-14 bucks and appetizers were about 6-8.   No alcohol just yet since they just opened, but they are waiting on their license.  I'll definitely venture this way again, and hopefully, Poor Calvin will be Rich Calvin soon.

Input: My first time at this DNB and I absolutely loved it! From the food, to the service, to all of the awesome new games I had an amazing experience! This DNB looks pretty new inside and the game area is huge. As you walk in you are greeted by their service desk that can help you get more points on your card. Behind them is the colorful bar and dining area with large screen tvs. Also, up front is a bathroom, so you do not have to run all the way to the back of the DNB to go.

It was super crowded because of the playoffs, but we were still able to check out tons of games. They had a few new ones, such as Monopoly, Rock em Sock em Robots, and Connect Four. All of them were super fun, particularly the Rock em Sock em as you had to physically move your robot with the controls and then press two buttons to hit the other robot in the face. I think something must have been wrong with the machine as  my friend kept hitting my robot in the face, but I kept winning--who knows?!? But it was fun--just a warning though your hands will be hurting afterwards, but just for a little while.

The food was on point as usual at DNB. I love that they had a texting system, so they were able to let us know we were on the list and then let us know that our table was ready. I just simply had to reply that we were still coming and they held our table for us. Our waitress was super nice and accomodating.  Because it was so crowded she brought us extra drinks. And even though it was crowded she still managed to check on us various times to make sure we were alright. The food was great. I ordered their new turkey sandwich, which had spinach, sundried tomatoes, aoli sauce, slices of thick turkey all topped off on this whole grain rustic rye bread. And instead of the fries I got a side of their broccoli which was cooked to perfectly,  but it did have a little too much butter at the bottom for my liking.

Overall I loved this DNB and if ot were not for the distance I would be back every couple of weeks to let out some stress and just have fun! They describe it as an adult playground and it so is!! So come, play, eat, drink, and be merry--leave the kidos with a babysitter!!

Input: We started with the tuna nachos which, if I'm being completely honest, are elevated "comfort" food. They're very well done, but if it's possible to feel trashy while paying $16 for nachos, this is the appetizer to do it. That being said, I'd totally order them again.

The crispy pork is a wildly under rated appetizer. Beautifully crispy, the savoriness of the pork nicely offset by the kimchi and vinaigrette. 

The short ribs were good, but not fall-apart tender. Austin is a BBQ mecca, so your proteins better be on point. By far, my biggest issue with the meal was the sour mash. It was extremely sour. Believe me, I'm a fan of funky foods: kimchi, kombucha, sour beers, I love 'em all. This was not a case of "little bit of sour cream in the potatoes." More like "the milk was starting to turn." It didn't make me ill, but it was very off putting, especially juxtaposed with the other dishes.

The bar was similarly underwhelming. Our table ordered a round of blueberry mojitos, followed by the tequila francois. Both were just okay, dominated by the mixers, with seemingly little actual alcohol. My wife ordered a glass of prosecco, and for the first time in my life, I was jealous of wine. Be aware, Plate is extremely proud of their cocktails, in this case it nearly doubled our bill.

Was the experience good? Sure, it was good. But at nearly $100/person, it wasn't mind blowing. Don't get me wrong, I'm glad to have true high-end dining in the Lakeway/Bee Caves area, but on the rare occasions I'm feeling fancy, I might just make the trip downtown anyway.

Input: Another Yelp controversy to weigh in on! 3.5 stars rounded up to 4 because the -.5 star is largely due to the sour interaction I had with one of the older dudes we were interacting with, reproduced below.

Johnny's Hideaway is definitely *entertaining* and deserves appreciation for that alone.  And even though there are certainly downsides, it's UNIQUE.  I like unique places, as a rule.  I'm probably decently likely to return when invited because amusement in the form of familiar old tunes and male attention in varying degrees of unwelcomeness is all but guaranteed.  

I went somewhat spontaneously with two girlfriends after picking up one of them at the airport at 1:00 AM (flight delay due to ATL weather).  I was DD.  One of my two girlfriends was supposed to get married this weekend - Johnny's was quite sympathetic and let her in without paying the $5 cover.  Then the DJ immediately played a song I requested on her behalf.  The bartender was quite nice to us and attentive.  

The bar is well placed and spacious, and there are lots of places to sit down all over in the form of round cushy low chairs and little tables . This is GREAT.  I know it is cool to stand up all the time, but annoying - I like having the option of sitting down and somewhere to set my drink.  This is rather necessary, because drinks are Not Allowed on the dance floor.  If you step onto the dance floor with a drink in your hand, you Will be accosted by a smoky dude in a velvet suit who calls himself Elvis.  This got annoying, but it's nice to know you won't get spilled on on the dance floor, honestly. And the mirror wall was fun, but I was not so much about it last night, when I had flat hair, glasses and no makeup on and was wearing the shirt I'd worn to work and just spilled wine on while watching "Australia" on my friend's couch.  

As for the crowd, I had heard of the cougar/old dude reputation, and that contingent was certainly represented.  This late, though, there were plenty of young kids too.  I didn't dress for the club because I didn't know I was going there, but I fit in fine, and felt plenty attractive despite my schlubby dress and appearance.  More importantly, my friend had a good time :)

I feel compelled to relate the following negative experience I had with one of the older dudes, possibly a regular (based only on the fact that he gave a big hug to "Elvis"), who appeared to be there by himself.  We will call him "R."  So he seemed to be interested enough in all three of us.  He was not half bad looking either.  He started dancing with my would-be-getting-married friend, and I was glad he seemed to be giving her attention, but then it turned into too much attention and she bailed on him.  THEN a guy we used to work with showed up and we started talking to him, right next to R.  I think R felt a little dissed.  Then R bought my other friend a beer and she ran off and danced with this adorable young guy.  Then he tried to buy me a beer and I said "sorry, I can't drink beer, it's Passover" to which my friend responded, "really? You're going to try to explain being a Jew in *this* place?" And then I ran away too, and I think he felt a little dissed by all three of us.  So, when we got back, he said "you all are f#$@ing teases."  And I was like, um, that's not nice.  And then he was like "lawyers, f#$% lawyers man, the last thing we need is more lawyers."  (All three of us were lawyers.)  I said in a slightly more confrontational tone, Um, seriously, that's not nice.  He was like, "I know it's not nice, but it's true."  So then I said, "well what do you do?" And he said he'd been a [X] (redacted for privacy) for 17 years - I sort of got the feeling he might not be employed right now.  So I immediately said, "f$#@ [X]-s." and he seemed kind of hurt, even though I was just trying to demonstrate how his comment had been totally out of line.  Later that night though, I felt really bad about it.  Like, he probably just said that because he felt bad about his interactions with us, which I admit were probably not ideal.  So I'm sorry, R.  I still think your comments were out of line, but I should not have responded in kind.

So, that was my night at Johnny's Hideaway.  Definitely a good decision to go, will most likely have occasion to return.

Input: Chick-Fil-A in a central Columbus location was a long time coming. They would have gotten a lot more of my money over the years had they had a location closer to me. I guess the best thing I can say is thank you.

Brand new place so everything is spic and span, but I don't think I have ever been in a dirty Chick-Fil-A. Not sure how KFC or Popeyes are going to continue with their footprint given the CFA expansion and growing footprint.

As expected they were busy, but they worked fast and friendly and never let us see them sweat. Service with a smile is a way of life with this chain.

I ordered a Spicy Chicken that was fried to perfection and was thankful for the extra pickles as a way to contrast the heat. The waffle fries were fresh, fluffy on the inside, and the right amount of salt. The fresh squeezed lemonade was the right amount of sweet and just enough tart to make me smirk.

Chick-Fil-A is all about their chicken and have the best variety of sandwiches in their industry. They have great kids meals (who else has grilled nuggets), awesome salads, fresh fruit cups, pretty good soups, and breakfast burritos and sandwiches that put McDonalds and Taco Bell to shame. My girlfriend is addicted to their shakes, they get me brownie points when I bring them to her with their fresh baked cookies.

The next time I say something bad about Chick-Fil-A will be the first. I highly recommend this chain to everyone I know except on Sundays.

Input: This place ended up being a great last stop on our afternoon trip to Icon Park.  As soon as I walked in, I could see this place had that classy sports bar sort of vibe.  A bar right in the middle of the room with TVs all over the place, yet very comfortable, spaced-out seating.  The booths were awesome too.  More comfortable than your average ones.  

We lucked out and arrived exactly as happy hour began, so we enjoyed $2 off our beer and cocktails and half off most of the apps.  We ended up just ordering all appetizers so we could try a bunch of different things and not break the bank.  

First off, the Pineapple Cider I had was pretty tasty.  It did, however, taste like I was drinking champagne while a large Hawaiian dude was smacking me in the face with a pineapple.  It was very sweet.  Still... not bad.  

The Boneless Firecracker Wings were on point.  They didn't come with a dipping sauce to cool them off though, which was easily corrected by just asking for it.  It definitely needed it.  They had a kick.  

The chicken lettuce wraps were interesting.  Impossible to eat... not bad.  The sauces were very strange though.  Not quite sure they went well with the dish.  The tofu was a nice twist though.

The Moo Shu Egg Rolls were awesome.  Definitely something I haven't had before.  They looked a lot like the south western egg rolls you find at some Tex-Mex places, but with Asian flavors.  The sauce it came with was weird to be honest.  It was like an apple sauce... but not really.  It's hard to explain but I kept going back for more of it.  

The fried calamari was decent, but I found the bread to squid ratio a bit off.  A lot of pieces just felt like I was only eating the batter.  Still, the tartar sauce it came with was pretty addictive and made up for it for the most part. 

The sliders are pretty great too.  The meat seemed like good quality stuff and the homemade sauce that came on it was really flavorful.  The buns were a bit of a let down.  I usually prefer a more potato roll-like bread with my sliders.  But that's just me.  Also, the fries were amazing.  Perfectly salted and really addictive.  

The star of the meal were the chicken nachos.  I couldn't believe it was an appetizer!  It was a huge plate.  Recently, the nachos I've tried from different places have been a bit of a let down.  These were a different story.   Loaded with tons of chicken, cheese, beans, and more cheese... they were awesome.  At a certain point I just avoided the mess and started forking off all the toppings and just eating them without the chips.  It was still really great.  

Dessert was no let-down either.  We got the sampler, which came with mini versions of three different desserts.  The chocolate soufflé was dense and very chocolatey.  Was more like a chocolate torte in a cup, but as a chocolate lover, I was enjoying every bite.  

The creme brûlée cheese cake was incredible!  I mean... two of my favorite desserts in one.  Nothing to complain about there.  

The peach apple cobbler was like an apple pie fresh out the oven.  The vanilla ice cream was a perfect little addition.  Also a great dessert.  

Service was all extremely friendly.  Even had one server come by and compliment us for our table full of food, saying "happy hour done right... I love it."  Food was for the most part pretty good.  The location of this place is great too.  Only a 20 second walk from the Orlando Eye.  There were a couple of other places to eat within a short distance from here, but I'm glad we chose this place.  Had a good experience.

Input: What kind of hole have I been living in that I have not been to Lineage yet for Brunch, despite it being but steps from my door? I finally crawled out of my cave for Sunday brunch and loved Lineage as soon as I walked in the door, it is bright, airy, clean, spacious, minimalist but still warm. - Bread basket - YUM - 5 piece assortment of scones, mini muffins, banana bread, all moist, light, and flavorful, served with delicious jams, and yes maple butter, I have never met a maple butter I did not like.

- Polenta with lardons - creamy buttery polenta (again, I usually hate polenta, but this was good and not too heavy) - the lardons big and chunky, were not greasy and went well with the baby spinach. 
- Prime Rib Burger - Very Juicy, flavorful, cooked perfectly on a light brioche bun. Nothing fancy but very good. Fries are thick, crisp and not greasy.

...and while this place is a bit more upscale than any other place in Coolidge Corner, it all came out to only $20 per person, which includes tax and tip. I noticed that their menu is dated, so it changes daily - so I'll be back in the hopes they'll bring back the lobster tacos. Overall this is a refined and delicious dining experience, and for what you are able to get, that will leave your pocket pleasantly surprised.

Our table of 3 polished off everything we ordered. The meats were so tender and well seasoned, none of the meats needed the sauces it came with, it was really difficult to stop, so we didn't.

Input: So lucky to have stayed here.  My friend and I made plans to attend the inaugural Skookum Music Festival.  It was this last weekend and I just got home.  We found availability in June and secured the last room! Phew.  It has a classic look to the lobby, high end, sort of older.  Properly attired porters and doormen.  Location is very handy.  It was about a 50 minute walk to our Event. Loads of shops, bars, restaurants, grocers, to walk to from the Sutton Place.  A nice merchant is located right there if you need to grab some quality beverages.  We were so excited on landing and getting checked in we selected a sparkling wine and 6 pack of local pale.  The Sparkling Wine was very memorable, Blue Mountain from Okanagan Valley in B.C. it was delightfully dry and the clerk even suggested.  That's an affirmation.  We got to our room to discover a wide, generous view of the city.  Loads of large almost skyscraper buildings.  Who is washing all those windows.  Anyway, I could gaze out that window all day.  It was especially nice since the day we landed - it was bright and sunny.  The amenities were nice, no fridge in the room, though.  Bummer.  
The beds were extraordinary.  They were incredibly comfy.  TV was fine, we had it on for background, opening day of football - but the guide was dumb.  It stated channel IDs, but not programs.  The concierge helped us a few times.  I like their style and demeanor here, straightforward, polite. We ordered room service one day for Breakfast!  Such a treat.  It was perfect.  I had a simple eggs, toast, potatoes.  We were on the 17th floor.  The price was reasonable.  I think less than $200 night for two Queen beds.  So worth it, warm hospitality, great location.  Pretty city, just needed a few more days of sun. One other odd thing, we had empty bottles that just sat there for a few days.  Left a note for staff to remove, they did. I couldn't find the fitness center - but I think it's in another adjacent building.  Was allowed an earlier check in - bonus!

Of note: there was a Santa graveyard below us.  The rooftop of one of the buildings below had a pile of decorative Santa Clauses, clustered together in the corner.  Kind of funny.  We didn't do any research on this siting.

Input: My boyfriend had been here twice with friends and kept telling me that he wanted to take me here as well. I was always kinda meh about it since it is "British" food, and I figured that would be a bunch of meat with some plain side such as mash. Finally I decided to give it a shot, considering it got 4 stars on Yelp. 

We came here on a late Saturday night. I was immediately excited when I saw how cute the restaurant looked! It was a little British looking house of some kind. We entered through the bottom floor and took the stairs upstairs to the main seating area. I was happy to see that it was busy, but we were still able to get a seat right away. 

One of the things that had me excited about the Fat Badger was the ever changing menu. We started with a Scotch egg and croquettes which were absolutely amazing!! Our mini Yorkshire puddings came out afterwards, making me want more. I had the rabbit on special for my main, and my boyfriend went for the bangers with mash. The portions were very generous, which is rare for these types of restaurants. I had to take some home as I was leaving some room for dessert. And am I ever glad I had room, because we ordered the sticky toffee pudding which was incredible. The hot toffee pudding with butterscotch sauce, mixed with the cold vanilla ice cream was probably one of the best desserts I've ever tasted! 

After this experience, I could tell why my boyfriend raves about this place. We are definitely coming back, and very soon!!

Input: Usually when I lunch at Leow's, I go for the salad bar, but I finally got to try out Saltwood's burger bar experience that all my coworkers always talk about. Essentially, they have room for 8 at a long wooden table in the back kitchen where you sit facing the cooks as they prepare your meal. You order a burger (or shrimp po'boy) of your choice along with a dessert. I came on a Wednesday during lunch with 4 other coworkers. Just a note: this in-kitchen dining experience is ending in a month, so be sure to check it out before then if it interests you!

I got the Saltwood burger with goat cheese and mushrooms and it was delicious. The French was also a hit, as was the shrimp sandwich and the Southern. It comes with your choice of regular or sweet potato fries, which are just standard.

For dessert, I opted for the Bananas Foster-type dish which was unreal -- it comes atop 2 mini Belgian waffles sandwiching a scoop of vanilla ice cream and heavily drizzled with caramelly bananay chocolatey goodness (and of course, bananas). Super sweet and rich, but I couldn't stop eating it. The ooey gooey cake was also a huge hit, but a little too much for me.

The in-kitchen experience was a little weird -- you're just in the kitchen which isn't particularly glamorous watching someone put burgers on a grill and prepare other food while the dishwashers work behind you. I guess you do kind of feel like VIP when you're back there though. I'm glad they serve the burgers outside in the main bar area as well so I won't miss out once they stop offering this experience!

Input: A friend suggested Elephants Deli for Happy Hour, which surprised me as I always thought of this as a place to go for prepared take-home meals, catering (I've hired them several times to cater holiday events for my team) and to purchase gourmet pantry items. Who knew that happy hour or sit down meals was an option? Obviously not me!

We enjoyed a cocktail and glass of wine, split a delicious margarita pizza cooked in their Italian open fire oven and then perused the various stations and offerings. There were so many sections of the store it was like a giant food and gift court under one roof:

- I was amazed at how large their gift area is, taking up a large portion of the store. So many items for that foodie in your life! And lots of cute things for kids. Elephants is on the "tourist" route and I'm sure many of these Portland influenced gifts make their way to other parts of the country
- Wine area with a varied selection, something for everyone
- Cheese, cheese and more cheese. Select 2 or three, grab a bottle of wine and baguette and a prepare salad and you have an instant picnic.
- The dessert area should not be missed! They have a "ding-dong" cake that reminds me of childhood and that classic treat. The Marionberry Chiffon cake looked divine and I convinced the person next to me gawking at it to buy it! He came back and thanked me - better the calories on him than me!
- There is an entire area dedicated to fresh made meats and salads with everything from orzo, couscous, potatoe, grilled flank steak, chicken cutlets, roasted veggies and more. Options are amazing!
- They also have a section dedicated to hot foods and their classics are all still there: chicken enchiladas, Mac & cheese, and tomato pic (get this when it's in season.) plus hamburgers, pizza and other hot foods made to order. 
- The freezer section is loaded with prepare but not cooked versions of the classics listed above and chicken pot pie, large variety of soups and so much more. Times when I have had to have surgery, I have stocked up here. And grab and go sandwiches and salads. Get the Jambon et fromage; classic and fab.

Throughout the entire store, on every conceivable counter, there are chocolates and candies and gummies piled high. Elephants reminds me of an adult version of Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory, with everything a foodie could want, in abundance everywhere you turn!

Prices are a bit high, imho, so rather than stock up, I tend to purchase specialty items or utilize for convenience when entertaining. Now I will also add Elephants to my list of lunch or HH meeting places to enjoy friendship over an adult beverage and really good food.

Input: I admittedly have never had the "art house cinema" experience, but with that said I do embrace new things, people and places. So despite never hitting up the Dobie before it closed I was intrigued when I heard Violet Crown Cinema was opening on 2nd Street.

The first big plus is the free parking. If catching a movie at VCC, park in the AMLI on San Antonio between 2nd & 3rd street right by How Do you Roll?, bring in your parking ticket and VCC with validate it so you don't have to pay (good for up to 4 hours).

The second plus is they have a reasonably priced menu with lots of beer, wine and mixed drink options. The food menu is somewhat small and the only item over $10 is the Antonelli's cheese plate. I loved the cheese plate which had bread, honey, pistachios, and a generous portion of 3 types of cheeses. The mister had a pizza which was OK and on the small side. 

The movies do not have previews. It was nice to go watch a movie without the corporates forcing you to watch 15 minutes of trailers.

The Australian made seats are comfy and they have the old school table trays that pull out from the side. The one down fall is it is hard to find room for a plate of food and a drink. Speaking of food and drinks, you order outside the cinema in the lounge/bar area and carry it in yourself (although staff offered to help us carry it in).

Bad seat? One does not exist at VCC. Sitting in the front row will not put a crook in your neck but instead you get the lazy boy of the cinema chairs.

I adore this place and will be back.

The chicken noodles, a bargain at $6.50 has a good amount of vegies and chicken, but the emphasis is on the noodles. It wouldn't be a bad strategy to take it home, divide into 4 portions and add your own vegetables. 

The spicy is covered with a nice coating of coarse chili sauce, but you will have to add more seasoning if you like heat. There is a large bottle of Sriracha sauce on the counter. 

It's great to watch the owner at the wok. Perfect timing. He formerly cooked at Du Kuh Bee.

Other countries discovered the allure of starch, oil, salt and spices, long before modern fast food, to captivate the tastebuds of their customers. That doesn't mean that  we shouldn't eat those foods across cultures, in moderation, today.

Input: In terms of a GREAT Friday night dinner/ bar scene, I would definitely recommend checking out Estragon in the South End. Our visit here stemmed from a craving for a few drinks and some small plates. I had heard about the restaurant in passing from some friends, so really didn't have an idea of what to expect. 

First, parking was pretty easy. There are plenty of metered spots on the street and also plenty of resident parking if you're from the area. From my understanding, there are also a ton of bus stops nearby. The signage for Estragon is also very easy to spot from the street. 

We decided to sit at the bar for dinner, and honestly I'm glad we made this choice. The bartender Joseph was great the entire evening. He was careful to pay close attention to our needs from our arrival, all the way through our dinner, and with our final cocktails. The bar scene was also great throughout the night. Even with some very excited female patrons (someone had just gotten engaged), the atmosphere was well suited to a nice, intimate evening. 

In terms of food, here is a quick overview:

*** Queso de Cabra con Tomate (V) (Warm Goats' Cheese, Tomato on Toast) - This came with 2 long pieces of toast with a heaping amount of goat's cheese. You definitely have to cut the pieces to make them manageable to eat, but they are VERY good. 
*** Garbanzos Fritos (VG) (Crispy Paprika Chickpeas) - I think these were overrated. You can eat a handful as a snack and they're okay, but wouldn't order them again. 
*** Coles de Bruselas (Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Chorizo, Golden Raisins) - Very good side veggie dish. Would definitely order them again. Heaping portion too. 
*** Espinacas a la Catalana (VG) (Sautéed Spinach, Pine Nuts, Golden Raisins) - Again, really good choice for a side veggie dish. Good portion and well flavored.
*** Pulpito a la Parilla ( Marinated, Grilled Baby Octopus) - This was also a good dish, but you have to be okay with the whole head and body being part of the dish. Well seasoned and a good portion too.
*** Conejo a la Cazadora (Braised Rabbit, Tomato, Onion, White Wine) - This was a great meat dish aside from all the bones in the meat. It was a great flavor w/ the white wine and the pieces of meat were pretty big, but I spent a lot of time spitting out the small bones. It takes a lot of work to get through this dish. 

HIGHLIGHT****
DRINKS: We had a few different cocktails on the list and nothing really stood out as much as the Absenthe Special Cocktail with Absinthe and Angostura Bitter for $9 a piece. This was definitely something you need to try!! Again, our bartender Joseph was great with this part of our visit. He took the time to actually create an experience with the Absinthe cocktail, which made it that much more fun for us and other guests. He actually set up a tall glass holding pitcher which dripped the absinthe mix over two small glasses set up with sugar cubes. He also lit the cubes on fire to burn the sugar while the absinthe dripped into the glasses. It was really the best part of the visit, as I have never seen this done at another venue, ever. 

The total at the end of the visit was also expected. Although somewhat pricey (as tapas often is), we thought the value of the meal met the price well. If you're in the South End and looking for a great, unique dining experience, check this place out. And certainly try to go and sit at the bar when Joseph is around. He's fast paced, pays close attention to his guests and definitely makes the experience worthwhile with regard to the cocktails.

Input: Chef Rob's certainly made an impression on my Caribbean palate. As a true island girl, it takes a lot for me to admit when island food is good but Chef Rob's was on point! I can only comment on the food as we had our food delivered. Overall, the food was great! I had the shrimp curry run-down that was very tasty! I usually don't like my food too spicy but this dish had the perfect balance where it wasn't too mild nor too hot - 2 thumbs up in that arena. I also had some conch fritters that came with a dipping sauce. These didn't blow me away. I've honestly had better but they weren't that horrible that I couldn't finish them. They were okay. 

The reason I give the restaurant 4 stars instead of 5 is for 2 reasons. 

Reason #1: They failed to make our substitution for rice and peas instead of jasmine rice. I was quite shocked to see a Caribbean restaurant have jasmine rice as their staple compliment to their dish. Rice and peas is the caribbean staple. You eat it with everything: chicken, shrimp, goat, ox tail, fish, beef. That jasmine rice just threw me for a loop. If that's the case, there shouldn't be an additional charge to swap out jasmine rice for rice and peas. It should be no cost for that. 

Reason #2: The prices are a bit up there for some Caribbean food. Don't get me wrong. The food is great but Chef Rob's will only get my business once or twice a month (and that's pushing it). For the shrimp run down and conch fritters, I was at about $25-26 and this was before tax and delivery charge. I consider this to be an indulgence, perhaps a reward for doing something good (eating well, losing some pounds, etc). 

Chef Rob's: Thank you for the yummy food on my trip to Atlanta but if I were a resident of the area, you would only see me on special occasions like tax return time or something :-) I still recommend that you try it and experience it for yourself. You won't be disappointed. Oh, and I also heard that the mango pie is to die for but I didn't get to taste it since my sis-in-law forgot to order it (why would she torture me so???) Happy eating!!!

It's a small little tiny place, reminds you of a place that high school students would hang out after the football game.  The wife ordered the Mike's Special Deluxe and I ordered the Applewood bacon burger. She upgraded her meal for a Marion Berry milkshake. 

The food did not disappoint at all. I thought it tasted really good. The burgers were not too greasy and the fries were cooked very well. That Marion Berry milkshake...oh yeah that was some really good stuff. 

A few weeks later we went here after playing basketball, this time her brother and my brother joined us as well. They ordered their meals but got soft drinks instead. Wife asked them...why didn't you upgrade? It's like $0.99 more. Her brother was like...really? So he upgraded his as did my brother. And the reaction was..."wow...that milk shake is really good".

I can defiantly see me dragging my daughter here for food in the future when she's old enough to hold a burger. Forget sushi...give me a burger!

Input: Reading the reviews of this place on Yelp, I was a bit hesitant to go.  I like to make my own decisions and with that I have to say my experience here was much better than most of the other reviewers.  I also never got here before they changed owners.  

I am originally from the east coast.  Some of you know that.  When I was younger, I wasn't a big hot dog fan.  The only place I would eat hot dogs at was Nathan's on Coney Island.  There was something about that place that made the hot dogs taste like the best things in the world.

Now I live in Portland, and don't get to Nathan's as much as I'd like to.  The mall versions just aren't the same.  Bring in Nick's Famous Coney Island.  Ok, I didn't expect to get the same thing I got at Nathan's, but the name still made me want to go.  That and the 2 for 1 coupons they offer that can be found in the local papers.   

The friend I went with likes to eat.  I like to eat.  This is a good place to do that and not spend a ton of money (with the coupon, that is).

The Coney dog menu has a few options.  The single, double, triple, home run and veggie Coney.  Prices range from $6.75-$15.  I'm sure you can guess the single is one dog, the double is two dogs and so on.  We went with...........wait for it................wait for it.............two triples.  In hindsight, two doubles would have sufficed, but when you have 2 for 1, you go for it.  The dogs come with a side of mac salad or potato chips.  Fries can be added for a buck.  Side salad for two bucks.

I should go back a bit.  The service tended to be a bit on the slow side, but everyone was super friendly there and I wasn't in a rush.  The bartender had a bunch of people she needed to take care of, but seemed to do it with a smile on her face.  The guy who ultimately brought us our dogs came by a few times to see how we were enjoying our food.  These are the little things that most places don't do that made my experience that much better.

With the knowledge that dogs were on their way, we ordered a few beers, took in the Atlanta Hawks-Miami Heat playoff game (Hawks won.  I am a fan.) and waited in anticipation for doggy goodness.

They arrived.  I wasn't quite sure how to eat them.  Covered in chili and cheese with a huge side of crispy potato chips, I decided to go with the fork and knife option.  I am usually a hands on eater, but there really wasn't a neat way to pick these up without dropping most of the contents on my shirt and subsequently on the floor.  Much rather the food was in my stomach and not on said floor.

I am not going to say that these dogs reminded me of Nathan's on Coney Island, but they were pretty good.  Had a nice snap when cutting into them and the chili with onions was very tasty.  This is also a meal I couldn't eat all the time.  So much food, but that isn't a bad thing.  I finished every bite much to the amazement of my friend as well as the bartender.  

So, hot dogs and beer.  Sounds like America.  Or something like that.  I enjoyed my experience here and plan on getting back again soon.  Hmmm.  Not the greatest ending to this review, but it is an ending.

Input: Been meaning to stop here for quite some time. I dig the whole industrial, concrete, steel gig they have going on. Nice street presence as you pass making you want to stop. Side dish of fried red pots were exceptional- cooked to perfection. Crispy edges, soft inside. BUT here it comes- I'm not salt sensitive, if anything I find myself adding salt here and there- but not here! Put the industrial salt grinder out on display and return to a regular table sized shaker. Wholly cow was it all salty. Tongue pissed off on the way home salty.
Oh but- I was given such a good portion I had left overs and the next day wooo weee was it excellent. Still salty but the layering of flavors in the gravy is exceptional. I think they make this fresh for each order (?) if that's the case have them back off the salt a bit and you'll be happily lapping up the gravy.

Dessert- They called it chocolate pie. It was somewhat 'old' seeming very thick chocolate pudding in a cup over a chocolate crumb dust/not crust. Eh. Not my thing for $5. 

Service was great, place was clean and you could tell it's a neighborhood joint with some regulars at the counter. Nice

Yeah I'll go back

Input: nomnomnom.  As my screen name implies, I truly heart sushi rolls.  I have been searching Austin for good sushi since moving here from LA in November and this place really hit the sweet spot in my tummy.  

My boyfriend and I shared a few dishes including the grilled chicken spring roll (nice and crispy, delicious dipping sauce), seaweed salad (standard but good), a spicy tuna roll (oh, LOVED this little one), volcano roll (oooooooooohmy), spider roll (crispy, hot, perfectly cooked) and the scallop sushi.  They had a lot of rolls with crawfish and the volcano roll looked the most appetizing to me - it was a California roll inside with crawfish cooked outside.  It was really tasty and had a slightly spicy/sweet sauce on top.  The scallop sushi was really divine.  It was buttery and completely melted in my mouth.  

This place is a little out of my price range to enjoy regularly but as a treat on a Friday night it was perfect.  Parking was impossible downtown so we valet parked which I completely hate but got over.  We arrived early enough (about 6:30) to be seated at the sushi bar but the room was packed by the time the normal dinner hour so I would definitely recommend reservations.  The service was great - everyone was so nice but not overbearing.  

I checked out the happy hour menu as we were leaving - they have a normal early hour happy hour AND a late night happy hour.  I will definitely be back during one of those time frames so I can eat twice as much sushi.
