Input: I feel embarrassed to even write this review.  I don't get four stars for my actions here, maybe not even two.  Let's relive it anyway.

I had the boyfriend place an order here while I was at the store so that I'd go pick it up after I was done.  The only mistake they did make was to leave out the order of fried shrimp.  That made me think that the order of . . . something else, I don't remember what at this point, was something we didn't order.  So, I told him it looked like we got one wrong thing.  The man up front apologized, put in an order for the fried shrimp and left the "wrong" order in the bag (well, box, we ordered too much!).  I texted the boyfriend and found out I was wrong and he did order what I thought he hadn't.  I felt bad and tried to pay for it, but he was very insistent that I didn't pay for it and helped me on my way.  One small misstep on their part (leaving out the shrimp), but a much larger misstep on my part and they handled it much better than they should have.

So, when I got home, I really wanted to be able to give this place five stars.  Unfortunately, I couldn't quite do it.  The food was good, but not good enough for me to feel justified in giving out a five star review.  There's nothing wrong with it, but it's not better than Chinese food we've had at other places.  We'll go back and hope to be able to give them the extra star.

Input: Feets don't fail me now!  When your dogs hurt,  your whole life can suffer.  No jumping jacks, no jump lunges, no stairmasters, no dancing in high heels.  Oh, wait, only one of those sux to be without.  Still, sometimes just walking around can be painful, and even tho I do enjoy laying about with my feet up, it can make you cranky to have work all day on your ouchy feet.  

So, thanks to Dej (who is in my shoes, so to speak), I checked out Dr Godhania yesterday.  One thing I have learned firsthand is, when you are searching for a doctor, don't pick one based on name alone.  I thought my last guy would really be able to sympathize with me as his name was Dr Payne.  Wrong, wrong, wrong.  He spent months on me and made me some "custom orthotics" that did not address my issues at all (he thought I had bunions, the catchall diagnosis for toe pain).  

Dr Godhania on the other hand (foot), did a little mashing around (ouch!) and some x-rays and nailed my diagnosis, sesamoiditis.  Great!  I already knew that as I have the internet.  He was very straightforward about the treatment options, very explanatory about my films, and very encouraging about my future in exercising.  He has sent me on to get yet another set of custom orthotics made, but he swears these will be the be all, end all of, well, them all.  

So I am reserving a star for future results.  I really, really hope he gets that 5th star!

Which is good, because the barkeeps here really do sling stiffies.

As for the Pickle Back. It's yum. Trust me. I am a pickle fan. I am an even bigger whiskey fan. Combined, the two develop an almost super power. Delish.

Input: Disclaimer: I've only been here once.

Setup: This is an all-you-can-eat where you walk in, throw ingredients in a bowl, add some sauces based on either several suggested guides or whatever you think is a good idea, and then they cook it on a huge metal surface with swords (seriously).

Recommendations: PAY IN CASH, follow one of the suggested sauce guides with minor variation, and I'd go heavy on veggies rather than proteins (less meat/tofu, more veggies).  Get a very full plate as many of them (especially leafy greens and tomatoes) will cook down to a much smaller pile.

Pros:

* Lots of great, fresh ingredients for a variety of palates

* A remarkable number options in the way of stuff to spice and flavor your food

Cons:

* Be aware that at checkout the default "suggested" tip is WELL above the generally accepted food service minimums (18/20/25%).  My food was great but really all you should be giving is 15% for a place that's only doing drink service.  Also, I give the guy at the grill $1 because that dude was on point.

* The spinach didn't look great when I was there.

Wishlist:

* A little clearer explanation about how things work for newcomers.

* Would like to see partial coverage of the various sauces (e.g. the top half of the container being covered).  I know all that stuff is very stable in an open air environment and gets cooked anyway, but it just seemed a little *too* open.

Input: Continuing our 2013, "Around the World in a wheelchair tour" the only reason I give Le Cellier 4 stars and not 5 is due to the poor interior design coming from a newbie wheelchair user.  At the entrance there is very little seating/waiting area for a chair, while I did find an area somewhat out of the way, I ended up waiting outside so that other visitors wouldn't have to brush up against the chair or knock over my crutches.  

Access to the dining area was okay, but tight between the tables, I can see why this is one of the harder reservations in Epcot to get, there just isn't enough seating, even with tables crammed in together to keep this romantic and inviting.

Our service was stellar, the light up menus was a nice little techno-nod to all things Disney.  Started with bread basket, Charcuterie plate and Canadian Cheddar Cheese Soup, it all matched perfectly.  Fine dining for sure.

My MIL and I opted for the Filet Mignon we both inhaled the meal, the Mrs. had the Lobster Macaroni & Cheese along with a salad and cheese plate for her meal.  That Lobster mac was amazing!!!  I was lucky to snag a bite prior to the elbows coming up to protect the rest of the plate.

The littlest one had the kids Seared Salmon, really we should have sent it back, frozen fish and well, it tasted like the freezer.  Coming from the land of fresh wild caught salmon of the Pacific Northwest, this was a major let down.  But it was made up by the kids Chocolate Moose, just google the image, it was cute and tasted pretty darn good.

Staff was very friendly, spot on with the refills of water, bread and oh my the butter....

Yup, we'll be back!!!!

Input: For me there are only a few things that make a gym good: quantity of routes, diversity of routes, and the people it attracts.

MetroRock really does a great job on all three. The route setters aren't just technical crimp climbers or jug setters with huge dyno moves. These guys dream up some of the weirdest and coolest sh!t ever. Sometimes I look at routes and think they can't be done and after a while working on them I can only see beta. This gym is great for that. Lots of opportunity to grow your mindset on how to climb. 

The quantity is good as well - as others have mentioned this place can get busy but more often than not you can find plenty of climbers to share beta and that's a huge part of climbing. Learning how you climb and taking bits from equal or stronger climbers is a great way to push yourself and become a better climber and everyone here is pretty cool. It's rare to find a climber that won't cheer you on even if you are just working V1,2,3. 

Although I don't often find myself utilizing the whole gym - I have tried out some of their top rope and lead and even on busy nights I can usually find a few open lines to work and they seem to be pretty unique/diverse as well. 

As a side note - they run a shuttle from the Wellington T stop for free so even if you live in the city and don't have a car there is an easy way to get out and back.

Input: I came to sunstone on the recommendation of a roommate who took classes there regularly for about a year. It was my first hot yoga experience. I signed up for the 10 for $10 deal and took 6 classes over 10 days. After the promotional deal was over, I received a couple calls for them about signing up for a membership, but refrained on account of not being able to justify both a gym and yoga membership.  A few weeks later, however, I purchased a 10 class card which I JUST finished, over a year later. yikes. Lately, though,  I've been going to hot yoga twice a week and practicing 3x a week.The key for me, I think,  is going in the morning. I love arriving a few minutes early and napping in the hot room on my yoga mat in Shivasana before class starts. I was initially a little skeptical of the who hot yoga/bikram thing, and I don't think all the sweat your toxins out hoopla is correct, but something about the heated room is really awesome. Now that I do both hot and not-hot yoga regularly, I can attest to the fact that hot yoga does help you stretch further, deeper, and better. You leave feeling invigorated, and your skin looks awesome. 

Sunstone's strong points are that it is clean, quiet, and really convenient for me. I've heard people complain about smell in hot yoga studios and that is NOT the case here. The instructors are really nice, enthusiastic about yoga, describe the postures really well, and correct you as they see fit. The studio provides mats and towels, sells water, has tea in the waiting area, and stock the showers with bath supplies and clean bath towels. I also like that they offer 1-hour classes in addition to 1.5-hour classes that are more typical of the stricter bikram. I can't sit through 90 minutes, but 60 is perfect. 

The rooms leave a little to be desired...the air conditioning is a bit loud and I've was dripped on by condensation once, however, I don't know that these things can necessarily be helped in a room that has to be maintained at almost 100 degrees and 60% humidity. I also wish they had more classes,  but I'm sure this must depend hugely on the volume of clientele at the studio. Also, initially, I was turned off by the sales-yness and the high cost of yoga, but the class cards work really well for me, and I haven't received any calls or emails since immediately after my promotional deal ended. Sunstone's prices are cheaper than or comparable to other non-donation based studios, and they discount your membership if you are under 25, which I really appreciate since I am not a student.

Sounds good to me, so I selected that option...the process is very simple: select your price point, occasion and recipient (you can choose to add extras like chocolates if you want) and provide the zip code. That's it...you then go to checkout and done! 

Not only was the process efficient, but the flower arrangement was lovely. My friend sent me a photo of it on her desk. Two thumbs up for Blooms of Dunwoody...

Input: I really wish I could give 4 1/2 stars because Benihana's was so close to being a 5 star experience. 

We arrived during the lunch service, lucky us because it is way cheaper to eat here during lunch hours! The bad part about this is that I think we arrived at a time when staff was still arriving and prepping for dinner service. There was only one table sat, yet we waiting close to 10 minutes for a table.

Once we were sat there were no more complications. Our server was very friendly and attentive to us all throughout our meal. Our chef was very funny, not too loud and obnoxious, and talented (of course). His comedic timing was perfect and he really put on an entertaining show for my kids. They really enjoyed him. I think the funniest part, for me, was when he tried to launch some shrimp tail into his hat...but they went into his shirt instead. I guess they were a little hot. Poor guy, but it was funny non-the-less.

The food was very good, a little gristly fat in the chicken that I couldn't eat, but other than that good stuff. My son said it was the best restaurant he can ever remember eating at ever. Ha, cracks me up! I took him to a 5 star restaurant before with the 5 star food, and he likes Benihanas more. lol. Funny thing is, he usually doesn't even like rice, but he devoured it at Benihanas. 

I could tell management wanted to ensure happy customers. I believe the manager or owner was watching the dining area from afar. Love that. Would be even better if he casually greeted customers and asked them how everything was. We would have said "excellent" and given some big kudos for the staff who catered to us.

We'll be back, but definitely hitting the lunch service if we have the kids in tow. Lunch portions, by the way, are plenty big enough for most people.

Input: Had lunch here on a Friday.  Arrived at 12:30.  Parking was a breeze.  Receptionist was warm and eager to share her favorites off the menu.  The waitress was close behind and equally enthusiastic.  So far so good.  Then I noticed that the ambience was conducive to conversation.  My lunch companion and I talked for over two hours and unlike most Austin places, we were not bothered by loud music, noise or a staff that wanted us out the door in a hurry.  The pleasantness of this place is key but the food is worth mentioning.  There were several great choices on the lunch specials menu.  My companion had the Shrimp Tostada and I had the salad with calamari.  We couldn't resist the cauliflower flan and roasted butternut squash.  Both side dishes were excellent.  Overall, the food was a cut above the usual Austin lunch fare--- if you want highly structured, well presented, complex flavored food.  In other words, if you are a hamburger, taco or pizza lunch person,--this is not the experience you are looking for.  I would say this is a Foodie's place.  Having said that, I would return 60% because the atmosphere and service are perfect for lunch.  If you are solely interested in food quality, then you can find fancier and more expensive but as a whole, this place is a good Austin option with personality.

Input: That idylllic life as I knew it is gone....with life so sweet and easygoing, and I could reach work by simply biking 2.2 miles down one street to the Children's Hospital. Walking or taking a bus to destinations was accomplished with the utmost of ease.

Now, being back in the Bay Area, that sort of simple existence has faded and reliance upon a big ozone-harming, fuelly-dependent car has come back to the forefront (you like that one, didja now!?). 

5th Quadrant: a fun spot along the Van-Will (Vancouver/Williams) corridor that is in fact on the Portland biking route of the city! Large place for microbrews and pub grub both outside or in....happy hours that offer decent deals and above average food. Prices are greatly affordable, and the vibe is very cool. 

The offbeat nerd in me has done everything from coming with girlfriends to catch up on our lives during busy, LOUD happy hours, to playing chess (uh, yes.. chess) after dinner.....even take part in their goofy game nights... I recall one being a trivia night. It's great, because in Portland, it's all cool, and being yourself has never been easier, with societal pressures just off off off!!!!

The beers are rather yummy (read: C-Note), and the crowd tends to be younger 20/30's. Portions of food are generous, and the grill seems to get it right, most of the time. I miss it, terribly. This place was one of the foundational premier members that came to roost along the now popular corridor, before members like Lincoln and EaT (the oyster place) came. 

Pix Patisserie, the fine chocolatier, is just next door for super $$ splurging on sweets. now *that's* SUH WEEET.
NoPo (North Portland), live on forever! 

PS 5Q is part of the big Lompoc machine and opened up around 2007.

It was so nice having somebody explaining the place and telling us about the specials. He probably were busy, or during his dinner brake, but we did missed having someone up front. It is weird get in a place and wait in the line just because people in front of you are doing the same. So it was great when he materialized himself there. The service was great. A blond girl with an unsymmetrical hair (saved in one side) help us. She was so adorable and so helpful. She clearly knew everything about the menu, suggested some stuff and was very funny. I loved her. 
The food was fine. Not the best hamburger I ever had, but fair (I had the main one with fries). It wasn't memorable. Like, something like Tacofino's crispy chicken burrito (just an explanation what I consider memorable) that days later, after eating it, you can still feel the taste of the dish just by thinking about it. They probably have better things to try.

The 4 starts are more for the service and the place itself. Beautiful decoration, clean, great services, price ok.

I would go back again to try the food and maybe change my review about it.

Input: TLDR; authentic-tasting Asian street food. I think the experience would be better if you went with a group so you can try more things. 

I was a little skeptical at first and didn't think it would taste that great. I assumed that because it was located in an area that wasn't predominantly Asian, it wouldn't taste authentic. Fortunately, I was proven wrong. 

Located on the BeltLine, which already sees a huge amount of people, the restaurant was poppin when I arrived for dinner. The bar is open seating and I managed to snag a seat. Hooks are provided underneath to hang your bags. 

The menu is pretty extensive, with multiple dishes from different Asian cultures. I wish I wasn't by myself...I could only get one item to try. Family-style seems like the best way to go, to get the best experience. There are so many small dishes to share. Since I could only order one thing without feeling too full, I went with the Mi goreng. My only experience with this dish is the packaged Indomie brand and I wanted to see if an authentic dish would taste the same.

My first thought after taking a bite was that this was nothing like Indomie's. The sauce is definitely different, tasting more closely to a pad see ew. Reminded me of Thai noodle dishes with the lime and the peanuts(?) sprinkled on top. But even though it wasn't what I expected, I enjoyed it. Ask for the chili oil to mix in for an extra kick! 

I'd love to come back with more people and try their other dishes. You really don't see a lot of Asian street food anywhere in the States and Hawkers can help when you're craving some.

Input: Last stop before leaving Austin. This was one of my "must go to places" on my list. I read good things about it, and they were listed as vegan friendly. We arrived and were immediately greeted by the hostess, I really wanted to sit out on the patio but we were on a time limit and it looked like there was already a wait. The hostess said we'd get faster service inside, after my boyfriend asked about the wait time. We were showed the way to our table and immediately greeted by our waiter Adam. I want to say that Adam was wonderful! Next time you're in there ask to be seated in his area. He was friendly, helpful and had vegan knowledge. He suggested some things on the menu. It's been a relief to me to be in Austin and have lots of vegan options. We started off with a bowl of the vegan chili.. it was very good. Spicy, fresh and tasty. I ordered the Veggie plate with green chili rice and my boyfriend had the Hippie vegan sandwich. It was all very good. I wished I would have had more time to enjoy the outdoor patio. Overall, it was a great experience at Shady Grove and I'm looking forward to exploring more of Austin the next we come down.

I was coming after work so was prepared with a swimsuit but they have little disposable underwear you can put on but you will be topless unless you want to sweat in your nice bra which I don't recommended. They then wrap you from head to toe and sit you in this small sauna machine where you head sticks out and there are little holes for your hands in case you want to use your hands.  

I put on some music and relaxed. They come to check on you about every 15 minutes. You sweat a TON. I was hungry when I went and by the end I actually started to feel queasy. They provide you with water throughout and apple sauce in the end if you need some calories, which was a life saver me

I'm not sure I really notice a difference in the way my body looks or clothes fit. But I did feel relaxed and overall it was a great experience and would definitely do it again!!

The place has a nice clean and open look to it, probably seats about 25-30, when I was there it was about half full, with two servers and two sushi chefs all of whom did a great job.  The Sushi was excellent, I am a big salmon fan and the Salmon Rich Roll was right up my alley combining salmon, avocado, and rice, topped with more salmon and avocado.  The spicy tuna roll was also good, I find a lot of places tend to mail this roll in, using tons of mayo and tempura, but Genki Ya didn't fall  into that trap letting the tuna shine on its own.  In fact perhaps to much so, my one criticism was that it wasn't up to my level of spiciness, but still very tasty and also more to my S.O.'s tastes, which in the end is more important. Input: My 2nd time at Liuyishou, although different location, but I still loved it! This location is in the bustling plaza at Garden City/Alexandra. Therefore, parking can be quite challenging due to the existence of many restaurants within this plaza. If you go right at the start of meal time, you'd have no problem finding parking (fingers crossed).

The 3 of us chose the tom yum seafood soup for soup base. The soup base, tangy and spicy, came with quite a bit of seafood in the soup. We ordered the ring of meat, the veggie/mushroom basket, duck blood... The ring of meat, consisting of lamb and beef slices, encompasses the pot made my dinner especially beautiful. I also wanted to highlight the quality of meat we got at Liuyishou. I NEVER eat lamb slices due to its gamy flavor; however, I absolutely loved the lamb served by the restaurant! I didn't taste any gamy flavor at all!

One of the perks of Chinese style hot pots (mainland style, as this isn't the case for Taiwanese hot pots) is the sauce station. While there was a charge per person (must be the norm), you do have "unlimited" access to many different sauces, condiments, in addition to side dishes (pickled vegetables) and fruits.

While everything we ordered tasted extremely delicious, I must say the prices are on the higher end. Some reviews I read indicated that the prices were pretty cheap!? Sorry, but I cannot agree with this. For example, the veg/mushroom platter was $13, and all we got were some veggies and a couple of sliced pieces for each mushroom variety. Another aspect I didn't really like was the service. The servers were pretty rude, i.e. no customer service. I get that perhaps this is the norm in China; however, this is Canada and you are asking for tips! Therefore, give some service or, at the very least, smile at your customers!

Input: This place was packed for a Tuesday morning. My friend and I arrived here around 11:30 and there already seemed to be a 30-40 person line out the door. We went inside, put our name down, and the hostess said it would be about 45 minutes--no problem, as we had plenty to do since it's downtown with some shops all around. 

From what I could tell initially, this place is very very popular, with cute decor all around and a coffee bar close to the front entrance....we went on our way to meander around a bit and came back exactly 45 min later--and about a minute later we were seated! Perfect timing.

WHAT WE GOT:

1) I got the Mocha with white lavender pistachio rose with soy milk---actually really good! I really tasted the rose in the mocha, and it wasn't overpowering.
2) Poisson Lem Marrakech--poached egg, cured salmon,wheat berries, pistachio salad with sesame yogurt : my friend and I really enjoyed this, especially the cured salmon! For $17 it was a bit pricey but I especially enjoyed the crunch from the pistachio and addition of the wheatberries.
3) Avocado Toast: on grilled focaccia, with a tomato salsa and egg on side..this was a different version than what I was imagining but none the less good, I just which the portion was a bit bigger for $6.
4) Liege style waffle: with the white choc pistachio rosewater---we shared 1 which I think was enough since we shared everything else. The liege was piping hot, a bit chewy, a bit fluffy, but a very nice sweet snack. I do prefer the Blue Bottle liege waffles in SF though!


Overall food was pretty good, it was super busy so service wasn't great (our waiter forgot about our waffle and didn't really check in on us). But they were pretty spot on with timing and good about taking our orders.

Input: 3.5 stars for Chang Thai. 

The service was quite good. Our waitress was both attentive and friendly. 

We ordered the Tom Kha in a pot, the catfish curry dish and Pad Kee Mao. The Tom Kha arrived unlit with a huge pile of goo underneath... once she lit it I thought I was instantly transported back outside to the 100+ degree heat!  Our soup started boiling and we were both choking down the flame exhaust. She came over and doused out the fire... too much! 

The Tom Kha was flavorful and (besides boiling) full of veggies and chicken. At $10 the Tom Kha could easily be a meal for two people. We didn't realize this but will have tons left over! 

My Pad Kee Mao was... good. It was good. I took most of it home due to being so full from the soup. It had a different taste too it, a bit of a sour spice versus the normal sweet peppery spice we see often here in Austin. It wasn't bad, it was just different. I prefer the more traditional black peppery spice serve at Tittyayas. It did come loaded with veggies which made me happy! I never can get enough veggies in my Pad Kee Mao. The catfish dish came highly recommended - I don't eat catfish so I didn't try it but The Fish Eater gave it a nice star ranking. 

Our waitress honored the 15% off checkin code offered on Yelp which was very nice, it actually expired June 30th. 

All in all I probably will be hitting up some of my favorite Pad Kee Mao places because we walked out with a $35+ bill for two people. That was a little bit more then I was willing to spend for lunch, especially when I know I can pay less for more quality at my regular stops.

Input: As a self proclaimed ice cream connoisseur I was very excited to try out Tipping Cow after reading rave reviews online calling it a hidden gem within Somerville. My roommates and I decided to pay a visit Sunday night to give it a try. The staff was very welcoming and friendly and mentioned that the ice cream is made fresh every week and new flavors were installed once old batches ran out. There was a limited menu with 11 flavors to choose from and sizes ranging from mini to large with a very fair price to portion ratio (ordered a small for $3.25 two large scoops). We ordered the Espresso Chip, Ginger Blueberry, and Cookie dough. After finishing our ice cream 1 out of 3 of us were extremely impressed with the flavors. The Ginger and Blueberry was very overpowering and tasted as though you were eating the ginger on the side of the sushi plate. The Espresso Chip was very strong but since I am a coffee fanatic it ended up being a huge plus. Be forewarned if you do not like strong coffee you will not like this flavor. The one flavor that they did nail was the Cookie Dough, an absolute classic that we ordered with a melted brownie. Overall we were fairly impressed with our experience and would definitely be repeat customers when some unique flavors that make our taste buds tingle come onto the menu.

Input: Many of the negative reviews are somewhat accurate - the owner (Charlie Federico) has odd hours (closes at 5PM sharp), never answers the phone, it's a dingy shop, and owns the shop only as a hobby.  That being said, they're unfair.

This store has been in operation since the 1930's.  The owner was a former engineer for GE - so he knows his stuff.  He's says he's also been offered millions to sell the shop, but refuses.

Plus, he will charge you NOTHING.  He raised my seat, lowered my handlebars, fixed my girlfriend's seat, and raised her handlebars - for $10!  A woman that arrived at the shop before me, he charged NOTHING to fix her chain (she gave him $8 anyhow). Check out what a tune-up will cost you at any other bike shop - $50 a pop!

The owner was also smart enough to notice another little knock in the chain that needed fixing  - and he noted that you CAN safely raise handlebars even higher than the "minimum insertion mark", without damaging the bike.

He doesn't answer the shop phone (telemarketers he claims), so call his house where he'll happily answer the phone (617-471-5368).  He even opened the shop on Saturday for us.

The owner is 82 and religious, but he didn't say anything offensive to us whatsoever.  He'll remind you of your grandfather - he said to be careful out there and always wear a helmet!  He also GIVES AWAY a lot of the bikes in his shop to needy kids in the neighborhood.

Honestly, if you want your bike fixed on the cheap, and you want to support a local guy, I'd recommend him.


More here:
http://southbostontoday.com/federicos/

"If you grew up in Southie the name conjures up memories of summertime and fun, bicycles, scooters, bicycles, baby carriages, bicycles, wagons, but mostly bicycles.  Beginning in 1938 at Emerson and Fourth Street, Federico's has always been the last word in pedal power or wheeled mobility in general.

Charles Federico was born in South Boston of parents from Patti, Sicily.  His wife Mary is from Finnian Terrace, Ireland.  Family lore says the marriage was a perfect deal.  Mary taught Charles to speak correctly and he taught her to put her shoes on the right way.  They raised a family of eight.  Namesake, Charles took over the family business and has been a part of our community fabric for over fifty years.

Bundle boys, who wheeled groceries home, made their carts usually with baby carriage wheels from Federico's.  Seniors needing adjustment on their walkers still count on Charlie.  Above all, the hordes of bike riders still flock to the only licensed bicycle repair shop in South Boston.  It is more of a labor of love and a chance to give back to the community than a necessity.

A senior jet engine designer for General Electric, Charlie designed the fighter / trainer jet in use by Beijing, redesigned the Singapore Air Force and is a patent holder for a G.E. jet engine.

Charlie and his wife Carolyn raised four children and he keeps on ticking like he always has.  "Our job on Earth is to help," a deeply spiritual Charlie states. He recalls at 14 dreaming of his house burning.  Sure enough the next night at 2:30 a.m. his house burned.  Charlie believes miraculous intervention by Our Lady Mother Mary guided his mother through the flames to his room where they escaped from a porch helped by a couple of sailors walking by.

When asked of his Southie memories he first wanted to let me know he considers the New York Times reporter who tried to call Southie "SOBO", to be an intellectual moron.

"When I grew up every corner had a football team.  Military drill was held at the high school, and spiritual guidance was our directing influence.  My parents taught me pride in who I was and where I was from.  Southie pride stems from the idea of teamwork which we learned at an early age.  That teamwork of helping and being helped is the way I've tried to live my life."  South Boston Today would like to recognize Federico's for the institution it has become and to thank Charlie for helping to make our community what it has become."

Input: I've been a member of the Pluckers club for a while and I usually make a point of being sure to reap the benefits that come with membership. One of those is a free meal on your birthday (up to $15). 

Usually I reserve this meal to try something on the menu that I haven't tried before. The reasoning behind this: I didn't pay for it so I won't be disappointed if I don't care for it. The catch 22 thought that cancels out that reasoning: I'll consider it a waste of a free meal if I don't care for it and be annoyed that I didn't go with something I knew was good. Sometimes you just can't win.

I ordered the fried jalapeño appetizer. The actual popper is pretty run of the mill (though my actual jalapeño was matured, I don't know if they always come like that or if you might come across green ones) and comes with a strawberry chutney dipping sauce. The actual jalapeño isn't spicy at all. If the pepper were spicy, it would make for a much more satisfying appetizer and the chutney would be that much more effective, but it's still pretty good. I didn't stray into the unknown per se in terms of my meal (an order of 10 wings) but I did try two of the wing sauces that I've not tried before. The hallelujah sauce is very good. At first it tastes a little sweet but there's a hint of a spice in the after taste that grows a little. The other sauce I tried was the spicy lemon pepper sauce. It had a good flavor, kind of a mix between a barbecue sauce and your standard lemon pepper flavoring. Both sauces are rated 2 X on the spice level, but I'd probably drop one of those Xs from both. If you like spice, you can appreciate the tiny kick and taste the marriage of flavors going on in these sauces. If you're really sensitive to spice, I'd say you can consider it dipping your toe in. You're not going to burn off your taste buds and you'll be able to finish your meal without sweating bullets. I ordered the buffalo fries, which is just their normal waffle fry with some seasoning sprinkled on. It's okay, but overall not worth the upcharge. 

I tend to reap my rewards during the afternoon when the restaurant is quiet, but I've been here during some pretty raucous evenings. In both settings, the staff pay attention to what counts. They don't hover, they refill drinks, and they come by to make sure all is well. They're pleasant and want to make sure that you leave satisfied. Another year, another birthday lunch, another job well done by Pluckers.

My dish had everything from salmon, to mussels, clams, calamari, and shrimp. I would have preferred a little more heat since it was a fra diavolo but it was still really good. As for the shrimp with red sauce, the dish was just as good. 

So after we were full, we got tiramisu on the house as well. I'm not really a desert guy but the tiramisu was pretty decent. 

All in all, dinner cost $93 for a bottle of chardonnay, calamari, two entrees, and two deserts. Not bad at all. I'd go back for sure...hopefully with freebies again.

Input: We walked in to Ben Darwish tickling the ivories, oh, now I understand why they named it that. I thought it had to do with elephant tusks.

Anyway,  the ambience is very nice, the colors are subdued, the sparkling chandelier lamps are fun. The bar is set up on the far side and the tables all are in the middle with the stage up front. They even have some comfy looking booths in the back.  Nice set up.

Servers were wonderful. One of them even squeezed between some tables to avoid my husband from accidentally taking a picture of her instead of the stage.  

They've got a nice wine list and the menu has some great choices. Oh and they have aviation gin.  I kicked back with my dry martini and took it all in. The sun was streaming from their windows and all was well so far.  We ordered an appetizer to begin and had broiled shrimp in a mornay sauce over half of an avocado.  Doug and I dug in to it and the shrimp were fresh and the avocado was ripe enough. The sauce was a little bland but that did not keep us from eating all of it.  There were quite a number of items that had fish, seafood, and even vegetarian on their menu for entrees. This was very encouraging since those items are what we order. I ended up getting the eggplant parmesan.  The eggplant was crispy and had good flavor. There was plenty of pasta and the tomato sauce was more of a fresh tomato vs. a cooked for days sauce. I finished my eggplant and left most of my pasta as I was full.

Very excited to have a new jazz space here in Portland. It's been too long. They've got a ton of live music lined up with free happy hour shows, and paid shows later on in the evening. I'm not sure what all the fuss is about cover charges. They just add it to your dinner bill just like the "other" jazz place down the road. It's normal business and musicians do like to get paid for a living.

Overall, two thumbs up.

Input: I first checked this place out in the middle of July when Oregon was in the middle of a heatwave. The line was out the door and it seemed pretty busy, but people were popping out of the place constantly, so I figured it was worth the wait and service seemed to be working quickly.

I've tried it again a couple of times since and granted the line always seems to reach the door, but service is pretty fast and the cashiers are always super patient and nice. For a Friday night (at around 7 pm) in October, the place was still filled with people, but not super packed like how it was over the summer. 

Their prices range from $4-5+ and most add-on's like the boba's (regular or clear/crystal) are $0.50. Split cups are the best way to go if you're still trying to familiarize yourself with the menu and figuring out what you like/don't like from their options. Buying a mason jar from them only costs $2.50 extra (which is surprisingly cheap...most people charge up to $5 more), and they also have a travel bottle available--it's a glass bottle with several designs and sleeves available.

My go-to and favorite drink so far is their Strawberry Limeade with regular boba. It's semi-sweet, but has a tangy/sour taste due to the limeade and is super refreshing. Both fruit flavors emphasize the sweetness of the boba.

I'd also recently tried their Peach Blossom and Lychee Crush in a split cup...both drinks are very similar to each other. They both had chopped up fruit in the drink and most of it contained fruit juice. Both gives you a summer feel and is very refreshing. The Lychee Crush has lime in it, which added to the refresh-ness. I got them with clear/crystal boba, which is similar to the regular but just a little bit less chewy and more dense. They ran out of regular boba when I went--around 8:30 pm on a Saturday. 

Parking is not a problem. It's in a small plaza next to Dollar Tree and Mio Sushi, so there's plenty of parking in the lot.

The only reason I've deducted a star is because the place is pretty small and is not ideal for sitting around to hang out with friends. There are a few two-seater tables on the side and one table that can fit maybe four people, but other than that, it's a place that's best for going in and out. It just gets hard to find a place to stand/wait for your order when it gets pretty crammed in there.

Due to the popularity of the place, I'm surprised they haven't come out with a loyalty program. It would be awesome if they had punch cards--some buy 10 drinks, get 1 free like Dutch Bro's or other boba/coffee places. 

I have yet to try their Mangonada drink, which has chunks of mango, but my boyfriend has ordered the drink with watermelon chunks and Tajin and he absolutely loved it! If you're a fan of these types of Mexican snacks, you'll surely love and enjoy Zero Degrees. If not, there are plenty of fruit juice options as well as a few teas (milk tea, Thai tea, matcha green tea). It's definitely a unique place...kind of like boba drinks with a Mexican dessert twist. 

Give it a try! It's worth it!

Input: I really wanted to give this place five stars but I just can't, at least not yet.

Having a young child of 11 months, we wanted to introduce her to swimming and after a few Google searches, found three nearby locations to this Michigan-based franchise, including their newest out in Norwood that opened recently.

I filled out an interest form and no more than 90 seconds later, my phone rang and the young one was booked for her first, mini class. A few days went by and off we were on a brisk Saturday morning.

The establishment itself is absolutely awesome. Bright colors, a nice fish tank and a huge viewing area which overlooks the pool, with chairs, for the family members who aren't actively participating in the swimming. There's some Tropical-themed changing rooms, a changing table and even a couple of centrifuges to help dry up towels and swim gear. They've thought of everything and it's all kid-themed and immaculate.

The staff is relatively friendly, especially the ones in the pool doing the classes and overall we've had a good experience. Well... except for the first time we went. The water heater broke so the pool was much colder than it should have been. No heads up, apologies or refunds. We had to check-in before our second class to make sure that things were back to normal and they were but it would have been nice to know ahead of time because we would have never driven out there knowing that my daughter would spend 30 chilly minutes in the water shivering and miserable.

So why only 4 stars? Mostly because of their front desk scheduling process and pricing models. Both times we've been they've been incredibly aggressive in trying to sell us on their $100/month tier good for 1 lesson/a week even though I've repeatedly said that because of scheduling, that we'd rather do the $25 walk-ins. They've told us many times that they can't fit us in many classes because they prioritize the people with the monthly plan which is absurd because why offer walk-ins if you're not going to honor anything?

Their schedules are also very limited on weekends with only 2-3 available 30 minute blocks per day which can make it tough for some people to make it. I was kind of hoping they'd have more per day but maybe that'll change over time? Who knows.

We plan on continuing to come for the time being and hope that they'll take a more passive approach to this whole $100 plan and let us do the $25 walk-ins. Rumor is they might get rid of it all-together at which point we'll probably go somewhere else since I don't want to commit to a lesson a week. They're aggressive to the point where we've had to walk out and get things scheduled over the phone which was much easier and quicker. Go figure.

But that aside, Goldfish is a great franchise and the staff clearly cares deeply about the experience they provide and the facilities are top notch. I'm a fan.

Input: You know those moments when you sit back in your seat and try to comprehend the amount of food you just ate? Yep, thats how I felt after my meal at Kyo.

This kind of meal is perfect for a large group, the more people, the more food options, and it gives you the opportunity to chat while you cook the meat and munch on sushi rolls. 

A huge bonus- if you order sake- they will ask you if you want it cold or hot. Always a nice option, but we know hot is the only way. 

The service was okay, it was a busy night but we did wait a while for drinks and found that we received some things we did not order. Make sure to check your order form when it comes back to you. Anything you don't eat, they charge on top of the base price. 

Lastly, beware that large groups have auto gratuity on the bills. Most of the group did not know and tipped on top of it.  Those servers made a lot from us that night. 

Live and learn I guess. I'll be going back regardless.

Input: A chain for bahn mis? I can't say that I'd heard of Lee's prior to walking in but they have stores in California, Colorado and Texas to name a few states. Bahn mis have always been in one off stores with just Vietnamese families usually running the business. I've been to An Xuyen, Bihn Mihn a few other local places and love the food out of all of them. So how does a company with 55 stores compare? Surprisingly pretty good.

House made mayo? Check. House made pickled carrots and daikon? Check. A 12" French bread roll? Check. I was quite surprised, pleasantly at that. You even have the option of getting regular sandwiches like turkey or roast beef (they refer to those as European sandwiches) There's even a mini grocery store of sorts where you can purchase Vietnamese sausages, coffee, the house made mayo, desserts, bread and other ethnic items.

As for my bbq pork sandwich? It was really good. All of the above mentioned items, plus cilantro, jalapenos, salt, pepper and a splash of soy sauce. The last being different from other bahn mis I have had in PDX. The roll was a bit sturdier than some of the one off places and nice and crispy. There was plenty of pork and lots of crunchy veggies. The price was very much in line for this type of food and and the fried banana I got to accompany was really tasty as well. The two together was barely $5.

I keep finding new food up and down 82nd. If you folks living in inner Portland or over on the west side haven't found your way out to here, you should. You're missing out on some great Asian cuisine.

Enjoy.

Input: My wife and I have been here several times and I have to say that I've never gone to a place that serves with as many variations and usually does them well and/or over the average. My wife and I stumbled onto this place awhile back looking for Asian type cuisine (for her) on a Sunday. This was one of few places open that day. 
Parking can be tricky at times as the parking lot is pretty small, you will most likely have to park on the highway or possibly on side street if there is a space.
The staff is very friendly and usually attentive. Although, they can be a bit slow once after you've gotten your food which isn't a big deal for me as long as they check up after the serve. They always looked out if I wanted a little something extra without charging the full price which is very nice.
So, now the food. My wife loves their Salt & Pepper Prawns and the Calamari dishes. She appreciates how Decoy does it fresh without overcooking the food, especially, the Calamari.
I've had their fish and chips, burgers, fish burger, and basic breakfast with sausage and a side biscuit and gravy. All of it was solid except for the breakfast. The breakfast was just...ok. Because the Decoy doesn't necessarily offer a breakfast that includes an option with biscuit and gravy , that meal got a bit spendy. Ran around $15-16. The biscuit and gravy didn't have much meat nor flavor, the sausage looked and tasted like something out of a Brown N' Serve package (in my opinion, of course). So, I'm not sold on the breakfast served there (at least, that one). However, that won't deter us from going there as they do very well in other food variations and looking forward to trying them as time goes on. Yes, I'm a fan!

Input: We drove past some beautiful beaches in the Dorchester area (and an industrial street) before arriving at the JFK Presidential Library and continued to be astonished by our setting.  The building has a pristine and modern look with a gorgeous glass pavilion.  It's located on a peninsula by Dorchester Bay with a promenade (lots of joggers) and great views of South Boston.  Admissions is $14 for adults and $12 for students/seniors. There is free parking with admissions.  I like how the admissions sticker is the seal of the President of the United States.

We started off with a 15-20 minute documentary in the auditorium, which exits into the exhibits.  They have done an incredible job in designing their exhibits and included video footages so we can relive historical moments during JFK's presidency.  My favorite was the Campaign Trail section.  There's also a replica of his desk in the Oval Office with his personal items on display and exhibits dedicated to his brother RFK and his wife Jacqueline.

Having been to both this Presidential Library and the Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza at Dallas, I can say that they are different.  Although both do an incredible job at exploring his campaign and presidency, the Presidential Library is more of a collection (in a beautiful setting) whereas the Sixth Floor Museum has panels and video clips with an audio guide to keep us engaged in additional topics such as JFK's assassination and its aftermath (after all, it's in Dealey Plaza where JFK was shot during his campaign for re-election).

The bacon and pork gravy fries were also solid, and I had never seen them anywhere else. Tilt did a good job with the fries, and the gravy really worked with the fries. 

The atmosphere was casual and inviting. It reminded me of my favorite brewery/college bar with delicious beer and a good casual atmosphere for friends to hang out and catch up. Since the drinks and ambiance were awesome, I definitely plan to come back next time I am in Portland.

Input: Pros: Good ball quality, lots of stalls, clean, good prices

Cons: No grass hitting area, empty lobby/pro shop, max distance 220 yards

I finally got my clubs shipped from my parents house in Omaha to my place in Oregon. Mind you, that's after four years of living in California and a year in Oregon, so I guess better late than never? I have a work golf event coming up, so I wanted to get my clubs. I also wanted to get some practice in before the event. Looking up places, I came up with Sunset Golf Center. About 10 minutes from where I live, and very close to Nike HQ, this place is a casual place for the casual golfer to hit a casual bucket of balls.

I was impressed by the quality of range balls I found. Most of them looked like fairly new Nike balls, lacking scuffs or chips. There are about 20 stalls, each with a clean mat to hit off of. I'm not a huge fan of hitting off mats, but they are clean and easier to hit off of compared to other mats at driving ranges I've been to before. The max distance is 220 yards, so hitting a driver full strength might not be the best idea. Probably a better place to practice irons, hybrids and wedges. They also have a putting green and a sand trap to practice those shots as well. $9.00 gets you 120 balls to hit, not a bad deal at all.

I always prefer hitting off grass than mats, and that this place lacks grass to hit off of is disappointing. Also, the lobby/pro shop area is very empty. Not much of a selection of golf items to purchase. They have some arcade games, a snack bar, and a big screen TV to watch. Seems kind of cavernous. The place also has a mini golf course and lessons. Since I haven't utilized either, I can't give a fair review of them.

Overall, hitting a bucket of balls is a great way to relief stress, spend some time outdoors, and even improve your golf game. Sunset Golf Center is nice to have close by and I'm sure I'll be back again, especially since now I have my clubs.

Input: As a non hillbilly, let me just say that this place is worth its weight in gold.  Look, zoos in general are not high on my list.  They keep animals that should be in the wild in containment, and even when they're based on rescue/rehab, a good part of time is spent interfering with what nature would be sorting out on its own...survival of the fittest and all that.

This place has a TON of gators, and because they allow you to feed them, they are so bloated and overfed that they never even take a shot at the plethora of birds in the water with them.  Hell I saw a duck actually pull a piece of hot dog OUT of a gators mouth and the gator never freakin moved.

Not a big fan of the gator wrestling show.  I know it's done to raise money for the rehab of gators and whatnot but....I dunno...to me it kinda seems like you're not giving proper respect to these animals to first wrangle them, then tape their jaws shut and let people pose sitting on them.  Just...not a fan, rubs me the wrong way.

With all of that having been said, the attractions are fun, the opportunity to feed the "wild" gators (An upcharge) was a good time.  I like that the place is here and tries to behave more like a refuge than a zoo...and the gift shop...holy shit the gift shop.  The gift shop is a miraculous blend of hillbilly, gun nut, and psychopath.  I actually drank wine from a pouch...like a capris sun, but worse.  I was saddened to see that between my visits on 2014 and 2016, they apparently sold out of the onesie that read "I'll nap when the huntin' is done", but was THRILLED to see that I should thank my military for having a teacher that taught me English.

Seriously, this place is a do not miss, as long as you don't take yourself too seriously and have an hour to kill in the gift shop.

Input: How does Pollo Norte take chicken, the wallflower of the meat world, and turn it into the bell of the ball? Your guess is as good as mine. Love? Gypsy Magic? Seasoning passed down from generation to generation? All of the above?! Sure! 

Rotisserie chicken is dope, so it's safe to assume a place that perfects that art would be likewise dope. Pollo Norte does one thing, and it does it right. You come here for the chicken, you stay for the chicken. Or you get it to go and gorge yourself in the privacy of your home, hopefully with your hands like an animal because that's what I always want to do but there is people around. If this place were closer to my house, my trash can would be filled with chicken carcasses. 

They offer a few basic sides. Rice, beans, slaw, potatoes and of course corn tortillas. I always get extra corn tortillas because they're on the small side and God forbid I run out while there is chicken to be had. Sides are good, not great. In full disclosure having grown up in a Mexican household, I can get on my high horse when it comes to beans and Mexican rice. For me it could stand a little more TLC spice wise, but that being said it is good and the price is right. I will say the corn tortillas are on point. 

I've heard they run out of chickens but this hasn't been my experience. Last time I was there they mentioned having increased production and that you can call ahead. So be smart, call ahead if it's your dinner plans and get that chicken on lock down.

Buffalo cauliflower wings - the best I've had and I've had many. They were crunchy, spicy and ever so delish!

I ordered the Gyro for my main entree and have had real gyro before since I eat meat. I prefer the vegan version for sure. The POS system was acting up and added gratuity to our bills automatically as well as didn't adjust off the Tuesday pint specials but management was great and comp'd a few drinks for us since it took them a while to fix the checks. 

This place was packed when we left so get there early. Or wait. The wait is worth it!

Input: Tried this place for the first time today, and I gotta say, I'm a fan.

 The place is right off of 62, and goes into one of those "Oh shit!" parking lots where it's suddenly upon you, and you suddenly have to turn into it. After parking across three spots and then across a handicapped spot to the stares of the people sitting in the hair cutting place, I finally found an actual spot and parked.

I had done some research of this place online before going, on, of course, Yelp, and I knew what I wanted to get when I got in there: this culinary concoction called "The Nest". When I walked in and ordered it, the boss (owner?) actually asked me if I was sure that was what I wanted. At first I was a little offended by that, but given the makeup of this sandwich, all is forgiven.

Quick service, friendly staff... that's all there. Now the sandwich.... The nest is a BRILLIANT sandwich, though surely not for everyone. Chicken Fingers, Mozzarella Sticks, French Fries, Grated Cheese and Tomato Sauce all in a roll. AWESOME. Since it's essentially a junk food collection of appetizers, I can see how this sandwich is probably more appealing to the high schoolers who are located right across the street, hence the warning I received.

I suppose a true test of this place would be to try one of the more mundane sandwiches and see how they stack up, but  they have passed my first test, and got me liking the place, looking forward to going back again, and trying more of their wares.

Recommend!

Input: Talk about a complete 180. I had a brunch buffet here a while back, and it was pretty close to the worst food that I had ever laid taste buds on in the wondrous food city known as Austin, Texas. Upon seeing that it was going to reopen as a reevaluated and revamped sort of gastro-restaurant sort of eatery, I was pumped.

I say gastro-restaurant because the alcohol menu sort of sucks, but they are not really just a "bar and grill"; furthermore, it also boasts some really interesting and tasty noshes. I very much appreciated the live music.

The outdoor patio is quite nice, and the happy hour is off the charts. With half-price appetizers galore, you could literally have a feast and get quite inebriated for under $15 a person. And by full and drunk I mean full and drunk. To put things in perspective: $4 flatbread, $4 onion rings, $4 guacamole... the list goes on.

I would recommend two appetizers specifically... namely because I got these, and I loved them. The roasted mushroom flatbread, with all its roasted mushroom goodness, boasts a nuttiness provided by the heavy dosing of truffle aioli, thyme, blue cheese, and some sort of shredded cheese. Does that not just scream UNCT. Not unctuous, but UNCT... like a grunt.

The charred corn guacamole was OK... nothing outstanding. But... the salt and pepper house chips are amazing. Super salty, super crisp, and a boat load to an order. This is a must.

More disappointing are the adornments that the entrees possess. The bison burger boasts a housemade aioli, which was a little lumpy; a spicy, but watery habanero ketchup; and a far-too pungent shiner mustard. The caramelized bourbon onions were sweet to the point of disgust. The pita bread that accompanied my chickpea chili was OK, a bit too dense. The mac and cheese was too runny, though the cheesy flavor was a nice touch. The chickpea chili disappointed heavily. It was too tomatoey in flavor, and the feta and grilled beet garnish literally added nothing, if not even detracting from the faux-stew.

Affordable is the grub here, and that truly counts for something. Other than that, I figure the quality on many items could be tweaked, but I am certain that I will return at some point for happy hour. I mean, $4 per order of whatever your heart desires? I shall not pass.

We ordered oyster pancake, xiao long bao, ma po tofu, a steak dish, a fish dish. There was a very long hair in our oyster pancake, but the server had no problem in bringing out a brand new one for us. Overall, the food was fabulous and delicious.

We expect the server to take the cake out of the box and put the candles on and bring it over. At least that's what supposed to be customer service. Instead, they just brought the cake over that was still in a plastic bag, unwrapped, and smacked it right on the table like it was nothing. I guess they have never taken care of a birthday party before in that restaurant. 

I'm not sure if they do this to every customer's bill, but they charge a 15% service fee on our bill. Maybe it's because we look like those super young college kids who are too poor to tip, but that definitely would be a mistake if they assumed we were. The service fee is no big deal. Input: I've been here multiple times to enjoy a happy hour or late cocktail at their outdoor area, which is lovely. And always have had a nice drink, especially when it's happy hour, the prices are great.

So, we finally made it here to actually eat inside for a early dinner and cocktail last Sunday afternoon.  Luckily, we ran into some fellow yelpers outside and joined them for a bit and we munched on the beer cheese and pretzels, which I have to say was underwhelming.  After saying goodbye, we went inside to dine.

The interior is aesthetically pleasing, the noise is controlled by smart design, and the service from hostess, to server, and to the manager stopping by to check on us was on point.  Yay!

Food:  Well, I was a bit worried after our appetizer outside, but we proceeded anyway.  My husband was in the mood for steak and after showing him a yelp review of the Delmonico steak on the menu, that was his choice without hesitation. He ordered it medium with the au gratin potatoes. When it came out, it was beautifully seasoned and charred, and the temperature was a perfect medium as requested.  He and I both thought it was an excellent steak.  It was juicy, not too fatty, but enough to give it flavor, and tender as heck!  Really, it was SO SO good.  The au gratin potatoes were also perfectly crisped on the outside and not too greasy or cheesy.  He and I would so get this again.

I opted for the angus meatloaf sans the portabella mushrooms (which I don't care for). It came out with two generous slices that were meaty and tasty, a gravy that was good, but not fantastic, haricot verts (delicious and crisp), and I opted for the mac n' cheese, which was simply awesome.  

Definitely will be back for not only cocktails and happy hour outside, but dinner inside.

Input: Go On Tuesdays for their $8 Mussels. I have to say that I saved room for this meal... and I could've shared one plate with my lovely friend I was catching up with.. but we were both starving so we each ordered the special.

We also got a beet and pear salad which, at regular price, I thought came in a rather smaller portion. I wish the beets had cooled because the salad was a little warm (I don't know if they plan to serve it that way). The decor is so cute... with one long banquette and tables of 2s and 4s. It is a little crowded as everytime the server spoke to the table next to us, you'd pretty much get someone's rear a foot away from you.

Service was friendly and informative, patient and not overbearing. The mussels came with fresh bread and a combination of yam fries and regular fries - what a lovely surprise. The plate of mussels were beyond massive. The plate /bowl it came in looked like an upside down sunday hat. The cream sauce was heavy, but in a good way. The bread was perfect for dipping as it soaked up the sauces as I savoured it in my mouth.

I ate every single mussel, and every single fry and couldn't walk or eat until lunch the next day.... but good conversation and good food can lead to great things (even if it means being full for a very very very long time).

I heard the main chef specializes in pastry.. if I had more room - I would've grabbed dessert for sure. They have $25 3 course meals with a glass wine / beer on Sundays.. definitely want to check it out!

The savory was so good, with the toast in a garlic and herb batter, topped with goat cheese, bell peppers, chives, and balsamic. As I mentioned I asked to add egg and sausage. I was a bit bummed that these things ended up on the side rather than on top, but that was easy enough to fix on my own. But I probably wouldn't have ordered my egg sunny side up had i known.

We were happy with out breakfast, and it was nice to try someplace new. I'm sure at some point we'll come back, but it's not a place I'd rush to. 4 stars for the win.

Input: When I first moved to Boston, I lived in Brighton and thought that Sunset was amazing. They have 130 some-odd beers on tap, plus hundreds of bottles (including a 40 oz. bottle of Schlitz). It was perfect, until I actually went there. It felt like a Ground Round. Not Beer Mecca. And I was unhappy.

Fast forward to now and there's the Hobo. I haven't found a place in Cambridge that rivals their beer selection. This place doesn't have bang-up food, but it's not terrible. I'd put it just above Tavern in the Square but well below Garden at the Cellar or Green Street. Last time I was there with friends, we ordered two BBQ sandwiches, a roasted red pepper soup with grilled cheese, and fried calamari. The soup was the winner, though the grilled cheese was pretty much a grilled cheese you could get anywhere, including your own kitchen. I tend to shy away from pulled pork at non-cue joints because I usually end up disappointed. This one wasn't bad, but I remember not being a giant fan of the sauce (full disclosure: memory a bit fuzzy due to too many beers). The calamari was good drunk food, not too greasy, and had a couple of deep fried peppers tossed in that I wasn't 
really expecting.

Need to go back to sample more beers, but also to try out their pretty extensive cocktail list. They've got some of the favorites (Dogfishhead, Stone Brewery, Bear Republic), plus a bunch that I've never heard of, along with a bunch of seasonals that you won't find in most package stores.    

Pro-tip: if you're sitting in the back corner near the waiter's computer, take a look at what's on the screen. The first time I went, the buttons said "Joey has" "irregular holes" "bearshark keeps" "raping harry." The last time it said "more passionate" "bang-bang" "sweeter" "finger-bang." I think that was from Valentine's day. Anyways, good conversation starter.

This is a Sunset for grown-ups. More of a bar/pub feel than crappy restaurant with a gimmick.

Input: A great place for lunch and brunch. I've been here a few times now, and have had great food each and every time!

It's gonna be busy on weekends for lunch and brunch. Expect at least 30 mins, possibly an hour. But the location is great because its in a shopping center that allows you to shop around while you wait. You receive 3 hours of free parking in lot. Just be sure to keep your ticket when you enter the deck. 

The decor is simple and clean, with lots of light coming in. It's a chill vibe despite it being a full house. Service is top notch. Some of the best servers I've come across. 

Food wise: The Double Burger Stack. It's simple, yet legit. One of the best burgers in town for sure. No frills, just two patties with American cheese, pickles, lettuce and onions. Sides are a la carte. 

I've also had Avenue A, which is smoked salmon (nova), schmear, avocado, grapefruit, cucumber, onion, and dill. It was fresh and delicious. Their iced coffees are also solid too-- nice and smooth, not bitter, not too sweet. 

I would also highly recommend the Pastry Basket. The first time I went, I made the mistake of getting it as an appetizer. These pasties are HUGE! But they were all so freakin delicious! I think it contains a cheese Danish, cinnamon roll, and maybe 2 different muffins. Needless to say, the second time I went, I got these as a to-go order, so I could snack on them all weekend. 

There's also an extensive list of brunch staples and deli style sandwiches. I can't wait to go back and try them!

Input: I had been meaning to try Panza for a long time.  For one thing, it's on the site of my former favorite restaurant in the North End, Cibo.  It's right across the street from The Wine Bottega, a sensational store that hosts free wine tastings every Friday night from 5-8 PM and several excellent events each month.

Panza was always crowded by the time I got to the North End.  Fortunately, my friend and I were in the area earlier (around 5:30) and got a table immediately.

We started off with the Italian Chop Salad, designed for two but could definitely be shared by 3 people.  It came in a large bowl and we served ourselves with tongs.  Its ingredients reminded me of cold antipasti and the pepperoncinis were an excellent touch.

For my entree, I enjoyed the daily special of pappardelle with lamb ragu, a sumptuous feast of broad, filling noodles and tasty tendrils of meat.

Overall, an exceptional meal.  We were disappointed that they wouldn't let us open the bottle of wine my friend purchased across the street and it did take some time to receive our entrees, given that it was crowded.

Definitely make a reservation or get there before 6 PM if you want to snag a table on a weekend evening.  This is a must visit stop in the North End!

Input: Baci!!! Travels for Baci!! Pet hotels #19!!

Valet was $42 I believe. Thanks, Valet dude! 


Normally pet floors are lower but I love high floors and well platinum membership got us a room on 20th. It rained the whole time but we enjoyed staying in and hanging out in the balcony. People watched in the rain and cold! 

The bed was comfortable. Room was nice size: a little on the smaller side. Just a tiny bit but still nice. Roomy. Baci love the bed and the couch! :) 

The lobby has Starbucks, a bar and hangout area with plenty of umbrellas for that crazy rainy weekend. We walked around in the evening for a bit but coming back was the best part! Especially for Baci. He doesn't care for the rain. 

The only complain was lack of microwave for my pups food. The room service can come and get it and do it for you. But seems like too much hassle. Ended up ordering new rice for his meals. A lot of food deliveries were ordered too!

And that 2 pm check out! Great for us to explore the Robson street the next day, walk the Canada place and the harbor. All within 5 -10 minutes walk!! Baci loved it so, I did too! Woof woof!

Input: I always forget about Victory because it's kind of tucked away a few streets up from the hubbub of Highland Avenue in Inman Park.  But each time I go, I'm reminded why I like it so much.  First, you can't go wrong with their classic Jack and Coke slushees.  I appreciated the pro-tip from our waitress this past time, who pointed out that you're better off buying the smaller size because it's not any cheaper to get the larger one per ounce, plus the smaller ones don't melt as fast. A good tip!  The other alcoholic sodas on the drink menu are fun and different, and on busy weekends, they serve froze out of the shipping container bar in the parking lot.

I also really appreciate their food menu here.  The sandwiches are all small and slider sized but packed with interesting fillings, sauces, meats, cheeses, and accoutrements.  And at $4, they're that perfect little bite to nibble on when you want something to eat while drinking but don't want a whole meal.  Each slider sandwich comes with a small handful of potato chips.  If you want something else to round out your drinking nibbles, I highly recommend the very pickle-y and dill filled dip for your chips.  The portion size of dip is huge - you may need extra chips!

They have a large indoor bar area and high tops, a covered patio, a game room, and an outdoor patio area with picnic tables with umbrellas.  And, they ever have a small parking lot (maybe 10 spaces) with free parking, which is basically unheard of in this area.

All in all, as drink spots on the Beltline go, Victory is worth a visit!

Input: A cozy restaurant located on Cambridge street in Cambridge. A small bar area for seating and a bunch of tables that can be made for small and larger groups. On a Saturday night, it was busy but not full. 

The wait staff was polite and helpful. Provided explanation to the dishes, menu and good recommendations. 

Ginza G + T was a typical gin and tonic. Strong and classic
Toro flight - was the nightly special so pricy at $28. 4 different cuts of toro. The best was the fatty fish as the other prices were more 'tougher' and resembled beef. 
Uni and rock crab hand roll - also a nightly special. Lots of rock crab and sufficient amount of uni. Probably one of the best dish of the night 
Kanpachi- good flavor with the pineapple sauce. Fish was thinly sliced 
Hien bronzini - not a typical fish on sushi menu so worth a try. Felt the sesame oil drenched the fish and overwhelmed the dish. 
Kalua pork onigiri- great presentation and loved that you had to wrap it yourself. Lots of filling - a plus. The pork was flavorful
Spam musubi- ate this at the end so was getting full. The spam was way too small for the amount of rice.  The proportion was way off. Definitely had better elsewhere. 
Short rib grilled skewers - did not come with skewers and there was no bone attached to the meat. This was nice. The flavor was good with lots of ponzu but meat seems dry. Usually short rib is a bit tender being close to the bone. 
Waygu beef dumplings- soup dumpling with 5 pieces. Soup was good. The dumplings weren't bad, maybe a bit dry since it was boiled. This cut of meat is better to be eaten seared, grilled instead. 
Loco moco - beef was tender and maybe a little undercooked. The egg was perfect and the sizzling aspect is a great presentation. Rice wasn't sticky enough to keep the shape from becoming a hot delicious mess. 

The general comment About the rice is that it's not sticky enough to hold the add on. 

Overall a great experience at Momi nonmi. Really liked the unique dishes.

Input: We made a reservation and we were determined to feed me some prime rib. We had a huge snow dump on Sunday so it made it extra beautiful up there. The view was amazing. We valeted because it was so snowy and the roads were gross so why not spend some more for the convenience of letting someone else handle it? 

We came in and it was a gong show. There was a private event waiting for their room to be set up so there was well over 30 people crammed into the lobby bar area waiting for their room. They were snooty and obnoxious and had no desire to move even an inch to let people through. I ended up shoving a few people who had drinks in hand. Sorry not sorry.

We were seated with a fantastic view of the city. So beautiful! 

I got the prime rib combo. I was so looking forward to it. The mushroom soup wasn't as thick as I like it but it was ok. I wouldn't order it again. The prime rib was cooked perfectly but lacked any depth in flavor. The Yorkshire pudding was delicious as were all the veggies and mashed potatoes (less the tomato). The highlight of my meal was the sunburnt lemon pie. Yum!

My girlfriend enjoyed her beet and papaya salad. She wasn't a huge fan of her striploin as it was underseasoned. 

Our server was fantastic. It was already a lovely evening with an amazing view and her service was just the icing on the cake. 

I am giving it 4 stars for the experience as a whole. If it were just the food that night, it'd be a 3 stars. The service would be 5 stars. The view would also be an easy 5.

We ended up taking a stroll outside to see the view some more but quickly went to get our car because it was so cold.

The third time I was more hungry and went for the Jerk Salmon. That was a clear winner. A huge serving of rice'n'peas, slaw and the salmon soaked in a very hot and spicy jerk sauce. Add some of the house made hot sauce and you will be reaching for the water jug!!!
As for the cocktails, I haven't tired them yet as I am always driving but I opted for the virgin Jack Sparrow version. So good. The Ginger Beer taste like actual Ginger Beer! 

Overall, the service has always been very good and the staff welcoming. I like the little complimentary fry ball with coconut butter, which is a guilty pleasure for the celiac diseased!!! 

The Reef is a fun place with a nice atmosphere and I will go back there again.

Input: I don't go to a lot of breweries as I don't drink a lot of beer. But I do on occasion enjoy going with friends because there's nothing like the ambience that many of these breweries provide. Usually you get a large space with different types of craft beers. There's generally some great music and food nearby. It just makes for a fun afternoon.

We came to Orpheus to celebrate a friend's birthday. We had trouble with parking (there's barely any) and most weekends it gets busy here. I suggest you Uber there. That day we went, they had over a dozen different types of beers and multiple people working the bar so you were never standing in line for vary long. On the screens above the bar they describe the flavor profiles in depth. For those who are non alcohol drinkers or just don't like beer, there are Jarrito sodas in the fridge. 

Every 30 or 45 min or so, they do a tour of their brewery in the back and actually provide cool information about the process (I find the science fascinating). They are the first brewery in Atlanta to make sours and of course now they have branched out into all types. Orpheus beer is sold not only in Atlanta but in different countries as well. If you stick around Atlanta long enough, you'll see their beer is pretty well regarded.

On occasion they will have a taco truck outside. They have a souvenir/branding store in the building and they also have someone who sells artwork. I do really enjoy the branding they use for their cans. It's genius!

Input: There's nothing more fun than a carefully curated, thoughtfully organized kitchen store full of everything you need and even more you want. I can wander around in a place like this all day long, debating the aesthetic vs functional merits of three kinds of rubber spatula or hefting utensil crocks to find just the right weight. And on and on....

I hate shopping at big-box chains so for that reason alone I'm thrilled that Kitchen Kaboodle is local and in my neighborhood! They carry many top brands so some merchandise is pricey, but there are plenty of basics here as well that are budget-friendly (less so when it comes to appliances perhaps, but good deals appear nonetheless). 

Surprisingly, I wasn't hunting for kitchenware but for furniture on my visit yesterday. And there's a whole section of it upstairs: not just kitchen-related, but for the living room as well (couches, tables, floor rugs, and so on). In terms of look, I'd compare it to something like Crate & Barrel or West Elm: modern and comfortable with an edge of safe eclecticism. Additionally, Kitchen Kaboodle's sources are smaller and more conscientious manufacturers, which is a plus. 

When I'm furniture shopping I'm fairly demanding (it took me months to find the right dining room table). I don't mind spending some money for good sustainable construction, but I lack an unlimited budget; the aforementioned shops are typically doable only with sale prices, plus I prefer to buy more locally and independently. And when furnishing a small space, a piece has to function within some pretty exact parameters (and look just right doing it). In this case, we were looking for just the right storage bench, and I was delighted to find it - on substantial sale - at the back of the store upstairs. Excellent construction from reclaimed wood, with lovely clean lines, and all at a price less than what the national stores advertised for a similar - and inferior - product. Happy!

Service couldn't have been friendlier or more helpful; the man assisting us had the bench wrapped up and outside to our car within a few short minutes. On furniture purchases (or at least this one) you still have a week to change your mind and return it, a nice option since sometimes you have to see how something looks in your home before you decide it's really what you want. No second thoughts here though!

Aside from all that excellence, Kitchen Kaboodle provides an hour of free parking behind the store so you don't have to lug your purchases blocks to your car or home on the bus. This is my future first stop for anything kitchen-related, and a nice option for furniture too (especially when there's a great sale happening).
