Input: I haven't been here in a long while. Remembering those good old days when I was a youngster, the sales person was very nice, very helpful, intuitive and really "professional". While time goes by...Precision seems to change...

The same guy always seems to be standing by the front door greeting customers. He shakes his head and smiles at us, yet doesn't say anything. ?!? Am I supposed to start the conversation? I thought to myself, "Do I need to take a number?" Do I just walk to the counter in front of me and ask for help? Do I just go get what I want then pay? Or, should I go to the other counter and ask for assistance? I try to make eye contact but everyone just seems to turn away.

Since everybody seemed so busy (which they weren't), I grabbed Josh (he couldn't escape cuz he just checked out a customer). I told him allll I need is 4 (damn) filters! One for each lens and a circular filter (then I'll get outta your hair!). He was very helpful and saved me some money on the filter deal. Cool!

The second time, I went back with hubby to get another battery, the same incident happened to us...We patiently waited for a sales person who was working at the computer on the counter. He saw us, but just kept minding his own business while we just stood there and waited.

All and all, they've got everything you'll ever need/want for all your photographic needs, whether it's new, old or used cameras, lenses or equipment. I'm not even going to talk about all of the professional camera equipment they have in there. They also provide photo copying/printing services, and have lots of "How to" training resources from classes, to books and to videos.  Anything you want to know about photography, they got it. One stop shopping for allll your photo needs, how bout that! 
   
Of course, I will definitely be back, since this is the only "professional" camera store in town. They have the best selection on all things "photography" anyway. (Even though I have to put up with SOME of the attitude here, hopefully that'll change) If it weren't for the professional advice they gave us "rookies", then, I'd rather go someplace else. Hubby disagrees though. It's not just me, is it?

Input: This isn't the kind of Starbucks where you'd want to hang out for a few hours, but it's super efficient, very pleasant, and has parking in the back. The staff are very friendly and smart - no space cadets as far as I've seen so far. It's a sheer wonder how they get through the long morning line so quickly. The first time I went in here at 8:15am, the size of the line made me think it would be a disaster, but before I knew it I was ordering my usual (grande iced americano in a venti cup with extra ice and water), a drink that very few Starbucks employees across the country have ever gotten right. Normally, I either get a blank stare, a quad-shot americano (I'm not looking for a heart attack, but thanks), or a grande americano at the price of a venti. This has become of a pet peeve of mine, to the point where I now judge a Starbucks by how well they handle this drink. Sometimes you have to wait a little bit to get your drink after ordering here, but the staff members go as fast as they can without messing up your drink, so I give them credit.

Not only are the people here extremely organized and "with it," but they also go out of their way to give you what you ordered and be nice about it. Today, my drink somehow got lost in the shuffle for a few minutes (not even that long), and they presented me with a certificate for a free drink next time. They even said they were sorry. Normally, when my order gets lost at a Starbucks, I get an annoyed glare for daring to ask where it might have gone.

Input: Went here last night on whim. I remember going to Smokey's when I was a small child, sometimes trekking from North Portland with my mom just for their pizza. They had the best pizza ever and I was tentatively hoping their current pizza could still live up to my memory of it. 

First off, the place is a bit "divey", located in the strip mall, and has seen better times, decor-wise. The room partitions are a bit shredded, the tables and chairs are probably the same ones from the 70's. But, in all, the place is clean and kept-up for what they have to work with. (Note about temps - the front is colder (a/c) and the back of the restaurant is warmer.) 

Being a Friday night, we thought the place might be packed, but it wasn't. In fact, it was kind of a ghost town in there. Not sure why. Friday night, pizza and beer....should be plenty of people. But I think there was only about 6 people total here. 

The employees were super-nice and friendly. Ever so helpful, too. This is one of the few places offering a gluten-free pizza (small size only tho), and they made sure to tell me about the sausage and the burger mix not being gluten-free. Any pizza joint willing to attempt making gluten-free pizza gets high marks in my book! (FYI, for those who don't know, gluten is what makes breads, etc, light, doughy, & fluffy. When left out, the result is often cardboard.) From what I could tell, there was no extra cost for the gluten-free option (another big plus, since GF stuff is EXPENSIVE!). 

My husband had their Smokey's Red beer. Super great, he says! If he had known it was going to be so good, he would've ordered a pitcher. LOL. Myself, I had lemonade. It may have been from a mix (they store it in a "Tupperware-like" container behind the counter), but it was really good, too.

The pizza took a bit longer than we were told (doesn't it always seem to, tho?), but we found it was worth the wait. The pizza was Small, but it was enough for us 2 people, plus a few slices to take home. The crust was, well, pretty good as far as gluten-free bread items go. Since it had no gluten to make it "rise", it was more like a thick cracker crust. They get points there for it. As we found out on our way out, they are fairly new to the whole gluten-free stuff. Since it is so expensive, it's not like they are able to make a bunch of "practice pizzas" - it would be really expensive to do so - and they are still figuring it all out. But it was definitely edible and palatable, even tho the workers that night all admitted that none of them had ever made one of the gluten-free pizzas yet. They did good. 

As for the toppings, we got the meat feast options, with added olives and pineapple. When the pizza arrived, it was heavy! LOADS of toppings! Heck, if I wanted to forgo the crust, a full meal could still be made from just the toppings alone! More points to them!

Our total bill came to $26.73. I guess that's decent these days for good pizza joints (why the heck is pizza, any pizza, so expensive nowadays?!). So, that's not too bad, really. As for flavor, taste, etc, they certainly did still live up to my memory of awesome yummy pizza! I am looking forward to dropping in again and making this our regular pizza place. It's like "pizza crack". Totally good and still worth a trek cross town for it. 

The bathrooms were clean, so that's another plus. Especially in older places, where they are often hard to keep clean. 

Keep up the great work, guys! Thanks for not being afraid to offer the gluten-free crust, and willing to keep working on it to make it even better!

Input: When I see an Italian Restaurant that features pizza on its menu my heart sinks, my head slowly descends to the table top and a gentle, rhythmic, banging begins. 
So we'd given Double Zero a miss until this weekend. We were on Roswell Road at 5:45 on Saturday and decided on a whim to give them a try for an early drink and antipasti. 
We self-parked, although there is a valet, and sat at the bar which is a little gloomy when coming in from the bright sun . Initially we had some difficulty reading the menu, fortunately Allie, our first server, had just bought some small flashlights, which helped until our eyes adjusted. Also behind the bar : Nick, from Grimsby UK, Chris, the beverage manager, and Trey. All the staff are friendly and helpful. 
One of the things I look for in a new restaurant is a wine list that contains wines that are unfamiliar to me, it's a good indicator of return visit potential. The list here is impressive with an Italian focus. Of the 80 plus wines on offer, at least 70% were unfamiliar to us and , most importantly, 50 or so are available by the glass. 
We called a friend we were meeting later to come and join us and had a couple of glasses of Soligo prosecco while we waited- the bar had one or two people seated and 20% of tables were occupied.
Our friend was feeling in the mood for something with a germanic profile (some weight and a clean finish). Chris was very helpful finding a wine with a profile he'd like - I Greco Filu Bianco.
We ordered a couple of small platters of cheese and meats, these are things that we serve at home so we had a basis for comparison
-Salame Toscano 
-Speck 
-Pecorino Grand Cru 
These came served together on a wooden board with a small bowl of green and brown olives, a couple of pieces of rustic bread and a spoonful of pepper jam. The arrangement was a nice touch - we've often ordered in this way and ended up with a separate plate for each dish.
All these were excellent with the Pecorino being a particular standout.
By 6:30 the place had started to fill up:  more people at the bar and the tables were around 50% full.
With another 45 minutes to spare we decided further investigation was warranted- we changed up wines and ordered more food. 
Wine:  a few reds from the House list: Barberani Polago Umbria and the Double Zero Pedirosso Campania. I like Barberani and this glass was a steal at $8 - highly recommended .
Food: 
Lamb Polpettine (sous-vide lamb meatballs)
Pork Belly Risotto served with a slow poached egg
Arancini

I went outside to check out the small patio: most of the area is occupied with a couple of small bocce courts (bocce in Sandy Springs!) one of which was being used by a family group, it's worth saying that I didn't notice any kids inside the restaurant,
The food arrived while I was outside so we didn't immediately catch the one error of our visit - instead of the Arancini we ended up with the Orrechiette. Time was too pressing for us to wait so we skipped the Arancini, and tasted the pasta - a little bland . The restaurant backed the Orrechiette off the bill.
The four meatballs were good - the mild flavor of lamb shone well through the seasoning and the crust was a fine contrast.
The belly was excellent - with the egg a great addition - certainly our favorite of the three dishes and something I would go back for. 

We left at 7:15, our total was $75 (excluding tip) - not bad at all. 
By the time we left the place was at 75% capacity and people were arriving for reservations. Age range 35-60 . Noise level acceptable. Pizza forms only a small part of the menu!
Rating: four stars - "on the list to visit often"

Input: Once upon a time, I went to see the Hunger Games (the first one) and my arm was viciously mauled by Bedbugs residing in the armrest of the theater's chairs. I discovered this as I was driving home and promptly returned and calmly declared that they had an infestation to take care of. Well the next morning I called and reported them for a health code violation and had the theater shut down for two weeks for fumigation. YES Houston friends, that was me. I don't think it is necessary to call out this super popular theater as I'm sure the forcible fumigation was enough. 

Regardless, why is this important? That bedbug mauling is what gives me trust issues when it comes to movie theaters. I've reached a point where I tend to only gravitate towards leather seats or make sure to wear long sleeves and pants if I'm in doubt. 

Regardless, I ended up at this theater to see Sin City: A Dame to Kill For. The theater we had planned on going to had a later showing, so we figured it wouldn't hurt to drop by here. 

My takeaway is that the theater seems to be trying to be a nightclub. It kind of reminds me of Lucky Strike in Houston, only instead of the gimmick being Bowling, it's Movies. Regardless, I like the pool tables, I also liked my decision to wear shorts and not a dress. Ain't nobody trying to be all cute and sit on the table to make a shot in a short skirt. I errr.... no longer try to use my feminine wiles to win competitive games. Wait, I take that back, all holds are off for my random occasional games of beer pong. We save those for ratchet nights. 

HOWEVER, what matters is the free blanket upgrade for the Premium Plus seats. I like having a blanket and a seat that reclines during a movie. But the premium plus seats have this weird microfiber cover that feels.... nubby? The way microfiber feels when it's slightly dirty. Which again brings to surface my trust issues involving bedbugs and movie theaters. Ironically the Premium seats have actual leather covers... aka bedbug deterrent. Come on iPic can't I pay $1 for the blanket? Or can the premium plus seats at least be smooth leather?!! I'm at a Catch-22; I want to be comfortable but I am super paranoid about bed bugs. I guess you can't win them all. I suppose I'll only get the premium plus seats when I wear long pants and long sleeves.... I can live with that.

I ate beforehand this time since we didn't plan on going here, but their menu looks pretty solid. I'd definitely be tempted to get food here next time!

Input: Back in October, I went to WE Day with Sherman and we decided to finish off the day with a bit of sushi. It's hard for two foodbloggers to go to a place neither of us has been, so thankfully, he was willing to do a "revisit" to a place that I hadn't visited before. This is what led us to Zipang Sushi. All photos are courtesy of Sherman. "Thanks!"  

Given that this was midday (and they were about to close after lunch), and he had already had lunch, we wanted to order light (and quickly). We started with their Assorted Sashimi. The salmon was amazing, and I really enjoyed the tako. The slices were cleanly cut and care was taken with the presentation.  

We wanted to try their rolls too, so we gave two of them a try. On either side is their Triple S roll, made up of Salmon, Scallop and Shrimp. I enjoyed the rice to filling ratio on this and could taste the sweetness of the scallop and shrimp quite clearly. The other was the East Meets West, filled with unagi, avocado and topped with prosciutto. As with most fusion cuisine where they pair Western flavours or ingredients with Asian flavours, the result could be a hit or a miss. The prosciutto seemed a bit dry and out of place with the roll. However, this would be an excellent choice for those who are squeamish when it comes to raw fish. 

I love Salmon Kama and when I saw that they had it, we had to order it, and boy, I'm sure glad I did. The skin had a good crispy char to it, and the fleshy collar was juicy and flaky. They served it with some grated daikon. Add some soy sauce to it and make a paste to dip the salmon into. The sweetness of the fish and the saltiness of the soy is a great umami sensation.

Although I wouldn't normally order Assorted Tempura, Sherman wanted to to give us another hot entrée to try. The prawns were really sweet and I loved the light coating. I normally have to peel apart some of the coating, but it was unnecessary here. The veggies were a bit heavy, more because of the thick portions they were cut into, rather than a heavy batter. Overall, this was a good place for a nice light lunch and I'd definitely come back if I was in the area again.

Take Note:

Closed on Mondays, and closes between 3-5pm.
Lots of options for non-raw fish lovers
Give the Okonomi a try, mini-pizzas. or the Takoyaki!
- See more at: http://xmasbb.blogspot.ca/#uds-search-results

Do you remember the scene for Ratatouille when the food critique took a bit of the ratatouille? Well, my first bite didn't bring me back to my childhood, but it gave me complete satisfaction. I'm glad they gave a heaping too. My friend ordered pot roast, cheese bread, sweet potatoes, and broccoli casserole. Although the pot roast was slightly dry, the dish was still delectable.  

Show your student id and get $1 off.

Decent selection of casual and dressier options for the "young, modern working woman" (no, my new job isn't in advertising). Service was there, but sort of indifferent. Input: We dined at Grain & Gristle last Saturday night and we were pleasantly surprised. We did a lot of research on different restaurants before we went out that evening and Grain & Gristle seemed to have the best prices and yummiest selections that night.

When we arrived inside the restaurant the lady that greeted us wasn't the friendliest. When we asked approximately how long the wait would be to sit outside (which doesn't seem like an outlandish request, right?) she snapped back with "we don't give out times - just put your name on the list." The man behind the bar wasn't any better. At one point he snapped at us when he asked if we were on the wait-list and we answered yes, instead of stating our name. Kinda strange, but everyone inside seemed to have an "I'm-too-busy" attitude.

We ordered a few drinks, sat there and thought, wow - not the best first impression, I wonder if this place was a mistake?? About 15 minutes later we were seated outside & got very lucky with a super nice waitress. She was very helpful and even made some suggestions on the menu.

We ordered the summer salad with tomatoes, stone fruit and whipped chevre with basil. It was so delicious we wanted to lick the plate clean! Next up was the Fressen pretzel w/ spicy mustard. This was also delicious. The mustard had a strong kick and you could feel the heat rising in your nose. We loved it! 

For entrees we got the Mediterranean sausage with cous cous and yogurt & the burger with a fried egg. We split both & once again wanted to lick our plates when we were finished! We couldn't have loved our food choices more.

I would definitely recommend this place for the food (the beer choices were great, too).

Plush arm chairs in front, but a dining room  made up of tables and plastic-backed chairs reminiscent of the small mid-western eateries back home. Dozens of wine bottles in varying states of emptiness sit on one of these tables set against the open kitchen's half wall. The overall feeling is one of uncertainty. But the smiling people, drinks in hand, affirm that yes, it's open. 

Drinks were ordered and brought first. It's the usual progression of things, so why not. We sip, talk, comment, generally lose track of time. Then, after Bek's stared at the bottom of her glass a while, and it seems I'm destined the same, we're asked for our order. Slow. Understandable, but slow. The restaurant is full. Nearly every table and chair taken. Not bad for a weeknight. Doesn't look like they expected it. There's the one waitress, a sous chef and the husband and wife owners. She's cooking, and he's preoccupied with some corner shelving; the waitress scrambling, looking deeply unenthused.

We order food and a refill for Bek. Should've ordered one for me to. More talking, no sipping (for me), more commenting. Now two empty glasses, no food. The owner stops by, gives us his spiel, "Indian food how it's made in India!" Great personality. No food. 

Eventually it comes. Two rotis, representing most of what is available. Chapatis and six bowls of various dishes. I like mine, Bek likes hers. We're happy and decide that we weren't really in any hurry. So, why not.

We leave full.

Input: I couldn't figure out why I kept coming here. 

Obsessively. 

Withstanding the TORTURE it is to come here:
- Cold patio. Warmish upper body, frozen ankles. 
- How the shack has nothing I want.
- The endless, endless, forever-feeling, tap tap tap, watch paint dry, excruciating wait for food...
- Ohhh, pile on some more wait... while intoxicatingly delicious garlic smells permeate your olfactory bulb and seduce your senses sooo baaaddd....
- Faackkk... the swirling thoughts like, "Why don't these fuckers deliver.. Why do I have to come all the way here... You know how hard it is for me to come here...!!"
- More empty-stomach wait. You can feel the hunger scrrrratch the insides of your gut. The lime drinking vinegar only exacerbates the feeling.

So.. what the crap is it about pok pok that got me hooked? Obsessed? Enduring ^that shit up there when I have hugely better and more high leverage things to do?

Is it the lime drinking vinegar that brings me here? (It's good! But no... it can't just be a mere gimmick that turns "tasty" to obsession..)

I was pushing around food in the pok dining room last night, and... I had an Anton Ego moment. 

You know, that one climactic part in Ratatouille where the evil food critic takes a taste of Remy's ratatouille and drops his pen. Dilates his pupils. Whooshes back to his childhood, countryside memories of his delicate countryside mother, cooking a delicate countryside meal... and it pierces away all those years of his wretchedness, and makes him feel human?

Yes! I had that moment! That WHOOSH. An amazing space-time bending whOOOOOsh back to my past. It's the fucking Kaeng Huh Leh. Which has the PRECISE exact flavor, texture, and taste of the only thing my evil filipino grandmother ever produced that lightened the burden of her evilness: Her pork adobo. 

And this revelation poured in both fear and delight. Fear that my grandmother was there. Delight when I realized she wasn't. Then bigger delight when I realized I closed a loop in my mind. I don't ever need to visit my grandma ever again! I realized the only reason why I went is so I could have pork adobo. And now, smacking me in the face in portland oregon, is a better ingriediented, unfathomably delicious, far superior version. 

Kaeng Hung Leh. Fuckin get it. It will change your life. 

I admit, that wasn't the dish that got me obsessed with pok pok. Owe that to Cha ca la vong. They put crack in that dish. Or some sort of people-catnip. 

When you read this: "Catfish marinated in turmeric and sour sticky rice, fried in turmeric oil with scallions and dill, served on rice vermicelli with peanuts, mint and nouc cham. Our stab at the famous dish from La Vong Restaurant in Hanoi, Vietnam." 

Beware. 

Even when you speak or think of it, all the tastebuds from the back of your tongue to the front will long for this, and pollute your brain with a hypnotic "go to pok pok. cha ca la vong. mmm. now." drone. And you'll skip out on your homework, or work-work, or whatever is important, and endure some fucking mean torture (see above), and then... 

Then you have it. 
And its really really good. 
And then its gone cuz pok pok's portions are fucking small.

Input: G & S Lounge is pretty cool.
its always described as a dive bar, and sure the place has probably never been dusted, but what kind of dive bar has a selection of beer like that. its great, i feel like a kid in a candy store looking at the coolers of all the different beers. i try to make it a point to at least have one beer i haven't had before, and i've been there quite a few times and don't think i've tried them all.
i remember the first few times about being hesitant with the popcorn, but its fine.
things i like
*the awesome selection of bottled beer
*the fact that they keep a freezer full of ice cold glasses that is customer accessible (the freezer next to that weird beach head game)
*the ms pac man table, which has the code on it to turn it into normal pac man... although ms pac man is vastly superior
*the fact there are two jukeboxes
*the lego aircraft carrier over the bar
*lord of the rings pinball
*the fast service

it seems everyone has something to say about jimmy, and i agree with one of the previous reviews that he's just as much a character as leslie, but i think jimmy is really a nice guy. he may seem a little gruff, but he's cool, he's always hustling behind the bar, picking up glasses, restocking the cooler, he usually has help but he pretty much could run that bar by himself even on friday and saturday nights, i don't ever think he takes a night off. he's two dogs are great, and anybody who has dogs as nice as his must be a good guy.

one of the funniest things i think i've seen at a bar was once at the G&S lounge around 7, before it was crowded, he threw an empty beer box on top of a pool table, one of his dogs, the bigger one, hopped up on the pool table and just played with the box, swinging it around and tearing it up with dog barks of joy... i think i even saw jimmy smile, and every time jimmy smiles, an angel gets its wings.

Input: You know what this place has? Vibes for days.

By this point in Portland, most any coffee shop is going to be able to pour a quality shot. They definitely do that here at Push X Pull, and they get bonus points for roasting their own beans from right inside the shop. Every coffee drink I've had here has been awfully good, though I'm somewhat cranky that their only non-dairy alternative is oat milk. I'm an almond milk guy and don't like how many carbs are in oat milk. Then again, I totally destroyed a pizza last night, so maybe I shouldn't be such a raging hypocrite? I digress...

So how's a coffee shop to differentiate themselves? For me it's all about the atmosphere, which Push X Pull has for days. I live for this open and airy shop. The blonde wood and turquoise accents are modern and different than anything I've seen in a Portland coffee shop. That plus the massive walls of windows make this a really lovely environment in which to spend some time. Oh, and they're currently playing Chance the Rapper, so I'm feeling pretty good about the music vibes, too.

This place has been open for a minute and somehow only has 6 reviews? I feel like maybe Push X Pull is still under the radar. Hopefully not TOO under the radar, however. This little corner of PDX is all that much better because of their presence.

Input: Pros: My experience with the customer service at spud.ca has been positive. The processing of my visa update was friendly and convenient and the delivery man never fails to bid a good day. Occasionally there are steal-for-it discounts, and new members for the first few weeks get 5 dollars off their invoice. The groceries are always carefully packaged and frozen items are kept fresh in an ice bag. The plastic bin is also useful to up-cycle your Save-on-Foods and Safeway bags and other recyclable items you forgot to put out for collection in the week. The grocery versatility is also quite appeasing and their website is easy to navigate. 

Cons: Items are generally a few dimes to one or two dollars more expensive than my organic grocery store a few blocks down. Always look for the weekly specials. Some items are over priced. I ordered a package of micro-greens arugula last time and it came in a plastic container barely enough for a single salad topping. The mango I ordered were 40 cents more expensive and 1/3 the size of ones I got from Donald's market. Sometimes the white mushrooms come with brown spots and salad greens are already decaying. 

If you are ready to invest a few extra dollars a week but save the half hour driving and carrying your groceries, and risk a few grocery mishaps, spud.ca is for you. Other wise, I would suggest running to commercial or the farmer's market and save spud.ca for one of those there's really no extra time weeks. I switch between trips to organic markets, green earth organics, and spud.ca to get the best offers. I would suggest not to be too dependent on the site, always have your alternatives.

Input: I agree with the other reviews.  The exterior rooms here leave a lot to be desired.  However......

We have stayed here several times (just got back today from a quick trip there) and only once was I moderately disappointed.  We usually purchase deals for this hotel through Groupon and have learned to pay close attention to whether or not the deal is for an exterior or interior room.  

Looking to save as much money as possible on this last trip we opted for an exterior room again and crossed our fingers.  The exterior room we got a year ago was in the back of the property.  It was musty.  It was dark.  It felt dingy.  Overall we felt isolated and did get that motel like feel.  This time we lucked out and got an exterior room toward the front of the building (facing Hotel Plaza Blvd) and overall did not get that same feeling as last year.  The room felt cleaner and brighter.  I didn't feel "unsafe" and it wasn't as loud as the rooms toward the back of the building.  

We love how close this hotel is to Downtown Disney (a walk across the street).  My kids love the character breakfast (on select days), even if it is only Goofy and Pluto.  I can't say anything about the pool as I'm not a fan of public pools in general and usually avoid them.

Overall I prefer this hotel MUCH more to the Disney "value resorts" (All Star Resorts) which definitely give me a motel feel and are slightly more expensive.  We are definitely planning on staying again and will try to book only interior rooms from now on.

Input: A small establishment with a large presence, their building is easy to spot from the turnabout as they have a large pyramid-like hat as their roof -- parking is available sometimes on the street, but if that's taken, try behind their bldg. 

If you're a falafel aficionado like I am, you would get excited like I did when approaching their establishment, but it doesn't last. As soon as you walk in, you see the entire kitchen prep area crammed behind a buffet bar and a small table desk. This allowed for some seating inside the location, but you would think they could use the extra space to prepare their menu items.

Instead, what you get is a quickly made falafel that was churned from an assembly line of ingredients. Don't expect a Chipotle-style experience, as this assembly line has a mish mosh of ingredients, half of which have strong Asian roots. The ingredients are fresh, but they are the basics and nothing more. 

The location is confused with its menu items, and this is evident when you see their name does not match up with the focus of their offerings. It's more of an Asian-Mediterranean fusion, which is cool and all, but the name "Falafel King" is misleading.

As for the food taste, their falafel needs improvement but it is a solid sandwich for its worth. This location does the bare minimum when it comes to respecting what it could be, and I think if they tweak some of their current offerings and add a few more, it could make their falafel sandwiches something worth boasting about. 

Oh well. It's too bad, they have great potential with that location to make killer profits. Overall, good food but their poor execution is holding them back from being a memorable eatery. Instead, they seem bland and blend into the mix of food offerings nearby.

Input: Like any great park or public center it is mostly magical based on the people who are interacting within it's boundaries.  This is a very blank slate kind of space.  Which is a big factor in how much I love it.

Don't get me wrong, there's one of our most charming Starbucks on the block, as well as an amazing array of steps which make you lovingly hope that someone doesn't try to enforce handrail codes someday, an amazing water feature and the visitor's center.  But where the magic comes in is on a nice day during lunch, or Flicks on the Bricks events and other things that bring people together in this massive city center open space.  I for one am glad Portland set aside some of these places early on as infill has already taken so many amazing spaces away.  It's important to preserve some of them and know they all have social value.

Obviously this is an oven of a space on a hot sunny day, but it's Portland so most of our time is lovely... shhhh, don't tell the tourists that ;)  If our secret gets out more folks will want to live here.

It's a nice break from what "normal" folks do downtown with lots of shopping and things to do around.  Take a moment and just enjoy watching those folks from a great perch here... on the bricks.

Input: Came here via Scoutmob (50% up to $20 off), not that it did much damage to our final bill.

Super trendy / kinda noisy / cool date spot sort of place. Ya know how it is. So that being said, this restaurant is kinda on the small side.. not a good place for a group.

As with many other sushi places, they provide for you a list of all the sushi rolls / sashimi that they have, and you have to write in the quantity of each one that you want. On the average, I'd say that each roll will set you back about $10 (6-8 pieces per roll). So we settled on four different rolls, plus this sweet potato thingy (that's cause we were craving some tempura!). Also ordered a couple of bowls of miso soup, and a sparkling sake to share. 

Sparkling sake - I've only had warm sake before, so this was interesting! Surprisingly tasted very refreshing and was enjoyable. A 250 ml bottle cost $14 HOWEVER, we were there on a Sunday, and our server somehow forgot to mention that they have a BOGO hot sake deal on Sundays. Uhh, not cool. 

Miso soup - I guess I'm supposed to be a miso soup pro cause I'm Asian or whatever... so yes, the miso soup was quite good. However, they failed because I found all of TWO little tofu cubes in my soup (last time I checked, H Mart sells tofu for pretty darn cheap), and also because they must not know that real Asians like to have their soup along with their meal, not before as an appetizer (that's a white people thing). 

Sushi rolls - All excellent! Fish was very, very fresh - could taste it melting in my mouth! Oh, and it turns out that the "sweet potato thingy" that I ordered earlier was a sushi roll, not tempura. I'm not sure how the idea of a making sweet potato into sushi came about, cause it sure tasted... strange. Don't get it, even though it's only $5.

Tempura - well, the sweet potato was not a tempura, so we ended up ordering some extra. Comes with 3 pieces of shrimp tempura, and 3 pieces of veggie tempura. Nothing special, just the standard stuff.

So a couple of mini blunders here and there reduced it to 4 stars. Really, I wanted to give 5... our server (Kate E) was very attentive to us (pluss her super cuteness didn't hurt!), and overall I had a great experience.

Input: I would've given Truluck's 5 stars were it not for the fact that I'm hardly ever able to actually dine here.  Trulucks has set up their system to discourage solo dining for whatever reason.  If you go to their website or their open table site, there is effectively no option for reservations for 1.  You can only reserve a table for 2 or more people.  If you try and reserve a table for 1, you'll get options weeks into the future at inconvenient times like 5:45 PM. 

I'll often walk in and ask for a table only to be ushered into the first-come-first-serve lounge area.  That's all well and good, but I walk into the lounge and realize there's 0 seating available.  That's the point where I walk right out of the restaurant and head over to Fleming's or Jasper's in the domain.  I eat out a lot and I try to eat at Trlucks a lot but I just don't get the opportunity.  On rare occasion I'll walk in at a reasonable time and they'll be able to seat me right away or they'll give me a 10-15 minute waiting time which is perfectly fine.  

I can't tell you how many times I'm craving Truluck's only to think "Well, will they really be able to seat me?  Nah.  Let's go to Fleming's or Jasper's or Driskill or Carillon instead."  It's just part of their culture I suppose.   I just wish they would have reservations available for solo diners on open table.  

Other than that, the food is good.  I love their parmesan mashed potatoes and they make a pretty good filet.  Their crab cakes are pretty pedestrian.  I think Bartlett's does crab cakes the best in Austin.  Their bread is excellent.  It comes to the table freshly baked, warm, and moist.

Input: My husband recently took me here for my 30th birthday and it surpassed expectations.  It was the middle of the week, a Wednesday night, so you do not expect the top service or chef to be in the kitchen.  However, the meal was flawless.  They had our reservation from open table and figured out exactly who I was since my husband arrived before me and sent us upstairs promptly to get our table.  We ordered a glass of prosecco to start and it was delicious and served promptly.  My appetizer, the fried artichokes, was perfect.  The batter was light enough not to overpower the artichokes and the aioli was a perfect compliment.  My husband's barbajuans were also delicious but I preferred the artichokes.  Our server was very attentive and there was always someone right there to bring the next plate or remove the old one.  Then came our entrees.  My husband had the pork special with a piece of pork presented in an artful way and some pork belly to accompany it.  I didn't taste it since I don't eat pork, but he enjoyed it immensely.  He particularly liked the pork belly.  I had the Beef Daube with Mashed Potatoes and we shared a side of the Broccoli with Garlic.  My beef was perfectly cooked, it was fork tender and the mashed potatoes were an excellent pairing with the meat and the sauce.  The broccoli was done perfectly and the most delicious broccoli I have tasted.  I couldn't stop eating it.  I do like my mashed potatoes with a bit more oomph, these were very light and thin and I prefer mine to be more solid.  The taste was very good, however.  We did not taste the desserts because we had birthday cake waiting at home, but we will be back for another special occasion and before that for the bar menu and to sample the desserts.  The decor was very classic with one exception we noticed, the ceramic beehive shapes in many colors above the fireplace in the dining room.

Input: Solid food! But in my opinion, was not memorable.

Tasty N Son's brunch menu has a something for everybody type of vibe and ranges from traditional breakfasts, to sandwiches, and fusion foods. They serve their food family style, meaning that the food will be served once its out the kitchen as opposed to serving the entire table at once. I am used to eating family style, though the portions are not what I consider family style. They are individual portions and on the smaller side.

Burmese Red Pork stew - Just okay. It was a braised sweet pork served over a bed of white steamed rice and topped with an egg both ways (fried and boiled). Having grown up eating Burmese cuisine, there was nothing reminiscent of Burmese flavors and spices. The marinated boiled egg with the sweet pork reminded me more of the Taiwanese pork rice dish. 

Breakfast Board - Good! I liked the simplicity of the ingredients that all came together. Awesome bread, crostini, boiled eggs, pate, bacon, and lebneh. 

Shakshuka - Okay. Nice tomato flavor bubbling together with eggs. It is enjoyed by dipping some bread into the sauce.

Input: I was next door buying a magazine at the Inventory Stockroom and passed by Sea Monstr along the way. The storekeep's coworker is a regular here and recommended I give it a try. 

By the time I sat down (5 pm), there wasn't much of a raw selection in the display case- which is weird considering how early in the day it was. I originally wanted their Uni/Ikura bowl (sea urchin & salmon roe, a steal at $13.50), but was told they don't serve uni when it's off season. Fair enough. 

I ordered the Chirashi Don instead and was pleased to see the unconventional presentation of the dish. The sashimi were cut into bite sizes and dotted with salmon roe and small slices of tamago (sushi omelet). The slices were layered in a haphazard way, reminiscent of a godzilla-esque sea monster on a rampage- or maybe that's just me. 

The sashimi is fresh, and according to the menu the establishment uses the "finest locally sourced seafood". 

The service was efficient, and I like how Sea Monstr serves water that has been distilled using equipment provided by Vivreau Pure Water- hence the specially designed bottles they serve water with. 

The decoration is simple- apart form a wreath of Sapporo beer cans hanging on a brick wall, way past Christmas but still pretty cool. 

Overall, it was a fun experience. A chirashi don for $12.50 is already good value! I'll be back to check out their rolls, and to see whether they are better stocked on other days.

Input: My husband and I went to ChenZ early-evening today, and really enjoyed it.

There were so many choices that sounded very tasty and interesting, we had trouble deciding what to get.

The service was great... food and hot pot concept thoroughly explained, water glasses kept full, very pleasant, attentive and prompt.  The young lady that served us was quite helpful with food recommendations and sauce choices.

We tried the sesame pockets appetizer.  The spiced pork, sesame pastry and cilantro were a great flavor combination.  All gone quickly, and plenty to share.  We'll try the onion crepes or lamb skewers on our next visit.  Or might get more adventurous and try the jelly fish salad.

We tried the hot pot, and will definitely go back to try some of their noodle dishes.  For our hot pot (ChenZ had about 40 items on the hot pot menu from which to choose), we chose the tomato broth and then lamb, chicken, quail eggs, shitake mushrooms and baby bok choy.  The broth came out simmering hot in its hot pot, and we were ready to go.  The tomato broth was a very pleasing combination of delicate, yet very fragrant and flavorful.

The lamb and chicken looked, smelled and tasted fresh, as did our veggies and the quail eggs.  Once all were simmered together in the hot pot, the combination of those together with the tomato broth was a delight to enjoy!  Everything we got was fresh, of good quality, and nicely presented.

Also, the restaurant and ladies' room were absolutely squeaky clean.

I do notice a good deal of fuss here about prices.  We eat at a variety of restaurants, so perhaps I'm used to a broader range of prices, but I did not find prices out of line at all for the quality and flavor of the foods we tried, and for the prompt, friendly service.  We had more than enough food for two adults, very much enjoyed our dining experience, and left happy and full for just at $50.00 including tip.

My only complaint is I did not save room for dessert.

Input: The Capital Grille dining area is beautifully decorated in dark wood, low lighting at dinner, jazz music piping in over the speakers, with paintings on the wall.  The dining chairs are very comfortable leather dining chairs. Crisp white linens adorn the tabletops. Black napkins are provided for dark clothing. After having the warm bras with salted butter, I had the cast iron shrimp which are delightful beyond words. The shrimp are completely peeled, served in a small iron skillet, over soft crostini, cherry heirloom tomatoes, basil, and covered in a butter, garlic, and lemon sauce. Soooo tasty! The lump crabmeat is served with a mayo based sauce with a tiny amount of horseradish. It is an ample serving - be sure to ask for additional sauce. 

The filet mignon with the peppercorn preparation is divine. We eat out five days a week and have had meals in many cities in the US and Europe and the filet mignon here was by far one of the most tender and flavorful cuts of meat (aside from my mom's slow roasted garlic stuffed  rump roast) I have ever had. Our waiter, Kenneth, was fantastic. 

The seasonal berries with crème Anglaise are refreshing, the flourless chocolate espresso cake is wonderful, and the warm chocolate with port wine infused cherries and ice cream are scrumptious as is the cheesecake.  The cheesecake is very light and has the taste of creme brûlée. 



The lobster bisque is more of a cup of soup, not a bowl by any means, and to be honest it tastes like hot goo and extremely thick. It is the soup du jour and was highly recommended by the waiter. I sent it back and ordered the French onion soup. The French Onion Soup was as delightful as the lobster bisque was bad. The onion soup had a rich brown base with abundant onions, cheese and bread. It could benefit from being served in a larger vessel. A lot of the rich broth flows onto the saucer and is sinfully wasted. Very nice course.

Input: I adopted two dogs from Northeast Animal Shelter just down the street. They recommended this clinic and I am so glad they did!

Both of my dogs have their own special needs. I have one who lost a back leg due to being shot in the leg (this was before I adopted him, and we don't know who did it or why). Needless to say, he is pretty nervous around strangers and doesn't really like to be touched. I would muzzle him when I brought him in, just out of caution, but I'm not sure that I needed to. Dr. Ingram was excellent with him! I don't recall him ever growling at her, which is what he does when someone he doesn't know approaches him too closely or touches him. She was always very thorough and explained everything she was doing. She would even call to follow up after every appointment!

My other dog was a stray for the first 18 months of her life, and while she is better with strangers she still does not enjoy being picked up or taken away from me. I'm fairly certain she give some of the techs a very rough time whenever they tried to take blood or give her a shot, but if they were ever frustrated or annoyed, they never let it show in front of me. After a few dramatic visits on my dog's part, they asked if I wouldn't mind coming back with them for shots to help calm her down. I know that most places don't allow this, but ever since then everything went very smoothly!

I have since moved across the country, and NEVC and Dr. Ingram are some of the things we miss most! I would highly recommend this clinic, and especially Dr. Ingram.

It's worth noting that one evening I had to come in for an appointment and it was not a night that Dr. Ingram was working. We waited for 50 minutes to be seen, and an additional 35 once shown into the exam room. I could hear the vet talking with other staff in the back about the clothes she bought for her own dog, and then about how badly another one of their (canine) patients smelled, for about 10 minutes before she came in to see us in the exam room. After such a long wait, I was not impressed that the staff was goofing around while I was stuck in the exam room, particularly at the expense of one of their patients. I also was not overly impressed with this particular doctor - she acted as if our appointment was an inconvenience for ehr. Thus, I recommend this clinic and Dr. Ingram together.

Input: I really didn't want to give this place four stars, but I had to, because it's just that damn good. 

I'm not exactly an indian food connoisseur, but I'm no indian food virgin, either.  And this is the best indian food I've ever had, especially for the price.  The shrimp masala (acutally, anything with masala at this place) is absolutely divine, and I really appreciate the condiments that come with each meal.  The condiments make the main dish what it is, and what it is is really, really good.

Mango lassi - also good.

What is not good is the wait.  I know, I know, I just have to suck it up and deal with it, it's part of the place's charm, blah blah blah.  Well, sorry.  Just because the wait is worth it, doesn't mean that I have to like it.  I don't.  Your food takes freaking forever to come (we're talking 20-30 minutes here).  This is by no means an unreasonable time for food to come at a normal restaurant, but at an "Indian Roadside Cafe" where there were no avialable tables, it was too much. The downstairs is tiny, so the only place I could perch while I waited was RIGHT in front of this guy who was peacefully sitting with his back to me, eating his food.  Let's just say he turned around in his chair and got an eyeful and loudly expressed his displeasure.  That was not fun for any of the parties involved. 

Also, when I went there recently, it was around 5:30ish on a Tuesday night.  I stood at the counter for FIFTEEN minutes (the only one in line) waiting for someone to take my order, but the phone kept ringing, and I kept getting ignored.  I finally left.  I know the guys behnd the counter are busy, and they always look harried, and they've never been anything but nice to me, but - come on.  Fifteen minutes is ridiculous.  And I really wanted that indian food.  

You still get four stars, Punjabi Dhaba.  But it hurts me to give them to you.

Input: Being one of the silly folks that choose to live on the south part of town, I pass Hapeville on my way home.  Needless to say, the variety of culinary options somewhat runs into a brick wall at some point below the split of the Connector, leaving us southsiders as somewhat of invalids in popular opinion.  Furthermore, Hapeville does have some interesting dining options, but considering they all almost exist solely for the Delta lunch rush and those who are stranded at the various lodging places nearby, the hours of said places are often in question.

I'd passed Slideways for literally months, intrigued by the idea of a place that specialized in sliders that wasn't a Krystal.  However, the hours of the place confirmed that they existed primarily for lunch, and went into the evening on Fridays and Saturdays.  Finally, an opportunity presented itself to where I could give the place a shot on my way home from work on a Friday with no genuine plans.

The location is a tad bit tricky if you don't know what the surrounding area is like, it's fairly easily accessible via the Virginia Ave exit off of I-85, or if you're like me and actually heading south, then probably the Sylvan Rd exit is the most expedient.  It's on the southern side of the train tracks, and has a fairly generous amount of street-adjacent parking spaces, that are thankfully free.

The interior is cozy and modern, and perhaps not something to be expected out in Hapeville, but then again the Which-Wich and Willy's on the same road have ushered in a similar modern restaurant aesthetic too.  Anyway we're greeted promptly by the friendly staff that doesn't rush us or pressure us to order, since being first-timers, we have no earthly idea of what to expect.

I ended up getting one of the specials (beef, mushrooms, bleu cheese) and a fish 'n chips slider.  Now admittedly, the prices stand out somewhat, because the sliders all seem to range from $2.99-4.99 that I noticed, and it should be made aware that this is for ONE slider.  I ended up paying $11ish for two sliders and tots (soda would have made it more), and IMO, that's close to almost unreasonable for a lunch cost.

However, when the food arrived to the table, both sliders looked good, and it put to ease the concerns over the price.

Basically, take a Krystal slider which is two sponges, with a centimeter-thick square of "beef" in it with like a pickle and some translucent caramelized onions.  You could mash your hand down on it and have maybe an inch-thick square puck of an edible sponge with the essence of meat in it.

Slideways' sliders were vastly larger; slightly too small to be called a burger, but noticeably larger than what Krystals and White Castles have led us to believe are sliders.  The buns are fluffier and still have some chew to them, and the meat portions are generous and cannot be contained by the edges of the buns.  The beef patty was slightly thicker than a half-inch practically.

The flavors of the sliders were good, but I have to say were not perfect.  The beef I suspect is handled way too much; perhaps it's in order to grind in the spices and seasoning into the beef, but in the end, the patty has a slight toughness about it that I think comes from it being handled too much, probably in order to get it to its almost picture-esque circular shape.  The flavors are good, but the consistency of the beef was slightly off-putting.

The fish 'n chip slider though, was fantastic.  The fish was fried perfectly, and had good flavor on its own, and had a mix of both vinegar and some tartar sauce on it, with some fries jammed in there.  I'm definitely getting this again the next time I swing by.

Not to be ignored were the tots.  Tater tots are obviously big in Atlanta, and there are so many places where they can be had.  I don't know what Slideways does differently than most of the other places throughout the city, but theirs are more flavorful, and awkward as it is to describe it as such, but more tender.  It's like chewier, in a flavorful mashed potato kind of way.  I know I'm doing a poor job of describing it, but I'll be damned if I didn't want some right now.

Overall, I like this place a lot, and I want it to do well.  Hapeville is somewhat of a bridge between the city from where I live and where I work, and I'm all for more quality restaurants making their way south of the city.  The prices might seem a little, but it's worth noting that you'll be getting your money's worth in product, and the bottom line is that you'll probably not be leaving hungry.

Good deal on the sandwiches for the amount of food you get. Friend had the chicken sandwich and it was definitely sizable and came with a side salad and a bowl of hand cut fries. Yum. It didn't quite match up to the eggs benny at Season's, but lots of extra points for the hint of parmesan in the potato hash, and the perfect crisp and flavor of the pancetta.

Best surprise, I thought, was that their drinks are reasonably priced for such a hotspot... I suppose it might be because it's brunch? Nevertheless, that was one tasty mango mojito for $8. I'll be back next time I'm in Vancouver; that lobster grilled cheese is calling my name.

Input: Shanghai River definitely specialises in XLB as it's one of the best I've tasted so far. They have the crab variety "Dumpling with Crabmeat" which is more expensive and comes in lesser quantity than the regular pork XLB - 5 pieces for lunch time.

We also tried a few of the lunch menu dishes including:

"Deep Fried Black Cod" which was marinated first and arrived with a side of mayo. Although it was very tasty, the skin could have been crispy as well.

The "Black Vinegar Spare Ribs with Nuts" has a nice strong burnt caramel flavour due to the thick sauce of black vinegar and sugar. The spare ribs were crunchy outside, then soft and chewy inside. It is also topped with pine nuts which I would have preferred to have been toasted first to it embarks a stronger flavour. However, this is still a must try if you want something on the sweet side.

"Deep Fried Crispy Tofu" has a nice crunchy batter filled with silken tofu and served with some watered-down soy sauce. I think they should come up with a more imaginative and tasty condiment with a mixture of XO sauce to make the dish stand out.

We also requested to see the dinner menu which they will happily take orders from so we ordered our favourite "Pan Fried Prawns with Walnuts". The prawns are coated with light batter so it gets a crunchy shell amidst one juicy bite after another. It's then tossed in mayo. It's topped with candied Honey Walnuts and sprinkled with sesame seeds. This is my all-time favourite Chinese dish which I'm critical of it's taste. So far everything has been perfectly fried except that the mayo sauce could be a bit more tastier and a tad bit sweeter like other restaurants that seem to have perfected the dish.

Overall it's a good experience if only you are able to skip the long wait which we were able to do by arriving an hour before they close for lunch. Ambiance is modern and feels clean especially with the open kitchen.

Despite the language barrier, our server tried to help us order what we were looking for since there were only a few photos that matched the extensive lunch and dinner menu.

Private parking allocated for the restaurant is available in the building they reside. As other reviewers have mentioned, make reservations before you arrive.

Input: The Macaroni Grill is a staple dinner/drinks stop for me and has been for a couple of years now.  I've been there a few dozen times.  It's definitely a favorite.

I'll categorize:

Food: the food is basically great.  I've had the opportunity now to try most things on the menu at least once, and even though I have my favorite dishes I'm rarely disappointed with any of the other options.  One very disappointing thing to note, though, is that my favorite dish of all time was removed from the menu about a year ago and I miss it very much.  Sausage and Pepper Classico, you will always be fondly remembered.

Service: this is usually good, sometimes great, sometimes not so good.  It depends on what night of the week you're in and who is working.  Sad to say, I've had lousy service here just about as often as I've had fantastic service.  The good news is that even the worst service at Macaroni Grill is still not too bad. 

Atmosphere: the atmosphere is pretty good and definitely feels Mediterranean Italian.  I like the atmosphere, especially in the bar area.  Fake plants, and paper table clothes?  Sure.  Have you been to Italy lately?  That's how they do it.  The point is, it feels like Italy and it tastes like Italy, more so than Olive Garden could ever hope for.

Prices/value: the price is moderate.  It's not a fancy restaurant so don't expect fancy prices.  Do, however, expect food that is frequently more fancy than the price you'll pay for it.  That is what you'll get.

Handy tip #1: you get better service in general in the bar area, on the stools.  The crew they have slinging the alcohol is the best in the place.  Probably the best in town.

Handy tip #2: don't bring groups of over 6 people here, especially if some people will be paying separate.  The wait staff is just not prepared to handle that, for some reason.  We had a shindig of about 10 people, all going dutch, and we were most displeased with the hassle we had to go through to get all the bills taken care of.  It's Keystone Cops for sure, so stick to small groups at most. 

All in all, if you're interested in a nice dinner and drinks, at a moderate price, Macaroni Grill is never a bad choice.  It's often the perfect choice if you're in the mood for Italian.

Input: I'm on the fence about this review. Really it was a 3.5 star meal. If this restaurant was on Park Avenue in Winter Park  it would get a 3 star rating from me for sure. Being that it is in lowly Apopka it should get 4 stars for being one of the best restaurants in town. This may be Apopka's only "special occasion" restaurant located, oddly enough, adjoining a Beef O'Brady's. The place is tiny so I would definitely recommend a reservation. At 6pm on a Friday evening we watched the place fill to capacity within 15 minutes. The layout is tight. We were seated at the table closest to the door so that every time the door opened we were blinded by sunlight. This would only be a problem until the sun went down, of course, but was annoying none the less.

Service was a little slow, especially at first. Our drinks took a while in the making but were good once we had them. Our server had limited knowledge of the types of alcohol available and squinted to read them at the bar from our table. I was starving and it took a bit to get our appetizer. Strangely they bring the bread and dipping oil only after the appetizer. It sure would have been nice to have when we first sat down. Anyway, the scallop appetizer ($16 but half off with a Yelp check in) was decent. The scallops were cooked nicely and flavorful but there was just too much oil. They ended up tasting slimy. My Chilean Sea Bass tasted better than it looked. My hubby's lamb chops would have been perfect if they hadn't been a tad over cooked. The three layer chocolate cake we split for dessert was rich but tasted dry, like a slice that had been precut then left out for a few hours to dry. 

So overall if was a good experience with a handful of small let downs. It definitely has potential to be great, and as far as Apopka goes is probably one of the greatest in the area. It isn't cheap though, as entrees will set you back in the $20-30 range. Still, if you plan it as a night out you'll likely leave satisfied. On a side note, the night we dined we saw the newly elected mayor Kilshiemer celebrating with newly elected councilman Sam Ruth. Word about this place is getting out!

Espresso Roma is the size of my left pinky. Men, if there is a woman (or another human being) you're lusting after, bring her here. Because it happens to be small, the vibe is homey but a little claustrophic; I'd never be able to read/ study/ talk/ hang out here. 

The service is all right - the workers have the cool, hippie-hipster thing going on (how Boulder!). I do feel a little out of it sometimes and am tempted to return sporting a semi-bedhead look with a wicked tattoo. I'd also get a nose piercing and talk philosophy while smoking pot. 

If you do go into Espresso Roma, try their stuffed croissants; I've had the ham + cheese (warmed) and it was delicious. I also hear their zucchini bread is good. 

Hooray for the $1 8oz coffee!

Input: I'd give this place 3.5 stars if I could but I'll be generous. This is a really fun place. The donuts are fun, the gold glitter sprayed brick outside is fun, the excitement is fun, the box is fun, etc etc. This is totally a tourist trap if you like cutesy semi unique things - making me a giant sucker for this place. 

I came here on Sunday of Labor day weekend so naturally the line was ridiculous. I'm sure its normally ridiculous though. I spent an hour in line. For donuts. Kind of crazy but I knew I was in for it. We had stopped by around noon but decided to walk around and get coffee first, and then came back around 330. The line was still the same length but thats what I was expecting. They really could use some signage or a greeter to direct people to where the line starts. It was confusing and I wasn't the only one who felt that way. I also feel like it would have been more useful to post the menu on the window in addition to their sign telling you to check the menu online. 

This place is cash only, but there is an atm if you forgot. I got a dozen donuts that I picked myself and it cost me 25 dollars and some change. I didn't get any sort of discount for getting a dozen, so don't feel pressured into getting a dozen unless you want that many. 

Voodoo Doll - I was surprised by how much I liked this. I'm not usually one for filled donuts, but this was good. The chocolate and the raspberry married well together. I was glad that I got two of these.

Bacon Maple Bar- Yuck. One of the people in front of me in line was raving about this and how you had to get one. I figured I'd like it because I LOVE maple bars. I like bacon. I like when my maple syrup gets on my bacon. But I did not like this. I had half of it and threw it away. Wish I had only got one of these.

Fruit Loops - I was really excited about this one but the fruit loops were stale. Buh. =[

Marshall Mathers - Ok I had to get this one. Plus I love m&ms. Very sweet, but what I expected.

Memphis Mafia Donut - I really liked this one, possibly my favorite out of the bunch. It was also really sweet and intense though, this ended up getting eaten in four different segments. I think this was sort of a banana fritter with peanut butter drizzle and chocolate chips. I'm not usually a peanut butter person but this was great.

Chocolate Orea and Old Dirty Bastard were pretty standard and what I was expecting.

I had a couple more that I gave away because I prioritized the others for eating myself. I really wanted the peach fritter, but they were out and I was super disappointed about that. As far as service the girl didn't really smile but she wasn't grumpy with me - but I also rattled off what I wanted and didn't stand there trying to decide. I mean really we were in line for an hour, the menu is available online, and some people seemed to have no idea what they wanted. 

The donuts overall were really delicious, there were tons of fun options, and for specialty baked goods I felt like the prices were pretty reasonable. Don't feel pressured into getting a full dozen unless you want that many. Don't forget your cash, and be prepared for a stupid long line. If you like donuts and silly cutesy things give this a shot at least once.

Input: Describing Double Happiness to my boss, a Taiwan native, I said it felt like I was in a China Town, in a movie, in a bar where the Chinese Mafia hang out in a hidden back room. 

This place is freakin' sweet! This is why I feel like I can ignore all the issues we encountered on our Tuesday night visit. First, their website says they close Tuesdays at 9:30PM. The sign in their window says differently, I believe 2AM. They also have lots of funky Chinese character lights in the windows to let you know they're there. We knew they were open because we were going to see a friend in a band that was playing there. 

Second, no one could use the bar because they had just set it's resin and no one could touch it while it was curing. The poor bartenders were kept on their toes as people still tried to put drinks on the bar. Because the bar was unable to be used, that cut their seating in half. Obvs, this is a temporary issue! 

Third, for some reason, they were unable to take credit cards. Luckily, I had cash.

Fourth, some staff seemed confused about the band getting set up, like they don't do it often. 

The stage set up was really awkward, but we got the one of two tables they had set up. My friend remarked it looked like they got it out of the dumpster.  I didn't care, it worked. There were also some random covered long tables that served no obvious purpose. Also, dispite this place being relatively new, it was really dusty. Most of their decor was covered in dust. Seriously, check out the Buddha by Fresh Street. 

Bottom line, this place is really cool. Fresh Street is a great addition to this space. My friend got a bulgogi rice bowl and said it was freakin' amazing.  You order and pay at their section of counter and they bring it to you. It definitely smelled really really yummy. Well drinks were $5, they charged a $1 for my club soda, which is pretty good. 
It's got some cozy upstairs seating for dining, the bar for hanging out, and the stage area, which if no one is engaged in the band or DJ, would be overflow space. When were were there it was practically empty, but we still had a great time. 

I'm looking forward to going back to this sweet hangout spot. I hope they address some of their "issues" in the mean time.

Input: Not much chance of beating Amy D to a new restaurant opening, so I settle for the next best thing - "Hey, you wanna meet up there?" I did hold the door open as she entered, so technically she was here first. You either have manners or you don't. 

But Karma will reward you with occasional moments, and this new Hanabi is one of them. If you're familiar with the original location on Anderson Lane, you'll walk in here, go "Wut?" and then mic-drop. It's a remarkable renovation, the interior is deceptively huge, and it has the most complete array of seating options I've ever seen - booths, tabletops, banquette, counter, and party rooms. There's also a unique section that looks exactly like Japanese sitting tables designed for Anglos. Wut? You'll know it when you see it. 

I sat at the sushi bar because I enjoy watching Chef Choo work. The Oyako app with wasabi mayo is fried and comes from the kitchen, but it's a pleasure watching a pro make your sashimi plate. What caught me by surprise here was his "Oil & Haemul" dish - I don't even know what that means, but it was stunning, beautifully presented, and a total delight to eat. 

I tend to shy away from "who has the best sushi" debates, I think it's just easier to agree on which places to avoid. So I'll put it this way: If you're up north here at the Gateway complex, with the need for impeccable Japanese-themed food and service, in a casually upscale ambiance, then start spreading the news - Hanabi has opened their doors for you.

Input: Mike is awesome!  Was welcoming from the second I stepped in.  I was the only one in there for a moment so we chatted about how he was from Chicago and has been here for 11 years and was like...that's it, Orlando needs some Chicago flavor.  Seriously, after having the staple beef sandwich, I am so glad Mike put his foot down.

I went with the regular Italian beef and subbed the peppers with onions, im a sucker for fried onions.  I also topped the amazing meaty deliciousness with a thick coat of melted sharp provolone cheese.  Score!

Now, being from Philadelphia I am a cheesesteak snob and when I compare those type of sandwiches here to the ones in Philly...mu #1 complaint is... Where's The Beef?? As it seems that anywhere south of PA they seem to skimp you on the meat so I usually end up ordering double meat.  Yes, a female ordering double meat...looks so sexy I am sure.  Well here, at What's Your Beef?  They load you up with the meaty goodness so no need to order double meat because that would be basically ordering an entire other sandwich...which actually here, isn't a bad thing.

The meat was just so tender and juicy, it had a little kick which was a nice surprise.  The roll was as awesome as the portion of meat, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.  Being this was my cherry-pop for an Italian beef, it was not as messy as I was expecting.  The au jus was perfect, moistened up the roll perfectly.  I believe I inhaled my sandwich it was so good and like I told Mike, if I was not heading out downtown, I would have gotten another one.  It was THAT good.  

I know I will be heading back to grad another Italian beef but I am also going to sample my usual go-to...Meatball Sub!!!

Their ingredients are all Chicago style so you must stop in to get this great taste of a northern city here in our awesome southern town...Thanks to Mike and his wife for opening such a great spot in DT Orlando!

Input: First off, what's not to like about this place. It has been around for a number of years now and is well-known by most of Boston's residents. Conveniently located in the Back Bay on Boylston Street, this venue is a great selection for tourists and residents alike. Whether sitting inside or outside on the patio (which often has heat lamps available), I've always had good services and great food.

For whatever reason, I have always started off with the lobster mac n' cheese when I am here. It is a generous portion with large macaroni, generous portions of lobster and a golden brown bread crumb topping. if shared between 2 people, this usually works well as an appetizer. The jumbo lump crab cakes are also a good option as a starter. With two large cakes seated on lettuce and the fresh fruit salsa, the combination of the crab and sweet salsa is excellent. In terms of salads, I would highly recommend the Traditional Hearts of Iceberg. It is a large wedge of iceberg lettuce covered with bacon and tomatoes. If you dislike blue cheese, you can also opt for 1000 Island dressing instead. 

In terms of entrees, I have always gone with a steak (of course) and have chosen either the typical filet or the Filet au Poivre (pepper crusted). I typically have the steaks prepped medium-rare. For sides, I would recommend the Grilled Asparagus with Hollandaise sauce, the Creamed Fresh Spinach, the lobster mac n' cheese (of course) or the mashed potatoes. 

The ambiance at this place is great for romantic dinners, a quick bite with a friend when shopping on Boylston or Newbury, a business lunch/dinner, or a celebration dinner. They do a great job to accompany larger parties when you call in advance and the service has never been disappointing. I would absolutely make this venue part of your steak house exploration in Boston.

Input: I would say that this place is definitely a winner winner chicken dinner! However, some kinks need to be worked out. Now, down to the nitty gritty. 

-The wait was about 15 mins to the cashier. There was a line outside of the door and a short line inside. It made sense because the area where you order is not that big. If they didn't have this system in place, everyone would be squished in a confined area. 

-We waited about another 15 mins until we received our food. They give you a buzzer and will track you down at your table which is fantastic seeing as there is basically no room inside to wait around. The only issue I noticed is that the seating is so staggered between the outside and inside, that the limited wait staff is zipping around all of these tables until they find the correct number on the buzzer. It's a good idea in theory, but having four waiters come to your table with the wrong food was a little imposing. Again, the system is not the wait staff's fault it's just the way it is until maybe the kinks are worked out.

-Now the food. I had the three piece chicken tender meal (combo) with fries and a drink. I will say that my chicken tenders were not plump and juicy. They were thin, the breading slightly brittle, and not exactly what I expected. The dipping sauces (the meal comes with your choice of two) I chose were the peri peri sauce and the garlic parm sauce. The peri peri was a warm heat that stayed in the back of the throat. It had a strong red pepper taste (like Sabra red hummus). I liked it even though I'm not a spicy fan but do NOT eat this if your stomach is sensitive. The garlic parm was sharp and there was a prominent garlic flavor. I was disappointed in the tenders; decent flavor (mainly salt and pepper and probably another spice I don't know) but not plump. If I go to a chicken Guy, I want plump! The sauce and mixing these two sauces made the tenders taste pretty good. 

-My fiancé ordered the chicken guy classic sandwich. Now that was T-H-I-C-K! It was reminiscent of a very famous chicken place's sandwich. The bun was buttery and slightly toasted. It came with cheddar cheese. We both agreed that a lukewarm square of a cheddar cheese did not jive well with a crispy and warm chicken breast. The condiments it came with (LTOP lettuce tomato onion pickle) were okay. I personally thought that the temperature differences in the sandwich kind of took away from the big bite. 

-The fries were lackluster. Reminiscent of Wendy's fries. The fried pickles were excellent--crispy and salty. The buttermilk ranch the pickles came with was creamy and definitely had a homemade taste. 

-OUR FAVORITE: the Cinnamon Toast Crunch milkshake!!!! Crunchy bits of Cinnamon Toast Crunch and a creamy vanilla base made it a sip from heaven. It was topped with whipped cream and crushed cinnamon toast for garnish. Delicious and DANGEROUSLY good. 

-Misc: packaging and branding was super cute. It's fun, colorful, and original. Other reviews show the example. Most eat with their eyes and I thought that their packaging was thoughtful on this concept. 

-More seating needed! We had to sit outside. Inside was ridiculously crowded. I think that the seating choices should have been more booth like; I noticed lots of families struggling to seat themselves at the small round tables. The place itself is pretty small though so it's hard to get around. 

-Overall, try it Guys! It's pretty good. $29 got us two decent meals with drinks and a milkshake. Fun experience.

The food was fresh and I only wish we could have ha a few more items from the menu!

Service was very good and at the end of our meal, our waiter brought out our check and let us know that Kome had taken care of the chasuke since it had taken so long to come out (we honestly hadn't even noticed since we were snacking away at everything else). I really appreciated how seriously they took their customer service and am pretty excited about the fact that our whole meal came out to $20 (for two people!!) as a result. The Food here is mostly southern home-style cooking. They have a little something for everyone. I'm a huge fan of their salad bar and fried chicken. They also have a carving station that serves Ham, Turkey, or roast beef depending on when you come in.

An added note, the drinks are included in your meal and they are self-serve so you can get refills.

THE BAD:

One of my guests had requested some shredded cheese for his salad and the staff that he asked told him they don't serve shredded cheese. They gave him a bowl full of shredded cheese from the kitchen but I was shocked to see that they didn't have it on the bar anymore. Who serves tacos and a salad bar with NO shredded cheese?

Input: After years of suffering with asthma, allergies and nosebleeds, I finally received the news that I needed Endoscopic Sinus Surgery. I put it off for 3 or 4 years, because everyone I asked about it advised me not to do it. After having the worst nosebleed  (it took an hour to control), and 2 days of nasal packing, I knew I needed something to change. 

Dr. Joshua Downie assured me that while all surgeries have risks, a septoplasty and turbinate reduction would help. I had my surgery 2 weeks before Christmas 2015. 

My recovery period was not that bad. For the first week, it's important to take all of your meds and rinse your sinuses ON TIME! The antibiotics, pain meds and steriods do a number on your tummy. But lots of soup, smoothies, jello, pudding and Icees will keep you full.

Keep plenty of lip balm. A light swab of mineral oil and your saline solution every hour or so will keep your nose moist.

After day 3, I could tell the immediate difference. It's been almost 10 months, and I haven't had an upper respiratory infection or sinus infection. I still have a runny nose associated with my allergies, but an occasional neti pot rinse and Zyrtec do the trick every time.

Dr. Downie is young, efficient, and knows what he's doing. You will love him and won't regret any treatment he recommends.

This place is one of the upscale dining spots in the Theme Park. I didn't take any chances so I made reservations for my party of 3 for an early dinner. Thank goodness because it seemed like it there was a considerable wait even though the place was not full. We checked in and waited a few minutes while they were preparing our table. While waiting I checked out the walls which are full of caricatures of family Hollywood stars. There's a ton of them so watch where you're going. Our buzzer went off and to our table we went. 

We sat in the Bamboo Room back in the back, a nice little private room. I love the decor and the intimacy of it. We all agreed that we wouldn't order entrees because we were still full from our lunch. I started off with a Margarita flight with the flavors of a Classic, Cherry, and Lemon I believe? Nothing bad about these drinks. I enjoyed them. i decided to get two appetizers. The first one was one of their offerings leftover from Thanksgiving so they might not have it any other time of the year: the Oyster and Brie Soup. I love oysters and I love brie so why not put them together? There are 3 fried oysters swimming in a creamy, brothy sea for cheesy goodness. Can you tell I loved it? The taste was very much melted brie and not like the taste of the spreadable cheese variety. Blech! I also ordered the Togarashi-Pumpkin Seed Crusted Ahi Tuna. I loved that this came with sushi-rice and seaweed on the side. Such a simple appetizer and just enough. It was very delicious.

I must came back and try an entree. Check them out!
