Input: The Clay Pit delivered really, really tasty Indian food with great service.

We ate dinner around 8:30 and the place was bustling. We ordered a ton of food. Potato bondas and Samosa chaat to start. Then, 2 mango lassis for our group of 3. 

Then for the main dishes, we tried the jalapeño & cream cheese parathas (I'd recommend passing on these...), the paneer parathas (delicious!) and the plain parathas (good too). We ate these with chaana saag (very good), vegetable mirchi curry (delicious - the best item on the table), potato kofta (too creamy) and saag paneer (delicious...and NOT too creamy which was a blessing for me!). We also ordered some jeera rice (which was AMAZING!).

Coming from Houston, my standard for Indian food is very, very high (given the number and quality of restaurants we have). So, I doubt that I'll be coming back or coming to Austin JUST to go to the Clay Pit as many other reviewers have indicated. 

But, if you're looking for good, vegetarian Indian food in Austin, I would definitely recommend going to the Clay Pit!

Input: Welcome to the neighborhood Poke Bar! Having just opened up 4 days ago, I was expecting mild chaos when I went in at noon for lunch, but the restaurant was surprisingly calm and under control. Seating inside is not very abundant (a few tables for 4 and some 2 seaters), but tables were filled with patrons noshing on their sushi/salad/rice bowls. The space is clean, modern, and has easy signage for first timers to figure it out. 

Ordering is set up like Chitpotle: stand in land and pick your size (small/2 proteins, medium/3 proteins, large/4 proteins) and base (salad, rice, nachos??, etc.) and then move on to step 2 where you pick your proteins (tuna, shrimp, octopus, salmon, etc.), and so on and so forth. It's a little overwhelming the first time, but once you get the hang of it, it's pretty straight-forward. They had a great variety of toppings ranging from pineapple, to corn, to seaweed salad, to avocado (extra $1). Sauces are also abundant and you can choose 1 or many. Depending on who is mixing your toppings, they might be heavy handed with the sauce. I had to tell the worker to stop with my wasabi shoyu cuz he just kept going and going. (My mom did not stop him and said it was a little salty because there was too much sauce.) Anyway, after you get toppings, you get ... more toppings! Toppings for everyone! And after that, at the register to pay, there are ... more toppings! I opted for a sprinkle of sesame seeds and fried garlic because, yum, garlic.

We ordered 3 bowls and they were tasty and fresh. They also have loyalty cards so I immediately got stamped for 3 bowls. (11th one free.) I will say the small with 2 toppings left me hungry after an hour. I'd advise patrons to go with medium or large if you want something more filling.

This poke brand is a global franchise. So while some things many not be within their control, I offer some notes for the business owners. (The entire staff was very nice, btw.)

-If possible, I'd invest in bigger bowls. We got 2 smalls and 1 medium and they were all in the same size bowl. Even with the small, it was hard to mix and eat without making a giant mess and getting rice/salad everywhere. Can't imagine ordering a large and eating from the small bowl.
-Possibly look into ordering sheets where patrons could mark what they want in advance so they're not holding up the line figuring out what they want. Not an issue if it is not busy, but I can see it being very slow going during a lunch hour rush.
-You may want to change your social media handles from Brookhaven to Chamblee. Chamblee residents get VERY defensive about being called Brookhaven. (I've seen the threads on NextDoor!)

Located in the new Solis Parkview condos/apartments next to Big Daddy's Burger Bar. There's a small lot in front of the restaurant and parking deck across the way. Overall, great experience. We'll be back!

The second time I went there was a 20 minute wait. Use that time to check out the menu, and the bakery in the back. 

My two gripes are the price, and service. $8 for a breakfast sandwich? This is sad-making. Also, their service ranges from bad to fine. It's hard to get ahold of the waiters occasional. HELLLOOO? Yes, I'm waving at you.

They have a creative menu with fresh ingredients. Delicioso!

Input: There are certainly more 'off the beaten path' places to get your Southern Food Fix, but Mary Mac's has a few advantages in certain situations: you're already in Midtown, you've got a boatload of out of towners and need a huge table, you're meeting people there (it's easily located), or you just want to experience a very 'Atlanta' thing to do. 

They'll keep serving that sweet tea up until you beg 'em to stop (the menu proudly bills it as The Table Wine of the South), you really can't get away without eating something fried and if you don't enjoy invasion of your personal space, the sweet lady that comes by and rubs your back may freak you out. 

If it's your first time, they'll give you a bowl of Pot Likker to try out for free. I won't ruin it  for you, and let you be surprised when you get it. 

For the most part, every time I've been here, the food is as expected. My only one sadness on my plate of Southerness is that consistently, the macaroni and cheese is not what I would expect from an upstanding meat & three. . . but watery and disappointing (see review for Busy Bee Cafe for some amazing mac & cheese). But otherwise, I've enjoyed every piece of fried okra and spoonful of potatoes I've stuffed down here.

Take out is really easy to facilitate too (you can even place an order online!) . . . which could actually be quite detrimental to your waistline if you live too close.

Input: I can eat for hours as long as I have a boiling pot of broth, a pair of chopsticks, and a metal net. 

We have been here several times for birthdays and special events. My first tip is to bring a credit card with a good limit on it. No, it isn't astronomical but you should really be willing to pay. If you are, then you're in for a treat.

First of all, I am pretty sure that they have employed the same service staff for years. Every time we have come here, I have seen the same servers. They are very pleasant, well dressed, and are fantastic in their service. I give a two thumbs up for that. 

As for the food. WOW. There might not be anything more fresh than this. When I think of Landmark, I think of fatty beef slices, cuttlefish balls, and geoduck....amongst many other things. Absolutely Fantastic. It is hard to stop eating. When you do, you are satisfied and not at all unhappy with your experience. 

As for parking. WOW. The free parking in the back is a fuster cluck. You will find your car blocked in by a dozen other cars and when you try to leave, the management calls the owners of the cars to have them move their cars for you. You can imagine that this takes a while. Meanwhile, there are normally 2-6 other cars waiting to park anywhere near. Not a good idea to try and drive down that alley way! 

Overall, for hot pot, this is the real deal. I give 4.5 out of 5.

Input: Came here a while back with 2 friends, using the scoutmob coupon (which they honored with no hassle).

To maximize our usage of it, we got 2 pizzas, the Steak and Blue and the Southwest Baja. To start off, I kinda just expected the toppings to all be thrown on like most places, but I was proven wrong as even the presentation of the food was nice, even, and symmetric. Of course that's not a huge deal if it wasn't, but it was a nice touch.

Anyways, the Southwest Baja pizza definitely was what it implied, and had black beans, corn salsa, grilled chicken, and jalapeños. It had a nice kick of spice too, but not too much for a pizza, and they didn't skimp on the amount of toppings, neither for this pizza or the Steak and Blue. Speaking of which, that the Steak and Blue was also pretty darn good, there was enough steak on it and it wasn't dry either, so it had a good flavor along with the blue cheese. One thing about the pizzas we had though was that they were really thin and crunchy; now I usually don't like thin pizza since I feel its a lot less filling, but that Maddio's kinda gave me a new perspective since it made each slice be crunchy, but not too hard. It wasn't moist either, or greasy, which shows something about the preparation, too.

To be fair, this is obviously an Americanized place, but that doesn't even matter honestly, because the food here, at least the pizzas we god, are MAD GOOD.

I'm probably coming back this week actually, totally worth the drive.

Input: This place was one of the most popular places on yelp that we saw for Portland so had to try it out! In a nutshell: I definitely liked this place (taste of everything was amazing), BUT i do think it's overpriced asian food. I would still recommend it overall but our bill was ~$85 for lunch for 4 people. Tip: Get there early, as we had to wait at least an hour for a table since the restaurant is small and it's so popular! Our orders: 

Fish Sauce Wings: 4/5
I don't like wings cause they're too much work LOL but these tasted amazing! It's also one of their most popular dishes so I would recommend it. HOWEVER, be sure to eat it with rice! Otherwise it's too salty (hence mixed reviews on the fish sauce wings) but if you eat it with rice it's really good! 

Neua Naam Tok (Flank Steak Salad): 5/5
This was my favorite dish at pok pok! It's basically steak with lemongrass/mint/greens. It's small but your mouth literally explodes with all the kicks in the salad dressing. It's good to eat with rice too! 

Pok Pok Special: 4/5
This comes with papaya salad, rice, 1/2 roasted chicken and some sauces. Chicken was okay but the sauces were pretty good and it's just nice that it comes with the rice and salad to eat with your other orders. 

Kung Op Wun Sen (the noodle dish): 3.5/5
These noodles were nice to have with the meal but I wouldn't say it's out of this world. 

Overall our meal was very delicious and booming with flavor, I just wish they gave more (amount is pretty small) or charged a little less. Still worth trying though!

Input: I've been to Krog Street Market a few times now, and this time it was a Friday night. I valet parked my car for $3 plus tip. I have been there before where I didn't have to use valet, but since it was Friday, that particular lot was packed. 

This time, a friend and I tried Fred's, and we were lucky enough to find a spot at the counter. I ordered a veggie burger and a side of the garlic fries with ranch. If you're going to get these fries, I suggest you get one order for two to three people. It's a lot of garlic, and you'll need less than you might think.

A delightful surprise: The drinks there (all bottled or canned - including glass bottle sprite and coke) were super cold. 

After Fred's (even though I shouldn't have) I went to Jenni's and had a scoop of the Savannah Butter Mint Ice cream. It was excellent and a great way to finish off a meal. 

If you're going to go to KSM for the first time, I highly recommend visiting on a week night. You won't have to pay for parking, and you'll be more likely to get a seat wherever you'd like. It's a pretty fun outing, though, and a great potential date spot.

Input: 3.5 stars rounded up because the place is really new still. 

No alcohol as of yet (I think they only opened two or so weeks ago) -- so I am excited for the warm sake next time. 

The place is all really new and nice. The one thing I appreciated was that there was very little wait time before we got started with the food. I hate when hibachi places wait to fill a table before the food starts. Only half our table was full and I saw them start tables with only one couple at them. There were no chopsticks (in their defense I didn't ask so they may have them available). 

As for the food, it was pretty standard hibachi fare. Nothing too notable in the negative or positive spheres. Prices were very fair and portions were large. Chicken with teriyaki was well done (not over cooked!). The fried rice and veggies needed a pinch more flavor (salt mainly) or the sauce dishes need to be bigger. I'm pretty sure everyone at our table had at least three refills of the two sauces. 

Hibachi entertainment was actually pretty awesome -- there was fire (woo!) and the chef was pretty entertaining in the beginning. Either we were a bad audience (not as responsive as we should have been) or he ran out of tricks because the entertainment ended in the first half of cooking. 

Their service is still in training -- they forgot to ask for dessert before bringing out final checks in a rush so we had to order it when we sent our credit cards in which made it take much longer. 

We will definitely be back to try their sushi next time and we are excited to have a decent hibachi place close to us !

I walked in, exhausted from two hours in that FANTASTIC Goodwill around the corner, expecting a quick meal of overpriced soup in an uppity atmosphere. 

Not so!

Keeping with the thrifty theme, I opted for a $3.25 "cup" of white bean chili and, not realizing how much soup I would get, the complimentary-but-you-have-to-ask-for-it bread.  The soup came out shortly afterward in a bowl as big as an average person's morning cereal bowl, garnished with crispy tortillas, with garlic bread on the size. Everything was very good.  The soup had nice spices, a nice chili consistency and tasted healthy. I was dining alone and appreciated the magazine selection in addition to the usual used newspapers tossed aside by other patrons.  I had no issues with the decor but I usually only notice that if it's uber cheesy or otherwise off the wall.  

I rarely venture into Beaverton but now I have two reasons to go back...  or at least a new lunch spot on the way to the coast.

Input: First Impression:
I had an amazing experience at Anthony Vince Nail Spa - Easton! As soon as I walked in I was kindly greeted by the receptionist's warm smile and offered a beverage from the bar....yep! The bar. This nail spa offers a full bar (though I cannot comment on it bc I opted for the strawberry-lemon infused water). 

Atmosphere:
The overall atmosphere in the salon is calming and very relaxing. The day sky mural on the ceiling, the waterfall over the sinks, and the open and organized stations create a welcoming ambiance and spa like feel. While the decor is pretty amazing, my favorite about AV's atmosphere is their ventilation system. The ventilation at this place is great! There's no nail salon or chemical smell like at most shops, and I could actually breath the entire time I was there. My second favorite thing would have to be the pedicure chairs Bc they not only massage, but they also recline. I've been to many salons but I don't recall ever going to one that had reclining pedicure chairs. 

Service:
From the moment I walked in the door I felt welcomed and catered to by the staff. After telling the receptionist I was there for a pedicure she informed me that I have the option of doing a mani-pedi combo and I would receive $5 off the combined service, so that's what I chose. AV offers a plethora of nail polish options, both regular and gel polish. While in the process of choosing my nails colors, my nail artist came over to greet me and took me to the pedicure area and began immediately working on my pedicure. I opted for the basic pedicure or the "Spa Pedicure" and the No-Chip Gel Polish Manicure. The basic pedicure includes a hot towel wrap for your feet and legs, which most salons consider an add on. My manicure was done very well and my nail artist was efficient with grooming my nails. My only qualm is, when shaping my nails all of my nails on my left hand were filed at an angle, but before proceeding my nail artist asked me if I was satisfied. I informed her that I felt my nails were shaped at an angle and she immediately fixed them. I appreciate having the same nail tech for both my hands and feet. I've been to other salons that will give you two different nail techs, which can be a pain when tipping. Speaking of tips, ANTHONY VINCE ONLY ACCEPTS CASH TIPS PAID DIRECTLY TO YOUR NAIL ARTIST, so please remember this of you decide to visit.

Overall, my experience at Anthony Vince was great! I don't want to ditch my old nail salon Bc I love them too, but I think I may have to make it a point to visit AV more often. For my gel manicure and Spa Pedicure combo I paid $73 after tax. The prices at Anthony Vince are a little higher than other places in the area, but you get what you pay for.

Input: We came to Granville Island this afternoon to do our big shop and support local businesses when we came and re-discovered The Grainry. We'd last visited about a year before in search of authentic Portuguese piri-piri (which they have, FYI) and decided it was time to restock the spice collection at home with all of this home cooking. While the shop is closed to customers as a precaution against COVID-19, the staff were extremely attentive, friendly and helpful in helping find products or giving recommendations as I wasn't sure what we needed to restock. 

I'm pretty sure it was the owner helping me out (as he seemed to do the buying for the shop) - it was awesome as he's clearly a foodie and passionate about using the best quality ingredients. He gave me about 5 different suggestions for different spices to use on steaks, beef and chicken all based on some of his favourite combinations. We tend to go for more Latin and Iberian cuisines, so it was cool getting new ideas on how to incorporate Middle Eastern and North African flavours! We only ended up buying a couple of staples this time (onion powder, garlic powder, green oregano, chiles de árbol and liquid smoke), but we're planning on looking in our cupboards and going back to restock in a couple of days with a comprehensive list.

We're happy to support small local businesses, and we're happy to add The Grainry to our repertoire. Super friendly, knowledgable staff, great selection of products with new stuff coming in all the time, and the prices are totally reasonable. Definitely check it out!

My only constructive feedback would be that, since customers can't go into the shop at the moment, to have a full list of products both on their website and available to look at onsite. Most folks may already know what they want when they come, though I think there are a few of us who get inspired by what we find! :)

There were carrots, green beans, and asparagus included, and-despite not being a major part of the course-were also cooked perfectly and paired extremely well.

Desert: My date and I shared the Warm Chocolate Cake, which was simply delicious.  It would be a sin not to try at least one of their deserts while dining here.

Summarize review: 9 Elm is simply perfect.  The wait staff is excellent, the atmosphere is simple...yet comforting, the food is nothing short of excellent.  What more can I say other than, it took me 2 years to finally come here, I hope it doesn't take me 2 weeks to come back!

And finally, it just feels good to support a local, family-owned business.

In fact, I was so pleased with my experience at Tire Man that I decided to write up a Yelp review, and when I looked at what other reviewers were saying I discovered that not only does Tire Man sell tires, they also do brakes! This was great news for me since Toyota had just told me I needed front and rear brakes at a cost of nearly $300 per axle. Tire Man came through for me again! I had called a few other places for price quotes, and all were in the $200-$250 range. Tire Man charged me much less, and informed me that I only needed rear brakes. Yes, please! I took my car in today, and in no time at all they had my new brakes installed and I was back on the road. They have earned a life-long customer in me based on my two recent interactions.

As ridiculous as this sounds, I have literally in the last week said "I love my new tires." about 5 times. Is it weird to love your tires? If it is then I don't want to be normal.

Input: The last few times I've been to Portland I go to Blue Star Donuts instead of Voodoo Doughnuts! Blue Star Donuts are donuts for foodies and people who like more sophisticated flavors. My favorite is still the creme brulee with cointreau. They were out the last time I was there, so I tried some other flavors. They make an excellent buttermilk old fashioned. So when I saw they had a raspberry rosemary buttermilk old fashioned, I had to try it! OMG the raspberry rosemary was the winner that day. The raspberry rosemary flavor was nice and bright, just liked I thought it would be. The flavor starts with raspberry and ends with a light rosemary flavor on your tastebuds. I hope they have it next time! The 2nd favorite that day was the olive oil orange cake donut. It was really moist and had a delicate orange flavor. The 3rd one I tried was the blueberry bourbon basil. I gotta say, that was the least favorite of all their donuts I've tried. The glaze tasted like sugar more than anything and the flavors were really muted. Overall, that donut was just too sugary for me. Can't wait to go there again, (I'll be crossing my fingers that the creme brulee with cointreau  and raspberry rosemary buttermilk are available!)

I'm not one to write reviews but after reading all the negative reviews before attending the concert, I want to set the record straight. All the people I encountered working at the Roseland were professional and friendly. Yes, the building is definitely old but that's what gives it character - you can't help but imagine all the history and the great music that has gone on there over the years. And the biggest misconception is the facility is not clean. I'm easily grossed out by public restrooms but can attest that everything from the restrooms to the concert area was clean. I'm convinced that the negative reviewers' experiences are due far more to the crowds they're attending concerts with rather than a reflection of the Roseland Theater and its staff.

Input: Food/Value: 5 Stars

What I like most about Genki Ya are their rolls. They are absolutely delicious, well made with a decent ratio of filling to rice. Seaweed is fresh. Everything just gives a very clean feeling when I look at the plating to the construction of rolls that are really geometrically prepared unlike places which just put together the rolls as fast as they can.

Value is also key. As Damien has mentioned, this place is great for the quality and amount of sushi they give you! If you want someplace you can go to for all your sushi needs on a regular basis, Genki Ya won't break the bank.

Some of my favorite rolls in no particular order: Volcano roll, Doomsday Roll!!!, Hawaiian Roll. 

They also do the traditional appetizers and udon pretty well.

Input: I highly recommend TFC if you're going through fertility issues. I saw Dr. Silverberg and I love him! He is genuinely there to help you achieve your dream of having a baby. I originally saw my OB gyn and had a myomectomy surgery with him to remove uterine fibroids. My scar turned out awful! Dr. Silverberg ended up having to do a 2nd surgery, but this time more minor through laparoscopy and hysterscopy to remove access scar tissues, polyps, and somehow small endometriosis. I really wish I should have went straight to TFC and maybe only had to go through 1 surgery instead of 2. After I healed, I ended up getting a cyst. I was very heartbroken and discouraged, but Dr. Silverberg helped me through it and remained positive for me. He discouraged me having to go though IVF even after all of that, and told me I was healthy enough to try the least invasive procedure, which was 2 rounds of IUI 2 days in a row and injectable medication to produce at least 2 eggs. I got pregnant on the first try with 1 baby, and I couldn't be any happier. It had been a 2-3 year process of trying, and now I'm so excited for my new arrival coming in a month that I don't even think about the surgery or the hardship that I went through anymore. Everyone at TFC was so helpful and nice! They really know what they are doing. I realized they have steps for all the procedures for a specific reason, and they're goal is to get you pregnant with a healthy baby. I also meet Dr. Vaughn and Dr. Probes (not sure if I spelled that correctly) when my doctor was out, and they were both very nice and awesome as well!!!! Do yourself a favor and see them if you are having trouble getting pregnant. I'm 36 right now, and who would have known how many more years I would have waited to get pregnant if I didn't see them. I just wish I could have seen them sooner!

Input: We first tried Vintage a few months ago on the advice of a neighbor and almost immediately fell in love with this place. This restaurant is almost always packed after 6:30 and it gives off an incredibly positive vibe: people laughing, servers whirling about, gas lamps flickering and music churning out in the background. 
    The food is every bit the complement, and the reason, for the positive environment. Pizzas are Neapolitan with generous amounts of fresh toppings. We've also been digging the Caesar salads and pasta dishes lately, particularly the lasagna, which has just the right amount of kick from the spicy sausage.
    Some yelpers have complained about the service but in the 20+ times we've eaten here I really haven't had a problem. It does get very, very busy, so take that into account if it takes more than 5 minutes to get your drinks. Overall, we consider this to be one the brightest stones in a part of town that has many culinary gems. 

Note to Kara and Mario: please, please, please consider offering delivery service.

Input: This is what a neighborhood cafe in Portland is all about! They serve standard cafe fare (sandwiches, salad, etc.), but the quality is what puts this place above the rest. When possible, they use local ingredients and herbs from their own herb garden. I know this because the owner is very hands on and will sit and talk with patrons as they come in. He also makes every effort to remember the names of those who come in. I have been there three times and he was calling me by name on my second visit, as well as my wife and son. 

They have a good selection of local microbrews and wines availabe as well as local coffee. There is an outdoor seating area that has a "kid's size" table and chairs, which makes this a good destination for parents. As a parent, a major selling point was a kid's menu WITHOUT fried chicken strips. In fact, all the kid's sandwiches are served on nutrient-packed Dave's Killer Bread. For the picky eaters, the staff will put together a "grazing plate" that can include a variety of whatever the kiddo may want to eat. 

For the quality of food, the price is right as well. To say I am a fan of this place would be an understatement. Again, this is what a cafe should be! If you're in the neighborhood, I would suggest walking or riding a bike as the parking lot is small.

Input: Spectacular!!

Been waiting forever to stop by at L'Abattoir and finally squeezed in a reservation Friday night. I was a huge PITA and shuffled around my reservation and they amazingly juggled reservations around to accommodate.

Clean decor, great cocktail list and a decent selection of wines. Did I mention great cocktail list??!?!!

Bacon brioche - reminiscent of the ones from Joel Robuchon's over the top bread cart

Poached egg and brocoli, pasta, pecorino sabayon - simple enough ingredients, execution speaks huge about the reserves of talent the chef possess.

Steelhead and crunchy potato salad - Damn right the potato is perfectly crunchy, steelhead perfectly cooked, moist, velvety, almost a smoked salmon texture, the night is definitely heading in the right direction.

Loin of rabbit - Poor rabbit had its loins cut out and stuffed with its leg meat, wrapped in bacon and served on its favorite diet of silky smooth carrot puree. Pickled radishes  and baby brussel sprouts (I detest brussel sprouts, these had no bitterness to them and were delightful little gems) complimented the dish amazingly. 

Roast scallops and potato gnocchi with chestnuts, mushrooms, celeriac - Light sear on scallops, delicately cooked, perfect sweetness.

Trifle with berries - I loved the bitter chocolate used in this, how it refreshed the palette with the citrus curd and slight bitterness from the chocolate and rum to finish the meal off.

In all, it was an amazing meal, a great testament to the chef's attention in placing wonderful ingredients that brings together great dishes and still execute each and every component to perfection.

Input: I was introduced to Boston's Fish House by some friends who know my standards. It's true, first timers will feel out of place. You'll wait in a line that doesn't feel like it's moving. It's worth it. The menu isn't pretty, and the food presentation is just okay, but the taste and quality is there. The service makes you feel like you're in a small town -- it's exceptional. The staff are on-top of every need you have -- as my friends reminded me of my high standards.

They seem to have things down to a science. Typically with fast-casual restaurants, I avoid appetizers because they usually come out with the food. They actually pace your experience. Drinks, appetizers, then entrees.

Try the food without sauces first. The fried shrimp and fish breading is very light and airy. Then add on their signature tarter and/or cocktail sauces, and enjoy.

We ordered the fried pickles to share, my friends thought they were really good, though I felt the batter wasn't adhering to the pickles well enough and they were a tad too salty. Neither which stopped me from eating them though.

BIG Portions -- Lunch is enough for a hungry man's dinner, and 2 people could easily share a dinner portion with some to spare.

Every time I've been, I've noticed the crowd is typically older (55+), with a few younger folks here and there. Sometimes I find it refreshing as fewer younger folks typically means cleaner language and behaved children (if any). I'm 31.

Some minor decor changes might make things pop better -- flooring (peal and stick laminate perhaps) and seat/booth cushions. While most of the staff don't wear matching attire, or aprons, they're easily spotted -- if they don't spot your need before you.

Input: Although we live less than a mile away, some how we had never heard of this little joint. We went as a group of 4 around 10:30 today (Sunday) and we just beat the rush even though it was raining. The inside is decked out in all old school tables and chairs and decor and they had a little waiting area with a bunch of old ovens where you could hang and get a coffee while you waited. As for food - super good! We all got something different. I went halfsies with my roommate on the Mexicali Omelet with
home fries and a biscuit, and he got the PB&J goes to France (basically flat top fried PB&J. Our table also got the Gingerbread Waffles with lemon curd and the Mediterranean scramble. Everything was very good. The biscuits were large and super fluffy. My Mexicali was like a breakfast burrito but inside eggs and the cilantro on it was a fresh touch. I'm not a huge home fries fan so I won't comment on those. The PB&J had the perfect balance of PB and Jelly - neither too overpowering. The Gingerbread waffles made us feel like to was Christmas in August but without the lemon curd to accompany it, the texture would have been a bit dry - what do you expect? - it's gingerbread! The other two scrambles also seemed appetizing as all of our plates were empty by the end of the meal. Cash only so just remember that before you come but they do have an ATM if you forget. Parking out back which could tight if it's busy. The entire staff was very nice and well organized and always on point to offer us more coffee and water. I didn't see any breakfast drinks but it's not really the atmosphere if you are looking for never ending mimosas. Most people are dressed in workout attire or just casual in general. Overall, a fun hidden little gem in the heart of midtown!

Input: Not sure how to review a boutique but I will try to share with you my personal experience shopping there. I first shopped at this Cartier around the early summer of 2011, when I was looking for an engagement ring for my GF. The sales associate, Jeannette Wong, greeted us, and took the time to introduce a variety of different options. She was extremely knowledgeable and helpful, and eventually we decided to get the classic cut of the Cartier's diamond ring. The whole process was pleasant, and we didn't feel being pushed into more expensive options at all.

What really impressed me was what happened post my first purchase. Jeannette followed up with me on whether my GF liked the ring and told me that whenever we were in this area, we should stop by and get the ring cleaned and polished for sure. We also received some informative Cartier magazines outlining their new and classic products. When we got married, we went to this store again to get two wedding bands and Jeannette had them engraved with the dates of our marriage.

Given that our home state is about 2 hours away by flight, we didn't really have easy access to this store (there are NO Cartier in our home state). However, I have been able to call up Jeannette to order some gifts for my wife, such as earrings and pendants. This Cartier store always uses Fedex next day to ship the stuff to me, so it is both efficient and secure.

Fast forward to the summer of 2017, we got a warm greeting card from Jeannette to celebrate our five year anniversary. Now that we are in a area with a Cartier store nearby, we don't have to fly to Boston any more. She introduced the local store manager to help us, which we really appreciate.

Cartier is definitely one of the more expensive brands out there. But the service of the store, the care and friendship from the associate Jeannette, as well as the styles of their offerings, all deserve thumps-up. I highly recommend this store and thanks their wonderful staff for making our experience unique and memorable!

Input: I bought my '98 Saab 900 S from Atomic Auto and had a great experience.  

After looking on Craig's List and finding the right second car for our family, I was surprised to find it was being sold from a mechanic's shop.  But I figured that's a great place to buy a car from - there shouldn't be any hidden problems and there's an actual place to hold accountable if anything goes wrong.  I really didn't need to be so paranoid.

The salesman at Atomic was super laid-back, no pressure, and friendly.  Their policy is that you can take a test drive overnight to make sure you're satisfied.  I noticed some vibration when braking and they had a mechanic go for a drive with me, then added new pads and rotors to the sale.  To top it off, my blood sugar crashed right after we agreed to the purchase and I had to leave.  We sealed the deal on a handshake and I came back the next day to pay for my new car.  They also took care of the title for me, too.  Not bad.

It's been three months and I'm still happy.  They don't have a huge selection, but they'll be the first place I check when I want to upgrade.

When it comes to glasses, I believe you should wear them loud and proudly! If you don't have some stupid outrageous prescription you can definitely get some affordable frames here. Unfortunately, it would cost me about 3 pairs of frames here for just the lenses I need. But I appreciate what WB is doing here. Hip frames for a low price without the pain of your typical optical experience.

Input: Having spent almost no time in the Gulf Coast region, I've never developed a taste for Cajun food, so when I see shrimp and grits on a menu I worry that I might be in the wrong restaurant. At Lucile's, that fear would have been totally misplaced.

The restaurant is a converted house so it genuinely feels like you're just in your grandma's breakfast nook, which will either feel cramped or intimate or both depending on how you look at it. We ended up seated at the communal table which was set for eight people, so you can make a new friend or two like we did, having a pleasant conversation with some locals about the merits of Cajun cuisine and the weather in Rocky Mountain National Park. The servers are all suavely polite, almost to the point of being smarmy, but they were taking good care of all the patrons.

The food is tremendous. We started with an order of the beignets, and I strongly counsel you not to skip these light, airy, powdered-sugary delights. My scrambled eggs were a little watery and weak, but the perfectly seasoned potatoes, savory andouille sausage, and enormous sweet flaky buttermilk biscuit more than made up for their minor failings.

Maybe I wimped out by avoiding grits or seafood or anything super spicy, but even if you go that route at Lucile's you'll wind up with one of the best breakfasts imaginable.

Input: Features Canadian artisan-made inuksuit and carvings.  I really didn't know about inuksuit and I was drawn into the store by the interesting looking sculpture of rough stones stacked in the form of a human figure.

Here's a little history: The people of the Canadian Arctic are known as the Inuit. They used to be called Eskimos, which came from a Native American word for 'eater of raw meat'. Now the Arctic people are officially known as the Inuit, which means 'the people', or singularly, Inuk, which means 'the person'.

The inukshuk may have been used for navigation, as a point of reference, a marker for travel routes, fishing places, camps, hunting grounds, places of veneration, drift fences used in hunting or to mark a food cache.

The store itself has quality art with a small section for the usual Canadian touristy stuff.  They are able to answer questions about the history and the artists.

I would return for their beautiful Canadian indigenous art.

Input: After getting Rick's (http://m8ryx.yelp.com/) highest recommendation, I knew it was only a matter of time before I made the short trek out to SE 122nd a few blocks south of Stark to give Puerto Marquez a try. I too grew up in Central Valley Cali and share his relative disappointment with the "midrange" chip 'n salsa Mexican restaurants in pdx, so I tried to temper my high hopes with a little cynicism.

All that cynicism went out the window within minutes of stepping in the front door. From the outside it's a very humble looking establishment (as are most on SE 122nd) squeezed into a little parking lot with a 7-11, a Panderia/Mercado, and a Mexican Furniture store - but once inside it's actually a fair bit larger than it appears.

They have a couple TVs, as well as the familiar painted mural walls, but here their depictions of a seaside Mexican village, complete with fishermen casting their nets into the surf, is actually relevant - Puerto Marquez definitely specializes in mariscos (multiple pages of fishy goodness). But for those of you not down with critters from the sea, they also offer a fairly comprehensive assortment of ground-bound food items and more "Tex-Mex" style dishes and combos - and aesthetically you're not left out either, as the north side of the restaurant has portraits of Gauchos and other standard Mexican-themed decorations.

Wanting to see Puerto Marquez doing what they do best, and always game for good seafood, My Lady and I both ordered up some Camarones platos - mine a la Diabla (upon the recommendation of Pablo, our server), hers Mojo de Ajo. Don't let the fact that we both ordered shrimp give you the wrong impression - their menu features bass, halibut, salmon, squid, octopus, scallops, even lobster - basically if it's edible and comes from they sea, they serve it! They've even got at least 3 different varieties of ceviche!

With mouths watering in anticipation we both enjoyed the chips (which tasted fresh and crisp, if not house-made) and to a lesser extent the salsa (decent, though pretty standard and not hot enough for our tastes), and My Lady really appreciated the bean dip, though she found it a tad too smoky - and vegetarians beware: it DOES have pork in it; in fact non-pescetarian veg-heads may be disappointed overall with the menu at Puerto Marquez, but those who partake in seafood will likely find exponentially more options here than most other Mexican restaurants.

As is common in many Mexican restaurants, the plates are huge but shallow, creating the illusion that you're getting more than you actually are - but fear not, the portion sizes on both our platters was more than ample. Taking a cue from Larry David, yes, we did count how many shrimps we each got - I got 8, My Lady got 9 - but these were very large, butterflied, tail on "jumbo-shrimp", so neither of us left hungry. In fact, these were some of the freshest, most succulent shrimps I've enjoyed anywhere in pdx!

My Camarones a la Diabla were terrific, and while it was prepared with more fire at Puerto Marquez than at many other places in town, I still found myself wishing it had a touch more heat. The spicy, red, tomato-chile based sauce was divine and contrasted perfectly with the sweet shrimp, and had no other veggies to get in the way. My Lady's dish was more of a garlic, butter, onion, and bell pepper affair - equally outstanding!

We both were really impressed by the rice - seasoned simply, with just a few tidbits of carrot and peas, and a mellow yellow color, it was way more pleasant to look at and devour than the often unnaturally orange-colored Mexican rice you find at many other places. I DO however wish they offered black beans, or at least whole beans, as I've just never been a fan of refried beans; they did let me sub in extra rice so it was no big loss.

The service was attentive, personal, and very friendly - and without resorting to the stock (though charming) "Hola Amigos!" that greets you in many other Mexican places. Pablo asked us how we'd heard of them, talked a little about their menu, and was happy to describe anything or make recommendations. They've been in business since 2000, apparently catering almost exclusively to a Mexican-American audience, but since being featured in The O and Willie Week last year, they've begun modest advertising (see their ad on pg. 18 of WW's "Cheap Eats 2009" guide) and have seen increased business from gringos and Latinos alike.

While their seafood prices are a little higher than the rest of the menu, it's right in line with (or even cheaper than) what you'd expect to pay for such fresh and expertly prepared dishes elsewhere. Really, I think the only area I'd say could be improved is to offer more than just refried beans, and maybe some more inspired salsa. Despite this, I'm gonna have to join the club and declare this one of my favorite Mexican restaurants in town!

Input: No words can completely do justice to the wonderment that is the Cantab Lounge. In a city with no shortage of generic Irish pubs, college-kid meat markets and overpriced, underwhelming dance clubs, the Cantab is a breath of fresh air (even if it sometimes doesn't smell quite as nice as that  metaphor might imply - part of the charm, right?).

The Cantab is a live-music venue for all those people like myself who prefer to drop $5 on a well-honed bar band than $30 on a over-hyped HOB show (Thanks, TicketBastard!). Its music runs the gamut from blues and country to funk and disco, but it's (almost always) live, and (absolute always) amazing.

There are two undisputed stars of the show here. Free Tuesday bluegrass is a Happening - yes, capital H. Come in, cozy up to the bar with the throngs, throw a couple bucks into Geoff's donations hat, and tap your toes away to the best fiddlers and banjo-pickers offered by the city of Cambridge (well, let's be real: Berklee College of Music). 

But for my money, there is undoubtedly no better night of dancing in Boston then the Chicken Slacks on Thursday. This funk-soul outfit brings together twentysomething hipsters, soccer moms, and a plethora of goofily grizzled barflies. Singer Diamond D is an endearing mish-mash of James Brown, Al Green, and that sketchy homeless guy that cat-calls weekend partygoers on the corner of Mass Ave and Prospect. Ladies: don't stand too close to him if you know what's good for you. (Where "What's good for you" = not acquiring syphilis).

I hear good things about the poetry slams and blues jams, as well, but I'm afraid to go, since spending four nights a week there will severely empty my bank-account and leave my social life unacceptably non-diverse. But I'll keep coming back to the Cantab as long as it offers feel-good music and an intriguingly varied clientele.

Input: Sarah Moss is amaaaaazing!!!

For myriad reasons this girly girl hadn't had her hair touched by a professional in well over a year. Cancer/chemo hair loss, a lost pregnancy, and other reasons contributed to the desperate state of my locks. 

Sarah greeted me immediately upon arrival and offered me a beverage, then proceeded to analyze my hair with her trained eye. She saw my vision of piecey layers but I needed her expertise with the color--I was going to leave it completely up to her. I have never, EVER marveled at my own hair color (I have gotten my hair colored in a salon religiously since college--20 years now--with the exception of the last year+) but she nailed it. She looked at my grown-out roots and skin tone then asked if I was okay just letting her do her thing. What I have now is a gorgeous warm chocolatey brown with a touch of red and gold. How she managed to add dimension in a one-step color process is beyond me, but she simultaneously brought out my hazel eyes and complemented my face shape while maintaining my natural summer highlights. She also gives THE BEST scalp massages In her shampoo. 

I had gotten to the point of almost dreading having my hair done in my former city with my former stylist--long and slow appointments, cold and industrial environment (going for a trendy, avant gard vibe, I suppose), lacking in basic customer service from the staff and overall experience as a whole, stylists chatting among themselves....we've all been there. 

Not only is my hair amazing, but the entire experience was a forgotten joy. It had been a while since I had allowed myself to be totally pampered. I almost fell asleep several times ("that's okay! you're not the first and you won't be the last," Sarah said) and she appropriately conversed/let me doze, taking my lead during the 3 1/2 hours I was there. Is there anything worse during hair appointment than having to entertain your stylist?

The ambiance is soothing, the entire staff is friendly, parking was a breeze (street parking at just $1.20/hour) and I left relaxed and happy. Can't ask for more. 

Thank you to ROAR! and Sarah Moss :)

Input: Max is a fucking superhero.

An abbreviated version of my home-buying experience:

After a few months of searching, I finally found a condo that fit all of my needs. I was using my bank as my lender, and made an offer on the condo, which was promptly accepted. After accepting it, the bank realized that the condo wouldn't qualify for my VA loan, and it wasn't an approved condo for traditional financing either. My bank said I was pretty much stuck with an investment loan, with the wonderful terms of 5.75%, 5-year ARM, up to 11.75%. They said that it might be possible to get traditional financing, but this would require the HOA president filling out a ten-ish page questionnaire to determine eligibility. 

Since I was three days into my option period, I started panicking. I called four lenders within the hour - Max being one of them.

After talking to Max, he said it didn't sound like there would be a problem, but he would need to check a few things.

The next day, he had a loan application ready for me to sign. He had determined that the condo was eligible based on the mailing addresses of the owners (to see if they lived in the condo), and calling the HOA president (he might have done more, I'm not sure).

Two weeks later (over half-way through my contract period)  - my bank and one of the other loan agencies STILL didn't have enough information to determine if it was eligible. They were still twiddling their thumbs, waiting on the HOA president to fill this paperwork out.

About two weeks into the process, it comes back that there's a problem with the HOA's insurance. It was an umbrella policy that covered many condos throughout the US. This, according to new regulations, meant that it wasn't available for traditional financing through Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Max immediately went to work.

He spoke with the HOA president, then his insurance agent directly, to see if this could be resolved. The insurance agent said that she could not provide an acceptable policy, after a week of stalling. Max then contacted several other insurance agents, got quotes for comparable policies, and submitted them to the HOA president. He even called the HOA president several times to make sure things were going smoothly. Without him doing this, I would not have been able to get a loan for this condo.

And, to top it all off, he extended my rate lock-in for eleven days past the original period (since the contract had to be extended) without any charge.

So, yeah. If you're buying a condo, I would definitely recommend Max. He is a badass.

Toppings were sparse but fresh and packed with FLAVOUR! Actually, I reminisced about my time in Rome while I ate my "Pizza Speciale". Settings were simple, clean and unassuming, and the sit down area small but adequate, considering the small space they're working with. I can only imagine how packed it will get (line-ups out the door?) when they receive more attention! Staff was attentive and personable. Water was available on tap (carbonated, too!) while I waited. Service was quick from ordering to presentation...10 minutes, tops! 
I have no suggestions for this place. Can't go wrong if you keep it simple!
If they go bigger down the road, I hope they maintain the rustic charm and simple recipes and they'll continue to have followers! 
When you eat a pizza like this, don't wait too long to eat it! The thin crust and toppings will cool quickly and while some might like eating cold pizza the next day, this pizza is best eaten fresh from the oven!
YUM! I'll be back soon!

Input: What do I love even more then a huge juicy cut of steak. A huge juicy FREE steak.

I was one of the super super lucky folk to be invited to the preview night at Jaspers. What does this mean, you ask. Everything. Free. I didn't believe it when I was told so I asked again. Free they said. This when on a couple of times until I finally got the picture.

I show up with my mom and sister in tow for the most expensive meal my family may ever eat. On the house.

Jaspers is an old fashioned "backyard grill steakhouse" except if the steakhouse was super posh and the food served faster then anyones uncle on a grill could cook it up. 

We began with appetizers, crab cakes, calamari and Bruschetta. Both the crab cakes and calamari were excellent, the calamari very tender, which I love and in a tereyaki sauce, but the bruschetta was to die for. Covered in goat cheese on other fabulous sorts of things, it made me slip on south beach, and thats saying a lot.

We all had salads too. Mine was a baby green salad with shallot vinaigrette dressing, nuts and blue cheese. Yum.

But the time I got to the main course I was almost stuffed but hey, I had to make some sort of dent right.

Prime Rib. OH MY GOD. Now, Ive only had amazing steak once or twice in my life ( many other times it has been more the  sirloin variety) and this was th best steak Ive ever tasted. Juicy and cut well, presented beautifully and they had these portabello mushroom "whippers." Good god in heaven.

Our waiters name was Robert and he was fabulous. And we had enough left over to eat lunch the next day.

A really amazing dining experience. Quick service, delicious food, friendly people.

Now Ill just save up enough to go back, as things are a little pricey. Tip. My sister, the picky vegetarian, had a pizza that she said was the best pizza she had ever eaten and was 9 bucks. Cheapskates...this might be your dish.

This is one of the first restaurants to open in the domain, and , trust me, should be on every yelper's to do list in the near future.

The parking space kind of sucks, but if you care about that then pay for a reserved spot...they have them. I used to live at Lamar Union, and this place is a night and day difference. I am relocating to Dallas, otherwise I would stay here till i bought a place. Also, I wanted to point out... they have 3-br's (normally college or young 20's) on the 2/3 floors. Input: A second meal at Belly Timber has added a star for me. Mmmmmmm. The subtlety in flavors and the delicate new pairings made me realize that high levels of thought and care went into making these entrees. Last night I ordered an appetizer of salmon chickpea crepes with celery and cumin. Wow! 

Since my belly didn't have the space for an enormous entree, I was thankful that dinner plates were offered in two sizes. I got the roasted pork loin with prunes and trotters, which was delectably tender and quietly amazing. As for "trotters", I didn't know what they were until after I ate the meal, and I'll leave you to discover it yourself. I might not have ordered it if I'd known, but I definitely would've missed out. My only complaint is that the brussel sprouts seemed undercooked.

My boyfriend got sweet potato gnocci, which was very smooth and satisfying, and a butter lettuce, goat cheese pomegranate salad. Yum. Before dinner, bread is served with butter and unusually flavored salts for more taste adventures.

Our service was again excellent, and one drink we ordered was very unusual: it was a Tom Collins with a Clear Creek Vodka that had a smoky flavor. The drink tasted slightly salty and had a pleasant similarity to smoked meat. Along these lines, there is a bacon bourbon Manhattan on the menu which we didn't try, but I really liked the Tom Collins. 

Again, the architecture--embossed silvery wallpaper, lovely dark wood, beautiful bar--was a wonderful backdrop to an evening of culinary discovery. I was left feeling satisfied and at the same time wanting more!

Input: We came here for date night seeking some good wine and perhaps a few bites. While my proverbial 'last meal' would be glasses of a big, spicy red and chunks of creamy pungent blue cheese, we decided to bypass the extensive cheese and charcuterie board options in favor of their full menu. 

I spent the next three days obsessively recalling the flavors of the evening. The lamb meatballs had a unique middle eastern take. If you enjoy recipes out of Ottolenghi's cookbooks, you'd love these. They were delicately moist but with a perfectly browned thin crust.

The greens on grilled bread appetizer were the only disappointment. On the bland side and way overpriced for what it was. But that was the anomoly in an otherwise delicious evening. Cyril's is being added to our regular restaurant rotation. I haven't described the great gougeres and local wine flight, but I should leave some of the pleasure of discovery to you.

Input: (Note: This is a review of the Doggy Day Camp service ONLY.)

Sometimes additional coupons are given via email or in the Pawgress Reports. I am pretty saving-savvy so I make sure to read all of them! :)

The store itself is clean and well-stocked and organized. I always get greeted by a friendly cashier or manager when I enter and leave. As for appetizers, the artichoke dip is truly amazing. It is not that gross, processed crap they serve at the chain restaurants. It has huge pieces or artichoke heart and real cheese and it's served with pieces of toasted, buttery bagel. In regards to sides, the grilled tofu, asparagus, fruit salad, mac and cheese (so good!), grilled tomatoes, and sweet potato fries are delicious. Finally, the milkshakes and fruit cobbler are wonderful. The only thing I haven't enjoyed as much is their specials. Those have tended to be overpriced and underseasoned.

Weekend mornings are super busy and you must wait for a seat, so I try to avoid going then, but for lunch or dinner, I've never had to wait. Basically, this place gives me the warm fuzzies and I leave feeling relaxed and well-fed.

Input: I think Salt Lick may have been the reason I went to Texas. 

A fairly short ride through the beautiful and scenic Hill Country outside of Austin leads you to the epic destination that is Salt Lick BBQ restaurant, winery and associated ranch. You park in a huge dirt parking lot right off the side of the road in Driftwood, TX.  When we pulled up, I was shocked by the number of cars in the lot.  

The restaurant is made up of two buildings and an outside area.  The outside area has popcorn, drinks and live music most of the time.  It has plenty of shade so it isn't too sweltering for those who have to wait to be seated. Everything about the setting feels authentic.  I came with two friends on a Sunday night and we were seated immediately in the building with the BBQ smoker.  The pit is a spectacle for sure and you should check it out even if you are sitting in the other building.  

For our meal, we were focused on the meats.  I ordered the half ribs, half brisket plate which comes with potato salad, beans and slaw.  They bring bread, pickles and onions for the table.  I will say the sides are nothing to write home about (between the three of us, we didn't finish one order of sides).  The greatness of the meat makes up for the lackluster nature of the sides.  As someone who doesn't eat a ton of red meat, I was pretty blown away.  The brisket is served in long, large strips and the pork ribs have plenty of meat on them.  

If you come with a larger group, I would recommend the Family Style meal so you can sample everything Salt Lick has to offer. It is about $20 and comes with brisket, sausage, and ribs in addition to the sides.  Or you might just want to order the meats...the sides just really aren't worth it. They also have a little gift shop where you can purchase commemorative T-shirts as well as Salt Lick sauces. Salt Lick is a Texas experience that you shouldn't miss out on.

Input: We had a wonderful experience at the Gunshow. Kevin Gillespie was there this night cooking along with the other wonderful chefs. This was an additional awesome surprise as we had heard he is not there all the time. What a treat!
We have actively been trying to get a reservation for a while now. Finally snagged a 9pm reservation on Friday night. It's was packed when we arrived but they seated us immediately.
We were not familiar with the concept but were pleasantly surprised, just think like a dim sum restaurant where the dishes that you share are coming around. The chefs prepare what you see on the menu but you don't order it. You wait for them to come around with the dishes and you either accept the dish or deny it. Pretty much like dim sum. Except not on a cart. The chef that prepared it brings it out themselves and describes it to you before you decide to keep or not.
We decided to accept the whole menu. We only denied one that thought might make us too full to accomplish this feat!
I can tell you that my husband and I are in agreement that every dish was spot on spectacular. They were very unique and even if it was a familiar taste to you, it had a twist to it. For example the Chicken Liver Mousse Split had sweet plantains and candied nuts? It was an unexpected combination but it worked very nicely together.
Our hands down favorites for the night were the Grilled Pork Belly (which Chef Kevin Gillespie) brought out himself, Burnt raw Kobe beef and the Bone Marrow. At last call we ordered a second Bone Marrow as the pre-dessert (I'll take another dish to dessert any day) to our Banana Pudding dessert. 
I won't go into describing the dishes because they change them every 3 weeks and that might crush you to go in to eat  something I describe and then it not be on the menu. But I can vouch for the fact that every single one was delicious and beautifully presented. We loved that we could ask the chef anything about the dish since they deliver the dish themselves. 
The place is very loud and it feels like you're at a party in someone's home even if you don't talk to the person sitting next to you. You will be seated at long tables and have perfect strangers next to you. But it works!
Enjoy the unique experience!

Side note:
Chef Gillespie graciously spoke with us before we left and being the To Chef fans we are, indulged us with a foto.

Input: I had not eaten at the South Congress Cafe in years, but remembered enjoying it. 

Stopped in for breakfast around 10:45 on Labor Day with my GF. The place was packed, but we were able to get on the list, were told it would be a 15-20 minute wait, and they took our phone #, sent a a text immediately confirming the 15-20 minute wait, and then texted us when our table was ready. Nice and efficient. 

We didn't have to wait long for our waiter Gabe, and we weren't ready (because there are a lot of seemingly delicious items to choose from on the menu), so he said he'd come right back, we figured out our order, and he was back in 2-3 minutes. 

We ordered the Migas, add avocado, with corn tortillas, and the Crab Cake Benedict: "spinach bacon quiche, crispy prosciutto, and potato pancake" with the chipotle hollondaise (you get a choice). 

Our plates were out shortly, and the meal was delicious. I was worried the crab cake benedict was going to be salty and too rich with the spinach bacon quiche, but it was delicious. I'm not usually a fan of crispy crab cakes, but in this case it was a perfect bite with the soft light quiche and the crispy crab cake giving a nice crunch.

The Migas too was delicious, and came with delicious home cooked tortillas. 

Service was fantastic, especially considering how busy the place was. We had one guy who was just going around ensuring people had coffee (great idea!), and a manager named Otis came by to ensure our experience was satisfactory. We told him it was a Yelp 5 star experience, and he came by again - spoke to me by name, thanked us for coming, and invited us back again. 

The South Congress Cafe is a class act. Fantastic food, reasonable prices, and runs like a well oiled machine. We will definitely be going back to sample more of their culinary delights.

Input: Studio 52 is a beautiful studio in the heart of downtown Boston featuring gorgeous vintage windows that let natural sunlight in during the day. At night, the studio has candles lit making the studio feel like a zen spa. The wood floors and exposed brick walls make the studio feel incredibly clean and spacious. Absolutely NO yoga studio in downtown Boston can even compare to Studio 52! I have visited studios in downtown Boston, Brookline, Newton, and other towns that serve wealthy clients, and by far Studio 52 exceeds in aesthetics and serenity!!

Now on to the yoga: The owner and lead instructor, Alena, strives to make every class unique, comfortable, fun, and relaxing! 
- For an energizing and physical yoga experience, I highly recommend the HIP HOP YOGA class. Alena chooses new and interesting music playlists for the class that makes you want to come back every week for a new spin on the fun techniques and new songs to add to your spotify playlist!
- If you work downtown, then you may want to try the LUNCH BREAK 45-MINUTE FLOW class to help get yourself energized and ready to tackle the stress that comes with the workweek. The lunch break class is not so physically demanding that you'll be going back to work all sweaty either!
- For those who have done yoga in the past, you know the feeling of refreshment and have seen the glow in your skin afterwards. One of my favorite classes that Alena offers at Studio 52 is the Friday WEEKEND GLOW class. You can go right after work and then go out (to a date, bar, club, or hang out with friends) with a refreshing glow!
- Along with the yoga to start the weekend, Alena offers a SUNDAY FUNDAY class to end the weekend on Sunday. This class is the best when you've either partied hard or (if you're like me) studied too hard all weekend long and need a light workout with an emphasis on detoxing and starting the week with a fresh mind!
- My absolute FAVORITE class is the VINYASA CANDLELIGHT FLOW class. Alena creates the most amazing atmosphere I have ever had in any yoga class or studio by lighting candles near the large windows (which are not facing any major building that has people who can look in, by the way). She also burns incense (not too much) that give the room a calming effect. Lastly, if you're lucky, Alena will give you a cooling neck massage during shavasana! I've only experienced that in one class at one other studio ever! It is definitely the best way to end a yoga session!
- Lastly, although I have not tried this class yet, I can infer that the PILATES YOGA FUSION class would be amazing! After attending all the other classes that Alena has instructed, I can only imagine how great of a workout and strengthening session this class will be! Now that winter is coming, I'm definitely going to try it out to work on my core and get those abs ready for next summer!

Moving away from the yoga to one of the best new features that Studio 52 has to offer is the website!! I was pleasantly surprised how easy it is to navigate and reserve spots on my iPhone! The website is designed to have everything easy to access right when you visit! NEVER have I seen a website for a yoga studio that is easily accessed on a phone (which is absolutely crazy since almost everyone has access to a phone at all times rather than a computer)!!! Now I can reserve a spot for any class within a minute!

Truly this is one amazing place with an innovative and inspiring owner/instructor to get your yoga on =)

Input: We used Cuisine Chez Vous for my daughter's wedding, which took place on Sept. 4th. Based on the reviews, and our experience throughout the wedding planning process, we expected great things from them, and they totally exceeded our expectations! We interviewed seven highly recommended caterers and did tastings with three, prior to choosing Cuisine Chez Vous, and they stood out, head and shoulders, above the rest. When we tasted their food, we were completely sold. They served us the best sea bass we had eaten in our lives, as well as to-die-for appetizers! In addition, they were competitively priced, but just seemed to put out that extra effort and enthusiasm that convinced us that they were just what we wanted!
Over the many months of planning the wedding, Walter was an absolute doll to work with. He was totally responsive to our frequent emails, and nothing seemed to faze him. He also seemed to to really "get" the look and feel that my daughter wanted at her wedding, which had a number of non-traditional and personal touches. What I loved about him, and about Michelle, is that they set their default to "yes", rather than "no". Whatever we asked for (and we did have a few non-standard requests), they always found a way to make it work, with good humor and caring.
On the day of our wedding, CCV took charge completely and made the whole affair seem seamless. As the mother of the bride, I didn't want to have to worry about or be responsible for anything during the actual wedding and reception. Michelle ran everything so smoothly, I felt like I was a guest rather than a host, and I was able to mingle and have fun with our friends and family, rather than worrying about the details or what would come next. Michelle is unflappable - that's all I can say!
I also wondered, in advance, if the food would be as delicious and as beautifully presented as it had been during our tasting. And it was - people are still telling me it was the best food they'd ever had at a wedding! There were plenty of servers too, so nobody had to wait very long for food or drinks. I loved how they used a number of servers to deliver plates to everyone at a table at the same time . That way, nobody had to wait, while their food got cold, for the other guests at the table to be served.
I could go on and on, but will only advise people not to consider anyone other than Cuisine Chez Vous! Thank you Walter, Michelle and everyone else at CCV!

Input: 5 Stars for lovely sales associates who are super helpful, not competing for sales, and are open to some light chatting as well!

I was walking by and realized that I have never actually been in a Lululemon shop, much less tried on any of their gear. I'm what the French like to call "le cheapskate" and Lululemon always seemed a little rich for my palate. But when on Park Ave, one often finds oneself feeling fancy af. 

As soon as I walked in, I was hit with the most calming of scents, essential oils and white privilege. I kid! I kid! But the oils were on point, not kidding about that.

As I perused and wondered if I was going to have a Pretty Woman-esque "We don't have anything for YOU here" moment with the sales associates, I started to notice that they had tiny sizes for miniature people (I am one of said minute folks). I have the hardest time finding winter jackets that fit my small shoulders and don't make me look like a child playing dress up. But, here, I was in a tiny shoulders heaven! I quickly grabbed two sizes in a jacket and took them to the dressing room area to try them on in front of a mirror. 

I was struggling. One jacket fit me like a glove, but being my mother's daughter, I felt compelled to size-up so it would fit me if I grow. (I stopped growing in elementary school, mind you.) I looked around with fear of making the wrong choice evident in my eyes.

And in came Catherine to save the day.

She not only offered her opinion when I asked, but she talked about the similar jacket she has and how it faired in cold weather and fit over sweaters. She helped me with enthusiasm and not a hint of judgement. (She let me shop!! Queue excited Julia Roberts gif!)

As I contemplated spending a small fortune on this jacket, I remembered that in trying to be more minimal with my wardrobe, I am focusing on buying quality clothes that fit me really well, despite a steep price, knowing that I will take care of them and wear them for many years. Plus, it was cute and I wanted it. 

Last thing I'll say- when I went to make my shamefully expensive purchase I told the man at the register that Catherine had helped me. He looked up, smiled, and let me know that they all work together (no competition for commission!). Then I commented on the oils and the woman at the other register started telling me which oils they use and we laughed about essential oils while both knowing that I would later be selling a kidney on the black market to afford the jacket I'd just bought. 

So, yeah. It's pricey. But if you are the type of person who wears things until they fall apart, this may be the quality and fit you're looking for.

Input: Had the most unforgettable experience at Ledger. Came here with my sister and her best friend on Saturday night. Our wait time was extended a few minutes due to the busy season, so once we were seated, the manager Danny came over to our table and introduced himself. Such a nice and personable guy. He sent out a few appetizers on the house that were all excellent and so well presented. We ordered a few more as well, the fried brussell sprouts were mouth watering, the salmon tartar was incredible and the popovers were just what we needed! Thanks so much Danny!

Our server was Bethany who was an absolute delight, she made sure to make every second of our experience was wonderful. She was great and such a sweet girl with a bright personality (and it was her birthday!). Her first words when she came over to the table were "Sorry about the wait - I'm going to make sure you have the best night ever!" And we did! She picked out some ciders for us to try and explained that the Chef is friends with a lot of local farmers, so most of the vegetables and ingredients used in the meals are straight farm to table. Which we love and appreciate! Hope you had a very happy birthday Bethany! 

I ordered the sirloin steak for dinner which came with fingerling potatoes and farm fresh grilled (or roasted) carrots drizzled with a light but creamy white sauce. The steak was a bit undercooked for me. It was a thick cut, so understandable. I asked for it to be cooked just a little more. Danny came over to the table again to make sure they cook the steak just how I would like it. So accommodating and understanding.

Next thing we know, the Executive Chef Daniel came over to our table from the kitchen. Kindest, most genuine guy. He personally explained the way they cook their steaks at Ledger and wanted to know exactly how I wanted mine. (We felt awful, we never do that). He makes all of the ideas for the menu come to life, and takes each and every feedback personally and to heart. We all have worked in food establishments for years, so we know a really great thing when we see it. Thank you Daniel!

To end our meal Chef sent over the angel food cake dessert plate. Which may have been the most amazing part of it all. With a note written in chocolate that read "Sorry about your steak!". And we were all in awe over it. Candied pears, home-made angel food cake, home-made sweet granola, a light and buttery spiced mousse and a fruity sorbet all on one perfect plate. Delicious!

We truly did have the best time and can't wait to go back. And the atmosphere is awesome too. THANKS ALL!

Jenna

Input: First time eating here after hearing heaps of raves.  Wasn't excited about having to wait in line (they don't take reservations), but managed to arrive and queue up about 10 minutes before they cracked the door open for the dinner crowd, so we were seated shortly after it opened.  

Our server was working with a trainee, but they were both personable and our main server was extremely knowledgeable and peppy.  Our drinks were never empty (including the water AFTER the bill was paid...always a great sign) and they were totally on the ball to turn the table, though we never felt rushed.

We started with a pimiento cheese appetizer - which is a zingy cheese spread served with celery and crackers...it was the perfect intro to the remainder of the meal!

We both opted for the buttermilk fried chicken dinner with mac and cheese on the side...I also swapped out the veggies for corn bread.  After eating my first couple of bites of the chicken, I had to exclaim that it was the best chicken I'd EVER had!  It was juicy, flavorful and you could cut it with your fork....SOOoo delicious!  It came with mashed potatoes (DELISH!) and a spicy sausage gravy that was good, but I think it would be better suited to biscuits and gravy rather than mashed potatoes.  The mac and cheese was the bomb (not the best ever, but definitely in the top 10%) and while the cornbread was a bit on the dry side, the whipped honey butter made it worth having!

I would DEFINITELY eat here again and have already raved about it to several folks!

You can tell that every member of the staff truly enjoys what they do.  From the tattooed rock a billy waitresses to the long haired boys in skinny jeans every one is extremely friendly and helpful.  When my waitress helped me select a local draft it was because she was passionate about the menu, not because it was her job.  

I have been twice now, once with my little sister who is easy to please, and once with my mother and her friend who is never pleased.  Everyone loved it!  Both times I had the bagel and lox (creature of habit) and it was wonderful.  My sister had the cheese plate and judging by the samples I filched from her plate it was tasty as well.  

If you live in Boston, Gulu Gulu is worth making the trek for, even if you have no either reason to be in Salem.  You will not be disappointed.

Input: This is one of the few coffee shops in Portland that actually does the whole 'coffee shop lounge' thing properly. Decent music not playing too loudly, a huge stack of newspapers (with some helpful clippings taped to the windows) and a fantastic staff. Input: We finally were fed up with sleeping on futon matteress and decided to go check out some bedding places. Went to Matteress World and my wife started talking with a salesman about the matteress we thought we'd like to own. Durring his entire sales speal he must have thought his teeth needed cleaning, and kept doing so with a finger nail. Yech! we got out of there. Went to The Matteress Lot and finally decided on a bed. Got it home and slept on it for a couple weeks and found it was too soft. We contacted the store and agreed to exchange it... great! but when the original matteress got back to the store, they are claiming it has stains, impossible! We use a matteress pad heater (like a electric blanket), and a matteress pad on top of that. and after a complete inspection, we've not found any type of stains on either of our pads... hum. Other than this problem, we think the store is a great place to shop, with wonderful people to do business with.

Input: My husband, toddler son and I had a great experience buying a Honda Odyssey at Curry Honda with the help of Anthony Davis. Anthony Davis was wonderful to work with. He is very knowledgeable about the vehicles, is friendly and was accommodating of my two year old son (my son got a fun coloring book with crayons from the experience) and best of all for us, he didn't pressure us, just provided us with asked information to help us make a good decision. 

I'm also including my husband's detailed write up of our experience.

We went to Curry Honda to check out the 2016 Honda Odyssey.  We were greeted as soon as we walked in the door and after a short wait were able to see the vehicle.  We worked with a salesman, Anthony Davis, who was extremely knowledgeable about the vehicle.  With Anthony's help we were able to thoroughly assess the Honda's features and how they would work for our family.  Anthony was able to answer every question we had, and was very friendly throughout the whole process.

Anthony gave us a very competitive price--they were very motivated to move their 2016 inventory so it was a good time for us to buy.  Ultimately, we went with a Honda because it was the best vehicle in the segment.  We went with Curry Honda because they gave us a good deal and because Anthony did an excellent job.

Downsides for us were that the building is a little cramped and lacking in the perks that other dealerships have in their showrooms.  Also, the business manager tried to push a bunch of expensive extended warranties and a financing package that was worse than what our bank offered.  Unfortunately, this is par for the course for car dealerships so I don't hold it specifically against Curry Honda.  I would encourage all car buyers to understand that a car is a major purchase--do your homework on financing, accessories, warranties, MSRP vs actual prices, etc. before you even walk in to give yourself the upper hand.  To his credit, the Business manager moved on and helped us to wrap up quickly once we made it clear we would be financing through our own bank.

All in all, purchasing from Curry Honda was a positive experience because they delivered where it really counted, on price and in helping us to get the info we needed about the vehicle.
