Input: It really only takes about 5 words to describe the Highball: "Big Lebowski meets Mad Men."

But with karaoke too. 

Seriously, this 50's cocktail-inspired fun zone offers up food, druink, bowling (on classic lanes flown in from out of the area), private karaoke rooms, skee ball, and classic cocktails, all in a seriously classic vintage 50's setting. 

What was the most surprising to me about this place is that these types of outfits usually only do one or two things well. They have a fun space but shitty food/drinks, or the food is good but the arcade is falling apart. I mean, really... it's hard to focus on so many things at once and do it right without taking on a corporate/regulated feel. 

The Highball does this well. While I can't vouch for the food, the drunks care way beyond what IU'd expect for a place like this. The service was always pretty laser fast and on top of the situation, and amenities were held together well. Our karaoke room was tragically tiki, but I think some people are in to that, so I can't dock them points. Plus, it goes with the classic dated style. The fixtures and décor in the rest of the joint scream old-style class. 

I wish we had a place like this in Portland. So cool.

Now, I can't disrespect an elder, so of course we do get the salad, and if you haven't tried Fungus salad, ya'll missing out! Common people, get ya dumplings!

Input: Awesome place to get a variety of Japanese "dons", or rice bowls. My cousin introduced my family to this place, and they were actually quite receptive to it! (As long as there's white rice Chinese people are happy).

We got a bunch of rice bowls - pork katsu, fish Katsu, tuna poke, and fatty tuna. We also got a variety of appetizers like the takoyaki, nanban, and seaweed salad.

The best part about this restaurant is the prices - dirt cheap! I think cheap might be the wrong word because the ingredients were super fresh and high quality, so let's just say low prices. Back in New York, each of these individual dons would LITERALLY be DOUBLE the price of here. I'm not even exaggerating; a fatty tuna don in NYC is at least $20. I wish NY would have affordable Japanese food like here - the college students in Austin are so lucky!

Service-wise, they definitely have a few kinks to work out. You order first in the front, and the worker was nice. Definitely ask him to explain exactly what comes with each don, because the tuna poke also came with a bunch of seaweed salad. You get a playing card which signifies which order you are (like 9 of spades of something). It's a novel idea but I don't think it's as efficient as a normal number system. The kitchen in the back somehow messed up our entire order (we got like $70 worth of food) and they kept asking ME what I ordered. I told them, and then they asked ME for the receipt???  I had to go to the front and ask the guy so I could take a picture of the receipt (no paper receipts here) and show the kitchen staff in the back to confirm what I ordered... what a freaking mess. Luckily we got all of the food eventually but something definitely went amiss.

The pork katsu was a bit dry, but it was a nice thick piece of pork. The fish katsu was really well cooked and had the perfect layer of crispness. I opted for the fatty tuna don and I added avocado for $1.50. For some reason they also added an onsen tamago and charged me for it, but I never asked for it?? It didn't even show up on the bill as an item but I was charged the price for it. This kinda changed the entire texture and flavor of my don so that was a bit disappointing... fish wise it was very fresh and had no gross fishy taste to it. Also I love the fact that they use real wasabi here (at least I think it's real because it has that fresh wasabi texture and taste), so +1 for not skimping on quality ingredients. 

The takoyaki was quite good actually, and you get like 7 pieces for $5 which is a great deal. The chicken nanban (fried chicken with a sticky sauce) was great as well. 

Overall I'm in love with this place despite the messy service. The food here is great, and for the price, it really cannot be beat. I hope the next time I come to Austin this place is still around. This is LITERALLY half the price of New York I'm so sad.

Input: Can't say enough positive things about this place. First off, was recommended them by a dear friend and when I first talked with them, instantly knew why.

I was in the market for a cheap car from a private seller which already is a daunting task at hand, particularly since I was doing the hunting entirely solo, and counting my dollars to make sure I could swing it! Found a 98 Toyota Camry that I liked a lot. Called Honest Mechanic to see if I could bring it in to have them look at before I purchased it but unfortunately, they were swamped and couldn't get it in for three days which didn't work with my, or the seller's schedule. So, I chatted with a guy named Peter on the phone for what was probably a solid five minutes asking him my fears of low coolant under the hood and his speculations on the potential severity of it. He didn't brush me off sounding completely rushed and annoyed I was taking his time unexpectedly on the phone, and he would even answer my crazy, totally ignorant "what if?" questions with total respect and legitimacy! As a female chatting with a car mechanic, this is BEYOND appreciated as you often get unfairly dejected right off the bat when it comes to car mechanics simply because you lack male anatomy. When I got off the phone, I thanked him and joked that we will probably chat again since my saga continues looking for an old cheap car, in which he replied with a laugh and friendly goodbye.

I ended up buying the car, and brought it in for a overall diagnostic check and look-over, which included a fluid top-off for $70-$80. A guy named Steve called back by mid-day telling me what they found wrong with the car, which was more than I was hoping it'd be, (when is it not?) but overall not bad for a 98 Toyota Camry. He gave me his personal opinion of "Honestly, if it were my car, I'd invest the money because otherwise, it seems like a gem for a nearly 20 year old car. They're hard to come by but I think you found one." It wasn't car-salesman gimmicky of "yea, come on...spend $800 at my shop" that you so often get. He even had no problem with me getting back to him after I called other shops about price quotes which, again...past auto mechanics have tried strong arming me into staying with them. Overall, he answered all my questions with patience and poise and that I'm eternally grateful for.

The added perk: about four days after getting the car back and a mini road trip around Oregon later, I got a flat due to a leaky air valve. I called them, brought it back in and Steve thoroughly inspected the tire, replaced the air valve, and rechecked all of my tire air pressures on my car and had it ready within an hour or so FREE OF CHARGE!

It's so nice to stumble on a gem like Honest Mechanic. They truly are honest and treat you like they're working on their family member's car. And you know what? Over 4,000 miles later after a roadtrip through Canada moving to the East Coast, my car is still perfectly running! That's the good news! The bad news is I probably won't find a mechanic as great as this one over here in New England :/

Go Here. You won't regret it.

Input: This is a wonderful, authentic place to go for Thai food. It's a pretty nondescript place from the outside, with only a few parking spots in front of the small restaurant. It's located on busy Austin Ave., so it can be easy to miss. However, if you're in the area and want some good Thai food run by a sweet couple, definitely check this place out. I ordered pineapple fried rice with chicken and they had it ready for me in no time. The lady had asked me about my preferred spice level (from 1 - 5). I didn't want something too spicy, so I said from mild to regular spice level. Usually when you go to Thai restaurants in the Lower Mainland and ask for mild or even regular spice level, it won't be spicy at all. This pineapple fried rice, though, had a kick to it. So be aware that they do Thai spice authentically!

All in all, it was some yummy pineapple fried rice for $13, and a good place to check out if you want some good Thai food in Coquitlam!

Input: We stayed in the Animal Kingdom Villas which were hands down, my favorite Disney property hotel thus far. I am a huge animal fan and for anyone else who is, you MUST stay at either the Animal Kingdom Lodge or the Villas within the lodge.

Nothing is more amazing then stepping out on your balcony and seeing animals. We had a balcony with a pool view that had luscious greenery abound with some animals in the distance. If you stay here, or even if you just go for a meal at Sanaa, Jiko or Boma, take a walk around the property! That's an order! Outdoors is absolutely beautiful. It is so fun going around checking everything out from the animals roaming around to the cool rockers placed around the firepit. They read stories some evenings. Also, when night falls, be sure to go to the night viewing spot and check out the animals with the night vision googles. It's a lot of fun!

The hotel itself is beautiful as well. The lobby is magnificent with amazing decor throughout. Get a tour of the AKL if you can!  There are super comfy chairs everywhere. We relaxed while waiting for a Boma dinner one evening in the couches, just taking in the atmosphere. There are some comfy chairs around an indoor fireplace which my friend actually fell asleep in front of as I was reading the story behind it. Plus, there are a couple of big balconies that overlook animal viewing areas which make for some fun!

We stayed in a Studio Villa which was huge! It had everything we could need...free Wi Fi (this is villas only), coffee maker, microwave, sink, fridge, all the mini kitchen fixens. We had our big bed plus a nice couch, table, flat screen tv, tons of space for the two of us. Plus, I loved the Animal themeing to the rooms (I will post pictures). The beauty was in the details of the room and hidden Mickeys were abound!

I loved Boma their 1 TS restaurant, Jiko their 2 TS restaurant is simply amazing, I haven't yet tried Sanaa, and Mara their quick service area is great as well. 

The pool is so beautiful! It's as if it's plopped write in the middle of Animal Kingdom---trees and greenery everywhere!

They have the usual great Disney staff throughout. I love their gift shop, as well! 

The only downfall is it's one of the few Disney Deluxe Hotels that you have to take a bus everywhere. It's close to Animal Kingdom but not too close to the other parks so there are no boats, monorails, or walking paths to the parks. However, we had zero problems with waiting forever for buses here or anything like that.

Input: I've gone to Lighthouse Seafood market for some time now. They have been my Go-to for fresh seafood. When I discovered they have expanded and opened a cafe I knew I had to try it. 

For our first visit we each ordered a Fried Basket. That's a great lunch with seafood, coleslaw, fries, and hush puppies. We were so excited to get started I almost forgot to take a picture for you. Needless to say, these baskets actually come with a little more seafood than the picture shows. Oops! Sorry. 

My husband ordered oysters and I ordered scallops. It has been my experience that inexperienced cooks can have trouble preparing both of these so I believe it's a good test if the quality of a kitchen. But really we just love scallops and oysters. 

These were cooked to perfection. If you actually LIKE to taste your seafood, this is the place for you. The seafood cases of the market line one side of the room, and the bar and cooking area line the opposite wall. You are immersed in a seafood culture. They were even watching a fishing program on the big screen TV. I thought it was appropriate. 

Back to the food. Everything was lightly seasoned and prepared expertly. I've never seen French fries cut into V shaped wedges before but I could see how customers who really like to pile in the condiments will LOVE these fries. They were yummy with and without my fav, ketchup. The server provided us with tartar sauce, remoulade, ketchup, and malt vinegar. 

It was more food they either of us could finish and we'll worth every penny. Seafood is never cheap so that should say a lot. These baskets were priced based on today's market price so I won't quote you a price. 

I've included pictures of the menu and a specials board they had out front another time I visited the market. You'll notice there are selections for the land lovers in your group. If they don't like seafood, order them a grilled cheese or a cheesesteak. :-D

Input: I know almost nothing about Columbian food but I know plenty about GOOD food and this place is far beyond "good" and in a class all it's own.  Entering the place is a little odd because you just kind of "enter" there is no hostess stand or anything.  Before you will even get a chance to think "umm what now" the friendly staff will be right there ready to seat you.  

The entire place is clean and well kept.  They have two full bars for those that like to party while they dine.  The staff is responsive and eager to answer your questions if like me you have no idea what you are ordering.  The menu seems a little overwhelming if you aren't familiar with the style of food but it's nothing to be afraid of.  

The beans are amazing, the rice is perfectly done and the addition of an over-easy egg on top only makes these staples that much better.  It's the proteins that make the food extraordinary.  The black sausage is well seasoned and absolutely wonderful.  The steak was perfectly tender and also full off flavor.  Everything on my plate was an amazing experience in it's own right.  The real gem though was the fried pork skin.  I don't even know how to explain how amazing this sinful and delectable slice of piggy was.  It was a decadent addition to the already full and complete platter of perfection.  

If you are looking for excellent food that is well seasoned and portions that will leave you immobilized then this is the place for you.  This is one of those places that you take out of town friends or family to show off Orlando.  I will be a regular here, I'm hooked.

Input: Before I moved to Atlanta in July '07, I had only visited the city twice. I knew that I would be working in Buckhead, but beyond that, I didn't know a lick about Atlanta's neighborhoods. I know that everyone loves to rag on Buckhead (which is why I chose it for my 100th review), but for me, it has been a great place to live. I have a short commute to work, my cost of living is reasonable, and I feel safe despite the lack of walkability in this uptown 'hood. 

No, I don't shop on daddy's dime and no, I'm not a Buckhead Betty. In fact, I work next to Lenox and Phipps but I can't even tell you the last time that I was at either mall. However, it's pretty cool to think about how many upscale boutiques Buckhead has, and it's impressive that they do more than 1bn in sales each year. Buckhead offers easy access to MARTA (which is only good when it comes to getting to the airport and Braves games), has quite a few nice hotels, and more than a handful of good restaurants. I love Chastain Park and its Amphitheater, the Buckhead Library, and our two movie theatres. 

Yes, Buckhead Village and its dive bars encourage post-college debauchery and a delay in entering adulthood, but that's a choice. I've realized that there is no such thing as a neighborhood that has everything.  Buckhead isn't known for its night life for anyone over 25, but I've come to accept that. For now, Buckhead shows promise of things to come (Streets of Buckhead, Buckhead Greenspace) and I'm happy to call it my home.

Input: I went to Gaslight last Friday night for the first time and I cannot say enough good things about it. It was my boyfriend's birthday so I wanted to take him out and try somewhere new to celebrate. We had a reservation for 8:45 and the restaurant was pretty packed when we got there. Originally we were seated at a two-top that was in a pretty crowded row of people with very little space. Normally I'm not one to complain about where a hostess seats us, but since we were celebrating a special occasion I was being picky and decided to go up to the hostess stand and ask for a different table. I told the hostess that we didn't mind waiting at the bar until a bigger/less crowded table became available and she was super nice about it and actually ended up having a perfect table for us!!

After moving tables, we started to look through the menu and wanted to know everything (we are never shy to bombard waiters with questions and ask for recommendations). Our waitress was Tanya and she was EXCELLENT. She knew everything about the menu and walked us through what everything was and helped us to order. We started off with a meat/cheese board (it was a little pricey at $34 but SO worth it and everything on it was incredible) and then we tried the escargot, which was also delicious. For dinner, I order the chicken and my boyfriend got the pork chop. The chicken was so juicy and came with this sauce that I would literally bathe in, it was so good. The pork chop was massive and my boyfriend couldn't stop raving about it.

By the time we finished, we were so stuffed so we decided to pass on dessert. I had casually mentioned while Tanya was over at the table that it was my boyfriend's birthday (but never went up to her and asked her to bring something over for it) but she surprised us with a creme brulee and a birthday card from the staff at Gaslight completely free of charge. It was such a pleasant surprise and a lovely touch, not to mention the creme brulee was out of this world. 

I rarely write reviews on Yelp but I felt compelled to after my experience at Gaslight and I will DEFINITELY be returning!!!!

Input: I am giving this place  5-stars for the entire fast paced, loud, interesting, experience. 
   Located in Boston's North End, it's nestled in the middle of the busy streets dotted with Italian shops and restaurants. It's pretty tiny, casual, and loud when crowded. 
   We arrived to find a line out the door at 6:15pm on a Saturday night. Even in the rain, we decided to stick it out and see it through. We had a feeling it would be worth it. And we were right. 
   The line would move up from time to time and once we got closer, a woman would come out and ask how many were in your party and to please form a single file line. We joked around that she was very strict, because she was. Maybe that was part of the charm here? 
   We finally found our way inside after an hour. We sat where she told us to. It was right next to the very loud and busy kitchen. So loud in fact it was difficult to talk at times. Also, the place had so much hustle and bustle that for me, it was difficult to relax at first. 
   We ordered our drinks and they immediately wanted to take our meal order. I realize they have a line out the door but I don't like to be rushed. But with their huge popularity I guess they don't have to worry so much about stuff like that. 
   So we ordered the Caesar salad, chicken parmigiana, lobster ravioli and a spicy fusilli pasta with lobster and shrimp. Everyone at the table agreed the food was absolutely some of the BEST Italian we had ever had. And we hardly ever say that. Seriously. 
    If you can overlook the busy, loud atmosphere and service, and are looking for a phenomenal Italian meal, this place is for you!!

Input: after an amazing first experience at tresca, my boyfriend and i decided to book table 77 (the bourque's personal table) for our 2nd anniversary dinner.  we arrived a little early for our 6pm reservation and were seated promptly.  we had perused the website beforehand and decided ahead of time that we were interested in doing the chef's tasting menu, along with the wine tasting.  a little pricey ($240 without tax or tip), but it was an important celebration and we knew we would not be disappointed.

i've done tasting menus before and, in my experience, they are typically items that are NOT on the menu, and allow the chef a little room for creativity, and some surprise for the diner.  tresca does things a little differently.  these are items that ARE on the menu, but entirely at the chef's discretion.  our waiter did ask us if there was anything we particularly loved or hated, so that the chef could make informed choices.  we're pretty open to everything, so i thought we would be pretty easy.  what i was not expecting was that we would actually receive entirely different meals; we each received a different dish for all courses, except dessert.  this was a welcome surprise, and allowed us to share different tastes.

appetizer for the lady: sliced bistecca with pesto and arugula salad.  the steak was cooked to a perfect mid-rare plus, and the salad was nicely dressed.  the pickled red onions were a good addition, and the pesto had a great zip to it.
pasta for the lady: spring risotto.  the risotto had a lovely touch of lemon in the background, and the asparagus and mushrooms played nicely together.  the rice was slightly al dente for my taste, but the flavors were quite good.
entree for the lady: veal milanese with black garlic vinaigrette dressed arugula.  the veal was delicious and, while i typically do not indulge in fried foods, this was light, crisp, and perfectly cooked.  there was no grease or heaviness in sight.  the arugula had delicious flavor and added a nice counterpoint to the veal, but- it was my second instance of arugula for the night.  i happen to enjoy arugula, and, like i said, the dish was wonderful, but i was a little surprised at the repeat of a featured ingredient.

appetizer for the gent: fried oysters.  OMG.  this was my favorite bite of the entire night.  the oysters were HUGE, i loved the little bibb lettuce addition, and the pickled/sweet element was lovely.  this dish is so perfect, i would encourage you to order it; you will not be disappointed.
pasta for the gent: fresh papperdelle with bolognese.  this was a knockout and, i have to say, my man very much appreciated the absence of the usual dollop of ricotta (he's not a fan).  the pasta was perfectly cooked, and the sauce was rich and deep.  this was a very hearty dish, right up my guy's alley.
entree for the gent: braised short rib over potato gnocchi with brussel sprouts.  first off- we've had the short rib before and it's to die for.  never mind not needing a knife- you don't even need a fork; you could eat these with a spoon.  the gnocchi were not the kind i'm used to; these were smaller and slightly crisp, which provided a nice textural element to the succulent meat.  the brussel sprouts were easily some of the best we've had.  they were practically charred and just awesome.

for dessert, we were brought a plate of tiramisu, along with partial cannolis filled with plain ricotta, chocolate, and lemon fillings.  the plain ricotta was bananas good.  i mean- i would have been happy with a bowl of the filling, it was just so light, creamy, and sweet.  the lemon was a nuance of flavor without hitting you over the head.  the chocolate was also quite good.

our wine pairings were good, though a little unusual.  we were started off with a moscato, which surprised me a little.  we had a montepulciano that was delicious!  dessert was served with an aperitif (i can't recall which) that was... different.  i wouldn't order it again; though it did satisfy my desire for surprise, i didn't think it married particularly well with the flavors of the desserts.

our experience was absolutely lovely, between the food and the warm and welcoming service we received.  our waiter was prompt and professional, the manager was attentive, and one of the owner's was absolutely glowing with pride and pleasure that we had chosen the restaurant for our celebration.

i can't recommend this restaurant enough if you would like to feel special on your own special occasion.

and, yes.  that same night we made a reservation for next year too.  ;-)

Input: I've been going to Austin Dental Spa for about 10 years. I had a major fear of dentists as a result of traumatic childhood experiences with military dentists so I'm always wary of new dentists.  From my very first visit, Dr. Mark and the hygienist put me at ease, enough so that I have never been to another dentist.

I've had a lot of stuff done over the years, so I can vouch that Dr. Mark does excellent work both routine and cosmetic. And the best part is he warranties his work for 5 YEARS!!  I think they've actually lost some money on me because of the 5 year warranty. haha

Everything is very high tech (digital x-rays, water laser drill, the machine that makes crowns while you wait) and they are very generous with the nitrous oxide. They usually offer it to me as soon as I sit down in the chair (even if I don't need any work done that day!) and they are happy to turn up the nitrous and turn down the oxygen when I request it (which is most of the time haha).

Everyone who works there is really personable and they remember details about your life even if you only see them twice a year. Amanda at the front desk is super sweet. I've had lots of "emergencies" come up over the years, and Amanda always finds a way to fit me in the same day.  My hygienist Candice always remembers my vacations and that I prefer one massage therapist over the others.  

Dr. Mark's chairside manner is amazing. He tells some stupid jokes but they are funny for the most part. Even if your teeth are a mess, he has a way of making you feel good about things.  He has such a positive outlook on life that you'll feel happy even after he performs a root canal on you. 

The only thing I don't like about Austin Dental Spa is the music they sometimes play ...but with enough nitrous, I hardly notice the crappy tunes.  :)

Input: Frankly, we're so happy to have an Indian market in NE Portland that they probably could have overcharged us and called us ignorant yuppies and we would have smiled.  Instead, they were friendly and very helpful -- and very obviously a family business!  They saved their yelling for each other.

Namaste Bazaar is 1/2 Indian street food deli, and 1/2 Indian market.  The market is medium-sized, consisting of four aisles of groceries and a back wall of freezer cases.  Like most isolated ethnic markets, most of their stock are items which are dried, canned, or frozen.  They carry little produce: really just a handful of herbs, and a strange selection of low-quality produce sold "by the bag" dirt-cheap.  On the other hand, if you need to buy 5lbs of fresh ginger, this is where to get it.

Here's what the market has lots of:

* dals (legumes) and grains in bags from 2lbs to 10lbs, three different brands and probably 13 different kinds
* basmati and other Indian rice in bags up to 50lbs, maybe 20 different brands
* "masalas" (spice mixes) for every Indian dish you ever heard of, and then some
* enough different chutneys in jars to induce option paralysis
* an entire aisle of Indian snack foods in bags
* a half-aisle of Indian cosmetics and soap
* tons of frozen foods, including complete foods like kati pouches, ingredients like pre-made vada and idly, and breads of various sorts

One of the few things which was surprisingly scant was raw spices.  Anyway, the shelves weren't quite full, and I suspect that as the business matures (they've been open less than a month) they'll fill them up with more goods.

The deli is basically Mumbai street food as far as I can tell.  It's entirely vegetarian, and consists of around 12 different options, many of them fried.  The deep-fried spiced cheese (Paneer Pakoda) was especially good, as was the Tika Chaat (fried potato patties covered in chick pea curry and "salad").  And the chai, as is proper, is free.

So we got two big bags of groceries, and enough take-out for the two of us to make pigs of ourselves, and paid $77.  So this is a great place to come if you want filling spicy food on a budget.

Looking forward to many more visits.

Input: Bella is the Bell of the town!

Since moving to the area, a couple weeks ago, I have quickly become a regular at Bella.  They are tucked away in a cute plaza off Butner Rd, in the Camp Creek area.  It is a quaint space with nice ambiance and some really good customer service.  You can tell they value their customers patronage and that is something makes me a repeat consumer.

Dishes that have become my go to's are their Lobster Tails that I couple with the Kale & Smoked Turkey.  The Lobster Tails can be ordered two ways steamed/sautéed  or fried.  I get mine steamed/sautéed because you can really get the full experience of the Lobster that way.  The Kale is so tender and cooked to perfection.  They aren't bitter and can really be eaten on its own it's that good.  I can only imagine how they taste coupled with their Sweet Potato Corn Muffin...mmmmm.  

For breakfast I definitely recommend their French Toast, Bacon, and Creamy Grits.  The French Toast aren't too eggy and not too dry there are just right.  They only give you one slice but for me that's all I need when I marry it with the bacon and grits.  The grits are so creamy and flavorful.  It's so rare that I don't have to add salt and pepper.  The chef properly seasons the grits and adds just the right amount of cream and cheese to them where it's a happy marriage of all the ingredients. 

Overall, I recommend this spot for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.  Oh, and they have some of the BEST mixologists in town so if you wanna wind down your day with a delicious craft cocktail then this is the spot for you!

Input: My partner and I came to Rosa Rosa for breakfast on Christmas Day, expecting it to be crazy busy. We had made a reservation the night before in preparation. Surprisingly, there weren't too many people. We were the second pairing to arrive and we got free choice of the tables.

The atmosphere in Rosa Rosa is elegant and refined, but there's no pressure put onto the guests to look a certain way. The servers bring you a pitcher of water (which is the best at a restaurant) and every person working there is very friendly. We got the brunch menus, which do change semi-regularly (we found this out once we arrived since we saw different items on the menu in a yelp photo). Many items on the menu looked delicious, but my partner and I decided on the eggs benedict and spaghetti pomodoro. Both were brought out fairly quickly and had perfect portion sizes. We shared each other's plates since we both wanted to try each dish. The eggs benedict was cooked to perfection, the bread underneath being just crisp enough to not become soggy from the hollandaise. Input: I commute past Giulia twice a day and watched with excitement before it opened last winter. I finally went last summer to celebrate my birthday and have been back three other times since--most recently to celebrate my birthday this year and sit at the pasta table.

I've never been the slightest disappointed with anything here. The food is all so fresh and delicious--not the extremely heavy Italian food you might have in mind. Ingredients are all as fresh as can be and the pasta is cooked to perfection. As with others, I highly recommend the parpadelle dish and we had the most incredible sweet corn ravioli when we booked the pasta table. Their desserts are amazing--the chocolate terrine is probably my favorite dessert I've ever had (it hits the salty/sweet notes perfectly). Portions are perfect--not so much that you want to die from being so full after but plenty to leave you sated.

The pasta table is also wonderful for a special occasion--we were a group of 12 (although I think you could definitely fit 14 if you were willing to be a bit tighter around the sides). Everything was served family style, which worked well for picky eaters (to avoid things they didn't like). There was an appetizer course with a big variety, then a mix of antipasti, two rounds of pastas (with two pastas in each round), a wonderful lentil, rabbit, and sausage main, and a variety of fabulous desserts. We did a wine pairing which was nice and the sommelier did a great job of explaining interesting things about each of the wines. It's not cheap but it's a once in a lifetime experience. The chef/owner came out twice to chat with us, which was really nice. We couldn't believe when we left that we'd been there for four hours! It was such a fun evening. They are also great about accomodating allergies.

The decor is both casual and relaxed but still thoughtful and charming. I love coming here and look forward to coming back many more times (perhaps even just for dessert at the bar).

Input: Wow. While not strictly Napoletana pizza, it's a really great iteration of wood fired pie.  I was impressed by the owner's dedication to the ingredients and the craft.

I had the Bolognese pizza.....not for the faint of heart as the chef is heavy handed with nutmeg......but this was a wonderfully welcome expansion of a classic Bolognese sauce.

(BTW, I'd only recommend eating pizza *here*.....otherwise anticipate a soggy pizza)

The wine offerings were solid and my pizza paired beautifully with a Willamette pinot noir.

For what puts this place to five stars.....the ice cream.  Really.  I tried three: bay leaf; farro; potato. The bay leaf ice cream was beautifully balanced with prominent notes of pine and a sweetish-lime flavor. The farro tasted of toasted cereal and cream.....perfect on a chilly day. The potato was subtle....you had to wait for a very soft potato/starch flavor....the texture was just a nick off as it wasn't as creamy as I would anticipate, but really nice nonetheless. 

I'm glad the hotel recommended Nonavos....I'll definitely be back whenever I'm in Vancouver.

Input: Oh, the Roxy ... looks like a dump from the outside but it's one of the best bars anywhere.

I started going here years ago when I visited Vancouver and it's always fun.  

The first thing we think of for the Roxy is the band.  I've seen the same band most nights -- thin male bassist, shaved head guitarist and short brunette lead singer.  They sing EVERYTHING and it sounds amazing.  Two of my favorite covers they did were U2's One and The Outfield's Your Love.  I still remember that and they're a cover band.  They are so talented.  One of my coworkers said they'd make a great wedding band ... but then nobody would leave your wedding because they'd want to hear the next song.

There are two bars so it's convenient.  The crowd is mixed from 20s to 40s at least.  We've seen the Canucks' opponent here after a game and the girls flock to them.

If I had one issue, it's the music is always super loud.  I try to stay in the back because I'm concerned about my hearing but it tends to be loud.  No one wears ear plugs because it's not cool but I couldn't go here every night or once a week if I lived in Vancouver because of the noise level.

Input: This is a wonderful place for a nice casual dinner with friends.  It's beautiful setting - surrounded by mature trees that border a small, modern strip mall.  But, it's nicely laid out so that it blends in well with the surrounding area.  It's a handsome, one-story brick building.  There is a nice outdoor patio in the front and upon entry, the casual but relatively dark interior indicates that you are in a very classy place.  The bar is lively but still very classy and the dining room is also a gorgeous place with superb ambiance.  We were really impressed by all the staff - all were enthusiastic about their food and drinks and were so very friendly and helpful.  We were especially impressed by the manager on duty, Janna and our server, Andrew.  It was very obvious that Andrew knew their food, menu, ingredients and preparation methods.

We were here once before as part of a larger party and we were very pleased with that visit.  So on our next trip to the Portland area, we wanted to come back on our own.  So, that's what we did and we were rewarded for our efforts.  It was weekday night about 8 PM so it wasn't terribly busy.  The benefit for us was that we were able to visit with the staff and learn all about the menu offerings.  Andrew was very helpful and in the end, we both had fish entrees.  During our relaxed start, my wife ordered an Old Fashioned cocktail.  Not many places make a good one but she really liked this one.  That was a great start!

I started with a cup of Turkey Curry Cream Soup, recommended by Andrew.  While it sounded kinda odd, it was delicious!  I ordered the Parmesan Encrusted Snapper.  She had the Grilled Steelhead.  My Snapper was perfectly done and it was good portion of fish.  It was fresh and real bargain at only $17.99.  My wife was also impressed with her Steelhead.  It was just $22.99.  We finished by sharing a Berry Cobbler with Vanilla Ice Cream.  It was truly a superb dinner and it was a flawless  performance by Oswego Grill.

We highly recommend this, unequivocally and for anyone and everyone!

Jim

Input: So, check this out: I'm not Vegan.  Nowhere near. As a matter of fact, I'm probably the farthest thing from it. So... why am i here? My wife is flirting with the idea of becoming fully Vegan, and our foray into Portland quickly became a tour of the Vegan underbelly with yours truly being pulled along for the ride. This was our first stop, and she dragged me here kicking and screaming. I walked out of this place full, satisfied, and not craving a cheeseburger in the least bit. Seriously. 

The food here is fantastic. We had the Mac n' cheese, the pierogis, the bibimbap, and the wife had the cheesecake for dessert. The Mac was creamy and rich, the pierogis were toothsome and reminiscent of a potsticker, and the bibimbap was by far my wife's favorite (not Dolsot, mind you, but still quite delicious). My wife tells me that the chocolate swirled cheesecake was clean, smooth, and sophisticated (her word).

My best Vegan food experience prior to this place was The Ravens restaurant in Mendocino, which is nowhere near as tasty and seriously twice (or in some cases, three times) the price. If Vegan food this good was consistently available at more places across the country, I might consider making the switch. MIGHT. All kidding aside, though, I was seriously impressed with this place and would be fully docile and cooperative if my wife wanted to take me here again next time we're in Portland. Peep it.

Input: We've been to Uni a few times now and every time it's been excellent. Drinks are always enjoyable; loved the Swizzle Smith - came in a pineapple glass with crushed ice which is always an exciting touch. (I'm a sucker for kitsch). The ramen was out of control and we can't wait to try it in the winter. The Mongolian beef was perfect and the gnocchi in the dish was like small pillows from heaven. I would eat a dish with just the gnocchi. Surprisingly the Sake Nigiri was one of the tastiest bites of all the raw seafood we had and it was the least expensive at $9. The Uni was exciting. I've had it before but served warm, so this had a completely different texture and taste. I'll admit I'm not usually an adventurous eater and usually have to have several drinks in me before trying something like uni nigiri. Loved it! It was my fiancé's birthday so I got him a surprise dessert - the Buttermilk Chess Pie. I'm not one for sweets but this was awesome. Slight punches of sweetness balanced out perfectly with the peaches and caco nibbles. Service is always excellent. We arrived early so we stopped at Sonsie for a quick drink where they had 9 employees huddled around the bar chatting and we couldn't even get our check (after asking for it) so we had to physically interrupt a personal conversation to thrust over our credit card to pay. This would never happen at Uni - the moment a plate was empty it was gone. Drinks 3/4  done, you're asked if you would like to order another. 10/10 recommend and can't wait to go back again. Extra points for the weather being perfect and while that had nothing to do with the restaurant it certainly added to a lovely evening.

Input: This is a great local place for fabrics, in a cool little white stone house on N. Lamar (across from Central Market). I wanted some silk for my wedding dress and flowergirl dresses and was overwhelmed (in a good way) with their selection - floor to ceiling dupioni silk for $15/yard, in every shade imaginable. She advised me that the higher-quality silks from India (which is what they carry) is not formadehyde treated before shipping, plus its a natural fiber. The only downside is a long shipping distance from India; but I was very happy with my purchase. My sister made my entire wedding dress for about $75.00 with the silk we purchased here. 

They also have an incredible selection of buttons of all kinds wonderfully presented in little baking tins in the glass case. 

My only suggestions to Silk Road would be to carry more organic fabrics (they have a limited amount), like hemp silk and more organic cotton and linen. Most of the linens they had were a blend of synthetic material and linen. Also, they don't have much in the way of notions or patterns, so do your catalogue-looking and zipper buying somewhere else before coming here. They also have many many catalogues of fabrics to help you look up what you might need for special orders.

Input: Some places like to experiment and do unusual preparations, and then get so caught up in the idea of "I CAN MOUSSE THAT!" that they forget to actually make, you know, GOOD food. 

Roe is not like that. Yes, there were savory panna cottas, a German style octopus preparation (out of this world), and various other unique ideas that showed the the chef was both having fun and very very good at what they do, but at no point did the flavors or overall concept of the dish get lost. That, more than anything else, really impressed me. You have to go in with a bit of an open mind, but you will be amply rewarded. Additionally, on the tasting menu, you get at least a couple of options to choose from for each course, so you can easily find SOMETHING there that will please you.

In addition to the great food, I can't talk highly enough about the service. We ordered the wine pairing, and the gentleman that explained the wines did a great job. There were a few things that stood out. First, he clearly knew his wines. He knew where they were from, he knew the tasting notes, etc. In some places (read: most of Portland), this sort of knowledge can lead to arrogance and condescension. However, he would explain the wines to us and then make some joke. For example, at one point he stopped and said "how's this level. Too nerdy? Want more information? What do you think?" I really thought that was great, and set a very good mood for the place. Additionally, he would not only explain the wines and the tasting notes, but also explain WHY they were selected for a particular dish. Specifically, he'd talk about why he thought which flavors of the wine paired well with which flavors of the food. That sort of connecting the dots was really interesting. Finally, we unfortunately did not understand that the dinner would be a bit of a time commitment, so we had to leave early. You could tell that it was very unusual for them to do so, but the waiters very kindly and graciously helped us box up our desserts so we could get out the door. They never made us feel bad or made us feel like we were putting them out, which was really fantastic.

Input: If you are a parent to small children, you know that most "play" places in Portland fall into two categories:
A) Places kids like, and
B) Places kids don't like.
Do you know where YOU fall in the picture, as the parent? NOWHERE. It doesn't matter if you like the place or not. You just need like one solid hour of surfing iPhone for Pinterest recipes, amiright?! Laydies? Anyone?
So, I have two boys. They are currently 4 and ~3. (Yeah, REALLY close in age... that first year was a doozy. I don't even remember it.)
THEY love Play Boutique. They love all the little cars you can "drive" around. They love the huge, new-park-grade play structure. They love the bounce house. The kitchenette. The train table. ALL of it.
But you know what? *I* love Play Boutique too. 
Yes, this place falls into the illustrious and mythical category of "Places We All Like." Even my husband likes it. Can I stop beating around the bush and just tell you why?
A) It's clean. The play area is clean. The bathrooms are clean. The cafe is clean. Lobby. Etc. Not musty-germ-smell-indoor-pizza-place "clean" but Clorox Wipe Worship clean. I can support that.
B) There is ALWAYS seating. Inside the "arena" (which is encased by a half-wall) there are benches and chairs for Mommies who need to be hands on (or are "helicopter" parents... no judgement. Well, kinda judgment: give the kid some space, he'll figure it out. But then again, what do you care what I think, you don't know me.) There is also seating APLENTY, around the outside of the half-wall.
C) Good coffee. Like that brand "ILLY" that always makes me think of skinny Italians on mopeds. And you can drink it there, while watching the kids. Not like some places where you have to set it on a special ledge and sneak to and forth for lukewarm, unsatisfying sips.
D) THE KIDS LOVE IT. I know I said this before, but "kids love it" falls into its own sub-categories:
  1. They "like" it for little 5-10 min increments, in between which they have to come and whine to you about something, declare their boredom, try to get your attention, or convince you to leave, after which you have to rile them up / threaten them into staying. (Not Play Boutique!)
  2. Places they like so much, they will LEAVE YOU ALONE for the entire two hours, and have to be convinced to come home with you, by being shown evidence that all the other kids are also leaving. YES Play Boutique! This, right here, is why I think $7 is worth the play. Because every other place is at least $5, and my kids do D-1 (see above), and for that extra $4, I can actually relax, keep an eye on the kids, and look at my phone. (Isn't that all we want? To look at our phones? Oh, don't even pretend otherwise, I will call BS RIGHT NOW on whatever pretentious lie you're about to tell. Look at your phone. Looks like you have a "like" on the pic of your cute kid you just posted. You know you wanna look. At Play Boutique, you can do so... leisurely.) 

The only thing I would change is to make the play time earlier, rather than the current 10:30-12:30. However, I'm sure this isn't some crazy nouveau idea the business has just never thought of... there is some reason for it (they have a preschool there, etc.). And now that my kids are post-nap age (booooooooo! booooo to no naps!), it works for me.

I've never bought anything other than coffee there, but I know they have food. Truthfully, my kids wouldn't stop playing to eat, and why the eff would I make them?! I see in some of the reviews that mommies think it's spendy. Maybe it is. But can I suggest something to all y'all mamacitas out there?... if you have a problem with something at a small business, reach the owner and voice your opinion. They WANT to hear from their customers. (To the person who was bragging about putting "dirty" shoes on in the infant crawlers area: beyond disgusting... and shameful. How about calling and asking them to put a bench near the cubbies? Gross.) Leaving negative reviews that may prevent a business from succeeding more quickly (or at all) does NO ONE a favor in this case. It's an indoor play spot... which we NEED. 

One more tip: Groupon / Living Social/ Sharing Spree "deals" are to help businesses gain exposure and develop a customer base. I'm always surprised at how entitled some of the people with social deals are. This is a BUSINESS. Be respectful. You don't have to keep coming back if you don't like it, but stop treating the businesses you buy groupons for, like a Walmart. Ok, go to timeout and think about what you've done. Mommy needs to read a blog... "read" = drink, "a blog"=wine.

Input: I've overhead Brian say to prospective customers, "All I need is one time, then I gotcha hooked!" Boy is he right about that. I absolutely love this food cart, and frequent it (probably 3 times a week, there, I said it) when school's in session. 
The brisket is pretty good, but nothing to write home about. The pulled pork is where it's at; I recommend getting it with both spicy mustard and spicy BBQ sauce on top. Juicy, tender, big flavor, the pork hits every note. The macaroni salad is also phenomenal, and I--in literally every other instance-- absolutely dislike macaroni salad, and can't stomach more than a bite of it. Not too much to say about the rice except for that it's tasty as well! 
Overall, it's the best BBQ I've had in Portland; 5 stars, grade A, highly recommended!

Input: Having moved to Austin not six months ago, I was really worried about having work done to my car because mechanics are always painted as bandits and I had absolutely no idea where to take it. Luckily, I have AAA, who recommended me B & B (as they are a AAA certified garage).

All the guys at B & B were SO amazing to me. I came in pretty frazzled and displaced by my whole car situation (I had gotten in a fender bender a couple of hours prior that then caused my car to die in the middle of the highway), and I feel as though they really did everything they possibly could to make me feel at ease about it.

As I had suspected, it turned out my radiator was cracked pretty badly and had to be replaced. Once we settled all my paperwork and everything, I went out to my car to grab my book while I waited for the results of their inspection, and a few of the guys went out with me and popped the hood right there and quickly identified/actually showed me where the radiator was cracked. It made me feel a lot better about the situation for them to physically show me what was wrong with my car, instead of disappearing for an hour and coming back with a laundry list of things that needed work.

I found that, at B & B, they really try to make you part of the process and feel like you have some control in what's going on.

Afterwards, I went back inside and they offered me a beverage and chatted with me a bit. They are seriously the friendliest and most welcoming staff ever.

Richard at the front desk walked me through my quote and was really, really great about it. They were unsure as to whether or not another part of my car would have to be replaced as it was bent in my accident (which they also showed me), so Richard quoted me the worst-case scenario and the best-case scenario because he didn't want me to have any surprises - which I REALLY appreciated. He has got to be the nicest, most genuine guy ever, which goes a long way when you're a worried customer.

The guys even offered to give me a ride home, a complementary service at their garage.

I called early the following day to see what the deal was because I was pretty nervous about my "worst-case scenario". My car wasn't ready yet, but they explained to me why and what they still had to do. They gave me a time to call the following day and said it would be ready then. They actually called me before that time, earlier the next day, to let me know my car was completed. (As well as sending me a confirmation email!) They didn't have to replace the other part on my car and were able to work around it just fine, so my final bill was the low-end of the spectrum Richard had originally given me (huge relief!)

When I went in to pay my bill and pick up my car, a different gentleman helped me, but Richard came out from the back just to (SUPER sincerely) tell me to be careful from now on. (Did I mention these are the nicest guys ever?) Since then, my car is running really great; you wouldn't even know the whole fiasco had happened!

In conclusion, I have definitely found my go-to garage in Austin. I will absolutely be back to B & B.

Input: I've been going to Johnny Fox's for the last 2 years but never got around to writing a review until now.Since its an Irish pub, I'll start with their beer.

 Many of the bars in Vancouver serve Guinness but, as advertized, Johnny Fox's serves the best. Not only is it on tap (unlike many places that serve it from a can) but they use the proper pour method. It may be the pour or some other magical secret known only to them, but I've never tasted Guinness (and i have a pint of it at pretty much every bar that i go to) as good as at Fox's. On top of the black stuff, they also pour Smithwick's and Harp, 2 more fantastic Irish brews. On top of the straight beers, they do mixed beers as well, all of which are delicious and poured with the proper separation of beverages in the glass.

On to the food. 

Johnny Fox's used to have a rather extensive food menu, but it was recently revamped and downsized. In this change they removed one of my absolute FAVORITE dishes: the Irish Patchos. The dish is essentially nachos but with slices of potato instead of tortilla chips, topped with cheese, green onion, tomato, black olives and jalapenos; certainly big enough to feed two people.  They held on to the Guinness burger and the Guinness and beef stew, both of which are superb. My final item that tops the food list are the Irish spring rolls. Even though they're not traditionally Irish, these crispy little badboys are a fantastic adaptation and a perfect starter to share. 

All in all this is one of my top spots to eat and drink in Vancouver. Its affordable, delicious and the beer cant be beat.

My only issue with Fox's.......BRING BACK THE PATCHOS!!!!

Input: The idea of having tapas for a birthday brought us here. Having everyone together talking,  sharing a meal together, enjoying themselves - ten ten tapas provided a GREAT environment to do so. I came here after much research for tapas places in Vancouver and I'll be coming back again. We had a reservation for around 6 and arrived to an almost empty restaurant. Quickly it began filling up and before we knew it there was a live performance - a singer. It made the night that much more special. We ordered a few different appies to share and I must say they were all great and had us wanting more. Roasted bell pepper and garlic hummus, fried potatoes with chorizo, mussels, calamari were the appies we ordered and it was good for five of us. Everything tasted delicious no complaints! I ordered the meatballs and crab cakes after as I was stuffed and didn't want a full meal but I was glad I did. The sauce the meatballs were made in was so rich and delicious, by far some of the best I have tasted! We were there to celebrate a birthday and management knew and they surprised the birthday boy with a desert and Pierce director of management took some great photos and emailed them right away. 

I would definitely recommend ten ten tapas for anyone looking for a great atmosphere, great food, and amazing service. I will definitely be going back!!

Also for all those Life with Derek fans, Edwin bartends here! Another treat for us when we arrived.. seeing him, pretty cool!

Input: Stuffy nose?  Sinus problems?  One dose of Tacodeli's Habanero or famous Doña sauce should clear it right up!  Seriously... I can't eat one of their tacos without my nose running.  And the tacos are fantastic.  Definitely the best in Austin (and this is coming from a self proclaimed taco connoisseur...) Austin Chronicle voters agree-- Tacodeli has taken the best taqueria award for the past two years!!

That being said, there are a few cons that I cannot ignore:

1. Tacodeli stops serving breakfast at 11am on weekdays..... It breaks my heart a little every time my mouth is watering for a potato, egg, and cheese taco only to find that I am minutes too late:
     (SUGGESTION: if you want breakfast, call and place an order at 10:55ish. so you can pick it up a bit later)

2. Tacodeli is full of yuppies-- I usually like the yuppie crowd.... but on the weekends, the line is out of the door, and there are just too many dang yuppies for me to have a relaxing taco experience.  They are usually pretty cool people, but their range rovers take up more than one space in the already crowded parking lot parking lot, they have a tendency to be overly pushy, and a tendency to yak obnoxiously on their iphones in line.

3. No dinner-- it is seriously a bummer taco deli is not open for dinner.... I would go for a Tacodeli dinner on the reg, but they close at 3pm daily.

4. The parking lot sucks-- I have always managed to find a spot somewhere, but the parking lot is poorly designed, there are not enough spaces for all of the businesses in the area. I frequently have to go look for street parking nearby.

All this being said,  I still love Tacodeli dearly, and I consider myself a Tacodeli loyalist  Best tacos in town, they use high quality ingredients, and the service is pretty good!

CRYSTAL IS AMAZING!!!

I was looking at different waxing locations near Vista and came across Sugar San Diego. I had never heard of sugaring before, so I read up on Crystal's website and did a little bit of Google-fu. She had a discount going for first time customers who wanted to get a Brazilian and seeing as how I had always wanted to try, I thought, "why not!?"

Sugaring is an all-natural method of removing hair and is often compared to standard wax. A lot of people say it's a lot more gentle than standard wax, so seeing as how I wanted to get a Brazilian, I thought this would be the best route to go.

I scheduled my appointment online. Super fast, super easy. The day of my appointment, Crystal texted me with some directions so that it would be easier to find her office. Really sweet and helpful of her to do that!

Once I filled out the new customer form, she took me to the back and we got started. It was my first time doing this, but Crystal was totally cool about it. She walked me through each step, explained what she was doing, and so on. I'm a bit of a baby when it comes to pain, so sugaring was a little painful for me. At one point, I had to ask to take a break LOL. Crystal didn't even blink twice at that request HAHAHA. She kept me distracted by chatting with me (she's so sweet and funny!) and gave me advice/tips & tricks on aftercare.

The session itself didn't take that long and she did a very thorough and fantastic job! Sugaring does get easier the more you do it, so I'll definitely be coming back. Crystal's prices are definitely fair and reasonable - especially since you don't need to come back for 4-6 weeks.

Definitely recommend Crystal and Sugar San Diego if any of you ladies are looking to try out sugaring! It was a great experience for me.

Input: I found this cool restaurant and concert venue one evening when we brought some out-of-town guests to see the spectacle that is The Oasis. We took a detour around the perpetual line, headed up the stairs, and went straight into Uncle Billy's. There was virtually no wait!

The restaurant is huge inside and has a lake-view deck that sits parallel to the overloaded one of its gaudy big sister next door. There are plenty of indoor tables, but we headed out back to sit on the deck.  I felt positively sneaky that we had landed a table so quickly while people stood in cue next door. This must be the best kept secret on the lake.

Uncle Billy's offers a BBQ menu and an array of somewhat offbeat appetizers (white queso, fried pickles, etc.) and the usual Tex-Mex fare. The food is good, as in better than next door's. Then there are the beers...Uncle Billy is apparently a microbrewer, as well. There are a number of beers on tap, a sampler to try several at a time, and some that are unlisted (see the chalkboard at the door).

Whereas the aforementioned next-door place books cover bands, Billy's seems to book the local original acts. I saw Ian Moore, Bob Schneider, Jimmy LaFave & Joe Ely on the upcoming list of shows posted in the restroom (which was very clean, btw). The concerts take place on the rooftop for an additional charge, but it didn't seem exorbitant. They do serve food up there, and I haven't yet tried out that arrangement, though I've recommended it to others with good results. Check out their website for more details.

I'm just excited to have such a cool Austin venue out here in the sticks. And now you're in on the secret, too. Pass it on...

**update 12/3: A quick review of Uncle Billy's website says they've closed for the season, most likely meaning winter.

Input: Have you ever heard of David Vendetti? If not then you're missing something in your life. And that thing is David Vendetti.

David teaches the all levels yoga class at SBY. It's targeted towards moderately practiced yogis but every movement can be modified for the beginner or the advanced. After a 90 minute session with David you will be drenched in sweat and sore in places you didn't know existed, but you will be glad about it.

David is an AMAZING instructor. He keeps you laughing through the class and is very encouraging when you feel like giving up (it happens, trust me). It's very hard to describe David. He's kind of someone you just need to experience. I think I fell in love with David before I fell in love with yoga.

I've also taken aerial yoga classes here with Joanna K. She's a really good instructor who walks you through the steps at a comfortable pace so you don't feel like you're going to fall out of the sling and die. The inversions are so much fun and I personally find doing yoga in the air very cool.

I've heard great things about the Pilates classes taught by Hanneke but haven't had the time to take any of them. I intend to if my schedule ever changes.

***************************************************
I forgot to add some things:

As more of a testament to David's amazingness, he knows a lot of his regulars really well. I'm sure these are people who come to all of his classes (I can only go once a week) and have been seeing him for years (I've only been practicing for six months). 

But after class a few weeks ago he extended a brunch invitation to anyone who wanted to come. My friends and I went as well as some yogis he knows well and a yoga instructor from New Jersey who was visiting. He and the regulars were super nice and treated us like old friends, despite the fact that we'd only really been introduced that day. They were so genuinely nice and welcoming and I had a great time.

Also, David and Todd (the advanced level instructor) are the cutest couple ever. No dispute.

As a testament to the great yoga practices at SBY, when I started in January I had scoliosis that had gone untreated since I was 12. It was minor, but it caused one of my hips to be an inch lower than the other and gave a slight curve to my spine that caused lower back pain. 

Last month I had to get an x-ray done due to a head injury. The x-ray showed that my scoliosis had improved since my last x-ray in August 2011. My one hip is now only a quarter of an inch lower than the other and the curve has straightened out a bit, causing me to grow half an inch. And while I still have some back pain, it's now more mild instead of moderate. 

The only lifestyle change that occurred during August 2011 and May 2012 was starting yoga, and I really can't think of anything else that would have improved my condition.

Input: Coming from NYC I have been spoiled by being able to take numerous Barre classes (Pure Barre, Physique 57, Flybarre, Exhale and others) and FINALLY I was able to try Bar Method (thanks to Classpass)  

Upon entry you are greeted by a very friendly staff who gives you a quick tour of the studio.  The studio has a decent sized changing room and 1 shower (which is a plus as that is not always the case in NYC)  

I like that the instructor read my profile sheet before class so she didn't have to ask about injuries (recovering from a car accident so I have wrist and lower back issues)
She did a great job of prompting me to the bar when it was time for pushups and other needed modifications. She did a great job of monitoring the entire class and making sure everyone's form was perfect without making you feel like you've been called out. (Like they do in Bikram Yoga! Sorry having flashbacks of militant instructors)  A little tilt of the hips or the legs can make all the difference. 

The class itself....I have to put it up there in my top 3 favorite studios.  If I lived in Orlando hands down this would be my #1 choice!!   (I am a Flybarre, Physique 57 fan and now The Bar Method) 

Why I do I like this over Pure which is right down the road? (To be upfront I didn't take the Pure here in Orlando and am basing it off my NYC experiences but I could have gone on Classpass but opted out) I prefer the flow of The Bar Method and the challenging moves.   While I don't really break a sweat during a bar class they got my legs and booty working and had very creative moves. Barre classes have REALLY helped with the inner thighs as my other classes (outside of Barre) work on the larger muscles (think squats, deadlifts, lunges).

If you are thinking of trying out a Barre studio....give this one a try and I am sure you will fall in love with it (all while your legs shake like never before!)  I was able to get in 3 classes during my stay....wish I could have done more!  

I will def be back the next time I am in Orlando!

Input: I am so grateful for the Children's Emergency services!  My daughter was sent home from school Friday with a stomach ache and a temperature.  Her fever quickly broke but after 36 hours of continuous vomiting and increasing pain I decided at 4AM Saturday to take her to the  ER.  

My last ER experience on a Saturday night 10 years ago was pretty awful, but that was before this new Pediatric Emergency branch was open.  We didn't even know it was a possibility until we saw the "Children's Emergency" sign on the way through the parking lot.

So this visit took less than 70 minutes start to finish, and all the staff were efficient but kind.   We did not even stop in the waiting room but I did notice age-appropriate programming on the TV and plenty of space there.   

I know that how much time you spend waiting in an ER is dependent on how may other people are there, so we were lucky.  We were immediately taken into the triage room,  and we did not wait after triage to be taken to an examining room.  Minor waits for the doctor, but my daughter could lay down so even if the wait had been longer we would have been okay.  

I will update my review once I get the bill (!) but since no unnecessary testing was ordered I feel confident that the charges will be reasonable.  My daughter came home with a prescription and slept until noon without vomiting once so I'm confident she'll soon be be back on track.  Thanks again to all the staff at St. Davids Children's Emergency on the Saturday 4am shift for their excellent care.

Input: What used to be fabuloso is no longer...

...because it's inside my belly being ultra fabuloso! 

I finally got to stop in and try the El Nutri Taco experience today, and all I can say is... wow. That's a mighty good vegetarian burrito. 

El Nutri offers meat, vegetarian, and vegan Mexican food options, and of course, I had to start with the vegetarian Fabuloso burrito because the name alone sucked me in. It's a mix of all sorts of goodness (onions, button mushrooms, nopales, other veggies, lettuce, rice, sour cream, cheese, beans and soyrizo) wrapped in a whole wheat tortilla. Is it an "authentic" Mex dish? Not any less so than any other burrrito. Was it delicious. Hell fuck yes it was. 

For the staggering price of $8 (yikes!) this expertly seasoned mix of hot and refreshing (crispy iceberg) had me immediately. It was love at first bite. 

You know when you start eating something and the experience of the flavors, the textures, and everything entering your mouth is so intense that your vision narrows as if you're wearing blinders? Your brain fixates solely on what you're putting in your mouth? About half way through my burrito I snapped out of "the zone" to realize that I was just sitting there making audible food-pleasure noises while face-diving into my burrito and blankly staring, unfocused, at the table beyond by prize. I was almost embarrassed for a second until I realized that the only other customer there wasn't paying any attention to me. Heh. 

Yeah, that's how good it was. It was the perfect mix of delicious grilled veg, tasty beans, rice, soyrizo (I think it was a chipotle soyrizo) and some crema. Yum. Let me say that again. Yum. 

While this might not satisfy a strong meat craving, as a burrito and a simply a filling-as-hell meal (I was stuffed at the end), this is an incredible burrito. I wish it wouldn't cost so much, but I know that quality ingredients cost $$, especially veggies. I also kind of wish it wasn't on a whole wheat tortilla. But hey, that aside, it's still a five-star burrito.

Input: I Googled "best bloody Mary Atlanta" and came across this spot. I'd been eating clean and not drinking and working out. Snorefest. It was time for Bender Sunday. I eat At Camelis all the time and hadn't even noticed this was next door (more on that later).
I walk in and quickly realize that maybe just maybe they cater to a gay clientele? Score! I stereotyped and immediately felt set free. No freakshow aging day drinkers hitting on me, no pressure to have polite conversation or hold in my tummy. Nada. The decor is very Bird Cage-esque. Lots of "things" all over that come together to create rainbow magic. As if I'd entered his home, I'm greeted by Ron. Such a sweetheart. It's obvious that I'm new as every single person at the bar is familiar. There's a splash of everyone there. Black, white, old, young (less of these) you name it. Other than age (mostly older), what do they have in common? KENO! Double score. I get lost in the game, win and eventually lose. All while having fun conversation and CHEAP drinks. 
Shift change, enter Michael. Gorgeous with amazing highlights and sweet as a honeycomb. 
This place is certainly not for everyone, but for everyone else it is. You gotta be okay in alternative environments. Also, like everyone said, it's adjacent to Murder Kroger, not Flower Kroger. You get what you get. 
I would have removed a star for the super intense ass smoke, but the service and prices totally made up. Bonus: I sorta ended up with two phone numbers. Both were straight guys. Yes they were so shut up!!!
Fun lookie look: Check out the cool new sign that finally identifies their business from the exterior. The guy who designed it was actually there that day. Super talented craftsman.
Lastly, there was a dog there enjoying the bar. They support all sorts of canine-related charities and welcome pups to join you when food is not being served. Call first if it's your first visit before bringing Fido though. Have a feeling it may be limited.

Input: I had the pleasure of getting a visit from Mike and Ernie of Mr. Rekey, and I received exceptional service. Ernie installed a door brace within 5 minutes and it now works properly, without any jiggle. They also completely removed the faulty charlie bar on the door and installed a pin lock for added security. In addition, they did a check on the front door, which was completely above and beyond what we hired them for, and made sure it was working correctly. Mike and Ernie completed the job within approximately twenty minutes, where a different company took around an hour over two days, and didn't even completely finish the job.

Lastly, Ernie did a quick repair on our bathroom door lock, which again, was completely above and beyond what I was expecting. It now functions a bit better than before.

Mike and Ernie seem to be locksmiths who truly value providing quality service. They completed the job efficiently and confidently. I want to thank them for a job well done.

It is hard to say what was the best but the korma was absolutely amazing and the flavor of the lamb was not overpowered by the cream sauce. 

This is one of those restaurants that if you do not live in Austin, you will remember for a long time.  The ambiance, service and (most importantly) food was fantastic.

Input: We went to Carmen last night for the first time. We used the Gilt city deal which allowed us to have 2 apps, 2 meals, and 2 glasses of wine. What we had:

Homemade meatballs w/mozzarella: you get 5 smaller meatballs, but they're pretty money. The meatballs come drenched in a spicy plum tomato sauce and are smothered with cheese. Excellent.

Fiori du zucchini fritti: when we ordered this I wasn't sure how it would work structurally but it came out great. The zucchini and goat cheese were fried in a light, almost tempura like batter and were served piping hot. The balsamic dribbled on top was a great touch.

Orchiette w/sweet Italian sausage: This was the highlight of dinner. The spicy sauce complemented the sweet sausage well, and the orchiette (not a pasta I've seen on many menus in the north end) were outstanding.

Black pepper tagliatelle with shrimp: the shrimp and pasta come in a not-too-heavy pesto cream sauce that we loved. There were only 4 shrimp, but they were MASSIVE and tasted like they were caught that morning.

The decor is cool, very dark and cosy. Plenty of candlelight, probably more ideal for a date than a group given the small size of the restaurant. Size-wise, the place is tiny, but still feels more intimate than cramped like some other places in the neighborhood.

The place is relatively expensive for Italian food, but the cuisine, ambiance, and service were worth it. They don't serve dessert, but I think it'd be a challenge to have room for it anyway as the portions are ample. After one night, challenging for one of my favorite Italian restaurants.

Input: I bought my 2003 Honda Civic from this location in March of 2003. I had just come off a lease of a 2001 Kia Sportage. (Cute car, needed to move onto something more reliable). Anywho - I brought my Mom along for some moral support. Keep in mind this was before I was dating or married to the hubby. Anyways, we were greeted by a salesman and I told him that I wanted to look at a new Honda Civic. I did not have a trade in, so I pretty much had to 'wheel & deal' on my own to get into a car. We test drove a Civic around the block and I quickly fell in love with it. It had the pickup and was easy to drive. LOVE it! We returned to the dealership and told the salesman that I was ready to make a deal. Of course they are all trying to sell you the rust packages, the protective stuff for the car, etc, etc.  No thanks. It was finally time to go talk to the finance manager. He advised me that I had great credit (duh, I already knew this, hence I could pretty much name my own price at this point). He kept asking for a $500 downpayment for the car. I told him no. He went back to the drawing board. He came back with another number. Nope. He asked again for the downpayment. Nope. Again, he came back again. Nope. Finally after the third try, I told him that if he came within $5 of the price I had in my head, we'd talk. At that time he dropped the monthly price considerably. It took him another 2 times before he kind of came close to the monthly price I was looking for.  You could tell that he was getting frustrated and wondered why some 20 something was 'wheelin and a-dealin' and playing hard ball. Finally I told him that I could not put a down payment down given that I just purchased a condo just days before walking into the dealership. He asked my price, I gave him $319, and he agreed. That price for 5 years at 0.9%. We finally signed the paperwork and walked out of the dealership about 2 hours later. New Honda Civic too!!

Talk about someone wheelin' & a-dealin'!!!!

Input: After a wonderful and full day at the Kennedy Space Center, Joe K had another place planned for us that consisted of southern style seafood cooking and cocktails.  Joe researched this restaurant in advance for our vacation.  We both love seafood and apparently this place is known for their shrimp!  

It took a little extra driving for us to find this place, and even noticing it from the main street was a bit of a challenge, but once we found the driveway, a feeling of relief came over me and I couldn't wait to settle down for some dinner and a drink!  Jeri was our server who made every effort to make us feel welcome.  Menus were handed to us and a complimentary platter of Corn Fritters got us started.  I always love to try new and signature cocktails at restaurants, so I chose a Dixie Delight and Joe got an Orange Blossom Pilsner.  The selections on the menu made it hard for us to narrow things down, so instead, we ordered a small banquet of dishes to share!  

Joe began his meal with the soup of the day - Shrimp Gumbo.  Then our food just kept arriving to the table!  Red Shrimp, and Rock Shrimp served with garlic butter, fried clams, fried oysters, and a side of cheese grits.  Our food coma was achieved!  Everything was delicious!  I only wished that the fried clams were a little more golden brown and the grits were less thick and dense.  But you definitely can't complain about not getting enough food here!  

I was impressed with this restaurant as a whole!  Even the ladies restroom was designed like it was meant for a 5 star hotel!  But in reality, it had a laid back, casual atmosphere with fun, interesting decor and plenty of dining areas.  In fact this place is huge!  Probably with good reason due to it's popularity.  I just wish we were able to return here again.  Now I can only remember it as one of the highlights of my Florida vacation.....

Input: It's Disney's Magic Kingdom... how can it not earn 5 stars?

This was my first visit since I was a kid - I remember bits and pieces, but I'm glad I got to experience it again, and have some more dates to look forward to this year.

Getting into the park tells you how they've updated their park:  they're technologically up-to-date with NFC working at the heart of everything - ticketing, Fast Pass, and paying at the vendors.  If you have Apple Pay on your iPhone, all of Disney is Apple Pay friendly, and we used this the entire day.  Although, it took some clerks a few minutes to realize what was going on and to get the register to, well, register; but this is fairly new.  

The rides and themes can seem a bit hokey at times, but it's Disney - They've got shows scattered throughout the day for music and character fun.  If you are going you MUST register your tickets with your Disney Experience account - if you don't have one, download the app on your smartphone, create an account, and register your tickets.  Then you will have access to Fast Pass on your phone and can select which passes you'd like so that you won't have to wait in line to do so at the park.  Fast pass is FREE but you are limited to three per day at one park (if you have a park hopper, you only get to choose one park).  Fast pass is great, so look ahead at ride times the day before (at the latest) to see what the waits are, and select the passes for the rides you want to ride with the longest wait times.

We really enjoyed our experience and can't wait to come back!
