It's easiest to drive here to any of the trailheads, but you can also walk here from the Washington Park Max stop.  The easiest trail to get to from there, as far as I could tell, is the Wildwood Trail, which is the centerpiece trail of the Park, ~40 miles and winding through its entire length.

Input: You have now until Monday, November 18 to have a taste of the Feast: Asian Dining Festival. For my last stop, I invited my friends to join me at Continental Seafood Restaurant to enjoy a $178 set menu for 6 people. 

it is my first time dining here. When I was selecting which restaurants to go, the menu from Continental Seafood Restaurant immediately attracted me. It is a 7-course menu that can feed 6 people. I invited four friends to tag along, and it was exciting for me because it has been a long time since I have such a fancy Chinese meal. 

The first two dishes are Crab Meat Fish Maw Soup and Roasted Pork with BBQ Duck. The soup is beyond my expectation, with a generous amount of crab meat and pieces of fish maw in it. The big bowl can fill up to 7 small bowls, so my friends can go for the second round! I love the crispy skin from the roasted pork, and the ratio of fat and meat is perfect. 

The Sautee Jumbo Prawn with Superior Soya Sauce arrives next. Again, I am surprised by the portion, which I believe it has more than 10 jumbo prawns in the dish. It is flavorful, but unfortunately, I wish the prawn itself can absorb more of the soy sauce flavor. It tastes somewhat bland on its own. 

The next dish is the one that excites me the most - Braised Lamb with Bamboo & Chinese Mushroom in Hot Pot. Lettuce is included on the side. Putting lettuce in the braised lamb hotpot is a common thing to see, as it can absorb all the flavors from the sauce. This type of hotpot is rare and often expensive in Vancouver. Therefore, I am surprised to see this on the menu. The lamb is tender and flavorful! I would totally order this again next time I am here. 

The last two dishes are also as fabulous as the others - Pan Fried Black Cod with Soya Sauce and Sticky Rice with Preserved Meat & Sausage. The black cod is cooked and seasoned perfectly. It is soft and flaky, but I hope it is more "pan-fried" than deep-fried as it looks they dipped the fish into corn starch prior to pan-frying it.

The sticky rice is one of the best sticky rice I have eaten in Vancouver. You might think I sound exaggerated, but I love the egg strings are so thin that the flavor is in every ingredient of the dish. It is not overly seasoned, and I won't feel too heavy after eating more than a bowl.

Unfortunately, we didn't get the dessert, which is also included in the set menu because we were too full with quite a bit of leftover. The server offers us red bean sweet soup and fortune cookies. 

*** Overall Impression ***

Continental Seafood Restaurant is rated at 3.9/5, and I think it totally worth at least 4.5/5. Almost all of the dishes are perfectly seasoned and cooked, and with this $178 set menu, it can probably feed more than 6 people. If you do the math, each person is paying around $35-40 after tips and tax, which is reasonable for a fancy, high-quality 7-course meal. The restaurant is spacious and clean, with good service. I will definitely return on my own time to try their dim sum and get the Braised Lamb Hot Pot once again. 

Taste : 4.5/5 * Service: 4.5/5 * Ambiance: 4.5/5 * Quality-Price: 5/5

GARDNER AFTER HOURS ..... 4.5 stars!

However, I'm not writing about the museum which is 5 stars, A ++ . I'm writing about the NEW Gardner After Hours event, a brand-spankin' new night time soire every third Thursday at the Gardner. Overall, I was impressed with the way that the museum was able to handle themselves with such a gigantic influx of people. The museum was the perfect place to relax while sipping cocktails--languid, romantic, and inspiring. However, I would have liked standing in line for cocktails less and also, some appetizers circulating. Perhaps samples of the treats in the cafe?

 The Yelp Elites got into the event free, but if you're not a member the charge is $12 to enter the museum, and $23 for a night among the arts, art-enthusiasts, and a performance (based on the theme of the evening). The concept is absolutely brilliant and I think Gardner will do well if they just change a few minor things. I'm really excited for them and oh, if you can, don't miss the Ginger Ice Cream in the cafe-my tongue is still tingling!

Input: Food (5/5): Please note this is a review for the dinner and not the brunch. I have had both, and the dinner trumps the brunch by far. I have been here twice, both times with the boyfriend. We always start out with appetizers, and I can say some personal favorites are the Gulf Coast Starter, Tempura Maine Lobster Tail, and the Crab Cakes. They are all amazing, but I personally like the lobster tail the most (you seriously cannot beat the contrast in textures and tastes of the crunchy tempura with the hot and juicy lobster meat). For entrees, I have tried the pecan salmon with lobster bread pudding as well as the cocoa-espresso ribeye on two separate visits, and I can honestly say both are FREAKING DELICIOUS. Really tender salmon meat, soft and buttery lobster bread pudding, easy-to-cut yet full-tasting ribeye. My god, I have dreams of these entrees. The desserts are sort of an afterthought - I have had the bananas foster and the bread pudding, and it's nothing to write home about. Still, Green Pastures gets 5 stars from me for really hitting the head on the nail with the appetizers and entrees.

Service (3/5): For such a nice place, I sort of expected better levels of service. It wasn't really anything special. The waiter assigned to our table seemed to be gone for a good amount of time, and I had to summon someone else half the time just to get more water or place another drink order. I think I'm speaking from one bad experience though as the young fellow who did help us out was extremely courteous, and I'm sure our dining experience would have been a lot better had he been our waiter for the night.

Atmosphere (5/5): The entire restaurant gives me the feel that this used to be an old Southern plantation home. It's your typical white Victorian home with vintage decor inside. My only regret is that dinnertime is much too dark to explore the grounds and the peacocks. Otherwise, this is a very lovely establishment and it's perfect for an intimate night out with your significant other.

Overall, the food is amazing and the service seems to be wavering dependent upon the servant you get. This is a great place to celebrate a special occasion with a spouse or significant other. If you have only been here for the brunch, I urge you to try the dinner. It is one of my favorite restaurants in Austin, and I will definitely be back.

Input: "..and they're always glad you came."

After visiting Cypress Street Pint & Plate for the first time to gather with fellow Yelpers to play UNO a few weeks ago, I came to think of Cypress as Midtown's Cheers. Everyone knows everyone's name and if they don't,  they'll quickly try to get to know you! The special on this particular dreary Saturday was an egg sandwich. Which I can honestly say: Rocked My world! What better to have with an egg sandwich than a bloody mary (or two). Perfectly served in a tall high ball glass with three olives. Service was fast and more importantly,  personable. 

The owner, Billy and Manager, Andrew L. are very friendly and genuinely personable. Seeing them out at Ecco on Friday night, I was completely surprised that they both remembered my name and were more than willing to give me a big hug and welcome me back to Cypress Street Pint & Plate. If that's not convincing, I don't know what is. After shutting down the bar at Ecco, I walked over to Cypress St. where I was pleased to be greeted by friendly faces. 

I took one quick look at the menu and didn't need to see anymore once I saw corn dogs on the menu! Six to an order, the all beef corn dogs hit the spot! I ate my order and half of Camille B.'s order!

Gordon, one of my favorite Atlanta bartenders, gave me a big hug when I left and asked Camille and I both to stop back in a see him sometime. 

There's not very many places you can go at 2AM where the bartender, and management are more than willing to offer up a hug and sit down and chat it up with you!

Input: YESSSS...5 Stars for one of my favorite brewpubs in Oregon!

I worked a block away from this awesomely located brewpub in NW Portland for the past 2 summers.  I would smell the beer brewing bright and early in the morning and once I had a whiff of that I knew it was going to be a good day. This place also probably takes up an entire block.

Im not going to lie, I might be a little biased towards Bridgeport beers but that's because they ROCK.  they make one of the best IPA's in my opinion and now with Hop Czar on the shelves I cant stop drinking beer.

So what if im biased towards the beers...Beers aside, this place is awesome, I never been in it before its remodel but have been there with family or friends a few times. Its like 3 stories tall and depending on how busy it is you're seated accordingly.  If its spring or summer you should check out the back patio, which is usually full but nothing beats drinking a micro on a nice sunny afternoon in NW Portland! Go there during peak hours and its a great social environment, everyone is happy and the atmosphere is bumping.  I've stopped by the bakery in the mornings a few times to get coffee and a pastry and im also impressed with their baked goods.

The food is upscale and presented well. It seems that they make most of their stuff from scratch. Its not your cheap brew pub burger and fries crap (cough..McMenamins). this place knows how to make food and probably has a good chef back there.  I usually get one of the Pizzas which are all named after different Portland bridges.  The pizza has never let me down especially with a pint in my other hand.

If you want a taste of one of Oregon's best micro's along with good food and a lively atmosphere (in and around the restaurant) this is the spot. period.

Input: Sushi by Yuji is amazing.
Before I start, I have to say make a reservation!! We tried to go here before and they had a sign up saying they were only taking reservations today. The second time we went we called ahead on the same day and it was all good, they ended up being full when we were there (it's a tiny place!). Also, both of these instances were on weekdays so I imagine you'd have to call even earlier for weekend reservations.

All of the seafood here was so fresh which just elevated the taste of everything.

We started with the carpaccio, half tuna and half salmon, and it really set us off on the right foot. The flavour was amazing, something I still think about the taste of even though this was weeks ago. The tuna was just a bit better than the salmon, maybe because it was more thinly sliced and was able to absorb the sauce better, but they were both amazing.

The shiro/house roll was really delicious as well. I think there was something in it flavour wise that was similar to the carpaccio, but whatever it was made it taste so good.

We also got the spicy bc roll, kura roll, and the chopped scallop roll. The only thing that disappointed me at this place was that they did the thing where they made the roll "spicy" by just putting a spicy sauce over it, but the inside of the roll tasted the same way it normally would. Their spicy mayo did have wasabi infused in it though, I'm personally not a huge fan of wasabi so I wasn't a fan of this roll but my boyfriend didn't mind it. The regular rolls were pretty standard, but definitely tasted a lot better with the fresh seafood. Really appreciated that the seaweed was easy to bite too and wasn't the kind that you get stuck chewing forever.

I think this is the kind of place you go to if you want to stray away from your regular sushi order and get dishes that are more specific to this restaurant.

Will be back here whenever I am in the area.

Input: This dealership has redeemed itself. 

I've always been a little leary of getting auto repair work done at a dealership. Over the years of having several different cars, Its been mention to me more than once, by mechanics, friends, and by my ex who was an auto sales representative for several years (now retired), that they are not to be trusted. So when my uncertified used (not under warranty) Hyundai Sonata's engine light started showing up on my dash about a month ago, I went to my trusty mechanic and he at that time, hooked that device up to my car to find out what was going on. It showed no code, he tightened up the gas cap and said to bring it to the dealership. OMG! On the way to the dealership, I stopped at the store, came back to my car, and lo and behold, the engine light was gone. THANK GOD! About a month later it appeared again, like a bad dream. Ok, I replaced the old gas cap with a new one, the light went off again. Another prayer of thank you crossed my lips. That last about a week, when for the third time, here it is again! Ok, ok,  I've had enough. I bring it to my trusty mechanic and he finds a code this time. Finds out what the problem is, Harness, sensor to the transmission needed attention. Although everything on a car is expensive, gone are the days of windshield wipers that use to cost under $10, or working on it yourself, the technology is so advanced now, even the auto technicians probably need to go back to school every six months or so to keep up. I say to myself anything to do with the transmission and/or engine is big dollars. My trusty mechanic told me how expensive this 4 to 5 hour job would probably cost. He called the Hyundai dealership, explained what the problem was to the service advisor Mike, and Hyundai agreed that it was under warranty and would do the job. Unbelievable!!! I called again just to verify and got the same answer, "yes its under warranty and we'll do the work", but they're busy and don't know when they'll be able to do it, but said if I bring it there now and can leave it for a couple of days, they'll work on it. I was there in less than 20 minutes!
Couple of days later I get an early morning phone call from Mike, telling me my car is ready! No charge at all, and here's the kicker, upon arrival, my car was washed AND my wheels were waxed.... My wheels waxed! What dealer does that! 
I love you guys! Thanks for the superb service!

She was very nice about it and did offer me a discount for the next time I came back, but I'm just too afraid. I don't want to spend the money and can't get authentic traditional food like I once did when I first became a patron. I hope they go back to the way things were. 2 stars for the service and courteousness of the staff(they are always nice) but the food was nothing special. I could make garlicy baked chicken myself.

So glad I didn't pay $4.50 for a bowl of it, even the small "dipper" size of it is $1.50.  This brought my total to about $8.50 with tax, not including a drink which would have been a couple bucks more.  

I don't believe there is much value in the meals here.  This meal should have been about $6 or $6.50 at most based on the quality of ingredients and portion sizes.  $8.50 was way too much.  

As far as service goes, they bring you your meal and that's it.  You dump your own trays and get your own drinks.  I don't have a desire to ever go back but if someone else was dead set on going back I would give it another try.

Input: I've been to my share of luxury day spas and since it was my birthday, I decided to treat myself to a facial. I had been following the reviews on  Buckhead Grand Spa for a while and decided to make an appointment for a facial.  

So on to the actual review . . . 

You might ask, why just two stars when everyone else has ranked this spa higher? Well, when a company puts the word "Grand" in their name, I think it should live up to that... unfortunately, Buckhead GRAND Spa did not live up to its name.  The spa itself is actually relatively small, particularly the rooms where the services are provided. I was hoping for a very relaxing experience, but something was missing. It was unfortunately one of the most un-relaxing spa experiences that I've had.  For the type of service I received (a facial with an added masque and exfoliation) I felt that the service was extremely over-priced.  

The facial itself was mediocre and typically most day spas will include a brief shoulder and neck massage with the facial and I didn't receive that with mine.  At check out, I asked the receptionist is this a normal practice and she replied that it depends on the type of facial I received.  When I told her the type of facial I received, she said, "oh well, you should have received a shoulder and neck massage." Then, she said, "well, maybe she just ran out of time."  Although some people might see not getting a neck and shoulder massage as something small, for me it adds to the relaxation factor of a facial. 

Needless to say, I won't  be back. Usually within a week after a facial I can tell a difference in my skin.  With my facial from Buckhead Grand Spa, I saw no difference in my skin, at all. At the end of the day I was felt cheated and disappointed that I had wasted my time and money at this spa.

I think I replied something like "yes, that is enough for now".

The odd thing was the waters were given to us in black mugs. Mine had a white powdered substance around the mug and at that point I decided I wasn't drinking from this dirty mug. So major points off based on poor cleanliness. 

So based on pretty poor service and the lack of cleanliness, this place gets 2 stars. One star each for the okay tasting dishes we ordered. Price point wasn't cheap and you would be better off ordering from a food court in a mall (like crystal mall/Aberdeen centre).

Input: I was excited to try this place, as some of the reviews were good.  I have only been here once, and based on what I ate, I may not make it back for a second time for severals months.  

Pro-
Plenty of seating and choices, having both tables and booths.  It looks like they could handle seating a large party with ease.
Padded chairs and booth seats.
Fairly decent decorations.
Serves Asian alcohol and spirits.
They have a fish tank.

Con-
Smelled like my great aunt's house (but to be fair, it might have just been a booth of older women near the door).
Atmosphere and decor was late 80's, I'm talking teal and salmon colors.

Since it was my first visit, I decided to try the ambiguous General Tso's Chicken lunch special, staple of all "American" Chinese restaurants. My soup selection was egg-drop, and I should have had the miso.  The egg-drop was very thick and very yellow.  I ate the soup, but it was nothing special.

When the chicken dish arrived, there was plenty of steamed white rice on my plate, along with a standard Chinese egg roll.  The chicken was cut into fairly large pieces, that did not seem to have any breading on them.  I was able to cut the pieces of chicken into 3rds (that's how large they were) with my fork, but it took some effort.  The chicken was overcooked and dry. I was not offered chopsticks until I was already into my meal, but I probably would not have been able to use them due to the chicken's texture. The sauce was fine, and had a good flavor.  The dish was accompanied by several pieces of steamed broccoli which I didn't have any problems with.

The thing I found most unsettling was our server was wearing shorts.  I'm no prude, as I think shorts are fine for restaurant employees, but only if the ocean is nearby. Needless to say, this wasn't a good first impression of Dragon Court, but I will try them again in several months, and hope to have a better experience.

Input: Interesting concept, generally tasty food, but wayyyyy overpriced.

To start, cocktails were tasty but were on the small side. The "Kirin slushy" was an interesting concept and cool presentation, but pretty disgusting-tasting IMO.

For food, the waiter suggested getting one or two large plates and a few small plates to share, so between three of us we tried a few different dishes. Upon recommendation, we ordered the large plate fried chicken, which was nicely executed but way too expensive for what it was- 4 nicely fried, nicely flavored, boneless chicken thighs (aka one of the cheaper cuts) and a large scoop of just-OK mayo-ed potato salad with a touch of seaweed, for $28. 

Next up was the small plate of corn, which was essentially a tasty coconutty (vegan) version of elote/Spanish street corn, 2 half ears for $~8... fine but not worth the price. The small plate kale salad was OK but again, not worth it for the price (~$10?). Last up was small plate roasted potatoes with ground lamb for ~$15, which was yet again way overpriced, and had some good flavors but weren't incorporated enough IMO (each ingredient- lamb, potatoes, yogurt, spices, pomegranate seeds- felt like it was added to the plate completely seperately, and it was only if you made sure to have each item in the same bite that the dish really came together and popped). 

On the plus side, they have a nice patio, cool interior, and attentive service. But the price point and portion size means I'm not eager to return.

Input: To being with the meal started off on an odd note, as the server indicated that they could not bring any salsa out, because they had run out and were making some.  This struck our group of four very oddly because it was prime time on a Friday night (10JAN, 7:30PM), but we went ahead and ordered some guacamole instead as we were looking forward to some sort of appetizer/beginning to our meal.  The guacamole arrived and then we were informed that there were no chips either, as they had run out of them too; again, super odd for prime time dining and presumably we were supposed to eat the guac with a spoon?  Not 2 minutes later our server, returned with our beverages and had an accident, dropping water and beer on the table and onto the floor, with the beer bottles breaking and glass shards going everywhere.  The server came back 3 minutes later and cleaned the table up, but 3 of the four people were REALLY wet, most of us looking like we had "accidents" with the front of our pants soaking wet.  The evening did not get better, although apologies were offered, since the manager was not called over to address the service issue, nor was the hundreds of glass shards on the concrete floor cleaned up.  We finally requested an audience with management, who did come over and offer more apologies, but no recovery to the event(s) were in site until we expressed our dissatisfaction.  Ultimately we were offered the guacamole (with no chips, mind you) as compensation for the errors.  We eventually moved to a new table, after asking, and the evening did not get much better as the manager became somewhat snappish with our utter dissatisfaction  As our food arrived later, mind you still no chips nor salsa was ready yet, only two of the four meals were served, and had to wait an additional 5 minutes for the remaining food to arrive at which point the first two meals were getting cold.  Then to make matters worse, the final 2 meals, sizzling fajitas, arrived not sizzling, and the server then accidentally dropped the tortillas on the floor, thus delaying our meal even further.  In the end, accidents occurred, no legitimate service recovery was executed, and the food service/food itself was very disappointing.   Many valuable lessons were learned this evening!!! :)

Input: I was going to leave 1 star but since the management took care of the sloppy service at the end, I am leaving 2. I have been getting my car washed here several times and it's been an ok service like at any other automated wash services. Basic car wash includes vacuum but don't expect a "vacuumed" car:). You would need to pay extra for real vacuum service. About 6 months ago I gave it a try for their best wax service as well, paid around $100. Job was done well, I was a happy customer! Today I decided to return for another best wax service expecting same quality (over $100 service). Well, this time it was obviously a sloppy job, spots were missed on trunk, hood, roof etc. Detailer, who I tipped generously ahead of time ( my fault ), did not apologize but mumbled that my car needed clay treatment to get it completely clean. I explained and showed him how I was able to clean the missed spots with my fingertips and made him understand that I was aware about clay treatments and when it is needed and in this case it was just a sloppy wax job. Detailer then disappeared and his supervisor showed up. We went over the missed spots again. He explained they are not able to remove all? :) I demonstrated once more how easily it was coming off clean with just slight touch and asked how come some areas of the car are clean and some not. After-all, I paid for their premium wax treatment. Supervisor did not seem to believe I had purchased their premium service  until I showed the receipt. There was no apology, just a quick reply: ok, we'll get it fixed within 2 minutes. About an hour later my car was re-finished and looked like brand new without clay treatment:) 
I doubt I will go back for premium services. I just don't feel like spending all day at the car wash justifying why I should receive the service I had paid for and especially do not appreciate being up-sold unnecessary services if there is no need. My suggestion to management: QA your services and be aware what service was purchased before handing back the car to their owners. I bet your ratings will start improving then.

Input: I've held off on reviewing this place for a while, but feel like I need to write something up now. I came here for an evening dinner date, and had a fairly mediocre time. 

During my meal, I ordered a salad, fillet, and a baked potato. 

The salad was good, but nothing to write home about. Quality ingredients, but nothing incredible. The steak was not cooked well. The outside had been burnt, and was hard when it arrived. Powering through that, the inside was cooked to medium as indicated, but I still felt like the taste was a bit off. The potato was bang on average, and trust me, I know my potatoes. Fairly small in size, and definitely skimpy on the toppings. 

Additionally, our service was relatively slow and inattentive - there were not a lot of people eating there at like 6:30 PM on a weekday, yet we were stuck waiting for refills on a couple occasions. This is unacceptable at a place that charges $50 for a steak. 

If I'm being completely honest, I would much rather go to Texas Roadhouse or Longhorn for my steak dining experience in Columbus, because I can get 3 BETTER meals for the same cost as the one I had here. 

And in saying that, I do not discredit these fancier steakhouses. I have been fortunate enough to be able to travel to Chicago for work for about a year. While there, I've eaten at places like Chicago Cut, RPM, Benny's, Chicago Chop, Remingtons, as well as a couple others. In all of those places, I paid upwards of $100 for my meal, but left feeling like I had just eaten one of the best meals of my life. 

I spent $75+ at Hyde Park and felt that I would have enjoyed my meal and had better service at a chain steakhouse that shows ads on tv. That is not okay.

Input: i LOVE the hotel. So many great things. The History, the space we had, and more! So why only 2 stars?  Well - the service let us down HUGE

So I recently got married, and we wanted a hotel that was nice, had space for my wife and her bridal party to get ready, and also would be good for pictures. Our reception was in Boston, and after looking at the Omni Parker House, and others, we decided we wanted to look for something classic, great for pictures, affordable, and not generic (example,w e could get a suite chain in quincy, but its generic)

WE booked a room block for guests (with 11 guests staying for 1-3 nights), booked a room for myself for the night before, and then also the Garden Suite for two nights (her, and then us the second). 
The suite was amazing (and at the cost, it should be). 1200+ square feet, living area, full kitchen, dining area, and a 600 SF balcony outside. it was PERFECT. All the room for her to get ready, plenty of room for guests to stop in, a fabulous outdoor space, and perfect for pictures.
My room was as expected. Small, since an old hotel, but up to date, clean, and well appointed. no complaints on it at all.

So where did we get let down

1. Housekeeping. When we checked into the hotel, the balcony had not been cleaned, with empty beer cans and cigarette butts abound. We called and asked them to clean when we were at the rehearsal dinner. They didnt.
We asked them to come twic eon Sunday, even if a cost to us, so it could be clean for pictures and then after. They came at 7am, cleaned for pictures, perfect. didnt come again
Despite several requests to several people, it just didnt get done. Although to the hotels credit, they did refund my prt of the room cost since it had not been cleaned as needed.
2. AS with a lot of weddings, we had gift boxes for our guests. Snacks, aspirin, Bottled water, champagne,etc. We arranged before with the hotel, who advised us it would be $2.50 each box to deliver. annoying, but in the big scheme of things, it was fine. We brought everything in, reviews. Good to go
right?
Well, 2 boxes got delivered to the wrong rooms. Two guests did not get them the first night. then the four guests arriving the second night, didnt get them at all. Despite several conversations with the manager, they disappeared. they said they were delivered. said our guests must be mistaken. said they didnt have them
THEN, the next day, after everyone checked out. THEY FOUND THEM! apparently, tucked away in teh bell closet.
well, great. not these boxes we made for guests, spending $40+ each on, didnt go to the guests.
The manager, Jeffrey, offered to ship them to the guests. I provided the address. and good to go. Better late then never, right? well, no
All the guests got the boxes. destroyed (I am guessing they got destroyed and crushed in the bell closet). All were missing items. (funny enough, teh same items missing from all four boxes - Bottled waters and homemade granola!). Now,w e know all boxes had them, so how was the same stuff missing from ALL the boxes!
To the hotels credit, they did ship (although incomplete), and did not charge me the $2.50 per box room delivery (which is good, since some went to the wrong rooms or not at all!)

Why am I posting this all now when they have tried to help? Well, three days later after emailing FIVE people there, including the group even coordinator, and the manager that helped us, about the missing items, and such, I have not heard back from ANYONE

I love the hotel. I really do. The suite was amazing. teh decor, and common spaces great. I love the history, location, and more!

But with such bad service, when spending SO MUCH money, how can I recommend it or go back?!

(I did not purchase the irons at Golf Galaxy) When I asked to get the clubs regripped after I bought the grips which was over $100 they said I would have to leave my club a there for about 4 days because there so many orders placed already. I was a little confused about this because I had already been there for almost half an hour and saw no one working on regripping clubs. But I didn't mind too much because I understand there were already a lot of orders ahead of me so I couldn't control that, so I just bought my own regripping tools at the store which was about another $30. After that I asked a worker if I could hit on the TrackMan because I just bought new irons so I wanted to get my distances, at first they weren't really sure, so I said I would pay for the hitting bay on TrackMan because I understand that they charge to hit on those bays. Around 3:30 they had still not arrived, so I called and was told it would be 1 to 1 1/2 hours. The technician was not there long, having found corroded batteries in the thermostat. The corrosion could have been cleaned out with soda water or vinegar and fresh batteries installed, and everything would have been fine, but he elected to replace a perfectly good thermostat with a new $178 one.
The economy is still bad, and everyone is trying to survive these days, but I won't be able to partner with Empire again because they have apparently forgotten how important dedicated and satisfied long-term customers are.

Input: Alrighty, let's start with the service: I came RIGHT at 8pm for oyster sunday so they were pretty packed, so I don't blame em for being pretty slow.. I mean, for $1 oysters how can I complain? The waitress brought over our own personal carafe of water.. i LOVE when places do that! It took a while for us to get the waitress's attention after that but oh well, they were busy.

My brother and I decided to start off with a dozen oysters each (http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=h5UrFxN1bejk5oiRL3LWsw&select=Sa7jYg00NTIu3u6Dm5GdmQ), then proceed our way day the asian-fusion inspired menu. They serve their oysters a little bit differently here.. they don't give you cocktail sauce (after all, it IS an asian-fusion restaurant).. instead they gave you this sauce which to me, tasted like a vietnamese fish sauce-based migonette (nuoc
 mam). In my opinion, a little too overpowering for the oysters..

Now the bad part. the oysters my brother and i were eating tasted a little off... it didn't necessarily taste BAD, but it didnt taste so fresh.. we thought it could have been the type of oyster.. but after finishing our dozen oysters, we didn't feel so good.. We decided to opt out on trying the rest of the menu and GOOD THING we did. A few hours later we both started throwing up. Now I know once in a while a restaurant can't help but get a bad oyster, but what are the chances that BOTH of us got bad oysters? I'm hoping it was a very rare thing and that their other customers felt fine, but i'm a little hesitant to try myers and chang again. Had only ONE of us gotten food poisoning, i'd for sure be down to try again, but the fact that we BOTH got it makes me a little uneasy..

I know it's not completely their fault, so I'll give 2 stars and maybeee in time I'll write an update!

Input: I think that I have written about Neptune Oyster previously and perhaps more glowingly.  I debated between 2 or 3 stars as my experience this last time was less than stellar - but I decided that "I've experienced better" sums up my last visit.  

I get the feeling that perhaps this place is riding the wave of their past popularity and have lowered their standards, both in terms of service and food quality.

We arrived right when Neptune opened on a recent Sunday morning.  We immediately got a table and after some time given menus and after some more time saw our waitress for the first time.  Even though the place was half-full at this time, she certainly seemed frazzled and having no time to wait for us to decide.  In fact, she walked away several times if there was a lull in our ordering.  This reflects the service overall, hard to get someone's attention to order another glass of wine or even get the check.  The staff definitely has an attitude and I am not sure that they buy into the customer always being right thing.

The food was ok.  No question it was fresh...but people come on...it's oysters and lobster...not the height of culinary sophistication.  Having said that those are two things that I love and crave on a regular basis.  Somewhat disappointed by the lobster roll...sure it was big...it should be for $28.00...but the lobster was tough and too much mayonnaise.  Would much prefer the lobster roll at James Hook & Co.  I can also say that the Shrimp Cocktail was horrible...the giant shrimp were tough and rubbery...should have definitely just ordered more oysters.

I think that everyone in my party came to the same conclusion...it was alright...not sure it was worth $300 for 3 adults and 1 small child.  There are so many great restaurants in Boston...not sure I would rush back anytime soon.

Input: I've been going to sally's for years.  I get my hair done professionally but I buy toner and some random things from time to time.   Never had an issue before now.  

Two weeks ago I went in on Saturday to get the toner i wanted.  They were out and i almost got a different one but I asked the pretty tan girl if they had any of the one i wanted and she said no that they would have it on Tuesday.  I asked her if it would do the same thing and she said no and that i wouldn't be happy if i used it.  So I took her advice and everything was fine with my encounter with her. 

Then Tuesday came I went in and two workers told me that they had a big truck the night before and were still stocking.  I told them I specifically was told to come today to pick it up.  They told me to call back later.  I was already mad at this point because i made 2 trips there and still didn't have it.  On my way back through town a few hours later I called a lady answered told me to hold and a guy got on the phone.  I asked if they found the toner yet and he asked me if i just called. I said NO i was in there a few hours ago.  He told me no and that they probably didn't even get any because the truck is auto ordered.  Which made me think he was just being lazy and not wanting to find it. he told me he would look at the invoice and let me know if they got it. about 5 or so minutes later he tells me there wasn't any on the truck and that they wouldn't have any til they get their next truck on the following Tuesday

There was no way I could believe that.  I called corporate and spoke with a man who was nice and understood my frustration and that i felt the guy was lying about having any.  He gave me a 30% off coupon code to use.  he called the store and talked to the guy and told him the same thing.  However the rep told me that he seemed nervous about the situation and that he would send the complaint the regional something...

Guess What!?  it's been a week and I just went back to sally's  and Still no toner.  I spoke with a lady who didn't know about the issue and i didn't bother explaining because it doesn't make a difference.  She was nice and called the warehouse to see why they hadn't received any.   It's not her fault im frustrated with going 3 times out of my way and leaving empty handed.  

So I had my boyfriend go to another store and pick up the toner I wanted.  They had at least 20 of them.  That's not the end of it though. When he gave my phone number to checkout and use my $5 OFF COUPON i received when i renewed my membership a few weeks prior they told him they don't have my information and that i don't have a card. even though i have the receipt that shows I renewed and the coupon.   not only that but they wouldn't accept the 30% off code that corporate gave me because they said it expired a month before.   (it has not even been a week since they gave it to me.)

I called corporate to get the membership straightened out and that was easy but when i asked her about the 30% off code she literally argued with me for at least 5 minutes saying there is no way that i have a 30% off code because those don't exist. she looked it up and said it doesn't say anything about giving you a code when you called last time, then she said it did but doesn't show how much.  she put me on hold to ask him about it and came back a few minutes later saying that he gave me a 30% mothers day code to use and it expired on Sunday.  Which I don't care that much about the code but I can not believe she accused me of lying about having a 30% off code and the others misleading me and causing me to have to wait over 2 weeks and making 4 trips for one product.  

If they would have just told me the truth from the start or told me to call before coming to make sure they had it none of this would have happened.  I am still Mad.

Input: I originally found Major League Maids on Craigslist.  They were calling themselves something else in the beginning but have since changed their name.  The first time I used them I was SO extremely happy!  Thrilled.  I spoke with Chelsea who is the owner along with her husband.  Only thing that wasn't perfect was the kitchen counter top not being cleaned.  They're granite.  The lady that came to clean was Hispanic and spoke broken little English.  This wasn't a problem for either of us. We got along just fine and I really liked the girl.  

I told Chelsea about the counter tops because she wanted to know if there was anything at all I wasn't happy with. She really wanted to make sure her clients were happy with their service as they were a new business.  So, on the next visit, Chelsea sent her husband to come in with a new girl who was a white English speaking girl.  She did a great job as well and the husband wanted to make sure I was very happy and I was.  Again, thrilled!  So happy to find a good cleaning service that wasn't just interested in making money.

Well, after that, everything went downhill.  Third visit, 3 Hispanic ladies show up. Only one speaks broken English.  She gave me a pre-printed list to fill out that shows everything they will do while there and I was to check off anything that I didn't want done.  This was great.  A detailed list.  Perfect.  

I left the girls to do their thing.  I paid them their money cash.  When I got home, I found the windows in my living room (which I have a lot of) were not cleaned at all. Underneath my dining table it had not been cleaned, tons of dust underneath. Two of the bathroom floors just weren't swept at all which also means not mopped. Two closets, not swept either.  No one swept behind the doors that were open in rooms or closets.  I was just really, really unhappy.  I took pictures of 2 things and sent them to Chelsea.  She was very apologetic, offered to clean the house with a $20 discount on the next visit.  Okay, fine, just as long as I don't get the same girls.  She said there were only suppose to have been 2 women there which was odd.  Why was their 3?  Were they paying someone on the side.

Next scheduling Chelsea tells me she's sending her best girl to me, they show up 1 hr and 15 mins late.  No phone call to tell me they were running late. After 3 calls to Chelsea and telling her I had to leave and forget it, 3 girls show up as I'm leaving my house. It's the same girls as last time.  The one who spoke English remembered me as well.  I was VERY unhappy.  

Chelsea then started sending me weekly texts offering a special house cleaning for $50 due to other clients cancelling.  This was weird.  This happens all the time now and she wants to fill her schedule?  If she can do the whole house for $50 why does she charge $77 normally?  It was just too gimmicky for me and I felt they got into the money making mode and quit offering just really good service.  I was willing to pay $100 each time for the service I got on the 1st two visits.  It's really a shame.  I was so happy to begin with.

Be careful and stay with the girls and watch what they do.  And no they do not all speak fluent English as her website advertises.  Good luck Yelpers!

Zales is great, just not at this particular location!

That, too, was impossible because unless we've handed over our credit card and made the purchase, no measuring because, well, you know, "the rules."  We questioned this policy, trying to be logical - how do you know if it'll fit if there are no measurements? - but we had to abide by "the rules."  So we abided by OUR rule - the customer is always right - and left Bridals by Lori never to return.

Input: I expected so much more with all of the reviews of this place but I was completely disappointed. 

I came here for lunch on a Friday with a friend. We searched Yelp and found the glowing reviews of this place. Once I stepped into the restaurant, I knew the restaurant was more about ambiance than the food. 

For appetizers we ordered the monkfish pate and nasu dengaku (eggplant in miso sauce). We got the eggplant first and my immediate reaction was a little disgust. The eggplant was completely covered in the dark brown miso sauce. It didn't look very appealing, I didn't even bother taking a picture of it. When I tasted it, the miso sauce was waaayyy too sweet. You can't even taste the grilled eggplant. My friend and I had to scrape off the sauce to get a decent flavor. The monkfish "pate" was really good but not what I was expecting. When I hear the word pâté I was expecting some type of spread. The monkfish liver came out whole, I didn't mind this at all because that's how I like it. I just didn't like how they tried to make it fancy on the menu. 

I ordered the sushi and sashimi lunch combo for my meal. My friend ordered the yellowtail roll and a dragon roll. My lunch combo came with sashimi pieces of red snapper, salmon, and tuna. Then my sushi pieces were just repetitive with the red snapper, salmon, tuna, and oh yay they added shrimp! What no yellowtail in there?! If I knew the sushi and sashimi were going to be the same type of fish I would have ordered something else. The cuts of the fish were ok but the quality was not very good. The red snapper was dry and the salmon was too chewy. I tasted my friend's dragon roll and it was ok. They had tempura sweet potato in the roll and that was different. However it made the roll pretty heavy. The eel was good and the sauce wasn't too sweet. I didn't get to try the yellowtail roll but my friend said it was good.

Unsatisfied with my combo, I ordered a toro handroll to hopefully lift my spirits. The toro handroll wasn't impressive for $17. There was supposed to be scallions inside but I didn't get any. The toro wasn't the best quality and the seaweed it was wrapped in was so chewy.

Our total bill came out to be $71 pre tax and tip. I couldn't believe how much we spent on the quality of the food. The monkfish liver was the only saving grace of my meal. The service was ok when it came to clearing our plates but we did have to ask several times for lemon and water refills. So sad this had to be my last meal in Boston. I definitely won't be back, I'd rather spend my money at a good hole-in-the-wall sushi type of joint than this place.

Input: I visited on a whim for a quick meal on a Friday night. I'd love to know which street they visited to find these "street" tacos, because as a visitor in search of "Boulder's best taco" I've been unimpressed with my findings. 

Chips and Salsa - the chips are the highlight, they're nice and crispy and exactly what a tortilla chip is. The salsas lacked kick - Mango salsa was very sweet, salsa verde was missing acid, and the red salsa was about where I'd begin to place "mild." These were not bad tasting, but were not necessarily what I was looking for. 

Tacos - I had barbacoa and carnitas, they were about 4x the price of a normal street taco. I was very surprised that there was no al pastor, cabeza, lengua, or even chorizo on the menu - traditional street taco staples. My tacos were not bad tasting by any means, but were not necessarily flavorful - bit more heat, seasoning, and maybe a little extra sear would've gone a long way. I was also surprised to find so many toppings, but that's personal preference - I like the meat to take center stage. The tacos were very juicy, which is a great thing, but that caused the tortillas to become soggy and rubbery. 

Overall, I was unimpressed. I feel like I'm definitely getting hung up on the "street taco" name, but these are very different from the tacos you get on the streets of Mexico City or Los Angeles.

Input: I was very disappointed. My expectation was that I would get North End quality Italian food. This was Bertucci-type of dining. The decor has vastly improved. Atmosphere was bistro-loud and happy. We all had something different and each dish offered nothing special in flavor or quality. 

Caprese  salad was on a small plate. There was too much dressing and there didn't appear to be any basil. Peppers were too much. This dish should be fresh, simple ingredients that speak for themselves. Kind of hard to get this wrong. 

Caesar salad was flavorless and light on dressing and appeared to have balsamic vinegar on it which was overpowering. 

Pasta dish with chicken and broccoli was too light in sauce and chicken was very dry and over cooked. 

Shrimp scampi was the best dish we had but the shrimp was over cooked, dry and rubbery, not light and fresh. 

Ravioli had a very heavy sauce which tasted fine but was too heavy. The pasta was very thick like a puerogi, not light and al dente 

Bread was cold, tasted ok but would prefer an interesting dipping oil. 

Drinks were a good price but not a great selection of wines by the glass. 

There was grated cheese on the table in a jar. Hated that. In a good Italian restaurant the cheese is parmigiana regianno and grated fresh at the table. 

Waiting staff while friendly was not attending to the water glasses being filled. 

Overall, it was a very average experience with nothing gourmet about it. It felt like eating in a Bertuccis masked as Giacomo's. 

They should take some tips from Papparazzi which has a nice experience for a chain. I also think they could learn a lot from Alta Strada in Wellesley that has really great food, and cooked well. 

Im hoping to see some improvement because I would like this restaurant to be a success.

Input: yep, I sure have experienced better. 

So, my boyfriend and I decided to take up the "Free to MA residents" Sunday morning admission. I read the reviews and didn't really expect it to be large or modern. And man, it sure wasn't!

This is more like a couple of rooms of collections. No real hands-on stuff.. and hardly any information, facts, etc next to the display items.

The taxidermy area smelled like a great grandma's attic. The animals were falling apart. 

The glass flower exhibit was set up like a school library... I mean, sure, it's awesome work... but I mean, I just wasn't into staring at fake plant/flower anatomy for more than 5 minutes. Also, these are mostly plants/greens. No brightly colored flowers or anything like that. 

The Mineral Hall is a large room with many minerals on display. Some were amazing. But again, I don't think we spent more than 15 minutes in that room. Kind of repetitive. 

The Arthropod exhibit is what I was mostly interested in seeing and ended up slightly disappointed. They didn't really have the vast collection I thought they would. There wasn't really anything to read when looking at them, either. 

The Climate Change Exhibit I can't really vouch for... we only went in there because a massive amount of kids stormed the gem room and we needed to escape. 

I am with others - I don't understand why Harvard can't update its collections... I mean, the animals were literally falling apart.

I also have no idea how kids would find this exciting for more than 5 minutes.

But hey, It was free.

There are lots of upgrades and updates that need to be made to fully realize its potential.

Input: I came with 4 friends, we wanted to be seated outside so we had to wait a few mins. We sit outside and there's plenty of umbrellas covering the tables. Our waiter was informative and explained the how the restaurant works. Our food was good and he did well checking in on us. 

Then a turn for the worst happened.

 We split our checks, most used cash, half wanted change back, and the other half didn't. He forgot who wanted change and who didn't, so he returned with the cash and said he messed up and forgot. So we begin to explain and he continues to look as if he's trying to remember. So I say "the Oaxaca burger and single burger are the only ones that need change". Calm and helpful right? Nope! His response "ma'am I've been doing this for 8 years, I just need quiet to figure this out." Then he walks away and I'm left stunned. I'm talking at the table about how rude he was and he returns and says "I'm sorry for being rude..." me "yes that was VERY rude" him "well I said I was sorry so you can either take it or leave it". BRUH!!! What in the entire hell?!?! So naturally, I begin to examine how my tone was and I was very calm, so then I realize hey it was just him with his panties in a bunch. I must have reminded him of a girl who broke his heart, circled "no" on his "will you go with me," a girl who cheated on him with his own brother, the girl who packed up her stuff in the middle of the night and left him...who knows! But I KNOW his anger was misplaced. The manager just so happens to come outside, I tell him the story and he apologizes profusely. I still believe he could've done more. I tell him I want all of my change, every penny. He returns with just the dollars...and in ones at that as if I was going to leave a tip. They kept my 23 cents. It seems like all restaurants are doing this now and I don't mind, but in this situation I was pissed. I decided not to be petty and didn't ask for it back though.

Input: I'm kinda done with Andina. Might bring out of town guests here, but I'm otherwise done. 

I have a real problem with having a 7pm reservation and not getting seated until 7:30. 
The noise level in the bar is out of control. 
The menu hasn't significantly changed in years. The vegetarian quinotto has been on there as long as I can remember. Maybe they change it a bit seasonally, but come on. It's good, so don't get me wrong on that front. 
There's no place to wait. So, when you are told your table isn't ready, you have to fight the loud band and 100 other people hoping for a bar table in a walkway used to run food from the kitchen. Then, you have to fight the band, the servers, the other waitees, AND  people trying to get to to bathroom once you pick out your eight square inches to stand. 

The drinks are great. The service is generally attentive, except for the time I was told a dish was vegetarian only to bite into a chunk of ham.  But, to be fair, that was years ago. 

The food on my last visit was meh. The asparagus tasted like grill, not like asparagus. The fried yuca was tasteless.  I know yuca isn't the most flavorful veggie to begin with, but this was like eating deep fried dried blah. The green salad wasn't anything special. 


Every time I go, my stress level goes up about quadruple normal.  The restaurant is SO enormous now, it feels kinda like being in a huge cafeteria.  A huge cafeteria that you are supposed to like because everyone else does.  They are booked out well in advance and I can get more bang for my buck at other places.

Input: I went here with 3 others after a long hike.  It was mid-afternoon, and the place was tucked in a well-hidden plaza near the Arthur Laing bridge beside Penang Delight.

The first comment I have is about the name and concept of the restaurant, which has a distinctly French name... in fact, the name would lead you to believe that it makes several products out of oranges.  However, the menu is a big mismatch - I would describe their cuisine as classic Japanese-style Italian.

I ordered a hamburger steak on beef hash stew spaghetti.  I never really understood hamburger steak; isn't it just a fancy way of saying meatloaf?  In any case, this was ok meatloaf and the stew was ok, but it wasn't unique by any standard.  The flavour lacks a punch of citrus that usually marks a good stew... maybe they could have included an orange wedge?

My sister had tonkatsu don with curry and it was an average dish.  The pork cutlet was just slightly past golden brown, and tasted good.  The curry was strange; it tasted like the spices were not cooked on their own before they were added to the sauce.  My comparison is always to Glico curry cubes which you can buy in any store.

I'm certainly not too impressed.  Maybe the forte of this restaurant lies in its desserts?

Input: Oh boy, I had such high hope for Uchiko since it blew me away the first time I had it when I used to go to UT. So when I came back with my friends celebrate a birthday, I really hyped it up for the group. For short - Do NOT waste your money on the Chef's Tasting menu - instead, order from the actual menu.

As many people have raved about the Chef's Tasting menu at Uchiko, we decided to "Go big or go home" and give it a try with our group. Usually, we'd love Omakase or Tasting Menu since the chefs would be presenting the best/signature dishes in a most creative order, to create an experience for the guests. However, I felt that Uchiko's Tasting Menu was just slapping on average dishes from different sections of the menu without much thought. There wasn't even a list for us to really know the dishes contain as the waiters/waitresses spoke as quick and as soft as they could, so sometimes we just tried the food blindly. 

Overall for the Tasting menu: everything was average (from the Crudo to raw oysters to the suhi). The worst item was the sushi roll - the look was comparable to the taste. The best items were the Chutoro sashimi (melted on my tongue yummy!) and the Peach Okashi (light and refreshing).

Usually you should be full after having a tasting menu--but we actually had to order items off the menu to satisfy our hype for the night. But actually, I was glad we did, because the remaining dishes of the night tasted fantastic, and my face as a foodie was saved! We really enjoyed the Short rib, Pork belly, Brussel sprouts - they were delishhh!!! The foie gras and otoro nigiri were amazing as well! And of course, the Milk & Cereal dessert was out of this world! :) 

It was quite strange that one of our friends got a really bad stomach ache towards the end of the meal - seems unlikely to have been the dishes at Uchiko since everyone else was fine, but I did have to tap into my pharmacy knowledge running to the pharmacy after our meal was over to rescue the poor guy!

Tl;dr: Overall, it was such a disappointment to have tried the tasting menu. I would stick to ordering from the menu!

Input: I was so excited to try out this restaurant since my husband loves eating pate. We thought their sandwiches would be reminiscent of the one he had in Paris since the reviews were so incredibly high. 

There was plenty of parking out in front around lunch time. The shop is pretty small but cute. It was rather busy around 1 pm. 

When it was my turn to order, I asked if their Brie cheese was pasteurized or unpasteurized. He said it was but I did a quick search on my phone to find out that it usually isn't. I also asked if they could cook my lunch meat either in a microwave or on a grill and his only reply was "we don't have a microwave" in a tone that it was beneath him if they did. I get that they are an artisan store and probably wouldn't have one but he made no effort of accommodating to my dietary needs. He should have asked another coworker if the cheese was pasteurized since it was important information to me rather than causally guess that it was. I shouldn't be ingesting unpasteurized cheese as a pregnant person. I was a little annoyed. They should really be more careful on what information they provide. 

The sandwiches were less than memorable. My turkey panini was dry and didn't have very good flavor. I could have made it at home myself in throwing some cheese, turkey and cranberries. I just didn't think it was too special to deserve 4.5 stars worth. In fact, I wished I went to panera bread since you at least get a soup with your sandwiches at their prices. My husband's pate sandwich was also disappointing since the bread was so hard. He said that his jaw and teeth hurt after eating the sandwich. Each bite was a battle with the bread. 

Overall, I was immensely disappointed with my lunch and surprised that Yelp was so far off the mark on this one.

Input: I was looking forward to trying this place as I had seen it plenty of times driving by and when dining next door at Chuy's. A friend and I decided to give it a try for our weekly Wednesday dinner and I was very disappointed. The restaurant itself it nice, it's very modern and trendy. My only complaint about the set up is that it is very dark in the dining room. It was almost hard to read the menu. The few lights they do have have these wicker shells around them which block most of the light. 

I got there first as my friend was running late from an appointment. I was seated right away because they were not very busy and our waiter asked what I wanted to drink. Once he brought the drink he never came back to the table, I was starving and would have liked to order an appetizer to enjoy while waiting on my friend. I sat there for 30 min til she arrived and not once did he reappear to ask if I wanted something while I waited. I figured once she arrived he would come back finally, wrong! We waited another 15 min before finally asking the hostess as she was passing by if she could please find out waiter. He never appeared, another waiter came by and said she would take our order because they weren't sure who our waiter was?? Once we ordered he finally came by after another 10 min to ask if I wanted a drink refilll. I had been there about an hour by the time he reappeared. Once our appetizers finally arrived they were ok, the avocado egg rolls were decent, but the deviled eggs were very runny almost like a soup was places in the eggs.  The runner who finally brought our meals to our table apologized for the wait because the kitchen was "really backed up," strange since the place was pretty empty and It's an open kitchen so we could see our meals sitting under the heat lamp for well over 20 min. My pasta was luke warm by the time it was brought to our table which really ruined the meal. We finished eating and it was another long wait for the waiter to bring us our checks he kept walking right past us but not acknowledging us at all. Once he brought the check he set them down and said, "ok I just want you guys to do one more thing, have a great evening." It was nice of him to say but was weird for him to be saying parting words, when he still needed to return to get our cards and run them. We wondered if he was gonna come back. I don't think he intended too until he noticed us still sitting there waiting 20 min later. I think the restaurant has potential to be good, but this experience did not make me want to give it another try. I felt like I had been there all afternoon, by the time I left.

Input: Lack-Lucster. You're first welcomed by giant chalkboards yelling at you what "don't" and "can't" do. Why not just sit people with a menu? People are packing in trying to figure it out, and when you do the host says "Do you know how to order?" Then you place your order and you're told to get get your own chopsticks, silverware and water. Why? 

The pho is not authentic and bland. In my opinion, if you're going to be a soup nazi (from Seinfeld) then you'd better have some damn fine soup. I'd like to say that they do, but if you've eaten there you know they don't. Cloudy dull tepid broth. Dense balled mat of noodles. Crudely cut rubbery brisket. You know the paper thin rare beef that's supposed to be on top? All grey and lumped in the bottom. The herbs on the side were paltry and oddly stacked so the bean sprouts covered the sprig of basil, lime, and very largely cut jalapeños. This ensures that you have to dig around to get to the then soaked in water herbs. I will on a positive note say I think they make their own meatballs. This is applaudable, but I also know that it's most likely a powder they mix with the unsold tendon.

The place seems to popular. Lots of folks taking pictures of their food. I just think it's good that they take their pics before they eat, because I doubt they'd be that happy about after. Or maybe they're just gluttons for punishment?

Two stars, because they at least served me my food.

Walking up to the restaurant I was in love with all the decor, definitely throwing the Miami vibes with candy skull art, neon art and faux grass walls. A cute little sign next to the front door, "Feed me tacos and tell me I'm pretty". Inside the space looked almost the same from the old Carmel (the restaurant in this space before), although there were a few cool additions, the funky art, cool blue toned walls and an impressive black and white mural on the right wall.

A friend and I visited for lunch, we were given the menus and were told only the small menu was available. Chips and salsa were a given, points for that lol

Since we only had limited options, I just went with the quesadilla, I know in these fancier Mexican restaurants tacos can be on the small side. My hope was to get a more satisfying meal than small tacos but to be frank even my quesadilla was a kids portion size for $11. It was accompanied with a small lettuce, side of salsa and sour cream. It was so unbelievably thin, I thought it was just a cheese quesadilla, the cheese they used was almost nacho style, really runny when biting into it. The dish presentation was really sad.

My friend ordered four tacos, she tried the Chicken Al Pastor, Lava Shrimp, BBQ Pork Belly and Chorizo. Although the tacos weren't too small the filling in each of these tacos were really scarce and cold. I only tried a bite of her shrimp taco and it was really chewy with a poor consistency.

Service was very attentive though, always asking if we needed anything or if we needed more water. I'd give this place 4 stars for the overall vibe and sevice but I'd rate the food as 1 star. Hoping the food will improve once the full menu is available.

Input: Maybe I'm a masochist for trying out very "traditional Americanized" Chinese restaurants, but part of it reminds me of my childhood. At any rate, I dragged my boyfriend to this place, and the experience was very subpar.

After getting seated in the corner, it took them about 10 minutes to come back and take our order. Okay, whatever, you have a lot of takeout orders. I guess I can forgive that.

After ordering, it was a good 15 - 20 minutes before getting the food. I know how a wok works, so it shouldn't take that long unless you're prepping your ingredients alongside. Maybe it's the amount of takeout orders slowing it down, but who knows?

We finally get our order of almond chicken and mapo tofu with two tiny bowls of rice. The food's pretty decent, though you can definitely taste the "cheapness" of the chicken. The mapo tofu was pretty solid; using black bean paste in the recipe is a nice variation. As other reviewers have mentioned, the portions are huge, so we easily had leftovers for the next night. 

After some more waiting, we finally got our check, and to our shock, we were charged for two tiny bowls of rice for $1.00 each. I can forgive waiting exceedingly long for service, and I can overlook the flavor in the chicken. I cannot accept them not informing us that rice cost extra.

tl;dr: If you do take-out, which I would probably recommend over the dine-in experience, make your own rice.

Input: We were heading to Disney for a couple of days so I asked my husband to book us a water park hotel (just stayed at one the previous month in Orlando). He found this on a booking site and it looked like fun. 

When we got here they said we didn't have to pay the $13 resort fees, which we thought we had to pay, based on the booking site. So that was a perk, but we soon discovered nothing is really free unless you do their sales pitch breakfast.

We had a renovated room which was really nice, had some ants and was an odd shape since it was in the corner, but we liked it.

We planned to spend check in day at the water park. 6pm we walk over there to be told it's $20 a person to get in and they close at 7! 

We went back to the pool next to our room.  It was nice and warm, but wasn't the waterpark we anticipated.

I am self employed and went to answer emails really quick and found that you must pay $10 per device to log in. We weren't told this. 

I needed to call the front desk and found the phones, while connected, had no dial tones. This probably saved us from sales pitches though!

The bed was super hard and killed my back.

Also our room overlooked the pool on the ground floor and the master room only has blinds, not black out curtains, which made it hard to sleep-in with the 24/7 lights lighting up the pool and yard areas.

The tram to the theme parks seamed like a great perk, but you can't come back on any tram headed here, if you get on the 10am to the park, you have to come back on the 6pm tram, you can't take the later one.

Our building seamed half full if that, bit parking spots at night were hard to come by.

The room was a great price on goseek.com, $62, but we were expecting a lot more based on the listing. They should have been more up front about fees, we would have gladly spent $20-30 more per night for a hotel that had a water play area.

Input: I enjoy going to concerts at most venues, but not the Biltmore. Every time I hear of a band I like coming to town and then see they are playing there I let out a long sigh as if to resign myself to having to be in that space. Knowing if they played somewhere else the experience would be so much better. 

Perhaps part of the problem is that this space does not appear to have been designed for playing concerts. The stage is centered between two hallways which lead to the washroom facilities. The stage itself is very low and is usually curtained along the sides.  Another issue I have is that the sound is ok when it is good and terrible when it is bad. I have actually left a concert early at this venue due how crappy a particular band I really like sounded. Trust me I need a good reason to leave a concert. Also, yes the décor is 'funky', but the space is also funky in the sense I don't want to touch anything. I would hate to see the place when the turn the ugly lights on. That and what is with the line up situation outside. More than once I have shown and there is a huge line up outside of people with and without tickets that isn't moving. Then have walked up to the front of the line feeling the daggers in my back from the people I pass to ask if it was ok to go in as I had a ticket. The door man quickly steps aside and lets us enter only to find out there is hardly anyone inside. They need to coordinate the front door a little bit better. A sign or two would suffice.

I do like how you can get up close and personal with the band. Although I have seen bands that look a bit uncomfortable and have commented during their performance on how distracting it is to see people walk past to the bathroom in their peripheral vision. However, the price must be right to put on a show here or groups wouldn't keep coming back. That and the bar tenders are always fast and efficient and the selection isn't half bad or overpriced.

Input: New to the neighborhood, we'd been looking forward to trying Kome, hoping we could add it to our regular roster. Food was fine, but the behavior of the host and management made sure our first visit would be our last.

5:20PM on a weeknight, my wife arrives with two hungry, summer-heat-wilted teens. I'm on my way separately, about 10 minutes out. She asks to be seated and is refused (incomplete party). She asks again -- look, it's really empty; we're hot, hungry and tired, and really want to get our order in. Host consults with management. The verdict: "Yeaaaah ... that really STRESSES us, so ... no."

First ... we're a family of four. They'd seat the first three of us at a four-top anyway. It's not like we were a gaggle of office workers trickling in, pushing tables together and slowly expanding over two hours. And they're a small-plates restaurant -- ostensibly they WANT us to order more! So seat my family already and let them get started!

Second ... why should I care about (or even HEAR about, for that matter) the "stress level" of any restaurant, let alone a premium-priced one?

Finally ... you know what stresses ME out? Arriving to find my family huddled in the hot waiting area while 60% of the tables sit empty, no food on the way, and an awful lot of non-stressed staffers lining the walls.

Food was tasty, waitress was competent but distant. No manager stopped by to see how things were, nobody asked if we enjoyed our experience. Dropped our 75 bucks and left.

You know, you can love your policy, or you can love your customer. Thankfully, Austin is rife with other restaurants who go out of their way to let you know your business is appreciated.

Input: I was pretty psyched about this place because of all the hype my friends gave it, so I decided to give it a try. I didn't know what to get but knew I wanted a wrap, so I decided to get the special they had of the day which was the lamb kabab.

When I ordered, I asked the cashier what was inside the kabab since I don't really tomatoes and what not. She told me there was lettuce, onions, and tomatoes, so I asked her to only put the lettuce inside with my kabab since I don't like raw onions or tomatoes. My boyfriend got the beef shawarma, and we also ordered hummus, an extra pita bread, and fries with the sauces on the side. After I finished paying, I looked at my receipt and saw she charged me for the lamb kabab on rice. When I went back to the counter to tell her, she said she would just change it to the kabab. I'm not sure how much the price difference is, but I feel like $9 for a lamb kabab is p pricey.

When I got my food, she forgot to give us the sauce on the side for the fries. Once I got home, I was pretty disappointed that the wraps weren't labeled. I basically opened it and hopped it was mine. Once I took the first bite of my lamb kabab, of course, there were onions, tomatoes, as well as cucumbers in my wrap. This would be absolutely horrific if I was actually allergic to any of those instead of just disliking it. Not only did the cashier get my order wrong and charge me for the lamb kebab over rice, she still got my order wrong and it had the onions, tomatoes, and cucumbers in there. As for the beef shawarma wrap, the meat was cold. It was so strange, but it was. It also didn't come with lettuce or anything. It was just the beef shawarma, tomatoes, and sauce. 2 stars. My boyfriend didn't even finish it because it was so below par (and he usually finishes everything including my food). The fries were okay. It wasn't crispy. It was p soft and p thick. The only thing I actually enjoyed was the hummus and pita bread. It had a nice flavor and creamy texture.

Tbh, the lamb kebab wasn't too bad, but I won't come back again because my order was wrong, the beef shawarma was cold, and the cashier honestly didn't pay attention to anything I said or asked for. This place has such good ratings, but for me, it was mediocre at best (which is a shame because my friends raved about it so much).

Input: Just finished eating dinner at Asta and all I can say is HUH?
Service and ambience were 8/10, but the food was one of the most underwhelming we've ever had. 
My boyfriend and I came in an hour earlier than our reservation and were seated because the restaurant was quite empty. The waitress poured us some complimentary sparkling because it is the holidays after all and we were excited to start the meal.
We both had the 8 course tasting menu and it took roughly 2.5 hours from start to finish. The time between courses were long and the portion size was tiny (yes, tiny even for someone who can barely finish an entree size pasta at another restaurant).
The amuse bouche was salty, the turnip dish though garnished with truffle did not smell nor taste anything like truffle, and the venison was covered in burnt ash that was way too overwhelming and bitter. The cheese dish was great and I wish there was more since it was ONE ravioli. Apart from that, I can barely remember any other dishes because they all tasted the same. 
The menu was mostly vegetable dishes, actually, 6/8 were vegetarian.
I don't want to give such a bad review, but for $110 a head without drinks or tip, it is insanely overpriced. I have had 8 course dinner before for much less and the quality of food that I experience today at Asta is inferior to say the least. The vision was there but the food was not.
I hope they will change up the menu, or hopefully do something different to reflect their price point and vision, it's safe to say I won't be back any time soon.

Pros: They open later than most salon. The wait is quick on my visit.

The story:

After getting a foot massage from Yuren I decided to get a hair cut as well. But it was 7PM on Sunday so most hair salon has been closed. I used Yelp and find out this place is still open. I decide to give this place a shot. The location isnt hard to find but be aware of parking. When i walked in there are no client there and the front desk mid age lady also the hair washer was playing with her phone while listening to an old fashion Chinese music. She saw and look at her phone to pause something on it and ask me wash and cut? i said yes. She then direct me to get my hair washed. While she was testing the water temperature, she kept looking at her phone. When she was washing my hair she constantly looking at her phone as she was multi-tasking. She washed 2 times and condition one times as it supposed to be. I can tell she has been doing the for pretty long time but she didnt use at least 70% just plainly muscle memories though times. There are still some part i would still like to work on but there are no words, she was too busy to play slot-game on her phone. (I found out later while she was washing other client's hair and she put the phone straight up.) Anyway the person who cuts my hair doesnt seems to speak English as well. So i spoke Mandarin with him in-case of misunderstanding and my hair suffer. But then i think they spoke Cantonese but understand a bit Mandarin. Anyway, as usual i told the hairdresser to leave my side longer to cover my ear, he cuts it a bit too short and his cutting style isnt smooth. Based on his movement he is probably at intermediate level who only cut less than three years. I have thick hair and he didnt thin it enough. I probably will have to thin it more after i go home.... 

I have to admit, My hair isnt the easiest to cut and I am pretty picky on my own way. I feel like the stylist strength is army cut hair style. Anyway in the end i still tip the hairdresser and the hair washer. While i gave the tips to the hair washer lady, she was eating dinner. She did said thank you but in an in-sincere way. Personally i cut myself hair better than the one he gave me. But i don't want to make a mess in the bathroom and i have no time... ok i will be honest, there are also laziness in the factor. I will not recommend this place however i will also not discourage because everyone is different, they may be a good match for your style but not mine. Good thing that they open late, that is their asset, if you need a quick hair cut with ok looking or just make it short when you dont have major parties or showing your appearance in front of social media you may consider this place, after all, hair will grow back! Good luck out there adventurers!
