Input: I am still looking for good Tex-Mex in Austin.  And I feel stoopid saying that.  Maudie's Cafe isn't it.  

The service was indifferent. In...  out...  buh bye, kthxbye.  

The margs were good, but $4.75 seems steep for the size compared to what I'm used to paying at my local haunts in Houston.  And when I ordered a second, the server took my glass and disappeared even though it wasn't empty.  WTF?  

The salsa. was heavy with chipotle and tomato.  I'd like to see some cilantro, some tomatillo...  It was like chipotle-Pace.  OK, but pretty stock.  

We ordered queso and sliced jalapenos as a starter. The queso was actually beschemel sauce with cheese in it.  I guess flour, butter and milk is cheaper than cheese.  It was fine for what it was, but it was not queso.  The jalapenos arrived in a bowl, with no plates or anything.  The small slices were fine, but I wanted to cut up the bigger ones to make them go farther.  I did that on the table surface.  The server came by twice and saw me doing this and didn't offer a plate.  Yeah, I could have asked...

 The flour tortillas were factory mass-produced, rubbery and perfectly circular.  They felt kind of waxy and tasted bland.

My wife ordered the shrimp fajitas, which were pretty expensive.  She liked them.  I thought the dish was heavy on bell peppers and that the shrimp were really unseasoned.  

But the shrimp fajitas were great compared to my chicken enchiladas.  The verda sauce was tasty, and it's a good thing, because that was the only thing in the dish that was seasoned.  The tortillas were the afore mentioned mc-tortillas.  The shredded chicken was basically boiled chicken.  No seasoning at all.

Like I said, I'm still looking for good Tex-Mex in Austin.  And judging from the reviews on Yelp, so are a lot of other folks.

Input: True story: My first week in Boston and freshly arrived from California, I descended into the Dugout with my new school friend, Carl, an old-fashioned redneck from North Carolina.  Carl ordered a Bud; I asked for a pina colada.  The bartender, a tough-looking guy with arms like a stevedore, leaned across the bar, set his face inches from mine, looked me in the eye with obvious distaste and said, "We don't serve pussy drinks here." While it may be five stars in my heart, the Dugout's a dive and it doesn't pretend to be anything but a dive.  You can't give a dive five stars--it defeats the whole purpose!

But this is no one-star dive like PJ Kilroy's.  Two stars all the way, baby!

Input: I went in for the first meeting and met with the owner. He was very nice and I felt like he really got to know me and what I was looking for. We chatted for about an hour. I was annoyed that these women hadn't even met me and they were the ones finding matches for me. Not him. 
I was then set up with a couple of guys who were really nice but I wasn't attracted to them. I only had one bad date with a guy who lacked social skills and with whom I had absolutely nothing in common. It was then that I started to realize that they weren't taking my profile into account when matching me up. They definitely would not have matched me with this guy if that were the case.
I had been told that they would take my feedback and use it to make better picks in the future. This was not the case. When I told my advisor about my experience with Mr. No Social Skills, she quickly replied, "well, how about this guy? I just happen to have his file on my desk right now." This was another guy that I clearly had little in common with. I truly think they just match you up with whoever they have to give more dates to in order to reach their membership minimum within the shortest amount of time.
While I met a couple of nice guys, I ended up putting my membership on hold and never went back for my two final dates to reach my guaranteed 5 date minimum. I was too annoyed. Input: Brought my 2002 Mazda Tribute in when it started getting rumbly. I already knew cylinder 2 wasn't firing properly and something needed replacing. They replaced my spark plugs, a couple other minor things and charged me $190 for a new ignition coil. 
When I got the car back it was still doing the same thing, so I took it to a mechanic I had used before and he almost immediately notice that yes #2 was in bad shape but #4 looked brand new! They had failed to look up the proper number order and replaced the wrong thing. My hometown mechanic went ahead and replaced all of the other ignition coils (at $70 each) and I got the right fix for about $150 less than what Honest-1 charged me to not fix it.

Input: We don't shop here much, but it is a decent place to find specialty items and different things than the chain stores offer. If you're after routine items like milk, produce, pet food, and box dinners, go to the chain stores; they'll be much cheaper.  If you're after local-grown produce or odd items or smaller brands, Weilands might have them.

(Seriously, they sell major-brand cheap pet food at a higher cost than their competitors. Even the nearby IGA on Oakland is better-priced. You'd think with billing themselves as a specialty grocery, they'd offer specialty pet food brands. But I digress.)

With that said, buyer beware. We've caught them twice now in substituting cheaper cheese for a more-expensive brand -- unfortunately, we didn't catch the sub until the cheese had been grated or sliced, which was too late to return it.

Specifically, what they label as "parmesan reggiano" IS NOT PARMESAN REGGIANO. It tastes NOTHING like real PR, and I'm guessing it's either asiago or a mild romano -- maybe a domestic parmesan from Wisconsin -- but it's not the real Parmesan Reggiano. The real PR has a very distinctive flavor & a hard, dark-yellow rind with "parmesan reggiano" engraved into it.  Some stores cut the rinds off & sell them separately, as most folks will throw them away anyway (tip: simmer the rinds in spag sauce), and that's ok, BUT that rind is the ONLY way to be sure that's the real deal, without opening the package and tasting before you buy.

Weilands, of course, didn't have the rind in the package. That didn't set off any red flags with us at first, for reasons stated above. BUT the cheese in question was the wrong texture/consistency (real PR is a semi-hard cheese that grates easily; what we got was distinctly softer), wrong smell, and wrong taste. In other words, WEILANDS WRAPPED A CHEAPER CHEESE AND SOLD IT AT THE HIGHER REAL-PR PRICE.

TWICE. TWICE.

The first time might have been a labeling mistake. We didn't want to accuse a store we liked of fraud, either. But the second time, a month later? No. That's deliberate. By International Law, only one type of cheese can be sold as Parmesan Reggiano, and that's the stuff straight from Italy, which is NOT what Weiland's is labeling and selling.

Shame on you, Weilands.  We're not regular customers, but you've still lost our business.

Input: This was my fifth time here through the years. When I first came here many years ago I was blown away by the hugeness of the buffet with a great selection of Chinese, Japanese , Korean and American foods.
It still has a large selection of different foods but the quality has taken a toll to the point where I don't desire to go back anymore.
Orlando is known to have an abundance of Chinese buffets, all mediocre at best.
Koy Wan was different. It had quality.
All of these buffets start out great and go steadily down hill until customers stop coming and eventually the restaurant dies and goes out of business.
I gave Koy Wan two stars due to the shear abundance and variety of foods.
About thirty five kinds of sushi, sashimi and negri. These were pretty good but not great. Soups including egg drop, wonton. miso and seafood. Wontons were very heavy with meat that was tasteless and too starchy. Hot foods like clams in black bean sauce were bland. Frog legs were deep fried and over breaded. Spare ribs were slabs of fatty pork or beef, not the usual type of ribs often found in Chinese restaurants. Lo mein and chow fun were good. Korean beef was thin and tasteless.
General Chow and Sesame chicken were tasty.
Tea was one dollar per person extra.
Service was mediocre as well. I had to get up numerous times to flag down a waitress for more water and tea.
Ambiance is nice with multi rooms to dine in.
In all fairness, I cannot recommend this place.
When in Orlando, be smart and stay away from buffets. A sit down Chinese restaurant is a better choice and search out Yelp for reviews before venturing out to eat.

We decided to sit outside because it was a nice day, there were three open tables and they were all dirty. So we ended up bussing our own table. Eh. 

Duck confit nachos: great idea in theory, totally lacking in execution. They were kind of cold. Lacking a lot of duck. Could have been waaaay better. Especially for $12. 

Since you have to go inside to order (I knew this before coming here, so whatever) my darling boyfriend let me order on his behalf. I got him the quiche of the day, however I left the menu outside. In my opinion, quiche is quite heavy and tastes the best with salad. Which is what I thought it came with. The bartender asks me "Do you want it with hash?" and I reply "what are my other options?" and he goes "You want it with hash." But the thing is, I DIDN'T WANT IT WITH HASH. However, since I didn't have the menu, I didn't really know what to do and kind of panicked and the bartender disappeared.... sigh. So, my boyfriend was disappointed with his meal. And the hash. Ugh. 

We also tried the grilled ham and cheese, and the hot dog, and those were both considerably good. Pretty much the only thing that saved this place from one star in my book.

While I don't mind going inside to order, I do mind having dirty plates and glasses sitting on my table for an extended period of time. We had an obscene amount of flies that wouldn't leave us alone due to this. Not very fun. 

And then there's the tip situation. What do I tip? You brought me the food, yes. You bussed my table after we got the check? No one really waited on us? But then I hate tipping low? And our check was super high for what we received, this place is not exactly cheap.

Sitting inside here for a snack and a few drinks would probably be a way better experience. 
If you're looking for a sit-down meal, I would pass this place by.

Input: I bought a Groupon and went here last week. Zagat rated??? Hmmmm. I'm reconsidering my trust in Zagat; this is my 2nd disappoint from them this year for GA recognized. Zagat NYC is not much better. 

My husband and I ordered 3 dishes (tilapia, curry, and pad see ew) between the 2 of us and a soup and a salad. The Tom Yum soup came out hot but nothing to write home about. The atmosphere was bland and IKEA looking, walls were a little too yellow and made me feel like I was in a bucket of mustard paste.  The tilapia was overcooked and expensive for such a small portion. The Masaman curry sauce was pretty decent but it's typical Thai fare you can get at any other restaurant. What disappointed me the most was the Pad See Ew. I was so excited that I saw this on the menu bc I haven't had it since my Seattle days. Pad See Ew has broccoli in it. I asked the server 4 times if it did because that is how I remembered it. She says "YES": it is broccoli stirred fried with noodles. The Pad see ew I got that night had 1 very small slither of broccoli, noodles, a few very thin slices of carrots. I looked at my one piece of broccoli in astonishment as it was slightly yellow and cut so thin. This one little cut of a broccoli crown was sliced probably in 8 ways before 1 of the 8 slices got to me. I was floored. My husband looked at me and laughed and said, I guess that is what the server meant by 'Yes' it has broccoli. Are you kidding me?

I don't recommend going to this place; not worth your hard earned dollars. Also, the location is almost scary. We had to go to two different parking lots to make sure we parked in the right place and had to bring my husband's laptop inside the restaurant because there is a BIG sign that says "We are not responsible for any belongings". (AKA beware because this neighborhood is not SAFE).

Input: I was sure I would buy my wedding dress from Charlotte's. They have a great selection and a beautiful space. However, my consultant made me feel very uncomfortable purchasing a dress from Charlotte's. She was insincere and only ever spoke to my family to shut down any opinions that did not match my own. I did, however, find a dress that I loved. We had half an hour left in the appointment when I found "the one" and everyone loved it. My future mother-in-law saw a dress on a mannequin she wanted to see me in, because she thought I would love it. She was so nice to come and only ever said sweet things so I wanted to try the dress for her, but the consultant interrupted, asking if I felt like I had to try on more dresses and completely disrespecting my future mother-in-law's wishes. I was so embarrassed. The consultant then kept pressuring me to take measurements and fill out the paperwork to order the dress. She told me I had to order the dress that day because ship dates were changing and if I waited I'd have to pay a rush fee and may not get my dress altered in time. My wedding was eight months away and I would be shocked if the gown wasn't delivered, altered, pressed and beautiful by my wedding, even if I waited the few days  the consultant said I couldn't afford. At this point I was already starting to feel like a dollar sign and an inconvenience and now I wondered if I was being taken advantage of.  I could tell my whole family was uncomfortable and I wanted to leave so I filled out the paperwork and went to order the dress, but my mom took me aside and asked if I would mind purchasing the wedding dress from a different shop. She was made uncomfortable by the pushy and insincere consultant and also worried that we were being misled  about the delivery time
so we decided to buy the dress in a shop out of state.

I will not be going back to Charlotte's as I do not think it is an honest business invested in treating its customers with respect and integrity. They do have a great selection and I did find my bridesmaids, mother of the bride and groom, and flower girl dresses at Charlotte's, but will be buying them from different shops. I feel bad, but they are not inexpensive purchases and I want to feel secure working with stores that will be supplying such important things for our wedding.

Input: This is an "ok" apartment run by very unintelligent people. First, it's just faux nice. They're so obsessed with conveying class that they put embarrassing carpeting in the elevators that say "Style follows you home." In fact, the walls are extremely thin, the cabinetry looks and feels like Ikea, and the amenities are just not very nice. For instance, the grills are always disgusting, and the pool is only a couple of feet deep. Also, my view is of a giant Phipps parking lot. And the blinds do nothing. And cell-coverage in this concrete eyesore is virtually non-existent. While they suggested once they would "consider" installing a solution to this cell service issue, it appears that since this might not be a concern of prospective guests (only actual residents), they declined to address the issue.

More importantly, despite this mirage of class, the property management team is really just ill-suited to manage anything. In a maintenance request where I suggested that I thought my toilet was not working properly, they chose to inform me that this was just the nature of the ultra-modern ultra-low flow toilets they installed. In fact, there was a crack in the base of the toilet which ultimately resulted in poop water spilling out onto my floor.

They have also instituted very bad parking policies because they seemingly enjoy messing with their residents. While the previous management team actually attempted to make new policies known (albeit, only via Email) with prominent subjects like, "Parking Changes," the new manager, Jim Stabler, opted evidently to impose new policies in a "Community Update," next to very crucial information like, "One of our property managers is leaving! Wish her well!" and "We are having a dinner!" and "We have Yoga!" This new policy made it so that, despite the ample parking in the building, guests need to park their cars, walk inside to the concierge, get a pass, and walk back to their car to put the pass in their car --no matter where they park. Indeed, despite announcing this policy so prominently in "Community Updates," they chose to leave "Visitor Parking" signs up misleading unsuspecting guests into thinking that this distinction might actually be meaningful. Apparently "Visitor Parking" signs are left up because they prefer people with guest passes to park in those spots first.

Indeed, although they are capable of physically posting signs about the unbelievable amenity of mini-muffins on Fridays, they couldn't actually take the time to post signs explaining that "Visitor Parking" actually doesn't mean that visitors can park there without a pass. I suppose a sign that says, "Pseudo-Visitor Parking" might detract from the faux classy aesthetic though. And yet, Jim Stabler evidently thinks that not only are these signs appropriate, there's no issue in casually booting Residents' guests and forcing them to wait 90 minutes. It's strange to live in a building where the management views current tenants as adversaries.

Input: Wow, this Chuck E. Cheese has definitely changed since I last stepped foot in here as a kid, to the point where I barely recognized it. I came today for my nephew's third birthday party.  Granted it has been over 15 years since I've been here, and I understand change is inevitable, but this place looked so empty and not like the fun and exciting place I looked forward to as a kid. 

The amount of games and play structures have decreased tremendously. I would say there are about a third of the machines left that use to be there. The huge jungle gym structure and ball pit have been removed. This place honestly looks sad. 

A lot of the machines and games were out of tickets and one of the machines that take photos were out of the paper. There use to be game attendants on the floor replacing these things. The birthday boy wanted to take a photo on the machine that was out of photo paper, but even after asking for it to be replaced, it was never replaced. A lot of game credits were wasted on these games/machines. 

Food is not really good here either, and it's also expensive. $20 for a medium sized pizza that tastes like it came from the frozen aisle of a grocery store. 

Also, the back half of this place where the reserved tables are held was extremely cold in temperature. It was just that one particular area, everywhere else was normal temperature. This was really odd. 

Two stars because I kind of feel bad. It is not really the staff that is at fault. I think the chain/franchise itself has gone downhill. I would recommend Dave & Buster's over this place. I don't plan on coming back here.

Input: I take my fried chicken pretty seriously. First of all, outside of Church's and KFC, fried chicken is surprisingly difficult to find. Sure, there are plenty of restaurants serving fried chicken breast or chicken fried chicken, but that's like kissing your brother. Real fried chicken has both meat and bones. Together.  On each piece. Emphasis on meat. 

Secondly, I can't make a habit out of eating fried chicken if I want to maintain this girlish figure. So I consider it a special treat for those times when nothing else will satisfy that ubiquitous craving. 

It was for these reasons that I decided to venture down to SOCO for some MRS P's. I had tried this place once before when it was on Rainey St. But that was a while ago and I think alcohol was involved. Mostly, I remember my son telling me how great it was. So I was excited to go pick up a 12 piece bucket to share with the fam. Key word here is bucket, which per the KFC precedent would imply an assortment of chicken pieces like breasts, thighs, drumsticks and a couple of superfluous  wings. 

You can imagine my disappointment upon returning to my home and unpacking the "bucket" only to discover 12 pieces of overcooked chicken parts that included 8 wings, 2 tiny drumsticks and 2 mystery pieces of boneless hunks. To be more accurate I wasn't disappointed so much as pissed off. Considering I paid $37 (which included 2 things of Mac n cheese) I expected more. Wouldn't you? No, because you are smart enough to read reviews BEFORE rather than AFTER trying a place. 

So, if you're a tourist hanging out around SOCO, likely enamored with the food truck concept, and you want a little chicken snack then by all means give it a go. It will be made to order and hot. But if you like traditional fried chicken with recognizable parts both meaty and bony, you best go elsewhere. Like your home town.

Input: These folks get two stars because, well, technically here I am, and nothing is broken. And I want to be as fair as possible.

Three years ago I used Eagle Lines to help me get from the Boston area to Austin TX. They were very good--so when I was looking to do the same move in reverse, I had no question about who to hire. A lot can change in a few years; I know that more than anyone.

Eagle Lines acknowledges that moving across the country is stressful. I believe they even market themselves as being a company that takes stress out of a move. If you're a go-with-the flow, flexible type of person, that's probably true: but then again if that were true, you wouldn't be very stressed about a move anyway, would you?

What I mean by flexible is this: If you don't really have to be out of a place within a certain time-frame (e.g. need to coordinate being out for a lease or a house closing), if you have a few grand or so extra to plunk down (without solid explanation as to where it's going or what forms of payment are acceptable), if you're not big on estimates or communication about what's happening (without investing your time in repeat emails / phone calls, etc. that may or may not be returned), if you're cool with multiple, random people contacting you as part of the move (without much identification or without leaving messages when you're not available), and with lots of pretty beat up boxes that make you cringe upon opening, then this is probably a good company for you to hire.

To end on a positive note I'll give some kudos to David, the main guy on delivery. Of course none of this was his fault--he was friendly and he did a good job. Another positive is that the time it took for our things to arrive was pretty quick. Good luck.

Input: Ahhhh Monumental Movieland. After calling just about every single hotel in the area and finding they were completely booked we ended up here. If I were to sum this hotel up in one word it would be cheap. As we are walking down the stale smelling hallways I'm staring at the movie and show posters. They were covered in dust. Why not clean them up a little to look presentable for the guests? I know they're old, but sheesh.
We finally enter our room. It had the same stale smell as the hallway. To be expected. Now comes the inspection.The bed frame wasn't an actual bed frame. You could see they've built it themselves. Not that this matters, but maybe that's the reason the bed was so uncomfortable? To make matters worse before bedtime I hear "what the heck is this?" And I turn to see my friend holding up what is supposed to be a pillow, but looks like a sack with a bunch of clothes in it. Seriously. Shower time might have been the funniest part of the hotel. I am totally aware hotels give you the crappiest little bottles of soap but this was just ridiculous. The bar of "soap" stuck to my body and the "body wash" smelled like plastic. Not even pretend soap, just plastic. My friend said he recommended staying far away from it because it must not be healthy or even safe. I couldn't help but chuckle.
I definitely regret not bringing my own towels because they provide you with sandpaper. The towel was literally scratching my body. 
I probably wouldn't stay here again unless I brought my own things to make up for this. Actually, I probably wouldn't stay here at all. I did not have a completely horrible stay, but there are far better hotels for the same price in the area.

Input: I really wanted to like Darryl's, but I came here with some friends last weekend, and we had the following experiences:

--My friend ordered the mussels, and one of them was bad.  She vomited.  (I could probably stop my review here.)

--I also ordered mussels.  There was sand in a lot of them.

--We had made reservations for dinner (and there was no mention of a cover charge), but when the bill came, we were charged for the cover.  (As a group, we spent $200+ before tip.)

--We had a bar tab before we were seated, and when we asked for the bar tab to be transferred to our table, the servers/hosts could not manage that.

--Moreover, my friend had left his credit card at the bar with the bar tab, and they wouldn't even return his credit card to him when he asked for it.  (He asked for it *so that he could pay the bill.*)  In fact, my friend had to get up and discuss the situation with several employees.  (They offered him a free drink for the confusion, which seems like an odd response.  There were six of us waiting for the bill to be figured out, and they offered one person a free drink?  So we would have to sit around some more?)

--Two members of our group ordered burgers cooked medium-rare.  The burgers were actually cooked all the way through and were very salty.

--Our table was about three feet from the band, so we felt like we were seated in the middle of the dance floor--there were people dancing on three sides of our table.  At one point, the *hostess* (not a customer!) was leaning against my friend's chair (she was gripping the back of the chair) so that my friend couldn't lean back!

The only reasons I rate this place two stars instead of one: the music was fun (although loud); the drinks were strong; the host was friendly to me; and our waitress was fine.

We placed our order and off he went. To start our meal we were given a loaf of sidewalk chalk with maple syrup. Oh sorry I meant bread with honey, it was hard to tell the difference. For dinner I ordered the fried chicken and my husband had the lamb chops. Fried chicken was tasty but not worth the $23 price tag for one piece. Lamb chops were edible but tasted like the one's that are frozen on sale at the grocery store.

The whole time we were there we were listening to other skippers and tables laughing, joking and having a great time. Ours wouldn't even come back to get us a drink refill let alone tell a joke or hang out for a minute. I never finished my meal because I was dying of thirst with an empty glass the whole time.  Couldn't flag down anyone because no one would even make eye contact. 

We paid left and will never return! Come on Magic Kingdom get it together.

Input: There was a dark time last year when mice ran wild throughout our apartment.  They came in through a little hole behind the fridge and took up residence in all the dark, secluded spots in our home.  We got home from vacation and there they all were...having a little vacation of their own.  

I called maintenance and it took them a week to come and fix the hole.  A week!  The reason it took them so long?  They had to answer calls of people who had lost their heat first.  Death by hypothermia trumps animal kingdom, I get that.  But the woefully understaffed maintenance is just the first example of the problems with the Samia properties.

The heat in winter is a huge problem.  Whenever it's really cold, it doesn't come on.  The rest of the time, our apartment is so hot we have to open all the windows.  I loathe wasting so much energy but I also loathe dying of heatstroke.

The bathroom is kind of ridonkulous.  There's no ventilation and as far as I can tell their solution is to paint over the mold that accumulates.  But since it hasn't been painted in three years large swathes of paint break off and litter the floor, exposing the grodiness beneath.  Also, the toilet doesn't really fit so there's a piece cut out of the bottom of the door so you can shut it!

They do reactive repairs, but I'm willing to bet this whole building is full of places like mine that need some serious renovation.  One of the walls has a jagged crack starting 1/2way and going all the way across to the ceiling.  The walls are thin and I can hear everything my neighbors are doing - luckily the woman who had sex in her extremely squeaky bed every Friday night (when I was working Saturdays) from 11 - 11:15 exactly has moved out.

Most of the time this place is OK, and I guess I'd rather be sweating in winter than freezing.  It will be nice, though, when we eventually have a place where we can have the toaster and the air conditioner going at the same time.

Input: Sadly, this is an update to my previous 5 star "glowing" review of A&B, once my favorite place in Salem. I've been there as AB has grown from counter service to table service to full fledged "restaurant" with full bar and outdoor seating. Their menu grew but was always good and the service was always top notch... Until now.

On my most recent visit - a few weeks ago, the experience was SO different that I actually thought AB had been sold to a new proprietor. AB started out super vegan friendly- 3 vegan burgers, vegan shakes... It's was truly the coolest place around and I thought it was amazing that they were so in tune with catering to all diet types (veg, vegan, gluten free, meat free, traditional) ... Bit by bit things began to change. The vegan shakes were the first to go. "We can't find a supplier, but we are looking for a new one" they told me; that was 3 years ago I think! 

Back to my most recent visit... I quickly noticed the menu had changed. 3 vegan burgers were now 2 and the lineup of traditional burgers was different. The sweet potato burger, which was amazing, was gone. I reluctantly ordered one of the vegan burgers, though had to get a lettuce wrap since they were "all out" of the gluten free/vegan buns. My friend ordered a bacon cheeseburger. When our food arrived, my little burger sadly wrapped in a warm, limp piece of romain was all alone - no chips. I inquired only to find out that the homemade potato chips are cooked in the same oil as all the fried meat and chicken and are therefore not vegan (not even vegetarian)! My friend didn't even finish her burger - she said it was just "ok". 

I spoke briefly to a manager about the changes. It was obvious she didn't really care and used excuses such as "seasonal produce" -- hmm, pretty sure sweet potatoes are not seasonal, also pretty sure that vegan/gluten free buns are available all year as well ... And frying potato chips in chicken grease is a business decision and not one dictated by season.

She thought I would be pacified by knowing the spring menu would have new "seasonal" veggies and more salads. It makes me sad that in a city as cool and progressive as Salem, what once seemed to be the coolest place to eat has succumb to typical corporate greed and money saving shortcuts regardless of whether or not they compromise the integrity of the establishment. Fortunately, Salem is always changing - so if AB has had its "15 minutes" there will soon be someone else to take over as the cool place to go in town.

Input: South Congress Cafe has a great location and a great vibe-upscale diner with a nice bar. 

My boyfriend and I were wandering SoCo looking for a place to eat on a Wednesday night and were drawn in by the curb appeal of South Congress Cafe. Unfortunately the appeal stopped at the curb.

We were sitted and asked what we wanted to drink. We seemed to lose our waiters interest the moment we asked for only water to drink. (Lots of folks had full bottles of wine on their table and what waiter doesn't want 20% of that!). He was apathetic and seemed uninterested in answering questions.The menu is interesting and looks chef driven so we were trying to generate a bit of conversation about it. But maybe because we are older and tee totallers, he didn't seem interested and gave us shortest answers possible.

We shared the lamb enchiladas. (Maybe another thing that annoyed him was our sharing a entree.) All I can say is "Eww".  For starters the sides were plain white rice and squash. When I say PLAIN, I mean plain white rice-like not even hot and not so much as a grain of salt on the rice for seasoning. And the rice tasted better than the squash. I don't know how to describe the squash dish except raw and rancid. The squash was cubed and crunchy-not sure it had actually been cooked. Then the taste would best be described as "rancid". Either what the squash was "cooked" in or the squash itself had gone off and it was clearly "off". We did not eat either side. The lamb inside the enchilida was stringy, salty (we found where all the salt went!) and unrecognizably lamb. All gross.

We told our kindly waiter and he replied (over his shoulder), "I'll tell someone". Sure you will, kid.

Input: CHECKED OUT

I love the Homewood Suites.  It is one of my favorite hotels for many reasons.  In fact, when I'm working in the area this is the hotel I typically stay at. 

I've decided to update my review because I was generous  on my last review.  I was still in the infatuation stage of my relationship with Homewood. Now don't get me wrong I haven't lost that loving feeling because I'm still in love with the brand but I may be on the rocks with this location. 

Everything started out great.  I was able to grab a room because if my status with Hilton.  So after waking up at 3:15am in Chicago and jumping on the first flight to Boston, I was able to freshen up and unpack my bag, before hitting the office. 

I started noticing things in my room.  Like the handle to my bedroom door was literally falling off.  The screws were totally stripped. My kitchen sink was dripping water every time I turned it on.  I could hear Justin T. singing "Cry me a Waterfall"!  I was going to call down but those were a couple of major fixes. First I don't want plumbers and locksmiths working in my room, while I'm at work.  What if they put my underwear on their heads and start making funny uTube videos.  Hey it could happen! Or they decide to take all the cash I hid under the mattress. Don't judge me there's no wall safe here. 

I've also noticed the heating wasn't working great. I was really cold the first night and it was set at 70.  Then I set it to 85 and it was still not pumping out major heat. I noticed in my last review I had issues with the AC.  I can't catch a break here when it comes to climate control. 

My final straw was when I returned to my room at midnight and it was not made.  Yes the maid seemed to ignore my room. It's not a good feeling.  I went down to see the night manager and he didn't seem very concerned. He then asked me if I left the "Do Not Disturb Sign" on the door! Wow! It's midnight and you are gonna pull the old...it's my fault! Dude it's not my first night in a hotel. I asked him for some fresh towels, which he grabbed for me in back. I just wasn't happy I had to go down to inform the staff about what they usually do. 

The food quality was also not great. I know everyone is trying to cut corners.  I was happy the first day for breakfast with hard boiled eggs.  Then on day two the hard boiled eggs disappeared. I asked and was told that they don't have them. They were serving the most gross looking egg soufflé. Two minutes later, the hotel worker that told me he had no hard boiled eggs offered to make scrambled eggs for some other hotel guest who was grossed out by the egg dish they were offering. Hmmm! Couldn't he had boiled me two eggs? In fact, he went on to offer scrambled eggs to other guests, who grossly looked at this dried out egg soufflé.  That's great but where's my hard boiled eggs.  It was the only healthy option. 

Last but not least the water in the shower here sucks.  You feel greasy when you get out of the shower. No matter what I do, I can not get the feeling of slime off my body.  I have no idea who's fault this is but it's just not a fun feeling in the morning. 

I love the concept of Homewood Suites.  In fact, this is the only location I usually have issues at. I just had to say something.  I just hope somebody is listening. 

PS The room with the issues was #114. Avoid it at all cost.

Input: I'd never heard of this place but im always excited to try a new spot. Upon walking in the place was nicely decorated and the DJ was poppin. However, it fell short in the most important areas (food and service) that I can't think of a reason why I would go back. 

Pros: 
The ambiance is very pleasant. 
Dj was really good and the music wasn't so loud that you couldn't have a conversation, yet loud enough to enjoy 
The biggest pro was the lyrics to You're All I Need on the wall of the ladies room.

Cons:
The bar service was unreasonably slow. The restaurant was only 20% full, but it took 15 minutes for the bartender to actually take our orders and make our drinks because she was busy socializing with the wait staff. The drinks are watered down

The seating isn't the most comfortable. We were sat at a group of wobbly tables with stools that didn't have back rests. The restaurant was pretty dark, we had to use our phone flashlights just to view our menus. (I guess that's the thing though bc I have to do that at other places too)

Our server came to our table and without greeting us or introducing herself, she asked us if we wanted appetizers. We had to probe her to find out what was good on the menu or if they had any specials. For the price of the food and drinks, we expected a higher level of service. She barely came to the table to check on us and the restaurant wasn't busy at all. Our food took almost 40 minutes to come out. I'd be afraid to come to this restaurant when they're actually busy because you may never eat or drink anything. 

It tasted like they put room temp tap water in fancy bottles and that's what was served (no ice or offer for ice)

I ordered chicken and waffles. While it looked good, the menu doesn't say that it's dark meat and the server didn't mention it either so I returned it.  $8 mac n cheese has to be amazing so I tried it, I wasn't impressed. It wasn't bad but it definitely lacked seasoning. To replace the chicken n waffles I got the strip club wings.....they should just call them jerk wings as they were not reminiscent of any strip club wings I've ever had. After not eating all day and having sent one dish back I ate them. They were flavorful though. The theme of the dishes was that they were all bland. The other people in my party ordered the etouffe which needed salt, and the blackened chicken pasta which she was underwhelmed and left most of it. I'm not sure whyyyy they would disrespect the sanctity of a real strip club wing. But they did. Their "strip club wings" are a jerk type of flavor drizzled with a sauce that looks like ranch, but isn't. For $12 you get about 8 drumettes. 

We were a party of 4, and our server added gratuity to our checks. I'm not sure if this is standard practice for all checks, or if they add gratuity for "larger" parties. Again, there were only 4 of us, so we were all surprised by the gratuity already being added to our bill. Our service was so bad, that we wondered if she added it because she knew she sucked and probably wasn't going to get a good tip. Nonetheless, I thought that was odd. We had no issue tipping, but she would've gotten 18% instead of our standard 22% in this type of place but hey, I get it, not everyone tips accordingly. Well, tipping accordingly would've been like 10-15%. Again the place was bare and we barely saw the server.

I give this restaurant 2 stars solely for the ambiance and the DJ. Everything else was a fail. Maybe the brunch is a better experience but I'm skeptical about that unless there's a different staff with a focus on service and timeliness. I don't want to imagine what the food wait is when it's at least 70% full, forget full.

Input: "Keep Portland Weird," reads the wall across the street from Voodoo Doughnut, the eccentric and beloved doughnut shop in Portland, Oregon. Judging from the dreadlocked ginger, dirty hippie girl with ring worm (seriously), obese monstrosities, various speed geekers, aging hipsters, and other creatures occupying the block-long line to get a doughnut at 3:00 p.m. on a Tuesday afternoon, weird is exactly what they're keeping it.

Among the weird was I. I'll admit it, I waited in the ten-plus minute line to try what authors Chuck Palahniuk and Anthony Bourdain once swooned over. It wasn't my choice to go or wait; nevertheless, I was there and I was intrigued. I'm not a big "sweets guy" (excuse me while I throw up in my mouth for saying that), but I'm all for decadence, and decadence is definitely what the people at Voodoo Doughnut are doing. Along with weird.

I tried four doughnuts: The bacon maple bar (maple frosting and bacon), the dirt doughnut (vanilla frosting and Oreos), the sprinkle doughnut (vanilla frosting and sprinkles), and an Old Dirty Bastard (chocolate frosting, Oreos, and peanut butter), the last two which were vegan. I only took a bite of each, and every one, even the vegans, proved too rich for me. As comedian Robert Kelly would say, "What the fuck does that mean, it's too awesome? You diabetic boring ass face."

I may not be diabetic, but I guess I'm a boring ass face. I just couldn't eat them; they were too rich. I'd rather trek the mile over to BUNK and eat a pork belly cubano with a side of bacon and egg potato salad and a "Mexican" Coke instead. (Like I said, I'm all for decadence, it just depends on what kind.)

Something that pleasantly surprised me was how supple and moist the vegan dough was. I've had vegan doughnuts in the past and they were abominations. Like eating chalk. Why bother? It was nice to see people doing vegan right when there is so much wrong in the world.

Ultimately, Voodoo Doughnuts is not a great place, nor is it a bad place. Simply, it's proof that if you deep fry it and put Oreos, Cap'n Crunch, or actual strips of bacon on it, curious people will come. So will weird people and, evidently, so will I, even though I'd rather be eating my pig with vinegary red peppers on toasted, gluten-full bread, not a maple bar.

Input: With 260+ reviews and an average rating of 4 stars, this review is certainly in the minority and I'm sure it will be dismissed by many. I know if I saw lots of great reviews and came across at bad one, I'd negate it too. Still, here goes...

My daughter and I were seated at one of only two tables in the entire restaurant without any lighting. Also, our table was in a little alcove, and with my back to the rest of the restaurant, I could only see my daughter and a wall. I felt very disconnected. As for the food and service? A big fat MEH!

Here's a list of all the hiccups:

1. They did not have lemonade. 
2. The bread wasn't great. It was some garlic hybrid.
3. Grilled octopus was very tough and had a bitter tangy sauce that overwhelmed it.
4. The waitress brought us more bread and it was nearly burnt. Super crispy and dry.
5. We waited way too long for the main course.
6. Waitress never asked if we wanted another drink.
7. Waitress wasn't very attentive. Not rude and didn't go MIA, but I expected more.
8. Main course was pasta and lobster in a bowl of butter (yuck, too much butter).
9. Lobster was chewy.
10. My daughter's salmon was undercooked.
11. Her dish was supposed to come with risotto, but it was just cubed potatoes.

Positives:

1. Pecan tart was delicious.
2. The pasta was cooked to perfection. Probably the best I've ever had.
3. Father/daughter bonding time (that's why I never complained to the waitress...I didn't want to spoil the mood).

Considering the way this place presents itself as high end dining, I was not at all impressed. I'll take The Capital Grille any day. There I feel special, hence making the expense worth it.

Input: My boyfriend and I decided to try out Kimura after reading so many good reviews about their omakase.
We made reservations and the place was pretty packed when we got there. Service was extremely slow, but we let that slide because it seemed like every table in the restaurant had omakase. My boyfriend had the $50 omakase, while I had the $40. 

In the middle of our meal, there was a long 30 minute wait. The table next to us who arrived over an hour after us, had already received their entrees while we had not. It turned out they had made a mistake and delivered our entrees to them. We had to wait another 10 minutes for our entrees. 
But my entree never came. They didn't even realize they had missed my entree until I asked about it. The waitress almost didn't believe me, she had me name every dish I had thus far. She then came up 5 minutes after I had told her about the missed entree, telling me it was last call, and I needed to place my last orders in if I wanted any. I reminded her about my entree, and she almost looked shocked, like "Is this girl gonna let the missed entree go?" After speaking to the other waitresses, and the chef, she tells me my entree will be coming in the next 10 minutes. My boyfriend finished his meal, while I waited for my entree. 
By the time we finished our meal, we had been in the restaurant for 3.5 hours. We were the second last table to leave, and the last table left came in half an hour before closing. Eight tables had come and gone during meal - three of which had omakase. Ridiculous. When our bill came, I asked if we could be given a discount for the inconvenience they caused with the mix-up. No can do, said the  waitress. 

Brief overview about the food, as I basically rated this restaurant on its service. First up was the baby spinach salad, which was extremely salty. Next was the raw oyster and oyster shooter with the monkfish, which was alright - your typical oyster shooter dish. I also had had the quail and salmon - salmon was tasty, but the quail was very, very bland. The soup, which I believe was squash, was good. My entree, the lobster and cod, was good - but certainly not worth the wait. The tempura was not so good, and the sashimi was pretty fresh. Nothing special.  

Needless to say, I will not be back. The food was mediocre, but it is not good enough to bring me back. I've had much better food and much better service elsewhere.

Input: This 99 is OK I guess, never had any real problems with it . Service can be really slow at times. I kinda wish that they would automatically bring you popcorn instead of having to be ask for it but not a big deal. (My memory goes back to when the 99 at the Liberty Tree Mall used to be a Ground Round with all you could eat free popcorn and peanuts :)

My problems are twofold. Firstly, I find precious little on their menu that interests me. The menu is boring !!! Potato skins are obviously frozen that they deep fry and they are usually mealy sometimes they seem like they're left over and heated in the oven. Food is average for a chain.

My second problem concerns the 99 in Seabrook, NH. My mother and I used to stop there when we would go to Cow Hampshire for the day.
The first time I got the New England Roast Turkey there ....IT .....WAS......AWESOME!!!!!!!!!!!   So much turkey, I don't even care if it was "Tour-kee Brand Turkey flavored Turkey substitute" , it looked, smelled and tasted fantastic ! It was moist even without gravy. The portion size was huge, kind of like you would get at home on Thanksgiving. A BIG mound of corn bread stuffing, very tasty. Nice gravy. Sweet honey\buttermilk biscuit. In a nutshell, each time I went it got smaller and smaller !! The taste of the food remained good but it was the case of the mysterious shrinking portion !  At 10.99, I think there should be a platefull. In fact, the first time I got it, there was so much food that they had to bring the sides on the side. They side plates would not fit on the dinner plate !. Now they bring everything on one plate and there is still room. The side bowl that held my squash is now a tiny ramekin that sits on the plate glued in place by a buttload of gravy. 

So, the 99 gets a big ....ehhhh from me

And the bottled oregano that they sprinkle on each and every plate as a garnish is over kill and completely takes away from the flavor of the dish.  Try FRESH parsley, basil or rosemary.  


We may try again in the near future but after failing a second time, not so sure about it!

Input: Two stars (versus one) *only* because the staff is excellent.  Honestly, every single employee I interacted with was courteous and seemed genuinely happy to help.

But, oh, goodness the rest.

I only stayed here once, for a conference, and while I generally enjoy travel for work, one of the perks is usually staying at a fancy hotel!  Not a hotel that just charges a lot but fails to deliver.

So, my issues:

The rooms are dark.  Even with all the lamps on, it just felt dim.

The rooms smell weird.  You know when you walk into a room, and you know it's non-smoking, but it still kind of smells like smoke?  And it's just kind of the scent of the weird industrial soap they use?  It smells like that.

They! Have! Bugs!  Okay, just crickets, but honest-to-gosh there is a sign by the front desk that just basically says, "Austin gets swarmed by crickets this time of year.  There's nothing we can really do about it, and they won't hurt you."  I could hear crickets chirping the entire time I was there.

The walls are paper-thin.  Tissue-paper thin.  I heard someone sneeze, I heard my neighbor hanging things up in the closet, I heard a cell phone alarm at 6:30 am.  

There was a special event with a band that was directly below my room, so after work I got to listen to country music for four hours.  After the first two, I called and they said it should end at 10 pm.  At 10:30 I called, and they said it should end at 11.  Really, they have 463 rooms.  They just shouldn't rent out the ones directly above that ballroom if they're having an event there, because it wasn't just the dull thumping base of loud music.  I could hear the drums, bass, lead guitar, and singer clearly and distinctly.  Or they could just rent those rooms to the people organizing the event.

I'm not sure where other reviewers stayed but I was not in a room with two flat screen tvs, I was in one with one small, old television.

The mattress was too firm.  It wasn't comfortable for me.

The room didn't have a refrigerator or microwave.

I hate how mid-range hotels offer free wifi but the pricier hotels charge for it.  This one charges $13 a day.

The water pressure was not great, and the light in the bathroom buzzed.

It was a simple mistake, we weren't mad that we had to take cash out, we weren't trying to get the girl in any trouble but the way our waitress spoke to us over a misunderstanding was really out of line. Input: Got a weird vibe with this place.

Tried to schedule my appointment online with ZocDoc, but was unable to do so, so I had to call and make the appointment over the phone. No big deal, but why have a ZocDoc link on your website, if it doesn't work?

Upon arrival the medical assistant who took me back seemed to have the wrong patient's medical history. She kept referencing family histories of conditions I had not indicated on my medical history form and asked for additional information which I had been sure to include on the form.

The actual appointment took all of 3 minutes. I was seen by the Physician Assistant, not Dr. Bhatt, and she seemed extremely rushed. I scheduled my appointment to discuss my adult onset acne. The PA looked at my face for about 5 seconds and proceed to prescribe 4 different medications. She didn't ask about what products I had tried using, what worked, what didn't work, my lifestyle, or anything. She suggested that I start all of them at the same time... how then, would I be able to tell which ones were working or not working? Or am I just supposed to take all four of them for the rest of my life?

The prescriptions she picked for me had to be ordered through 'special' online and over the phone pharmacies... she wouldn't give me the script to bring to my own pharmacy/pharmacist but insisted that the required pharmacies were "cheaper." Sounds like inducement to me.

After the PA took her leave, the medical assistant returned to the room with samples of only two of the four items I was supposed to purchase... apparently I was just supposed to take their word for it that I wouldn't be allergic or have an adverse reaction.

The Medial Assistant then proceded to contradict the instructions given to me by the PA, saying that "she usually tells her patients to do things differently than the PA because she thinks they work better that way." Very professional.

All in all - just a weird vibe. Didn't feel like I was receiving great care and felt super shady having to call all these 'special' pharmacies to fill prescriptions that I couldn't try out. I will probably utilize a different practice from here on out.

Input: Normally I'm not much for reviewing, but I was having lunch with a friend this weekend and she had the same exact comments I did. 

This place has the potential to be excellent, but it seriously needs to work on its customer service. We went on a Friday night around 7. It wasn't busy so we assumed the crowd came in later. It took us 2 hours for a meal for 2 people!! I wouldn't have minded the time if the service was quicker and we stayed to drink, but the majority of the time we waited for drinks, water, or to spot the server in general.

There was one bartender making all the drinks. It took about 15 minutes for us to get our drinks. We ordered 2 rounds and stopped after we realized it wouldnt be worth the wait time. The waiter looked unusually perplexed, as if he was in a completely different time zone than us. He would always have a pitcher of water with him, but never refilled our glasses unless we specifically asked him. Also, no one ever cleared our dirty plates. We would even slide it to the end of the table as a huge hint. Nope. Nada. I would be more understanding if it were busier, but being as slow as it was I couldn't excuse it. We also noticed that the staff kept running across the street to black olive. I can only conclude that the staff was running 2 restaurants at once. Lol. Maybe that's why the waiter was confused, he didn't know which place he was at. 

As for the food, it was really good. The only saving grace for this place. The dishes were exotic and different. We order a few sushi rolls, appetizers, and I believe 2 entrees. Each was delicious and presented well. I would come back to this place if it had better service. Hearing that my friend had the same experience, I think I'll pass.

She took our drink order and gave us water. It then took another 20-30 minutes just to get our drinks. We even went to the bar to get our own drinks (which took way faster) while we waited. We then ordered our dinner, which took about 45 minutes to arrive. Our waitress barely came back to check on our drinks to see if we needed more while we waited for the food. The wait for the food would've been bearable if our drinks just kept coming! The food was good, nothing amazing or worth the price, and my dinner came out cold. Overall, I think this is a cool and trendy place to get drinks or just hang out, but definitely not good for dinner. I would not come back here or recommend The Lawrence to any of my friends until the service gets significantly better.

Input: I visited this place frequently when I worked at Lenox Mall right across the street years ago.   Though it hasn't been a regular hangout of mine for some time, I found myself here to watch a couple of the NBA Finals games the past couple of weeks.  While I had a fairly decent experience here the first time I went (if you do go, request the waitress with the short red hair - she's great), last night's experience ensures that I will never set foot in this place again.  

Being out on the patio with only one TV per side was bad enough (not ideal for viewing unless you're directly facing it, which is hard to do with rounds) but we had the rudest waitress I've possibly ever encountered in any restaurant.  Not only did she ignore us and the two tables next to us for most of the night (to the point where we had to go to the bar to get our own water refill and additional napkins), but when we did manage to get her attention, she was both abrasive (getting upset with us when we informed her we did not order the beers she forgot to put in "for our table" - our table had no alcohol at all) and condescending (when we decided to order something else, she responds "I was just here a second ago, but what do you want?").  Really?  The food that my table did order took forever to come out - over an hour- and was mediocre.  I am sure the kitchen was backed up (typical for a sports bar on a big game night), and I would have been more forgiving if she had not been so rude, had at least apologized for the wait, and if other tables (who had different waitresses) hadn't gotten their food pretty quickly after their orders were placed.  

One of the tables next to us finally asked for the manager, who didn't seem overly concerned until he realized it had happened to multiple tables, and he did end up comp'ing our table's bill.  Between him and the awesome red haired waitress, I added a star back, but based on last night (and my overall "meh" impression of the place), I will go somewhere else next time.

Input: Pad Thai...comfort food.  I was feeling slightly hung-over and exhausted from braving Washington Square the day after Christmas, thus I needed a little comfort.

Hangover food should be a little on the heavy side, maybe a little greasy or oily.  Sadly my hangover was not properly nurtured.  My Pad Thai was rather on the dry side and was surprisingly lacking in flavour of any kind.  My order came with a little pack of nearly flavourless peanut sauce and one slice of lime that did not even come close to moisturizing the abundance of noodles.  

The scallops were nice and juicy and I polished those off right away.  But once those were gone I had little incentive to go near the unenticing pile of noodles before me.  Come on, lure me in with some spice, some egg, and heck some moisturizing and tantalizing sauce.

On the up side, the guy behind the counter that took my to-go order was super nice.  He brought me water while I was waiting and even noticed how dehydrated I was (goes with hangover) and brought me more water.

Alas, next time I am looking for a scrumptious Pad Thai, I will probably look elsewhere.  As lovely as the service was, really the food only rates 2 stars as "I've experienced better."

Input: Ugh, I feel like I'm cheating on my secret lover (so secret even he does not know), Paul Qui, by writing this review. It was unique: sliders style with the bun mimicking a King Hawaiian roll, containing slightly melted brie, green apple slices, nori and kimchee.  The brie and apple went well together as you might expect, but the kimchee definitely fought with those flavors......and well, the kimchee won.  It over-powered the delicate, the tart and the sweet.  Paul: whatever else you change with the other ESK trailer menus, please, please, please, don't ever replace the Liberty's delicious Brussels sprouts salad!  p.s. - I still love you!

If you're a meat eater or here from out of town and want to experience Pok Pok . . I  say go for it and you'll probably be happy. Input: TL;DR: Tried to rope me into unnecessary work that I didn't ask them to look into in the first place. 

Brought my Accent in for a manufacturer's recall. I didn't even expect or ask for them to diagnose the vehicle in any way. They said the car would be ready around 2, at which point I sent a text through their system asking for a time estimate. Got a phone call about a half hour later saying the recall work was done but that the tech flagged a number of issues and he would send me a list so I could sign off on the work - didn't explain what the issues were or give me any idea of their severity. 

I get the text and much of it is valid - new wipers, oil change - I knew that when I brought it in (although again, I did not ask for them to look at any of this, I have a mechanic I like already). Some of it was extremely suspicious, like brakes that I know work just fine. Some of it seemed to be outright nonsense, like the transmission flushing procedure that I knew I had done a year ago - and I have not driven anywhere near 60k miles this year, I've barely driven at all due to covid. I decided I would take it to my regular mechanic because I'd rather have them work on it regardless, as they are much closer.

So I go back to Beaverton Hyundai, and they say they need to get the car ready for me to take it (I can see it parked right there, I'm capable of backing out of a spot). The guy I talked to on the phone comes in and somewhat resentfully says, "You didn't confirm any of the work, does that mean you don't want it done?" Yes, you didn't communicate with me at all so I didn't think I had to inform you that I was on my way to get my own car back.

Then he says he has to do some paperwork, which is fine, records are good. After a short wait, I go to sign it and he says, almost spitefully (the tone of the whole interaction was bizarre and off-putting) that the brakes are a safety issue and that if nothing else, I should get them looked at immediately.

Well guess what! I did get them looked at, and the mechanic I trust says they are fine but they squeal a little from some warping. This matches my experience perfectly, because the brakes do in fact work just fine.

So thanks for the recall work, but I'll be sticking with my regular mechanic for everything else.

Input: We'd been wanting to try Waffle House for awhile, and our other choice this past early Sunday afternoon meant driving a little too far.  So we picked last week to go for the first time.  We got menus right away and the waitress took our drink order.  The place was busy, but it wasn't swamped and there seemed to be plenty of people working.  I got coffee with cream as requested, but no spoon.  

The workers seemed busy enough, though distracted, even sitting occasionally.  We apparently were invisible.  We waited and waited and finally asked if someone was going to take our order.  We weren't at some far away table.  We were right by the gap where the waitresses came out from behind the counter to the tables on the floor.   Eventually, someone came over to us. 

Then we waited and waited for food.  We had to ask for silverware to eat it when some of it- not all of it-  came at last.  I got my scrambled eggs long before my waffle came, so I ate them before they got cold.  They were good; not overcooked or undercooked.  My girlfriend got her All-Star Special without her bacon or waffle.  We had to ask about the rest of our food.  We had to wait for the waffles.  It's not unreasonable to assume that when they came to the table, they'd be hot.  However, the margarine (not butter) didn't melt; they were just warm.  

My girlfriend said the food was good, they knew how to cook over-easy eggs, but the bacon was definitely a cheap cut.  The waffles tasted good, but they were a little too sweet for my taste, and rather thin.  I got one cup of weak coffee; no refill.  I didn't feel like asking once more for something, and it wasn't good enough to want more.  

The food was kind of like home-cooked food, and the workers were like one of your good-natured but absent-minded sisters of whom you could ask, "Hey, while you're up could you get me x?" "Oh yeah, sure."  We were never rude; just puzzled that we didn't seem to merit attention.

I've had better, more abundant food much faster for a better price.  The restaurant seemed messy, the staff didn't seem organized or trained to notice when customers needed something even though we were right there in front of them.  I gave two stars only because the food was good enough for what it is, but paying money for absent-minded service spoiled the experience.  We won't be back again.

Input: * Stress leads to prematurity problems *

I had heard their pulled pork was superb, so I had to shuffle on by and give it a try.

One couple gave me an evil eye when I walked in the door and got seated right away - which confused me until I heard their conversation later.  They were lamenting how long they had waited for a table but that, "It emptied out so quickly now."  Thankfully I missed that joy of a line by coming a bit off-hour.  But seriously, giving me a nasty look because I happened to get lucky on my timing?  Sheesh.....

The customers all seemed stressed out.  I'm not sure what it was, but there was a definite stressful vibe to the place.  Perhaps it was the wait they had been through.  Perhaps it was the ghost of Guy Fieri and staring at his graffiti he left above the door.  Who knows?  

The waitress also seemed stressed, and brought a half a cup of water.  That was odd.  In too much of a rush to fill the full glass?  Odd.  

After ordering she quickly brought some condiments which were basically signaling to me that the pulled pork would likely be on the milder side for the West side target market and that they offer ways to kick it up a bit in case you like spice.  Photo:  http://www.yelp.ca/biz_photos/YlIyVA-wkv20VhzuJrVkzA?select=-73Pt_oW8asE-oH79_4ofg

The sandwich arrived.  It was a generous portion of shredded pork.  It did not taste like it had ever seen a smoker though.  I think this was more of an oven method.  That was disappointing as I really like the smokey nature of a good pulled pork.  It also was underseasoned - I don't know if it ever saw a spice rub prior to cooking?  Or perhaps it was rushed and not allowed to season long enough before cooking?  It basically didn't have that long and slow rich smokey spicy flavouring I would look for in good pulled pork.  The bun was warmed nicely and had a nice texture at least.  The slaw also had not marinated long enough and tasted rawer than I would prefer.  And there was MAYO on the bun?!?!?  WTF?  Mayo with pulled pork?  Meh.  Fries were fairly standard commercial variety, but served nice and hot at least.  Overall it was nothing I would come back for.  Photo:  http://www.yelp.ca/biz_photos/YlIyVA-wkv20VhzuJrVkzA?select=nvE5XwIuy6YvyqheYoXJ3g

I'm really glad I didn't wait on a line to get it, as then I would also have likely been just as stressed as all the other customers.  Instead I was just disappointed!

Input: I don't get it.  I read a ton of great reviews about this place, but it was just meh. 

Service:  The hostess had a "why are you bothering me" type scowl/attitude.  Our servers was nice but was being berated by the hostess I think, because she looked like she just listened to a recording of her dog getting run over.  Poor girl looked about 3 seconds away from crying the whole time, although she was attentive. 

Appetizers:  Both our appetizers were great, I had the crispy soy nugget, which was amazing, probably one of the best appetizers I have ever had.  You get a star for that.  

Main Dishes: Meh.  I had some sort of dish that ended up tasting like poorly made kimchi.  It was actually pretty boring.  Just not good. At all.  My partners dish was equally bland, although they enjoyed it more than I did.  I couldn't even bring myself to steal bites of it when she wasn't looking, which is rare.  

Dessert: Tried rice pudding and I think a cake or something they had special, I can't remember the 2nd dessert exactly.  The rice pudding was...bland.  Like no taste.  The cake was clearly one of those ones you get in the fridge case at a supermarket, only warmed in a microwave. 

Atmosphere: Noisy millennials shouting at each other.  I don't know if everyone between the ages of 20 and 33 has hearing loss from a life of wearing ear-buds or what.   But really, there's no need to excitedly shout your boring stories about your boring pointless lives.  You're not making up for lack of personality or character by amplifying the volume at which you render your mundane milquetoast recollections of some awful craft-beer you had.   Even the older people that were there were shouting constantly.  This one lady pulls out her phone, puts it on speaker at full blast and starts having a conversation with what was apparently her partners.  I kept whispering "dump her" at an elevated volume to try and plant the seed in the other person's subconscious.  After that riff-raff cleared out, it was actually decent inside; tables were cleanish, artwork on the walls was nice, etc. 

Bathroom: The toilet was leaking all over the place.  Which is gross enough on its' own, but here's the issue:  Since my last review some time ago I have become incredibly wealthy.  You know when people find those half-unfrozen mammoth or mastodon carcasses in the tundra?  I pay to have a chunk carved off from whatever mega-fauna is thawing out and ship it to my cobbler.  On this particular day I was wearing my mastodon leather shoes.  Which were subsequently coated in the spewings of the toilet.   I may have to get on my private jet and fly to a desert island you've never even heard of just to get them to dry out.  Not good times.  Really though, the toilet leaked from the bowl when flushed.  Gross gross gross. 

Overall: It wasn't terrible, but other than that amazing appetizer this was nothing I saw here that even reached the bar of 'average'.   I would probably go back again and order completely different things, and also wear cheap shoes in case the crapper is still leaking.

Input: "Two hearts, two hearts that beat as one...."

Is it just me, or does anyone else zone out to the muzak in these places? The listless cruising of the aisles wouldn't be so bad, but sometimes I start singing along. In the produce department.  

In another store, that might be cool and you might even get the produce guy, or another shopper to sing along, but:  (1) Freddie's employees tend to be a little surly and (2) Endless Love definitely falls in the guilty pleasure category and probably not what you want to serenade the produce guy with while you're squeezing the melons.  But that's just me -- boundaries.

I've been coming here on a weekly basis for over a decade and they cover most of the bases. The natural foods/organic section is surprisingly good and I can get decent produce and most of my household items. And thank goodness they have the sense to stock both Tillamook and Umqua ice cream.  

One thing I should mention is that I've had two bottles of wine I purchased here in the last couple months go bad. One of them was the cheap stuff, but another was a nice Napa Valley Chardonnay, so beware.

I still can't believe they offer free daycare in this store. I only used it once or twice, but still a neat option.  They miss the boat in the prepared foods section and I don't think I've ever gotten food to go.  Something they really should expand.  Nice that they offer free cookies to the kids in the bakery and have a large clothing section with Levi's, Dockers and Columbia.

Still can't figure out the whole family friendly aisle concept. To me family friendly isn't the removal of magazines, but the absence of toys and candy bars at the check-out.  

The key to the whole Freddies experience is to size up your checkers.  Some of them are excellent and others I know will take a really long time. 

-------------

Update: I've dropped my original four rating, since it seems that I prefer almost every Fred Meyer location to my local branch. Sigh. But, convenience is key and I know this store like the back of my hand.

Input: They tried. Came to this place for the first time at 5pm on a Saturday in January. I ventured out from my home wanting to sit somewhere nice after a long hard week of work, eating tortilla chips and having some good drinks. Tried a few chain restaurants and places by the Vancouver waterfront , all of which were jam-packed with people: most restaurant availability (mcmennamins and Wild Fin and   Stack) at this time on 1/16/21 were at a 45 minute wait, even for a party of 1.  Ended up here, due to having a $10 gift card from December.. The building looks very suspicious, with no windows, and a hard-to-find door. I found the door (no minors allowed), and was greeted by a bouncer who wouldn't let me enter without seeing my ID. I don't recommend eating here for a good experience with ambience. However, since it wasn't raining, and I had a $10 gift card, I was hungry and thirsty, so I stayed. The fried shrimp basket and fries were "pub quality" decent. The Cadillac Margaritas were quite good! Kudos to the bartender for that.  The signs all over the smoking section said it was a no service area, so we needed to bus our own tables.  Bottom line? great drinks and accommodating bar service, but probably not worth the price.. I don't want to pay $30 to bus my own tables, bring myself my own drinks, clean up my own dishes, and have to sit outside in an unheated area at 48°, at a community bench staring at a trash can.  They don't have Cointreau, BTW. All I ordered was 2 drinks and a shrimp basket.  I left having paid $20 for dinner  $5 tip (after the $10 coupon was applied from restaurant.com.) Pub quality food at best, but good drinks help you forget about food quality. Input: While this store is very convenient for those who live in the area, as it is quite large with a wide selection of produce, prepared/takeout food, natural foods, an Osco pharmacy, and a health/beauty products section, this is much that could be improved.
Sometimes the produce is acceptable; other times, not so much. I've had green beans go bad in a few days, opted to skip buying entirely wilted heads of lettuce, and the cucumbers are often too soft for comfort. If you're a vegan like me, shopper beware - you might be better off going somewhere else.
The prices are quite high compared to many other markets just outside the Boston area (MarketBasket in Waltham has the same products for nearly HALF the price. Examples: veggie burgers, pineapple and cantaloupe, tomatoes, tofu, and cauliflower -  $4 a head? Really?).
There never seems to be enough people working there, so the lines always move incredibly slowly. This has been the case for at least the last 2 years since I moved to this area and began shopping here. Despite there being about 8 checkout lanes, I've never seen more than 3 staffed, even during the busiest times. Sometimes the self-check out lanes are also closed down. On numerous occasions I've also witnessed employees walking around the front of the store seemingly aimlessly, while they could be helping bagging large purchases (there are rarely baggers helping here FYI). 
Why do they have such high prices if they are so poorly staffed? My guess would be building rent, and for those who don't have the time or the means to travel elsewhere, you're stuck with paying the high prices.

Input: My bf and and I were looking for a new place to try and had driven by this place a few times and said why not.  The outside decor seemed hip and inviting and well lit.  When we walked in on Saturday night (around 6pm) the bar was somewhat busy and the dining area so so.  We were greeted with a smile and brought to our table.   

First off, I grew up in the restaurant business and for over 20yrs have seen the ins and outs of how to run one.  One thing I learned is to keep the patrons happy.  So I think it's quite annoying that we were seated right next to a large table when there were clearly other open tables that would have kept us at least a table away.   I understand that if we were seated at this open table there is potential of another party sitting next to us but at that time it would have been the smarter choice.  

Our server arrived promptly and service overall was 4 stars for me but it's not just about the service.  

We ordered the broccoli spring rolls as an appetizer.  They were just ok.  They were a bit too greasy and could have used another touch of salt/pepper.   My bf ordered the short ribs which were tender and juicy but again lacked seasoning.  The sides with his dish was mashed potatoes and brussel sprouts.  The mashed potatoes were ok but the brussel sprouts were under done and had no seasoning and all.  I ordered the scallops over the parsnip puree.   The scallops were a smidge under cooked and the puree was way too sweet.  We also decided to get dessert, also a disappointment.   The brownie sundae and apple crisp were huge and the menu should indicate the size of these desserts.  There also were nothing special,  though the apple crisp lacked bring crisp, it was basically a scoop of vanilla ice cream over apples.

The one thing I will say is the pricing was worth the ratio of food you received.  

Overall the atmosphere and ambiance of this place is great, I would recommend going to hang at the bar and meet up with friends but not for the food unfortunately.  

As always never take my word for it and give it a try yourself.

For 12$ I was expecting something pretty amazing but as expected, 1 roll will absolutely not fill you up and 24$ is not worth getting full on kimbap. We also ordered the bulgoggi which did not really taste like bulgoggi?? Each bite got progressively boring and a single order is way too much for one person?? Ended up throwing away almost half. Not sure why the portioning and pricing is so all over the place. Korean snack shops are usually not "family share" style unless they offer items in multiple sizes and in varying "sets" with other items. I found the menu to be pretty limiting and this is the first time I ever saw ddukbokki as an appetizer and again only coming in one size. This location will have to be a pass for me.
