Input: I also live around the corner from the hub, & I've been anticipating the grand opening on this place for quite a while...The old tenants were "the Pit"- possibly the worst BBQ joint in Austin and back then it looked like the building was in real bad shape...

THANKFULLY the new proprietors really cleaned the building up- its nice & clean with new bathrooms too- perhaps a little too sterile, though. It just lacks the cozy atmosphere you'd expect from a good neighborhood joint..

on to the food

all i have to say is one big "EHHHH"

What I mean is it's utterly mediocre and lacks any uniqueness whatsoever...Sorry.  I really wanted to like this place.

the menu is really small- like what you'd expect from a golf course pro-shop grill or your average pub-grub kinda place: burger, chicken sandwich, BLT, club sandwich, salad, shakes & malts, and that's about it.

I ordered "the Flatty"- a 1/4lb burger with avocado & tots.  The veggies were fresh and prepared just fine, but the meat was overcooked and bland.  The bun was the whitebread, concession stand kind- a little stale and cold.

the tater tots were cooked just right, but too salty, and i usually don't mind salty stuff...just WAAYY too salty.

They had like 4 different bottled beers and 2 wines available - so its not really a place to go drink, or I'd have given them a little credit for the lackluster food. they did have like 4 flat-screen tv's though.  so maybe cool to take the kids there on a Sunday after their soccer games or whatever...just not my scene.

Sorry to be ripping this place...but I'm just disappointed.  I mean- have some friggin pride!  don't just cater to the lowest common denominator.  We don't need more mediocre restaurants in this town...but this neighborhood DESPERATELY needs a quality, reasonably priced restaurant with good atmosphere...

Unfortunately, The Hub is NOT up to the task.  If you want a decent burger around this neighborhood- try the Boulevard Grill on Far West (actually they have great burgers), Waterloo Ice House down at 360, or pony up for some great food at Che Zee.

Input: Is 26 West worth the overpriced rent? No.
Is 26 West the best apartment you can find in West Campus? Definitely No.
But is it as bad as other reviewers make it out to seem? Eh.

Prior to living here, I felt like I had made a big mistake after reading all the Facebook memes and reviews about this place. After living here for over a full month now, I feel that I can give my honest opinions that may help others who are deciding on a place to live.

THE GOOD:
The 4x4 is very spacious and I like how the rooms are divided into two sides. The gym is nice, and there were free school supplies in the computer lab downstairs. The location is very close to campus (and the food trucks!) and the pool area actually isn't too shabby. My roommate requested a bathtub resurfacing and she was able to get it completed a day after she called them.

THE BAD:
Walls are really thin! You can hear everything and even people walking above you. The exterior doors to get into the building are constantly broken and therefore do not lock properly. The door leading to our unit has broken over 4 times now in the time that I've lived here so anyone can just walk in. When I moved in, the lock to my room was also broken and although maintenance has come to examine it, I have yet to get it fixed. Speaking of maintenance, someone had come in to fix our light in the kitchen but for some reason also felt the need to replace the eyehole in our door even though it was not broken and no one had placed a work order for it. 
The trash disposal is also located in the parking garage and is really far away from some of the units. The exterior hallways sometimes have throw up, but in my experience this is usually cleaned up within 24-48 hours. 
The mailing system here is a bit whack. Sometimes I receive packages but do not receive any notice from the front office, and they have lost a package that I had delivered before. They are also really inconsistent about requiring photo ID for pick up. 

I think the weirdest thing that they just implemented is the wristband rule. Supposedly if you are to have a guest over, you must have your guest wear a cheap rubber wristband to use the amenities. They also give you a wristband for yourself, and if you lose these wristbands they make you pay ~75$ (wth? these are literally those cheap bracelets you get for free y'all). I have not personally seen this rule enforced, and I find it to be just another sleazy tactic to rob college students. 


Overall, I don't regret my decision to live here as I feel that a lot of these problems occur at many other apartments in West Campus HOWEVER I will say that I lived at The Ruckus last year and did not experience any of these problems. Despite all the cons, I'm still able to enjoy being at my apartment and do not constantly agonize over the "horrible conditions" that many others have lamented about. But after they reopened in Someday Cafe's old spot after some months without a store, I tried them again, and I just can't believe what a difference the bigger location and new staff has made.  I had to wait a half hour for my crepe each time, even though there were usually quite literally no orders ahead of me at all, and additionally, sometimes the staff was actually dismissive or snobby towards me.  After about five tries of having the same disheartening experience every time, I finally gave up.  (The other people I know who used to go to their old location have similarly quit trying.)  Food has to be really really good, to me, to warrant that kind of wait, and while this food is pretty good, it's not at that level.

Input: The actual work that Magic Beans does is very good. However the business practices make me unable to recommend them. Their first engagement was for a spring cleaning. They came out and did an estimate and I approved the work. Halfway through the work they told me it would cost roughly double the estimate, or they could stop work and leave the project halfway completed.  Everything was visible during the estimate, and if these are true professionals, they would understand what work is required. In retrospect I believe they low-balled the bid and planned the up-sell, as I have seen other folks making a similar statement that the work price changed mid-project. 

Following this, there was miscommunication where Megan sent a text that implied they would be doing ongoing maintenance. While the text stated they would be coming out weekly, the price was about the same as what they quote in their monthly contract at $220/month for maintenance of a mid-sized yard. (Their actual contract document shows a somewhat lower price). Regardless, Magic Beans actually did not do any work, and after a month the place was growing significant weeds again. I asked Megan to look at this and advise me what was needed. 

A short time later she replies that they have already started work and want almost $1400 - and that the previous quote of $220 was per week. That is utterly ludicrous. $1000/month for maintaining a Martin Acres yard? But she was going to discount it by30% because of the communication problem. Since she already started work, she wanted me to pay the whole price or "half and they will stop work then." This all happened within an hour and a half of my message. There is no way that more than an hour of work had occurred at that time. At no time had I told her to start work. 

In the end, I paid her for one hour of labor at her absolutely unfounded labor rate of $75/person for 2 people for an hour. I feel this was still an extortionate amount and especially since I had not approved the work. 

As I said at the beginning, the actual work is good. But they are way beyond expensive, and I feel that they use deceptive business practices. If you use them, be sure to have an absolute agreement as to scope and prices.

Input: Got the Groupon deal as well. I REALLY wanted to like this place. The people all seemed super nice and friendly, for the most part.

Chiro:
The Groupon didn't even include a chiropractic exam, they offered a free 15 consultation along with our massage - why not? The chiropractor was definitely a pushy salesman type, pushed the discount x-rays, pushed for follow-up exams and kept nagging about the follow-ups even after I was done with my massage and checking out. 

Massage:
I've had 2 hour massages and 20 minutes massages and backrubs from bored partners. In my opinion, 30 minutes isn't really much to write home about, no matter where you go. My massage was meh-worthy. The gal was nice, the massage was ok, the room was warm and very calming. 

Float:
This was our first time floating, we really had no idea what to expect so we went in with open-minds. The lady that got our tanks prepped was telling us about how the heater in the one my husband was going in kept cutting off, but since we were just doing the 30 minute float - it'd be fine. She tried upselling us to the 60 or 90 minute floats, but we said we were fine with 30 minutes to start. She said she'd knock 5 minutes before our time was up, then knock when it was time to get out. 

We put in our ear plugs, waved bye to the outside world and closed the door to our separate float tanks. Blackness. Silence. Warm water. Lean back. Float. The places my mind took me were amazing. I literally tripped the eff out. I was meditating at first and then just friggen left the planet. It was so relaxing and warming and loving and amazing. GREAT GREAT GREAT! Then I started thinking, "hrm. it seems like I've been in here for a really long time.... Crazy how time sort of stands still when you cut out the senses.... let's count seconds... 1....2....3" You get the idea. Then there was a knock. "ok wow! so now i have 5 minutes. lets see how long that feels!" I think. Then a LONG while later, I hear/feel the second knock. "Ok! I'm done!" and I get up slowly,  open the door and my husband is standing there wide-eyed looking at me. He asked me if I'm ok and told me that I was in the tank for ONE HOUR AND FORTY FIVE MINUTES!!!!!!! The lady forgot about us! He got out on the first knock, took a shower, went to the steam room and started to worry about where I was. That's when the lady came back and knocked on my tank the second time - 20 minutes after the first.... 

I got out and felt like I was on a mysterious planet. Naked. Dripping. Smiling ear to ear. I was a friggin prancing faerie. Took a long shower and was so excited and happy and soooo relaxed. I loved it!

The gal came in to apologize and seemed very worried that I'd be upset. I said it was totally fine and loved my experience. I'm thankful she sorta forgot about me! I had a blast! BUT, if i were someone else, they may not have appreciated wading around in the friggin water for almost 2 hours.

By the way I stepped on a piece of glass while walking around naked and barefoot. Word to the wise - bring slippers.

By the way pt. 2: Yknow how the lady mentioned the heater cutting out in my husbands tank? Well it cut out and his water got cold and he was shivering by the time he got out. Yknow - an hour and a half later... Pretty lame.

2 stars are mainly for the nice people that worked there. We will not be coming back to this establishment. BUT heck yea, we will be floating again!

Input: My friend and I had a reservation here for breakfast and it's a very different type of process...One that Disney must be testing for future quick service restaurants but I truly hope that doesn't become the norm. It's clunky, confusing, impersonal, no bueno. You have to have a reservation for breakfast, then you check in once, check in again, are given a rose so they can find your table (now this was the cool piece of the meal), pick your meal from a computer, then go find a seat. The whole process was confusing and wasn't explained to us nor were we offered help. We didn't know if we could sit anywhere, we didn't know we had to grab our own drinks, ugh to the whole thing!

This all made my dining partner a bit crabby first thing in the morning which wasn't fun. Breakfast is $26 each, no cheaper options for people like me who can't eat a lot...and we just were not impressed at all. No character interactions to justify the price. And the food wasn't amazing. We tried the breakfast sandwich and Feast A La Gaston. They actually brought us a platter of pastries to start out our meal which we picked at a bit but couldn't find any we loved. The feast a la gaston includes scrambled Eggs, Herb-Roasted Potatoes, Apple Smoked Bacon, and Sausage served with Fresh Fruit and a selection of pastries. The breakfast sandwich was open face with poached Eggs, Applewood Bacon, Brie Cheese, and Arugula on a Croissant served with Fresh Fruit. Everything was fine but just wasn't worth our confusion or the price. 

The dining rooms are very cool though decorated with various Beauty and the Beast themes. I recommend exploring the entire castle!

 I'd like go back at some point for the lunch and dinner but it'll need to be with someone new because my best bud said he'll never go back again! Wah wahhhhh.

Input: If its a warm, sunny morning in Union Square, I'd love to be on the tiny patch of grass abutting Bloc 11.  They serve what I consider to be the perfect cup of coffee (dark roast that isn't simply torched and then watered down) and I love the staff (Hi, Steve!)

HOWEVER...

A perfect cafe these things do not make.  

Not being a sweets person, I don't jump for joy at the sight of pastries, muffins or donuts and being a blood-thirsty animal "lover", I don't care if they're vegan or soaked in pigs blood for that matter.  If I'm going to treat myself in the morning, I crave the perfect breakfast sandwich.

To sum up the bloc 11 sammich: Flavorless, unseasoned, overcooked, CRUMBLY eggs on focaccia bread that absolutely cannot hold up to it.  You CANNOT eat this sandwich on the go and frankly, you can't eat it at a table, either.  Ham cannot save this sandwich and even the default cheddar cheese just sits there.  It cools and becomes firm almost immediately because the bread is hardly toasted.  May I suggest an orange, melty and somewhat salty Gloucester Cheddar?

In my business, if you can't cook eggs, you shouldn't be cooking at all.

Bring me a sandwich I can eat without having to pack a fork (or a net to catch all of the eggy bits jumping ship) I'll change my review.  

Oh, and talk about overpriced wifi!  Go to the Sherman Cafe, instead.

Input: A while back, I read an article called "Cheap Steaks" listing the non-steakhouse restaurants with a cheap, but good, steak on the menu.  Brick was listed as selling a baseball cut steak and loaded potato casserole.  

My husband chose the steak, but substituted mac and cheese for the side.  His steak was really good and cooked perfectly to medium.  He didn't have a steak knife, but had no trouble cutting it with his butter knife.  

I chose the Big Fat Italian burger with brussels sprouts for the side.  I was really surprised at the sprouts.  They were fried and sauteed with onions and bacon (I avoided the onions) and lightly dressed with an orangey vinaigrette.  The sauce balanced the bitter sprouts with some sweetness.  I thought the burger was good, but not great.  It had some nice flavor with salami, tomato sauce, and banana peppers and it was moist.  I liked how the bun had a toasted, buttery, garlic flavor.  

My husband convinced me to share two of the mini cheesecakes for dessert (I didn't need much convincing).  One was bacon and chocolate and the other was plain with berry and chocolate sauce.  Each was about 4 inches in diameter.  One would have been enough, really.  He liked the plain one with berries better than the bacon one; the bacon was weirdly chewy.  I thought they were both rather bad.  The cheesecake itself had a gummy texture that was worse on the outside and top.  Nothing like cheesecake should taste like.  I would not order them again and do not plan on helping eat the leftovers.  They didn't taste good enough to warrant the calories.  Overall, I thought the main meal part of the dinner was fine, but not enough to go out of our way to eat there again.

Input: Deviating a bit from the Chinesebites.com Signature Dishes Tour, we were invited to try out a new Japanese-fusion restaurant in Yaletown, KiBo.  I was joined by Romina, Rick, Grace, Alvin, Kevin, and Sherman for an intimate tasting of their dishes.

A few of us also ordered drinks.  I found the drinks to be quite sweet to taste and not that interesting.

We started off the evening with garlic toast served with negitoro ($8), which was served with toast.  The negitoro was pretty standard and was heavy on sesame oil, green onion, and tobiko. 

We sampled the Kibo set, a platter of three types of sashimi ($24). Each one had their own sauces on them already.  I enjoyed the tuna since it was fairly light on the sauce, but did not like the heavy seaweed taste on the salmon.  The fish seemed to be fairly fresh.

The beef carpaccio ($9) was a weird combination of parmesan cheese and wasabi dressing.  I didn't enjoy it because the cheese was too heavy, covering the beef itself.  The kibo salad with tuna, mango ($13) was also unexciting for me, especially since I had quite a decent mango salad the evening prior at Indochine.  I disliked the dressing, and this unfortunately seemed to be a recurring theme throughout the meal for me.

We tried a variety of aburi kibo sushi set ($17).  I sampled the salmon and the scallop, both of which weren't bad. 

The chikuwa cheese ($6), which is essentially Japanese fish cake stuffed with cheese them deep-fried, was alright.  Not sure what the cheese inside was, as it was not stringy (and hence not mozzarella).  The Japanese short ribs ($7) were pretty good and not tough at all. I liked the grilled taste of them.

Any meal would not be complete without bacon; we sampled the ebi bacon ($9) -- skewers of prawns wrapped in bacon.  These seemed to be grilled and was pretty good.  The bacon wasn't crispy, but that was alright since the prawn itself was crunchy.
 
The hamilton roll ($14) was essentially a dynamite roll topped with a variety of sashimi.  By this time I was already really full due to prior froyo consumption.  The volcano roll ($12) was pretty different from the other rolls since it was deep-fried.  I thought this was pretty interesting.

The caterpillar roll ($12) was also of the dynamite variety, except topped with unagi and avocado.  The Philadelphia roll ($12) with salmon and cream cheese was not bad.  I'm not huge on cream cheese in rolls, or rolls for that matter actually.

The marinated sablefish ($14) was quite good and soft.  It wasn't overly oily despite being an oily fish, and I really liked this dish.  At $14, this was well-priced.
 
The kibo beef ($15) itself was good and not thought at all, but I really disliked the sauce.  We wondered how the rack of lamb ($16) was Japanese because it was cooked with mustard seeds and cumin. Not to mention lamb isn't really a Japanese thing.  I only had a bite of it, but I thought it was a bit overcooked to my taste.  I like lamb quite rare.

To end the meal, I thought we were being served green tea, but it was actually soup.  A really delicious soup.  The seafood dobin ($10) tasted like a beautiful umami combination of shiitake essence, with clams, fish, scallops, and prawns.  It was really tasty and probably the most enjoyable part of the meal.

Input: I can't comment on the food, because we left before eating here.  We came to have a meal and conversation with some old friends, but after we sat down, we discovered that Taverna is not so much a restaurant as it is a Greek-themed circus that serves food.  The inside of the place was mostly filled with with parties of 15 people or so who were all yelling at the top of their lungs.  We opted to sit in the glassed-in patio, hoping it would be more quiet.  It wasn't much more quiet than inside, because the restaurant blasts really loud, over-amped, distorted music throughout the place.  The clownish waiters run around yelling OPAH!, lighting cheese on fire, and throwing napkins in the air.  I've traveled extensively in Greece, and I can tell you that I've never seen anything remotely like this in any restaurant in Greece.  Greeks would never eat in a place like this.

We were there at 7PM, and it was already chaotic.  I can only imagine what it would be like later in the evening.  If this is the kind of silliness that appeals to you, go and enjoy.  If you want an authentic Greek meal that you can eat in a grown-up restaurant, look elsewhere.

Input: I really want to write a good review for this place, or at least, a better one.

This was the first place in Austin that I've seen carrying the Hangar One Vodka line, of which, I am a huge fan. So when I walked in and saw my favorites sitting on the top shelf of the bar, I was immediately excited.

Unfortunately, what I received with my drink order... wasn't Hangar One Kaffir. I'm not sure what it was. It could have been well, or Tito's, I'm not sure. It simply wasn't what I ordered. The two other people with me didn't get what they ordered either. A Hangar One Buddha was... again maybe well, but clearly not what was ordered. An order of Crown Royal somehow magically turned into Patron Silver...

In the wait staffs defense, it is damn loud in this place, really, really loud. A normal conversation at a table is hard to keep up, so mistaking an order could be rather easy. Also, when the mistakes were pointed out, the situation was quickly solved. Good job on that, honestly, I had hope again.

The menu is a bit overwhelming. Lots of choices, and paragraphs describing each piece. It was super hard to choose, lots of the food looked good.

I went with the special of the night which were lamb sliders, and the scallops which were wrapped in bacon and bazil.

The scallops were good, not great, but a cool concept.

The lamb sliders were overcooked, dry, and served on a piece of bread about three times the size of the lamb. Super sad panda.

In the end, I'll probably go there for the huge bar selection. It was also dead at 7:30 on a Friday night, not the best of signs. 

The whole place feels dated, big time, which it can't be because of the building it's in, that's basically brand new. The plates are unattractive, the chairs are uncomfortable. Paper napkins are a bit sad at the price level and atmosphere.

I'll give it another try, but the first impression, as my friend would say "It was not readied."

Input: The entire experience as a whole, was 2 1/2, maybe 3. I began by calling Mary, and her business to set up a surprise Spa Party for my friends going through a breakup. Everything seemed fine, until the actual day of the party, she came, was on time, (had her son assist in bringing equipment which I wish I was privy to earlier) after that, my front door was left open multiple times upon set up and breaking down equipment, this allowed one of my cats to almost escape. Not a huge deal, I looked it over, I know there was a lot of equipment and it was heavy. The equipment scratched my hardwood floors, again not the worst, but irritating and I took note of it. After this she did inform me that they would be doing mini facials, after I had already only requested two treatments to keep my costs down, I thought that was very nice. Things slowly just went downhill from there. Upon arrival she said she forgot her extension cords, so one foot bath (these were both just store bought machines, not even the same ones) so one foot bath has warm water and bubbles, and the other had just hot water form my sink (I wish someone would've informed me they'd need to use that) after the water became cold, that was it. I do not own a microwave, they couldn't really heat up their stones. So by this time I'm fairly just annoyed, but I'm still going forward with services because why not. Two of my friends start off with the foot baths, two of us start with the massage. This is what was truly just irritating and disgusting to be quite honest. I had Mary, deep tissue, it felt amazing. What I did not enjoy was the singing, the story of her husband leaving her when my best friend was just broken up with, I'm paying you to provide a nice, quiet, ambiance for my friends and I. And then she began coughing on me as she was massaging me and not once stopped to wash her hands, or even apologize for literally hacking all over me. It was disgusting. Once again, I looked it over and bit my tongue, this was a day for my friend to be relaxed. She then proceeded to tell me she forget her essential oil kit, and I said I had mine she could use. Throughout the remainder of the sessions she CONSTANTLY put down my oils that I had so kindly let her use throughout the spa treatment she failed to be prepared more. This is was changed my mind completely to be honest, the fact she consistently said hers were better, better grade, whatever, you shouldn't have left yours at your place of business and then ask to use mine only to put them down, it was rude and very unprofessional. After that she attempted to push her DoTerra oils onto me and my friends by giving us samples and catalogs and by saying that 'Can you smell the richness, and the difference) it was again just rude and I was done by this time. Finally everything was done. I wanted just them to be gone to be honest, and then she sat down, called her son to come get them, and then sat and waited, this again was rude because you shouldn't be in my home when everything is done, and just unprofessional once again. She then asked the group where she should go eat, on the phone she very obviously said 'We're going out tonight' after I handed her the payment. Tactless in my opinion, why blatantly just be rude and ignorant as you're still in your clients home? Upon breakdown, once again her son left my door wide open for my cats to potentially run out. The second lady wasn't all bad, I did not get a massage by her so I cannot honestly review her performance. Mary seemed to bark at her a few times throughout the process, if she wasn't finished when she was and what not. She was quiet which is what I would've preferred from the other. I couldn't wait to get her out of the house. I also wish they would have uniforms or some type of united-ness or professional look. They were very casual, and to be honest Mary was a little larger than what I felt was comfortable to be moving and hanging over me. I felt a little closed in when should lean over me. The total services came to $466 I gave her $500, and asked for no change. I feel I should have tipped less. I would use the service again, but not form Mary, and I'd be much more frugal and specific with my orders. I'm not pleased at all, but I'm sure other people have been or else they wouldn't be in business. I'd just be careful with this business, I feel it could go either way and my experience just turned out to be horrible.

Input: I've given 2 stars because we did have an outstanding server - Jeremy F. - who did his best to recover for the entire restaurant experience. In short, we will never return. Here's the recap:

Dinner Reservation at 9:30pm on 2/14/15 (yes, I know it was Valentine's Day- all the more reason for this restaurant to have been prepared). 

We arrived via Uber at 9:25pm - it's a good thing. They offer valet but apparently it's around the block and there were grumblings about this. 

Hostess was polite enough, checked us in and said it would be a few minutes before they could seat us. She offered us a menu and said we could wait at the bar -- lol!

Ok, so I'm looking around for the bar and realized she meant the make shift "cluster" bar they attempted to establish. 2 high top tables backed up to a counter with a trough/well on top for ice. I question the validity of food safety on that. 

Anyways, the bartender's back was to us the entire time - she never asked to take our order. We were
Seated at 10:02pm- still no drinks--
At the "chef's table" facing the open kitchen.  Server greeted us almost
Immediately and brought water. We ordered 2 aperitifs + 2 appetizers. Appetizers were delivered and complete before I complained about our drinks. At 10:28pm, we finally received our cocktails. It's obvious bar was understaffed and not having a worker friendly station - a real bar- Is also wasted time. 

We ordered dinner. I had the kale Caesar - which was fantastic and the steak - lovely. My husband ordered the duck - smallest portion of duck ever and we wonder if it was something ordered in bulk from say Sysco. 

Poor wine selection although we did settle on a bottle of Pinot noir for dinner. 

As the restaurant began winding down the kitchen staff began to get a little lax. Meaning, I watched the kitchen staff eating and or drinking various things in front of us! Remember, we were sat at the fancy "chef table." For the untrained eye, it probably wouldn't matter-- however, I've worked in the industry before and eating where food is prepared/cooked is a hazard.  

We went on to order dessert, after dinner drinks and have conversation with Jeremy about the restaurant because in the 2.5 hours we were there - no table touch from a manager. He listened well and made apologies as best he could. 

It was pretty disappointing to pay $$$$ prices for a 2 star experience. If you turned the lights up in the restaurant and really looked around -- it's a diner at best.

The wings themselves were alright. Good flavor, sizeable portion. One major criticism is the crispiness. I wouldn't know the wings were "fried" unless you told me. Tasted grilled if anything. 

Overall, probably won't come back again. Though I can understand why some people enjoy it. The day I came was maybe an off day.

I ok'd the price then I figured he would delete the second entry. When prompted for my card I handed it to him then asked about the total. Well he had already swiped my card and charged me twice for a pair of $90 kicks. Then a person I assumed was the manager assured me the total wouldn't end up on my card while returning the item charged incorrectly. I knew my card would charge me the full amount then refund the $90 at a later date which it did/has. Essentially putting that $90 in limbo for who knows how long. My advice here would be to hang on to your card until you've verified what they will be chargjng and make sure it is accurate. The initial error was obvious and I just assumed the clerk would right it with out specific direction. I was wrong which in the end is really my own fault. Next time I'll visit niketown.

Input: So this is tough. It amazes me, when a company you believe in and support as an online entity only, decides to open up an 'antiquated' brick and morter store, and they take such drastic steps backwards in customer service and you have to think if it is worth going elsewhere from now on.

I have been purchasing clothing from Indochino since 2013. I have purchased I believe 8 suits and 10-12 shirts. to say I like their fit, choices, quality, etc is obvious. so why the negative review? I have spend in excess of $5,000 on clothing with them

Until 6 months ago, I have always done everything through the website. Take my measurements, submit them. design and customize, order, and receive. I have had to have things tailored a little after the fact, which I did with a local tailor I trust very much (see my other reviews)

So what changed?

My sister is getting married, and her Husband to be wanted suits from Indochino. Great! But I had to go into the store to order it, and get the accurate pricing, I couldnt do it online.

This is where the first issue happened.
I was measured, ordered, etc. all fine. 
I customized the suit to my liking, as Indochino allows. I talked with my future brother in law, to make sure what I was doing was ok - he was on board. I would match, but be able to customize a suit i would end up using for work after the wedding. 
Well the suit came in, and it was not customized as I desired. and as I ordered. When I called indochino, the girl said she had to change my customization, because she reached out to the Groom, and he said to. I called him, and he refuted her story. he was fine with what I did, and never spoke with her. She LIED to me, and took it upon herself to customize the suit. When I said I wanted a new one made to my specifications, she refused

ok, upset. it happens

Fast forward to the past three weeks. I ordered another suit, using the same measurements. I increased the jacket wrist measurement to fit my watch and cufflinks for french cuff shirts (yeah, first world problems). It came in a little bigger then expecting (I think they increased the diameter versus the circumference). No biggie, Customer Service said I could bring it to my own tailor and get reimbursed, or to the studio and have it fixed for free. Hindsite is 20/20, and I should have gone to my tailor even if paying.

I went to the studio to save money. was told 1-2 week turnaround. fine! I have a wedding this weekend (the 20th) and it was the 2nd of May), so worst case scenerio, 2 weeks I could pick up on the 16th when I had a day off.

then the issues pop up
1. The clerk helping me with new measurements wants to change this, that, etc. no, please just change what I am asking do not retailor.

2. I call on the 15th, since it has been two weeks, and I have not heard. no suit. they said it should be there on the 16th at 7pm. to late for me to pick it up, but ok. they said they would call and I would get an email when it was there. On the 16th, no call, no email

3. I called on Wed the 17th. time getting close. I called again. Girl on the phone said she would check on it, and call me back. no call. no email. no jacket.

4. i called again today. The guy on the phone said he would check. That he didnt know what tailor it was with, but it wasnt back (going on 2.5+ weeks now). He called around, and said 'hopefully' it might be there Friday the 19th - too late for the wedding of course.
He said they were busy, and busier then last year, so alterations can take 3-4 weeks

WHAT?!?!

to say I am frustrated is an understatement. To say it strains my belief in the company is an understatement. Having in person assistance in a brick and morter location has made the location WORSE, and has led to me getting product that is not how I want, not customized how i want, and left me very unhappy.

With a lot of other made to measure studios, both online and locally, it is hard to support a company that doesnt seem to want to support their customers or stand behind product. I have purchased product online with House of Bespoke with success, and with 9Tailors locally, and been happy. I guess I have to push any future business their way, since Indochino does not seem to value customers and proper service.

Input: As a consumer that has free will and the ability to make decisions we have to take some of the blame when it comes to making bad choices.  Most Americans do not have the slightest clue when it comes to making a good choice on a supplier of a must have utility.  Knowing the per cost of therms, kilowatts, etc is the most important detail.  If a supplier claims they can get you lower bills overall in comparison to your current supplier, that could be true but it requires work.  Most of these details are not readily shared anywhere when making this choice.  As a renter or an owner, if having to pay for electricity or gas to heat or power your home, take some time to understand your bill.  Call your local providers and ask customer service to explain the bill to you and what is necessary to know.  First talk with the major supplier of the utility.  Most of the time they would provide you with all the details you need.  Go online  and do some research.  Most often there is some sort of free website to gain details about utility providers and must know information provided by ex- employees of these companies, local government and npo's that want more information out there for the common consumer.  I.E Citizen's utility board, etc.  

Know that if having gas service you are charged per therm.  These rates rise and fall all the time.  Calling in and asking to be "locked into" this rate gives you 12 months at that rate.  Call in any time during that time period to make use of changes if the rate reduces.  Providers make money on you.  Your rate will only change if you call your service provider in a timely manner.  They will NOT undertake lowering your rate.  IGS requires a phone call to make changes.  Its an easy way for them to make money on your irresponsibility.  Imagine if after your first 12 months you do not call, they adjust it to whatever rate is available at their discretion and so forth.  Most consumers assume a lot of things; like that rates rise and fall and that it reflects on their bills.  NOT true.  At anytime you could be paying more or sometimes less than any of your neighbors.

When the sales person for IGS told my parents they could lower their Nicor bills they agreed and signed on.  The salesperson put them into some sort of "budget" system without explaining all the details or the fact about rising and falling rates.  Seniors tend to hear what they want, so when sales guy said "lower rates than Nicor" that's all my folks needed.  What IGS did was take the average number of therms used throughout the year and charge for that all year round.  Their claim is that it saves you money.  Call your local major utility provider to find out exactly how much you average in the summer versus winter.  These numbers are grossly different especially living in the Midwest.  Some years are colder and some warmer and you may not need that many therms but are being charged for them.  Imagine your neighbor is paying $50 dollars in the summer and your bills are over $200 year round.  With this in mind, say if its a very cold winter and would expect higher bills, according to Customer service since you are budgeted you would still only pay whats within your budget right?  I don't think so, at least that's not what I saw in looking at all of their monthly bills for a year.  There were rises  and falls in cost.  Some details are not clear and when calling customer service much information is not clearly shared.  There is a lot of bicker about what the major provider charges which is charged on top of the charge from IGS.  Which is why its important to understand your bill.  You know whats not cool..? When you type IGS Energy in Google and the first six or so entries are about ripoff reports or other websites where concerned Americans are bitching about service and unfair business practices.  I'm from Chicago.  One call to understand the bill with Nicor and I learned A LOT.  Three calls to IGS where one was useful but the other two were talking circles around me.  Realizing you have been overpaying for over two years hurts the heart and mind.  Also note that if you opt to stop services with a secondary provider it can take up to two billing periods or so they say.  They can continue to get your money at a high rate till the change back is made.  WTF right.

Another thing to keep in mind is the energy is still coming from the major supplier.  These major suppliers have options, pricing options, the same deals to save you money as the secondary suppliers do.  Also if you ever have any problems with service, you never work with IGS but are told to call customer service at the major provider.  Isn't that crazy? Other than collecting your money, what else is IGS doing for you???

Read my review once or twice.  If you like, contact me via Yelp and we can talk about it.  Hopefully I'll remember all of the information I learned in the last few days.  I would rate them a solid 2.5 stars if I could.

Input: I found this place to be more expensive than it's worth.  I'm no stranger to high prices for small plates, but there's usually something special that stands out about them.  We started with queso fundido, which was tasty and of a decent size.  We ordered two dishes:  Pastel Azteca and Tinga Poblana.  The former was unique and tasty, but could have used some more spices to kick up the flavor more.  The Tinga Poblana, I'm afraid, was a very poor dish.  It was basically a small portion of pulled pork in a watery tomato stew with very little flavor.  $26 is far too expensive for that dish and it's the most regrettable purchase I can remember in recent history.  I tried two different drinks:  The Mezcalina is very, very tasty and I would recommend it; the El Naranjo Martini with tequila and mezcal was a decent martini, but nothing outstanding.  If I was to recommend this place at all, I'd have to say it's a good place to have drinks and an appetizer or two.

Their mozzarella sticks are more of a mozzarella sandwich (mozzarella between Texas toast) and it was just so-so.  It was pretty bland, I felt like it needed salt.  It was served with red sauce which was pretty good.

For dinner, we got the pumpkin ravioli and shrimps & clams in white sauce.  The pumpkin filling in the ravioli was really good, but the butter sage sauce was bland (again, maybe salt would have helped?).  The seafood was cooked well and tasted fresh, but the white sauce was bland and tasted like plain oil and butter.  Again, the portions were huge and we each took half our dish home.

Overall, the food was just okay.  The bright spot was our server, who was very sweet and attentive.  But unfortunately the food was not worth a return trip.

Input: Moshi has been on my "restaurants I want to try" list for a really long time, so my hopes were pretty high.  Maybe too high.  The initial impression was good, as the tiny restaurant has interesting art and fixtures, and the glasses are neat, but it went downhill from there.

Mostly, the food here is just overpriced.  My wife and I paid more than $36 for five little pieces of nigiri, three unusually small rolls, and two bowls of miso soup.  At most sushi places, when you order a combo, as I did today, you get both miso soup and salad, but here you have to choose. Input: I must agree with the reviewer who wondered , "Do any of the people who give Central Sq. 5-star reviews actually live here?" I am thinking that as well, because I certainly don't get the charmingly bo-ho, Williamsburg-y feel they get. Perhaps things just look prettier from far away ...

Take it from someone who has the misfortune of waiting until their lease ends, so they can move out of the smelly crotch of Cambridge: there is very little "charm" in the scabby bum who sleeps in front of 7/11 and once prominently displayed his own fecal matter for passersby. There is very little charm here at all, just a lot of crappy post-war housing with faulty plumbing and a whole lotta bum fights.

Now I've lived in a city, so I'm not some frightened country bumpkin in her first apartment. I'm used to Philadelphia (also known as both Killadelphia and Filthadelphia) but for God's sake, parts of Central Sq. make Philly look like the Hamptons. It's the amount of dirt and garbage that lines the sidewalks (I'm not sure where it all comes from) and the crowds of loud, crushing people--homeless and otherwise; again, not sure where they all come from--and the fact that during the summer, it smells like rotting milk and human feces. At first, it was appealing, like a miniature Mission tucked away in Cambridge, Land of the Ivory Tower and Hemp Pants. But really, I think it's just a dump, masquerading as a very hip place to live. It's similar to being Amy Winehouse: for a few seconds, it sounds great, but after that, you realize it's just a receptacle for crack-cocaine and insanity.

The pros, and the reason it gets two stars, are the fantastic ethnic eateries within a two-block radius. There are some great cheap eats (Moody's Falafel is the cat's pajamas ... the cat's falafel ... the shwarma's pajamas?) And I love the produce at Harvest Co-op. I'm also of the opinion it's generally a safe area. There is a police station literally off Mass Ave. I was only threatened with grievous bodily harm once, and I think it was by an Emerson student. But at the cost of having to deal with some of the most unpleasant homeless people in existence? (They're honestly disgusting. See also: the time that lady proceeded to eat her own leg scabs at the #1 bus stop.) Or what about the time that I stepped on a bloody maxi pad? The ridiculous apartment housing costs, for pretty shite living conditions? 

Nay. This bitch is moving to Brookline. Deep down, I too am a yuppie Jew. I'm done with the fauxhemian life.

Input: I was very excited to experience this restaurant -- I came here with my fiance for a romantic dinner. The decor is rustic -- lots of stuff on the walls, seems reminiscent of the old "Public Houses" of Europe, but with white tablecloths and wine glasses on each table. Seems like it started out country but then changed its mind and became fancy.

That, however, was where the fancy stopped; this was mostly to do with service. Our server, Joseph (a young man in his late 20's), seemed to know about as much about the menu as we did -- right from the initial greet he was stuttering and soft spoken. He went into the hors d'oeuvres specials, seeming as though he was asking us about them ("It's a lobster macaroni and cheese? Served in a carafe? Big enough to share?") My fiance asked for a beer recommendation for the steak; he seemed as if he had never been asked that question before, and stammered that he would go and ask the chef. I requested a wine recommendation as well, and he once again stammered (questioningly) a wine which was delicious if only he had recommended it with confidence. I felt nervous about ordering it because HE was nervous about me ordering it. 
About halfway through our hors d'oeuvres, the server finally asked if we wanted our wine and beer right now, or with the meal. This was around 30-35 minutes after being sat. Halfway through our hors d'oeuvres, and around 15 minutes after we had given our entree order to the server, he came up and rather tactlessly informed us about the entree specials AFTER WE HAD ALREADY ORDERED. Kind of like an "oh....and if you wanted to order this....sorry..."

To start, we ordered the escargot and the onion soup. The escargot was simply seasoned, but the sauce was great -- similar to another reviewer, I too dipped the bread in the sauce because I really enjoyed it. The onion soup was AMAZING: I actually tipped it to get the last of the soup out because I didn't want to waste any. I ordered a glass of the German Selbach Reisling, which was delicious and went with everything I ordered; my fiance ordered the Durkel, a dark German beer that he raved went perfectly with his New York Strip steak. 

For our entrees, as mentioned before me fiance ordered the New York Strip steak medium rare -- he was obsessed with the au gratin potatoes, and we both agreed that the carrots were cooked wonderfully. The steak left a bit to be desired -- then again, obviously this isn't a steak place, but the cut of strip did not seem to be the best, with a lot of fat and a bit tough. We both wished that the pepper sauce had a bit more kick to it, but it was very good as well! Another suggestion for the service -- when the steak arrived, Joseph then stated, "let me go get you a steak knife." Three minutes later, he arrived with it. Since this restaurant brags a fine-dining feel, having to stare at a delicious-looking, hot steak for three minutes not being able to cut into it seems a bit amateur. I won't eat until he can, so why not have the steak knife as a pre-drop, so both of us aren't watching our hot food become cold while you get him the proper utensil to eat it with? I ordered the coq au vin, and it was GREAT -- one of my favorite dishes to order, and the reason why I came here. My chicken was cooked perfectly, the sauce and mushrooms were great, it was the highlight of my evening. The coq au vin and the food are the reason for the two stars that I did give

We did decide to order an additional side of the truffle fries, just to see what they tasted like and they did not come out with the meals. I reminded the server about them, at his first (credit given: diligent) check-back: he informed me he would get them immediately. 20 minutes later, he checked back with us twice and informed us they were coming -- 25 minutes later, we were finished and asked for them to be cancelled. 

I ordered the creme brulee for dessert. I also ordered a cup of coffee. The coffee was delivered, and it was then that the server asked if I would like cream and sugar. I replied with the affirmative. My creme brulee arrived (with only one spoon for a couple....thank goodness my fiance didn't want any), and I reminded the server about my cream and sugar -- once again an item getting cold and untouched because of the server's inability to plan ahead for his Guests.

The flaws in service were ignored at the time because I will not let a bad server destroy my romantic evening. I definitely think that Joseph should be put through some additional training (wine/beer knowledge, food knowledge, and maybe a serving class) and next time in order to receive a better, classier experience I may request one of the older more experienced servers. The steak was nothing to write home about, but everything else was great and I would definitely eat here again if not to try more items on the menu. Especially my truffle fries, which I was looking forward to trying but then never received.

Input: Can you say disappointment?  I've been to this location many times, and it's never been disappointing.  Sure, the food seems pretty meh to me, but the good company and decent service usually makes up for it.

Wish I could say the same for the last time I was here. Even the best company couldn't save this visit because of the awful service -- err, I mean, no service.

Granted, we came in on a late night -- Thursday, just after midnight, to be exact.  But isn't one of the selling points of this place round-the-clock service?  Well, what they don't tell you is you get no service if you come in then.

Me and the date were seated promptly, but it all went downhill from there.  It took us at least 5 minutes to see our server, and then at least 10 more minutes for him to come back with our drinks.  Speaking of, the fella I was with ordered a sweet tea, and they said they didn't have any sweet tea.  SURELY YOU JEST.  So, the Mr. had a chocolate milk; me a water.  And yes, 10 MINUTES.

We couldn't decide if we wanted an appetizer or dessert, but fortunately (or unfortunately) we had plenty of time to figure that out.  We never saw our server again.  I mean, we did, but he was tending to every other nearby table except ours.  On the bright side (if there is one), I learned that I have the power of turning invisible at Kerbey Lane.  Oh, that's not an advantage?  Darn!

After a few more minutes of trying to be patient and understanding, me and the Mr. decided to get scooting.  He was waiting for our server to return so he could pay for the milk.  I looked at the menu, saw it was $1.97, told him to leave a couple bucks on the table, and said "Let's roll".

Pity we left our server a three cent tip.  That seemed far excessive.  And turns out, the fella I was with said his chocolate milk wasn't really tasty.

Kerbey Lane, y'all did FANTASTIC that night.  For those who have trouble reading sarcasm, that was sarcasm.

So, you've been warned.

We went around 8:30 and they had already shut down patio which made us feel unwelcome at the get go. While we waited for our food, we saw almost 10 people that were turned away or turned off from coming in because it was almost 9, which is when they close (super early considering it is next to a university). They continued to close up the entire time while we were having our dinner, which made us feel awkward and rushed to get out, again, even though it wasn't even 9 pm yet.

The food was pretty lousy. I order the Japanese flavors with noodles, tofu and vegetables. Not much flavor at all in any of the components and not much food regardless. I'm not really sure how adding vegetables on top of the dish adds much considering one of the vegetables was a cole slaw. The cole slaw was actually decent on it's own, but it was really something I wanted to mix into my noodle bowl? My boyfriend got a kale salad on his and same thing, just sort of random for a topping. He ordered the chicken, which he barely touched because it was chewy and just generally unpleasant. 

Kind of a bummer since the concept is fine. 

Recommendations:

More sauce, more flavor, rethink arbitrary vegetable toppings, replace weird frozen chicken with real chicken strips, don't make patrons feel unwelcomed especially when you are still open.

Input: This was our first time coming here for dinner. First and foremost, our server was great--no complaints there at all. The kitchen really needs some help, though. 

Long story short, it took 20 minutes (conservative estimate) after ordering for them to let us know they were out of the fish and chips two of us had ordered, at which point we had to order something else. I can understand coming back right after we ordered to let us know, but 20 minutes later?? We were promised 25% off our replacement entrees due to the wait, which was appreciated. Food arrived another 20 minutes after that. I ordered a medium steak, which arrived a textbook well-done. The server agreed it was beyond overcooked and removed it from our bill. When the bill came, the other replacement entrée wasn't 25% off, but we'd been there for over 2 hours at that point and were just ready to leave. We paid and walked out, then realized we forgot our leftovers on the table. We came back no longer than 2 minutes after leaving but they'd already thrown away the to-go boxes. That was mostly our fault, but it seems like they might wait 5 minutes or so to see if we came back...

Also, there is no kids menu at all. We had to pay for an adult entrée for our 3-year-old, who of course only ate about 20% of the meal. 

Again, our server was great and very apologetic about everything, but the kitchen was another story...

Input: I'm sure that this is akin to blasphemy, but I really do not care for Juan In a Million.  When it comes to Tex-Mex, I am very easy to please.  Throw some cheese, sour cream, chiles and cilantro on most anything, and I'll happily devour it.  We are soooo spoiled in Austin, because coming here from pretty much anywhere else in the world, our Tex-Mex joints blow everything else out of the water.  

Moving on...I have heard friends, tv shows, media, etc...praise Juan time and time again, so I feel kind of crazy not being able to agree, but I just think that...get ready...the Don Juan taco is gross.  Being from Atlanta, GA, I grew up on all things pork lard-infused, and DO love them, but pork lard in my tacos...no bueno.  Gotta draw the line somewhere.  Juan in a Million is the opposite of Curra's.  Curra's breakfast tacos are clean-tasting, bursting with flavor and let the ingredients stand on their own, whereas the Don Juan is like eating a garbage pail trainwreck.  

The only reason I give it 2 stars is because the Juan is so charming with his whole "i come to everyone's table!" schtick and the prices are really pretty amazing.  I truly couldn't finish even half of my $3 taco...but that's for other reasons.

Input: After hearing positive comments about Toro Bravo, my boyfriend and I were truly looking forward to celebrating my birthday at this restaurant. For first impressions, the the ambience is appealing, space being limited and quaint, we opted to grab a drink next door while we waited for our table. The wait time was not anything ridiculous considering it was a Saturday evening (about 30-45 min), however, after being called for our table we realized the table we had waited close to an hour for, was a table lack thereof: we were seated next to the kitchen within a couple feet of the servers' pick-up window for all outgoing dishes. On any other visit this would not have been such a letdown, however we requested a nice table for our celebratory evening.

The hostess was nice enough to mark gluten free options on our menu for us, making the ordering process hassle-free. Considering we had never eaten here before, we were curious about portion sizes and how many tapas to order. Oddly our waitress seemed annoyed when we asked this. We ended up ordering the sautéed spinach and wrapped dates (both were very appetizing) along with some Spanish red wine. The raciones we ordered didn't take long to arrive either. Once the entrees arrived we were hoping to order another glass of wine, however, our waitress had disappeared since taking our order and never even checked in throughout the entirely of the meal. While we still had some food on our plates she asked if she could clear our plates several times, we definitely were clued into her attempt to move us along in order to bring another batch of customers to this "table." 

Considering the food was good, the atmosphere was welcoming (when not next to the kitchen), and service was lacking, we may not be able to justify a reason to revisit. Plenty of other good eats in Portland.

Input: This was my 2nd visit to Sweet Samba and have a big complaint - the service requested was not the service received. I had called in and reserved their version of a deep bikini. (As a side note, their waxing service menu is not as straightforward as it should be. Each style has cute names rather than clear distinctions.)

My service was excellent and painless. The aesthetician and I had such a good time chatting (I know some people prefer just to watch the overhead TV) that I wasn't really paying attention to what was or was not being waxed. For some waxing newbies, this may seem hard to believe, but I'm a veteran waxing customer and it just doesn't hurt anymore. I'm used to it and pain is a non-issue. Anyhoo...

Afterwards when I got to the desk to pay, my bill was more than expected. I told them I had asked for a deep bikini (The Barely Bare) but apparently had received the French Kiss (brazilian with a landing strip). I had the feeling there had been a little bait and switch. I know what I requested and was not happy that somehow there had been a miscommunication between the front desk reservation and what was told to the aesthetician. 

To sum up, the service is good & the place is cute but I do not like feeling like I had been tricked into an upgrade. My advice is to pay very close attention to the confusing waxing menu and be sure to reiterate to your aesthetician exactly what is being done so there will be no confusion.

Input: We avoided any wait at all and had an early Thursday evening dinner at the Waterford location. We were warmly greeted and, based on the significant number of "full service" seats available, declined the absolute worst table in the restaurant that was first offered. Thankfully the hostess recovered nicely and seated us in a non-traffic area. 

Our server, Lisa, approached us with a smile and genuine greeting. She was a bright spot throughout the meal walking us (first timers) through the menu and checking on us unobtrusively 3 or 4 times. 

My burger was cooked exactly to order and was tasty. The "house made" pickle was a small but nice complement. My dining partner ordered the opened face "Mom's Sloppy Joe." She found it tasty as well. 

The downside...the food was not hot. My burger arrived "warm" but clearly (hopefully) not to the restaurant's standard. The bun had clearly not been warmed at all. And, the same was true for my friend's open face sandwich and our side of tater tots. Very disappointing.

All that said we concluded that, other than our server, the experience provided little compelling reason to visit anytime soon or to rate the dinner higher than a "2." And that number was driven by an excellent server. 

Don't be misled by the lines at the door. There are better options.

Input: Just came back yesterday from a spring break vacation trip with the family. We stayed here at StaySKY Suites, which also owns Lake Buena Vista Resort Village & Spa, so we thought this place should be good. 

When we checked in the guy at the front desk was Aaron, although he was just doing his job, he was not the most friendly guy. My wife has a disability due to her hip and I wanted to save her a trip from walking to the front desk and the guy would not allow us to check-in unless he saw her face, even though I had her driver's licenses and mine.

We stayed on the fourth floor, which was nice as we were very close to the elevator, which makes it easier for my wife. However, during our entire stay, we had to use the stairs about 90% of the time because the elevator is so extremely slow. My 7 and 4 year old son and I ran down the stairs and was always able to beat the elevator to the 1st floor and that is without it stopping in-between floors.

Overall, our room was nice and the beds were very comfortable. Unfortunately, one of the biggest problems we had at this hotel was that there is no hot water, only warm. (0 being cold, 10 being burning hot, it was about a 5-6). My wife was not happy about taking moderately warm showers. Internet... The hotel has free wifi, but it is very slow, less than 3MB download, and less than 2MB upload.

StaySKY offers free breakfast and like other reviewers say, it is nothing special. However, all of the ladies who handle the breakfast in the morning are outstanding, they do a fantastic job and were so very friendly and helpful. They were wonderful and are such hard workers, because this place gets very packed for breakfast. The first day I ate breakfast they had these powdered circle eggs and some nasty corn beef hash that gave me an upset stomach. On a positive note though, Saturday they have a very good breakfast, so if you stay here, definitely eat here on Saturday. They make freshly scrambled eggs and serve freshly cut ham, it was a total 180 compared to the other days.

Not to be so negative with my review, but during our stay the hotel lost its power for a minute or two and our hotel room door had a hard time opening. We had to literally hit the center of the door to get it to open, it kept sticking. We definitely had a lot of issues at this hotel, but I am glad we stayed here instead of their resort (Lake Buena Vista Resort Village & Spa) as one of their reviews say their truck got broken into. 

This hotel does also have a pool, it felt very nice and warm and they have a hot tub as well. Sadly, we did not get to use it though, but it was open. Also, if you need ICE, make sure you turn the ice maker on inside the hotel room, as the hotel charges for ice. There is no ice makers outside in the lobbies of the hotel.

The best thing about StaySKY is its location. It is very close to all the major destinations and the hotel is very affordable. When you visit Orlando, you will spend a lot of money, so you are better off getting an ok place to stay, so you have money to visit the overly expensive theme parks.

Input: Dropped in after a post-dinner walk from Unchai to have a snack and dessert. We whiled away a half hour savouring a dessert before trying the calamari at the Happy Hour price.

As usual the server wasn't exactly thrilled especially as we didn't order any alcohol (none of us being drinkers). But the place wasn't exactly packed either.

Calamari ($14 or $10 during Happy Hour)
-We were informed the $10 happy hour portion is the same as the $14 regular menu portion. 
-Not recommended even at $10. Seemed flat somehow. Lacked seasoning? And price for portion at $10. 
-If you do get it, try to pair each piece with the fried jalapeño slices to get some bite to each bite.

Billy Miner Pie ($7) mocha ice cream on a chocolate crust with hot fudge, caramel, and almonds 
-Simple idea that's tasty. Ice cream is soft and easy to spoon through but doesn't start melting into a puddle right away. Still, if you're going to try more than one dessert I wouldn't ask for them all to be brought out at once.
-Seemed like a surprising portion for $7 so if you're dining solo or duo, plan ahead.
-Our server said their cheesecake was made by the Keg but offsite and distributed to the outlets so this was probably the same. So you can expect supermarket quality for their desserts in general.
-The portion is big enough that if you get bored midway you can experiment with the pepper and salt at your table. Go heavy on the pepper to get enough impact. For the salt to get that salted caramel taste, go easy as that salt grinder gives you rather large chips.

There is a shuttle that takes you to the testing center but apparently they forgot about us and they end up sending us a shuttle  at 745 instead of 730. We are supposed to be the testing center by 8 o'clock. They got us there in time, but it's never good to have these last minute issues.
Same thing happened with the shuttle that was supposed to pick us up. It supposed to meet us there at 3:30 PM but they were never there. We called the front desk and they probably sent us a shuttle.
The continental breakfast on the club lounge is a joke. It consists of bread, watered eggs, and bacon. They also have some juices and such.
Overall, if you're coming to Atlanta for the clinical skills exam, just stay at the hotel that is right next door to the testing center.

Input: After reading quite a bit of good reviews for this restaurant, my husband and I trekked over looking forward to some great beer and a  late afternoon meal. Unfortunately,  we were  sorely disappointed and wished we had gone elsewhere. The place was packed when we arrived but we were able to get a seat at the end of the  bar that was very tight and uncomfortable for dining    Anyway,  the place really assaults your senses on every level and not in a good way.   Once seated I just want to leave and go to a quieter, cozier  place to eat, drink and relax.   We went for the extensive beer selection as it sounded interesting.  My husband was happy to see a German wheat beer that he loved, however, it was poured in the wrong glass, a Pilsner glass verses a Weizenbier or Weissbier glass.  When we asked the bartender for the correct glass we were told they got rid of those glasses, and only use the pilsner!  She also tried to tell him that he is actually getting more beer as the Pilsner glass is slightly larger. But that is not the point, as there are reasons for the correct glass, as it is tapered to trap yeast at the bottom of the glass, and the correct beer glass should be used.  My husband is German and he would never come back here for this reason alone.  The manager really needs to look into this, go to The Barking Dog or the Grill Next Door and look 
ah how they handle a large beer selection with the correct glass for each beer,*** IF YOU ARE GOING TO CHARGE $7.50 A BEER THEN USE THE CORRECT GLASS!

Lastly, there is no bar atmosphere here, people should go in and sit at the bar to see what I mean....There were at least 10 bartenders, and each bartender had a small area, appeared to each have 2-4 customers each..  The moment we sat down we were handed a menu, as if we had sat at a table.  The bartenders were hanging around everywhere and when we decided not to order food,  she swiped up the menus and we had to flag her down for our second drinks, clearly she wanted us to leave for turnover sake.
Anyway, very disappointed.

An acquaintance from Italy stayed in Boston area for a while and before going back to Italy he told me that the only authentic Italian place he found around here was Pulcinella Trattoria in Cambridge.

Input: Gyu-Kaku is a Japanese-based chain of Yakiniku, or grilled meat restaurants.  With several dozen American locations and over 600 in Japan, they are the "Olive Garden" of Japanese-Korean tabletop grill eateries.

Similar to "Olive Garden," the operation is formula-driven; one of commercial-grade marinates, lower-grade proteins, inattentive servers and gimmicky promotions.  With a group and with alcohol flowing freely I can see how the social dining experience might be enjoyable.  As a businessman dining alone, and with evening work awaiting his return, my experience fell far short of that mark-- it was an genuine ordeal.

The dining room is large, yet partitioned into small dining cubicles. Seated in a back corner of the busy restaurant, I decided to use a coupon I'd received to bring the $49 "Ultimate All You Can Eat" (53 items / 90 minutes) into an acceptable expense account range.  The gas grill was ignited as I placed my first order.  Unfortunately, the grill had numerous and unpredictable "cold spots," a fact which plagued my dining experience throughout the evening.

Ordered on the first pass was fried pork gyoza, fried cheese wontons, Angus beef rib in sweet tare sauce, beef tongue, pork belly shio, garlic shrimp and shishito peppers.  The kitchen was out of the beef rib.

Both of the fried appetizers were very obviously pre-fried, then reheated when my order arrived.  The gyoza were tasty, but both were woefully overcooked and unappetizing in appearance.  Pork belly, shrimp and the peppers weren't bad-- once reliable cooking areas on the grill were found.  In each case the marinates used were soulless and poor imitations of quality Japanese grill preparations.  Further, the kitchen's attentiveness to trimming proteins of sinew was inadequate for this style of cooking.

My second order, garlic shoyu chicken and garlic mushrooms, revisited the same type of insipid commercial marinates, but were eatable.  The mushrooms were delivered in an aluminum foil packet, making it impossible to determine their cooking time without repeatedly opening the packet.  Both were considerably better than what had been served previously.

Service bordered upon slow for the duration of my meal, but the process of getting a check, then getting my credit card back, redefined all standards of slow service.

I would characterize Gyu-Kaku as a poor value for the money, and not a chain to which I would choose to return.

Input: When I first found Purple Carrot I was so excited that there was a vegan version of Blue Apron out there and couldn't wait to try it. I subscribed to the service for a little over a year and even upgraded to the TB12 meals as they are higher in protein and lower in sugars and processed ingredients. I will say that all the meals Purple Carrot cooks up are, for the most part, extremely tasty. They also provide colorful easy to follow recipe cards and even sent me a really nice TB12 binder to put all my recipe cards in. 

In March 2018 I decided to cancel my subscription. It seems that Purple Carrot's Operations team just can't get it together and despite several mishaps, I finally had enough. Also, the quality has gone down...way down. I'm sorry, but when I pay $78 per week for a meal delivery service, moldy ingredients, missing recipe cards, and missing ingredients is simply inexcusable. I have given Purple Carrot multiple chances to get it together and they're only getting worse. Every time I receive a box and there's something wrong with it I send them an email and I receive the same response, "I'll let my operations team know..." yet nothing changes. Today, for example I received a moldy onion and a green onion that's literally a day or two away from going bad. This tells me that their produce isn't being turned around fast enough likely because they're losing customers left and right (based on the reviews here). Prior boxes have had missing recipe cards and missing ingredients. How can you be a meal delivery service and have ingredients missing from the box?! Recently I have noticed mistakes in the recipes as well such as ingredients being provided but not included in the recipe...or it will tell you to chop something but won't refer to it again in the recipe so it becomes a guessing game. 

The quality is also declining. Part of TB12's slogan is "Eat Like a Champion." I highly doubt Tom Brady eats boil in bag quinoa and microwaveable minute rice. I joined Purple Carrot for healthy home cooked meals, not ingredients that are boiled or nuked in plastic. 

Lastly, every time I log into Purple Carrot, there's a link letting me know I can send a free box to a friend....so I did and I quickly realized that this a shady deal offered by Purple Carrot disguised as them being generous. In order for your friend to receive a "free" box they have to sign up for a subscription and enter their credit card info, which if they're not familiar with the skip deadlines, which most aren't, they wind up getting charged for a box. I see several people have complained and this happened to my friend and he received poor customer service. What really grinds my gears is that I thought I was doing something nice for a friend and really wanted to show him how tasty meat-free can be but now Purple Carrot has soured the situation. Additionally, I feel this shows how devalued I am as a customer of Purple Carrot...that they would provide my friend who I referred, poor customer service. The whole thing is shady and shows that Purple Carrot is desperate for customers but what they don't realize is they're losing customers by engaging in these shady practices. If you truly want to spread the word about how delicious and healthy your food is then do that...don't make people sign up and charge them for stuff they don't want. I can't stand when businesses do stuff like that...it NEVER works out for the business in the long run. 

Look, I have been vegan for over 3 years now and I'm pretty hardcore about it. Often times I struggle with what to cook and what to eat...or how much to cook...so this service was perfect for me. It sucks that Purple Carrot has left such a bad taste in my mouth. No pun intended.

The brochure mentioned the Canadian Trail. I was intrigued. I like to learn about the places I visit. The Canada Trail was nothing more than colorful (somewhat muted) bricks inlaid into the ground that were labeled with Canadian place names. No explanations. No information. Just...boring.

Despite Canada Place being pretty darn lackluster, you may notice the two stars that I've given it. One is for the view. It's on the water's edge and it does allow for some beautiful views of the water, city, and nearby mountains. The second star is for FlyOver Canada. You can check my review for that ride seperately, but I have to give credit to Canada Place for housing the attraction.

Input: Planned on eating dinner here tonight, but ended up with a plate of buffalo wings at the Ninety-Nine. 

Only thing sweet about this berry is the service, food is sour (literally).  Open tables on a Saturday night is never a good sign.  Based on the patrons on either side of us, this is a place for drinks, lots of them (nothing wrong with that), but not for food.  

Quick rundown - didn't touch the Bolognese after the first SOUR bite. No tomato sauce, just pasta tossed with tough meat and hard carrot chunks - a dead giveaway this "sauce" was just mixed together for a few minutes before serving (taken off the bill - classy service).  French Onion Soup, which a tavern should nail, was absolutely tasteless.  No seasoning, could've been warm water.  The wife, who was nice enough to escort me to the Nines afterwards for my buff wings, got the Turkey Tip special with mashed potatoes.  Again, no seasoning, literally could've been eating anything warm - like military or school cafeteria bland.  Other reviews are right, great service, tasteless food (unless you get the bolognese with the sour kick).  Disappointing for the wait staff and such a great location.

Input: First, let me say that their food is probably worth three/four stars. It was decent pizza and their cheese is really good. However, as many of the recent reviews have stated their customer service isn't the best. I tried out Yelps new online ordering and I was very disappointed. On a Friday night around 8, I figured it would take about 45 minutes or so for a pie. That's fairly typical and I'm aware that they aren't a huge chain that delivers. Place my order and as stated above, it said around 35-60 minutes. As it got closer to 9, they updated saying it would be delayed and to expect it about 9:17. Ok, and hour and 17 minutes, I can accept that. It then became 9:30 and I hadn't received an updated. I call and was put on hold for 5 minutes, nothing terrible. The woman was nice enough but didn't seem to have an idea as to what was going on behind the scenes. I can over look that to... maybe she only works front end. The manager, maybe owner, gets on the phone. He's pretty abrupt and almost sounds as if I'm causing him an inconvenience by calling. Once he finds my order, he lets me know that it's just now being made and will be ready in 20 more minutes. I question the timing since it's been an hour and a half already. He informs me that if you order online or ask for delivery, your order gets out at the back of the line to everyone else. I was a little annoyed since it shouldn't matter how you order it should be treated the same (within reason and as to not totally eff your dining in customers). I told him that I would be willing to come pick it up myself since it may take less time then the 2 hours it was already going to take. No mention of, "I'm sorry it's taking so long; Can I get you xyz so that you're not paying for the delivery charge?" Simply nothing. Got to the restaurant and there were 3 people inside. It was completely empty. He was on the phone with another very upset customer whom was saying whatever they got was inedible and was asking them to remake them. Let's just say the rest of the conversation wasn't very pleasant either. He hung up and the woman up front started bad mouthing the customer. I got my pie and left. 

The food was decent. Better than a chain but not worth 2 hours. There are a lot of places to get pizza and if you're going to make it as a small business you need to treat your customers better. If they are unable to handle online orders from multiple websites, then they need to pick one and only one. I was really hoping to find a new pizza place since moving to this side of town. Alas, the search continues. Pitty.

We also didn't discuss how short I wanted the layers, and they are too short.... basically....EVERYTHING IS TOO SHORT! I still gave her a nice tip and  I'm not gona cry about it.
