Input: The Yelp phrase corresponding to two stars reads: "Meh. I've experienced better" - and that's exactly how I feel about this place. For a girl who loves coffee shops & cute, independent stores, I'm totally unimpressed by this place, and I can tell you exactly why:


1. Speed of Service:
HOLY heck is this place slow! Since I work close by, it's convenient to come ... but I regret it every time when I'm twenty minutes in, and still food- and coffee-less. In fact, my team - which has been around here for years - has stopped going in the past few months, because they really just didn't have the time to wait around.



2. The Stock - or Lack Thereof:
More often than not, the real culprit behind the speed isn't the person making the food or coffee, but the fact that they don't have the things they need. Even though it's 3pm in the afternoon - aka that time when everyone starts to fall asleep at their desks - they'll be out of coffee, and have to brew a fresh batch. It's worse with food; here's my experience from yesterday:

I wanted a chicken caesar salad for a quick lunch. Hardly complicated - but literally fifteen minutes after my colleague and I had ordered and paid (she got the same thing), we are informed that the store doesn't have any romaine lettuce.

No ... lettuce? in a place ... that sells all variety of salads?!

(Why do I always seem to have problems with lettuce, in the bizzarest of situations?! Seriously.)

Thanks to that hiccup, my "quick lunch" takes 30 minutes just to procure (sigh)


3. Price/Quality Ratio
I'm not saying that every place has to have stellar service or always be on top of their game. But if you're not going to be top-notch, don't charge me accordingly. Mohr & McPherson Cafe is, from what I can tell, the most expensive cafe in this neighborhood ... and not only is the service slow, but the portions are small, its baked goods are often dry/stale-tasting ... not really a bargain.


Bottom Line: If you're nearby and too lazy to walk elsewhere (and also need to kill some time), then this place may be what you're looking for ... but if you're just a normal person who has a job to get back to, this detour may prove to be too costly (in all senses of the word).

Input: Park Creek Kitchen is an odd congregation of contradictions.   There's definitely a neighborhood feel to the restaurant.  Several people were greeted as regulars while we were dining.  I could totally see a South of Lane UA dad putting on his hawaiian shirt, khakis and Keen Sandles (I swear I see variations of this outfit every time I'm out to dinner in Upper Arlington) and walking over for dinner with his family.  It's in an interesting space, too--formerly a bank building.

High concept entrees mix with classic sandwiches and burgers with varying outcomes.  My etouffee was pretty good, my wife's crab cake was a bit bland but we both agreed the mac and cheese was outstanding.

Smart decor (If you get seated towards the back of the front room you'll see the old bank vault--very cool) mixes with paper napkins and those nasty old chairs you see in fast food joints.

And fantastic bartending mixes with some off the mark cocktails--my Woodford Reserve Manhattan was spot on (and strong--holy moly), but my wife's Lemon Drop was a big miss.  

Mainly, we were a little surprised by the price of our dinner--two drinks, one appetizer, two entrees and a side ended up being over $100 with tip.  For that price, there are better options for a night out.

Input: Went here for lunch last month, while visiting Austin for the weekend. Many of my friends have raved about the food here. We chose to sit outside, since the decor was really cute. 

The dumplings appetizer was delicious. I enjoyed the sprinkle of crispy fried shallots on top and the ginger chili oil the dumplings were in. The oil sauce was not too spicy and had a tang of lemon. 

We waited 35 minutes for our food, after we had gotten our appetizer. Many people, who had arrived after us, had gotten their food before us. 

I ordered the specialty bánh mì. I like the bread of my bánh mì toasted. The bread was cold, and there was not anything special about its contents: pâté, roasted pork, and liver mousse. Overall, it was dry, cold, and lacked flavor. 

My boyfriend ordered the bún with flank steak. The steak was cold.

Food is pricy, which I had known looking at the menu, while waiting for our table. My bánh mì was $11, my boyfriend's bún dish was $16, and our dumplings were $12. I spent $60 on a meal that I felt was not worth $60. Our server only came to our table twice. I was very disappointed at the experience I had here.

Input: Avoid this company, they are disorganized and give out misleading information! Their application and screening process are ridiculous and they are not honest about what is required to qualify for an approval. When I went to meet their agent for a viewing, I specifically asked about using a combo of income and savings instead of just one or the other to qualify. The agent said that this would be fine as long as the combination amounts to what is required. So, I applied, because my income/savings combo was more than enough to qualify. I have good-excellent credit, by the way, and a decent 2 year rental history. 

Five days later, I get a call from Bemrose Consulting (the screening company) that I'm about to be denied only because they have not received a rental reference from our current landlords. So, then I get involved as a middle man to resolve that issue: I make multiple back and forth phone calls between the landlord and Bemrose due to supposed problems with the landlord not getting their FAX (what is this? 1990? Most places use email now!), the landlord and Bemrose blaming each other for the miscommunication - this went on for about an hour before I ended up resolving it as the middle man between the two. Finally, I call Bemrose to confirm that they got the fax from the landlord. Good, they finally had received it. 

So I wait to hear back from RPM. RPM finally calls me - I'm denied because I don't have EITHER an income of $50k OR $50k in the bank. Or you can get a guarantor who makes or has 5x the monthly rent, so above $80k. They don't accept a combo of income and savings from either applicant OR guarantor, despite the fact that the agent TOLD me that this would be fine! So it ended up being a stressful and complete waste of my time and money! I would have never applied if they didn't accept a COMBO of income/savings. This place is unprofessional and charges a ridiculously high application fee of $52 per applicant for Bemrose to turn around and basically force me to do their work for them - obtaining a reference from the landlord. 

I would give zero stars if I could. Stay away! Just look at the other Yelp reviews - this place is consistently subpar and doesn't even seem to care. What is absurd about all of this is - not only did the agent tell me to apply anyway when I disclosed my situation (income/savings combo), but before the miscommunication between Bemrose and my landlord happened - RPM had already seen all of my financial documents as I had submitted it 5 days prior to Bemrose contacting me about the landlord reference. Why did they not just flat our reject my application when they saw I did not have enough or at least contact me and tell me that it I did not qualify solely based on income? Instead I had to waste an hour of my day stressfully acting as a middle man between Bemrose and the landlord only to have them call me hours later and say that the income requirements did not suffice anyway. RPM needs to train their agents not to give the WRONG information to people - otherwise your business just looks like a racket trying to collect application fees from people when you know for a fact they will not meet your income requirements. This, combined with the absolute unprofessionalism of Bemrose makes this entire application process not even worth it - even if you did meet their income qualifications.

The place was not that busy, and there was no reason for us to wait over 20 minutes for our drinks and our checks.  Horrible.   OK, now to the the pizza.  Pizza is usually one of those things where even if it's not that great, you can still stomach it.  Well, this pizza changed my mind.  I ordered a small, pepperoni, sausage, and mushroom to go. When I got home (5 minutes away), it was ice cold already. So, I warmed up the oven and waited for the pie to re-heat.    After the first bite, I was ready to stop eating it.  One...there was almost no cheese at all on the pizza.  It was all sauce and toppings.  First I'll talk about the sauce.  Acidic, metallic, and no tomato taste at all.  It also had the consistency of tomato paste. Horrible.  The toppings:  couldn't even taste them, because the so called sauce was so overwhelmingly bad.  Pepperoni seemed to be OK, but there was barely one piece on each slice. Mushrooms--actually tasted great, but again, very few and far between.  Sausage--I don't know what this was.  Little grains of grey substance,that had no taste.  Not even worth adding to the pizza.    Long story short, I suffered through one slice,and thew the rest of the pizza in the trash.  Worst pizza I've ever had.  Pizza Hut is better than this, and I HATE Pizza Hut.  
In summary, I will probably still go here for Happy Hour because it's close to the office, but will never, never order this pizza again.  I heard some horror stories from a friend who used to work here, and I should have heeded their warnings.   I won't get into that, because it was pretty bad.  Let's just say the sanitation in the kitchen was non-existent.    
Thank you.

Input: ***BEWARE OF THIFTY/HERTZ WHICH OWNS THIFTY***

If I could give this company no stars at all I would! I rented a standard SUV from Thifty for the week of Thanksgiving. When I arrived to the counter at Thifty it took 10 minutes to get someone to come out of their office and it was only because of the lady at the stand next to them went to go get the guy. Then I told him that I had rented a full size car but because we were traveling with our two kids, luggage, car seats, and stroller I wanted to see what the price would be for the standard SUV. He then quoted me a daily price that was identical to the price I could have booked prior to arriving on the same website that I booked the full size car with. He then proceeded to tell me that I would not get any of the money applied to this upgrade from the previous rental. Because my hands were tied I asked him the "out the door price", which he gave me and told me that he didn't have very many which is why it was so expensive. One of the things he asked me was if I needed tolls covered, I told him where I was driving and he said no you don't need it. That was all that was said about tolls. I took the offer and he handed  me an envelope after typing on his computer and told me to go outside to pick my SUV. We get out to the lot and there is 8 different vehicles to choose from(not many left) we pick the one we want and we got on our way to our destination. As we were about 30 minutes into our drive my wife checked the account and wondered why our account was showing an extra $400 more then what he quoted taken out of our account. I called Thifty customer service and told the lady what happened and she told me that I had to call in after I return the car and they will refund the entire amount of the upgrade because he overcharged me. She gave me a case number and said that would be proof that what she is telling me is true and that all the calls are recorded.
After Thanksgiving I returned the car and waited until the next day to call Thifty. After explaining what happened to about 6 different people because i kept getting hung up on without a callback, customer service proceeded to tell me that even with the case number that there was nothing they could do. They then escalated the issue and still nothing! They told me i could email in and that's the only way they would review the calls. So I then emailed into Thifty support and 10 days later they email back to tell me they will do nothing for me. 
Almost a month later I checked my bank account and all of a sudden I got charged $65 in tolls that I wasn't even aware I went through. And, also was not supposed to get charged for at all because the gentleman at the counter told me I didn't need it. After calling in again, they told me that I was charged for the toll transponder, even though it was not on my agreement.
I will never rent a car from Thifty again, which by the way is managed by Hertz!

Input: To all my military and goverment employees I recommend you stay away. Where do  I began!  If you value character and professionalism stay away. This  place seemed to be "Ghetto Managed" This post is in regards to my stay at the Fairfield Marriott from 7 to 10 June 2016. I had a incident that I tried to address with the GM where a front desk employee exercise some untrue words in regard to my character and professionalism . 

Prior to me writing this post I noticed a review dating 14 June 16 where the same staff member that I am complaining about seem to have a run in with a elder couple. My first thought was.... when will someone hold this place to the "Marriott standard". I don't know if this place has had a staff / management change or not but based off the last few reviews it is going down hill (my opinion). As of today I will advice all military and government employees that I know about my experience here.

I contacted the GM on a Monday to express my concerns at that point he said that he would get back with me, left him a voice mail to verify receipt of my email and no response.  Friday came around and still no response.  I had to go through customer care to get him to call back and address my issues. 

When he did call back my expectations was that he had feedback of video that would prove that his employee had indeed lied about the things that was said....ahhh no , his response was that his associate is entitled to his opinion.  So with that being said I have discovered to more things about this place.

1. The GM doesn't care about customer complaints , if so he would of contacted me and not me hunting him down . His response for not contacting me was that people are some times off, true but for 4 days.

2. The management supports employees lying to cover their own tracks. Why even tell me you would look at video if you send 4 days and don't come back with a statement saying what was said and what wasnt. I wish I could post the conversation that a recorded between us...sad!

On to other issues: Each time I stay at a Marriott property I requested that I stay on the bottom floor due to my excessive equipment, each time at this particular property end up on the 3rd floor. In most cases at other properties I get this request 95% of the time because of early reservation.  when I brought this up to the GM his response was that it is a"requested" I got it but maybe if you prebook according to request you won't have these issues, they seem to assign your room once you arrive versus prior to arrival, well that is what we'll managed properties seem to do.

The LACK of concern for customer complaints can be seen by the generic response from management on most of the reviews on this site. 

To close I will say I have been staying at the Marriott for many years and plan on continuing.  I love most of there properties just not this one. When you look at there ratings for the airport area the are rated worst than the Country INN and Suites and just a bit better than the Super 8.  Common this is a Marriott property they have to do better.

Input: This is certainly not run like the normal B&B and is really a bed and make your own breakfast if you get up before 9am. We arrived on Thursday a half hour before the scheduled check in time (4-7pm) for a four night stay and no one was there.  So we left to do some things for awhile and came back at 4:45.  Still no one there, we waited awhile and then made a phone call to an answering machine before we left, ready to find other accommodations. When he called back he stated, " I forgot you were coming". He said he'd leave a key in a basket on the porch.  There were no instructions on where to go, what to do.  We wandered through the house looking for our room. The next morning we came downstairs at 7:15 and made our own coffee.   Got a voicemail at 8:30am from the owner that breakfast would be at around 9am, call if any problems.  We had stuff to do, couldn't wait until 9.  The next morning (Saturday) it was the same routine, and we met another couple who had arrived the night before to the same circumstances.  The owner (husband) showed up at 9 to make breakfast for the 4 of us, and at first his attitude was as if he was doing us a favor.  He then sat at the table with us and was quite pleasant but that was the only time we saw him, and we never met his wife.  On Sunday we had brunch plans so there was no sign of him all day and no housekeeping service.  We were hoping to get fresh towels after 3 nights but it was not to be.  While in the house for the two days before we met the owner, we noted that there was no toilet paper in the downstairs bathroom and a dead roach on kitchen floor which we mentioned to him and was rectified on Saturday.  Our room was comfortable but there was no lightbulb in one of lamps.  The website stated that guests had Neutrogena products in their rooms - not the case - and Ozarka water.  There was a water cooler in the kitchen that remained empty throughout our stay and there were no water bottles or any other water offered. The front porch light was never on so it was hard to find the door lock when coming back in the dark at night.  Monday morning we had to leave around 7:30 to get on the road so again we made our own coffee and left the keys near the front door since we were not given any instructions.  Most B&B's advise their guests of the hours of breakfast service and are on the premises to greet their guests. We would not recommend staying here if you want any kind of service or interaction with the proprietors.  It was the oddest experience we have ever had at a B&B

Input: Not really surprised given other reviews, but yep, I couldn't get in with priority pass just now. Asked anyway, just out of curiosity, whether the sign out in front was true, and the person there said, with a huge smile, "yes, it is *very* true", and started in on the spiel of other places I could go (implied, but not stated outright, "to hell" being one of the available options). I don't totally blame her, I'm sure she gets that same question a hundred times a day and she's super sick of it, but... if I look in and it's maybe 30% full on a Monday afternoon in the off-season, and an hour later I look in again and same thing, clearly they just never participate in PP ever. Which is fine, that's their choice to participate or not, but if they never participate ever, why advertise that they do? I don't assume other lounges will take priority pass - cause they didn't say they would. Being full is one thing, but they... weren't. At all. Or if it's just based on day and time of day, they should just put the times they do or don't accept PP on their sign and the PP website like some other lounges do instead just saying "based on capacity", which really seems to mean "whenever we feel like it, for no particular reason".

I hate when people post bad reviews based on "it wasn't open", but in this case I feel that's kinda justified. (But do note, people who don't have PP and could get in for some other reason: I don't have any idea how good the lounge is, first-hand.)

This location is a joke. They MUST do good with the late night happy hour crowd because every single time we've gone during the day, the place has been empty, even though it's in a fantastic location! Unbelievable.

Better advice? Don't even come to this location.

Input: Unfortunately I just had the most distressing experience with the owner of this store. I purchased a pair of $180 Adidas UltraBOOSTs in April of 2019 for an extended trip abroad. I came to the store to have my foot fitted for the correct size shoe as I would be doing a significant amount of walking. The salesperson did not have this shoe in my size (9.5 or 10) and kept insisting I needed a size 10.5 which he did have in stock. I knew when I paid for the shoes that they were too large for my foot (toe long and the heel slipped) but I felt the salesperson was annoyed by my questions and he knew best as he was the professional....and I just needed a pair of shoes as I was leaving for the trip the following day. Got home, decided they were just too big and put the shoes on the shelf in my closet and forgot about them. Quarantine time allowed me to clean my closet and locate the sales receipt. I called and was told by Allie (super nice young lady who is very polite) that they would be happy to exchange them for a shoe that fit me properly. I did not want a refund, just to exchange the shoes for a half size smaller that fit! Came into the store, located Allie and she spoke to the owner.  I was told because of the length of time since purchase that they could do nothing. Ok...that's fine. On the way out I saw the owner and very politely let him know that, while I took responsibility that I was not prompt in taking care of the return, I felt it was the responsibility of his employees to fit me with the correct size shoe. He grabbed the box from my hand and his exact words were "I don't give a s*it, I'll give you your money back". Excuse me? I told him I did not expect money back, only asking to exchange for a pair of shoes that fit properly. I asked for my shoes back and left as his behavior was embarrassing me and the employees and other customers were staring. I've purchased many shoes here and have recommended this business to others in the past. This was my final visit. Apparently, the current climate is making people completely lose all sense of manners, politeness and common human decency. Why would  you speak to anyone in that manner when you depend on customers to purchase your product?

Input: On 1/17/19 I made an oil change appoint for 9am 1/19/19. 

When I took the car in on the 19th I was told it would take about 1hr. I asked if I could use the complimentary shuttle to get a ride home and was told it was in Arlington. Previously when I'd used the shuttle i was told repeatedly that its only offered in a 5 mile radius. I was confused why they would send the shuttle to Arlington which was significantly further than that. The person at the desk very rudely responded with "We decided to help out an 80yr old woman is that ok?"

Since this employee decided to violate the company policy I was denied the shuttle that they said would be available. Instead I called my father to come pick me up and told him that I'll be back in 1hr to get the car. I called 2hrs later to ask about they car, and he said they still hadnt taken it in. 4hrs later I called because I needed to go somewhere that evening and again he said they still hadnt taken the car inside and that the shuttle was still not available. At this point they've had the car for 5hrs and havent even started. I did not expect it to take this long given that I went through the Sullivan tire website and made an appointment. I not longer had time to wait for me car

So again I had to call my dad to give me a ride to the shop. When I asked for the keys back I was told that they didnt take my car inside because there were people waiting in the shop for their cars. I didnt know that superseded the appointment i made to the tune of 5hrs. Ultimately they never did change the oil in my car and I had to go elsewhere. 

If this is in fact the Sullivan tire policy I cannot reasonably take my car back there. It just doesnt make any sense when Jiffy lube will change my oil in 15 minutes and they are 2 miles down the street.

I wasnt even going to post this review, but they just did the same thing to my wife today with our other car. When she reached at 9:15am this morning she asked how long it would take. At first they said 11:30, to which she said "well then I cant do it now because i have to pickup my daughter from school at 11:30". Then they said they could get it done in 1hr. When she called back at 10:40, they said they just took the car inside and said it would take another 1hr.

If the estimates for completion are off by such a large amount, then they are useless. We plan around car maintenance since it means we will be without a car and thats very limiting in Bedford. Its really hard to plan if the shop gives such bad information.

Input: I interviewed several moving companies and finally chose Gentle Giants because, even though they were the most expensive, they sounded like they would take the most care and would send the best of their crew.

 The movers were nice, courteous and the move went quite well. Because I was going to a temporary residence, I had to put everything in storage with Gentle Giants. 

When I was able to have my belongings delivered to me, I unpacked everything and discovered a lot of things were missing. When I contacted them they sent a manager out to my house. Because I had kept all of the inventory papers, he spent hours going over them and determined that there were 6 boxes missing. He reassured me that they must have missed a container and would find it and promptly deliver them.

When I heard nothing back from them I called and spoke to the head manager of the company. He was rude and told me that they couldn't find my belongings. I was very upset, as there were many extremely valuable family heirlooms, irreplaceable paintings and many many other things of value which were very important to me. 

When I told him that I wanted them to search the warehouse until they found my things he got rude and accusatory. He implied that the boxes of my precious belongings never existed!!! I was livid at this point. He said her would continue looking and would get back to me. 

I didn't hear back from them. I allowed what should have been sufficient time for them to find my belongings and called them again. I was told that they could not find any of the 6 boxes!

I had to contact the Consumer Affairs Dept. and when I did the movers said that I should write out an inventory of the things that were missing. I listed everything I could think of and was very honest in my assessment of each items worth. I was reimbursed for those things.

For months afterwards, and to this day I frequently remember something else of value that I had forgotten to list. I knew that they would do nothing after they had already settled with me. I was out thousands of dollars more as I remembered more and more things that were missing. 

It was one of the most difficult experiences of my life. I am still heart sick over the huge losses I incurred. This was inexcusable and to make matters worse I was treated terribly when trying to claim what I was owed. A terrrible experience that I have not gotten over all these years later.

Input: My last visit here was an epic nightmare.

I came out on a Friday for a late lunch with 3 other co-workers around 1:30 pm. We intentionally went a little later to miss the lunch rush so we could get back to work in a decent amount of time. 

The hostess was pleasant and sat us promptly.

After that it was like being in the Twilight Zone. One of my co-workers ordered one of their featured wine spritzer drinks from the bar, the rest of us got fountain drinks. We sat there for at least 20 minutes between the time our drink orders were taken and we actually received the drinks. 
At this point I start getting nervous, because we'd already used 30 minutes including driving time of our 1 hour lunch, and we hadn't even ordered the food yet.

Another ten minutes went by, and I had to get up to ask a women,who I think was the assistant manager, if we could please put our orders in, because we were now on a time limit.

About a minute later our waitress finally came to take our order.
It was pretty simple, we all got wings, each a different style or sauce, and a side salad or fries, not rocket science. We also placed one additional order to go for another co-worker who was manning the fort in our absence.

In all seriousness, another 15-20 minutes went by with no food and no sign of our waitress. We flagged over another waitress to get an update. After checking with the kitchen window it turns out our waitress had never put in our order! My co-worker and I were quietly trying to calm each other down to prevent the other one from Hulking out at the table.

Finally the general manager came over to our table after we had literally been there for over an hour. He was clearly beside himself about the situation, apologizing profusely and telling us that our entire meal with the exception of alcohol would be comped.

Meanwhile we still had not received our food, and were praying that we all still had jobs (we called in late, of course).

When the food came, all I can say is it was not the saving grace I was hoping for. MY WINGS STILL HAD FEATHER HAIRS ON THEM. My co-workers were equally unimpressed with the food.  I ate 3 of my 10 wings and did not bother to get the rest to go, no way was I going to eat anymore now or later.

All in all we walked out of there with about $75 worth of comped food, and of course tipped nothing (this is probably the only time in my life I have ever not tipped). We never did see our waitress again after she  took our food order, and the bill was registered under her name. 

From the time we left work which is about 10 minutes away to the time we got back it had been about 2 and a half, almost 3 hours. Our bosses were flabbergasted, but luckily we live to work another day. I have definitely crossed this location off of my go-to lunch spots. NO WAY. 

I will say the manager did handle it as best he could once it was brought to his attention, but after the food was horrible to boot, so not worth it.

Unfortunately that is where the positives end. Upon delivery of my fridge, I instructed the drivers to go through my back door, since kitchen is adjacent. They decided to not follow my advice, so I quickly placed carpet runners down to protect the floors to the kitchen. They removed the carpet runners and consequently my home was damaged. The hand truck gouged the wood floor in my foyer, and also cut a v shape of about 4 inches long in my linoleum in the kitchen. Again, I wish I could give them stars for making the best out of a bad situation by quickly remedying it. As of today, Sept 14th, I still have these damages, and what has happened between then and today has been a whole lot of headache. 

I reported the damage and sent photos in that day, June 9th. By the end of the month I was instructed to pick out a new kitchen pattern since the only way to repair it is to replace the floor. I was given the contact information of the person they hired to install the new kitchen flooring (which hadn't been ordered at that time. 

This person they hired opened up a whole new type of headache: at the very best he was a flake. He made arrangements to come install the flooring on three separate occassions, and he no showed each time. At the worst, he was nightmarishly unprofessional. He sent long, hypercasual text messages asking me when he was going to get paid, (I wasn't paying him) sometimes at 9pm on Sunday. When I did hear from him, hours or days after the appointment he failed to show for,  instead of saying "sorry I need to reschedule I was injured" he actually sent me graphic pictures of his injuries. After several weeks of this and his third time not showing up to an appointment, I finally asked Appliance Ranchers to hire someone else and to give me a set date when the repairs would be made. I have decided to break my silence since I believe over 90 days is too long to wait for such a simple repair. They are now in the process of finding someone else, and while the owner has been in communication with me, I know that he could have gotten this done months ago if he actually wanted to.

Input: When I took my Chevy HHR 2006 to this shop, it had one minor issue that didn't interfere with the car's driveability, but despite giving them, in total, nearly $3,000 for "preventative maintenance" and then a for number of new issues that came up almost immediately after they gave me back my car each time, I ended up having to get my car towed to a different shop within three weeks of getting it back from them, and paying that shop another $800.

The first time I took my car to this shop I think I told them the car shakes at high speeds and just doesn't run as smoothly as I'd like. Other than that, the car worked just fine, and there was no check engine light on. They told me to leave the car with them so they could make a determination as to what, if anything, was wrong with the car. I get a call around noon, from a mechanic who seemed very alarmed, telling me I needed $1800 in repairs. I was astonished, because as I said before, the car ran fine and I had no noticeable indication that it was about to break down at any second. The mechanic convinced me that all the things he suggested were really important and if I wanted to prevent breaking down in the middle of nowhere soon one day I should take care of the issues now. Maybe I was gullible, but I believed him and bitterly gave him almost $2000 to "fix" my car. Once I got my car back, I was expecting it to run like brand new and thought I wouldn't have to think about it again for a long while. That is not what happened.

Within a couple of days I noticed the car was shaking like before, and I called to let them know. They told me to bring it back to check on it, but I'm busy, and I was already bitter about the $2000 I spent before, so just decided to live with it. But then, something new happened. About three weeks after getting the car back the check engine light came on. I was pissed, because I JUST gave these people $2,000 to "fix" my working car that had never had a check engine light before, and now the check engine light was on. I continued to put off taking it back to them for awhile, until I had got a flat tire (with no spare). They put on new tires for me the last time, so i figured I'd take it back to them to fix the tire and figure out what was going with the check engine light.

I left the car with them, to get a call explaining I had a whole NEW SET of problems that was causing the check engine light to turn on. I'm confused because I gave them my car no more than a couple months before and when they did their check of everything that "needed" to be repaired, none of these new problems were brought up. I say this to the mechanic, and he accuses me of being aggressive and confrontational (maybe I was, but I was pissed). They again tell me these new problems need to be fixed right away, or my car would be at risk for breaking own. This time it costs like $200 to repair. I pay the money. They called me to get my car and warned me that the car wouldn't sound right for a bit because of the issue had been occurring for so long, i.e., the month and half since I got the car back originally. I don't know anything about cars, so I take their word for it.  I start the car to leave the lot and it sounded at bit funny, but since they warned me, I just left and assumed it would clear up as they said.

I kid you not, the NEXT DAY, I went to start my car, it would not start - not even a flicker. I call them and explain what was going on and they tell me I must have had an old battery. I'm livid. I said there was nothing wrong with my battery when I took it to them yesterday. They tell me batteries can go bad at any time. Later that day, I ask one of my neighbors to give me a jump, and he explains that it couldn't be the battery b/c the radio still worked and the headlights came on (of course!). The following morning I call them back an tell them it's not the battery.  They have someone tow it to them, at their expense. I get a call back later that morning telling me the starter had gone bad. They won't charge me for the labor but the part cost like $500, which I would have to pay for. I was like hell no! 

At this point, I'm angry as hell, and my husband who is in Tallahassee has to call to intervene. He says its not worth the fight and decides to pay for the starter (I disagreed vehemently). They replace the starter, my husband pays them, and I take the car back from them. 

Within three days, the check engine light was on again. I'm totally frustrated, and just ignore it, until three weeks later the car doesn't start again. This time it makes the noise as if it wants to start, but doesn't. At this point, I want to tow the car back to Orlando Import Auto Specialists, just so I can burn the car and the place down at the same time. 

Of course I didn't do that, nor did I call them again, b/c I'm not that much of an idiot. I found another shop who told me the computer had went bad, and charged me $800 to fix it.

The server was rude and pretentious and unattentive from the outset to the conclusion. This was my first and last meal at Bricco. Expansively expensive for what was placed before us. Input: I honestly was hoping I didn't have to do this,...but I think you need to be warned!  I really do hate that I have to write this review because my initial impression when I walked into SK Northwest was really positive.  

Well in February I purchased a Can-Am Spyder from a private party with 3100 miles.  It was time for the 3000 mile oil change and inspection, so I researched the local dealers that could perform service.  Needless to say, all the dealers in the Portland/Vancouver area had really bad ratings so I just picked SK Northwest.  I really hoped my experience was going to be great because the folks there were nice and the facility was clean and organized.  However, when I received my Spyder back from service, a couple things were extremely wrong. When I got home I noticed that one of the body panels were cracked.  I called SK and naturally the service manager told me they didn't do it and I had the option to bring it back in so they could tell me to my face they didn't do it.  Ok, I have zero proof that they did it but it's a stress fracture and,...they did it (I'm a material science engineer,...28 years, beside the point) looks like I'll have to eat the $249 repair!  Secondly, the the left fog lamp didn't turn on.  Just tonight, after spending a couple hours researching this on YouTube, I took a panel off that exposed the wires to the headlamps on the left side of the Spyder.  Low and behold, they didn't reconnect wires when they took the panel off to change the oil and filter (if they even did that!).  

I'm a stickler about quality and safety and I take pride in my work to ensure quality and safety is a design fundamental.  If SK NW is going to be in the business of repairing state of the art motor vehicles, it's imperative that quality workmanship and safety consciousness be at the forefront of their service business model!  Based on my experience with SK NW, it makes me wonder what else they forgot to do.  I would hate to experience an SK NW catastrophic failure on my 3 wheeled vehicle at 60mph not to mention the countless 2 wheeled vehicles they've serviced in just the last 30 days.

This is for potential customers of SK Northwest.  I paid $325 for them to essentially cost me an additional $249 damage to my Spyder.  Hopefully I can reconnect the fog lamp wires but one would think that would have been included in the $325 oil and filter change? 

One more quick note.  My wife actually asked the Service Manager, "why are your Yelp ratings so low?".  He said, "There was a person at their shop that no longer works there.  And a couple customers were dissatisfied and tried to put the blame back on us".  SK, I think you terminated the wrong person or not enough people!  Well, at this point I'm not going to argue with the service manager about the damage to my Spyder nor my POOR CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE.  I'm going to have my Spyder re-serviced by a reputable dealer to ensure it's safe.  Additionally I'm going to help you SK NW by writing Can-Am Corporate to request they audit your ability to service their products!  

Check out the pics!

Input: So last Sunday night we wanted to have some cherrystones and a few drinks.  Legals is in waking distance to where we live and has an outdoor bar, so it was our #1 choice in the neighborhood.  Usually the inside service for shellfish at this Legals location is good, and before heading down to the outdoor bar we confirmed with the indoor staff that raw bar was available outdoors.  They confirmed it was.  Great we thought.  Rawbar outside on a beautiful summer night.  Heaven!  So we head down to the outdoor bar, which bar is indeed a rare offering in Harvard Square.   We sat right down at the bar and ordered 18 cherrystones and 2 draft beers.  The service was initially attentive and our order was taken right away.  Off to a great start.... so we thought.   Our beers were served promptly and every thing was A OK. 20 minutes passed, we finished our beers with no sign or mention of the raw bar order.  Our waiter Ryan had disappeared, so we asked someone who looked like a manager to check on the status of our cherrystones.  All he could say was "I'll get your waiter."  Lazy and poor response we thought.   Ryan resurfaced, apologized and said "I'll call upstairs" which he did right away.  He came back to say they were backed up in the kitchen but they should not be much longer.  25 minutes after we had placed our order, the rawbar planner was delivered by a lady from upstairs.  She said "sorry for the long wait, these are on us."   A nice gesture, and the least they could do we thought, but what was on the platter were 18 littlenecks and not even the cherrystones we actually ordered.  If you know anything about shellfish, there is a world of difference!   Roger B. blows it again.  Not our first underwhelming and disappointing experience at Legals.  Not sure why we keep going back.  Something about the definition of insanity, doing the same thing over and over and expecting a different result...

Input: Yesterday I used a groupon that I had a very poor experience with and is now leading me to see a dentist to try and correct what happened. I'm just going to tell you the situation in full so hopefully this won't happen to anyone else. 

First off, the establishment listed, "Million Dollar Smile," is located inside of another place. The number listed rings and then leads to you an automated system... which then proceeds to hang up on you. I called it multiple times. After wandering around for ten minutes I entered the salon by chance to ask them if they knew where Million Dollar Smile was. The woman, doing someone's hair, told me to sit and wait because the person that was supposed to do my appointment went on break. I told her that I tried to call but the number listed and no one answered. She laughed and told me no one answered that phone. Okay... So she gave me the person's card that was supposed to be handling my appointment and told me to call her to let her know I was there. I called her and she let me know she would be there in five minutes. So I sat and waited. When she walked in she let me know that it would take her a couple minutes to get set up and I should wait where I am. When she came back out, she led me to her "office". The office was a small, dirty room. This is when I should have walked out. But she hurried me in to lay down on this chair. She then asked me if I had ever used whitening strips before and I told her I had been to the dentist where they whitened my teeth. She seemed confused by my answer and asked if I had ever used the whitening strips and I told her yes. She didn't probe any further. She squirted some gel into a mouth tray and told me that this wasn't going to be comfortable but to wait for a couple of minutes and it would go away. I trusted her and so I let her put the tray into my mouth. She let me know that she would let me sit for twenty minutes, then we would take a break, and do another twenty minutes of the treatment. It did sting pretty bad, but since she told me it would go away I didn't say anything. She set the timer on the light for ten minutes, put it over my mouth, and left. 

By the time the ten minutes was up, it was still stinging. She came in once to reset the timer for another ten minutes and left before I could say anything. 

The ten minutes is up again. This is when I was supposed to take a break- one that I really wanted because it was very uncomfortable. She came in, talking on the phone, reset the timer, and left again. 

Another eight minutes goes by. She comes into the room and by this time I'm trying to get her attention. I want this stuff out of my mouth, it's really starting to hurt. She takes the light off my my teeth and I take out the tray. She asks me if I want to rinse and gives me some water. I take it gratefully and as soon as that stuff is out of my mouth I feel a lot better. Then I take a look at my teeth in the mirror, and I'm floored. There are white spots all over them! My teeth were a little uneven before, but this is bad. It looks like it didn't whiten my teeth at all, except in those tiny white spots. 

At this point, I'm pretty upset and I tell her that if it's going to make those spots even worse, I don't want to do that last ten minute session. She lets me know that it wasn't her fault. If my teeth were uneven before, It was only going to make them worse. Which is confusing, because guess what? I've had my teeth whitened before, and i've never had them look like this. Either way, I wasn't letting her touch my mouth again. I let her know that I didn't want to do the last session and she asked me for my voucher from groupon. I gave it to her and she said thank you and have a nice day. I told her that the groupon came with a whitening pen as well so she went to get that. At this point I just wanted to get out of there so I took the pen and walked out. To top it off, this morning I brushed my teeth and half of my gums came off with my toothbrush. This is dangerous and now I'm in a lot of pain! I have no idea why I paid 78 dollars for this. 

As you can see, it's a long story. But long story short, this woman should not be able to do groupons anymore! She has no idea what she's doing and now I'm going to have to pay either a doctor or a dentist to look at my mouth to make sure I didn't do any serious damage. I do NOT want this to happen to anyone else!

Input: I pride myself in networking good services to people. If the service is performed well, I share that info with friends & they do get referrals & references from me & my repeat business. I hate writing 1 star reviews, but feel this needs to be told.

I met these guys at Barton Creek Farmers Market. The sales guy, Dale, was very nice. They are a contractor & I need my house painted & gutters installed. He came out & gave me an estimate. The bid was fine, but I was running pretty busy & did not have the time in the summer to get the work done. 

In November, he approached me with a sweetener. They were slow & they "pay the crew even if they are not busy." This was enticing to me & they could start right after Thanksgiving. Great I said. He quickly came to my house to get me to sign a contract & took a 50% deposit on the agreed price. That was the last nice exchange I recall.

Maybe they are having growing pains. Maybe they hire people who should not be working with the public or are not qualified to do the job at hand. Maybe they hire a painter to do brain surgery. Whatever the case, from the paint swatches to the power washing to the repairs, there have been delays, lack of or mis-communication; & more time spent fixing mistakes.

The Nightmare: 

Paint sampling. I picked the colors, but their foreman could not be bothered to get the samples from the paint manufacturer. I had selected Sherman Williams & Kelly Moore Colors to sample. He first brings Home Depot paint, but the samples do not match the swatch. He goes to Sherman Williams for the Kelly Moore color, & again, not the same, but different from last. Then he finally goes to Kelly Moore for their colors & the swatch is closer to the sample. Not a big deal in theory, but it wasted 3 days of cycles just to pick colors & I need those to get HOA approval. 

Weather Delays. That & wasted time delayed the start date to December 18. In 30+ degree weather, they began to power wash my house. Unfortunately, they blasted my newly cleaned windows. 

No Shows & Excuses. People were sick, or they were short handed, so the painter & his worker started on the repairs & purchasing of the materials to do them. One day, I swear there were 5 people outside. There was an issue with wood rot near the back door, & some guy started running the saw with the door open & no sheeting to keep sawdust out of my home. I just had the place cleaned for my Mom's visit. They used the cheapest possible materials to do the repairs & not even siding on the trim, but fence pickets!?!? 

Fed up. On December 21, I kicked them out & said not to come back until after New Years. This circus of bad repairs was stressing me out. I had company & wanted to enjoy the holidays. The repairs would need to be fixed by a carpenter.

More delays. Weather is problematic most of January for painting, but they did not do any repairs either. Someone would randomly arrive to paint & I would send them away & ask them to send a carpenter or someone skilled to fix the repairs. This went on several times. Then they would schedule someone to do the repairs, & they would not show up or call. I got everything from illness, to sick kid in the hospital to no excuse at all. I guess their dog ate their calendar & chewed off the finger that dials the phone too. 

Glimmer of Hope. The repairs were FINALLY done correctly on March 25. In spite of my request to clean up after (nails & debris), I keep finding them & am worried my dogs will end up hurting their paws on them.

Flake Factor. I was told painters would come the next day. No show, no call. The next day, no show, no call. This has been going on over 4 months & I set an expectation early in March that I wanted it done by the end of March (as that would be 4.5 months since we contracted this) or I wanted a full refund. 

Are you kidding me? It is March 27, no show, no call. After a few tries, texts over 2 days, Dale called me back & assured me I am the priority the next 3-day weather window (20% chance of rain tomorrow?!?). I could have done it faster myself with a toothbrush & cotton ball. 

Just get it over with. I may write an update after/if the job is complete. But suffice it to say, I would not recommend these guys.

Only good thing. I like their gutter guy (they sub the work to him) & will likely review him under his own business, so as not to have his reputation mixed in with theirs. 

Do your homework. I have since looked them up. While I can find no reviews that are legit, the BBB gives them an F rating as of now. I should have gone there first. My bad. 

Sigh. So if you come to my house, & I have red swatches all over my front door, I am not waiting for the angel of death to pass over, just for the Lone Star Painters, a division of Saving America Energy to get their act together & finish the job. 

Bad Joke. How many SAE workers does it take to do a 3 day job? When all is said & done, probably 18 people & 6 months :(

Still waiting for The End! ...of job

Input: First, the buying process was incredibly painful. I knew exactly what I wanted, and drove down from Boston to see it, and if it was sound, negotiate a fair price and buy it.  Instead, I was kept at a sales desk for nearly an hour before I pleaded to see the car. Then the salesman, Cy proceeded to use every used-car tactic in the book to "sell" it to me - even though I had already decided on what I'd offer.  Then came the week-and-a-half of jerking me around pretending to negotiate, but never really budging (e.g. "yes, my sales manager has agreed to your price - if you finance through us, otherwise, the same old price.").  Oh well, it was painful, but I got the car I wanted, and the price, while a premium over some other dealers wasn't that bad - since this one had "brand new tires" and undergone "thorough maintenance."  And they agreed to buy me floor mats and fix a broken console piece.

Then the real problems began.  A week after buying it, the battery went so dead that the doors wouldn't unlock.  They never got me the floor mats or fixed the console (it's been two months and several phone calls).  As soon as I drove it over any bumps (there were none on the test drive - and no highway), I heard a persistent clunk. At inspection I learned that it was bad shocks - one was even leaking. And the front brakes were down to 15%.

Then I needed to replace a tire (probably because they were underinflated when it was sold to me, and the dash indicator was explained away "because it's cold out"). I learned that my "brand new" tires were three years old and too worn to replace just one or two (on an AWD car, the wear must be equal or it screws up the transmission).  So I spent $1200 replacing my "brand new" tires.  Oh, and the tire place showed me that the rear brakes were pretty bad.
And I've only driven a couple hundred miles.  

**Also watch out for: They only provide one key, no manual, and no floor mats.  They say to buy them on eBay (where I presume they're selling them).

Input: For months I've been walking past the empty store front at  2072 Mass. Ave. Today, to my surprise, the building that had once been an old KFC had been fully transformed into a Banjo's Roast Beef.

My boyfriend and I were so eager to try the place that we found ourselves ordering take out at Banjo's only an hour after we had just eaten dinner. Between the two of us, we decided to get a Jackson BBQ sandwich and a baked potato. The roast beef sandwich was decent - satisfying comfort food, but nothing more. 

Now, on to the baked potato. Banjo's forgot to give me the fixins for my potato so I ended up with a very sad Yukon Gold wrapped in foil all by its lonesome. What the hell. You would think that with nearly 10 employees in the store, one of them would have thought to put some sour cream or at least a slice of a chive in our take out bag!

I really had high hopes for Banjo's, especially since it's only two blocks from my apartment, but it just wasn't meant to be. With clever names for sandwiches like the "Harvard Extension," a sandwich lacking substance just like its academic reference, I expected a bit more than a crappy Arby's rip off. 

I vow never to return to Banjo's. They shouldn't be sad that they lost a customer, they should just be happy that I didn't throw my naked baked potato through their window.

We have so many issues here that I don't know where to begin.  First, the charge you for "amenities" and then don't provide them.  This place is supposed to be "luxury" living, but it's far from luxury service.  Let's start with security.  The key fobs went weeks, if not months, without working.  So while carrying arms of groceries I had to fumble to find the correct key and struggle to unlock the door.  Meanwhile, resident's got so tired of dealing with this fiasco, so folks were just letting anyone in the building.  Not secure; not impressive!  Second, they have "plenty" of maintenance staff that works here, and they are pretty pleasant and hardworking guys.  However, if you need something done on the weekend.  Not gonna happen.  Example.  After two months of getting a really low (pennies) water bill, they came by (during a weekday, of course, since maintenance doesn't work weekends) and told me they had to perform some sort of maintenance to the meter.  Weeks went by and they left a notice on our door to let us know that they were coming by the next day to perform the work.  Who gives that kind of notice?  Making matters worse, my husband took off the day so he could be here (because who wants a third-party stranger here with their staff alone in your house?).  Unfortunately, not only did they not show up to work, they didn't even call or somehow notify us that they weren't coming.  So late in the day the hub's went to the management office to inquire and was told they ran out of time and would be here the next day.  Fortunately, I had the day off (holiday), so I was the chosen one who got to wait all day for no one to show up.  Again, no notification or call to let us know they were too busy.  Three emails later, on Monday, the management office offered nothing but empty apologies.  This after keeping us waiting and wondering if this was the day the staff would show up.  THESE PEOPLE ARE RUDE.  Parking.  When we first moved here, we paid for an assigned parking spot.  However, someone else continued to park in the spot.  And when we brought this to the attention of the management office, they just brushed it off.  Who does that?  Safety.  the complex next to this one is managed by another national company.  They have a security service that patrols the area.  Not Jefferson at Dedham Station.  I've seen and have taken pictures of a high-end SUV with all the tires removed; made me wonder if it was VANDALIZED. 

And finally.  Much like one of the other posts, I can attest to the fact that they trump up charges after you move out and they deduct those charges from the security deposit.  This was so blatant that I had to file a complaint with the MA Attorney General's Office.

Input: We have been getting food from Bacci's for a couple years now.  It has been our go-to place for pizza and calzones.  The food was always excellent, they were always very accurate with their delivery estimates, and the person who usually answers the phone was always very polite. Today however was a very different story.  It was the usual person who answered the phone when I called. He was polite as usual, and said the delivery would be in about a half hour. After another 10 minutes went by, I called back to see if they could call and ask the driver where he was and when he thought he would be here. The same person answered, was polite, and called the driver. The driver said it would be another 10 minutes.  Seeing as this would put the delivery at an hour and 10 minutes, plus my concern that the food might be cold, the person who answers the phone said to call him when it was delivered and he would give me a credit the next time we ordered.  After the food got here, I did just that. Only when I called it was not the same usual person who answered the phone.  I explained to the person who answered that the guy who usually answers the phone told me to call and he would give me a credit on our next order. The person who answered said it was not his problem, that he was the owner, and would not give us a credit. I said how that wasn't right, and he gave me a huge attitude and raised his voice and told me never to call again when I let him know how dissatisfied I was. Needless to say I will never be ordering food again from Bacci's. The owner does not deserve any business whatsoever given his extremely poor  customer service and lack of respect for his customers.

Input: I want to write to AirTran to describe my experience flying on August 20th, 2013, Flight 32 from Atlanta, GA to LaGuardia, NY.  I was flying with my mother, father, two little girls, and wife.  When we boarded the plane my daughter Maisie's seat (23B) would not sit straight up (it only reclined).  Her tray was angled downward.  My daughter Marlowe's tray literally came off.  Neither of these things bother me but I am setting the stage.  During the flight I had to be careful not to allow Maisie (age 5 y/o) to put her beverage down on her tray as it would slide off.  When Marlowe (age 3 y/o) spilled her drink and I went to help her, Maisie put her drink down and spilled as well.  I had a double spill in aisle 23 and still neither of these things really bothered me.  You see, I work for a public hospital in NYC, I take care of the poorest people in the city and I love my job.  I see the worst things in the world and so a double spill doesn't really get to me.  It is annoying but it is also somewhat laughable.  Next, a stewardess walked over and asked if the seats were wet.  I said, "No, I've dried them off."  She then asked again, "Did they soak through the seats?" and I said, perhaps with a slight edge but nothing more, "No, I dried them both off."  Now, she did not ask if I needed help, if there was a problem, nothing like this.  She then said, "Well, I will need to change the seats if they have been soaked through, you don't have to yell at me."  

Let's be totally clear here, I did not yell.  It takes a lot to get me to yell.  I have people threaten me at my job, my physical safety, and I don't yell.  What I find so terrible about the service that was given to me and my family is that there was no interest in whether we were uncomfortable.  There was no interest in me as a consumer.  She was reprimanding me in front of my children and my family even though I had not raised my voice at all.  I wanted to respond that I did not yell but I did not want to escalate the conversation which she had already done.  I stopped and went back to my kids who were of course quite uncomfortable.  Later in the flight my wife asked another attendant for the other woman's name and she said that my wife would have to ask the woman directly.  Is that the correct response?  I think their jobs are very difficult, so is mine.  All of this occurred in some way because to begin with our seats were malfunctioning.  The plane was shoddy and the service was very poor.

Input: Ummm, so 36 hours after barely eating here, we're still sick ....... we got here for a late birthday lunch.....so excited, sat outside, great weather,  good server. ....but the food  . Ordered mussels...., almost threw up after the first taste. The mussels had gone bad, and once we returned it, they had to take it off the menu for the rest of the day and sited "mussels are in mating season" as the reason for me feeling sick.

Another manager tried to give me some flounder, but after 2 dishes that made me sick, why would i even eat anything else? We decided to stick to finishing up our self-made mimosas.

So in the end,  what was done?  Nothing really.  I still ended up paying full price for all my drinks,  and got a measly 20% of the 3 items that we were able to eat, and some free desserts I was offered after we left but I had to come get my parking validated.... basically an "after the fact fix"..... would I come back,  HELL NO..... 

But Legal Seafood Corporate, yall need to fix this shit.... like now!!!! Worst experience than buying sushi from a highway gas station!!!!!

Review update:
Less than 2 hours after leaving Legal,  2 of the 4 of us ended up sick.  We spent the rest of our night back and forth between the couch and the toilet....... and the only thing we ate was some fried oysters, sreamed clams and the clam chowder....

Input: So, I gave this place a pretty good review a few months ago.  I'm disappointed to retract it now.  A couple of days ago (August 8, 2012 if I recall correctly), I was here with my family for the nth time.  We frequent(ed) this place and pretty much walk in and out of here without remark... until now.

As usual, I order a half-portion of their Texas Cheese Fries for an appetizer.  Something unusual came with it this time, though.  As I was chewing a mouthful of gooey, cheesy fries topped with a jalapeno and some bacon bits, I noticed something was hesitant be shredded to bits by my teeth.  And believe me, I was trying.  For a moment, I considered giving up and just swallowing.  I didn't think much of it.  Until I kept chewing...

I put my fingers in my mouth and reach for this un-chewable, hard thing.  To my extreme disgust, I pulled out a GIANT fingernail.  This thing could have been a toenail.  Anyway, how do I know it wasn't mine?  Because I don't grow my fingernails out half an inch.  It was also coated in cheese.  I had to wipe off the cheese to make sure it was what I thought it was.  I took a picture of this fingernail, right next to the mouthful of Texas Cheese Fries I spit out with it.  I wish I could share it here to validate my story.

By the time the waiter came back with our food, I politely told him to take the food back and let us pay for the drinks we ordered so that we can leave.  He fetched the manager; an Asian lady I've seen many times before (although she does not know/recognize me).  Even she was shocked.  She was profusely polite (and not just then - she always has been quite courteous).  She asked if there was anything she could do.  Nope.  I just wanted to walk out of there.  She declined my offer to pay for drinks (not even the margarita was a good-enough chaser) and gave us her sincere apology.

Now, I've been here countless times before without incident.  I really liked this place.  However, after this, in good conscience I cannot recommend that anyone eat here until whatever sanitation issue in the kitchen is resolved.  A fingernail, folks.  Not a little clipping either.  And I THOUGHT TO SWALLOW IT.  I was under the assumption that those in food service had to keep their nails clipped...  I just gagged again.

- Heavy Clean Microwave - $3.75 (3 other roommates charged same amount)
- Heavy Clean Stove Top - $11.25 (3 other roommates charged same amount)
- Re-caulk Tub - $7.50 (1 other roommates charged same amount)
- Replace Bedroom Carpet - $81.69

Axis also didn't find time to send me this final bill until August 25 and stated that all payments had to be mailed in my September 1, otherwise you would have to deal with their asset management division or the collections department.

Input: I have never had a worse experience with a business of any kind. When I saw them listed for ATL Burger Week, I was excited to support them as a local small business (and as a business owner myself). I called ahead to see if I could get the burger to-go (for timing issues), but I understood when I was told this was not possible. To-go has never been allowed in the past for ATL Burger Week, but thought it might be different during a pandemic. I went to dine in and there were two other patrons in the restaurant, one with a mask hanging off his ear, one with no visible mask. The bartender/server also was not wearing a mask at any time I was in the restaurant. 

When I went to the restroom to wash my hands, I also noticed that the tables were not marked for social distancing. Not a big issue when the restaurant is empty, but there was nothing to keep another group from sitting at the table next to me. 

Again, it wasn't crowded, so this wasn't a major issue. What happened next blows me away. I knew that me and the owner (who I have met before) have a mutual friend, so I asked her for his number so I could give him a heads up about the Governor's Executive Orders regarding restaurants and they could be fixed before someone else noticed and reported them. I texted him with the information to help him owner-to-owner instead of reporting this to the Governor's office or writing a review. He proceeded to call me and yelled at me for 7 minutes about using his personal cell phone number. There are businesses on the brink of bankruptcy and some that have gone under because they are following the laws and trying to keep their patrons safe. Instead, he would rather focus on HOW I contacted him instead of WHY I contacted him. Timmy, I'm sorry I used your personal phone number, but I will not apologize for caring about my community. It is not too much to ask that your staff wear a mask while working handling food (gloves should be a given, regardless of a global pandemic). According to the owner, he was trying to do his best for his employees that have to feed their families. We all get that. Masks are not going to break the bank. Working together as a community helps us get past this, not yelling at the people who spend money and reach out to you personally to help.

Input: I purchased a '18 Tundra from this location about 2 weeks ago. I've waited a week to post this review to see if Carr would do anything to remedy the fact that they lied about the truck I bought online, and was supposed to get a call back last Friday. All their online marketing for the truck stated it was Platinum trim. We agreed upon a price and I purchased it, easy enough as I had been looking for 2 months and knew exactly what I wanted. On my drive home I realized it was not what they said it was. It was the Limited trim. There is a $7K MSRP difference between the trims new, I understand this is not a new truck, but I bring this up because the difference was downplayed multiple times while trying to get Carr to fix their deceptiveness. 

So they lied about the level of the vehicle, and when I brought this up, the only option Cody gave me was to unwind the deal. Since there was no dialogue, no real solution, and no option given, I threw out oil changes as something to at least start up the communication to find a happy medium. On the phone I was told they couldn't refund any money since the deal was done, Cody then informs me they can give me 4 free oil changes, of course I would have to drive from Beaverton to Vancouver to get them. OR they could cut me a juicy check for $200. What a deal!! I told Cody I wanted to sleep on it. 

I text him the following day telling him I would keep the truck and we'd go our separate ways, me obviously being unhappy and I'll let everyone I can know that this dealership lacks integrity and I'd never do business with a Carr dealership again, they bait and switched me. He wanted to talk. So we talked the next day, pointless conversation of course. I knew they wouldn't do what needed to be done to make me happy, which was $2,000 reimbursement. I would not pay over $40k for a platinum, and $38k for a Limited, these were my guidelines. I didn't even ask for it because I knew I was wasting my time and we were miles away from a win win solution. I accepted what happened and can't do anything about a business with trash customer service that lacks honesty and accountability. He continued making excuses about how the "accident" happened, darn VIN was at fault of course, apparently it was the 1 in 10,000 (or whatever number) vehicles that the computer screwed up and auto populated all the wrong info. Stupid computers am I right? Well I don't care who's fault it was, the company screwed up and bait and switched me, and then simply waits for me forget about it, not doing a damn thing. 

Deb and Cody were nice enough to deal with, I have a problem with the company and their policies when it comes to them screwing up and lying to customers.

I could have unwound the deal, I should have looked at things in more detail, but I trusted the company to not mis represent their products and it wasn't even in my head to think they were lying. At the end of the day, instead of me feeling like I got a good deal, I feel like I walked in a paid sticker price at a dealership like an idiot would. Yes, they had the truck booked out as a Limited (per Cody), but wtf do I care about that. Also, the truck had been sitting for over a month and they took my offer immediately, wonder why?! Then Cody tries to tell me the dumbest and most common load of crap a salesman says, THEY BOUGHT THE TRUCK FOR $39,900, yet were selling it to me for $40K. Sure, I've heard that identical story from 4 different used car salesman the past 2 months. Weird how these poor car companies are always the ones getting the raw deal. Poor things. 

I will never do business with Carr again, and will forever tell anyone I know about this experience to make sure to stop as many people as I can from doing business with them. I've been in my own business for close to 20yrs myself and have made many mistakes, my employees have made many mistakes, but you know what? I always rectify them and make them right, not sit there and point fingers and have an attitude of "oh well, crap happens move along".  I'll be waiting to hear how I'm the bad guy from Carr.

Input: I've been here a few times   I actually love the location, view, and vibe of this place, however, the wait staff is either not well trained or not well managed. In my most recent visit from Houston to reward the employees associated with my medical company, I asked the Austin staff to meet me at the Oasis. All was well, we had a great time on the patio, except our waitress, Theresa, seemed unhappy to serve us. She was a bit older than my mid thirties team, maybe early to mid forties. Since this was a company reward, I decided to treat the team to whatever they wanted, and just hang out since we are so far apart most of the time with our headquarters being located in Houston, where I currently reside. 
Theresa seemed to be much more engaged with her other tables than she was with ours, our drinks were left empty for long periods of time and our table left with dirty dishes while we had our post lunch meeting. 
When I received the check from her I noticed a gratuity was added. On the actual receipt it mentioned gratuities for parties of 7 or more...  our party was a party of 5 for all of the time we were there, with 1 additional employee showing up after we ate, and only ordering 1 glass of water. 
While I do understand that we did sit there for a few hours enjoying each other and the scenery, we were buying drinks, and continuing to be kind throughout the entire visit. 
When I received the bill, I intended on tipping her for the time we were occupying her table, but as I read the receipt I saw that she had placed the gratuity on our table of 5 eaters and 1 water only drinker. Keep in mind that I also own a restaurant in Houston in addition to the Medical company whose team I was meeting with in Austin. I feel as if Theresa saw my table of mid thirties masters and bachelor degree professionals, who all make 6 figures a year, as one that would not accommodate her time. I went ahead and left her only her requested gratuity, even though normally I would have tipped way more for this type of event. 
Employees like Theresa, give this place a lower review that it should receive. 
My suggestion would be to not assume anything. And to let Theresa go..

Input: Do not use this company under any circumstances.

What you need to know is that Seaport doesn't actually move your stuff.  They outsource to people who will pick up your things, then a driver who drives your it, and hire people at an abysmal hourly rate at the far end who unload.

None of these people have ANY INCENTIVE to be careful with your property.  The ones who picked up our things did not bother to label ANY of the boxes. They did not even keep hardware with the furniture they disassembled.  They just threw everything into boxes as fast as they could, probably because they were paid a flat rate.

Furniture was damaged.  Our bikes were compressed at the bottom of the pile and will never be the same again. I know where our TV is, but have no idea where to find the cords, the remote, the VCR.  There was no rhyme or reason, no order, to how they moved us.  They don't care if you can actually use your things again.

At the other end of our move (from Portland to Tucson), the people who were hired to unload the truck were stiffed by the driver, which understandably made them very angry.  The result is that our furniture was never reassembled.  Does Seaport care? Here's how you know the answer:  they demand a cashiers check at the end, so you can't challenge the charge if you're not happy with the service.

Don't let your property and your life be treated shabbily by this company.

Input: I wish that I could give them a 0 rating. 

EXTREMELY pushy and desperate sales associates. I was just in there not too long ago looking for rooibos teas with rosehips. I was shown a few but then I was offered "higher quality" teas(how she put it). These higher quality teas were white teas, which according to the person I was buying it for, are horrible tasting. 

The salesperson shows me the white teas after I say I'm interested in the red teas only. Then after saying that I'd take a half pound of red tea, she continues to push the white teas on me after telling her I haven't liked it in the past. In the end she was so adamant about me purchasing white teas that I agreed to sample them.

I asked for a cup to go. What did she say? "The line is so long though, you should just get it you and your friends will totally love it." I agree to get 2 ounces of a white tea to sample at home. She begins to push for me to purchase an entire pound of it. I respond with "Why would I get an entire pound when I don't know if I like it yet?" 

I begin to get impatient. At this point I just want the sample of the tea she wanted to push on me. BUT SHE ISN'T DONE YET. I need to get an additional sample, a sample of another type of white tea. So I ask for another 2 ounce sample. She AGAIN tries to convince me to get an entire pound. 

I just stand there and look at her in complete silence, clearly frustrated. So she finally decides to ring me up. 30 BUCKS!!! 30 Dollars for a couple of 2 ounce sample baggies. I take her word for it though, I assume that my friends and I will love this tea. 

After the transaction she then lets me in on a little known secret regarding white tea. They're very easy to screw up and make bitter. She tells me to put an ice cube in with the tea before adding hot water. She tells me that I need to steep it at  vey specific temperature. I love tea, but I'll be damned if I sit there with a thermometer monitoring the tea as I steep it. 

I go home and make using her ice cube trick though. It taste HORRIBLE. I bring it back. They are not happy with me. Tough titty I say. They had to throw the tea that I returned away. Again their own fault. 

Word of advice? If you have a good product, let it sell itself ok?

The noodles in the mac&cheese weren't cooked enough and were drenched in a watered down liquid cheese sauce. I did enjoy the grilled zucchini, this was shocking because by this point I was expecting a wilted, frozen vegetable. Their BBQ sauce is some generic/basic/overly sweet type ketchup nonsense.
