I informed them that my friend still wanted to pay for the hotel as a gift and I was told it would not be a problem as long as she filled out form and returned it in a timely matter. Which of course we did. We made sure to do everything that was asked in order to avoid any issues when we arrived. My friend even called the day off the reservation to make sure everything was in order before we arrived. She was told the name had been changed to mine, vanessa Munoz, as well as it would be charged to her card (she noted card was on file). When we arrived we were quickly told that I was to provide a cc for payment. I explained to him the situation and the gentleman at front desk told me there was no card on file and I was to pay. I then explained again the situation and informed him of form we had previously filled out. He did not seem in any way reluctant to help me with this confusion. He quickly grabbed his manager, which of course I was told the same thing, there was no form to be found. I felt as though they were being very defensive as though they didn't believe me. I was quite embarrassed to have this discussion in front of other customers. As I mentioned before, my friend was the one who originally booked the hotel, but due to a family illness was not able To make it. Well because the front desk as well as the manager made me doubt myself I then called my friend to confirm that she actually made the changes and calls. She was enraged to get a call not only when she was in the hospital but to have to confirm what she had called earlier to avoid this from happening. She made it a point to call ahead of time to avoid this from happening. She brought up a valid point, if there was no form then how did the reservation name get switched but no card on file??? She emailed me the forma she filled out, and I then showed it to end manger and like magic he found it. 
situation solved!! They did not seem to happy to have found out that there was in fact a paper. But they proceeded to give my hotel key and we went about our way, a 30 min mishap that should have been avoided. We told them we needed valet for parking, we were told it would be charged to the card. I asked if we could get it complementy for the troubles, of course that was a no. later that night we received a complained of being too loud so we quickly decided to call it a night not until no more than 2 min later got a knock and was told we needed to hush or we would be evicted from our room. We were not even giving 2 sec to get ourselves together. 
The hotel itself was pleasant rooms clean and stocked. Nothing to complain on that.
My issue was lack of customer service. I have stayed in the same hotel every time I visit Austin and decided to explore other hotels. Def the wrong choice in choosing this one. I felt embarrassed, belittled, and overall disappointed. The situation should have been handled in a better manner. Maybe it was a bad night for the staff and manger (Jonathan and lucus) maybe there were overwhelmed that night, I don't know. But what I do know is no matter what the circumstance is customer service should be superb 24/7. A customer might not always remember the little things, neatly folded towel, stocked toilet paper, chocolate on the pillow, but they will always remember how they were treated, and that is what makes a customer a returning one. I did not have the fortune to feel that way during my stay, but hey you can't satisfy everyone right. Oh I forgot to note 2 other parties had also booked there because of my recommendation to stay here. Them and myself will definitely not be likely to stay here again when we come back to visit. I will not be wasting my money where it is not appreciated.

They think a verbal conversation is how to conduct business in terms of rates and length of term. They agreed to rent me a storage area for 223 a month (Normally goes for 350)  (more than I needed, but they had someone for the smaller unit and I agreed based on the deal, it would be easier for me and willing to pay more). We never discussed the length of the term, but when I actually showed up, the manager who was nice to sell it and rude upon my arrival...... basically said "Yea, it's for one month". I questioned him and he walked away....Not only that, but they have some long term people who store merchandise in and out of there who are the rudest people I have ever met. They wouldn't give me space for my truck, dirty looks, rude to my movers....This went on for the whole 2 hours. Management never said a things and walked away. My term became longer than expected (3-4months) and when I called to pay for the next month, they jacked my rate up and were extremely rude and not willing to work with me. Quite frankly, if I thought this would happen I never would have agreed in the first place. All over a 100 bucks a month and when I did them a favor and they keep telling me they did me a favor??? I could have taken the smaller unit. I was living in back bay in 500 square feet apt. BTW I'm a contract lawyer and any larger company would never be able to do this. There would be legal ramifications.  Conversations V. legal contract don't hold up on court. I signed a actual contract that states all the terms and my rate. If it was only for a specific time, it should have been written into the agreement. Nevertheless, if they acted nicer and gave me a break for the month I owed, I would have been more sympathetic. They now have a renter for the space and want me out or pay for it.  I WOULD NOT RECOMMED USING THIS FACTILITY AS THERE ARE MANY OTHERS IN THE AREA THAT ARE CHEAPER. Take your money somewhere else, there are plenty of other ramen places who won't treat you like dog shit.

Input: We had a reservation and were on time. We waited 15 minutes before I had to get up and go to the hostess stand to ask for a server. The artichokes came timely. It was kind of a bit of a wait for the tableside shrimp cocktail. The oysters were still not there. Input: I almost hate to do this but it is what it is. I want to start by saying my previous review of this restaurant prior to their renovations was 4 stars and we were regularly returning customers. ALL of that has changed, and we will not be returning and will advise others to steer clear.

I'm not sure what happened, but the new management has all but ruined this place. Allow me to start from the beginning:

We returned to Rock Bottom because we were again in the area to see a comedy show, and it's our routine to go here prior to the show. I was glad to see it had reopened since it was down for renovations.

The night started off alright as we were seated outside which is nice. When I went to order Chili, the waiter informed me they had ran out. Okay, no big deal. I ordered the Bourbonzola Burger, the waiter asked how I would like it cooked, medium was my answer. My girlfriend ordered the Lobster-Shrimp-Pasta dish. 

Well, when we received our meals it was quite surprising to see that the $20 Lobster-Shrimp-Pasta dish was basically a bunch of pasta with a few shrimps and a sad tiny piece of a lobster... Now, we certainly didn't expect a ton but for the price this seemed a bit ridiculous. Not to mention my burger was well-done, not medium. So, we contacted out waiter and he seemed willing to help and understanding so he took the dish back, asked what she would like to do she asked if she could just have them add some lobster. 

Soon after the manage came over, and honestly this is where things got bad. Instead of offering a fair solution he decided to talk down to us about how all of their restaurants have the same measurements and that he can't add anything without charging us... Wait, so you can't even provide a meal worth the $20 and you want to charge us MORE to make it right... Yeah, some how I don't think so. He continued his poor customer service act, until I had enough. My girlfriend refused the food (even after he comped the meal) and didn't want anything else as substitute. At this point because of the way he was treating us, I decided to voice my opinion on my own meal. Honestly, I hadn't planned to say anything at all but his demeanor ruined the good mood of both us. I told him and even showed him my burger's cook was well-done not medium, and what is his response? That they actually cook their burgers as sliders and they are not cooked to order. Okay... then why was I asked how I would like that cooked?? He said he will have to re-train the waiter because I wasn't supposed to have been asked... Wow. The fair, simple and proper solution would've been to add a bit of lobster, send the same plate back and off go two loyal customers in a good mood, feeling that the restaurant made right out of the bad situation... instead this.

He did comp both of our meals, but only the burger was eaten anyway. So, in closing I would just advise people to stay away. Check out the other restaurants in the area first. This experience will be our last at Rock Bottom. Their management's customer service is non-existent.

Input: Okay. As much as I adore the NPs at this clinic, I cannot say the same for RediClinic's operations. It turns out the extra $50 price hike back in September was a result of the front desk ordering a lab test that was neither asked for, medically necessary, or communicated to me, the patient. Additionally, this extra lab test was only $25 -- so why on earth was I charged an extra $50?

Trying to get this money back has been an absolute ORDEAL. The clinic itself was unable to refund this to me directly, and I was told to contact corporate, who have not responded to repeated inquiries. By this point, I have been refunded the $25 for the lab test (without any communication whatsoever from corporate -- not even a short, "Hey, we're sorry we performed this 100% unnecessary lab test, here's your money back") but I never received the additional $25 extra charge. I have had to open a dispute with my credit card company, complete with invoices, to recover that $25 -- and if RediClinic resists, I am going to raise absolute hell. $25 doesn't seem like a lot, but it's the principle of the thing.

I myself work in a medical clinic and understand that I might be judging the front desk staff a little unfairly. However, BECAUSE I work in a medical clinic and have often had to settle billing disputes, I know this was handled in exactly the wrong way. Medical visits must always come with itemized invoices. Fees must be explained upfront. I should not have had to find out from an NP a month later, after I expressed confusion at being charged my usual amount for a follow-up visit, that the front desk had ordered a test on my lab specimen that literally could not have returned a positive. 

I initially started going to the RediClinic because I was uninsured and needed frequent last-minute appointments, but now that I once again have insurance, I will likely be transferring back to ARC, which has never given me any kind of billing hassle in the last few years.

If you visit any RediClinic, make sure you know up front EXACTLY what services you are receiving here. Do NOT let the front desk staff give you vague excuses about price hikes -- I doubt this is a result of maliciousness, but incompetence is equally as damning. Whichever staffer was running the front desk at Tech Ridge on September 15 at 4:30, thank you so much! You are singlehandedly responsible for this one-star review.

The onion rings were lukewarm , and the grilled vegetables were raw, with a char on them, also cold . I ate some onion rings .  I flagged the waitress down for our check, she never asked how our meal was, she offered another explanation about a party of twenty showing up in the dining room, and there being only two cooks in the kitchen. Still doesn't explain why other people were getting their food, and ours took so long. 
I grew up going to the Tides, when it was owned by the former owners, and NEVER had a bad meal or bad service. This was a $40 disappointment that I I will neither forget or repeat again. The beautiful view can only make up for so much.
I will never recommend the Tides to anyone. If the service was this bad on a Thursday noon time, I can't imagine what it's like on a weekend!

Input: Great location, but truly the WORST customer service. When checking in, we were not greeted at all, and the woman barely spoke to me and gave me zero information, acted out out when I asked about the very complicated parking situation and didn't confirm a total or make any sort of welcoming gesture. When we called the front desk for sheets for the couch bed, the attendant said "sending some" and then hung up the phone. When checking out, same experience as check in-rude, uninterested and unfriendly clerk who was doing the bare minimum. For as much money as this room was for the weekend, and based on other location experiences, we were expecting ABOVE AND BEYOND what we received. Truly have received better service at most other places we've stayed. 

The parking is asinine.  If you don't valet, which we were not given an option for or instructions, you have to park in a garage that is not attached to the hotel and make a ridiculous trek with all of your stuff. And on top of it, you're paying $33 a night to do so! 

The air conditioner did not work properly. It was either very hot or very cold, and the cold didn't last long. It wasn't responsive to our requests, and it just made for an uncomfortable nights sleep, both nights. 

The TV offerings were by and large the worst of any hotel stay we've ever had. The TVs themselves are old, bulky and out dated. They have blocked it to where you cannot use your own prime stick or Roku, which some hotels do so that's whatever. But to not have any channels that are worthwhile, a guide that is from the early 90s, and movies to rent that are $20, the whole thing was atrocious. 

We have paid hundreds of dollars less a night and had much better of an experience, from the service to the TV to the parking to the outdated and not terribly clean rooms. I would not recommend this hotel, not for any price but especially the $600 it cost us for 2 nights. 

Stay somewhere else! Trust me!

Input: First of all, I have wanted to go to Salty's for years and finally convinced my husband to try it out since my parents were in town.  I made our reservation online using Open Table.  This went well and someone from Salty's called to leave a confirmation message.  Our reservation was for 7:15.  I called to let the hostess know that we were running about 10 minutes behind and was assured that our table would be ready for us.  
When we arrived at 7:20, we waited 20 minutes to be seated.  The hostess informed me that there had been a mix up and someone else had taken our original table when the name of our party had been called.  I'm not sure how this happened since I was standing right beside the hostess stand from the second we checked in, but I was willing to give her the benefit of the doubt.  I was not thrilled that the table we ended up with after the mix up and the wait was back in a corner of the restaurant with almost no river view - the primary reason that I had wanted to visit Salty's in the first place.
It was a Friday night, and the place was hopping, so I wasn't completely surprised that our initial service was slow.  However, as the evening wore on and the restaurant emptied out, the service did not improve.  There were extended periods of time between visits from our server and delivery of drinks and food.  By 9:05, my father (who never complains) was ready to get the bill for what we had eaten so far and leave.  He made eye contact with our waitress, who turned around and walked the other direction!  At three different times, someone from our table had to be sent to track our waitress down for requests.  She finally let us know that the kitchen was "plating our food" and a full 10 minutes later it was finally delivered to our table.  This was an hour and a half after we sat down, and two hours after our original reservation!  I have not waited this long for food since I was in the Peace Corps and the restaurants would go buy, slaughter and clean a chicken in that amount of time!  At this point, the restaurant was practically empty.  
The waitress apologized and told us that things were slow because 400 people had come through that night - however I find it very hard to believe that this should be a problem for a place the size of Salty's that is used to large crowds.  

On top of all of this, the food was average and the bill was large.  Neither the waitress nor the hostess made any attempt to offer any sort of compensation for the glaringly poor service.  The 18% gratuity was added to the bill because our party was 6 people.  I suppose this was lucky for our server since she would probably have gotten significantly less after her stunningly bad performance - although it is difficult to say how much of the evening was actually her fault - other than ignoring our table for extended periods of time.

Interestingly, when I got up this morning and checked my email, there was something from Open Table (time stamped at 9:00 pm) saying that Salty's had canceled our reservation - which leaves me wondering if there was yet another screw up.

Then she told me that he was unqualified to tell me anything. "He's just a delivery driver."

Did she not know how to perform the simple functions that a mere delivery driver had mastered? I am sure I will never know because after I contacted the call center. How can this sort of mistake give rise to accusations of drunkenness on my part, I'd like to know. One can only surmise that it is I and the poor unqualified delivery driver who ultimately will bear the blame for this piteous ineptitude. Input: I went here for the first time over my lunch break in hopes that I had found my new nail salon without going very far.  The reviews were really good and it is walking distance from both my office and house!  I was however a little disappointed when it was all said and done.

Everything started out great, I walked in and was one of two in the salon so I was able to sit right down, always a plus!  They were very nice and offered me a complimentary bottle of cold water which was much needed after the walk from the office.  Sue did my nails and she was nice.  She didn't talk much, but that was okay, I just let her do her work.  A lot of the reviews raved about how fast the service was, so I thought I would get both a balance and pedi while on my lunch break.  I don't know if she was having a bad day, but I was there almost 2 hours and had to cancel my pedi because I had to get back to the office.  I thought my balance service was okay, at best.  At first glance, they looked fine but after I left and got back to the office, I started noticing a lot of flaws in my nails.  There are air bubbles under the gel, and my nails are pretty un-even.  It is something I can easily fix with a nail file at home, but when I just paid them to do it, I shouldn't have to.

I want to go back and try a pedicure, because I want to support local businesses downtown.  It was very clean, and again, it is easy access to my everyday life but I think they may be a better place for just getting a mani/pedi, maybe fills and full sets are not their forte.  All and all, it was okay at best for what I got.  I didn't feel it was as low as 2 stars but 4 stars seemed a little high for just having nice people.

UPDATE:
I originally gave this business 3 stars, but after a week with the job they did on my acrylics, they are FALLING OFF!!!  So I am changing my review to a 1 star.  This should NEVER happen to acrylics after a week.  The nail gel was on my cuticles and it is lifting so water is getting underneath the gel and the glue is not holding.  I called the salon earlier today and they said it was not thier fault, and if I wanted to come in a fix it, I could but they would charge me for a fill.  I THINK NOT!!  I will be going to another nail salon and see what they can do, and will NEVER return here.

Input: I brought my 2004 Toyota Prius into the service department after buying it used. It needed a 600 dollar sensor replaced and at the time I stated to the nice man that I wanted to get all of my scheduled maintenance up to date. He said there was no scheduled maintenance that needed to be done, but to come in at 80,000 miles to get my plugs and wires changed. A few months go by, I drive the car quite a bit. I take it to a jiffy lube for an oil change and they inform me that I'm 23,000 miles overdue for a transmission system flush. Basically, I'm pissed that I wasn't informed of this at the dealership, which is supposed to be more knowledgeable. I'm trying to resolve the issue with the dealership and keep getting put on hold and switched from one person to the next. An apology would be nice, instead I was told that "we assume you had service elsewhere". How could you assume that when I spoke in length with the technician about how I had just bought the vehicle used and wanted to get all of my scheduled maintenance up to date, and was willing to pay the going rate. Input: I GOT SCAMMED.
It has been several years since I have used K&M and I have been meaning to write a review for a long time.
I used K&M several times to clean my carpets and mostly to clean my vents and loved their service...until the last time.
I had them come by to clean my air vents. The guy said he found excessive mold in my air ducts and then went up in my attic to look around. He said there were several holes in my vents and to keep the mold down we would have to seal everything up.
This included taping the AC unit, utilizing spray foam sealant, RTV and killz moisture sensing paint. 
The price kept climbing and the time needed as well.
From a a simple $99-149 duct cleaning, it turned into $3000.00 AC system sealing.
During the process the technician kept coming up with what I thought were legitimate concerns that would cost more $$ to fix. The whole time, in the back of my mind, I had a nagging feeling I was getting scammed. I should have listened and acted. I didn't.
The process took 3-4 days. 
About 3 months later my AC guy came by to service my AC unit and asked me what all of this tape and RTV was doing on the unit. I told him the long story and he told me never have someone than an HVAC person do anything to to the AC system.

The owner of this company is pushy and sleazy and apparently hires scam artists.

I take full responsibility for getting scammed out of $2800.00 but I am writing this review to warn others.

Maybe things have changed with K$M but I will never use them again.

Beware of any of their techs suggesting anything more than you have requested and ALWAYS listen to your gut feelings when dealing with these kinds of services.

Input: I experienced an overall lack of quality with this dining experience.  

First off,  the actual meal I had intended to eat ended up costing me five dollars over the twenty dollar Groupon value.  It doesn't do me much good to buy a Groupon when it won't cover a meal to begin with.  

Their website did not list the sizes of their sirloin steaks by ounces.  I had to talk to the manager (Geoffrey) in order to get him to update his site.  I would think any customer-oriented business would want their potential clientele to know what they are ordering to avoid any issues down the line. 

The largest sirloin they offer is 10 ounces, which is fine for most people but rather small for those of us who are used to eating 12-16 ounce sirloins regularly.  Most steakhouses offer large steaks.  I was rather disappointed  to find out that Texas Steak Out did not.  

I had to negotiate over the phone with the owner to get what I wanted and even with that, I still paid $5 more than the value of the Groupon!

I ordered a sixteen ounce sirloin steak meal.  They allowed me to sub out the salad/baked potato/roll for grilled asparagus and onion rings.  

Sirloins are lean cuts of meat and that has been my experience whether dining out or buying meat at a deli.  Naturally, when this steak came out, I was shocked to see a slab of fat on the side which probably weighed about four to six ounces itself.  When I finished cutting away the fat, there might have been eight to ten ounces of actual meat there.  I gave my feedback to the manager on duty (Marlon) and he refused to serve a new steak nor refund the purchase price.

To summarize:  The taste of the steak was fine and the sides were adequate; it was the value for the cost of the meal that was lacking, as well as the quality of the cut of meat that is in question.  This steak was roadhouse dive quality.  You would not see this type of cut at a butcher or grocery store.  

The worst part of this experience was the ineptitude of management and ultimately, the owner (Geoffrey).  They knew I was using a Groupon, knew I was trying their product for the first time, and STILL could not deliver on the promise of a good impression.

The meal I had would have cost $25 without the Groupon, and quite frankly, it was wasn't even worth half of that (value-wise).

Lower your expectations if you are going to try this place, or better yet...grill your own steak at home for about one fourth of the cost.

I am amazed they are still in business.

Input: This experience could not have been more horrific!! I wouldn't touch this gong show in a million years and consider it a public service to warn people off this terrible company. The woman who runs this service "Diane" is clearly completely delusional and needs medication, but first, I'll try to recap. 

First of all, the package rate for a 2 bedroom condo is on the website as $300 including carpet cleaning. Seems clear enough right?  Apparently not. In my case the "extra" bedroom somehow required another $45 fee because only 1 bedroom in a 2 bedroom condo should be carpeted or some bafflegab. Ok, well, I agreed to pay more hoping I'd get some sweet cleaning. The price was supposed to include 2 cleaners for 4 hours including carpet cleaning. Fine. I booked for a Monday morning. 

Unfortunately I had to cancel Sunday but called and left a message. I called later on Monday to reschedule, and a red flag should have gone up when she insisted she never got my message. I absolutely did leave a message, have the call logged on my phone to prove it, and my husband clearly remembers me leaving it. But anyway, pushing that blip aside (beware the blips) went on to book a Wed apt. I work from home Wed so the 2pm time was possible. I was 4 mins away from the condo on Wed when they called and said they were going to be late and could they come at 3:30. Aside from the fact that I live half an hour away, I didn't plan on taking the whole afternoon off to let the freakin' cleaners in, I agreed to come back at 4pm. I had to turn around and drive the 1/2 hour back home, and go back to work for an hour to met a crazy deadline, then explain to my boss why I had to leave again on a day where we had several deadlines due. Then I drove 1/2 hr back to the condo again. Fine. Whatever, people are late. I was prepared to be forgiving. 

They finally arrived late at 4:20 and spent the next 15 mins and several phone calls later kevetching that there was no parking and their stuff was heavy, poor babies. I agreed to move my car in the underground to get them on the $&:@ task at hand. Three girls showed up and promptly informed me that they don't do carpet cleaning. THAT would be a separate appointment I would have to arrange sometime later. What? First I'd heard of it. Given that my landlord was due to come the next evening to do the final inspection I was fairly alarmed by this. 

My condo wasn't bad. Just needed a good deep clean, but was empty. The carpets were cleaned 6 months past, they didn't have to clean the walls as the landlord was painting. The girls agreed it would be a breeze. Phoning the office "Diane", I said I was not prepared to pay more for the 3rd cleaner and wasn't happy about the lack of carpet cleaning. She suggested 3 hours instead of 4 to account for the extra cleaner, plus a 10% discount for my trouble. We booked the carpet cleaner for the next night. She wanted an e-transfer of the money right away because (bafflegab) machine not hooked up, whatever. Her office was closing back east, could I do right away. So, like a dummy, I did, in between almost getting an aneurysm picking hubby up from work, going to another appointment and this crazy woman's phone calls. Thank god I didn't pay for the carpet cleaner but the amount still didn't square. The package was supposed to be 2 cleaners for 4 hours including cleaning for $345. She wanted $306 just for cleaning and she said she'd do the 10% off when it came to settle the bill. 
 
Hubby saw the cleaners out and frankly the cleaning job was about as basic as you get. What 3 girls did for 3 hours I don't know. The sinks weren't sparkling, the floor tiles still had marks, they must have just breezed over. But I didn't see this until the next night when we waited at the condo for the carpet cleaner that never came. Diane never called, I called her at 5:30pm and she said she hadn't heard from him all day. We heard nothing more. Meanwhile the landlord came and did the inspection and we've made other arrangements to clean the carpets (more cash out the door). 

This morning I called to get a refund. She decided to go off on a rant whereby she blamed me for everything. My condo was horrific, she tried to accommodate my difficult schedule (I work during the day, that's it) etc etc. Yelling at the top off her lungs she went full psycho and wouldn't let me say one word. I hung up. THEN the crazy cat phoned me back to say the call was being recorded for quality assurance whereby I started to laugh!! Seriously?? And she started her rant up again!! OMG!! Needless to say we figure she stole about $150 from us as the carpets were never done and her package deal is a scam. 

My hubby tried later on this morning to reason with her and she was in her own dimension, out and out lying to him about what I had agreed to (and he knows because he was there). A refund will never come.

Protect yourself- Don't do business with thus company. We'll be making a report to the better business bureau.

Input: I made my second trip here the other day to give this place another chance but unfortunately it will be my last. They have very cute items and the store is set-up very well. There is a super-cute chair and a pair of shoes that I would die for but I just cannot do it. I thought they had new stuff but it turned out everything was just moved around. Someone must have a degree in merchandising because they do a great job but they need to go take Customer Service 101. The attitude on the girl in there was absolutely appalling. Cambridge is a very diverse community with a mix of people but this store seems to think they are in the middle of Beacon Hill. How about a hello? Or maybe it was because I was wearing sweats and my $1.00 flip flops from the nail salon down the street. Maybe if I had pulled out my DVF sandals from my bag they would have acknowledged me? 

I love vintage items and when I go to a store that markets itself as vintage I expect vintage. I do not expect Bebe shirts and knock-off Louie bags. To give them the benefit of the doubt it's vintage with a modern twist - but to me that's deceptive and it's like buying something for $50.00 and getting the bill for $200 because you didn't read the small print or it's like going into the dollar store and nothing is a dollar. They know how to get people in there but they sure don't know how to keep them.

I met the cutest little old lady outside who wanted to sell her shoes from the 60's - she said she was treated awful and that the girl said "Those aren't vintage!" and turned her back and walked away. Come on Lady Luxe - you are in a family neighborhood - at least be somewhat considerate to the people who make up the neighborhood. You've got to be welcoming of all people or you are not going to make it.
I won't go back there ever again. I will continue to frequent the Cambridge Antique Market and Vintage Revenge - the owner there is friendly and very welcoming!  At least there I know I am getting authentic vintage merchandise and I don't have to weed out the items from the mall. 
The good things about my experience there is they caused me to need a drink and I went down the street to Guidos for a drink and met some interesting people. 
You can see the attitude yourself without visiting the store by reading their snide comment to a Yelper who wasn't that satisfied. Instead of being sarcastic why not contact that person and see what you can do to change their feeling about your establishment?  Offer them a coupon or a personal shopping experience to help them find what they need. Maybe the "dynamic sister" duo should stop concentrating on the over-done reviews by their friends and start concentrating on how to be personable and welcoming.

Input: Apparently overbooking is not just an airline problem. 

What has transpired today in dealing with Sear's Home Service can only be characterized as shameful. I personally have never in my life seen such poor customer service come from such a well-established brand, and leaves me questioning ever doing business with your company again. After you read this incident that occurred I would like for you to tell me why I should continue doing business with you again. I challenge you to change my mind. 

Back in March, during an annual Maintenance of our double oven we purchased at Sears, the repairman suggested that we sign up for an extend plan for our Samsung Refrigerator, he convinced us that it was money well spent, and that they could take care of any issues that arise. So we signed up.

Three weeks ago we had an issue come up with the refrigerator and was told we could be seen between the hours of 1 and 5 on 4/28 three weeks later. 

They informed us they would have to defrost the refrigerator 

On 4/28 my wife took the afternoon off and waited for the technician, and defrosted the refrigerator in anticipation for his arrival, when 5:05pm came around my wife called Sears Repair and spoke with Nancy 

Nancy told my wife that he was on a big job and we were the last call of the day and he will be giving us a call before coming to our home... (Lie as it turned out) 

7:20 pm - Still no Technician 

Again my wife called and again spoke with Nancy and asked her where he was. After a long pause she said the Technician ran long and they had overbooked the day and we were bumped...when my wife said that no one called us, Nancy started to get defensive and my wife requested her supervisor.  Nancy informed my wife that she could handle the situation and that giving her to her supervisor would not make it any better... when my wife insisted she was transferred to her supervisor Dolores. Dolores got on the phone and immediately hung up on my wife, and never called back.  Both of these ladies should be reprimanded for their actions or should I say inactions.  

We called back and was once again placed on hold for 20 minutes, this time I spoke with Cole and told him of the situation and asked to pass me onto his supervisor where I spoke with Audrey, I will say that Audrey was very professional and tried to accommodate my situation, but this is where Sears failed.

1. If a customer is a victim of overbooking then they should be pushed to the top of the list for next day...not four days.
2. Don't wait for us to call customer service they should been on top of this.

3. If the customer took time off from work to wait for the technician the first time they should not be inconvenienced to do so again the next time if it was not their fault. Compensation should be reflected.
4. Here it is Friday night and apparently there is no technician out on Saturdays, so now we are waiting until Tuesday. Sears should address a situation like this when it is convenience for the customer, not for Sears. 
5. Supervisors should be given more autonomy to resolve customer issues with direct actions that can be measureable, again another failure for Sears.

Input: Took a chance to take the wife to a low key local pizza parlor birthday dinner. This place was close to home and had a good four star rating via Yelp, thought I'd give it a go. 

We walk in. Classic semi-run down but cozy old school pizza parlor. The young guy who was working the front could've at least tried looking like he enjoyed his job. (Or at least greet us when we walked in) Nope. A few of the reviews mentioned the service wasn't so great, but the food would be worth it, right?

We ordered a medium Mega-Supreme with a pound of their "famous" Jo-jos. 45 minutes later, no sign of anything. We walked in at 5pm, with one person ahead of us. I'm used to a 20+ minute wait for fresh pizza... but 45 is pushing it. I walk up there to be told that someone was supposed to tell us they burnt the pizza and it's being remade. (Nope. didn't happen) The guy running the pizzas yells over it'll be another 5-6 minutes. 15 minutes later, the wife is in the car frustrated, I'm standing in line to get a refund. (Again - this was a birthday dinner)

Our food was magically boxed up and ready to go as I walked up to the cashier. Wow. I guess they knew they dropped the ball to the point they boxed our food to go. 

Lousy first experience. (And last!)

Let's get to the food now. That's right! We came here to eat food! 

The pizza was okay. My biggest critique: why use canned mushrooms on pizza? Also - the Mega-Supreme we got was kind of a hybrid of a Taco Pizza. Which makes me question if they were in a rush to fix their mishap they just make-shifted an existing order to expedite ours. 

The Jo-jos were good. But honestly, the poor experience really ruined the meal. Also: how can you screw up jo-jos? 

Just like what I told the cashier when I was leaving. Just do better guys. You dropped the ball big time and it's quite unfortunate. The wife even tipped you and this is the pay out we got.

Extremely poor service. Mediocre pizza. 

Very dissatisfied and will not be coming back.

Input: It is not safe to eat here if you have food allergies!

What can I say, the fastest way to a one star review from me is to poison my wife.  The first thing I ask the server at any restaurant is whether or not they can safely accommodate my wife's food allergy. The second thing I do is make it ABUNDANTLY clear that her reaction is severe and life threatening (I use the scene in pulp fiction, when Uma Thurman O.D.s, and they then have to stab her in the heart--substituting an Epipen--to illustrate the severity).

With that information, there is absolutely no excuse for then topping the food with that very ingredient.  That's what happened tonight at Nuestra Cocina. When the food runner pointed out that her ticket said not to use the ingredient in question, they simply scraped it off my wife's meat, and tried to serve it to her.

Luckily I could see this entire interaction from where I was sitting in the restaurant, and I insisted the food be remade. What they SHOULD have done then is remake her dish from scratch, making damn sure it wasn't contaminated by the allergen. Unfortunately,what they did instead was simply give her the next one that they had already been cooking. By the time we got home this evening, my wife's throat had begun swelling shut. I had to stab her with her epipen, she can barely talk, and it will be days before she is fully recovers.

Yep, you really EARNED this one star review, Nuestra Cocina.

It is heartbreakingly difficult to get my wife to try a new restaurant. It is terrifying for her, and it shouldn't be, because--as a veteran of over a decade in food service--I can tell you that it takes just three things to avoid what happened to my wife tonight.  Empathy; good communication between the servers and kitchen; and an intelligent approach to food prep.   

Unfortunately it is sometimes infuriatingly difficult to get servers in Portland to take food allergies seriously. Every...single...time my wife has been poisoned, it is because the server did not--despite my effusive examples of how serious her allergy is--simply write "food allergy" on the ticket to the kitchen. There is an ENORMOUS difference to a cook between receiving a ticket intimating that a customer wants "no peanuts", for example, and and one that lets him/her know that the a customer is "allergic to peanuts", because in one case cross contamination won't really matter, and in the other it can kill them.

So again, if you have any sort of food allergy, Nuestra Cocina is not for you.

Input: This was the second time I went here for brunch. The first time was a very nice experience! Good hearty diner food, fast and friendly service, etc. I came back expecting the same, but this time...ugh. It was mostly the waiter's very weird and poor service.

Our waiter was not good. He spoke very low, so it was hard to know what he was rambling about. And did he ramble! But he didn't smile either. He lingered after bringing us our food. 

My partner who I was with only got two of his three slices of french toast ordered, and the waiter made an excuse about some other waiter taking our food to a different table (poor form, I'm sorry, you don't talk crap about other coworkers to the public like that). 

My partner also wanted to order more food at that time, and when told they didn't have what he wanted (a bagel...basic breakfast food) he rambled yet again about east coast/west coast bagel politics and didn't even suggest something else...just walked away (FINALLY) without my partner having a chance to order something! 

I honestly can't remember if he returned to refill our drinks himself because they have a friendly young lady doing that for the whole floor...which makes me wonder if the house splits up the tips or what. She deserves some percentage for sure!

So, when it came time to tip, I had to get change (which I did from the front register myself because I honestly wasn't confident we'd get change in a quick and smooth way without some mumbled crap from the waiter. Then, my partner and I agreed to honestly just leave exact change because he was pretty upset about never getting a chance to order more food. You know, the basic thing you do at restaurants?

THEN, what do you know, the waiter FOLLOWED US OUT OF THE RESTAURANT to ask why we didn't tip! 

Not only does that leave his other tables totally unattended, it made me feel REALLY UNCOMFORTABLE. If you don't get a tip, quietly assume we're assholes or quietly consider what you did or didn't do well. DO NOT CHASE US DOWN THE STREET.

It wasn't like he was super overwhelmed and busy, like he was trying his hardest to do the basic. We didn't get the basic service, we got this guy waxing poetic about bagels and philosophy while our stomachs growled. Then we got followed by him out of the business. That's wildly inappropriate and I will not be returning to, nor recommending, Genie's in the future.

Input: Man I wish I could learn from my past transgressions.  Years ago I swore this place off after they seemed to insult the entire nation of Thailand with a disgusting riff on phad thai.  Yet proximity (it's our closest Thai), hunger and desperation conspired against me and i actually had a 3 star experience here at some point while our little one was an infant and we were in that- order takeout or don't eat- up all night delirium phase  (she's one now, we're out of it).  

Last night again, the desperation crept in after a long night of work and putting baby down, I was flying solo so ordered some delivery.  I ordered the spring rolls and the buddha noodles.  The spring rolls were fine, fried straight out of a freezer and nothing to complain about.  Now let's pause and think about the situations that potentially led up to the Buddha Noodles. 

1.  The place was actually closed, but a couple of drunk frat guys broke in looking to steal Singha beers, saw my order come through on the computer screen, and took pity so did their best to recreate the buddha noodles.  Which involved canned vegetables, a lump of old rice noodles and some wet peanut butter thrown on top.  Thanks for trying guys, three cheers for alpha tau omega. 

2.  Order comes through the screen, is received by an uninspired employee who has never actually eaten real Thai food, old noodles all stuck together are plopped on a bed of formerly canned and overcooked yet completely unseasoned vegetables, and a ladel-full of soupy peanut butter is dumped on top?  Garnish? ha! Let the food speak for itself.  

3. I was featured on some reality show called "Eff this guy with gross Thai".  I'm still waiting for my release form

Look- I much prefer to write a positive glowing happy review.  This place does have big portions, this place isn't that expensive, I'm sure the people that make the food are nice people.  Clearly though, I'm not who they are pandering to. I've spent months of my life in Thailand and have a weak spot for the food, for the flavors, the heat, the sour, the sweet, the salty, the people the culture etc... I want to smell the fish sauce and the K'fir limes, I want sprigs of cilantro and crushed peanuts, I want authenticity!  I know I'll never get it as good as it is on the streets of Chang Mai, but I do expect a little more from the streets of Boulder.

Input: The absolute worst adoption experience you could ever encounter. If I could give zero stars I would!

After having a dog for 9 years, we decided it was time to get a second dog. We looked up Pet Rescue by Judy, read all of the information on their website about adopting, submitted an adoption application, notified our landlord and obtained written permission to get a second dog. After a few days we were contacted by the organization and began emailing back and forth with an adoption advocate and after answering several more questions, we were pre-approved to adopt a special needs dog that we selected. We made an appointment to pick her up and pay the adoption fees. 

When we arrived it was a bit chaotic but everyone was friendly and were so grateful we were adopting a "special needs" dog. We signed the contract and as I was handing over my debit card to pay, an old lady randomly asked me if MY dog was spayed. I was caught off guard by the question but was honest and said no. Suddenly the lady flipped out and said that we couldn't adopt one of their dogs and that it was their "policy". I was confused because MY dog is a female and so was the dog we were adopting. I tried to talk to this woman because I didn't understand her reasoning and she just kept repeating over and over again that she had been doing this for 26+ years and she wasn't making an exception. The other employees/volunteers looked downright horrified and embarrassed by how nasty she was being. They urged me to stay quiet and be patient while they tried to "convince" this woman to change her mind or at the very least let us foster the dog if we agreed to get our dog spayed. Nope. She only got more nasty and started talking down to my husband and I and then went on to lecture us and roll her eyes when she found out who our vet was (which by the way we've been using for 9 years). We pointed out that NO WHERE on the website does it say existing dogs in the home must be spayed or neutered, which she admitted to, but was VERY shady when we repeatedly asked her why it's not something they say up front. On our application we even stated that our dog was not spayed and we were still allowed to continue with the adoption process.

After finally realizing we would not be allowed to adopt (we waited an HOUR until the other employees/volunteers gave up trying to convince her), one of the volunteers apologized for the way we were treated and told us that if we took OUR dog to get spayed, we could come back and adopt. She also admitted that the nasty woman that made us feel like horrible human beings was THE Judy from Pet Rescue by Judy and that she's nasty to everyone and isn't a "people person". She told us that if we do decide to come back to do so because we care about the dog despite how poorly the organization's owner treats people trying to adopt. 

There are so many dogs available for adoption through other organizations, please do not waste your time, feelings, or money adopting a dog from an awful organization like this one. Here are some other organizations to consider:

Orange County Animal Services
Pet Alliance of Greater Orlando 
South Lake Animal League
Florida Little Dog Rescue

***UPDATE***
A few months later (October 2015 to be exact) we adopted a dog from Orange County Animal Services and let me tell you, the experience was beyond my expectations! The employees were sweet and friendly and the adoption process is easy breezy. They let you wander around as long as you'd like to browse from their huge selection of breeds, which to my surprise, included plenty of puppies. The price to adopt a dog is $55 but they often have promotions and specials if you're on a budget. By the end of October both my 9 yr. old dog and my newly adopted dog (2 yrs. old) were spayed/neutered...and we did it because we wanted to, not because it was forced upon us.

The first red flag was how they insisted on taking extensive X-rays of my back as standard practice. After exposing me to high levels of radiation without a second thought, it turned out my spine was healthy.  I was expecting a mild adjustment, and maybe some preventative advice on back care.  

However, Ms. Zygmont recommended a long-term treatment plan for my intermittent "lower back issue", starting with my coming in on a daily basis for an entire week!  She had me do the whole shebang, including the electrical stimulation, adjustments, massage, and physical therapy.  The front desk was aggressive about scheduling me to come in the following day for another adjustment, and, giving them the benefit of the doubt despite a bad feeling in my gut, I came in.  Little did I know that I was to undergo the stimulation, therapy, massage, and physical therapy as well, without any justification.  They had the balls to try to reschedule me for the next day, but I put an end to it.

Looking over the insurance claims and seeing the $1100 they charged my insurer for those two days, I realize that Zygmont Chiropractic took maximum advantage of the generous chiropractic benefits of my insurer for a patient who didn't need these treatments.  

Zygmont is no different from any other sheisty chiropractor.  I imagine that with the increased overhead from their new location, such exploitative practices will just get worse.  Stay away.

My son grew up in a Barbershop until his Godfather passed away five years ago and closed the shop. His Dad was a barber and he stopped cutting. We moved to Florida and he struggled to find someone he trusted. I will not say any names but I was given a Black Barber name as a recommendation. My son loved how he cut so we would make the 50 minute drive. My son now goes to school in MD and plays Basketball. His team was getting interviewed by Steven A. when he returned. He wanted to cut all his hair off and chose this Barber to do it. I reached out and got a 10:30 appointment. We left 1.5hr early because a Saturday in Orlando has traffic. I got there at 10:35 and my son walked in. The Barber barely made eye contact and told him he was late and could not take him. I walked in to confirm if he said he couldn't take him now or not at all. He immediately got defense. Saying I should have called and so what if I live 50 minutes away, he lives an hour away. He told me when I made the appointment he could take me at 10:30 because he had a 10am. Then he told me I was his first and he came early for me. I honestly think he made a mistake and didn't apologize when he realized it. Instead he went on to tell me how he's a Barber and this is a Business. Then maybe he shouldn't have been raising his voice when I only came to clarify. I owned a Salon before returning to corporate America and have a huge respect for the art. I had my two year old in the car and was literally at the light at 10:30am so I didn't think it was necessary to pick up the phone. He was clearly half way through the client head in his chair. That does not take 5 minutes. He had to start him earlier then 10:30. My son was so upset because he has been preparing for this day to cut his three year hair growth off. So I went back in and asked if I could have someone else. He clearly sent me to a guy who was not as comfortable with Black men cuts or experienced in general. For drinks, she told us, the only two seats left were  in an awkard corner between the bar and the window. We actually tried to sit there because we really wanted to try out this place, but it was just too uncomfortable. So instead we left, wondering what crowds could possibly show up to have dinner after 9 pm on a Monday night to justify keeping all those empty tables and losing two customers. I sincerely hope that being a biracial couple had nothing to do with why she treated us that way (but the place had no diversity at all tonight, so unfortunately I did have to wonder). We were both still wearing business casual from the day at work, so I know for sure it was not that. Input: So...the door man/bouncer (apparently his name was Jason) here had the displeasure of throwing out my friend by her neck..  Her NECK.  My friend and I (two twenty-something females) were in Portland visiting for 3 days and were told we simply HAD to come to Sassy's...big mistake.  It was a slow Tuesday night in the strip club, and we were there fairly early in the evening.  As a result, we made up two of the three total people sitting by the stage tipping-everyone else there was at the bar away from the stage drinking.  In between shows, my friend and I would go up to the bar and get drinks from their awesome bartender working that night-I think she was from Australia.  While at the bar we met quite a few of the dancers having drinks and food as well, and were chatting and just getting along swimmingly.  I think that the gals working were glad to have some girls their age come watch them instead of creepy old dudes most of the time.  

Anyway, once we were seated back at center stage hollering and making it rain for our homegirls, one stripper who we really hit it off with was performing.  She was also doing some amazing acrobatic moves that i've never seen before and singing along with the song that was playing (I think it was drake?), but I digress.  Whilst getting catered to dance-proximity wise, my friend next to me pretended to spank our homegirl when she was pressing her boobs on all of our ones to pick them up off the stage.  Feeling safe as one usually does in a strip club, and a bit like friends almost with the current performer, we did not think anything of this at all.  Apparently the bouncer felt differently, because he materialized out of nowhere and began to escort both of us out by our shoulders saying that "we could not even pretend to touch the dancers and had to leave immediately."  I don't know about everyone else, but when i've had a few drinks and someone is punishing me for something I did not even do.. I might as well do it.  Just bringing you inside the inner-most workings of my friend's mind, because at that point she said well f-this and spanked the dancer on the way out.  This did not delight the bouncer whatsoever, who proceeded to lift said friend by her neck and back and toss her outside into the street.  She was literally airborne and landed painfully on her back thanks to that brutish idiot.  

I was enraged that he felt the need to get physical with two girls-I can see if we were creepy old guys preying on young girls, maybe.  But that was over the top testosterone-fueled force and I sure did get up in his face and tell him that he was a misogynistic asshole and that I was going to write a really bad yelp review.  That's about as threatening as I can get.  To this he simply chortled and told me to "go ahead, his bosses saw the whole thing and were laughing about it."  Our homegirl came outside after and was really riled up about it too.  She apologized on his behalf and offered to even give us a ride home!  We declined however, seeking instead another bar to sooth our wounded pride (and back).

A little cherry on top: my phone was still behind the bar charging when this all went down, and instead of letting me get it, the aforementioned misogynist threw it outside on the asphalt where it broke.  Neat!  Thanks Portland!  Can I give negative stars??  Vomit.

Input: I really wanted to enjoy this place as there were so many positive reviews. I am a bit of a foody and cook at home at least six nights a week so it's a treat to go out to eat and I have high expectations when going out to eat from the kitchens of professionals. I want the meal to taste more delicious than what I could cook at home. My parents owned a restaurant for over 20 years, so I know what cooked to order food is like.  

I had seen some negative reviews on google and trip advisor, but yelp is my go to, default location for restaurant recommendations. Our dinner was not, in fact, cooked to order, unless you consider microwaving to order as an equivalent. 

I read a review on another site complaining that they microwaved their french bread and was skeptical of the reviewer. We did in fact order the bread and it was definitely microwaved because it was warm, but the moisture had been whisked away. The music is low so it was difficult to have a private conversation at your table and I could hear the microwave multiple times in the kitchen. I kept imaging what Gordon Ramsay might have to say in an episode of Kitchen Nightmares. 

My bourguignon was ok, but my friend's rabbit was very dry, most likely because it was microwaved. Additionally, the rice that was offered as a side was dry and, again, microwaved. You could tell because of the chunks that were clumped together and hard and inedible. The bourguignon had some decent flavor, but the rabbit was not at all delicious. 

I just want to be able to offer another perspective for those expecting high quality French cuisine. If you expect the cuisine of French restaurants in New York or LA, you will be sorely disappointed. 

I do believe if they did have fresh ingredients, cooked to order, and threw away their microwave, there could be some delicious meals here at Au Rendez-Vous. Until then, I would steer clear.

Input: Never come here! They tell you a lot of lies and have a very deceiving haggling process. 

I came in to search for new 2018 Kia Sorentos, because there is a manufacturer discount on those, up to $5,000 in cash. 

When I came in, the first thing I asked for were the 2018's Kia Sorentos. The seller (S****t), started lying.  Some of the lies he told us:
- Well, you know, our best deals are actually on the 2019's. Truth: he just didn't have any 2018's. 
- The 2018 is now considered a used car, you will not get the same warranty. Truth: it is not, is just a different model year. 

Then he showed us the 2019, we liked it, and the haggling started. 

First he said that the car cost $45,049. That is a lie. The MRSP for the 2019 Kia Sorento EX Premium which was the car that we were looking at is $42,950.00. Basically they did this so they could, even without us asking, starting haggling it down to trick you into thinking it is a good deal, when you are paying MRSP (or even more). 

Then they made us an offer, which the seller said with all the words it was all inclusive, of taxes and fees. Both my wife and I understood it really well. When we came back the next day to close the deal, he said he would maintain the same deal from yesterday and came with the sheet for us to sign. I started carefully reading though the numbers, and it was actually the value he told us + TAX and + fees. When I questioned, he lied again. Said it was never with taxes included. The manager came and said he wouldn't be able to honour that. 

We went to a different Kia dealership the next day and purchased a 2018 Kia Sorento as we wanted, without any lying! The negotiation started at MRSP and it was always very clear what was included or not. 

Please, never come here! We shouldn't allow dealers like these to grow.

Well we arrived and it was $30 for VIP or a few steps over $20. This is all self park by the way. Whatever. We enter and are seated. We're at a table right in the middle two tables from stage. Good seats. 

We had THE WORST experience with getting a freaking waitress...like wth?? I asked a waitress and my husband spoke to 3...yes 3 different people including the "manager" before somebody finaaaaalllllyyyy came. The show was almost over at that point, yet we had been trying to order or find someone since before it started!! My husband also mentioned that all the waitresses who came by were musty. You may say why bring this up...well hygiene is important and you're  interacting with people in a small space...but I guess if they don't respect themselves enough to bathe properly why should we expect proper customer service.

All sides including my fries are $5. I ordered a glass of Merlot and he a margarita. When the food finally came I had a tiny portion of fries and they were almost cold. She also brought a beer. Neither one of us drink beer. She tried to argue with him about it. He just said ok so we could enjoy the show. They automatically charge 15% gratuity to your bill so I'm sure that also plays a role in them not giving the best service. After we were done eating my husband explained that he wasn't going to pay for the beer. After some back and forth it was taken off. 

They charged $15 or $16 for a margarita. This place is ridiculous. Now I see why people in the reviews kept saying this place will nickel and dime you. Money isn't our issue...it's the horrendous customer service. His shrimp were ok. Nothing to rave about. We didn't get VIP tickets because reviews stated it wasn't worth it and customer service was lacking there too. The set up is mostly tables for 4. Input: After my cat was found to have a heart murmur I called them and was quoted for an echocardiogram and since their prices were fair and they were close to home, I took my cat in.  Once there, they took it upon themselves to run a large amount of blood tests, acting as though this was part of the appointment. No one asked if I was okay with it so I assumed it was standard. As I was checking out, the receptionist told me "not to freak out" because the bill was slightly more than I was quoted for. $500 more! I was so flustered I just paid the bill and left, without so much as a diagnosis for the heart murmur. I will say this, everyone in the office was very kind and when they called me a few weeks later to tell me that they had figured out the cause of the murmur, I took the risk and bought the medicine that they recommended for another $275. During the treatment I called many times to ask if something my cat was going was a side effect of the medicine and very few times was my call actually returned by a doctor. I was supposed to take my cat back for a follow up echocardiogram after the medicine was done but I've since chosen not to at this point.  I guess they got enough money out of me thus far because I haven't heard a peep from them. Disappointed because I initially felt as though I had finally found a vet that wasn't in it for the money.

Input: I had high hopes after reading previous reviews, however, this location was another LabCorp disappointment. I can't speak for all the staff at this Winter Park location, but the employee behind the desk Sophia was the most passive aggressive labcorp employee I have ever encountered. Her lack of empathy and general "I hate my job" attitude is what prompted to write this review.

I came in on time for an appt, after providing my information and specifying which Dr provided the order (as I have been seen by a few Dr's that have ordered lab work recently and sent in the order electronically ) I was told to have a seat. A few minutes went by and I was given the patient responsibility form to sign with my estimated costs. I signed it sat back down to finish reviewing it and realized that the wrong order was processed from a physician I haven't seen in months. 

I realize that this is an honest mistake, however, had I not reviewed the entire form I would have paid to have unnecessary lab work performed from a months old order that I would have never seen the results to as I am no longer a patient of said doctor. Not to mention I would have shown up and paid for a follow up visit to my actual Dr only to find out that my lab work was never performed. 

Honest mistake, however, I not once received an apology in fact  the total opposite she became frustrated with me because of the extra work her mistake had now caused. At that point I didn't dare to mention that I had confirmed with her from the very beginning the Dr who had actually ordered the lab work in the first place. 

I work in the customer service field and I understand the challenges that working with the public creates, however, when I am in the wrong an apology goes a long way. But with a company that overworks and underpay's its employees and in an industry where the insurance companies only gives us 2 major lab companies to choose from I can see how hiring and retaining good quality employees is not a priority.

Input: This restaurant is so awful that the first thing I thought about upon waking up on Saturday morning was writing a condemning Yelp review about it.

It's a familiar story at this point; we arrived around 8 p.m. with intentions of eating at Sunset and were diverted to Patron's.  It wasn't until around 9:40 that we were actually served our food.  I had to ask, as other unfortunate Patron's patrons have had to, for the shockingly meager serving of chips and salsa we were given to tide us over about an hour after we ordered.  Finally, four of six dishes came out at the same time (one of which was not what my friend had ordered), and we all picked off of our plates and waited until the remaining two dishes were served- one of them, the fajitas, incomplete and served in installments.

We were finished eating and very ready to leave, but as you probably suspected, it took forever for us to get the check and another seemingly eternal stretch of time before our server actually picked it up.  If you want to go to Patron's for dinner, I'd suggest going while you're still eating lunch.  And don't get too excited about your post-dinner plans, because you'll miss them.

The manager came over as we were getting ready to leave and asked how everything was.  When I told him that, "Honestly, it took forever," he apologized, made some excuses, and told me that "next time, we'll do something for ya."

Ha!  Next time.  At least he had a sense of humor.

Here's what my boyfriend had to say about this experience:

"I was at this table as well, and agree that this was the worst service I have ever received at a restaurant, with little to no apologies to top it off.  It was almost as if it were our fault for deciding to get dinner on a Friday night...
What enraged me the most was when a table of 6 sitting right next to us arrived at least 30-45 minutes after we sat down, was served their food BEFORE us, got their check BEFORE us, and paid and left while we were still waiting for our plates to be cleared.  
They never offered to wrap our leftovers, never apologized for the almost 2 hour wait, and included the tip into our check, which added insult to injury.  The food was okay-at-best, and cannot compete with their sister restaurant Sunset.  As others have mentioned, the servers were not rude, but extremely inattentive.  Toward the end of the night (since we didn't get to leave until almost 11:30pm!) I noticed more staff members running around than during the dinner rush.  I wondered if someone had gone downstairs, told the Sunset crew to throw on Patron's shirts, and help clean up the disaster upstairs.  Perhaps these issues are "growing pains" but they should cut into the owner's bottom line for the first year, not ruin the customer's night.

Food: 2.5/5
Decor: 3/5
Service: 0/5"

Input: I have gone to this place twice now. The first time went I had bought a groupon. While they were a little late taking my car in, and it took about 25 minutes longer than they said it would, I would have still rated it 4/5. The lady at the front desk was super sweet, bringing me home cooked curry to eat while I waited. So I went back. They honoured the groupon price without me having to purchase another groupon- great. Same lady, same food- great. Late taking my car in and more than 45 minutes longer than they said it would be- not so great. But the reason for the 1/5 rating is because I realized after this last oil change that the sticker they put on my windshield to tell me when I needed another oil change was for 5,000km. For a synthetic oil change, this should have been at least 8,000. So I called to tell them, and to ask if they could see if the same thing had happened with my last sticker, and sure enough, they had written 5,000 after the first one. This means that I bought another oil change at least 3,000km early, and only 3.5 months after my last oil change. I explained my frustration to the guy, and non-chalantly he suggest he could "throw in a tire rotation or something next time to make it up". I think you can say that the first time was a mistake (forgot it was synthetic), but doing it twice certainly makes me think they are being dishonest, assuming most people wouldn't notice (I didn't- it was my husband who did). Anyways...I don't usually review places, but I feel like this was pretty disappointing, and maybe others who have had their oils changed by these guys should also double check the math so that you don't waste your money too! Rant over.

We noticed they weren't really frying their wings all that well. They constantly switched between sweet fried bananas and the salty ones without telling customers. They started putting less of the red sause on the chicken so then you'd end up with oddly textured fried wings with a dried coat of sauce.

Then one day, they got our order wrong. We ordered 2 "bbq" chicken wings with french fries and 1 order of the original fried ones with salty fried bananas. SOMEHOW we ended up with 3 orders of normal wings and sweet bananas. We drove all the way back just for the guy to hand us a cup of red sauce and to tell us they had no more of the salty fried bananas. Oh, the chicken looked weird. 

Never went back.

Input: Had gone here once with no issues but on my returning trip is when it all started. I picked a polish that seemed to almost be down to the end and I'm assuming older than the rest. Had an issue with the gel bubbling up 3 times on my thumb which I don't believe was the nail artists fault at all. It was nearing closing time and we decided that it was less noticeable with a shiny topcoat even though the rest were matte. We left it at that because it was around 15 minutes after closing time but I was never told that I could come back if it still bothered me. Which after spending $80+ for a gel mani and there being a noticeable bump, inevitably the next day I wanted a repair on just the one nail. I tried to book a repair online but there was no option. I called and they got me in the same day which was nice. 

Once I arrive, I am asked what number the color was... as I am not a nail artist I didn't have the nail color memorized so I let them know it was the forest green of which there was only one on the swatch so I figured that would be helpful. I was told "there are a bunch of forest greens, I will go find it" in a negative tone. This is from a different nail artist as my previous one wasn't in. I am sat down and she fixes the nail with not a lot of issues. All is good or so it seems lol. 

The next day, a whole separate nail has chipped for no reason as I have an office job and not one with much manual labor. I call again to schedule another repair for the new nail. This is all within 3 days. A gel mani should last a minimum of 2 weeks... so they get me in right away (nice) and I come in to find they are out of the color I had on this new nail. We pick a color close to the last. She fixes this nail super quickly and I leave. 

Within a few hours of this repair, I g the same chip. I don't even bother calling or going back because of the way I was treated the past two times as if they were annoyed I was back for them to fix their errors. I had to pay 3 times for parking in the short north (which is not easy to find btw) with not one apology or discount offered for my next service. 

If this had been a $30 gel mani elsewhere I would expect this but not at a seemingly upscale nail salon such as W nail bar.


Edit: I reached out to the email provided below about this review a month ago with no response.

Input: Complete Auto in Grove City was a frustrating and upsetting experience.  I don't recommend this auto shop.

They had given me a $1965.00 quote to fix my very old 2005 Kia Sedona.  The mechanic (I think his name is Jerry) insisted he was giving me a good deal. The Kia dealership a few miles away quoted me less for the same repairs.

I had also specifically told the owner and written down my concerns about my Sedona, saying I would not be interested in fixing this auto if the repairs are too much money.  $2000 for a 13 year old beat auto is too much money.
   They didn't care or they didn't listen.
   Instead, the mechanic encouraged me to spend even more money by getting my tires replaced with them while my car was at their shop.

I refused to let them fix a thing.  And, I'm upset that they wasted my time by lying about "helping" me and giving me a good deal.  Also, I wasted my money since the diagnostic charge was $115.  In the end, I paid them to do nothing to my car.

My impression of the mechanic and the owner is they are not honest nor do they have integrity as their sign on the building says.  I found them to be unhelpful in every way that was most important to me.  I also felt they wanted to argue with me about the cost of my repairs and the service they gave.  That was very unprofessional.

If I was closer to home I would not have taken my car here.  But, I was 2 hours away from home when my Sedona was leaking coolant.

If you are looking for someone to repair your car, I suggest avoiding this place.  Maybe take it to a dealership and ask them if they can give you a discounted price on repairs as I did with Kia.

Input: I am saddened by the end results today.  The sales department was very professional and very helpful in getting us a loaner car as we were told that it would be 4 or more hours before our Jeep was done with service.  But THAT is an entirely different story.  


Mike Orcutt - what the heck?  You and I shared emails. You personally spoke to my husband - yet the Jeep is still NOT fixed the way we wanted it and the way you promised it would be.  

We do appreciate that the parking brake was fixed.  We do appreciate the transmission fluid being added.  We do appreciate the thought of rotating the tires.  But I have a few questions:

Why after being there for 2 hours were we told it would be another 3-1/2 to 4 hours before Jeep would be ready as they had to disassemble part of it to look at transmission (we asked that it be looked at since it was difficult to put in reverse).  Do you remember that conversation?  We were offered a loaner car since told it would be 3-4 more hours for repairs to be done.  We got loaner car and within 45 minutes we were called by Wes saying the Jeep was ready for pickup?  Huh?  When Wes called me back after I had to call you he stated that they could not look at the transmission today as they do not have a transmission repair person on the weekends?  Then why the heck were we told it would take another 3-4 hours to have it looked at and fixed?   We would not have asked for a loaner if it were only another 45 minutes to wait.  And why were we NOT told this when we asked them to look at the transmission when we brought it in?  

Here is where it gets serious...  

After they rotate tires, do they balance the tires?  Do they check the tires?  The answer is no.    Please tell me why on the way home today I had to pull off the highway and check the tires as every time I apply the brakes the Jeep pulls harshly to the right?  And why does the front end shake when I hit 50 MPH?  It has never done this before.  

It took me an hour to get home as I had to exit the highway and use side streets to get home in fear of losing a tire or not being able to control the Jeep over 50 MPH due to the horrific shake and shimmy?  Would you want your family to drive something like this?  Would you drive a vehicle like that?  NO?  Then why should I?  I thought about turning around and bringing Jeep back to y'all to fix but figured your would only mess it up more and I do not trust your staff at all to do anything right.  

We had plans on going out to meet friends Saturday night.  DId we go?  NO!  WHY?  We were afraid to drive the Jeep.  

We will be taking the Jeep somewhere else for the 5 tires we need.  We will be taking the Jeep somewhere else for the transmission that we EXPLICITLY told them to look at --- and all we got was fluid.  Well, I guess that is better than nothing. 

I am truly disappointed in our return trip today especially since you and I had emailed each other and even more so since you spoke personally to my husband.   Yes, I believe in maintenance on vehicles and have a passion for keeping our only vehicle in good running condition - we kind of need it to get to work.  

One recommendation - get your staff either hearing aides or teach them to LISTEN to the customer when we come in with concerns.  Not just hear us, but LISTEN to us. 

So, yes, another whole Saturday, Saturday night and now Sunday shot to hell!  Due to your staff NOT doing their job the right way yet a second time.  

What can you tell me you will be doing to fix this?

Remember, I work for an international company and deal daily with customer care all day long.  I can read and smell customer care poop an ocean away.  LITERALLY.  Right now, I am smelling cow poop from Landmark Service Department.  Maybe take a lesson from Sales Department on professionalism and listening skills? 

Hope you have a wonderful rest of the day and hoping that you serve other customers a whole lot better than you did us.  

Nuf said.

Annie Watson
