Input: I haven't written a one star hotel review in my life. I consider myself a positive reviewer in general. But I swear to you my stay at the Disney Swan was more a prison sentence than a holiday.

Check in: They did not have the room I had reserved. I was put in an overflow room on a floor that stunk of mildew and no daylight. They eventually moved me the next day to the room I reserved facing the boardwalk.

Room: My room was covered in mold, and anything with metal fittings was rusting. Gross would be describing it kindly. When I called and asked to be moved to a different room the front desk acted like I should have been grateful to even have a room because they were overbooked. I asked about being moved to a different hotel and they said that it was not an option. When I escalated the manager (whom I spoke to more often than I've ever spoken to any hotel manager in my life) offered me a $75 credit which I could not care less about because I'm staying here for work and my company is picking up the tab. I explained that it was worth more to my company for me to be well rested and healthy than to save that money on my room. She said that she would look into it and never got back to me.

Starting on my second day they started doing construction with power tools on the room directly above me because, as I learned later, their balcony had broken. Once again, a call to the front desk yielded nothing and the manager came back with her $75 credit offer, but she said they couldn't stop the maintenance people and if I would like to leave my room for a few hours they should be done when I got back. This is where I started to feel like a prisoner. They won't swap my room, they won't move me to a different hotel, and I can't leave because I have a presentation due in a couple of hours.


Staff: I don't know if this is where Disney puts its rejected greeters or what but nobody here is nice.I see a lot of reviews referring to nice staff, I find that to be the exception rather than the rule. Every time I talk to anyone they act like I'm bothering them.

Awful. If you got a great deal and you're here for Disney parks then it's probably fine because you won't be spending much time in your room, though I worry about your kids' health with all this mold and mildew. Make sure your kids are up to date on their tetanus shots.

I am a priest and was on my way to Worcester for a funeral of a family member when I had a problem with my car and called someone to come get me. I told them to meet me at the Walgreen's parking lot because it's a place we both know and do business. My intention was to leave my car safely in the parking lot for a couple of hours until I could travel to Worcester, deliver the eulogy and return. By the time my ride arrived, it was beginning to get a little on the late side, but I felt getting the manager's permission to park in a corner of his lot would be the right thing to do, so I went in, asked for a manager, was directed to a young lady to whom I told my story and the urgency which I was now beginning to feel to get on the road. She told me she would have to speak to a store manager and left to do just that. A few minutes later she returned and told me that the manager had denied my request and that under no circumstances could I park in the parking lot for a couple of hours. I was devastated not only by the lack of empathy but also by the fact that the manager was not even courteous enough to come see me in person.  Needless to say I had to waste more precious time finding another place to park and ended up arriving late for the funeral. Because of this incident and the callousness demonstrated by the manager in an establishment where customer relations are so important, I will be switching my business to CVS.

Input: I first signed my lease when Alta At the Estate was in charge of the property in 2014. They were an amazing company that put the comfort and safety of their residents first. Ultimately, since Bell Watertown has taken over there have been continuous short comings. This should be abundantly clear by the number of staff that has gone in and out of the leasing office over the course of their time here-not to mention the maintenance man that was physically removed on the property by the other maintenance man in front of residents. 

Maintenance requests are consistently not addressed, even after one month, and a variety of calls to the office. This includes requests to fix the washer and dryer that is included in the rent. I initially called on December 23rd and have yet to hear (January 26th) back from a member of the maintenance staff. In addition, the other requests made includes safety orders like changing a filter and checking the stove after 7 years. Furthermore, there is mold. 

The biggest issue, however, is not the appearance or upkeep of the property, but the management team both locally and globally. The lack of response, and clear lack of respectful and kind communication does not match the price tag to live here. Further, I was threatened by another resident in the gym, and asked the management staff to address this. Rather than addressing it, apologizing for not coming down the hall into the gym when contacted about it, or even showing any semblance of empathy or compassion, I was answered with a letter from a lawyer. The letter stated that I made an accusation that is completely false, and there is no basis to back this up. In addition, instead of taking this as an opportunity to reassure a resident of their safety, it was used to twist my words, accused me of things I did not do, and tell me to incur unnecessary legal costs as a result of poor management.

Ultimately, as I have over the past 7 years, I will likely stay solely because of the convenience factor and that this is my home and has been since 2014. However, I know that by deciding to re-sign with Bell Watertown, I will ultimately be charged hundreds of dollars more than newer residents and continue to receive zero updates or maintenance checks in my apartment as new residents do. If you think loyalty is appreciated here, I urge you to note that it is punished instead. If you are looking for an apartment complex that treats you with respect and dignity, please do yourself a favor and continue looking.

Input: I purchased a Groupon for a dolphin/manatee tour in July 2014. My Groupon ended up being about $40.00 for 2 people. I was a little thrown off by the additional charge of $3.00 to park on their grassy patch upon arrival, but at that point I didn't have a choice. The tour was 2 hours long, but in reality, it took about 20 minutes to get to the island and back, so you had just over an hour on the island. As well, they throw in an additional surcharge of $7.20 for gas. Nice. And no water is provided on the boat for guests, so be prepared to bring your own.
The web-site indicates that the island is 'remote'; however, the island sits right next to highway 528, so for the more adventurous, you could park your own car on the side of the road and paddle over with a canoe or kayak. The island is also situated next to a bridge, so boats are frequent passerbys. 
We were fortunate however, to see a couple of manatees in the distance and 1 dolphin. The island itself is small and nice, but it dismisses the rural field as you are near boat and street traffic. In fact, in the distance you see all of the Disney cruise ships, which may be nice for some folks to see. 
What bothered me most though, is that it was expected that you tip the captains. I used to be a tour guide, so I understand and respect the idea of tipping and always do that. On the confirmation email by the company, they expect you to tip on the 'full' amount of the tour, not the groupon amount. For me, I was expected to tip $18.00. I almost choked. It was expected that I pay a captain $18.00 for driving me 20 minutes to the 'island', leaving me there with a tour guide on the island, and then they pick us up later and drive us back. Granted, the captains provide us with a bit of information, but they certainly did not earn an additional $18.00, on top of the costs snuck in by the company. In fact, if anyone deserved a tip it was the tour guide on the island who actually spent time with us and gave us information on the manatees and their habitat. 
Overall, I felt that I was mid-led and the company demanded more money from their custumers than they were upfront about.
I would not recommend this company to anyone.

Input: First off, in full disclosure; I'm not a prolific Yelp reviewer. In fact, I only take the time out of my day to review a business that demonstrates itself to be the worst of the worst. I do this solely out of a sense of civic responsibility; as a believer in providing "social justice". 

Using choice adjectives to describe this business would undoubtedly make even the Yelp moderators blush; so let us instead use a litany of more civilized adjectives to describe this business: pernicious, unscrupulous, dastardly. In other words; you would have better luck getting an honest deal out of a plaid leisure suit wearing used Cadillac salesman named, "Four fingers Larry".  

A casual glance through the reviews should be a sufficient cautionary tale, but for those who require a flashing neon warning sign, consider this: Why would ANY company make it compensatory to sign a NON-DISPARAGEMENT AGREEMENT prohibiting clients from making disparaging remarks/statements? Ask yourself, "self, why would a company have such a clause? Is it because they prize their sterling reputation so much as to ensure it's safe guard?" . . . perhaps. And perhaps Donald Trump is a certified genius. 

Here is just a few of the ways 1836 Property Management will delight in bending you over and frivolously extracting your cash to maximize their profit:
1. Overcharge you for sloppy maintenance
2. Charge you for services they did not provide
3. Attempt to sell you services you don't need at inflated prices
4. Provide canned, default answers to your questions
5. Pit tenants against owners by providing half truths to both sides

1836 Property Management should expand into other like minded businesses of ill-repute to take their exploitative practices to the next level. Perhaps adding a senior citizens caretaker firm, time-share sales, and telemarketing services could round out the portfolio. 1836 Property Management isn't owned by Martin Shkreli, but if he knew about it, he'd be proud!

Input: I think I got pranked... I drove way out of the way to try this place because the photos looked fantastic. I ordered the "house" noodle bowl , a skewer and a tea egg. The tea egg was good, you could really appreciate the flavors infused from whatever tea was used to marinate the egg. Ok that was the good part... and then less good was the skewer... it was cooked well and overall wasn't offensive but it walked the line as it was so caked with salt and other seasonings that I could barely identify it as a piece of meat at all. ... and then... the comedic "piece de resistance"... the noodle bowl I was so excited for.
This noodle bowl was literally nearly indistinguishable from a can of Campbell's canned beef and vegetable soups. It was full of overcooked  potatoes, gelatinous carrots, grey green beans and peas just like your favorite lunch you ate when you were five years old. It tastes like a can of soup and a few squirts of Sri racha. .. but the "hand pulled" noodles were great, right? Well, maybe at some point they were noodles but what was served to me was almost mush, they had been over cooked or perhaps sitting in water for too long... not sure but they tasted like... well like the noodles from a can of soup. 
Then it occurred to me- maybe this is a play in the classic childhood bowl of soup meant to tug on the nostalgic heart strings of a weary traveler like myself... nope- I looked on the restaurants website and the photos of the dish looks very different.
Something went wrong here, very wrong. Don't risk it and certainly don't make the mistake of going out of your way to try what sounds like an exciting Chinese style dining experience- it wasn't even a dining experience for me because I couldn't barely finish 10% of the dish before I threw it in a bus box.

Input: I wish I could give this place negative 10 stars. My recent experience has left me completely disheartened, not for the horrendous service of this establishment alone, but for the general authority bouncers, managers and owners believe they have over their patrons. This review can pertain to both men and women, but as a woman who was accused of having a fake I.D., separated from my group of friends and dragged out by a man double my height and width, I am especially writing this in the hopes that someone else will see it and it won't happen to them. 

I was allowed in at the door with this supposed "fake I.D.", paid the $5 cover, and bought a round of drinks for my friends with my credit card. They held on to my I.D. at the bar, and when I went to close out my tab, the bartender immediately got the bouncer. This man held me by my arm and my back and I was not allowed to tell my group of friends. He pushed me through the crowd, and when I reached the door the manager, a squat, gray haired man, took my I.D. like it was trash and put it in his pocket. I showed him my passport, and he informed me that both my license and my passport were "the fakest ones he's ever seen". They did not call the police. They did not have any procedure. They simply wanted to victimize me, as I'm sure they have done and will continue to do. After 45 minutes, during which time my friends were involved and the police were called (by me, not the establishment), another bouncer came out with a stack of I.D.s and shuffled through them to return mine.

 The problem here is this: when I contacted the Operations Manager, he told me that they have no real procedure. They pick and choose whose I.D.'s they confiscate. They do not notify the police. They do not give the "fakes" to the police. They "throw them in the trash the next morning". I'm hearing through other people that they sell these I.D.'s. The Operations Manager has since refused to return my calls and no action has been taken against the bouncer. They gave me no explanation of why they pushed me out of the place, or why they selected my my I.D. as a fake, but I suspect it was because they supposed I was vulnerable - a woman "alone" closing out her tab. Easy target. Luckily, I am not one to play the part of victim, but I wanted to write this review as a lesson, a warning to all.

Input: I'm relatively new to Yelp and I am trying to build up my reviews, so after numerous trips to Kickass I feel compelled to put my constant disappointment out there.  

I'm really not one to bash places, ESPECIALLY tasty dessert places. I mean, we're talking about cupcakes here.  Something simple, something trendy, something that is suppose to make you happy.  Kickass has a cool name, is in a great location, and has great SOUNDING cupcakes, yet they continue to disappoint me!  I've gone back several times because I didn't want to give up hope on them, but I gotta break down and say it.  This place kinda sucks. 

First off, I've met the owner several times and she always has a puss on her face and acts like she's doing you a favor by letting you buy her dry, bland cupcakes for, what are they now? Like $3 a piece?  She's always had an attitude every time I have gone in and inquired about the some of the more ambiguous sounding flavors.  The flavors always look and sound cool, but the cupcakes are tiny and the flavor just doesn't deliver.  I will say that the frosting is usually pretty good, but the cake itself?  Meh.  

Since a new cupcake joint is pretty much opening up every day, I would think they would step up their game. I also think it would be wise to not be all snarky about the fact that the majority of the public thinks your business kind of stinks.  I'd rather endure the traffic and bad parking in Harvard Sq and go to Sweet any day of the week, or get a basic, old fashioned, but moist and tasty cupcake at Lyndell's right up the street for half the price.  Kickass? More like Blows Chunks.

1st - the cocktails are GREAT! - a big bowl with long straws what could be bad about that?
The menu for dinner was a four course price fixed dinner

the app was a teriyaki steak tip on french break- this was the best thing we had all night- the steak was tender and seasoned correctly and done to the correct temp

Dinner- was choice of Wood fired angus beef tender long on smoked oven peking chicken-

Input: They say to never judge a book by it's cover. So given that adage, I ignored the fact that New Mandarin is located in the same strip mall as a thrift store, Family Dollar, and pawn shop and gave this place a try. In fact, I gave this place several tries. Ladies and gentlemen...some books should be judged by their cover.

First off, the ambiance. It's dark in there. And I'm not talking "sexy" dark, I'm talking "weird maybe I shouldn't sit down and eat in here because something un-sexy may happen to me" dark. So the majority of the time I just ordered my stuff to go. Next, the customer service. They aren't rude, but they're definitely not friendly. At first I just chalked this up to them being busy. But then I went in there when they weren't busy and got the same treatment. Basically, a "gimme your money, here's your food, now get the hell out" vibe. Finally, the food. The flavoring isn't bad at all and is just as suitable a gut-filler as any other Austin Chinese restaurant. However, when I'm presented with a plate overflowing with fried rice, I expect to find more than four tiny shrimp and two tiny packets of soy sauce. 

So my suggestion is that if you find yourself literally dying of hunger and can't possibly crawl across the street to McDonald's without getting hit by cars, then visit this place. Otherwise, I'd say stay clear of this place.

Input: First of all, anyone that is giving this place a good review most likely has no idea how much unnecessary money they are being cheated out of.

My significant other and I are moving to a foreign country with our cat, and specifically called ahead of time to make sure that VCA could fill out the paperwork and perform the necessary tests on our cat. We informed them of our travel dates and they said they were able to do everything we needed and to come on in.

We went to Lori Feldman, who had some good reviews, but as soon as we started talking with her she told us the paperwork had to be filled in within 10 days of our flight. So, okay, that was the main reason we came, and this stipulation was NOT mentioned by the front office, but she assured us that she could still complete the necessary tests.

Lori then told us that Nietzche (our cat) had a heart murmur, which was very upsetting to hear. She recommended we come in for a $500 EKG the next week to "see if he could fly or not". Because we are not millionaires, we decided to get a second opinion before spending another $500.

Fast forward a few weeks to my significant other taking Nietzche to her family vet in Miami. Imagine her surprise to find out that they have to redo the $300 worth of tests because THOSE also need to be done within 10 days of our flight.  I wish Lori Feldman had filled us in on that before subjecting Nietzche to what sounded like some very painful tests (based on his yowling from the next room).

Oh, and they also couldn't hear any signs of a heart murmur after carefully examining him twice.  As we suspected, that $500 EKG would have been nothing more than a waste of our already meager funds.

Thank you, Lori Feldman, for attempting to weasel $800 (and successfully weaseling $300) from a young couple who just want to travel safely with their cat. 

I am also VERY attached to this cat and almost cried when I was told he may have a heart murmur. I hope she can sleep at night.

In the meantime, I would recommend that anyone who values their pet and their financial stability stay far away from this profitable clinic, and find a place that actually cares about the health of their patients.

Input: We were there last Sunday (4/26/15) celebrating our anniversary. We had already been there once for Sunday brunch and we decided to give it another try, since the first experience had not been good.

We got there before 9 am and got in line. We asked if it was possible to sit downstairs at the bar and we were informed to we could just go inside (instead of waiting for a table), since the bar was apparently empty.
Yes - it was "apparently" empty. There were around 5 or 6 employees congregating at the bar downstairs. And the presence of customers did not intimidate them at all. From the time we got there (9am) until the time we left (10:30am), there were still a few of them laughing out loudly, as if that was not their workplace, but their living room, instead. 

We went upstairs to get some food and suddenly there is a waitress chastising us - in front of everybody else - because, apparently, we could not have started serving our plates from the specific table where we were. We should get in line, in front of the other table, and then move to the other tables from there. 

First of all, there is no indication/signal or anything whatsoever to inform the customers about where the line is supposed to start or from what table we are supposed to serve our plates from.
And the thing is: we wanted the specific food which was on the specific table where we went. And there was absolutely nobody else at that table. Which means: we were not cutting the line in front of anyone else. If there was a line for that specific table, we would have followed it.

Now: why on earth would I have to get in line at - what was supposed to be - the "main table" or the "starting table", since what we wanted was on the other table?

We are not to be blamed for the fact that the space is not well divided and well organized, and they allow the place to get so packed that you can hardly move around.

It was an extremely unpleasant situation and the tone that she used was extremely rude. I tried to explain to her why we were serving from the other table, but she just walked away.

Apart from the "incident with the waitress" and the "congregation of employees at the bar", the amount of people allowed inside while they wait for a table is ridiculous. While we were eating there were at least 3 different groups standing close by and staring at us in order to see when we were leaving, so that they could have our seats. It is uncomfortable, to say the least. And it is also a sign of mismanagement, just like having untrained staff.

Needless to say: We will not be returning. The experience starts with good service. And they lack it.

Input: Sigh...I hate it when I really want to enjoy a night out of dining with friends, and the restaurant we choose seemingly does not want this to happen.  

A friend of mine recently moved to Quincy, and my man and I decided to go visit him, and dine at Fuji 1546, because we had all stopped in there once before, and thought it seemed cool.  sigh...

To me, Fuji is the antithesis of what a good sushi restaurant should be.  Most importantly, the ambiance is way off.  I think of sushi being a peaceful experience, if somewhat exotic at times.   Fuji was loud and strange on a Friday night, full of south shore dudes who may or may not have gone to my high school... with large flat screen TVs showing the Red Sox game.  The actual interior design was cool and modern, but this place has a pretty busy bar scene, and the whole thing just didn't sit right with me.

After waiting quite a while longer than expected for a table (thanks to the GIANT theatre-sized Red Sox-showing plasma screen in the dining room!?!?!) we finally were seated and ordered up a grand amount of apps, sushi, and a couple of entrees...which was not without debacle.  My husband ordered an acid-cooked NY strip steak entree, which our clueless waitress had no idea was on the menu, and kept trying to confirm as the filet mignon entree, which was much more expensive.  After showing her the menu to confirm that the dish existed, we thought things were fine.  Then another waitress came over to tell my husband that they were out of that, but that there was filet mignon...then walked away without giving him a menu.  When we flagged down our waitress again, my man grabbed a menu and ordered some pork dish...and we thought that was the end of it...until our freaking waitress came back AGAIN to ask my husband if he wanted the filet mignon!?!?!?  Maddening.

Long story short, the waitstaff was inattentive and clueless and our sushi and entrees ended up coming out so far apart from each other that all of us were done eating when my husband's food finally came out (which by the way was nasty and gristly, and cooked completely to death).  Also, did I mention that the menu here offers such yucky offerings as sushi hand rolls containing ingredients like mozzarella cheese, bacon, and hamburger...ack!   Cheese and sushi don't mix...at least not in my mouth.

To be fair tho, I should mention that the tetaki tuna was delicious (the only star i'm awarding goes to that), and my lemongrass chicken wasn't too bad...a bit bland but edible.

Input: This is a place located in the middle of Atlanta. I heard that this place has a reputation of being a chef's restaurant. The location is open late, and it is a very intimate place. I found the place very crowded and hard to maneuver around. Additionally, a lot of the food is over priced and quite unhealthy for the heart. 

I had the pleasure of eating at this place multiple times, and I must say that the experiences were not consistent. 

The Pork Buns was too sweet for me. Most importantly, very greasy and fattening. The flavors were not mixed well together because it contained too sweet and too salty. Additionally, the greased buns did not help it go down the throat easily. 

The Bread Company Soft Pretzel was your typical pretzel, but over drenched with salt and grease. After consuming the pretzel, it left me wanting coke to wash down the salt and great out of my mouth and tongue. 

Cornmeal Fried Oysters were terrible idea because I should have known that if the restaurant is going to grease and fatten everything the place serves, the restaurant will take a full advantage with a fried food. 

Farm Egg and Carbonara pasta was actually filling for a small dish, and it was very good. The carbonara sauce contained a lot of cheese and butter, and it was very easy to spot the sauce's rich flavor and fat after the first bite. 

Bacon Caramel Apple was too sweet and greasy for me. It's more unhealthy than the movie theater popcorn. Instead of the butter the theater popcorn uses, this popcorn is covered with bacon fat. 

The Daily Raw Oysters were ok. It's not the most fresh tasting oysters, I was able to spot the taste and the smell of "sea." Real fresh oysters are not supposed to have that smell or taste of sea, but these did. 

Lastly, the almighty burger that the restaurant serves late nights for limited time and supply. Not worth the wait, money, time, and stomach. If you want a good burger, then try Bocado. I feel that Ronald had a better idea about burgers in McDonald's than these Holeman and Finch Burgers. The pickles in these burgers were so sweet that it overwhelmed the burger itself. Additionally, the bun were covered with grease, and the patty might as well been lard. The burger was flavorless and the fries that came with it was wet with oil. When I took a first bite, I felt as if a ball of grease was going down my throat. The patty was moist, but in a wrong way. It was so oily and fattening, that it had to be "moist." Making it "limited" raises the hype about the burgers, but the burger was very disappointing. I felt like I wanted to clean out my arteries after consuming this burger. Bottom line, this burger is tasteless, greasy, and too sweet. 

Overall, I wouldn't go back to this place unless I have to. The restaurant is very cramped, and the food is greasier than Varsity burgers put together with a fat kid's  skin. I find the place completely overpriced and over hyped. Additionally, the flavors of every dish is overpowered by the wrong ingredients. Either the chef has lost a lot of his or her taste buds due too much smoking and drinking or he or she just loves overpowering every dish with random ingredients that throw the entire dish off. 

Don't take your hot dates here because you're going to be wasting your money.

Input: This review is for the new Reflections location on W. Morse Blvd. in Winter Park. The receptionist at their original location is super friendly, so I'm not sure what happened here.

I arrived for my 8:30 appointment at 8:15, so I'd have time to complete new patient paperwork. The front doors were locked, so I just waited outside for someone to arrive--I didn't knock, look into the windows or try to get anyone's attention. An older lady with short blonde hair and glasses--clearly annoyed and talking on her phone--threw open the door and accusingly asked me when my appointment was. By this time, it was about 8:20--a perfectly reasonable time to arrive for an 8:30 appointment--but she was visually annoyed and pointed for me to go upstairs. No greeting or acknowledgement, whatsoever. She didn't even stop talking on her phone to tell me where to go. 

Tip: Don't schedule 8:30 appointments if your staff can't arrive early enough. 

My wait time was short (during which I completed my new patient paperwork), but my appointment was shorter. I went to have some moles and a small scar checked out. The PA looked at them for about 30 seconds, then went on to recommend products for acne--which was not the purpose of my appointment. She spent the next several minutes up-selling prescriptions and products, taking no time to 1.) ask about my skin and its sensitivity, 2.) explain how these products worked or 3.) find out which products I was already using. The entire appointment was maybe five minutes long.

Finally, when I went to checkout, the receptionist was curt and told me someone else would take my payment, like wanting to pay was a total inconvenience to her. 

The only person who was actually pleasant in the office was the nurse who brought me into the exam room. 

TL;DR: I paid $75 to deal with rude staff members and listen to product pitches. Go here for zero help and a bunch of products you don't want.

Input: I went through the drive-through on 6/3/20 and ordered a torta with some ingredients removed. When I got home, the torta was made completely unlike what I ordered even though the order was correct on the receipt. I called the restaurant and asked to speak to a manager and a young woman came on the phone named Angela R. She confirmed she was the manager. I explained what happened and said that it had taken a really long time to go through the drive through and I was tired and wasn't coming back to get a new order and asked for a refund. She was very nice and even offered to refund me AND give me another torta free which I said was not necessary as mistakes happen. She got my receipt number and confirmed she'd refund me and I should see it within 3 days. On 6/12/20 I still hadn't gotten the refund so I called them back and was told she was not working but said I could talk to the manager. 

The manager, Mario, came on the line and after explaining why I was calling, he proceeded to give me quite a hassle, why was I calling 9 days later, Angela is not the manager only a cashier, etc. I had to repeat the same thing over and over for several minutes and finally I asked him if he was going to give me the refund I was promised and he said he would be but only for one order. I kept saying I wasn't asking for anything else, only what I had paid for but didn't receive. I'm sure there was a language barrier because he was obviously struggling to repeat back what I was saying and that didn't bother me. What did was his accusatory tone and his insinuations that I was lying about talking to Angela because she's not a manager. 

After 15 minutes of his rude customer service, he said he would refund me and I should see it on my card in 2 days. I've already been told this by a much nicer employee than him, and given his tone and rude behavior, I don't have a lot of confidence he will actually refund me. 

I was going to also tell him about my experience on Sunday, 6/7/20, when I ordered the same item again, a torta with no guacamole or mayo. Again I got home but this time the torta I ordered which should have had carne asada, cheese, refried beans, lettuce and pico de gallo, only had a very small lump of steak and some grated cheese. There was a lot of bread that had no meat at all and the bread had been squished down to 1/16 of an inch. My friend who ordered a surf and turf burrito (and this was his first time there) got hardly any steak or shrimp. He was not impressed. 

Last week I called in an order at 10:00 a.m. from work for me and two coworkers and explained that I needed to pick up the food right at 12 noon as we only had 30 minutes for lunch. When I arrived at noon, the order wasn't even started. I asked why and the same manager, Mario, came out and told me it was because I didn't pay in advance. The woman who took my order didn't tell me that or ask for payment. When I told him this, he acted like he didn't believe me. So of course I was late getting back with the food and my coworkers and I couldn't eat our lunch because we had to get back on the phone. Of the 5 times I've ordered there in the last month, every order had something wrong with it. Twice I've had to deal with the manager and both times it was a negative experience. 

But the experience on the phone with Mario, the manager tonight, sealed the deal. I am never going to spend my money there again because there's no consistency with the food, they make lots of order mistakes, and then the manager is rude and hassles you when you tell him you didn't get what you paid for. Buyer beware, this is not a restaurant that cares about its customers.

I asked if it had keyless entry when I saw that there was only one key. "Of course it does, the extra keys and key fobs are locked in another room and we can't access them until Monday. Day after getting home the engine light comes on. I call Merced, he basically tells me it's not their problem. I ask about the spare keys and key fobs and seat belt, "they will be mailed soon". A week later, just after Christmas, we are surprised to find that $136 was taken from our account which caused a total of $252 in over drafts. Merced, the finance mgr, never gave us a heads up that out trade in payoff was$136 more. Merry Christmas to us.... yet, we still made the $250 payment on the 10th of January as the first half of the $500 cash down we got manipulated into promising. On time. Like we agreed. Of course we got the whole song and dance routine of "we aren't making any money off of this truck, the cash down makes us break even"  pppbbbbbbbb, whatever.... I call yesterday to ask about my key, key fobs, and seat belt, asking to talk to a manager. They transfer me to Merced. I ask if I can speak to a different manager or the owner and he raises his voice and tells me to talk to him or never call them again and promptly hangs up on me. I text our salesman asking about the spare keys and keyless entry fobs and he texts back that there aren't any. Sorry. I go to a local Ford dealership and they investigate, only to find that the truck didn't come with a keyless entry module. But they can order me one. Also, they can make me a spare key but it's $99.95! So now we have almost a $300/mo  payment on a $23,000 truck that has the engine light on, a ripped seatbelt, only one key, and no keyless entry! Input: Ever since Norm's Garden closed in May of 2015, I have been in search of a comparable  Chinese restaurant.  Sadly, so far, no luck!  Canton Phoenix was my latest try and unfortunately, it wasn't a hit. 

I ordered several lunch combinations (Mongolian Beef, General Tso's Chicken, Dry Sauteed Green Beans and L6, which included BBQ Pork, Sweet and Sour Chicken, Fried Rice and Sub Gum Chicken Chow Mein) so we could try a variety of items.  I also ordered a separate order of BBQ pork fried rice and an order of MaFa chicken.  Three of the lunch combos came with a spring roll.  Ugh, soft, squishy and not good at all.  The best of the three combos was the Mongolian Beef.  It was tasty, but the beef was a bit chewy.  The General Tso's chicken was super sweet and had no spice whatsoever.  That was disappointing.  The Dry Sauteed Green Beans had an odd flavor, almost like soap. Ick, really bad!  The BBQ pork and the Sweet and Sour Chicken in the L6 combo were good, the BBQ pork was actually the best item ordered, but there wasn't much of it.  The Sub Gum Chicken Chow Mein tasted like sesame oil .... just sesame oil, there was no flavor of the vegetables or the chicken, and the chicken was rubbery and weird looking.  One bite of that and it went in the garbage, along with the soggy spring rolls and the green beans.  Total waste of money! 

The MaFa chicken had potential, but it was so greasy that I had to roll it in paper towels to draw the grease out before tasting it.  Also, they line the bottom of a styrofoam container with slimy, stringy lettuce that then sticks to the pieces of deep-fried chicken.  Gross!  

The fried rice that came with the three combos was brown and flavorless ... in the garbage it all went!  The separate order of BBQ pork fried rice was a little better, but not a whole lot.  

Another thing that turned me off is the to go containers are all plastic or styrofoam.  Putting hot food into plastic containers is nasty.  Not a Chinese takeout box in sight!  Everything was put in a plastic container, including the whole order of BBQ pork fried rice, and the deep-fried MaFa chicken was in a styrofoam container.  Not good.  

Overall, very disappointing experience and a lot of money wasted since much of the food ended up in the garbage.  I certainly won't go back to Canton Phoenix, but I will continue my search for some decent Chinese food in the local area.  Norm's Garden, you are missed!!

Input: I have had chronic pain in my hand and wrist which has, in the past, resulted in surgery to remove a ganglion cyst in the center of my palm. The pain returned and it seemed like I would need to have surgery again, so I scheduled an appointment with Dr. Gadaria. At the time I scheduled the appointment I was in the very beginning of a pregnancy. I also had really awful insurance with a very high deductible- so basically everything was out of pocket. When I called to schedule the appointment I asked the scheduler if it mattered that I was pregnant. I didn't want to spend the money on seeing the doctor if the doctor was unwilling to operate on a pregnant lady.  The scheduler said she couldn't tell me whether or not Dr. Gadaria would operate on a pregnant lady and that I needed to come in and talk to him about it. So, I went in and immediately asked Dr. Gadaria if he would operate on me despite me being pregnant. He said that he has blanket policy of not operating on pregnant women except in life threatening situations. That question was the extent of my appointment. He couldn't help me. I didn't understand why this policy could not have been communicated to me by the front desk before my appointment. As I leave, I am asked to pay $200! I paid it but was so upset that I was in tears by the time I reached the elevator. I went back in and explained to the office manager that I really couldn't afford to pay $200 to ask a question to a doctor that could have been answered by the scheduler over the phone and that I would never have scheduled with Dr. Gadaria in the first place had I known he couldn't help me due to my pregnancy. The office manager was clearly annoyed, unsympathetic and unwilling to refund me the $200. I then asked to speak directly to Dr. Gadaria about it. He was far more graceful and understanding about it and told the office manager to refund my money. I was extremely grateful but the office manager went about angrily processing the refund all the while making it very apparent that she despised me for even asking. 

Fast forward a year later. I have given birth and finished nursing and the pain has intensified. I am now in a condition to have surgery and my insurance is now much better. I call Dr. Gadaria's office because he has the best ratings and because I remembered how he did right by me even though his office manager didn't want to. I try to schedule an appointment and after giving my name to the scheduler she puts me on hold. The office manager then picks up the phone and angrily says, "you came here last year and there was a problem. The doctor does not wish to see you as a patient" and then hangs up.

Input: The first thing you should know is this is not an British Pub.  This is an American mall version of an British Pub.  So it is bigger, louder, dumber and (in its defense) a lot cleaner than any version it sets out to emulate.  As others have mentioned, it is kind of like a Disney amusement park version of an British Pub.  Various English Premier League logos and flags are displayed prominently, as are the logos of british and european beers and whiskeys.  Perhaps more so than you would see in the real version.  The servers all wear kilts--which is actually Scottish (and, to a lesser extent, Irish) traditional dress.  So, a muddled message in execution of concept.

On the other hand, they have a lot of modern, customer friendly, conveniences like flat screen tv's and wifi.  They even have tables with built in beer taps--an interesting, but potentially disastrous idea given that most of the patrons will likely try to drive home from this suburban location.

All things considered though, this was a fun place to spend an evening on St. Patrick's Day weekend.  They had a couple of good bands booked and, with a boisterous, inebriated crowd, I think a good time was had by all.

Service was a little spotty, but that was probably due to the sheer volume of business they were doing on a busy weekend.  I'd be interested to see how the service is on an average day.

As others have mentioned, the Kentucky Bourbon Ale is awesome.  Give it a try if you go.

Input: I have been staying at this locations for a decade and various Hilton name changes. Obviously, it must be okay or I would not continue coming. Through out my dozen or more so stays here I have always observed a blatant abuse of extending gold member perks (free breakfast buffets) that I can no longer ignore. It's no easy task to achieve gold status , ( as a matter of fact... It took me purchasing Hilton grand vacation property in New York City to finally obtain) and I resent "handouts" to those undeserving.  As I checked in and observed the person ahead of me handed a stack of cards for their family , or the request for 6 beside me , I couldn't help but remember just a month earlier i was checking into Hilton Anaheim and explained to the clerk that our third person checking in that night was our air force daughter flying straight in from a six month Iraq deployment and couldn't Hilton please include breakfast for her .... Which I was quickly reminded "no, Hilton has a strict 2 guests per gold member breakfast daily limit" . 
Guess that doesn't apply to non-gold guests in Atlanta. It wouldn't take very much math for the owner of this location to see...... Out of 100% guests.. 90% eat breakfast for which 5% is paid in revenue??   Really don't see how restaurant stays open.
Other than favoritism for guests.... My room has always been clean, the bed is comfortable, place is quiet and parking is good. Shuttle very convenient and covers mall and good restaurants. 
Also, if you are gold or diamond , don't expect your automatic room upgrade; they also allow slumber parties in their rooms so make sure you speak up and ask if you can move if you notice a ton of kids and parents toting large coolers on the elevator.

Input: My husband saw this spot on Man V Food so of course we had to come here. We made the two hour drive down from Olympia in the pouring rain. Obviously, in this part of the country you can't let standing in the rain for 30 minutes stop you. 

We used our line time to scan the menu online and choose our flavors. The longer we waited the larger our wish list grew. We settled on a dozen donuts for the two of us.

The Maple Bar was the best donut of the bunch. The Grape Ape and Mango Tango were good too. I liked the sugar crunch and the flavor of the powders with the icing and donut. Everything with cereal on top was a disappointment since all of the cereal tasted stale. Cereal on top of the donut sounds interesting, but just doesn't work.

Keep in mind that they only accept cash so make sure to hit the ATM before visiting. I want to say that there was an ATM on site, but I wouldn't count on that. At the time I visited there was also only one table inside because most of the space is used for the line. Plan to have somewhere else to enjoy your donuts.

These aren't the best donuts you'll ever have in your life, but the donuts and the shop are unique. Would you really want to visit Portland and miss the iconic Voodoo Donuts?

Our server asked us if regular spice was okay and we agreed but our group was under the impression that it would be very spicy. We definitely did not want food that we wouldn't be able to eat. The tofu and the wings came out first. I did not detect any sort of spice in either dishes... The tofu was crispy but was kinda bland.... Wings were tasty but not spicy. A little bit of spice would have been appreciated. Fried rice had a kick to it and was good!!! The eggplant was definitely my fav dish. The chicken in it was tender and the carrots were a nice touch. We all got dessert which consisted of deep fried pineapple, banana and ice cream. Batter was great. I know some places have the Batter too thick (pastry like). The service isn't too great here and the tables were so close together that it made it very hard for our servers to come to our table. I wasn't able to try out the other dishes that were recommended on here but all in all it wasn't bad. 

Would I come back? Probably only if I was invited... I would still give it another try.

Input: July 2019

We saw a video online and we were tempted to take the drive from Boston to Texas just to try it.  We do random stuff like that so it wouldn't have been shocking had we done that.  I ended up booking a whole trip for his birthday.  I based the vacation around his wanting to try this restaurant.  

The wait is crazy long.  Its a pretty cool place and the story behind the start of the business is pretty interesting.  The food is just okay though.  The portions are kind of small.  I am assuming the wait is super long because the tables are long (seats at least 12 people per table) and there are no small ones.  My boyfriend and I went and waited over 3 hours for a table.  We were sat at this huge table.  We almost felt guilty taking up a huge table just the two of us.  They should consider seating another couple at the opposite end of the table.  

On another note, the wait staff was super nice.  They were definitely overwhelmed with how busy it was but still kept a friendly demeanor with the guests which was nice.    

What really surprised me was that they serve sliced white bread with the food.  I was under the assumption that corn bread was served with BBQ food.  According to our waitress, that is a northern thing.  So if you go, don't expect corn bread.    

We had high expectations of this after seeing the videos about it online and the photos.  It was a one and done type of place.  We are glad we went, we probably wouldn't go back.

Input: We've driven by this place countless times, but have always been skeptical about trying it because it looks like it's either part of the auto repair place or gym that it's next to. We finally looked at the menu and confirmed they can accommodate a gluten allergy and we gave it a shot.

I had the honey and chicken almond salad, which was very tasty and a good amount of food for $12. My sister had the burger and she was impressed with how well it was cooked and how good it tasted. The breadless turkey club was also good, but not particularly memorable. 

Weak beer selection - not much interesting beyond the usual subjects on tap.

Input: With TSA in Austin getting slower and slower, and the worst TSA "mall cop" experience in the Austin airport, I decided to fork out the $85 for TSA pre-check. Once approved, this is good for 5 years and allows you streamlined access through airport security at the more than 150 participating US airports.

The paperwork is all online, and once submitted, it gives you a choice between an office at ABIA and these guys to complete your appointment. All availability is posted in 15 minute increments, so it was easy to sign up for a convenient time slot. 

Upon arrival, there was no waiting. I was 10 minutes early and after showing appropriate identification and handing them the credit card I was paying with, I was walked back to one of the appointment rooms. 

It is a little impersonal and "process" oriented, but I felt like I did not get the memo. The woman taking my info was all business. She had a foreign accent and as I tried to make out her name (she never introduced herself), her name tag was hanging from her lanyard, upside down, and she shot me a stern look. I mentioned I was trying to see her name, but it is upside down. It started with a "w" but was not a common name or one I would remember. 

I was asked to have a seat, and when I set my coffee on the table, I was told to place it on the floor. (Okay) 

I was in a small office on the guest side of the desk. There was a large computer screen to my left. Screen by screen, I was asked me to verify the answers of questions (that I had already completed on-line). Then came the digital fingerprinting. FTR, if you have small hands, this is not for the faint of heart. First came my thumbs which both had to be on the scanner glass at the same time, but the barely reached the scan area. I felt like the woman was torture stretching them just to appear in the glass. She would press them down hard so the camera could capture all the grooves, but was having some issues doing this. She said if it did not work the third scan attempt, I would not be able to complete the appointment. By some act of magic, the third time was the charm and my thumbs feel a quarter inch longer (not cool). Then came, one hand at a time, the digital scan of 4 fingers for each hand. Again, she pressed them down on the glass hard, trying to get a good picture. I couldn't help but wonder if this was old technology, because a scan of my fingerprints at the DPS a few years ago was much more efficient and painless. 

Once my fingers were tortured, ahem, I mean scanned, they processed my credit card, handed me a receipt and told me I would receive an email with a UE ID (Universal Enrollment ID number) and could check the status on the web. She said it could take 30 days. I was escorted to the lobby and sent on my way. 

Three business days after my visit, I checked on line and I have already received my KTN (Known Traveler Number) and was informed I should receive a letter in the mail within 10 business days. The next time I fly, my TSA pre-check will allow me to bypass the long security line, keep my shoes and jacket on, and my laptop and liquids in my backpack. 

I will say that the process to get a TSA pre-check is on-line and fairly painless. The in-person interview was cold and absent any feel of human interaction. A robot might have been more suitable. The fingerprint scan was painful, bordering on torture. 

While Identogo did what they were contracted to do, they could hire people who like working with the public rather than stone faced government worker types. I did notice that they seemed to have plenty of time to take walk-ins. 

Identogo does not just do TSA pre-check services, but offer a full array of identity/background related services including live scan fingerprinting, fingerprint cards, FBI and state identity history checks, notary services, and photo services for things like passports and visas. They are a private firm designed to take a little of the bureaucracy and line standing out of the equation, and they do that. Their bedside manner leaves a lot to be desired (but that was just my experience). 

With thumbs up on the fast process and zero wait time (I was out of there in 9 minutes), but sore thumbs down on the fingerprinting and bedside manner, they get are a the only alternative in Austin to having to pay to park at ABIA for the same service. 2.5 stars, rounding to 3 (because I am nicer than they are).

Input: After driving by a million times, my sweet man-friend and I decided to head in for breakfast early on a Sunday morning.  Expecting a wait based on the reviews here on Yelp, I was pleasantly surprised to find a very short line, and we could have even sat inside if it hadn't been so nice outside.  

The biscuits are good - that is a fact.  I had the biscuit with cream and fresh fruit, and was treated to a delicious tender and flaky biscuit, unsweetened whipped cream (DELISH!) and beautiful huge marionberries.  

I had higher hopes for the grits - they were fine, I guess.  The texture was creamy, and yes, the little kick of spice was nice, but they were lacking in dimension.  They could have used a bit of extra-sharp white cheddar, in my opinion, or at least some SALT.  Totally bland, for all the hype I read about them. 

Man-friend had the Reggie DeLuxe, which looked like a heart attack on a plate.  A deeeeelicious heart attack on a plate.  I didn't try any, but he said it was pretty good.  

Stumptown Coffee:  always a fan.

Service: nothing to shout about.  I assume everyone working that morning had a raging hangover.  It seemed like it.  But hey, they were functional.

BONUS: If you get there before 10:30 am, Triple Nickel lets Pine State customers use their picnic tables out front.  Great for summer - winter? Probably not so much.

Over all, pretty okay.  I took a star off for the bland grits and blander service, and a star off for the inflated price.  Our breakfast was $20, which just seemed too high for what is essentially a one-trick pony take out joint.

My co-workers ordered the lunch boxes and some sushi. I got a side of yakitori and a tofu dish. Both were rather good and I was happy with my choices. The downside was the cost as it was a bit pricey - for lunch. Granted we figured that would be the case and considered it a splurge lunch. (Yeah, we wished we had the corporate card to charge it to!). 

The decor is fun and they have some neat light fixtures in there. There is a bit of modern starkness that does have a bit of a cold feeling. Every employee was dressed well in suits or similar. As we exited the restaurant, it was like we were royalty or something as every single person who worked at Haru said good bye to us as we walked past them to the door. It was a bit much and a little awkward.

Overall, not bad.

Input: I checked Yelp before coming out to Zab E Lee, but yelp didn't really tell me anything about the sushi. So, here we go as you can see in my pictures the sushi looks fine for the most part. With the exception of the yellowtail. The yellowtail is poorly colored, to say the least. Each piece of sushi has a very small clump of rice, which would be fantastic at just about any other sushi restaurant. However, the fish to rice ratio is way off for this establishment. As the fish Is what I would call "sub-medium Quality", the rice portion should've been larger and the fish portion should've been smaller to hide the inequities. 

The yellowtail was also rather salty and the best way I can explain the texture would be spongy. The tuna and salmon were very brightly colored and looked great, but they just didn't have great flavor. In the case of the squid, it popped like cartilage, but it didn't have any creamy textures. Plus, again the flavor wasn't really there. 

The only piece of sushi that I remotely liked was the unagi, but even it didn't have as good of flavor as I'm used to. The only consolation about the meal was that for all you see in my photos, I only spent $31 (plus tip). 

Now, you might be wondering why I gave this restaurant three stars when I'm saying that the sushi was just god-awful...

I also ordered some of their coconut soup. Remember, this is not Hey Japanese sushi restaurant. Zab E Lee is a Thai restaurant that just happens to serve sushi. The coconut soup was pretty good. My personal preference would be for a little bit less lemongrass and more chicken, but it was a delicious soup.

I will probably order from them again... Definitely not the sushi... But I will probably order some Thai food from them as it seems like they'll do that very well.

My honest recommendation to the chef to prepare the sushi is, please look for a better fish vender... Perhaps ask the people at a Happy Sumo. I would also recommend that you cut the fish a bit more thinly. Sushi Is an art form that is all about balance in beauty and flavor.

Input: We knew we'd get here eventually, since it is now the closest Ted's for us, but today was a surprise.  Sweetie had a craving for their mashed potatoes and sauteed mushrooms (and for Ray Ray's brisket, so I went on a trek...)  She used to work at a Ted's and we've been there a few times, so it's a fallback place for us, and always good.

This location just opened, and they are still working the kinks out.  Still, it was good, and I'm sure we'll be back and they'll have things together better.

It's in the "suburb" of Easton just to the east.  There is street and lot parking, though of course since it's Easton it can get pretty busy.  I snagged a spot out front, and they weren't too busy mid-afternoon on a Sunday.  It's decorated like other Ted's, with lots of wood, fairly fancy overall.  However, this one is far more bright and airy than the other Columbus locations.

Service was great, from several employees.  I sat at the bar to order our carryout.  Mashed pots and shrooms for her, trout dip and the chopped salad for me (hey, I have to eat healthy sometimes.)  The bartender asked if I wanted meat on the salad, so I said sure, bison, done medium.  I noticed the fresh lemonade jug at the bar, so had one to pass the time.  That turned into two lemonades, and one to go, because, well, it took forever.  None of that should have taken long; maybe the longest would be the bison, but still, half an hour for a to-go order?  The staff were apologetic, and offered snacks (and free refills.)  When the food came out we were missing the pots and shrooms, the whole reason for the trip.  That was swiftly corrected, and I was on my way.

The food was... a mixture of good and okay.  Sweetie loved the mashed potatoes and gravy, and the mushrooms.  I liked the trout dip.  I had expected bits of trout in a sauce, but it is chunks of trout, good trout, with a bit of sauce and seasoning.  Served with good tortilla chips, it was the star.  The lemonade was very good (though not as good as homemade.) 

 The salad... was just okay.  The salad itself was sad, and nothing like the description.  "Iceberg, roasted corn, garbanzo beans, vine-ripened tomato, green pepper, red onion, cucumber, smoked ham, basil vinaigrette."  Lots of iceberg, half a dozen chickpeas (literally,)  a couple dozen kernels of plain corn, a few small bits of tomato, no cukes, no peppers, a tiny bit of ham and a couple of slices of red onion.  And, missing the promised dressing.  The meat was another disappointment.  I figured it would be crumbled ground bison, and might add $3 to the $6 salad.  Nope, it was a separate bison patty, clearly intended for burgers, and added $9.  To a $6 salad.  I had a chance to pass when I saw the bill, and didn't, to avoid further slowdowns.  I would recommend passing on the added meat, and probably the whole salad.  Still, it was healthy, I enjoyed the trout dip, and (added to some Ray Ray's brisket) I was full.  Plus, Sweetie was happy.

So, ups and downs, to be expected for a new place.  I figure things will smooth out soon and they will join other locations with 4-5 stars.  Even with the wait and other issues, we had a good meal and will be back, to dine in or for more cravings...

Input: This place should get about 3.5 stars - it's good, but just slightly overpriced.

Menu offerings are extensive for such a small operation.  The sandwiches all sound amazing, and many of them are. Trident fries are vegetable fries that are novel, unique, and well done.  Cheesy tots are overrated, as are some of their baked goods.  Most sandwiches range from $10-12, and breakfast entrees around $8.  It shooooould be a dollar or two less per item, for what you're getting.

All in all, a good joint for those of you in Back Bay looking for a nice, easy breakfast.

Input: YVR Poutine Crawl:
Like any hokey tourist, we love to try local foods no matter how stereotypical they might be. While poutine, I believe, is more of an eastern/Montreal specialty, I'm not going to pass up gravy, fries, and cheese curds. Since our layover was from 1am to noon, we were limited in our chance to explore beyond our hotel and thus the YVR Poutine Crawl was born. Here are our rankings:

1. Canucks Bar & Grill (USA terminal/AFTER security): Above and beyond the best we had, but we figured this would be the case. They offer a classic poutine, and a version with mushrooms and bacon. We got the latter and thought the mushrooms were chewy, but the bacon was a good addition. The only bummer with this was that Canucks Bar & Grill had surly staff and they seated us RIGHT in front of constantly buzzing kitchen door despite tons of other seating. They have no Canadian beers on tap, but a bunch in bottles.

2. A&W (National terminal/BEFORE security). This was our first taste and I actually really liked it. The cheese curds were squeaky and not too melty, the gravy was good and plentiful, but the fries were a tad soggy. I thought I would like soggy fries better, but crispy actually taste better!

3. Burger King (USA terminal/AFTER security) The cheese curds were melted and the stringy gooey mess was delcious, but a pain in the rear to eat. We basically needed to use our hands to pull it apart. The crispy fries were a bonus. They do technically offer bacon for $1, but they were out.

Honorable mention: White Spot (National terminal/BEFORE security): They serve poutine, but  only once breakfast is over at 11am. 

**Note: It is VERY easy to walk between the National/USA/International terminals. The YVR airport is wonderful with tons of shops, but quite small overall.

Input: **I'm editing my review to note the following: I am not recommending you don't visit. You should! The food was fine and fresh, just not to my taste on this visit. The owners contacted me afterwards expressing concern over my dissatisfaction; customer service is second to none.  **

New World Cafe is similar to New World Deli but just doesn't have the charm of its original Hyde Park counterpart.  Between the TV tuned to CNN, the dark lighting and the beer signs I might have mistaken the place for the Boulevard Bar and Grill a few doors down if not for the extensive sandwich curation.

I ventured down to this location tonight (a Friday night) and it was relatively quiet, save for a few patrons.  My guess would be that they see a big lunch crowd and the evenings are not as popular in general.  The server at the front recommended the curried chicken salad after I learned they don't carry eggplant parm at this location and so I ordered the 1/2 sand and soup (broccoli cheese.)

What can I say?  The food was very safe.  In my head curried chicken salad is usually served with melba toast to ladies who lunch (tm) on a bed of lettuce.  The salad, not the ladies.  This was served on my choice of bread (sourdough) with crudites.   Was the sandwich bad?  No, but it was bland, sort of old-style Southern charmlike in its 'exotic' curry flavoring and remarkably underseasoned (though that may be my sinuses talking).  

I lost my appetite after eating the broccoli cheese soup - definitely not canned, but bizarre in that it was cheese soup with bigger-than-your-mouth broccoli florets - and took my sandwich to go.  I think I'll come back for the burger but I need to do it during the day time when NWC doesn't feel so much like a poorly lit sports bar.  Some candles or possibly eliminating the glowing lights of the television would go far in giving this place a modicum of the charm of the other location.

The stars go to the server and the cook, who were charming and remarkably efficient.  My soup/sam were out in two minutes - yowza.

P.S. They'll be getting wine soon, for now only domestic bottled beer (and only one local, some beer with the Austin mural logo across the front). Meh.

I liked the Roseland, and would probably go to another show there if they were hosting a band I wanted to see.  I'd give them a 3.5 if I could, but I'm gonna have to settle for a 3.  Not a bad venue, but not fantastic either.  Some upgrades could go a long way for this place.

Input: I decided to give this place a try since all the rave about vegan food. Although I'm not vegan, I've had some vegan food that was great so I was excited to try this place out. I had to take a "double-dutch approach of when I would go because some reviewers had consistently mentioned 1-3 hour wait times. I had absolutely NO interest in this so I figured after the newness wore off, I would be in the clear. I then learned that they don't open until 4 PM so that added another layer to planning. I figured that an early, weekday trip would spare me the wait. I was wrong. What added to my time was trying to find parking. I ventured out around 3:30 on a Monday and upon passing by, there was already a line forming. When I finally made it to the line, I realized that the long lines are sectioned off with dividers to prevent blocking neighboring businesses. From the time of getting in the line at 3:50 and getting my food, it was about 2 hours.  It's sort of like a catch 22. Once you've waited for 30-45 minutes, you feel defeated if you leave because now you realize that you wasted 30-45 minutes of your time which didn't include time you wasted for parking. Nevertheless, they have a rep that will periodically come outside to greet and inform customers of the burgers they will serve on that particular day. They have a limited amount of burgers that one person can order which is cool because I'm sure you'd have some people who are willing to avoid the long wait and have someone order for them.  They have this cool theme for first time "virgins" or people who's first time eating at the slutty vegan. Once inside, the service moves pretty quickly. I decided to try the Menage a Trois. All of their burgers comes with fries. There's their slutty vegan sauce they add as well. On my first bite, I was waiting for something to happen but it didn't happen. The burger wasn't bad but it wasn't worth the wait. It lacked flavor and the sauce was too spicy. The shrimp that came on the sandwich was pretty good but because I'm not a fan of spicy, I wish I would have asked for it on the side. The fries were seasoned well. At the end of the day, I came, I tried, and I probably won't return because of the wait time didn't balance out my experience with the food. Great customer service. Cool slogan/brand and they have a great marketing team. Also, they don't have indoor dining/seating options although we did see people showing up with lawn chairs.

Input: This is my go-to gym during the week.  It is conveniently located within a short drive of where I work.  Since I drive to work, I do enjoy that you can use the parking lot, starting at 5:30.  Depending on how I hit the lights coming over from work, sometimes I get there as soon as 5:20.  Most of the attendants will let me park, though it is possible you may get turned away for showing up too early.  Getting street parking, as a non-South End resident, may be tough. The gym isn't enormous, but they have figured out a way to pack everything in there without feeling like you are on top of each other.  For the size of the gym, there is a lot of cardio equipment, particularly treadmills.  

The class schedule is part of the draw for me.  If I come after work, I make sure to sign up for a class, that way you're not spending a lot of time looking for empty cardio/weight machines to use. The locker rooms are a bit on the small side, particularly when you show up at peak times, like 5:30-6:00 area.  But, magically everyone seems to find a place for their stuff. Input: I thought for a good ten minutes about whether I could give a better rating than a three. I just can't. 

The beer is solid. I like it. It's not the best beer in town but it's a nice line up especially for what this place purports to be. I would happily drink the beer again if the beer was served somewhere else. I just can't get into the venue.

Before moving on, I will say that I did not try the food but people seemed to be enjoying it. I don't know one way or the other whether the reviews criticizing the food are right or whether the ones professing adoration are right. 

Parking is a mess. There's not enough on-site parking and it's hard to find off-site parking without the risk of being towed. Once you finally steal a parking spot you have your choice of sitting at long communal benches outside or long communal benches inside. Outside is cool when it's cool outside. Inside is fine except it's also a music venue built out of steel and concrete so there's no escaping the very loud music. 

Ordering inside is relegated to the two line counter system that seems very popular these days. It's not efficient but I'm not getting bent out of shape about it. I could get a beer in reasonable time. The water is at self-serve stations which I like because it makes it easy to keep drinking water along with the beer.

The worst thing about this place is all the kids. Alright, I'm not from Austin where things are more kid friendly and I do think it's weird to bring kids to a place where people are getting drunk, spilling beers, having adult conversations, dogs are running around (which are not always friendly to noisy kids), etc. but it's not my job to parent other peoples' kids. On the other hand, it's not my job to parent other peoples' kids. The kids were everywhere with little to no supervision. Somebody else called ABGB a boozy daycare which is very accurate. The kids were running all over cutting through crowds, running into people carrying beer and racing around the servers carrying hot food. At one point some kid came down to where my wife and I were sitting and started throwing rocks at us. We couldn't even complain to the parents because there weren't any around. I can't blame the kids. There's nothing for them to do. Of course they get bored and want to run around. They're kids. 

I hate to criticize ABGB for the poor environment caused by all the kids because they neither encourage nor discourage their presence but it's also their business and they let the environment be what it is. If adults were doing the same things the kids were doing I would expect the staff to do something about it. It's no different just because these patrons happen to have their parents with them.

Input: It's a motel, not a hotel, and is one of the cheapest options if you want to stay on a Disney property.  Rather than parking right in front of the entrance the way I would at other motels I was forced to park in a parking lot while I checked in.  It confused me because there were several other vehicles who were loading/unloading in the front.  We stayed in one of The Love Bug buildings.  The color scheme wasn't soothing.  The room was modest and could use an update (such as new paint as the paint was chipped in many areas).  There was a small refrigerator in the room.   There were two small, flat pillows on each bed.  The shower did not drain properly.  Like pretty much all motels, we could hear when everyone else around us were using their showers and toilets.  It's a good option if you want to save money on lodging while at Disney and spend most of your time at the parks (rather than in the room).  The front staff was always courteous.  On the day we left a male housekeeper knocked on our door (we had the curtains open so it was obvious we were there, but we had the "Do Not Disturb" sign on the door handle).  He asked what time we were checking out.  I said we'd be out before the checkout time of 11:00 AM.  He was very persistent on questioning me as to the exact time we'd leave.  It was rude, intrusive, and annoying.  I reported this (and the shower draining issue) to the front desk staff.  Since it's on Disney property, we were able to utilize the Disney buses to get around.  The customer service at breakfast was disappointing.  When I ordered the egg white omelet the female worker sighed heavily.  I asked her if there was a problem.  She said that everyone was working those that morning.  I again asked if that was a problem (since it was a listed menu item).  She said that the eggs were sticking together.  I told her she could use regular eggs rather than egg whites (I ordered the egg white omelet because I wanted the veggies in it, not the egg whites), but she used the egg whites, which appeared to be frozen.  My roommate was able to get hot water (to make instant coffee) for free.

Input: Saturday Nite- out and about Atlanta. Purposely decided to head over to Gino's. If  you recall the place prior to Gino's was caught in a fire and destroyed. Somewhere between then and now Gino's NY Pizza  Bar resurrected from the ashes. The place is spacious.  Two parking lots but they are difficult to maneuver to the movie driver. Watch for potholes and running water with a scent.!! There is a full bar in the rear of the design with poker fans playing with chips and brown liquor. Looked pretty impressive. Noticeably cooler back there. Sitting near the front of the restaurant from the inside joy can view the outdoor patio which was not to far off from the previous design before the fire. I decided to go here because it had been years from the last time I went. Same owners/same family. 
Very hot in the inside area near the desk where you place your order. Service was a bit slow but I guess that's part of the pizza game. The a/c setting must have been on the "budget setting." It was way to HOT!! It was hotter inside that it was outside. 
A plus about eating outdoors is that there are fans on one side of the patio that blow harder than the a/c indoors. The pizza- was just basic. I would give it 2.5 stars at most. The service once we got going was 3.2 stars. Just busy I guess. The specialize in pizza slices for the person on the go. We ordered a whole pie all veggies. The sauce had a mild sweet flavor to it. Just could have been the base sauce. The crust was thin and average texture. Nothing lite and airy. Overall it was a good experience. The drinks were GOOD- although the next morning I did have a tummy ache. Lasted about 9am the next day.  Not sure what that was about because I love Pizza. The service or at least our waitress was better when things died down. I would go back for drinks and maybe try a different  option on the menu. The owners daughter was at the cashier location. I did not get her name but she was polite. I did not get a chance to review the restrooms but that will be when I go back for drinks. Coming next is the review of their neighbor Tokyo Valentino..

A friendly waiter came by and we placed our orders. I ordered the garlic shrimp with rice and sweet plantains, and my husband ordered the ropa vieja with rice and beans. Input: We love Saigon's original location on Goldenrod, and this one being newer and closer to where we stayed at this time, we decided to visit here instead. This place is huge, a stand alone building with its own parking lot.  It looks like part of the restaurant can be used for banquets, with props and karaoke machine. 

Well, it's a different chef, and somehow the food isn't quite as good as the original.  The spring roll came out way too fast and was barely warm; it probably had been sitting out.  Some of the beef in our soup was also chewy and dry.

As for the service, it certainly wasn't rude, just plain weird... I appreciate the waiter trying to be friendly and helpful, but maybe tune it down a bit.  As we were sitting down, the waiter mumbled, "we have Vietnamese beer."  He put down the menu, "Saigon beer, from Vietnam."  Then he turned away and mumbled "two Saigon beer."  It took a moment for my brain to process what he was saying and yelled after him, "no I don't want beer!!"  Okay, I am not disputing that I am a beer lover, but I am not sure what body signal I gave for ordering a beer.  (I suppose fellow Yelper Derock H. got the same server we did, just that he "ordered" the chicken soup without saying a word.) 

Then, while we were eating, the waiter returned and said, no, you have to put the basil in.  We said, yes, we did.  And he insisted that we need to put in more.  And he stood there and waited for us to put more basil in.  No, you need more.  And kept watching till we threw in a few more leaves into our bowls.

Input: This is a 3 star review but I want to start out by saying I will still go to this place... I know not all 3 star reviews convey that.  

The good:
-We showed up at 7p on a Saturday with a group of 10 and they got us a seat inside immediately.  
-Staff was super nice about our large group (birthday) and even brought plates for us to use for the cake I brought (even though I brought plates)
-Initial drink order was prompt and correct

Note: I so appreciate a wait staff that is nice to large groups.  I know we are a pain in the ass sometimes, and they serisouly were SO SO nice to us.  Very accommodating.

The less good
-Then our waiter disappeared.  Took forever to get an order in because he was no where to be found.  When we finally got our food we were starving.  Then..... gone again.  We literally ended up staying an hour longer than we intended because we simply COULD NOT FIND THE GUY.  I think they may have had him serving outside, which is not his fault. But I think we saw the guy twice in 90 minutes.  We were going to order more drinks, but it took so long in between sightings we just decided to go.
-The pizza was very meh.  Seemed under done.  Too much cheese.  May have been a fluke.  
-The check was wrong for 3 people (mind you, I completely appreciated that he split it without asking, but then it took us 15 MORE minutes to try and sort out the check situation, when we would've been happy to split it and write out amounts ourselves if necessary.

This could all be a fluke but it was a little weird.  Hence, the mixed review.  The good news is that there is plenty of seating, the staff was very nice (when you got to interact with them), and good prices on food and drinks.  Just be prepared to wait for a while for food and check.  We will definitely return to see if our experience was abnormal, I'd love to provide a positive update!
