Input: Decently priced for a theme park restaurant, suprisingly better than most places you could potentially go to here. For ~$15 you can get a shake, fries, and burger/chicken tenders/chicken sandwich/or bean burger.
Fries--well seasoned, excellent salt to fry ratio, possibly a hint of old bay seasoning?? But not in an overwhelming sense--get them, they're delicious!

Hamburger--well done, decent amount of meat. 
They have a spot for condiments: ketchup/mayo/mustard packets, napkins, and straws...however, the straws are UNWRAPPED, which I think is a health hazard, it's gross--everyone reaching and grabbing straws, who knows where their hands have been? 
Are they trying to pull an 'eco-friendly' move by having unwrapped straws? If so, kill the condiment packets and have condiment pumps everywhere.
Okay, now that that little rant is over, I will say it was nice that we were able to sit on the balcony, there was an excellent view of the hulk ride and other rides across the water, and you had pretty bushes and flowers by the balcony. 
Clean-ish tables and seating area, and clean bathrooms, and overpriced fast food at an amusement park...it is what it is. At least my cousin and I were full for about 6hours after lunch!

Input: Stephen Mulrey, as the owner of Amrheins, I hope that you're interested in the feedback of your patrons, especially from one who was at your restaurant just four hours ago.

We were a party of 12 on the patio, and the food was great!!  The buffalo chicken dip was indeed fiery, and the clams casino special were tasty and substantial.  Each clams casino order had 2 clams and the shells were bigger than my palm and piled high with clams and stuffing.

Our party also ordered lobster mac and cheese - lots of lobster meat by volume, very rich and a full order can feed 2 people; sirloin tips - rare came out rare and medium rare came out medium rare, well flavored with good portioned side dishes; parmesan crusted haddock - the plate was cleaned off; lobster pie - tons of lobster by volume, very delicious.   Even the bread basket had ouch-it's-hot rolls that were light and slightly sweet with a great garlic/parmesan/olive oil dip on the side. 

What holds back Amrheins from being a top notch restaurant is the service.  Don't get me wrong, the waitstaff is polite and engaging (if you engage them first).  But they are not at all proactive in the service that they give.

Please don't tell me that you don't know about our surprise party reservation for 12 at five o clock, especially when the reservation was made 2 weeks ago and reconfirmed by us just yesterday.

Please give everyone a round of water right away.  And pay attention to refilling water glasses without being asked.

Please take our orders before my hair turns grey

Please check back at least ONCE to make sure that everything's ok

Please don't forget our dessert order for the one person who didn't have birthday cake (at least it didn't show up on the bill)

Maybe it was our waitress, Casey, was the exception, but I don't think so.  Mr. Mulvey, if you improve your staff's service level and attentiveness, Amrhein's will be top notch.

Input: Soleil is a beautiful, Italian-Mediterranean restaurant located next to The Oasis.  My mother-in-law and I sat outside on the patio to enjoy the beautiful sunset on Lake Travis.  It is a fairly new restaurant, so I wasn't sure what to expect, but I was already impressed.

For starters, our server was great and I wish I could remember his name to give him the well deserved kudos.  It's hard to get good service these days.  All I remember is that he was from Boston because we talked about how my husband just happened to be in Boston on that day.  

He started by recommending a very nice Malbec.  Great recommendation!  For an appetizer, we ordered the calamari.  Although it was cooked to perfection, it lacked flavor.  This was very disappointing, but we weren't going to judge the restaurant on an appetizer.

I ordered the Fettuccine with Gulf crab, shrimp, and lobster cooked in a delicious lobster cream sauce.  It was excellent, and I wanted to eat it all!  It's a little pricey, but you definitely get a large portion, so it's worth it if you like leftovers.  

My MIL ordered the crabcakes and we both experienced a first with this plate!  She got one normal crabcake, and the other one was a crispy softshell crab.  We were laughing because we couldn't figure out if you were supposed to eat it as is, or not.  Our server assured us it was perfectly fine to eat it as is, shell and all!  It was the same batter used in the calamari, so again, it was a little bland.  But it was worth the laughs and good times!

Unfortunately, I only give Soleil three stars this time because only my plate was excellent that night, and the rest was just okay.  But, this is a new establishment and I would love to see it grow and succeed!  I would like to try it again to give it another shot because I think it's worth it.  The service, the beautiful scenery inside and outside the restaurant is worth visiting at least once.  Maybe you can decide for yourself!

- Biriyani ($17.00) - basmati rice cooked with vegetables and we opted for lamb. Lamb was dry and needed the raita sauce. Biriyani itself was good but not worth the price point.

Input: Last Saturday after my alcohol-induced buzz had reached levels that, while not epic, certainly diminished my orienteering skills, my friendly neighborhood DD shepherded our party of 4 to a bar I'd never in my life been in before, and for the life of me I had no idea where we were. It turns out we'd arrived at the Skybox Pub - a place I'd previously never heard of, and after setting foot inside, found to be somewhat out of place in the Sellwood/'moreland area.

The place is clearly a sports bar - the walls are festooned with jersey's, posters, and other garish bits of memorabilia and sports bric-a-brac. They even have a life-size mannequin in Jordan's #23 Bulls jersey, though we reached the conclusion that they must have used the lower half of a Charles Barkley dummy because I don't remember MJ's sticks being as thick as old growth redwoods.

They also have a good number of TVs, most (if not all) of the flat-panel variety, though many were only of middling size. I'd imagine the Skybox is a good place to just show up and watch whatever sporting event is on the tube, but the place is a bit small, and they don't have the best "stadium, big-screen" set-up, so I'm not sure if it's the best place to watch a really big game.

We didn't have any food, but I thought they had a pretty impressive beer selection for a somewhat random sports bar - not as good as the A&L or some other larger places, but way more than the standard Bridgeport IPA, Widmer Hefe, Black Butte Porter on tap - I enjoyed a pint or two of the DBA (Double Barrel Ale) from Firestone Walker, which was quite a nice West Coast take on a British Bitter.

The thing about this place though is that it's very bright - I mean, almost blindingly bright - inside! I don't always NEED dark/dank in my watering holes, but this was almost like walking into an operating theater the lights were so bright. Coupled with the visual commotion from the TVs and all the junk on the walls, and the Skybox is not what I'd describe as a "relaxing" atmosphere.

Ultimately if you're looking for a friendly little sports bar and live in the neighborhood then you should definitely give the Skybox a shot...but I wouldn't go out of my way to visit, and it certainly is a subpar destination for non-sports related drinking.

Sticking with my Varsity analogy, a night at the Clermont without Blondie is like a hotdog at the Varsity without a "What'll ya have?" Input: I was meeting up with my girlfriends at Medina Cafe and being the typical non-adventurous person that I am, I got the typical foods you would eat at Medina Cafe. Those being - the waffle, a flavoured coffee, paella and fricassee. 

The flavoured coffee I chose was the white chocolate pistachio rose mocha. I had the lavender last time, which was not bad but a little too strong on the lavender for me. This though, was surprisingly flavourful. I could taste the rose and I got bits of pistachio in my mocha. Unfortunately, exactly like what I was dreading, the white chocolate made it too sweet. But other than that I enjoyed it.

Rating: 7.5/10 

The paella was very spicy, maybe even a little bit TOO spicy. The chorizo and pepper made it very spicy and overwhelming that it masked the flavours of the base. The only flavours I could detect was sourness and spiciness, nothing else. I tried to use the avocado to tone it down, but it didn't help. Trust me, I love chorizo but unfortunately the balance of the spiciness of the chorizo was totally off in this dish. 

Rating: 6/10 

The fricassee was somewhat lacking flavour. It was more on the sweet side than the savoury side. When eaten with the leafy greens on top it was better balanced but nothing about this dish really stood out. The meat was pretty fall apart though which was a good thing. 

Rating: 6.5/10 

And finally of course, we had to finish with a waffle and salted caramel sauce. I've had the salted caramel sauce and it was pretty good so I had to order it again. The waffle though was somewhat disappointing. It was served warm which I thought was good, but the exterior lacked crunch which was disappointing. I remember last time I had it, it was crunchy so I guess it's just a consistency problem? 

Rating of waffle: 7/10     Rating of salted caramel sauce: 7.5/10 

Overall the impression that Medina Café gives me is that on weekends there are usually long lines out the door (luckily I went on a Tuesday at around 10 and we were seated within 5 minutes) and it's on the more expensive side. The service was pretty good. I think why a lot of people are attracted to this place is because of the hype and because there's snot much of this kind and style of brunch food that is open everyday. 

Rating: 7/10

Input: Chung Wah Hong is perhaps the most consistent supermarket presence in Chinatown as I grew up. With the revolving door of Ming's (the original one burning to the ground when I was little), the 88's, the acquisitions of C-Mart, this little place keeps chugging along. It is owned by the same owners of Bao Bao Bakery around the corner. It has a very limited selection, but the pricing is reasonable. 

I come here to purchase very particularly... bok choy. They keep a very diverse selection of the vegetable always, from the more bulbous milky bok choy, the regular large ones, to the more elongated, almost endive-like baby Shanghai bok choy (though nowhere near as bitter) that does wonderfully when braised with a bit of ginger. The bok choy is stored in the open, rather than in the chilled refrigeration section. Sometimes, I get scallions and cilantro here when it looks fresh. The produce selection is a bit more limited than other places, but it isn't that large and they do compact the selection. I also acquire ground pork here for dumplings, Chinese steamed meatloaf, and stir-fries here, the grinder here a bit finer than at other places in the area.

I don't really purchase the produce outside often, but the tangerines I've picked up for sauces here have been alright.

Also, if you have a candy fix, this place seems to be the most consistent low pricing in Chinatown for Pocky, chocolate filled Koala cookies, and hard candies.

For example, this store sells the promotional fresh fruits in boxes.(fragrant Korean Melons, chamwoe, or Korean Pears $35 for 7 in one box). And, these are expensive, fragile, go bad fast and shouldn't be exposed to the room temperature, but be refrigerated.

They also sold the "date-expired" Luna New Year gift set (Colorful Korean Traditional Rice puffs, Hangwa, Liquid Teas, or Royal Jelly, etc) at the discounted price. They do not disclose the date at the box outside (or erased). But, when I opened it, the snack was 2 months expired with the manufactured date in individual packages.
 
At other retail grocery stores, the items that are close to the expiry dates will still be sold. But, here, H-mart Cambridge sells 2-3 months already expired products, with the old date stamp on it. That is dishonesty. 

When I mention these issues to the same manager, on the phone, there was ZERO sincerity, or he explained No known store policy. He forgot to "apologize(expecting Korean Manners, and, isn't it Universal to apologize for such a letdown?)" for my inconvenience to travel to Cambridge and back home, and back next time to return.

But, Koreans in the head office didn't act like Customer services. Hopefully, you don't run into issues like I did at all costs.

The aisles  are too narrow and  impossible to get by if there is another cart or a wheeled basket.  3 customers in 1 aisles is too crowded.

*Shelving issues- poor categories
They stocked one frozen sea food next to Kimchi, but, dumplings are found opposite of the building, next to the ice cream! These store management really need to benchmark other major supermarkets. It all starts with Flower, Produce-Bakery/Deli- then long shelf life products, then, Meat-Dairy, Frozen, then, cashiers.

These Asian cashiers do NOT speak English. They are not from USA, unlike many Latino workers hired in Burlington (Most speak English and documented).
 
It is impossible to have any basic communication at the cashier's. The friendly part-time assistant manager has to come to each cashier area to translate English to Chinese. And, to other fellow yelpers, LOCAL tax payers & Voters,  
it is important to support the independent small business. A Large Big Box store can ruin the local community by taking over their business one by one. Input: Since going back to BQE I needed to update my review 

BQE is still 5 stars up in my book! When it comes to FOOD...so I came here for the 12-5 day party on my birthday and enjoyed myself. The day party at BQE is every Saturday from 12-5. They serve brunch from 12-3 at affordable prices and from 3-5 they have a small affordable entree list you can select from. 

Drinks are very affordable, in fact it is much better  to get a party size depending on the number of people in your group. They have valet parking for $10 or $7 which is perfect because you don't want to struggle to look for parking or you can self park in lot, a block over for $5. 

After somewhat missing the brunch schedule, my party and I had to order off of the (after 3 side of the menu). Now, I am not a huge waffle fan, but I must say after tasting the red velvet waffles and tenders my cousin ordered, I can easily say I am impressed. I also ordered fried wings and fries which came back to be very well seasoned. Our waiter was very animated and helped us to enjoy our time there. 


Now on to my second experience...I decided to come back for my mom's birthday this past weekend. (The day party again) and our visit wasn't so great this time around. (Now pay attention to this next piece of what I'm about to say because it is very critical) We DID NOT make reservations because it would only be 3 of us. We were able to come right in and sit down. (Just as before) this time we were able to order on the  brunch menu and get mimosas. Now champagne bottles CAN NOT be shared by customers who did not pay to have mimosas. You must pay $22 per person if you and someone else wants to drink. Because both my mom and I wanted to drink I decided to pay the $22 per person.
A hour into drinking and eating. The waiter comes over and tells me my time is up. I start looking confused because I had no idea I was on a time limit. No one told me about this prior to sitting down. Well I spoke to a a manager and was told walks-in have 1 hour to eat and reservations have 2 and then you must leave. When I asked why this wasn't explained to me when I arrived, I got no answer. The best they could do was move me to the "standing bar area"'so I could finish my second bottle of champagne that I wouldn't have ordered, had I know I only had a hour to sit. To my surprise I was not the only customer treated this way as I saw more people, who was asked to leave their table, standing at the bar area with their champagne and wine. 

To say the least my bill was extremely high and I had to spend the rest of my visit standing up finishing a bottle of champagne. Because I wasn't informed of this. I won't be returning...the food is great, but the staff is sorry for failing to inform customers of this. That's poor customer service in my book and comes off as a dirty way to make money.

Input: My friend and I went here at about 10:30 on a really cold Friday night in December. The bottom floor had some lingering diners and a decent bar crowd. Didn't spend too long here, but it seemed nice.

Second floor was pool tables and one small bar in the front. It was nicely crowded here as well. The third floor was closed for a private event, so it was hard to get a pool table. We had a couple drinks and chatted with people around the bar until a table opened up. It was expensive and I wouldn't come here just for a night of pool. But as a diversion between mingling and dancing upstairs, it's fine.

Around maybe 11:30 they opened the night club (with a $10 cover) on the fourth floor. Over the next hour, virtually everyone from downstairs went up there. It's a pretty small space, but the bar runs all the way along one side and practically the whole rest becomes a dance floor. I thought it was pretty good, actually. Nice and cozy. It is pretty loud though, so if you don't already have someone to dance with, it's going to be hard to talk to someone new. And this place didn't quite seem like the spot for the grind-your-way dance floor approach :-)

Went back downstairs around 1am and the other floors were practically empty. There were a couple pool players and a couple boozers on the bottom floor and not much else. It was freezing cold out that night, so possibly a little slower than other Fridays.

One other note: I think the entire staff is good-looking women. Maybe not in the back, but behind the bars and hostesses, that's all I saw.

EDIT: I went there for a friend's birthday on a Saturday night in january and had a blast. Great place to go with a group. It's too loud to really talk and meet new people (at least on the top floor) but fun to dance and hang out with a group. Also the weather was not as cold and there was a better crowd than the previous time. I would upgrade to 3.5 stars if that were possible.

Input: My husband and I were actually on our way over to the Tradesman Cafe on a Saturday morning at 9 am when we walked past this place and saw the cute Mercato sign. We glanced over the brunch menu that was in the window and said, brunch? Why not? Unfortunately, once we were seated, we were handed breakfast menus and told brunch service doesn't start 'til 11am. Whomp whomp. Not their fault, we could have asked. 

The interior decor is well-thought out, with rustic touches throughout and the restaurant is connected to the Hyatt Centric hotel on the other side. We ordered espresso drinks, which are made from the coffee bar inside the hotel and brought to your table. 

I ordered the eggs benedict and my husband ordered the potato hash. There were maybe 2 other parties seated besides ourselves, so the place was rather empty. There was a couple who sat down after us who had ordered, received their food and finished their food before ours even came! We really don't mind sitting and chatting over coffee but we were at the point where we genuinely thought they might have forgot to place our order. My husband got up to see if our server knew if our food was coming but there was literally not a single person around. 

45 minutes after ordering, our food finally arrives. 

The eggs benedict was okay. The eggs were poached nicely with a perfect runny yolk, they were sitting on top of a bed of wilted spinach, lots of bacon and an english muffin that had been buttered and salty very generously. It was too salty, I actually had to remove some bacon and realized that it wasn't just the bacon but the english muffin had been loaded with salt. The hollandaise was nondescript, not creamy or tangy, just kind of bland. 

The potato hash looked delicious but the potatoes were only barely cooked through. They were charred nicely, which gave the appearance of doneness but the insides still had that almost slightly raw/crunchiness to them. 

It really seems like this place has potential but still is working out some pretty big kinks.

* They also have infused water and regular iced water available for free

Input: Let's face it...cheap accommodations are not easy to find in Boston. Especially at the last minute. I was supposed to leave the day Hurricane Florence made landfall, and I knew Logan and every other airport was going to be crazy. So I decided to stay in the city a few extra days. The problem was, the place I was staying didn't have any rooms available, but I was able to get a room at the Farrington Inn through booking.com. 

Because the stay was going to be more than just a couple of nights, they gave me a room with a private bath and a kitchenette. I can't speak to the rooms in the original house or the shared bathrooms. Given what others have said, I'd suggest trying to make sure you get a room in one of the other houses.

That said, it is a cheap inn, but it did what I needed it to do. I was able to sleep and have a warm shower--pretty much all I require when traveling. 

Andrew helped me with my bags and showed me the room. He was great, giving advice about laundromats and other places in the neighborhood. 

Yeah, the houses are old, and the rugs in the hallways are stained. I didn't notice any of the obnoxious odors others have complained about. There was a small cockroach in my room, but I've camped with bugs, so to tell the truth I didn't really care all that much. I know it would freak out some people, though, so just thought I'd give that warning.

The bed was probably the worst thing about the room. It was one of the old spring bed frames, except there wasn't any spring left in it. It sagged badly and my back really hurt in the morning. 

Other than that, it was fine. There was a small desk along with the kitchenette, the bathroom was pretty clean, and I was able to spend an extra couple days in the beautiful city of Boston without bankrupting myself.

If you want everything nice, then you probably need to spend two to four hundred dollars a night at a different place. If you just want a place to put yourself at night, then the Farrington Inn worked out for me.

Input: I gave this hotel a 3 star rating because it is truly just A-OK. there's nothing too special about it. If you've never stayed at an Embassy Suites before you might be wowed by their nightly cocktail hour, or their daily made to order breakfast, both come free with your stay. But for those of us who travel a lot, you know this is standard. Not something to gain additional stars for.

The pros:
I checked in late and they held my reservation (I called ahead to let them know).
They gave me 2 bottles of water upon check in because of my Hilton Honors account.
My room was large - to be expected because it was a suite. The king bed was comfortable, one of the nicest I've stayed on in a while not counting mine at home.
Restaurant on site as well as room service.

The cons:
They held $100 additional for incidentals - seriously? This always annoys me because I never use credit cards, always just debit.
Parts of the room seemed to be from the 1970's - scratch that, parts of the hotel too. For example the coffee maker and microwave are in a closet with slat doors. Hmm??
My entire room smelled of disinfectant, which should me me happy but it wasn't homey at all. It actually gave me a headache.
The parking is free, so that's a pro for a hotel of this size. But the con is that there's not enough spots up front so you have to park all the way behind the hotel just to find a spot. Then drag your bags around the building just to check in.
The pool is right outside the elevators, so you have to look at nasty old dudes in the hot tub, or have them gawk at you every time you go up to your room.

I'm sure I'll stay here again, the rates were reasonable ($175ish an night), about the same as everything else in the area and with this I got to enjoy a suite. Like I said, all in all this hotel is A-OK.

Input: Only because I've been to the Winter Park location a number of times, will I give this a shot again. We just left a late Easter lunch at the Lake Nona location. Having worked as a server to put myself through college and law school, I would never leave no tip. However, I believe the gratuity fairly reconciled with the level of service provided. ...Our studio villa had no couch!

A fan of...
...The staff! They were the usual great Disney cast members.

...I love sitting outside the restaurants and shops by the water and just relaxing. The feel of the main area of this resort is so nice and calm.

Input: With all my hours spent watching the Cooking Channel, Travel Channel and The Food Network, the Lobster Roll is a sandwich that has always looked fantastic when described on any one of these shows.  With that marvelous site of abundant lobster meat busting out of a NE style hot dog bun, I've been craving the sandwich for a while.  Since I'm no where near the state of Maine, where the Lobster Roll originates, I began my pursuit to find the closest thing to the real deal here in Orlando.

It came down to CityFish, Winter Park Fish Co. and Boston's Fish House.  The reviews I read for the Lobster Roll at CityFish didn't look encouraging at all.  The Lobster Roll reviews I've come across for Winter Park Fish Co. were bi-polar.  Boston's Fish House looked the most promising since they actually have their Lobster's flown in weekly from Maine, have appetizing pictures of the roll on Yelp and from what I've seen, all great reviews.  So Boston's it was.

We arrived with a party of 8 and perused the menu, paid first and then were seated.  

Everyone got their own meals but we decided to get their Boston's Seafood Combo Platter.  Codfish, Sea Scallop, Shrimp, Onion Rings and Oyster all fried.  This was a mistake, as I preferred the platter broiled.  But I didn't have a choice in the matter.  Majority rule.  When the heaping pile of fried seafood hit our table, we all dug in.  To me, I couldn't differentiate flavors between the 4 different pieces of seafood on the platter because they were all fried.  They all tasted like fish fry.  I could have gone to Captain D's or Long John Silvers for this!

From this point forward, I'm convinced that it is a SIN to fry seafood.  Breading seafood, then deep frying it in oil zaps all the natural flavor and essence.  

Mahi Tacos, Mahi Sandwich, Salmon, Fish and Chips, Lobster Bisque and fried Catfish were also ordered in addition to my Lobster Roll.  Both the Mahi dishes were delicious with flavor since the Mahi was broiled.  The Salmon was also delicious.  The Fish and Chips, and Catfish were fried, so there's nothing to report there.  Again, think Captain D's.  The Lobster Bisque was a disappointment.  Although it had a couple of nice chunks of what looked like leg or claw meat, the soup overall was underwhelming.  We've certainly had better.   We should have gone with their Clam Chowder.  I've read and have been told it's a legitimate NE Clam Chowder in texture, ingredients and flavor.

Now the Lobster Roll!  Right away I can say I'm a fan of the sandwich.  I really wish I had 2 of them that night.  There was an abundance of Lobster that looked like it included tail, claw and leg meat.  It wasn't heavily mayonnaised, but just enough to hold all the meat chunks together on the NE style, butter toasted roll.  At the bottom of the roll and under the Lobster meat was a bed of fresh shredded lettuce.  Lobstery. creamy, crispy, buttery, toasty, fantastic.  

With that said, I do think it could have been approved upon in 3 different ways.  

1:  I expected the roll to be slightly bigger.  But for the price of $12.95, compared to the norm of $20.00 to $25.00 for a roll, the size met the price.  I wish there was an option to get 2 rolls or 1 big roll for $20.00.
2:  Instead of using lettuce, they could use bits of celery.  This way the sandwich gets more crunch and added texture.
3:  The top of the lobster meat could have been dusted with cayenne or paprika just to add a little zip and offset the tang of the mayo.

But again, as is, I personally enjoyed the Lobster Roll very much.

Overall, the experience was pleasant.  I'm rating my experience a 3 out of 5.  I badly want to give Boston's Fish House a 4 out of 5 but there are a couple of reasons for the 3 star rating.  The fried seafood ordered all around me tasted the SAME.  I realized I shouldn't take points off because everyone around me so happened to get fish fry, but at least add some FLAVOR to the fry.  Seasoning, a different batter.. something.  The Lobster Bisque was disappointing and even though the Mahi dishes and Salmon were tasty, they were nothing out of the ordinary. Lastly, most of the entrees and sandwiches come with 2 sides.  Unfortunately, none of the 14 different side options are healthy.  We thought getting a side of broccoli and green beans would be a nice alternative to french fries, or onion rings.  Wrong.  Their sides of veggies are mixed in with mayonnaise and candied bacon! So needless to say, it's difficult to be a discerning eater here.  

With all that said, I'd come back for the Lobster Roll and attentive service.  Not much else stood out enough that I couldn't get at CityFish or any other seafood faring restaurant closer to me.

Input: With Namaskar sadly gone (although I have cautious hopes for the new spot opening in its place), I've been on the prowl lately for an at least solidly good Indian spot in the Medford-Somerville area. Guru certainly helps fill the void, but not so much for going out, so when my Indian food craving hit the other week, we were off to Masala for dinner. 

Overall the meal was, as Yelp puts it, "a-ok." The setting is typical and the service quite good--our waitress was friendly and quietly competent. The restaurant was rather quiet, but then again, this was around 8pm on a Monday, so that's not really surprising. If the windows are open, I would recommend asking to sit a bit away from them. It's certainly nice to get the breeze from outdoors, but the seats in the window feel a bit too close to the sidewalk. 

Unlike many Indian restaurants I've been to, Masala actually has a full bar, and they had a number of impressive deals to go along with it ($5 mojitos, anyone?). That being said, I have a hard time skipping my mango lassi, and Masala's rendition did not disappoint. It was a little less sweet and more tangy that others I've had--very tasty.

Masala offers two menus: a larger Indian one and a smaller Nepalese section. I was intrigued by some of the Nepalese options (not a cuisine I've had much), but I came in there with an Indian food craving and that was what I was ordering. The Indian side of the menu is fairly standard with the classics you'd expect.

After some nicely made pappadam we started out by splitting an order of the lamb samosas. They were my favorite thing on the night. Too hot to eat when they arrived, I couldn't help but try to eat them anyway thanks to their crispy exterior and well-spiced filling. Our entrees consisted of chicken vindaloo and malai kofta, with a side of aloo paratha. The vindaloo was okay, but certainly not the best I've ever eaten. The chicken pieces were a little bit strangely cut: the texture on them wasn't great, although the amount of chicken included in the sauce was generous. I also thought the dish could have definitely been spicier--I wouldn't be afraid to ask them to kick up the spice level a bit if you like your food hot. I also wasn't in love with the veggie dumpling part of the malai kofta. The texture wasn't great, and they were a bit dry inside. That being said, I greatly enjoyed the dish's sauce and would consider ordering them again just for it. The aloo paratha was solidly good--the bread had a nice texture.

Overall, Masala was no stand out, but certainly a decent choice with some definite highlights (lassi, bread, samosa, one of the sauces). I wouldn't recommend going out of your way to eat here, but if you're in the area, it's definitely a nice option to consider.

Input: 2 words:  not. memorable.

I came here on a Saturday night with a group of friends, with the intention of snacking / sharing food and getting drinks.  I got the "Day of the Dead" cocktail, which was tequila / lime based and was served with an inverted bottle of corona.  The drink was so cute and "insta-worthy" I must say, and the beer really helped mellow out the sweetness.  

Even though I really enjoyed the drinks here, the food itself was the part that was pretty forgettable.  We had the chicken karaage, fried shiitake mushrooms, beef tataki, a few rolls, ebi mayo, and creamy miso yaki udon.  The udon noodles did not taste like miso at all, and kind of reminded me of a tasteless cream sauce that you can get from a jar in the drug store.  

Don't get me wrong I love the modern esthetic / hip vibe of the place and its a cool place to grab drinks with friends if you plan to be on Davie street (you should make a reservation).  But if you're here with the intention of having more than a light bite, you might be disappointed.  There are plenty other Asian spots with more superior flavours!

You have to ask for wasabi and soy sauce, and what I especially don't like about the wasabi is that it is served to you in a communal container. As in, they don't swap the spoon, or the container, or the wasabi inside, or anything. This is different than a ketchup bottle- you don't have to personally reach inside the bottle to get the ketchup out, but you do with the wasabi. This is unsanitary to me. I get that it's traditional, but you're at the mercy of all of the customers before you who ever touched the wasabi when it comes to getting sick or not.  Speaking of unsanitary, Kura has received very poor food inspection scores in the past. Anyway, the line is also very long at times, but this is also the best time to come and eat because that is when the conveyer belt is stocked most. I have been during slower hours, and the conveyer belt was practically empty. There is also a very large portion of the menu that you must order off the iPad if you want to experience it, including some sushi selections. I get that the conveyer belt can only hold so many options, but it takes away from the convenient concept if you have to place an order and then wait for it to be delivered on the second belt. Finally, there are some foods that could use better quality control. For instance, on multiple occasions I've ordered takoyaki that were frozen in the middle. I get that it's unrealistic to expect fresh takoyaki to be made from scratch, but serving still-frozen food to customers is not acceptable. Also, a warning to those who are picky when it comes to sushi- Kura has a limited selection of rolls and mostly serves raw nigiri style sushi. I'm totally cool with it but others who like mostly cooked rolls will not be totally satisfied. Anyway, I'd recommend the salmon dishes and the crunchy rice dish from the iPad, it's good.

It's "A-ok."

I go for the burgers, but always end up getting an app first too.  The apps have been good, and I totally love the hummus.  Its a great sized portion with an awesome tomato pesto and pine nuts on top.  Bomb.  The bread is a crispy (fried) little bunch of wedges.  They hold up well.  Love it.

Least favorite is the Mexico... its not really hot at all (to me at least, but I'm no weenie.)

The beer selection has a few nice rotating offerings as well, usually with at least one good hoppy choice.

Service at the bar, as i said, is great.  Friendly and inviting.

Why do I not give it a full 5 stars?  Well, the burgers are good, but thats mostly due to the great toppings.  The meat itself is kinda bland and dry.  I would never go for just a plain burger.  No way.

As far as the service goes, as i said, sit at the bar.  They have had some poor servers work there that have helped me in the past.  the bartenders should thank them, because this just encourages me to sit at the bar all the time.

Ever see the movie "waiting?"  You remember the really angry server girl from that film?  I think she works there.

Kudos to the bar and burger toppings (and hummus!).

Input: 3.5 stars!

Jon-- 

I don't want to brag, but I grew up in LA and I've been eating at Chinese seafood restaurants since I was old enough to walk. Needless to say, I have some high expectations. Boston's gem falls short on some, but excels in others.

Wife and I had the ginger scallion lobster, fried taro nest with shrimp and scallops, and some sauteed pea stems. The pea stems were pretty good- a bit garlicky, but a good refreshing counterpoint to the other two dishes.

The fried taro nest was pretty nice, but we could barely taste the XO sauce. C'mon! I've had seafood baskets before, but never one made of taro. These guys could have scored a touchdown with this one, but the lack of the advertised XO sauce punch was like getting tackled on the 4th down at the one yard line.  

Ginger scallion lobster: take it away, wife!

Jenny--

So I was a little disappointed when we didn't get to pick our lobster (so we dropped them half a star), as our good friend had advertised. Perhaps we should have spoken up. The lobster meat was very sweet though. I thought the flavor was a little bland, but after a couple more tastes I was thinking that the chef probably doesn't want too overpower the natural sweetness of the fresh lobster. 

I didn't mind that I couldn't taste any XO sauce...I think the flavor of the nest contents (broccoli, mushroom, carrot, shrimp, squid, and other seafood) was pretty good. And the taro basket was so addictive! The husband and I devoured 3/4 of the hefty thing. Pea stems were good and we were given a huge mound of them.

The prices weren't too cheap or expensive, and I think the freshness of the lobster really trumps all the ginger scallion lobsters I've had in LA. 

Tip: Get the fried taro nest!

Input: Came here for a little NYE dinner, had an 8:30 reservation through open table and was seated promptly. They placed us in far back end table for two on the bar side against the wall, quaint little spot but not that great considering it was the closest table to the restrooms, lots of foot traffic. 

Started off with the 4 course pre fixe menu, ordered the venison tartar -  roasted suckling pig -  grilled ribeye, and a desert that apparently i do not remember, that explains that besides the picture.

Waitress was emotionless, seriously.. I didn't know if she was happy or about to meltdown crying... No freaking idea... Everything was said with a straight face, no opinions or recommendations of the food when asked. This whole waitress issue ruined the experience overall... I felt like we were causing her physical and or emotional pain by just being there... I was scared.

The venison tartar was great, balanced texture with a truly raw taste going on, much enjoyed! Quail egg I believe, on top completed the dish. The roasted suckling pig, boy oh boy did you guys trick me! Even the guy next to me asked what my dish was because he had the same dish and didn't know if it's what he ordered (we both let out a good chuckle) This dish with undercooked pasta (yes, undercooked) I don't need no lesson on properly cooking a pasta dish...  was so disappointing, and the "pig" part, well good luck trying to find the quarter sized single piece under all the glorified cafeteria children's pasta, accompanied by a 1 inch streak of some type of BBQ sauce in the corner of the plate. The grilled ribeye, you were cooked amazingly rare, just how I ordered it. Sliced well, displayed well, you were delicious, and the best part of the meal. You saved my soul after experiencing the prior dish. The Desert was desert, some type of rice pudding banana treat I believe, nothing to remember. 

If the service was different and the pig dish didn't exist or I ordered a different 2nd course, but seriously... you read - roasted suckling pig - what the hell else would you order!?!  This is my second time here and wanted to give it the 2 time chance review but it let me down. It's a well deserving 3.5 if that helps. Input: I found this place walking around Harvard Common about 7 years ago. I liked the outdoor atmosphere & it had decent reviews. I celebrated an anniversary here. The hostess was curt when we requested a certain table. The service was a bit hostile. It reminded us of New York at the time. We ignored the high prices because the food was so good. 

Subsequent visits proved to be as tough as the first one. An empty dining area never guaranteed good service. 

I went there today. Stood at the hostess stand for a while. I tried to make myself known but was blown off. Once the hostess came she didn't come to me, she motioned for me to come inside. My companion was starting to become agitated because we had only 45 minutes. It was awkward for no real reason. 

The Red House has recently started offering a dozen oysters for $6. The best deal in town, as far as I know. They bring it to you on a plate w/o ice. The oysters are not cleaned. The cocktail sauce comes with plenty of horseradish considering there is only a half ounce. I used my water glass to clean off the sludge. The oysters are plump & tasty but the grit & lack of condiment is disappointing. The fact that the .50 oyster only applies to the first dozen, if you get 2 dozen you pay $1 an oyster ad nauseum. That doesn't sit well with me. 

They have recently installed an outside bar with draft beer. I was pleased that they had local brews. But when I asked for a recommendation our server asked if I liked IPAs. I said no. He said; you won't like them then. Why would a bar stock only one type of beer on draft? Well, one was a Porter but is that really a choice? Makes no sense to me. 

It's a great location. Smack dab in Harvard Square & on bus & T lines. A decent place to go if the beer garden at Charlie's Kitchen is full but I have a sneaking suspicion that that's not what the owners of Red House are looking for. 

I dunno, a place that can charge $33 for a Chicken Lobster gives you a wooden fork with your oysters, I don't care how frugal they are, isn't thinking big picture. 

There are better places.

Input: We stayed here during a conference being held at the Doubletree because it was half the price of the Doubletree. The room was great. Ours was clean, included a mini fridge and microwave (so we could buy groceries and save money), and housekeeping seemed to do a great job. The breakfast, however, left much to be desired and it was always a madhouse in the dining area. The bread and bagels tasted very cheap and were not filling. The sausage looked unappetizing, so I didn't try it. The scrambled eggs were okay. The coffee ran out my last morning there and I didn't have time to wait for them to bring more. The first morning, I was about to sit down and one of the staff members grabbed my chair practically out from under me and gave it to someone else. I stood there looking at her and then she said she would find me another chair. While some of the staff were very pleasant, some were quite rude (especially around the dining area). Also, they have an Orlando ticket booth set up in the dining area and I overheard the ticket agent tell someone, "Epcot is just learning about different cultures. There are no rides there. If you want your kids to have real fun, take them to Universal." I thought that was tacky and unprofessional. She should have given a description of each park and let the parent decide what would be "real fun" for her kids. Also, they were painting the walls in the hallway while we were there and I found the smell of the paint fumes to be nauseating. The location was walking distance from the Doubletree, so we were able to save on parking and they did let us leave our car there for a couple of hours after we checked out. I would recommend this location if you need an affordable place to stay, but would also recommend making other arrangements for breakfast. We ended up supplementing with granola bars and sometimes had to buy coffee somewhere else.

Input: My girlfriend and I were relaxing the day before her wedding, trying to take her mind off the day of. We had finished all of the things on her to-do list and decided to get manis and pedis. We spent approximately 20 minutes on the phone calling places for an appointment and looking up reviews. We called Arboretum Nails and Spa and their prices were reasonable, and they said they only had a 10 minute wait. No problem. We told them we'd be right over and gave our names. Unfortunately, we should have realized that 10 minutes was a severe underestimation when we walked in. There were approximately 8 people in front of us. Since we'd already spent so much time looking up places, we decided to wait it out and choose our nail colors.

Forty-five minutes later, we were seated in the pedicure chairs.  Twenty minutes later, no one had even come over to us to begin, to inquire about what we wanted, or to talk to us.  Her rehearsal dinner was fast approaching and all brides feel the pressure of being on time, so we began debating whether or not we should leave. Typically, an hour is more than enough time for a pedicure and we'd already been there for over an hour by that time... but they hadn't even begun to work their magic yet.  The ladies overheard us talking and assured us that we'd be next, but we realized they would be skipping over another party to appease us.  A party, ironically, which was also trying to make it to their rehearsal dinner on time. It wasn't fair that they'd be skipped, so we got up and left.

There was NO way we should have been told a 10 minute wait.  I expect honesty and if my wait is going to be over an hour, you should tell me that when I call. You may notice that I still gave them three stars - I recently went back with my sister and we received great treatment. It was an off-day, not very busy, and we received great service. I do think when you actually receive service, they do a great job.

Input: Pricci is another upscale Italian restaurant in Buckhead Life's fleet.  Just like some of the other BL restaurants, as soon as you walk through the doors, you are hit with old-school style and elegance.  Pricci's interior reminds me of a cruise ship dining room with its combination of marble tile, carpet, wood, and white tablecloths.  We booked reservations on OpenTable for Friday and were seated immediately.  The restaurant was not very busy.  Most of those dining were your typical Buckhead Life crowd (middle-aged to blue hairs).

Pricci's dinner menu offers a simple variety of Italian appetizers, salads, pastas, and entrees.  They also serve pizzas Neapolitan-style.  I didn't really think of Pricci serving pizzas and I am intrigued about what they are like.  We didn't end up ordering any.  Instead, items off the menu I tried included:

Polpette - veal and parmesan meatballs with tomato basil sauce
Malfatti - ricotta gnocchi with braised Vidalia onions and sauce
Ossobuco - braised veal shank with Carnaroli risotto and lemon gremolada

The restaurant's meatballs are supposedly "famous" and they were hot, hearty, thick, and juicy.  I liked them.  The ricotta gnocchi was light, fluffy, and melted in my mouth.  The veal shank was served with the bone was cut open and there was a small silver fork inside which one can use to eat the marrow.  It was actually pretty good, especially when eaten with the meat itself.  The meat was savory.  I also tried a bite of the day's grilled fish.  I forget what type of fish it was, but it was served Asian-style, whole with bones, and had a crispy exterior.

The hostess and server were friendly.  The server was knowledgeable, but service was slow even though the restaurant was not busy.  Valet parking is available for $2.  Pricci was fine, but between the two Italian Buckhead Life restaurants, I am more of a Veni Vidi Vici fan.

Input: How does one go about reviewing what is essentially a shipping service? BC Ferries' cargo is people, and their rates are fixed. They do try to make the journey comfortable, with a decent, albeit very overpriced, White Spot restaurant and snack bar.

I've traveled via BC Ferries on the Horseshoe Bay/Nanaimo run every weekend since July 2010, so have a lot of trips under my belt now, both as a walk-on passenger and as a vehicle driver, so here's some observations:

- if you can take the bus or bring a bicycle, do so. You'll save a ton of money. 
- pack a meal or a snack with you. There's a microwave in the café area for passenger use. The food on the ferry ain't cheap.
- a motorcycle is 2/3 of the cost of a car, so there's some savings, but you'll be proportionally ripped off considering the deck space a bike takes up vs a vehicle. You will, however, get priority boarding and don't need a reservation.
- you usually don't need to make reservations for a vehicle unless you're traveling during peak times (holidays, 3pm - 9pm)
- keep an eye on the weather; if there's any chance of high winds, your sailing may be delayed or even cancelled.
- if you're busing on the Nanaimo side, spend some time at the bctransit.ca site and plan your trip. Nanaimo's transit system is dismal when it comes to meeting sailings and even worse on Sundays and holidays. Note: there is no public bus service for Duke Point, so unless you're looking for a 10k walk to Nanaimo, take your car there or arrange a ride.
- if you're driving a car, please leave your car alarm off or you'll just get called down to the vehicle deck when it starts sounding due to the motion of the vessel.
- electrical outlets for your devices are on board, but you may have to go scrounging for them or share them with other passengers. Charge your devices at home first.
- the ferries have wifi, but I use that term generously. It's intermittent, and if there's a large number of passengers, you'll most likely not be able to connect (my personal theory is that the wifi is nothing more than a shared connection tethered to the Captain's cell phone).
- if you're bringing young kids on board, please don't park them around the business workstations. Most people on their laptops are trying to get some work done, and there's a kid's play area on every ferry.
- you can have a good chuckle over their tag-line "Experience the Difference!". I'm not sure what the difference is being compared to (swimming, perhaps?) as there are no other competing ferry services. If you're taking a car, then you may want to consider one of a handful of small airline companies that service Vancouver Island; it's almost as 'cheap' and will save you hours of travel time.
- weather permitting, get outside on the upper deck and take in the scenery. Regardless of which ferry route you take, you will be rewarded with BC's natural beauty every time!

Input: I had been looking forward to trying Pinolo all summer. Having spent a decent amount of time in Italy, I've grown to love gelato and generally prefer gelato over ice cream, of which Portland has an abundance of popular shops. 

I'm also vegan, and was impressed by the non-fruit based, dairy-free flavors Pinolo lists on its website. In the shop, however, the only dairy-free flavors were fruit-based. When I asked the employee whether they had any of the flavors listed on their online menu, like caffe or almond, she seemed very confused and said it was "weird" that the online menu is so different. I was surprised that she had no idea about what the online menu listed. While I understand and appreciate that Pinolo may rotate its flavors seasonly, it is misleading to advertise so many non-fruit, dairy-free flavors and actually have none of them (in fact, the website lists 10 non-fruit, dairy-free flavors). Fruit sorbets are easy to find but other dairy-free flavors are less so. I was so looking forward to dairy-free caffe or bacio as the website had listed and as I love to enjoy in Italy!

I chose blueberry and yellow plum which were fine sorbettos, but not what I was hoping to eat. I recommend that Pinolo change its stated list of flavors on its website so no other dairy-free customers arrive expecting a wider variety of flavors. 

Meanwhile, my sister ordered the special flavor-- ricotta with apricot preserve-- and received a scoop with zero of the preserve.

Input: Wait, did you guys know that there are a lot of clubs in Boston? Don't tell anyone, I don't want to let the cat out of the bag.

Oops!

Seriously though, every club/lounge has it's own draw, and the beauty of BOND is definitely unparalleled in these parts. 

On the flip side, there is a LOT of competition for greatness, and BOND doesn't blow me away by any means.

Came on Saturday night for drinks. No cover (yay), coat check (yay), nice entrance up the marble staircase (yay). Weird layout (boo), generally odd setup at the bar -- EVERYONE RUSH THE BARTENDER (boo), and no where to sit or stand except right in the main walkway (boo). 

Drinks are expensive, not anything to right home about. The bartender ran out of cranberry, so he told me I would have to wait. No biggie, I patiently waited and didn't make a big deal of it. After a few minutes, he says "it's going to be a little while".. I said, okay yah no problem. I thought they were just loading up the cranberry in the machine, so I was okay with waiting. Finally he says, "look, it won't be fixed for a while. What else do you want?" Kind of an asshole, if you ask me. Here I am being patient even though your bar is out of a staple mixer, and you're giving me an attitude? Come down off your high horse, bartender. 

I would come back with a small group (like three others or less), because it's just too weirdly setup to have a big group all together blocking the walking areas and there's no where else to be.

Input: It pains me to give Chow Baby three stars, but this is mostly because this new-ish restaurant hasn't really gotten all of the kinks out of its system.  I've been three times, so I'm certainly a fan, but there is certainly room for improvement.

Heracles strengths: Something to please anyone!  Chow Baby is a 'mongolian grill' type restaurant, where patrons fill bowls that are then cooked on an open flat-top grill.  If you happen to be really into vegan-super-spicy-noodle-goodness, while your BFF is into beef-garlic-y-vegetable-rice-goodness, the odds are good that you both can find something.  The menu specifies what sauces and other items are vegan/gluten-free, as well as containing good descriptions of what each sauce tastes like.  Vegetable offerings change daily. 

Aphrodite factor:  A bit loud, but not necessarily a bad date spot.  You're more likely to see larger parties here, as well as smaller groups.

Hermes rating: This is essentially the restaurant's Achilles Heel.  Chow Baby hasn't quite mastered the ebb and flow of traffic, and they don't always take reservations.  Sometimes there is no line to fill your bowl to get it cooked, and at other times there is a line that will take you 20 minutes to get through.  There doesn't seem to be good timing in terms of seating, so servers get swamped rather quickly.  Additionally, there are always TONS of large parties here for dinner.  I'd be interested to see what lunch is like with a business crowd.

Achilles heel: If you don't like your dish, you have no one to blame but yourself.  Go back and try again!  Also, the restaurant inexplicably has a DJ on weekends, so it can be quite loud.

Libations: Chow Baby has an awesome cocktail menu, but I wasn't impressed with my last trip.  I'm usually a huge fan of the Ginja Sour, because it had more of a syrupy-sweet taste than the awesome ginger note I was expecting.  I'm guessing it just depends on who is bartending.

Offering: Chow Baby is an all-you-can-eat restaurant and is priced accordingly.  Lunch is quite a bargain.

The lobster claws, yes claws as there were many of them in my sandwich and falling out of it and into the basket, were not seasoned so you can just enjoy the natural flavor of the lobster. Input: Oh Ikea, why do I often feel you are the third sign of the apocolypse?

Everything you have in your store is so practical and cute...and how dare i not mention your low low prices.  Yet something within me is just not quite satisfied with my 800 pounds of rickety bookshelves i procured from you just a short while ago.  That's right, it may weigh a ton, but be hopeful a stiff wind doesn't come by and knock them over.

In all seriousness, the shelves are still holding together, though I highly doubt they would survive another move unscathed.  Another great example of the old addage:  you get what you pay for.

The food court on the other hand..delicious.  I find it hard to deny the $4 plate of meatballs on every trip to the store. That's right, no Ikea review is complete without mention of meatballs.  There you go, I did it.

My favorite Ikea sections however, as the crafty goddess that I am, is the fabrics.  Cheap, pretty decent quality stuff.  You're not getting prices like this at the shop down the street, and it really helps to supplement my stash with bright bold solids when I just can't afford to go out and get my beloved Kona cottons.  Sometimes, I even settle for solid colors of sheets from their bedding department.  What's a poor young diy junkie to do?

All in all I think I would deem Ikea to me as Kryptonite to Superman, yet I can not stay away.

Touche Ikea, Touche.

Input: Probably not saying anything that hasn't been said before, but here it goes anyway:)

went for RW and although the portions were tiny, the food was unique and inventive. great for a very light and expensive meal, perfect for something like an interview or business meeting when you are looking to impress.

what i enjoyed more than the food, however, was the lounge area. a great place to go and relax, as long as it does not get to crowded. as a bostonian who recently came back from nyc, it was a great mesh of the two; boston charm with nyc pretention. the lounge is a great place to meet a date or for a drink after dinner. i may not come back for the food, but the lounge is on the list.

1. **Tone**: Attribute Description - The overall tone of the text, reflecting the author's attitude and emotions.
Attribute Value: Informal, casual, and slightly humorous.

Attribute Value: Mixed (positive surprise with the lounge area, but underwhelming experience with the food portions).

3. **Food Quality**: Attribute Description - The author's opinion on the taste and uniqueness of the food.
Attribute Value: Positive (unique and inventive, but not enough to justify the price).

4. **Value for Money**: Attribute Description - The author's perception of the restaurant's value in relation to its price.
Attribute Value: Negative (expensive, with small portions).

5. **Ambiance**: Attribute Description - The author's impression of the restaurant's atmosphere and decor.
Attribute Value: Positive (great lounge area, perfect for relaxation and impressing others).

6. **Target Audience**: Attribute Description - The type of people the author thinks the restaurant is suitable for.
Attribute Value: Upscale, professional, and possibly romantic (suitable for interviews, business meetings, and dates).

7. **Comparative Analysis**: Attribute Description - The author's comparison of the restaurant to other experiences or locations.
Attribute Value: Favorable comparison to NYC, with a unique blend of Boston charm and NYC pretension.

8. **Return Intent**: Attribute Description - The author's likelihood of returning to the restaurant.
Attribute Value: Unlikely (for the food), but likely (for the lounge area).

9. **Emotional Connection**: Attribute Description - The author's emotional response to the experience.
Attribute Value: Positive (felt a sense of relaxation and enjoyment in the lounge area).

10. **Sarcasm**: Attribute Description - The author's use of irony or sarcasm in the text.
Attribute Value: Mild (e.g., "Probably not saying anything that hasn't been said before...").

These attributes capture various aspects of the author's sentiment and opinions about the restaurant, from the food and ambiance to the target audience and return intent.

Input: Ok...  So the manager is nice.  She knows the restaurant business.  From the sounds of it, she runs a tight ship.  

But, the food is surprisingly bland.  

I asked the bartender/assistant manager (???) what the Cuban spices are and was told they're cumin, oregano, and some garlic.  Sure enough...

We had a margarita, two appetizers (rellena and mofongo), an entree (Bistec de Pollo Empanizada (With Mango Salsa), and dessert (tres leches), reviews are as follows:
Margarita:  Was actually awful - and I've never had a margarita I didn't like;
Rellena: Is exactly as described, it reminded me of smashed tamales rolled around seasoned ground beef;
Mofongo: Similar to dry mashed potatoes;
Bistec de Pollo Empanizada: Scallopini chicken breast, very dry, slightly breaded;
Mango Salsa: Fantastic - very sweet and had a nice, slow heat
Tres Leches : Nice and moist - honestly, one of the best I've had

There were very few waitstaff and there appeared to be too many tables for them to cover; we even had to flag the waiter down to get water and the bill.

Will I go there again? Probably not.  
Would I recommend it?  Probably not.  
Would I decline to go if others wanted to? Probably not.

Input: Overpriced. Which doesnt mean that the food isnt great, it just is over the price at which it should be. 

With an air of romanticism and modernity the decor seems to fall below its own standards. The restaurant was really neither, it was an attempt, and quite a feeble one as a place where you could take a date or your cool friends. 
Overall though, the place was clean and tidy, no item really stood out. The waiter was friendly enough and acknowledged that he had an idea about the menu. One dish out of the three entrees came out substantially later than the other two, that is a big problem, a huge mistake, the waiter should hold the other two plates in the kitchen, where it would be warmer than sitting in front of you. 
The venison stroganoff did not have the correct consistency in the sauce nor in the meat, but had good flavor regardless. The ragout and confit of the second dish was tasty, it lacked effort in design and visual aspects. The third entree on our table was the trout, it was fresh, well cooked, and had the sides of vegetables and mashed potatoes kind of thrown in really, no time was dedicated to its presentation. Oh, right, I really liked the bread and what appeared to be a hummus spread, it was the best done part of the meal. The water glasses were definitely too small, modernity should not lack comfortability or utility in restaurants, we go to eat and relax and have a good time, not drink shots of water with constant advisory to fill up all the glasses on the tables. The drinks were whatever, nothing special, the margaritas served in rocks glasses, the beer had a bit too much of head on it, which is fine really. 

The unmarked bathrooms are obnoxious, please, no one needs to have to ask where the restrooms are, its annoying and slightly uncomfortable. Out of the 8 tables in the house, 6 were occupied, and this was during normal dinner hours, its a good thing 4 more people werent eating there, or else we wouldnt have gotten a seat. I cant recall anything that stood out positively really, the lack of range on the menu really surprised me, and at that, it was limited in quantity and quality. 

all in all, it wasnt worth the money, but it was food in a centralized location, with warm tones that can welcome you in

Input: It hurts me to have to rate Grezzo so low.  I'm a strong believer in the raw food diet, and while I don't follow it strictly, I am vegan and make it a point to eat as many raw foods as possible.  I found out about this lifestyle year or so ago from Alissa Cohen's (owner) website and became completely obsessed with the "Raw Food Talk" message boards (a great place to find out more about the raw food diet, if you're interested).  I was ecstatic when she opened her first restaurant so close to me, so when my dad expressed interest in raw foods, I jumped at the chance to finally try it.

The location is wonderful - a couple blocks off the main streets of the North End, I almost felt like I was back in Rome.  The atmosphere is dark and quite cozy, and shuffling the clunky chairs around to let others in/out of their seats can get kind of annoying, but that's the least of their problems.  It's obviously a small space, so it's inevitable the chairs and tables are going to be close together.

The problems come with how they handle the flow of people in their space and with their service in general.  A few minutes before 9pm, several groups of people arrived (they take reservations at 5, 7, and 9pm - it seems like they should stagger their times a little to avoid a sudden, disruptive influx of people like this), leaving at least 10 people crowded by the door/three surrounding tables, letting a freezing cold draft into the entire restaurant.  The group of six that had entered first was asking to be seated for their 7pm reservation.  All the tables were full at that point, but instead of being turned away, or asked to wait until others with reservations were seated, they were given room/seats at the bar to wait for the next open table.  The next group actually had a 9pm reservation, but because there was no room for them to wait inside, the waitress/acting-hostess suggested a cafe down the street to wait in until she called them.  The total downpour certainly did not help make this option any sunnier.  In this situation, it should have been the people on time who got first priority, and the group 2 hours late should have been asked to wait elsewhere.  The whole point of a reservation is that there will be a table available for you at a specific time.  Grezzo's lucky so many people are eager to try raw food, because at any other place, I know at least I would've just left.

That fiasco didn't have anything to do with me, except that the scene unfolded a few feet away from me, but the service was just as airheady for us.  Our waitress, while very smiley and friendly, constantly talked AT us and rattled off ingredients so quickly I couldn't even process what she was saying.  She also would come over and say something like "I'm so glad you're enjoying the food" without actually asking.  Just because I'm eating it, doesn't mean I love it.  She wasn't great about answering questions, especially when it came to explaining what ingredients are.  They should realize they're many of their customers have not encountered all of their ingredients before and should take the time to explain what things actually are in a way everyone can understand, particularly when asked.

The food itself was completely dynamic.  The flavors of fresh foods was so powerful, though at times overwhelming.  This is not the fault of Grezzo, and not something they should change.  For me, this really highlighted how limited and bland my own regular diet is.  I loved experiencing such a high level of food creativity.  I got the tasting menu and was glad I did.  It was a LOT of food.  The portions are not huge in the sense that you'll get 1 lb. of pasta on a serving platter all to yourself, but the dishes are very nutritionally-dense leaving me with a very full (but not too full) belly.  

The food at Grezzo renewed my enthusiasm for raw foods and I'm thrilled it's so close by.  However the service really needs to do some reevaluating in how they interact with customers and how they control the incoming flow of patrons, especially when it comes to reservations.  Also, it'd be great if they rethought the bulky acrylic menus.

Input: I have never been to Chili's before, fearing it was too spicy for me (the logo has a hot pepper on it after all). And this despite the fact there is a branch about 2 miles down the street I live on. I finally stopped into the Danvers branch today because a friend had a gift card and wanted to treat me to lunch.

All in all, I was impressed. The waitress was very pleasant and helpful. The food came quickly (perhaps too quickly...see below), and my meal was very nice. I started with a "house side salad" which was practically a meal in itself and very fresh. This was followed by a Margharita flatbread, which was delicious. Now obviously my choices were not "tex-mex" but they were very good.

My partner for lunch, however, was disappointed with her meal. She ordered the "smoked bone in wings" and a salad for lunch. The wings were on the menu as "Bone-in wings slow smoked in house over pecan wood. Served with Chili's classic BBQ sauce". The wings were not smoked, they were deep fat fried and had absolutely no seasoning on them at all, let alone the "smoked" seasoning promised. And the "classic BBQ sauce" was plain old ketchup with no BBQ taste whatsoever.  There were very few customers in the restaurant, so there was no real reason to take a shortcut and fry the wings.

So, a mixed review: my lunch was excellent, my companion's was not at all as advertised.

Input: Two recent visits to No Mas were as different as night and day and consistency may be the biggest challenge facing the restaurant.  The most recent visit restored our faith in No Mas.

Previously, service was robotic and awkward and our server lacked the most basic social skills.  The owners were in desperate need of training for their service staff.  This time we had a delightful waitress who engaged in our playful banter and provided seamless, relaxed service and it definitely made for a more delightful meal.

On an earlier visit, the atmosphere was raucous, the restaurant filled with groups of 10, 12, 20 or more celebrating birthdays, a girls night out, prom dinner and any occasion where more's the merrier.  Our two top felt terribly out of place.  This time the restaurant was festive but filled with more traditional groups of three or four, although as the night wore on, tables were being pulled together for parties of 10 and 15.  And atmosphere is important here, with eye-popping décor making it unique and unlike anything else in Atlanta.  The owner's passion and love for all things Mexican is evident in the details used to carry out the theme.

Our table commented that on previous visits our food was decent, but not dazzling, and while we liked it fine, other Mexican restaurants had more flavorful food that satisfied us better.  This visit, though, provided the best food we've had yet.  We started with chips and salsa - light, crispy chips accompanied by a bowl of smoky chipotle salsa.  We added a guacamole appetizer, a bowl of creamy, slightly chunky avocado with a pile of diced tomatoes on the side plus a lemon wedge.  We mixed it all together and three baskets of chips later we testified that this was one terrific appetizer.

Two of us got the combination platter, where you put together your own mix of tacos, enchiladas and tamales with a choice of sauces.  I got the Playa del Carmen, a plate that comes with two shrimp enchiladas with a light cream sauce, plus a fried fish taco.  I kept the rice but subbed mixed veggies for the refried beans and they were superb.  All-in-all a lighter meal that was full of flavor.  Perhaps new hands in the kitchen are better equipped to deliver great Mexican food.

We used a $30 Groupon with no problem and since another one of our party bought the same Groupon, we'll be returning again and reporting on whether they've maintained the higher standard.

Input: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder.  And the Orlando eye is no exception.  If you are a Florida native, you may find it a little cheesy with hazy vistas of other Florida theme parks and miniature downtown Orlando buildings.  Or if you are a tourist this would be just another trap that you'd be happy to get caught in.

The gf and I were able to take advantage of  the "First to Fly" weekend, so we can ride it before it opens to the general public.  You get a free pin to commemorate this day along with green screen photos that are reminiscent of those cruise vacations.  You start with a 4D movie of Florida landscapes which was actually pretty cool.  Gave me a little pride for my state!  Once that's over, you are escorted to one of the pods.  Ours fit about 10 people and they so graciously stopped it from moving in order to get a grandma and her walker on there safely.  Our pad also had an attendant that answered a bunch of questions regarding the structure of the Orlando Eye and any other points of interest that you can visibly see.  They say you can see Ft Lauderdale on a clear day.

Once the 20ish minute ride is over, like any other good amusement park/attraction, it takes you to the souvenir shop.  You can buy your green screen photos complete with a binder of more Florida facts.  Or you can buy pencils, teddy bears, mugs, etc at the shop.  I was upset that the frame that they were selling wouldn't fit the picture that we bought....fail.  After it was done, we went for ice cream at the nearby Ben & Jerry's and took in the remaining hours of daylight on the softest astroturf I've ever sat on.

So anyway, pretty cool.  I'm sure it's going to be one of those, one and done things that each Floridian will need to do sometime.  If i end up going again, i'll probably try and go at night when they light up the wheel.  I'll probably also wait until the new shops and restaurants open.

It took the waitress a very long time to get our food to us, and a couple who ordered after us got their food before us. It also took her a while to give us our check as well. Input: Here just for the weekend and was excited to find a Japanese place near the Airbnb. Needed a quick break from typical BBQ so decided to come check out Kemuri. We walked in (2 people) on a Friday night without reservations at 9pm and were seated within 15 minutes. In the meantime we grabbed some beers and really enjoyed the ambiance of the patio initially and the inside as well.

3 stars because the menu is quite limited. For a yakitori place I was pretty surprised by how there were about 10 skewer options on the menu. Thankfully they had staples such as beef tongue and chicken heart and things like that. The skewers we got: beef tongue, miso scallops, chicken + leek, head-on prawn, and chicken meatball. Our favorites were the first two. Skewers come on 1 stick so keep that in mind if you're sharing.

Other delicious things: the guaca-poke was really good. Fresh zesty guac, raw tuna + sesame oil, some pickled shallots and radish were a nice touch with crunchy pita-texture chips. We also shared their original ramen which was not bad - I liked the heavy helpings of green onions and thought the sweet egg was top notch - also points for creativity with adding a smoky piece of pork to flavor the soup.

We also got a hamachi sashimi special with a smoky chimichurri sauce which was interesting but the teeny-tiny portion was disappointing. Sashimi portion was like the size of my thumb.

I regret not getting the street corn because pictures look amazing. Good news is if the wait is long - there is an outdoor area where you can chill on some drinks.

Input: At the end of a long day exploring Epcot, we ended up at Nine Dragons (using the Disney app, we made reservations a few days prior that ultimately proved unnecessary as the restaurant was not busy at 5:45 PM on a February Thursday). We were seated quickly and the restaurant did fill up quickly around us. The menu is fairly limited, but standard Chinese favorites are accounted for. We had the pan fried dumplings and the pork belly bao to start. Dumplings were fantastic. The bao had too many toppings. There were the crunchy sesame sticks and red onions...when all it really needed was the delicious sauce and a bit of cabbage for crunch to be perfection. The buns were perfection.

For my main meal, I stuck with the tried and true honey chicken (which came with a small side of white rice and a little bowl of asparagus tips). I wished for more rice to go with the enormous portion of honey chicken (truly, it tasted just like a nugget dipped in sweet and sour sauce). Bae got the fried rice and said it was a decent fried rice (he ate it all, so no complaints, obviously). We skipped dessert in favor of finding something sweet in the park.

Service was excellent and our waiter was very pleasant and quick to refill our drinks. Ambiance was nice, pretty standard Chinese decor (a little flashier than back home - in a good way). We enjoyed the escape to the A/C and getting off our feet. It was certainly an enjoyable way to end our Epcot escapade.
