Input: I've been going to Dr. Crook for about 6 years now. I have noticed that she can be a bit awkward in the chitchat phase of my annual exam, but that's not a big deal. I'm awkward too, after all she is about to give me a breast exam and discuss my digestive tract. Not to mention the ol' pap smear that we'll both have to endure in a few minutes.

So lets get to the meat of this review, but in vague, hazy terms so I don't share my medical problems with you people. That's my business! You just came here to hear about Dr. Crook.

I had a serious problem a few years back and instead of sending me to a specialist, Dr. Crook sent me to a surgeon. I'm not saying her decision was wrong, but I am saying that its a pattern of behavior.

This year, I had another serious problem (unrelated to problem #1). My symptoms at first were pretty nebulous, and could have been a lot of things. At my appointment, she didn't give me a physical exam. She diagnosed it as the most common option (again, not necessarily the wrong thing to do but neither was it thorough) BUT when i called a month later to say that there was no change and i was following her prescription and diet suggestions, she told me that I just needed to give it time. Another month went past. Finally I just thought, screw it. I made an appointment to see her. At this point I had done my research. I realized there were multiple tests she could have done to confirm her diagnosis. At this appointment, I showed her the list of changes I had made to accommodate her diagnosis, so she would realize that I was taking her seriously. I mentioned testing, I mentioned a referral to a specialist. She finally gave me a physical exam and immediately realized that it was probably something else totally unexpected. She sent me off to get more tests. I'm still okay with it at this point. Maybe not handled great, but we're getting stuff done. Its that when she called me with the results she said "Good news! You're not imagining things ...etc etc"

Seriously!? I knew i wasn't imagining things. That's why I ... waaaaaait... did you think I was just making it up?

Anyways, she sent me to another surgeon (still not the wrong thing to do). But now its three months after I noticed the problem and I have to get surgery. And the problem had only been getting worse for that two months that I was misdiagnosed, and the month spent with the whole surgery process.

Pros:
- She is not a bad doctor.
- She is capable.
- She will take care of you.
- She's gentle with your lady parts. Or man parts.
- Oh the jokes you can make with her name!
 
Cons:
- Diplomacy/tact not her strong point.
- Prefers surgery referrals to specialist referrals (at least in my experience).
- Needs firm responses and evidence to reconsider a diagnosis.

-the clam linguine was a well put together dish. the clams were smoky flavored and not at all fishy, this worked great with the little pancetta cubes, and yet was not like some crazed hickory pasta. came out a bit salty, but I would definitely suggest this dish.

-calamari appetizer: blech. not breaded (which would normally be fine).  the calamari tasted fishy and was at best, shallow-boiled in a weak salt/garlic base. came with uber-burned toast that tasted like ash.  the calamari came with a cream sauce that somehow magnified the fishiness. I shudder just thinking about this dish. *cries*

-cheese plate: tasty, consisted of a soft cow ripened cheese drizzled with honey. a sheep hard cheese and a goat bleu. also an interesting fig 'sausage' (not really sausage tasting but, still enjoyed it.

we were here for a birthday and the staff was incredibly friendly and helpful with the birthday cake and our dozens of photo ops (asian girls + 3-4 cameras = danger!!) + sunburns from all of the camera flashes

Input: Atmosphere and food are good. Service can be atrocious.

Without more than a passing apology from the front of house staff, and then with a server who claimed to be focused on turning the evening around but couldn't even manage to bring us bread. Despite being asked three or four times. Over an hour. Or water. Pretty basic things that you shouldn't have to ask for half a dozen times, especially after you've been left waiting for so long before getting a table.

Food took literally 45 minutes to come out of the kitchen that night (which, after a 30 minute wait past reservation time to get seated, plus a 15 minute wait to see a server, started to really suck). Portions are perfectly sized - not too large or small. I would've actually split a dessert under normal conditions, but I just wanted to get out of there. To top it off, their validated parking didn't work once I got back to the garage. 

The other experience was better, but the last experience really turned me off - I expected at least to have a manager stop by  and see how things turned out, but apparently no one was interested in feedback. As a consequence, I haven't gone back since.

Input: We went for breakfast. Saturday around 11. It was pretty empty. 

We got mochas, meh, they were fairly expensive and too sweet. But caffeinated, so that was good.

Let me start by saying my kid had one of the worst in public meltdowns she has ever had, because a fly landed on her eggs. So, this isn't necessarily a completely neutral review. There was only one little fly, it's not their fault, but my daughter just lost it. I think she had too much sugar at school at the party on Friday. I digress. 

Hubby had a Denver omelet. He stated it was underseasoned.It had red and green bells in it, which he liked. But this is the man who usually complains about too much salt. He peppered it, seemed satisfied. Had toast and hashbrowns and water.The young server came and filled our water glasses without asking. I was impressed he braved my daughter's tears and still came to the table. Points for that. 

I had a Greek omelet. It had spinach, feta, onions, and tomatoes. The omelets here are very flat, not loaded with ingredients, but the eggs were tender and nice. I liked my omelet.A little more feta might have been good  but the spinach was tasty, the onions were soft and yummy, so it was ok.My wheat toast and hashbrowns were fine. 

Daughter had ordered an omelet special, ham and cheese, which was $4.99. Nice. Too bad she didn't eat it. Her first bites seemed happy enough. Until the whole fly thing. She wound up eating my toast and jam, which she liked. Hard to mess up toast ( although we have run into that before). 

The restaurant seems a little dated,the table wasn't completely clean, and the music was awful. But the server was nice, and the lady at the register was nice, and I might go back if I can get over the embarassment of my kid's tantrum. Maybe I will  leave her at home though.

P.S. the baklava at the register looked yummy.

Input: I planned a dinner with a couple of my girlfriends and I wanted to try out a new restaurant in town. Price, cuisine and location were not of concern.

Now the rice was on a whole different playing field. I could taste the chicken broth and coconut throughout. Now this is what I would go back for. 

My overall experience was pleasant, well except that the place is poorly insulated and I was freezing the entire time. I think we even asked if they could turn the heat on, but no such luck. I am not dying to go back but, if someone was interested in trying it out, I might tag along.

Input: I think just about every time I come in here, I see at least 2 people from high school.  I would never think a chain to be a towny place, but thats really what this place has turned into. The food is satisfying, but there isn't any WOAH! factor.  They have some good lunch deals that are pretty cheap.  It's anything you would expect from an Applebees.  The appetizers are good, but typical.  I guess the big thing now is the mini cheeseburgers.  There is a good selection of entrees, but I don't think I would get steak from here.  I would rather spend the money at a steak house.  The desserts are pretty good too.  Overall, I would say the food is average.  

If you do make a stop in here and aren't from the area, beware of  high school reunions going on around you.

I'm giving them "3 stars" because it would be unfair to trash the place when I didn't give them an opportunity to correct the issue, but it was an absolute "zero star" drink. Stick to beer.

I think this place is a bit hit or miss but it's pretty value priced and not bad if you're just looking for a quick dinner. Input: I have now been to Sushi House Hayakawa four or five times so I can safely write this review.  The rave reviews about this place (even from well-trusted yelpers) made me believe that perhaps I was missing something...or that I had gone on bad nights.  I haven't written anything on this place up until now because I really wanted to like this place.  However, I'm just going to come out and say it now, that it has not lived up to all the hype. 

Let's talk about the good points first.  It can be a fun environment.  The sushi chefs will sometimes play games with the patrons and it is USUALLY a very welcoming environment.  (I'll get to the "usually" later)  Some of the food is pretty good as well.  They make a nice agadeshi tofu and some of their appetizer dishes are quite good.  Strangely enough, after at least four visits, I have concluded I prefer their appetizer dishes over their sushi.

Now onto the negatives:  I haven't ever been there when the the fish was that impressive or fresh.  Initially, I thought that I was going at the wrong time of the week before a fresh shipment, but I've been there on different nights of a week.  The waitstaff also seems a bit flustered when things get busy. While everyone seems genuinely very nice and usually very welcoming, it seems that the restaurant just doesn't stay cool under pressure.  Again, the people are nice, there just isn't a great system in place.  We've had our food delivered to the wrong table and our glasses almost always empty.

Would I recommend this place? It definitely does not make my top Atlanta sushi restaurant list.  However, if you are in the area and are looking for sushi, I wouldn't write it off either.

Input: This is an honest review - I got my lashes done by Michelle yesterday in hopes that her work lived up to her reviews online. I'm new to Austin and wanted to find someone I could trust to do a good job considering lash extensions are on the pricey end...

I wish I could say that I'm satisfied but I'm not at all. I've had two previous eyelash technicians in the past whom I regularly went to and always did a phenomenal job. They're full set price points were 125 for volume lashes and I paid Michelle 150 for a set that looks quite honestly like a sub-par at home job done with one of those individual semi permanent lash sets you buy at CVS. I honestly wish I would have done that myself rather than paying 150 dollars for the same look. I am always willing to pay for good work and would have had no problem paying that if the results matched her rates. 

The lashes were not applied close enough to the root of my lashes (which are blonde) so you can literally see a gap of natural lash between my lid and lash extensions and it looks tacky! Not professional at all!! And since they are applied this way, they twist and flip and don't sit naturally. They are also falling out quite quickly - and yes, I haven't gotten them wet or picked them or slept on them.. they're falling out because of the way they were applied. 

Also, the room / office she works out of is not relaxing or professional feeling at all. It wreaked of strong perfume and it was quite cluttered. I felt dirty there. And I'm sorry, but if you charge 150 -200 dollars for a service... this includes a cleanly, relaxing and professional environment. Which is NOT what Michelle has as her set up. It's a tiny office in a professional business building downtown. The whole thing is weird and feels very out of place. I should have gone with my gut instinct and left when I saw her work space. 

I texted Michelle, kindly explaining my concerns asking if she could squeeze me in today to fix them and I haven't gotten a response in the four hours since then. So now, I'm writing this review as a very frustrated client. At this point I would rather remove them then go to a wedding with my lashes like this.. it's a shame. And only makes me realize how lucky I was to have such talented technicians in the past. 

Of course this could be one unfortunate instance, but first impressions are lasting impressions. I don't recommend and would not go again. I work hard for my money and it sucks when you pay for a service that is less than satisfactory. If I would have gotten a response from her, I would have loved to give her another chance and resolve this between the two of us. 

Perhaps I didn't explain well enough what I was looking for but I was just really surprised with what I ended up with and not in a good way. It seems like many of my lashes are without any extensions so the entire set was sparse and both eyes were uneven in the number of lashes on each side. Input: Who's Got Soul was voted as one of the best soul food restaurants in metro Atlanta, according to a recent AJC article. I think for the most part, they live up to that standard. Favorite menu items include turkey wings, collard greens, yams, baked chicken, pork chops, and their corn bread. Pretty much everything I've had here has been good, and the quantity matches or exceeds the price. They even recently remodeled and slightly expanded the interior. I do like how most of the food is already made, so even if there is a long line, you still receive your food in a timely manner.

My wish is for the improvement on service. It can vary, and staff appear to have changed frequently over the years we have been here. And tonight when we dined, they close at 9 pm, but they were selling out of a lot of foods by 8 pm. However, when a customer tried to eat in the dining area around 8:15 pm, they said the lobby area was closed. When we were still eating, they were already cleaning up the dining area and putting up chairs. When we left at 8:30 pm, they closed the main gate in the front, making the restaurant appear closed altogether. I just think if you close at 9 pm, you should close at 9 pm. 

Parking can be tricky during busy hours (especially Sunday afternoons). They have a parking space, but it is very limited, so sometimes people park illegally on the street to the right. Overall, this place is close to home and they have pretty good soul food, so we will see them again.

Input: I'm really quite undecided on this place and I think that's because my experiences at A Good Yarn have honestly been extremely inconsistent. The first time I went in (broke, jobless, but still loving to knit) I asked if they had any Lion Brand. I just happen to knit a lot with Lion Brand. The woman I spoke with with very rude. She said "What?!" in almost a "how-dare-you?" tone. When I said something to the effect of, "Or...well...anything with acrylic or synthetic fibers? I don't have a lot of money right now." She responded with raised eyebrows and said "No. We don't carry that." Okayyyy....So I basically avoided this place for a couple of years.

Second time I went in, staff was almost shyly friendly. Kind of smiling, kind of quiet, not overly helpful, but rang me up with a smile when I bought some merino on sale from their sale-bin. Cool.

The most recent time, everyone was VERY friendly. But it's really anyone's guess as to what kind of service you'll get on any given day. I haven't seen the service steadily improving, is what I'm trying to say.

I have to be honest. I also echo what a lot of reviewers have said about there often not being enough of a certain color or type of yarn to complete a large project. And their selection can be iffy. Great if you have a decent amount of money, but with knitting becoming so popular among younger groups you'd have thought they would carry some more inexpensive yarns. I do most of my shopping for yarn online. I can just find a wider selection at cheaper prices. But A Good Yarn has been my main source of buttons, books about knitting, and free or cheap patterns. Sometimes I'll find good deals for smaller projects in their sales bin and a few times I've caught an employee on a good day and managed to get some nice advice about types of cast-on's, techniques, and fibers to use for certain projects.

Save yourself some hassle and go anywhere else, unless you don't plan on leaving the hotel.

EDIT:  Upon speaking with the manager at check-out, we received an apology, and were informed there is additional parking available.  The night staff did not have this information for some reason.  The renovations on the interior are complete, but exterior is not expected to be for awhile.  Excluding the parking issue, this is a nice hotel to stop at if you are looking for a clean/economical stop.

Input: We found The Pinewood pleasant enough but not quite a match for all the hype.

Grits tots were delicious, a hard act for hush puppies to follow. Tasty dipping sauce.
The brussels sprouts ($7) were quite al dente, and too salty for me but just right for others. Also, the stems were left on - why? We do these better at home.
All the above served in cute galvanized pails with wooden skewers to spear them.

The beet salad ($7) was overwhelmed by too much vinegar, balsamic or otherwise.

Entree portions were too small for the prices ($22 burrata cheese ravioli was about 5-6 small ravioli, little evidence of the "asparagus confetti"; $22 trout also skimpy). 

Can't speak to the libations except that the Jackie O was too sweet for my taste and the member of our party drinking old-fashioneds confirmed that they were indeed old-fashioneds.

Service desultory, on a slow Monday night. Long wait times between visits by server, no pleasantries. Server wanted to clear plates with food still on them but left empty plates throughout the meal. Party of five, we ran out of water twice (they leave it on the table, in old liquor bottles that don't hold much).

Input: +3 for the price and my first haircut there.
-2 for those other two haircuts. 

I've been here three times so far. I don't have very long hair, but I get tired of cutting it myself. Plus, like previously said, 30 bucks for a wash/cut/style including tip is great.

The first trip was in 2007. I tall guy with a tattoo on his neck did it then. I should have got his name, because he did an amazing job! And yelled at me for having bangs, because I don't have a big forehead. He was great to talk to and made me feel very comfortable.

The second trip was ok, I don't remember who did it, but I felt comfortable with them. The layers that were trimmed into my hair were ok. Nothing amazing. It grew out well though.

The third trip was this afternoon. I got an older woman, Roza was her name if I remember correctly, and she seated me as soon as I came in. There were no real pleasantries, no chit-chat, just trimming. I explained what I'd like to see and not to make it too short. It's kind of too short. She also styled it weird. mousse and that whole 80's fluffed up thing.... I had her at least part it before I left. When I got home, I soaked my hair a bit, rubbed out some product with a towel and went to blow drying it myself. And it's uneven!!! The layering/feathering that is going on on the right side of my head is not echoed on the left, at all. In fact I don't think she even did the same thing on both side..... And she trimmed my bangs weird. I hope it grows out well. 

I must also note that I am more or less blind without my glasses, so when I do get my hair cut, I can't watch what they are doing......

-edit-
Adding two more reviews for this place. I went back again on my 4th time and got Bridget. She did a really great job on my hair and listened to my gripes about the previous encounter with Roza and she sympathized with me about it. She also told me that I have hair that is difficult for some reason. BUT! She got the light layers in, evened everything out and made sure it looked right while it was dry. 

My 5th time was ok. It was a newer girl and she talked me into the special.... I paid 20 extra dollars for results that weren't great. This is my deciding factor on not going back again, unless I get Bridget.

Input: I'm on the fence on how to rate my W Hotel experience... 

PARKING 

Valet only. $39 per night

CHECKING IN

Check in is at 3pm. We had booked 2 rooms for a 2 night stay. We arrived at the hotel by 4pm- only 1 of the 2 rooms were ready. I had to contact the front desk at 6pm to follow up with them about the second room. To their credit, they called me right back and shared that the 2nd room was finally ready. However, the fact of the matter was it was ready 3 hours past the advertised check in time and I had to follow up with them. Major points deducted. 

ROOM

Like other Yelpers, I'm feeling the trendy decor. However, for the cost and reputation of a W hotel I found the rooms to be lacking.  Our corner suite was just a queen bed. Why-- where's the king? The room layout was odd too. Like others mentioned, it advertises "space" but the strange layout appears to just be an attempt to have a room. Certain room amenities are also missing:

- drawer space
- a KING bed-- if you're sellin' sex and mayhem provide proper spaces!
- outlets near your bed (They should invest in the nightstands or lights that have outlets. Not the cheap Ikea nightstands. This is a huge pet peeve (can't you tell- lol) and provided that Austin boasts of being such a techie city I'm taken aback with the lack of outlets near the bed.). On a positive note, they do have a charging station with hook ups for older iPhones, iPhone 6 and Android phones.
- no coffee maker 

SERVICE

- 24 hour room service
- guests can text the front desk their needs
- concierge
- the staff was friendly

NIGHT LIFE

Not a local? Or are you a local 25-40 year old? The 4 linked louges provide a energetic night spot with a little bit of something for everyone. If you're staying a night, make sure to check it out. In town or a local weary of the same "6th Street" crowd- come here.  There are 4 different rooms providing a little bit for everyone at this venue.  

Happy Hour is also from 7pm to 10pm.

LOCATION

Within walking distance to the downtown mayhem.

Input: Not very authentic and so-so tasting in comparison to Thai restaurants in Los Angeles. Since it has good reviews on Yelp, my brother and I decided to give it a try. The Tom-Kha soup..what the hell!! First of all, Tom Kha is supposed to be WHITE and not orange. I didn't taste the lemongrass, lime leaf or lime at all. The soup was supposed to be sour, not too spicy and a bit salty. All we tasted was sweet and way too much coconut milk. The soup was not supposed to be thick. It tasted more like a red curry to us. The sea bass fillet with garlic, chilli and lime (pla ma-nao) was decent.  Papaya salad (som-tum) was not bad and it came with sticky rice (kao-niew) and 3 very thin slices of pork jerky. I told them a few times not to put ground peanuts in, but they still put 2 spoonful on it. Chicken with basil leaves (pad-kra pow) was okay. 

Anyway, service was pretty good. 

I know I shouldn't compare this place to those in Hollywood, but since I've lived in Los Angeles for 7+ years and spent many years in Thailand, I know what real, authetic Thai food tastes like. It's not too bad if you like the Americanized style, but it's just not for me.

Input: First time to FBS was for a Thanksgiving eve party. I went with a group of friends. First impressions are the location is a bit strange and difficult to locate on our first attempt, we needed to drive around the block to find it. The Kendall neighborhood is supposedly up and coming with bars and more nightlife which could benefit this spot drastically.

The interior decor is spacey and modern with some elements of street grit to go  along with the tech design aspects. The elevated Dj stand is a cool touch... We wondered all night " how the hell did the Dj get up there?!"

The bar left something to be desired. Not a great selection. Not many flavored vodkas and they don't serve any energy drinks or Heineken. Also my drinks were taxed every time I ordered, seemed a bit strange to get a bill each time for 4.36$ for a 4$ beer. Seems like a pain in the ass for the bartenders...I haven't experienced that before.  On 1 trip to the bar I asked the bartender how much my beer was to quiz him and he charged me the $4 . Seems like he just didn't want to go through the hassle of collecting change.

All in all this place is cool, haven't tried the food, one friend reminded me that it looked like Toro in boston and that it's more of a bar/ grill so i have to try the food sometime. The open kitchen is a nice touch. Judging solely on the nightlife aspect it could use some work promoting but I liked the crowd that showed up and Cambridge is awesome so it has potential.

Input: Because I enjoyed the last visit, I decided to try them again to see how some of their other items stacked up.  The breakfast burritos are very large, but honestly?  Eh.  The eggs tasted overdone, like when there is a lot of browning on scrambled eggs.  Maybe some folks like that but it really wasn't for me. I guess some folks prefer it that way?

We also ordered a quesadilla (my roommate isn't too adventurous) and wow, disappointed.  :(

Listen I get it's a quesadilla.  It's cheese in a tortilla.  But after trying it, I can honestly make better ones at home.  Chipotle of all places makes a better quesadilla.  This one was folded into thirds and large portions of tortilla had no cheese at all (which is probably why they rolled it into thirds).  But because of this, large amounts were just tortilla.  The tortilla was also cracker crispy at points and chewy in others, despite both lacking cheese on them. The whole thing was just bland overall.  Again I get it's cheese plus tortilla, but it wasn't very good despite being one of the simplest things one could order.

I think Victoricos does some dishes super well.  Their street tacos (lengua, so good) were amazing.  So I'm not bashing them, but I feel like quality is really inconsistent based on what you order/when you order it. Just a little disappointing.  I prefer Don Pedro's in Portland.  They can rock a breakfast burrito and also serve menudo.

Input: I always refer to Southpark Meadows as the place where Austin's average restaurants end up. This is no different. 

Service was friendly. I have no issue with that. Prices were steep and on par with Pappadeaux. But the food wasn't as good. 

We tried the charbroiled oysters which were probably the best of the meal. In fact, I have grilled up something similar before. The raw oysters were small and unremarkable save for the fact that this was my first venture to eat raw oysters since I became ill from a selection at Pappadeaux back in 2009. I am happy to report no ill effects here and I am back on the oyster band wagon. Port A Cafe does have happy hour prices on shrimp and oysters which might be interesting one day.

My Crawfish po boy was edible even with the crawfish being cold. I expect it's fried up in a batch, reheated later and served. Fries were hot and tasty, but I only had a few bites of those. But the price of this was a ridiculous 13.95! Compare that to Cawfish Shack and Oyster Bar on Wells Branch where a similar yet superior offering is 6.95!

My wife had a salad with a bowl of clam chowder. She always likes chowder and had no complaints. 

Happy hour does look interesting with a selection of 3 for $5 sliders made from fish. That might get me back in. For a lunch or dinner destination it's unlikely I will return.

Input: I debated between 3 and 4 stars for awhile and 3 stars won. I want to give it 3.5 stars... I can understand why people would not like this place, but I actually like it. Usually.

I've gone there a good number of evenings during the week with friends after working out, when I want food and some beer but don't really want to shower or care too much. On most weekday evenings, it's not too packed. The menu is HUGE (so you can always find what you're craving) and all the food is... good. Nothing I've found so far is too amazing, nothing is horrible. It's a bit pricey (aka not cheap) but the portions are huge so I'm mostly forgiving. They have an extensive beer/wine/cocktail list as well, and you can get pitchers of things like beer or sangria. And it's all tasty. Right after work and on weekends, it gets a bit more crowded, but not too bad.

They have about a million TVs, which is great when you just want to chill at the bar, or watch a random sports game (one time my friend wanted to watch the WVU game, so the bartender changed one of the TVs for him, which was awesome). However, when big sporting events are on, it gets super crowded and rowdy and the crowd quickly escalates into drunken douchedom. 

Last Sunday, we went for the all-you-can eat buffet for $16.99 for the first time. It was actually a pretty good deal. Drinks weren't included, and the service was spotty (our waiter gave us multiple death glares when we asked for things like iced tea or water). But they have a selection of standard breakfast items (pancakes, eggs benedict, scrambled eggs, french toast, hash browns, toast/bagels, etc.), some lunch items (which I didn't try, so can't comment on), a "make your own omelet" station, fruit and desserts. Some things were a bit dried out- I was excited for eggs benedict and pancakes and both disappointed me. But I ate about 20 pounds of bacon so that redeemed my meal for me. Overall, a fairly good deal.

Input: Let me just start off with saying that their queso and quesadillas are fantastic. The chips and salsa are also very good. The soft tacos are awesome! So why am I giving this place 3-stars instead of 4 or even 5? Simple, the service is absolutely not there.

Colibri has a ton of potential, and a lot of competition in the area. You think the service would be impeccable, due to the competition and amazing view of the lake. Wrong.

I've been to this establishment on several occasions and the company I work for frequently orders from this great restaurant. Nonetheless, I feel as if the service is just lack-luster, from when I've dined in and have taken food to-go.

I've stood at the front of the hostess area for 3 minutes while two employees are folding towels or something at the very front, and when I told them that I was picking up, they directed me to the bar. It would have been nice if you had told me 3 minutes ago...

It doesn't seem like anyone is happy to be there. It's just bland. Maybe it's just me being in a beautiful town like Baldwin Park, but I'd expect the restaurant to be a few steps above the Subway and Five Guys just a few blocks away in terms of service. It isn't. What a let down.

I picked up a carry-out order of some tacos that I was informed were part of the Taco Tuesday promotion, and was told by the manager that it's for dine-in only. This wasn't mentioned or listed anywhere on the website or on their menu. Nonetheless, the manager gave me the promotional discount, but let me know that it's for dine-in only. No problem and the gesture was greatly appreciated. The issue still stands: This exception wasn't mentioned anywhere, and it took me being vocally frustrated to the manager to get the promotion. The person who took my order over the phone did not let me know either, though. Regardless, the tacos I received (and a hearty bag of chips and salsa, which I've only received one out of the two times I've ordered carry-out, but a GREAT gesture nonetheless!) were excellent. I'm not sure if the chips and salsa are included with every to-go order or not, though...

If you would like solid food with an incredible view of Lake Baldwin, you won't be disappointed by Colibri. If you're expecting great service, you're going to have mixed feelings about this place like I do. As I mentioned before, the restaurant has a lot of opportunity to improve with their service. Having servers being more proactive, more relatable, more friendly, and more attentive would make this place easily up there as the best Baldwin Park establishment.

Just note that the Taco Tuesday special (and I assume every daily special) is dine-in only.

Input: We came in on a Thursday, probably around 5pm when nobody was in the restaurant, but a little after about three more tables had been sat. I found this place on Yelp actually, as one of the better places to have dessert in Coquitlam. 
I ordered a Peach Ice Tea, a Cotton Candy Frappe and a Brussels Melowna Waffle (Their liege waffle machine was broken so I had no choice). Their peach ice tea is amazing, it's not too sweet but not too plain, it definately tasted like peaches, it's actually comparable to 'Good Drink' if anyone's has that before (It's bomb, you gotta try them). My waffle had white chocolate, cantaloupe, melon and melona ice cream on it, the Brussels waffle wasn't too bad, it wasn't sweet at all, almost need a little bit of sugar actually. But it wasn't bad compared to other I've had. The fruit pieces were really sweet but didn't mix well with the waffle, luckily the melona ice cream did! Overall it was a good dessert dish just cause I could eat the fruit alone and eat the ice cream with the waffle and both were tasty, it could've used a little bit more white chocolate drizzle tho just because the little bit that was on there, pretty much froze up from the ice cream and I could barely taste it and it would've helped the plainness of the waffle. My boyfriend ordered the cotton candy frappe and it was sweet, he didn't finish it, but what do you expect from a cotton candy drink LOL 
Atmosphere: The decorations felt a little but rustic-hipstery, the store was really spacious because of the high ceilings and the huge hallway(?) in the middle that lead up to the counter. The place looked new and clean, but nothing amazing.
Service: The girl greeted, seated and brought us menus right as we entered, she took our order and brought our food but we had to pay at the counter, I always find that intresting and question whether you're supposed to tip or not, but there was a tip jar so I suppose it's a pooled tip. The employees always looked like they were doing something rather than just sitting around for customers, which seems to happen a lot at places that aren't that busy. I found it intresting that they had table menus but they also had a large board up with the food menus on them sort of like a quick service restaurant. 

Food: 4/5
Atmosphere: 3/5
Service:3/5

I'm rarely in this area, so I'm not sure if I'll be back, but that doesn't mean I wouldn't recommend it, for being near the mall and in Coquitlam, it's not a bad waffle place, maybe they should consider putting bubble tea on their menu to start competing with Ninja BBT cause Ninja BBT actually came up first under desserts in Coquitlam.

Input: Marriott's SpringHill Suites in Portland needs an upgrade from the '70's in decor and some help in service and upkeep, but it was an all right hotel stay.  I wouldn't stay here again due to the noise and some service issues.

I'm a Marriott rewards member, so I chose this hotel for the points after scouring many Yelp reviews for a hotel in Portland by the airport.  I stayed here for a couple of nights.  

Check-in was easy, with an odd request to fill out a separate piece of paper regarding the car I had, promising I wouldn't park anywhere I wasn't supposed to, yadda yadda.  Haven't seen that at a hotel before.

The hotel room came with a mini fridge, small microwave and sink area, along with a pull-out sofa, desk, flatscreen, and a full length mirror which I thought was a bonus.  The sink is separate from the shower and toilet.  The bed was comfortable, as well as the pillows. Loved the light canceling curtains.  Ironing board and iron in the closet along with a blow dryer. 

The only complimentary toiletries are Paul Mitchell brand shampoo, conditioner and lotion with bar soap.  Anything else, be prepared to purchase it in the mini convenience store next to the front desk.  Glad I packed Q-tips.  

No room service here.  They have a swimming pool and whirlpool, but I didn't use them.

Free breakfast from 4-10 am was nice. You can make your own waffle, and they had an assortment of fresh fruit along with scrambled eggs, sausage links, oatmeal, yogurt, cold cereal, breads, juices and milks.  The second night I was there, the serving area was packed and lucked out on finding somewhere to sit.  Other people were taking their food to their rooms to eat.

Went to watch TV one night and couldn't get the TV to turn on.  After fiddling around, figured out that it wasn't plugged in!  Then, after settling back into bed, the freaking remote required me to push each button 5-10 times before it would register.  Put some fresh batteries into the remote!  They don't offer a movie menu - that really stunk.  

Another night, I went downstairs at about 9 pm to buy something to drink from the mini store and no one was at the front desk.  Another guest came over and asked me for directions.  Not having my cell phone to help her out, we were both standing around for ten minutes before I gave up, put the drinks back and went back to my room. There was a sign on the desk that the one employee had stepped away for a minute.  That said, have your break later at night when clients aren't going to be needing assistance.

Be prepared to hear planes, trains and automobiles.  Also, you'll hear your neighbors showering, talking, banging suitcases, etc. as the walls are paper thin.

The elevator is slow, and hearing the door scrape, metal on metal, slowly every time it opened and closed killed the ears.  Get that fixed.

Input: This is a review for take-out only.  I started out exceedingly skeptical because it's just so expensive for the amount of food that you get.  Also, their menus seem a bit messed up - their takeout menu is somewhat minimal compared to the regular menu, and when I called they said their takeout counter was actually closed and to order off the regular menu.  Well there are two versions of their regular menu on their site - the one that's written on the "menu" page that doesn't include the "combos" section (not sure why), and then the menu you get from the Download button that does, but lists the prices incorrectly compared to what they actually charge in the restaurant.  They've got a little housekeeping to do.  I was also pretty damn sad that there was no bbq sauce included with my takeout order.  Fix please!

The bottom line on the food:  The burnt ends are hands down the BEST burnt ends I've ever had in my life.  Ever ever ever.  Like, the crack version of meat.  Oh my god.

Everything else was underwhelming.  My bf said the brisket was good, but to me it looked like a slab of grey meat.  Their side game is pretty weak, both in terms of the choices and quality.  My boyfriend doesn't eat pork and doesn't like coleslaw, so really all I could get him was the cornbread and the seasonal side.  The cornbread is definitely good, but the seasonal side was sliced zucchini, essentially raw, with a sprinkle of cheese, a ton of cilantro, and really no dressing to speak of.  Super weird, and really not worth any $.  The beans were tasty but nothing to write home about, and the pimento mac + cheese is super gross cold.  Warmed up I actually really liked it, but acknowledge that it's an acquired taste and that I had the luxury of a microwave. It sounds like from other reviews that they serve it pretty cold in the restaurant.  I wish they had more sides, and that they were better.

So, the burnt ends themselves would get 10 stars - I will pay absolutely whatever they want to charge for a bulk order of that.  Everything else though, or eating in at the restaurant, isn't really worth it as of now.  Perhaps they'll improve as they get a bit older!

Sure, we could do multiple loads at once, but we ended up finding a few detergent stains on our clothes and the whole experience cost us ~$25 to wash and dry two loads of laundry. Here's hoping our washer is fixed sooner than later!

The rooms are decent but the bathrooms are quite narrow. I'm not a very large man but felt like one in the bathroom (see photo). Otherwise, the rooms are perfectly fine and offer some beautiful views of the water and downtown Portland.

I was there at least 24 hours and I was a little surprised. Not only unsightly, but also opens it up for whoever wants to take it. Just unusual for a Marriott. 

But I guess the major disappointment came when I wanted to try out their highly-rated restaurant, Truss. It has great reviews so I set out about 7:00 pm to dine there, only to be met with a sign that said "Sorry We Missed You." They were closed, even though they were advertised to be open at that time. 

My loss, I'm sure. 

I went down to the lobby bar restaurant and had dinner. A steak salad that was very good. 

So all in all, a nice hotel and I'd stay again. Just hope to be able to try Truss.

The Thai Tea and Lee's Coffee were absolutely delicious and quenched my thirst immediately. The Thai Tea wasn't too sweet and had a creamy flavor from the splash of half and half. The coffee was sweet from the condensed milk, which complemented the shots of dark espresso very well.  I'd definitely come back for a Lee's coffee, which will keep me awake all day.

Input: ****************************3.5 stars**************************************

So on Cinco de mayo me and some buddies decided to celebrate this mexican holiday (and my bday) by going out and getting some food and drinks (hopefully on the cheap). So we were set up to go to no mas cantina at 7:30 (not a good idea). when we drove by it was packed to the brim everyone was waiting outside and it was a 2 hour wait for food and that was just an estimate (which is ridiculous). seeing our options dwindle we decided to head to mid-town and check out the prickly pear. 20 min later when we got there it was a cluster-f*ck. It was an apparent Cinco de Mayo 'block party' being thrown by two restaurants. Forget trying to put ure name a list of any sort it was complete mayhem and drunk guys to boot. Usually its not an issue but since the lady was in town this didn't bode over well with me. seeing an open table we sat down thinking it was part of the 'block party' but apparently Marlow's Tavern wasn't part of it. But seeing as we didn't want any part of any cluster-f*ck we decided to stay. menus were delivered promptly and the waiter came out to get our drink orders. 

Looking at the prices on the menu it didn't really jump out as expensive or pricey, pretty much on par with say 6 feet under or any other atl establishment. So off we went to order. Since i was hungry and wanted to drink i didn't wanna get anything too filling so the lady and i decided to just do appetizers. We ordered firecracker shrimp ($10), marlow's tavern sampler ($12) and some fried calamari ($11). And keeping with the theme we also got a margarita ($8) and a blueberry mojito ($8). 

So as we waited we just enjoyed the festivities and chatted up with some buddies. 15 min later as conversation was running dry and my buzz slowly slipping away i could wait no longer and jumped over next door to prickly pear to grab a drink. when i got back there were our drinks, oh well more for me. There was also an apparent mistake and two margaritas were delivered. So making quick work of the one in my hand, we continued to talk. Soon after, the food arrived and not a moment too soon. 

The food was nothing too special but well executed nonetheless. The sampler, which included shrimp and crab nachos, firecracker shrimp, and hummus was pretty good. Nachos were nice and cheesy and the filling was sufficient. Fire cracker shrimp were crisp and tender not over fried but seemed like it was just fancy Long John Silver's. the hummus tasted home made and earthy but had a layer of oil on the top so i didn't really know what to make out of it, but it was still good. The bigger order of firecracker shrimp was also well fried. The calamari was a little disappointing. Pieces stuck together and some of the tentacle pieces were a bit over cooked and dry. At least the cocktails were good. The lady really enjoyed her blueberry mojito (too bad she could order only 1 since they ran out of blueberry liquor). and the margarita i had could've been a bit stronger but its a cocktail so i wasn't expecting much liquor in it anyways. 

Overall Marlow's tavern was accommodating for a busy night. Their appetizers are good but nothing special. Their cocktails are better than their food but could be a bit stronger. and their prices are right on par with a restaurant of their caliber. I'd come back if i was in the area... dunno if i'd make the trek out here solely for the food since parking can be hectic... Decent food, Good drinks, good atmosphere, decent service.... Happy eating...

Input: I LOVE french food. So when my chance to go to Little Robbie's, I gladly accepted! Here was the biggest problem - We drove into the South End, because sadly I moved out of Back Bay into the suburbs - and I COULD NOT find a parking space to save my life. We drove around for 20 minutes... and in the heat, that does not go well in my book! We resorted to suing valet parking. Here was the worst part of this parking dilemma - the valet circled around - driving my car for 20 minutes and I saw my car pass me, sitting outside approximately 20 times. WHAT IS UP WITH THAT!? So DON'T valet park - the valet guy thinks its his car to cruise around the streets! 

Let me get to the better stuff - they sat us right away - the service staff were friendly and kept coming by frequently to refill water glasses and make sure we didn't need anything. 

We started with the trio of pate - it was good - didn't like the chicken liver part but it's an acquired taste so it doesn't hurt my impression of the restaurant. We also ordered escargot and it was Sooooo good! The bread was hot and toasty that we devoured it quickly with the pate and escargot. I had the Chicken coq au vin with buttered noodle. I was hesitant at first because of the buttered noodle but the waiter explained its not what I would think and he was right - I couldn't taste any butter. I probably won't have coq au vin only because I didn't like the red wine reduction as much as I thought but the food was still extremely tasty. My friend had the special - the rabbit leg - and as an act of bravery, I took a bite and it was extremely delicious! I should have ordered it!!! Better than chicken! My fiance ordered the rack of lamb and I didn't try that but had a bit of the potato that came with it and the sauce was delicious! 

We also had dessert - I had the profiterole with vanilla ice cream and fudge - it was sweet and I probably won't have it again but worth a try. My fiance had the Creme Brulee and they did it JUST RIGHT! YUMMY!! Our friend had the Frepe Suzette and that was good too. 

The experience was good only if I didn't see the valet driver driving my car up and down the street so many times during my stay at the restaurant.

Input: My take on this joint...

- It's different than the other bars and clubs around time. Instead of smashed against by a bunch of drunk horny people, you can sit at a table, drink your drink and sing along with the piano playing men...and laugh at those who go on stage and make a fool of themselves.

- The bar is full-service and there are a few very cute male bartenders there too. For those who love to take shots, they have a list of some fun, innovative ones to indulge in, but steer clear of the Gorilla Fart shot. It tastes and feels just as bad as it sounds. It's warm 151 and wild turkey...ick!

- The people are a nice blend of Central Florida residents/natives and tourists which makes for an interesting crowd. A lot of bachelorette and birthday parties happen here which can get kind of annoying.

- You can win a free happy hour party for you and up to 100 friends which means free and very cheap drinks, the place to yourself for 2 hours and some food. However, don't get too excited because the food usually consists of hot dogs, nachos with that fake, canned cheese and salsa.

- This place doesn't serve any kind of food aside from the happy hour parties, so eat beforehand. The good thing is that there a large number of restaurants surrounding it.

- For the most part, the servers are nice, but I've run into a few snobby and rude gals though.

-The women's bathroom attendant is by far my favorite part about this place. She is a loud, proud African American woman and she is always saying some off-the-wall but honest stuff. Love her!

Overall, it's okay. I don't make the long trip to I-drive often but I'll go for a special occasion every now and again.

Input: El Sapo is located on the crowded Manor Rd where a bunch of other well known restaurants reside.  The location has been multiple establishments and the original building is a formatted auto shop.  The layout of the place gives outdoor seating to enjoy the sun or fully A/C indoor area with tables and a very large bar.  This places focuses really on two things.  Unique burgers and unique drinks all served in mason jars.  You can get burgers with jalapenos, black beans, fried egg, guacamole and other options.
I ordered an El Azul and my friend got the El Chilie.  The burgers are well sized and cooked about well done.  It is a flat wide patty cut burger.  Buns are toasted, toppings are very fresh.  As always a burger place gets judged by the beef.  It has an average flavor, no seasoning, and cooked well with decent texture.  My friend got the queso fries which are freshly cut fries topped with grilled onions and the queso sauce.  I felt the fries could have used some seasoning on them also.  The onion rings I got were thin cut, decent amount but very average breading.  Dude, whats up with no salt & pepper on the table.  I mean shouldn't that be a standard at a place serving burgers?  Drinks are served in the mason jars.  They also serve milk shakes and banana splits for dessert.  
Now this place would be great if you want to go just for drinks.  The alcohol drink menu seemed to have a good variety and you can sit up at the bar or lounge outside out on the bench seating.  This place is a good addition to the east side spots and I would go back.  I just felt the taste for a $10+ burger was a bit average.  Its a good cooked burger but it is not amazing and I would probably know several other burger spots I would pick besides El Sapo.

Input: The Rundown:
I would give Shanghai Fresh 3.5 stars if that was possible.  Authentic flavors and style, but misses the mark in terms of actual quality.  

Context:
Came here for dinner.  I am Shanghainese and have spent several years living in the city.

What I got:
Beef and Scallion Rolls (7.5/10)
I know this dish as Taiwanese (forgive me if I'm wrong on this), but one of my friends recommended it so we ended up getting it.  Surprisingly, this ended up being the best dish I had.  The flavors are quite simple - a scallion pancake wrapped around beef with some hoisin sauce for flavor.  The highlight is of course the beef - which was cooked and seasoned well.  The actual roll itself was a bit too doughy for my taste, but overall I was very satisfied with this dish.  Would likely order it again on a repeat visit.

Shanghai Soup Dumplings (7/10)
These were very nearly the best soup dumplings I've had in Boston - but unfortunately there's a critical flaw.  In terms of flavor and texture, they're spot on.  The thin skin was steamed well, the filling was the proper amount of savory, and as a whole it was quite satisfying.  So what's the issue? The soup.  There was nearly no soup in my soup dumplings, which is really a shame because the rest of the dumpling is quite good!  This problem is further exacerbated by how many of our XLB were stuck to the bottom of the basket, making it nearly impossible to eat without spilling some of the (already limited) soup. 

Traditional Style Sweet & Sour Pork (7/10)
I didn't expect the pork to be breaded, which was fine I guess. The actual flavor was traditional and certainly reminded me of home - this is what sweet and sour should taste like.  However, the stuff this sauce was covering was rather underwhelming - the pork hardly even tasted like meat for some reason and the breading added very little to the dish.

Rice Balls Simmered in Sweet Rice Wine (6/10)
A traditional Shanghainese dessert - not exactly done to its full potential here.  The rice balls were fine - although that's pretty hard to mess up.  The issue of course, is with the broth.  To put it simply, the "rice wine" part of the soup is vastly overpowered by the "sweet" part.  This dish is supposed to properly balance these two aspects and have a much more prominent rice wine flavor.  This is almost entirely absent and the end result is mostly just sweet.  Fine - but I wouldn't get it again.

Input: Ok, I'm big on sushi and have been to many places around the country and in Japan.  Almost all of my reviews are of sushi places.  I originally went to O-ya but they were booked up so they recommended that we go to Oishii.   

Here's my rating:
Decor ****
-The decor is very modern and hip
Service **
-The sushi took a long time to prepare.  I was very shocked with the price of one of the specials, i'll write more about this later. 
Sushi ***
-I had some traditional pieces, no rolls.  The fish freshness was average.  The Katsuo did not taste very good.  The fish wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't very fresh. The maguro was not that fresh.    I'm also not a fan of seeing all the piles of sushi in the sushi bar cases all wrapped up in cellophane.  This tells me that the restaurant buys the fish in bulk and holds if for longer periods of time.  This may be a Boston thing.  I also find it strange that no one sits at the sushi bar.  Note that the price is for one piece.  I didn't read carefully so we had to wait another 30 min to get a second order.   We ordered 10 pieces for 2 guys.  I would think that the waiter would recognize that i misread the # of pieces per order.  Why would 2 guys order 5 pieces each, where every piece was different?

Overall my experience here was ok.  Here's what really bothered me.  I asked the waiter about the fois gras sushi on the menu which was $15.  I asked him to compare it to the "special" fois gras sushi that was not on the menu.  He highly recommended the special fois gras.   I expected it to be more expensive, perhaps $20 or $25.  But when i got the bill, it showed $50!!  I feel like the waiter should be obligated to mention the price if it's more than 3x the price of the similar one on the menu.  You can get a lot of good sushi for $50.  The special was good, but not $50 good.  I felt deceived.  This is why i gave the service **.  I certainly will not be coming back and will make reservations at O-ya in the future.

Input: Stayed here as part of a Costco and Disney package. Checked in well after midnight and the staff in duty was excellent. Day two we had no issues. Sheets not being changed. Ice bucket not being cleaned and ice bag not being replaced. These things are minor but you would expect it to be taken care of. Not to mention housekeeping really has nothing to say to guest in passing in the halls. I've stayed at other hotels and staff is pleasant in passing. 

If housekeeping were like the front of house I'd be rating a four to five star. But housekeeping needs some work. Overall the place is nice. The pool, fitness room, kid zone, the little store. It's all nice. The American restaurant is a little pricey though. Maybe that's why it seemed empty most of our stay. If you find yourself here it's not as bad as some others say. But see for yourself!

Input: I never dine in here, so this review is purely based on the food and take-out/delivery service. 

When my roommates and I moved to JP this was the first place we dined at and I'm pretty sure we didn't eat anywhere else for at least the first three days while we were getting unpacked/situated in the new place. The menu is massive to the point of being pretty overwhelming the first time you want to order something, but it's pretty fair to say that it has more hits than misses. Some of my favorites include their loaded skins, the Texan, the Columbian, and my roommates all swear by the Chicken Ranch as well as their pizza. Some disappointments I've had include their chicken fingers as well as their Top Shelf Italian. 

The staff are usually pretty friendly, but as I stated before, I usually just order take-out from this place. It's super convenient that you can call in to order or just do it on their website. Also, I once accidentally ordered take-out from their Roxbury location but went to pick it up at the JP spot and they were super friendly about it (even though I felt like an idiot) and made my sandwich for me fairly quickly. Also, on their website, I'm in love with the "preparing" icon of an animated knife cutting a tomato. 

All in all, it's a more than decent sandwich shop that is priced incredibly reasonably, particularly due to the fact that often one sandwich will feed me for two meals.

Input: This place is a flat out 3.5 stars for me based on their services, atmosphere and the food itself.
I've been here twice. Both at peak hours of the day and week. Luckily I was able to find seating for 2 and seating for 5. Its a pretty small place and parking is also limited. The people working behind the counter generally only speak Chinese with limited English. Like when you order in English, you should just tell them the number vs what it actually is cause they may not catch you properly. It doesn't look like they have a system on how their orders should be or how to serve people. So in other words, there may be a long wait for you or your order may be wrong. 

I also want to say, if you hate the smell of durian I suggest you to not stay here for long or even walk in. Once they make one durian dessert,  the whole place smells like durian. From what I remember, they have durian pancake and mochi. I also witness this one time that this customer ordered mango pancake, But cause you can't see the inside of the pancake, she got the durian one. Man, she spat it right out and was hardcore looking for water. It was such a funny scene. I totally understand how she felt when you were thinking it's mango in the middle but you got durian. 

The food itself is ok. No complaints nor is there one thing I love a lot that I have to go back for it. But I think in order to enjoy the dessert properly, I suggest you to take it to go. This place does make good mango desserts hence the name mango yummy. But personally I just don't like being in the store for too long. I would suggest people to come and try it out if you enjoy mango and don't mind the smell of durian.

Input: Its Kroger right? Welllll if you had ever gone into this location before the remodel, you would understand that this is NOT the same store. I graduated from OSU and lived on 8th for 2 years and avoided that old scary run down Kroger as much as possible. 

NOW....Since I was in the area, and there is not a Kroger very close to my current home I stopped in. This place is great. There is plenty of well lit parking, everything is well organized and neat on the shelves. 

I was not impressed with their selection of local produce from local farmers. It looked like it had not been watered, and needed to be restocked. Buying local is important to people these days. Having the display is a step in the right direction, but a "fail" based on what the produce looked like.

Also, I may have liked it better if someone had asked me if they could help me find anything. It still throws me off sometimes that the "Natural Foods" section is on the other side of the store as all the "other foods(?)" sections. I thought it was all edible food...but who am I?

A competetor store is closeset to my home location, but they cannot compete with Krogers prices. That is definately something that will keep me coming back, especially to this shiny new store.

There were plenty of cashiers waiting at the check out, and the bagger even helped me to unload my cart. Good stuff!

Upon leaving, the police officers in the parking lot made me take a second look. A Tuesday evening in a Kroger might be a dangerous place?...hmmm

Overall, a giant step in the right direction, but needs help keeping the momentum.

Input: Some places are hyped up and can't live up to it, other places are praised and have stood the test of time for good reason; Mr. Bartley's is certainly that of the latter. Right in the middle-of-it-all on Mass. Ave in Harvard Square, this family run business has been serving up Boston's best burgers for almost fifty years, and they're not afraid to show it. Bombarded by "Best of" signs from any publication possible and Boston memorabilia scattered throughout, Bartley's has no shame in showing its the tops and that its all Boston all the time. But do they live up to it? Well, yes, mostly. Listing over thirty burgers on the big board, there's something for everyone, not to mention house made Raspberry Lime Rickey's (superb) and frappes (also superb). For around ten dollars you get a burger with fries or onion rings and a pickle. The burgers aren't huge, weighing in at 7 oz., but honestly, I can't say that I need much more then that these days anyway. One of us receives a very generous portion of onion rings while I seem to be lacking on the french fry end. The fries are good, solid, if unspectacular. The onion rings, however, are beyond awful. Limp, mealy and downright offensive, they have to be among the worst I've had in some time. The burgers, ground daily from choice beef, are nice, they come served on a delightful toasted sesame bun and my burger (the Tom Werner) comes with bacon and cheddar cheese. The first thing I notice is the cheese, as it oozes its way from all sides of the patty into melted cheese heaven, there is a perfect symphony of bread, meat and cheese in the first few bites. After that, however, I feel a little dryness, not in the burger itself, which is juicy, just not overly-so, but without condiments included in the sandwich, I feel the need to add some ketchup. (thankfully we're not at Louis Lunch) Ketchup could go either way for me, if I need it so be it, but its not a make or break situation, in this case I do need something, and I'm okay with that. My last few bites are all bread unfortunately, a big pet peeve of mine, and the meat was good, nice flavor, but not the best I've had. I will compliment them in that they are the first place to actually cook my burger properly. ( in this case a nice and red medium-rare) The waitress also offers a follow-up inquiry upon first bite to make sure it is cooked to my liking, so a huge compliment for that. Maybe its not the best burger we've had yet, but its up there, and there is something about this place you can't help but love. Maybe its the history, the fact that its still a family run establishment and all the sites, smells and sounds of a great burger place are all prevalent. Worth all the press and accolades? I'd say so, but still not burger perfection.

Input: Porter Square Books is conveniently located close to where I live, so it's usually the first place I'll check if I'm looking for a book. Sometimes it's the only place I have to look, but often I have to check somewhere else. Maybe I'm looking for some pretty unpopular titles. 

More likely it's that PSB is-- relatively speaking-- a tiny store, a good portion of which is occupied by the cafe. That said, the selection is a pretty decent cross section but it's a tad dilettantish. While it's not Waldenbooks (are they still around?) or the South Station book stand, it still feels like any generic bookstore you might find at any other mall.

 I wonder if they might do better or worse by cutting back on the mass market stock and bulking up on more quirky and/or niche-market titles. With the space they're working with,  it seems like the only thing that is giving them any competitive edge over the good bookstore and great bookstore just a mile or so east on Mass Ave is the Cafe. 

It's a decent bookstore, and a conveniently local one (for me), but it could benefit from a little focus.

Input: Truthfully:  1 star in the Winter and 4 stars in the Summer.  

I know that averages 2 stars but as it is now Spring and there is no more rain, snow, sleet, "winter mix", and other painful things that fall from the merciless skies- I'll give it 3 stars.

I get to Charlestown Bridge at least 4 times a week, seeing as I live in the North End and my grocery store, my running route, some restaurants, lots of people I know, and church lies in Charlestown.  I know you are saying, why not use the locks in the winter?  It just adds so much more distance to my pedestrian commute.  :P  

In the winter, there is no place with more wind, rain, and anger being forced onto you as this bridge.  The street turns into massive puddles that become tsunamis when buses and bad Boston drivers splash through them.  I've seen the splashes go up to 15 feet high and have been splashed so many times my SADD seems more than justified.  

I know the gratings scare people, but I've learned that bridges were built to hold 5 times their maximum possible strain.  Still, it can be scary to look down through the grating during a storm and see the white caps and get reminded of scenes from Perfect Storm.

Anyways, it is Spring now, which means the bridge is beautiful again.  In no time, the bums will come back to live in the abandoned rotational tower and all will be well again.  At night, the bridge is beautifully lit up- more like a midway carnival booth and not in mood lighting like Zakim Bunker Hill Bridge or the TD Garden.  

Recommendation- walk on the left side of the road on the way to Charlestown to avoid the tourists and their silly picture taking.  It also allows you to descend to Paul Revere park easier.

Input: So cruising for a place for breakfast and noticed cultivate opened in the new development off of howell mill. Clicked on the post and instantly saw RUMCHATA FRENCH TOAST and I instantly said this is the place for me! I mean who wouldn't love Rumchata French's Toast, right!!?!!! 

A friend and I arrived to the restaurant and it looks really cool, great decor, Uber modern fun pop'ish art and inviting.  We were greeted by the host and sat down in the coffee bar area, the environment was terrific, and felt like it was almost out of a west elm catalog... (kudos to the decorator) 

Our server was friendly and attentive along with anyone we came into contact with during the course of our meal. At one point my friend made a comment there seems to be more workers than patrons in the restaurant and as I looked around he wasn't kidding... everyone looked happy and worked together in a unified team of people who really enjoyed where they were working...

Ok, now down to business... 
there was no doubt in my mind that I was gonna get those Rumchata French Toast... but after viewing the menu, I was instantly thrown in a conundrum of am I making the right decision. I questioned my need for what I really came here to experience because  EVERYTHING LOOKED D'LISH!!!! 

Holding on strong, I stuck to my gut and got the Rumchata French Toast and a cup of coffee, my friend got the Breakfast sandwich with and extra dalup of pimento cheese... because, you know, duh, why not (!!?!) and an ice tea.

To my dismay the coffee wasn't as yummy as I was hoping... Maybe it's was because it was just stronger than I expected? Maybe it's because of the acidity? Maybe it was just not a good batch? Maybe it wasn't the kind of coffee I was hoping? Maybe my taste buds were just off today? Maybe, maybe. I typically like a medium mild smooth coffee - so maybe it was just me. Maybe. The cream, yes- I like cream in my coffee curled the moment I poured it into my cup but it didn't smell bad so I thought well maybe it's just me being a brat.. it wasn't sour but also didn't look great in my morning cup of joe. 

Sigh, ok- I know you want to know my thoughts on this infamous Rumchata French Toast I've been going on and on about - it was super disappointing and I regretted every moment of this decision, especially when I looked around and saw everyone else's plate and, it ALLL LOOK AMAZING! 

Rumchata French Toast Review:
When my meal arrived it was a plate of toast with a side squirt of whip cream, a side of mixed berries and a small ramekin of a berry compote - question mark??? It also came with some very liquidity syrup.... I don't know about you but 'i think' syrup should have a more dense consistency? What do I know... 
 
But trying to be open minded I dug into my meal....
um......
WHERE WAS THE RUMCHATA!?!?! 
Again, 
WHERE WAS THE RUMCHATA!?!?! 

The French Toast was dry, (maybe not dipped in the batter long enough? ) with a hint of cinnamon. So, what does one do, add more drippy syrup and oh how about the compote... ok, lil'l better- thank goodness for the side of dry berries, it helped. 

So in conclusion - Rumchata  French Toast - not good. So Sorry. But you can't when them all right? 

On the other hand- the breakfast sandwich was fabulous! It was everything my friend could ever want in the world and he enjoyed every bite!! 

Looking around the avocado toast looked just as yummy ...

So, sorry for the long drawn out review...
Don't know if I'll be back... but glad I tried this place.

Input: I've visited twice now, and while the food (or at least the one thing I ordered twice) is astounding, I don't think I'll be in a rush to return. Why not? Because they're clearly not in a rush to serve it.

That delicious dish that I ordered twice? Their poké bowl. It's fan-frickin-tastic. A healthy portion of ahi tuna served over a bed of rice and cabbage and god-knows-what else. It's perfectly portioned, hearty and healthy and really, just amazing.

So what's my problem? The wait. On my first visit, I waited 30 minutes for my meal. There was only one guy in the cart, and he apologized for the wait, saying that usually he has his wife there with him. It was frustrating, but he had a good excuse and the food was delicious, so I vowed to come back. I returned today, when the husband-wife team was both in action, and waited 40 minutes for the same dish. Again, delicious food. Again, apologies for the wait. I'd be much more likely to believe them if they were actually hustling to get stuff out, but they were moving around with what I saw as no sense of urgency. I get that you're serving island food, but I'm not on island time. I have meetings to attend and places to be, and waiting this long for food from a cart? Not ok.

At this point, the only way I'd return is if it were on a weekend and I was enjoying some beers in the pod, with nowhere else to be. One last time, the food is delicious. It just takes way, way too long to get out to you.

Input: This looks like it's going to be somewhat of an unpopular opinion... but I was not as impressed with Mediterranean Exploration Company as I would have liked to have been. But also, this review is for the happy hour only, so take from that what you will.

Food + Drinks:
- Octopus ($13): This is the thing that I saw on Yelp that made me go "Aha! I want to go there," because I love octopus-- especially grilled octopus. The presentation was of course, lovely, but to be perfectly honest, I did not think it was flavored as well as it could have been. I thought it was cooked well, with the right amount of chewiness, but the flavor was somewhat lacking. I have had better.

- Bacon wrapped date ($1 ea): This was alright. They replaced the pit of the date with an almond, which made for a nice crunch at the center. I feel like you can never go wrong with a good bacon wrapped date, but it wasn't anything wow-worthy. Pretty standard.

- Greek potatoes ($5): These Greek potatoes were a surprise hit with out table. We initially skipped out on ordering them, but we wanted more food, and I, being a big fan of anything potato, wanted to try them. The outsides were perfectly crispy and the seasoning was yummy.

- Hummus "Pitriyot" ($11): I loved the addition of mushrooms to this hummus. That made the hummus more unique and scrumptious. What I liked less was the price tag and the fact that the hummus came with a lone piece of pita. In order to eat all of that hummus with the one pita bread, I feel like you'd have to heap a small mountain of hummus onto each bite of pita. We ended up asking for another pita which unfortunately, took a rather long time to come out, so i resorted to just eating spoonfuls of hummus by itself. Which was not bad. But also not my ideal way of eating hummus. And yes, I know the pita is freshly baked, which may account for the long wait time for pita.

- Radicchio ($8): I am kind of obsessed with the radicchio salad at Pollo Bravo/Toro Bravo, so I really wanted to try the radicchio salad here. It was literally the first thing I decided to order. Did not like this version of the radicchio salad as much as the Pollo Bravo version, but this also wasn't bad. As one would expect, the MEC version has a way more mediterranean flair to it, though I did feel like the yogurt dressing got a bit overwhelming for me after a while.

- Turkish Coffee Stout ($3): I am a fan of coffee stouts, and this one did not disappoint.

Service: Eh, it was alright. Our server didn't seem particularly knowledgeable about the menu. We would ask him questions and he would always have to go back and check, before returning to give us an answer.

My overall impression of MEC was that it was a fine restaurant. Tapas style, so obviously everything is meant to be shared. And with tapas restaurants, unless you order a ton of food, you probably won't end up super full by the time you finish. 

tl;dr: My main reason for the three stars is that while the food was fine, it wasn't really wow-worthy for me, yet it was accompanied by a high price tag. Granted, this is my opinion of happy hour only. Given all the high praise that MEC is getting on Yelp, I wouldn't mind coming back to try a full dinner here.

Input: I have been dying to go to this place since I heard about it on Vancity Buzz. I'm glad that a Facebook friend notified everyone in a status that you have to make a reservation before going or you will likely be turned away. So I made a reservation for today, about three weeks ago or so.

My best friend who loves cats as much as me came with me. It was a bit of a bitch to find the place, as it was in the International Village mall, but luckily we have excellent time management skills and got down there early enough to find it without being late. We checked into the cafe side of it. There you will find an assortment of pastries and drinks available to order, along with some cat paraphernalia available for purchase (shirts, books, travel mugs, etc).

We then went into the cat part of the Catfe and signed the waiver, read the rules about interacting with the cats. There were seven cats but we saw about 4 as a couple were sleeping. I felt a little bad for the cats; I mean, I'm glad that this business has helped with the adoption of the cats (they had to shut the place for a bit due to lack of cats) but most of them looked frightened or distressed. It makes sense, being surrounded by people all day.

And that was part of the problem I felt: so few cats and way too many people. The literal opposite of the type of place I want to be in. Everybody is crowding around the three cats available so getting time to interact with them is difficult. Or so many people gather that it scares them and they skitter away. 

The space they have to roam around is wonderful! Cubbies on the walls, tunnels, plenty of toys. It's great. The price to get in is 8 bucks or 5 bucks if you purchase a treat from the cafe side. The food is a bit pricey but I didn't really care. There is also more souvenirs available for purchase on the cat side: earrings, coin purses, pins. I got a cute little coin purse in the shape of a cat face/head.

So, seeing as I can't compare this place to anything else, as I have not been to anything like it, I'm giving it three stars. I wasn't wowed by it, but I'm glad I visited. You have an hour there and my friend and I left after 25 minutes. Plenty of time in my opinion. Something that stuck with me after is how I would rather volunteer at the SPCA as I feel I would get better/more interaction with the animals there than I did here. I don't know if I will return. I feel like I understand what this place is. It's a cool concept, and it's still new and working out the kinks. So maybe in time it will be better.
