Input: Stopped in on a Wednesday night and found out that it was Restaurant week - place was packed! We found two spots at the bar and took them quickly. 
As always, I like the style of the place - yellow lit bar an overall modern and cool vibe. Ppl are all nicely dressed and the bar always seems to have a few bleached blonde ladies with their well-groomed man friends.
It's really crazy how we've had an almost identical experience every time we've come. Here's the summary: bar tender comes over, very friendly and cool. Gives advice and seems knowledgeable. We order our food, excited. There are always mistakes with the food. They apologize and fix it quickly. And a manager always comes to apologize, offering a discount for the mistake. We enjoy the food, then the bar tender forgets about us. Except this time he didn't forget about us.
Anyway, my fiancée got a petite syrah, which was nice - strong and full bodied,  but still fairly smooth. I got the Red Wedding, as it was featured in a magazine we were looking at (weird) and sounds SO good. I was disappointed. It had a pleasant mild flavor - but with all those great ingredients, I was expecting lots of flavor. This was bland and uninteresting. My fiancée thought it was fine - she doesn't like sweet drinks like I do.
We ordered the restaurant week deal (which was excellent, price-wise) and an additional meal.
Again, the place was packed, which explains why the food took forever, but it really took forever - like probably 15-20 minutes to get the appetizer. It was supposed to be a beet salad, but ended up being chowder. Which they took back after the bar tender seemed pretty dumbfounded. And didn't seem to care or apologize to us. The beet salad then took another 15 minutes. The salad itself was good - decent size and well flavored.
We then ordered the Norwegian salmon and stuffed chicken breast.
My fiancé liked the salmon - came in a butternut squash and apple puree. I thought the salmon wasn't strongly flavored (seasoning or fishy-wise), but the puree was really good and together they were great. She liked the salmon on it's own.
The stuffed chicken was pretty incredible. Stuffed with prosciutto and gouda, cooked really crispy. Really flavorful and pretty great. Mashed potatoes were also really flavorful and seasoned - really good. Also, the Brussels sprouts were well seasoned and nice and crispy. Entire meal was great. 
We ordered the blackcherry cheesecake for dessert. Turns out they were out of it, which they didn't realize until it was time to bring it out. They gave us some sort of chocolate ball stuffed with chocolate moose. It was quite good. 
Food was excellent, service was terrible. We waited so long for the food that my fiancée really wanted to leave. 
Manager came over, apologized, and gave us a discount. Very apologetic and nice. Too bad that things went wrong in order for that to happen. Again.

All Sofra would need to do is put up a few signs asking people to order before they sit, which plenty of cafes do successfully. Also, the vast majority of the patrons seem to sit at their tables for hours after finishing their meals. Not sure there is much that Sofra can do about this, but it makes it challenging for people to find seating to eat (literally only need to sit for 15 minutes to eat my meal, but even that is a challenge, and nearly impossible if there are more than 2 in your party). 

I used to overlook the cramped / impossible seating and the challenging parking enough to go to Sofra with regularity, but without the pita, I am less likely to make the trip (and my husband has emphatically declared that he will not be returning until the pita is brought back!).

 https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/midori-sushi-austin?select=FANdLnlLHVYa9bl0T7pgKA

Input: We stopped in for Restaurant Week, and were pleasantly surprised to see that pretty much their entire menu was available for the $28 prix fixe. You could get any appetizer except the table-side guacamole, and any entree, though the crab cake appetizer was $3 extra and the steak entrees were $5 extra. You don't have a choice in dessert though, everyone gets the Tres Leches. 

We both ordered margaritas - mine had pomegranate juice in it, and my wife's had mango. Neither were particularly good, they were WAY too salty, and that was even before any of the salt on the rim fell in. Once I let the ice in mine melt to dilute it, it tasted a bit better. But overall, a $22 mistake. 

The appetizers were good. My wife got Queso Fundido and I got Empanadas de Hongos. The queso was way too much for one person, but with the empanadas you only get three small ones, so that's a bit more difficult to share. 

For entrees, she got the Enchiladas Mixtas and I got the Salmon Manchamanteles. From the description, she thought that she would be getting three enchiladas with one major listed ingredient (skirt steak, grilled chicken, chorizo) each, but what you get is two enchiladas with all three ingredients mixed together. The salmon wasn't wild-caught but it wasn't advertised as such on the menu either. It wasn't bad. I liked the mole manchamanteles that came with the salmon, and the plantains were good. 

After all that, we ended up getting the tres leches to go. Overall, I liked the meal and my wife just thought it was OK. Even with restaurant week, it seemed too expensive for what you got. We didn't regret coming but we probably won't be back.

Input: What can I say about SilverCity Riverport?  It's kind of your average Cineplex - there's not much to differentiate one from the other these days.  This one has I think 19 theatres (!), but this means there are usually multiple showings per day of large commercial blockbusters - still no room for indie movies, although there is the occasionally Bollywood or classic film shown.  Hit up 5th Avenue Cinemas on Burrard if you want to see award-nominated films or things reviewed in the New Yorker. 

Some cool features of this Cineplex are: "serve yourself" beverage machines that allow you to customize your drink - for instance - you want a low/no calorie beverage? Click the button.  Want Coke Zero, Diet Coke, or Diet Sprite? Click the button.  Want Vanilla, Cherry, Strawberry, Lime or Orange Diet Coke? Click the button.  You see where I'm going with this.  World of Coke in Atlanta (Coke's world headquarters) has a tasting room with these exact same machines that is basically their main attraction, so having the machines handy at SilverCity Riverport is kinda nice.  They also have a full "Poptastic" popcorn centre, which is like Kernels, with lots of pre-popped flavoured popcorn on offer (this month's flavour? Maple Bacon.  UGH.)

I will say that I have had some good service interactions there.  On the last cheap Tuesday I went to, I bought my ticket at the automated kiosk ($7.50), while my friend went through the traditional line ($6.75).  I asked why there was a difference in price and a manager immediately came out to inquire as to how he could help, took note to call the programmers for his automated machines to change the price, and refunded me the difference.  You don't necessarily expect places like Cineplex to have great customer service but I was really pleased, anyway.

Input: I purchased my vehicle in 2018, it was a used vehicle and I was doing a trade in. I was ''offered'' 4K less than what my car was worth first off. Then I provided my Kelly Blue Book code which shows the true value of my vehicle... they took the code and revised my trade in amount, eventually resulting in a deal. But must do your own research or they will bite on the unknowledgeable person!

Second, my car purchase came with lifetime oil changes...A++. I recently went in for an oil change AND a wheel alignment. I brought my vehicle in at 4pm and it was miraculously complete at 4:59 which already was suspicious as they shut service down at 5pm.

Not to my surprise I was charged for a wheel alignment and the only service that was done was an oil change! They even printed out a before and after report of my wheel alignment. Pah!

I was baffled that a technician and management would really do this to a customer. Someone could of easily said ''we couldn't get to that today, would you mind coming back?'' Or something along those lines. That's good business and transparent to a buyer. That's what builds trust and a returning customer. I knew my car I knew an alignment was not done. So I called them to let them know this isn't right. They never apologized to me and I went back the next day. They quickly put me in the waiting area and ''re-did'' my wheel alignment.

Just know your car, your values and do your own research. 

The people in the customer service area however generally were polite to leave this on a positive note.

Input: Review of the AYCE Sushi option.

We were dropping off my sister at the Orlando airport and it started to downpour. I mean you can't see one foot in front of you rain. Instead of driving through the rain to get back to Tampa, we decided to find someplace to eat dinner and wait out the rain. This means that I didn't have a chance to do the meticulous research I normally do before going somewhere. Instead I pulled up sushi restaurants in our general vicinity with a good rating and off we went. 

There are four options of ordering here. You can get AYCE Korean BBQ, AYCE Sushi/Sashimi, AYCE Korean BBQ/Sushi/Sashimi, or order off the menu. We went with the AYCE Sushi/Sashimi which was about $17 a person. 

I noticed that many of the rolls are either deep fried or include cream cheese. The AYCE option doesn't really include your healthier or more creative options. I actually ended up liking the spicy crab the best (it may be that it was good and I felt somewhat healthy eating it). We also tried the Golden California Roll, the Yummy Yummy Roll, the Las Vegas Roll, and the Volcano Roll. They were all perfectly fine, but nothing great. We also got Salmon and Escolar Sashimi. I found the Escolar to be a little fishy. The Salmon was ok. 

If you're looking to eat a ton for relatively cheap, then this is the place for you. Since I rather have quality over quantity I'm not a huge fan of this place. That being said, I will have to come back sometime to try the AYCE Korean BBQ.

Input: Ruth's Chris has always been my go-to steak place. When it's done correctly you won't find a more flavorful steak. A good steak doesn't need steak sauce but bearnaise sauce is the perfect compliment to the perfect steak at Ruth's. You can get a baked potato or mashed potatoes anywhere so do yourself a favor and get the au gratin potatoes. They're meant to be shared but if you're dining with me you'll need to get your own (yes, I eat them all). Ruth's creme brulee is consistently the best I've had anywhere. And I've had it at a lot of places supposedly known for their creme brulee. None have matched Ruth's. Nice and creamy with the perfect caramelized sugar crust on top.  

I only get to go to Ruth's once or twice a year so the anticipation of the deliciousness I know I will experience is high. On a recent visit before a show at Atlanta Symphony Hall we didn't have reservations so we sat in the bar. It was only 6:00pm but the service was slow. Took forever for someone to acknowledge us and take our order. The servers were friendly but we had two different ones who seemed a bit distracted and not really communicating with each other (both delivered the same check to us). The steak came undercooked (medium rare when I asked for medium), the plate was not sizzling hot, and it was drowning in butter. It took a bit to get their attention so I could send the steak back to be cooked more. When it came back the plate was sizzling (yay!) but the steak was once again drowning in butter (I literally soaked up the excess butter with bread). The perfect steak comes on Ruth's signature 500-degree plate with just enough butter you should hold your napkin up until the sizzle dies down a bit to prevent any splatter. If the temperature of the steak is undercooked just slightly you can cut it and place it briefly against the sizzling hot plate to finish it. On this particular visit the steak was too undercooked and the first plate not hot enough to be able to finish cooking.

Sometime in the last year Ruth's has begun charging $5 for a very small ramekin of bearnaise sauce. I understand an upcharge if you ask for your steak to have a peppercorn or blue cheese crust but it doesn't seem right to have Ruth's nickel and dime you for a sauce that used to be complimentary. Especially when they only give you a tablespoon or two--if that. For a couple bucks more you could have an entire vegetable side or dessert.

While ambiance is not why I go to Ruth's the ones connected to an Embassy Suites hotel are a bit lackluster and don't seem to be on par with what you expect from Ruth's. There were a lot of teens and pre-teens in the bar who were clearly just staying at the hotel which made the atmosphere very casual with a different kind of energy than you come to expect when dining at Ruth's. You wouldn't find that at a stand-alone location. I've had numerous four and five-star visits to Ruth's--I'm beginning to wonder if that's still possible?

Input: It had been a few years since I'd last visited a Flatbread location, and I'd so enjoyed my last meal that I eagerly anticipated a visit to their Davis Square location. Oddly enough, the restaurant is co-located with a bowling alley, which detracts considerably from the experience simply due to the often-overwhelming noise level. This becomes a particularly acute problem during interactions with the staff.

Dropping in on a Sunday afternoon, I was pleasantly surprised that we were seated without delay. I though for sure that given the bowling alley, there would be a wait. Shortly after sitting, our waiter stopped by, and after providing the day's specials, he understandingly departed just as quickly since we hadn't yet had a chance to review the menu. Despite two excellent-sounding specials, I instead chose Flatbread's take on my favorite type of pizza: a sausage, sun-dried tomato, caramelized onion, and mushroom offering. I paired this with an Opa Opa Winter Warmer, though I received Opa Opa's Winter Strong Ale instead because the Warmer was no longer available; I'd have preferred that the waiter ask me for an alternate choice rather than making the decision for me, regardless of whether or not I would have ultimately ordered the Strong Ale.

Our pizzas arrived quickly, and noticing that it was sliced into rectangles, I grabbed my first sliver without hesitation. I was not disappointed by my choice in any way. The bold flavors of the maple fennel sausage and sun-dried tomatoes worked well together, while the mushrooms and caramelized onions added a noticeable and pleasing depth to the mix. The dough is thicker than I prefer, though far from a deep-dish style, and neither significantly enhances nor unduly detracts from the pizza. In almost no time at all, I finished three quarters of a large pizza, contradicting Flatbread's proposition that this size could comfortably feed two people.

I truly enjoyed my pizza, but the noise level, combined with the waiter choosing an alternative beer for me, marred my experience. As for the physical location itself, it is sparsely decorated save an expansive montage of images of Davis Square. The kitchen is open, allowing diners to watch as the staff deftly spins pizza dough in the air and carefully navigates the two large, wood-fired ovens. Despite their worn appearance, the chairs are also quite comfortable. The ambiance overall is very relaxed, making for a nice way to spend a Sunday afternoon or to unwind after a round of bowling.

Input: On Boxing Day, we headed out to Steveston to avoid the crowds (before attempting to dive into them again later in the day).  Sure enough, the village was eerily quiet.  I felt like I was playing The Walking Dead, but that may have been because I was playing it everyday for the past few days.  (It's a really good game; download it now.) Of course, everything was closed, including Tapenade Bistro.  We walked around and ended up at Cimona Cafe for some brunch.

The special of the day sounded interesting -- steak omelette ($9.49).  At that price, I couldn't say no, but I was also a bit hesitant because of the price.  I wondered about the quiche-like dishes neighbouring tables were dining upon, only to realize that they were also actually omelettes.  I'm not picky on tradition and I do like quiches, so I didn't mind.  This was somewhat disappointing.  The steak was probably the worst part of the omelette, since the meat was quite tough and lacked flavour.  I also disliked the tomatoes, but that's just because of my distaste for them.

I also contemplated getting the country omelette ($8.49), filled with bacon, mushroom, and cheese -- which Doro ended up getting.  This was much better.  The bacon had flavour! And bacon and mushroom is always good.  The hashbrowns that came with all the dishes were just alright -- kind of dry, but lightly seasoned.  They reminded me of the ones from SFU Dining, which I'm also unenthusiastic about, unless they're slathered with gravy and egg.

Kem had the old favourite ($9.99), with choice of meat, eggs, hashbrowns, and pancakes.  The pancakes were somewhat fluffy, but they weren't that exciting.  It kind of felt like a fancier version of the breakfast at Bob's Subs, but I actually prefer Bob's way more.  Shredded hashbrowns are so much better.  And it's greasier and cheaper there.  Doro also ordered a french toast ($1) which was also just decent.  It seemed like it wanted to be a HK style french toast, but it also wanted to be a bit more traditional as well. Meh.

Cimona was okay.  I didn't really enjoy anything particularly, but it wasn't that bad at all (except for maybe the steak in my omelette).  Prices are fairly low, but if I wanted a cheap breakfast, I would just head to Bob's instead.

The restaurant is fairly neat and tidy. They are not wheel chair friendly. To use the bathroom facility, you have to go up a flight of stairs for women, and for men you have to go down a flight of stairs. 

Will I go again? For the wings? it's a definite YES

Input: I have a new groomer! yaaay!

I've been loyal to my neighborhood boutique dog store and groomers because it's an easy walk down the street, they offer great prices, and are friendly.  But I decided to "cheat" on them just to try something different for my dog's birthday, and I have to say... I think I'm about to enter a new relationship, lol :)

LOCATION: Off Cheshire Bridge road, right next to an Auto Body Shop (at the intersection of Woodland Avenue). It's suuuper easy to miss since it sits back from the road and isn't very noticeable. (It's close to Gail Fabrics)

PRICING: They have some general prices on the website, but you will have to call to get a quote as it will be based on the size, coat, etc. They are a bit more pricey than most groomers, but not by too much. For example, I usually pay between $42-$50 to get my toy dog groomed, but they charged me $60. 

DECOR/ATMOSPHERE: I must say, it's not as "pretty" as the boutique retail dog stores you may find nestled in Midtown or places near, but it is clean and neat. Its similar to most dog daycares/groomers with concrete floors instead of wood. I love that they have a lobby area where you can sit down-- a lot of places weirdly enough don't have that, lol. I also love that they have grooming station up front where they have your dog when you come in, they do a few last touches and voila your dog is ready to go!

CUSTOMER SERVICE: Pleasant. No issues thus far, let's hope it stays that way! Barry was also very friendly and nice-- which is important.

GROOMING: Fantastic!  I got the full groom and it took about 6 hours.  The cut was more precise, blended, and complimentary to my dog's body than ever before. My dog was also very happy and relaxed when I got there which made me feel like they took good care of him and were gentle with him. I've gone to some places and my dog seemed super anxious, like he couldn't wait to leave the place, lol! But this time he was happy, tongue out, tail wagging-- all the stuff a parent wants to see! Also the groomer owns dogs, including two poodles, which means he knows first hand how to take care of them and deal with their hair type. My only gripe is that I don't think they cleaned my dog's ears good enough, it was still a little hairy and waxy-- which is a no no for hairy breeds. 

SUMMARY: All in all this place gets an A in my book. It's a little pricier than other groomers, and takes a couple hours longer, but the groomer does a solid job. My little pooch will start to go here on a regular. I may go to my neighborhood spot sometimes since it's so close and they often can take my dog same day, but still at the very least my dog will certainly get all his cuts here.

***UPDATE***: While I love the clips given by Canine House of Style, the last time my dog received a cut he came back with TWO gnashes/knicks-- one large area on his foot, red and bleeding, and another on his private area, red, scabby, and long. It took 2 days for the bright redness to mellow down to a deep pink... this really is unacceptable. They should have ATLEAST acknowledged the clearly new wounds from the shave or cut they gave, but instead they just handed him to me like everything was okay. Very Disappointing. Also, his nails were uneven-- clip them, then file please... don't give a rush job. Lastly, while the girl upfront who wears glasses is always very nice, calm, and mellow the other one is sort of loud and aggressive-- basically she comes across too strong at times and talks really fast. I'd much prefer her to be a little more calm in her tone.  With all that said I have to change my 5 star review to 3 stars, well more like 2.5 but I'll round up to 3 for now. Hopefully they do better next time or else I'll have to change it to 1... I really hope they stop rushing and accidentally cutting my dog to the point that he draws blood.

Input: I'd rate this new location at 3.5 stars.  Their menu is grammatically correct and properly laid out, which is already a good sign for Kissimmee.  We tried a few items, as their menu is extensive.  The traditional cheese pie was actually very good.  I'm not sure it would survive the cut in NY, but this is actually NY style pizza, as Avanti claims.  No sauces for the crusts, nothing stuffed into anything and one choice of crust thickness, just like pizza should be.

We also tried the Buffalo wings, which were quite good.  Other ancillary items - mozzarella sticks, onion rings, and fries were obviously frozen food service items and fine but nothing special.  Garlic knots were good, as is the case when pizza crust is authentic.  They could have used a garlic butter sauce rather than being served dry, but they did travel better.

This was a delivery order; oddly enough we live less than a half mile away but the order took an hour to reach us and as a result, the pizza could have been hotter.  They also need to learn how to prepare a Styrofoam box so that items inside aren't wilted by trapped steam.  Avanti has been open at this location only a couple months, so there's time to smooth out the details.

All in all, we were pleased and welcome Avanti to the area as a new pizza location.  Prices are fair and I don't believe there's a delivery charge (though there is a $15 order minimum).  They also offer calzones, strombolis, hot and cold subs, gyros, empanadas, salads, all kinds of appetizers and desserts.  There's always a warning flag when one restaurant tries to trade in all manners of cuisine, but if you stick to the Italian specialties and pizza, Avanti is worth checking out.

3/17/16 - UPDATE (Critical)
I have to unfortunately remove two stars from this review.  After several tries, they just can't seem to work out delivery times.  That's probably because the entire operation takes up a corner of the counter in a Mobile gas station.  We found this out when we ordered 4 cannolis (we had a credit from a nearly 90 minute order delay previously.  The desserts, which are filled with sweetened ricotta cheese, were bad.  As in, rancid.

We called to make sure they stopped using it and planned to return the next day after it became clear that the service girl 1, refused to let us speak to a manager; 2, refused to give us or did not know the street address; and 3, instead of crediting the dessert back to us actually charged us again.

The next day we called the manager (or gas station owner) and he clearly did not understand the overcharge and neither of them had understood their food was bad so never pulled it from the shelf.  We went down in person and worked everything out.  To his credit, the gentleman was very courteous and tried to make everything right.  Unfortunately, this is a pizza made in a gas station, has had problematic health inspections twice since August, 2015, and customer service is lacking.  

The pizza is still good, but we cannot recommend this establishment for health safety concerns.

Input: PARKING: Big gravel lot.

ATMOSPHERE: Yikes. This isn't some pretty "industrial" rebuild in the pearl district, it's the real deal. Cold, spartan, almost spooky, like you could imagine a slasher flick being filmed here. It's cavernous, not intimate. Cold this time of year. Wear a warm jacket, maybe a hat. Big TV (projection, I think) with sports, but no sound. Music was unmemorable. What I do remember is the awful speakers, probably not helped by the acoustics of the place. Tables were basically slabs of wood on wheeled steel frames, presumably because this is a working brewery that's only open to the public on weekends. One of the crazy things about this place is the two-stool bar! 

SERVICE: Kinda lousy, but no big deal. Don't be timid and dainty, and you should be fine. This ain't Applebees, you won't have a perky polo-shirt-clad server.

BEER: Quite the barrel program here. I didn't realize. I had three, found them to be solid, with just one offputting flaw (or possibly deliberate; one never knows).  

FOOD: I hear there's a cart outside, but I didn't see it. 

PRESENTATION: Glassware is style-appropriate.

PRICE/VALUE: Printed taplist and chalkboard taplist is unpriced, but I know what beer goes for in this town, so I knew what to expect (except for that San Diego outfit...you know what I mean). But then I noticed off to the side of the taplist it says all beers are $5. Pour size varies from 4oz to a pint (16 I guess, they didn't look imperial). I think I saw a mention of $4 on Mondays, and there's a HH discount but I didn't see that mentioned anywhere (Shhh, don't tell them I told you).

RESTROOMS: Through an office and down a winding hallway, apparently shared with other tenants of the building, I would guess. Two, single occupancy. Funny, I was distracted by a bulletin board, and they both became occupied at the same, so I laughed at myself for being an idiot, and moved on. 

OVERALL:
I think this a love-it-or-hate-it place. I'm more on the hate side, but I do like the interesting approach to beer (weird one-off stuff). Maybe I'll try again when it's warm and the door is open.

Input: The fresh spring rolls here were excellent. Unfortunately, I ordered the shrimp ones for takeout that were supposed to come with avocado. There was no avocado in them. Boo. I loved the dipping sauces they came with, though!

I also had the mango cucumber salad, which was refreshing, but overpriced.

Finally, this irked me: I saw the bartender sipping on a Thai iced tea and got a craving, so I asked for one. The man behind the register (who I believe to be the manager) gave me a pseudo-confused look and asked, "Excuse me?" I repeated, "Could I get a Thai iced tea?" He sighed and said, "We don't have Thai iced tea here." I replied, "Oh, I thought I just saw him drinking one," and pointed at the bartender. The drink in question was beside him. The manager then changed his story and said, "Oh, well, we have the ingredients so the staff sometimes makes them for themselves. But we don't have that on the menu." "Oh...so I can't order one?" "No. But we are considering adding them to the menu." Umm...what? If you have the ingredients (which are most likely just condensed milk and either a powder or a syrup, I doubt the staff is brewing the stuff from scratch) then you can't just mix one up for me? Especially after I observed one of the staff members drinking one? Not exactly wonderful customer service.

It was a little expensive for Vietnamese food. I would get the spring rolls again but probably not a full meal.

Input: Getting my nails done is a treat yo self type of thing that I'm willing to spend big bucks on. I love getting a fullest and will spend good money to get them done nicely. I read the great reviews for the salon and was super excited to go! And my visit did go very well! I got a mani-pedi and the pedicure was one of the best pedicures I have ever gotten in my life. They really massaged my feet and just overall I had a fantastic experience. I got a fullest with a power dip top coat. The technician I had, Amy, took her time and was in no hurry. My nails look fantastic and I was extremely happy. 
Until two days later and when putting away the dishes in my house, of my nails came off. My pedicure had chipped too and I was also slightly upset but it was the nail that really made triggered. I called the salon and made an appointment for the next day. I came in 15 minutes early to my appointment and told them that I had an appointment but they wouldn't take me. I waited 45 minutes, had three people come in and get helped before I finally spoke up quite annoyed and said I had an appointment for 30 minutes ago and that all I need was one replacement nail. When they finally helped me I was literally done in 7 minutes so I didn't understand why I had to wait 45 minutes for that little job. They did the replacement nail for free which was nice but also kinda a given because it fell off with no provocation two days after and I also waited a ton even though I had an appointment.
A week later two of my nails came off and by then I was just fed up. They treat you really nice and take their time but their services are just not durable. I spent a total of $96 and had three nails come off within a week an a half. I treat my nails well because I spend so much money on them and for the full set to just come apart a week later really annoyed me. I really liked the salon and the technicians but their services are just not worth the money. Input: We were starving when we pulled in here, it was lunch time and people were really piling in. We started out with wings, which sort of threw me off, since they were going to rock it all fancy and just add lines of ranch of and buffalo sauce over the top. Like some fancy ice cream sundae. Applause for originality here, but boos for, where the hell is the sauce? I uploaded a picture of them and no I was not drunk when I snapped it, just appears that way.

They had an okay flavor, and then I added a Mozzarella salad for $2.95 and was surprised by the the size, the flavor was good. I was feeling pretty hopeful about my selection of shrimp tacos. My son had the cream of broccoli soup, which was pretty good, he gave me the last 1/2 cup of it or so. The small version was pretty large and he said it was getting really rich. 

Then they lost their other two yelp stars after that, the shrimp tacos were a major let down. Zip on the flavor and lots of stale chips on the side. Oh, they were pretty reds and blues, but tasted like they'd sat out all week. the shrimp tacos and chips came with two tiny cups of a sauce and salsa, not enough to dip chips, if you even were considering it and barely enough to add to the shrimp to bring em back to life. I asked for extra sauce, and the waitress didn't remember to bring it, and I was pretty much over it by that point. 

They are friendly enough, but if I had to do it again, I might have stuck with the lunch special for $5.95, in the picture it looks really small, but we saw them going by and it would have been plenty. My son had a lunch pizza and said it was really good and said the crust was really light.

Input: I went to Texas Roadhouse for a late lunch with my family last weekend. We were a party of 7. Since one member of our group was late to meet us we decided to wait on her before being seated. After we had been there a little while one of the hostesses pointed out that there was a table that could seat 7 open at the bar, and we should go ahead and grab that, since it could be awhile for another large table to open up. 

The table at the bar was an odd L-shaped booth, but we managed to fit. Our server, Tiffany, was really good. She was on top of things and was able to answer all of our questions.

For an appetizer I ordered the fried pickles. A couple people commented that they were too salty, but I thought they were pretty good. They were thin sliced dill pickles with a thin, crispy breading. And of course while we were waiting on the meals we all stuffed ourselves with the rolls and cinnamon butter. Those things are addictive, and our server kept bringing more.

Our meals were really good. The kids ribs portion was great, my daughter really liked that. The chicken critters are a huge pile of chicken tenders, and could easily be split between two people. Actually, most of the entrees were large enough to split. I had the chicken critter salad and had the tenders tossed in buffalo sauce, that was really good.

The only negative in our whole meal was that one of us had ordered chili, and it came out cold. And out of the whole meal that was the one time Tiffany wasn't around to check on us. After a few minutes of staring at the cold chili, one of us actually got up and walked it over to the kitchen. A fresh bowl of chili was brought out shortly, but really, that shouldn't have happened.

And I'll second the other reviewers, I don't like peanut shells on the floor. Why do restaurants keep doing that? There is a warning outside about peanut allergies, and that just makes the whole peanut shells everywhere thing seem even more pointless. Why do something that is messy and harmful to some people?

Input: My boyfriend and I came for brunch on our one-year anniversary. We had a reservation so we were seated quickly. The decorations were a little lacking - not very elegant. Thin, green carpets and beige everywhere. 

Service was also, sadly, not up to par, especially for a really nice restaurant. We had to request water each time our glasses were empty. When our server brought our dessert, he just plunked it in front of us and walked away, greeting the table behind us cheerily. We may be just college students, but my boyfriend is notorious for 25%+ tips. Not this time. 

Food was A-OK. The appetizers of fruit kebabs were all right, but my boyfriend loved the dipping sauce. 
  My boyfriend ordered the fried chicken florentine and claimed the chicken was the best he ever had - he could cut it with the back of his knife. The wilted spinach was allright, but lacked flavor: some garlic would have been great. 
  I ordered the flight of french toast. The syrup was sooo good, but sadly, my french toast was in a pool of it, making it way too sweet. The french toast also had a thin layer of creamy white stuff - mascarpone perhaps? Overall pretty tasty, but hard to justify the $14.95 it cost. 
  The heavenly cheesecake was, in short, heavenly. It was light and fluffy, not at all like the heavy dense cheesecakes many places serve. The strawberries with the cracked pepper balsamic was delicious. 

Overall, the experience was all right. The view was great, the food was ok (not quite worth the price), and the service was lacking. We may come back during dinner just to catch the sunset, but afterwards, we probably won't come again. There are many restaurants that have phenomenal food that match the prices.

Input: Add Russian to the growing list of diverse Portland food cart cuisine that I've had. I'm not sure if this is the first Russian cart Portland's had, but still a rare find. The owners of this cart are from Moscow and want to give the people here a taste of what Russia has to offer. The menu here contains items like pelmeni, borscht, and piroshky.

Piroshky are usually baked buns that can be stuffed with a wide variety of fillings. Savory fillings can have meat or no meat, while sweet fillings are usually fruit-based.

I first tried the piroshky with lamb, potato, and onion ($2.49). A good, light blend of seasonings on the filling.  The potatoes were soft and the lamb retained some juiciness. The bun itself looked like a flat strudel-like item.

The "Very Berry" Piroshky ($2.49) at this cart is not a filled bun, but a flattened biscuit with berry jelly and a maraschino cherry on top. I do wish the jelly got injected into the bun here instead of having it spread on top. That way, I'm more likely to get the jelly in my mouth instead of having it end up in the container. It ended up being a bit messy.

All in all, two comforting food items. Nothing extremely memorable on this visit, though.

I'm not an expert on Russian food, so I can't speak to its authenticity. But hey, with very reasonable prices, this cart is worth a stop.

Input: I stayed here for a wedding for three nights. Overall I had a good experience, but there were a few things about the place that were just frustrating.

First, the good: the rooms were a decent size. Comfy beds. Sunlit with large windows that open and blackout shades. Located next to the T green line at the last stop Riverside. Good shower. Nice bar/restaurant with decent hotel food and a great post-wedding atmosphere. Cool pool area for evening lounging.

Now the less good...

1) service: I didn't feel the staff was that knowledgable or helpful.  In particular, We asked about areas to run and getting around without a car (best transportation options, are the surrounding streets walkable, etc). They didn't tell me anything beyond what I learned from basic google searching, and I am from out of state and unfamiliar with the area. 

2) Room amenities: no mini fridge, just one room temperature bottle of Fiji water. No ice or vending machines on our floor. Okay, it seems petty, but I had no way to keep anything (like a bottled water) cold! 

Then I am a heavy sleeper, but the door rattled all day and night from some sort of draft in the hall. The dead bolt didn't help, so we put our bag in front of it. If I were a light sleeper this would have been maddening.

The elevators were painfully slow, and during cleaning hours it seems they shut one down for the maids, so the one functioning elevator was always packed on a busy weekend. We wound up taking the steps each time to our 6 floor room, which wasn't bad because the lobby level is 2 and I actually prefer stairs. But if I had mobility problems, (again) the constant wait would have been maddening.

No room service printed menu, only a fuzzy one on the TV channels that is hard to read.

3) location in relation to Boston: if you stay here, rent a car. Being a NYer without a car, I saw it was next to public transit and thought it wouldn't be necessary. We were pretty stranded there and ordered delivery when we missed lunch. It also takes 45 mins to 55 mins to get into the city once on the train. It took us 45 mins each way to get to and from Fenway one weekend afternoon. Compared to NY or even DC, the T is just really, really slow. Plus a bunch of the ticket machines at the riverside station are in the sun and you can't really see the screen, so on BC'a alumni weekend, we waited in line to buy our T tickets because three of the machines aren't usable. If your main draw to the area is to see Boston, don't pick this place. But I could see it being a good location if you have a car or if you are going to be in the Boston College area. It was a $50 cab from Amtrak South Station. We had the wedding rate all weekend, so it was worth staying further out. But I notice the regular rates are very pricey, and I wouldn't have paid that much to be so far from the city otherwise.

We asked the hotel where we could walk to get food, and we were told to take the train several stops to Newton Center. Please see above commentary on the T.

Bottom line: yeah, it is a nice hotel. Some small issues could be bigger for other people. And it's location could be good or bad depending in your situation. Biggest negative was I wasn't overly impressed by the front desk.

Input: Review from an in-frequent gambler.
Seek table, odds, or dealer info from someone else. 
I was here for the concert entertainment.

I enjoy gambling on cruise ships. They are encouraged to have patience and help everyone play the games. Here, I felt the glances, head shakes and scowling of players and staff.

OK, I'll pick up my chips and go home.

This is no movie "James Bond casino atmosphere. This is sweatpants, and black NASCAR T-shirts kind of crowd.

I came here for an evening of entertainment. My group had different opinions. We sat in the O.H. restaurant and watched a show while dining. The "people watching" on the dance floor proved to be the entertainment. So now I can confirm that after dining at 2 restaurants, there is zero reason to come here for the food.

Here's what you should know about the FREE concerts promoted on their website. Baseball analogy~ The band plays on a respectable size stage with good audio and lighting. The stage is home plate. The O.H. Restaurant sits back from the 3rd base line. A limited seating bar with bar stools sits about 3rd base. VIP casino players sit in padded, roped off, elevated area at 2nd base. Casino tables and machines would occupy the outfield and 1st base line. A very large screen above the stage projects the entire stage show to the outfield, so you never have  to leave your gaming table. So where do you go to see the show? You stand! There is a large open area/dance floor in front of the stage for people to fill. It's from the very front of the stage to the VIP velvet ropes. Several viewers stood in the aisle behind the VIP seating. If you are lucky enough to catch a seat at the 3rd base bar or edge of the 3rd base line you can see most of the stage. They don't kick you out of the OHR if you finish your food and are watching the show, but they do keep asking "Will there be anything else".

I found out from a regular that minimum bets are increased on tables Friday and Saturday. Since the onslaught of people crowding the tables prevented me from playing comfortably, I bailed on that for machines. I had to ask someone where video poker games were. I found them back in a corner near the restrooms. Options to play for $.25, $.50, or $1 was a surprise. Bored after a short time, I walked the floor. I noticed only 4 servers moving around the floor with trays of drinks on a Friday night. I never saw a one come near the machines while I was seated.

Bathrooms were clean enough, and debris sitting on flat surfaces were not an issue.

XP

Input: Okay, I'm going to do my best to give this place a fair review. After all, it seems unfair to compare the sushi from a shopping mall in New Westminster with the sushi that we had in Japan. So here goes... Woomi Sushi is located inside Royal Square Mall.

I wound up ordering their Special Bento Box E ($11.50) which included 2 pieces of tuna sashimi, 2 pieces of salmon sashimi, 2 pieces of yam tempura, chicken teriyaki, 4 pieces of California roll, salad and miso soup. I showed up just before noon on a weekday and it wasn't busy at all (not unexpected given how hidden this stall is).

The salad was crisp, the miso soup was hot, and the California roll was typical of sushi from a shopping mall... nothing outstanding here. Of everything, the yam tempura was probably the best as it had a light and crisp batter and seemed fresh. Meanwhile, the sashimi was the troubling part of this dish and you can kind of see it in how the sashimi appeared in the picture... it seemed to be still partially frozen. I even waited until the end of my meal to give the sashimi a chance to warm up a bit but I could still feel the slightly icy crunch from the inside of the flesh.

As for the chicken teriyaki, it tasted precooked and reheated and was served on a light bed of cabbage and limp broccoli. It's a shame because the people seemed nice and I really wanted to like this place more than I did.

Input: Let me say, I fully realize the implications of what I'm going to say during this post.  Pretty much everyone I've ever met in Austin talks about eating at the Salt Lick as an almost religious experience.  Well, this describes my experience: MEH.

First, the positives.  I LOVE the atmosphere.  It is the absolute perfect place to bring an out-of-town guest that wants a glossed over, stereotypically Texan experience without getting their hands too dirty at a more bare-bones, hot as hell BBQ joint (aka anything in what I view as a lil piece o' heaven, LOCKHART) You sit outside, drink beer or wine from the cooler (it's BYOB, for those that weren't aware) under huge, shady trees on long picnic tables.  On a beautiful, cool day, it is an absolutely sublime way to spend an afternoon with a group of close friends.  It's also perfect post-tubing in San Marcos.  If you haven't already noticed, there's a running theme here: booze.

In my humble opinion, though, the food is just alright.  I suppose it depends on your preference.  Salt Lick covers their meat in a bland sauce so you could be eating turkey, pork...whatever, and you'd never know, whereas, the more authentic places in places like Lockhart, view BBQ sauce as akin to blasphemy.  They passionately (and VERY rightfully) believe in the quality of their meat, and, thus, believe that it should speak for itself.  Some places will offer sauce (Black's), but it's definitely frowned upon.  Maybe if I'd never eaten at places like Smitty's or Black's, I would really dig Salt Lick, but, for me, the experience was pretty much ruined.  Don't get me wrong, I had a TON of fun.  But, after eating the insanely good, flavorful, delicious smokiness of the various briskets, homemade sausage and pork ribs lovingly cooked by the real Texas BBQ capital, nothing really stands a chance.  Also, the various owners are completely charming and the sense of history covering the walls of the restaurants is totally humbling.  Think, all the UT quarterbacks since forever ago thanking the owner of Black's, and personal letters of adoration from LBJ.  

So, this has completely snowballed into one long rant about how I kinda like Lockhart.  Just a little.  Bottom line, if you're looking for a place with ambience, then Salt Lick is a fun excursion to take friends from out of town and wind down after a raucous afternoon boozin it up on the river, but if you want the real deal, BBQ that brings you to tears of joy, Lockhart ALL THE WAY.

I was a little annoyed, therefore, I passively took out my frustration over the pushiness by drawing on the paper table cloth (see pic). 

They get 3 stars rather than 2 due to location and company and medium stars for food. 

You would expect the bathroom to be fancy, however, was disappointed that it looked like an upscale hole in the wall. 

I've had this on the list for 3 years but it was over hyped.

Input: Like most of McMenamins historic locations, their Rock Creek Tavern is gorgeous, but this one was seriously lacking in the service department.

We seated ourselves upstairs, and waited for a server to notice us. He eventually did  and looked incredibly bored and mildly annoyed to be there. The food itself was ok, but it's nothing spectacular. The selections themselves are limited to salad, hotdogs, a few sandwiches and burgers. They had wings, but our waiter had no idea what they were like or how many were served. Between 2 people we ordered tots and a pork sandwich.  Nobody at the table requested that it be cut in half, but that's exactly how we received it. Two separate, sloppy plates with half a sandwich and a few fries thrown on. To make the sloppy plating worse, there were finger smudges of blue cheese on the plate and the dish did not contain any blue cheese.

After he cleared our sandwich plates, he came around again and asked if we wanted anything else. My husband still had some beer left, so he said not right now. The waiter took that as cue to bring us our check. We were considering ordering more drinks, but the check indicated to us that he wanted us to leave (and he did come around 1 or 2 more times to see if we paid the check yet). We eventually relieved him of his duties and went home completely dissatisfied with the service.

Not sure if we just got lucky with our waiter, but they really need to check their staff!

The Wild Striped Bass presentation was beautiful and the flavor was bland. Both entrees could have used a heavier portion size given the cost. Both entrees were delivered in a timely manner.

5, A long wait for the check. I understand that by the time we completed out meal the restaurant was now full. However having one waitress for all those tables seemed excessive especially since there were multiple other staff available that could have dropped off the check. Another long wait for her to return with the charge card.

I'd say it would be highly unlikely that we'd return to Salts. Having eaten at many five star restaurants all over the world Salts falls short of a five star rating.

Input: TLDR, the service here is fantastic! But stay away from the burgers and sandwiches on the lunch menu:/ Try coming for Sunday brunch or dinner though! There's a lot of good reviews on that! 

Decided to come here for lunch with my bf. They had complimentary valet on our way in and that was very nice. The ambiance was very refined, bright and beautiful! We were seated inside by the huge glass window/walls that displayed the river and garden they had going on outside. Everyone we encountered there, from the hostess to our waitress, was incredibly kind and welcoming. Our waitress was very knowledgeable about the menu and recommended us some nice dishes. We got the salmon appetizer to start, I got the angus burger, and my bf got a fish sandwich. 

We got some bread and butter to start. It was good, solid, nothing to write home about. Then the appetizer came out and was presented and plated fantastically! It tasted very fresh and delicious! The sauce was delightful! I was so eager to eat it that I forgot to take a photo!!! Sorry about that guys! 

Next, our entrees came out and unfortunately this is where Canoe lost 2 stars from me. The burger looked amazing. I had also read reviews and saw that a lot of people recommended the burgers here. But it was for the duck and beef burger, not the plain lunch angus burger. So maybe that's where I went wrong. Anywho, as soon as I bit into it, I realized that it was SO DRY and also BURNT on the bottom. I figured, ok, maybe I haven't gotten to the center where all the juices and flavors are. So I keep eating and eating (Bc I was also starving so i just put whatever into my mouth) and by the time I'm 3/4ths of the way finished, I realized wow...this burger is really just unseasoned, unflavorful, super dry, bitter, and hence was completely burnt on the bottom. I opened it up and yep. It was burnt and it looked like they tried to cover it up with sauces and stuff. 

That was probably one of the most disappointing and mediocre burgers I ever had in my life. I definitely would've enjoyed a shake shack burger more than this. My bfs sandwich was pretty good at least, but again, nothing spectacular and he even went as far as to make a joke that a McDonald's filet o fish would've been just as satisfying. At least the fries that came with our meals were delicious.

Overall, I can't rave enough about the amazing service and kindness of everyone, but I was incredibly blown by how meh the food was (except for the salmon appetizer, that was amazing!). I want to give them the benefit of the doubt and say that it's a great restaurant, but maybe only the dinner menu. The lunch menu is a hit or miss. Most of the great reviews on yelp are of the dinner or Sunday brunch menu. So I guess if I ever do come back (ehhh maybe??), I'll have to come back during those times:/

Very expensive for those ingredients and preparation.

Red Sangria was very good. Like we've had in some South American countries.

Input: (Dined 03/04/20 WE @ 12:00pm): This lad's arse was feeling pretty lard after eating this ginormous donut!

On the grounds of Universal Studios Resort Orlando (Universal Studios Florida to be exact), I had to drag my travel friend along to Lard Lad Donuts for a gigantic snack and its iconic Big Pink Donut from the animated series "The Simpsons" fame. I loved donuts - apple fritters to be exactly - but as a tourist I had to get this massive pastry. Did this donut have any merit or was it totally for show!?

PURCHASE
The Big Pink Donut ($7.49): This giant donut with sweet, creamy thick fluorescent pink frosting and rainbow sprinkles was a sight to behold, be held, and be eaten with all the childlike giddy tendencies you could muster. The pink frosting was layered on thick yet didn't crackle off which was a good thing while the actual breading was more dense than airy fluffy as I'd hoped, and I wished there were more rainbow sprinkles for complete coverage. A fun "meal" but could've been better https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=bWGb5pG-ZXX3cUN-0hbekg&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw.

SERVICE
I was greeted by a middle-aged somewhat curmudgeon woman who wasn't in the mood for any pleasantries which I found odd. And when asked if they had the apple fritter, she vehemently retorted, "we have had those for over a week now!" Furthermore, unlike the Hollywood location where they had several donut types to choose from, these were the only options here. Anyway, I got my donut, paid up, and walked over to a nearby bench to grub down.

PARKING (Varied; N/A this instance)
General parking for the massive theme park started from $25.00, but my friend and I took a Lyft ride in and skirted parking altogether. Also, I believed if you stayed at any of the resorts in the area, shutter services were available.

ATMOSPHERE, DÉCOR, AMBIENCE
Truly a wooden shack the size of a large storage room with only a walk-up order/pick up window with barely enough room to fit two individuals inside let alone any available refreshments, you ventured nearby for a table to enjoy your purchase or walked with it. Input: Downtown Orlando needed a 24 hour diner and this place fills that niche when you're craving for breakfast , lunch or dinner.  I've been 2x now , once for lunch and once for dinner.  I do love the cool 50's theme with huge booths and fun sayings on the walls.   I see this being a popular choice with the weekend folks after a late night around Downtown. 

The menu has your usual diner fare - breakfast items, soups, salads, sandwiches and heartier entrees. On my first visit I had the Brioche grilled cheese and tomato soup. It was more than enough food for me and it came with waffle fries too! I loved the tomato soup and finished it off . Perfect comfort food. They also carry desserts by The Dessert Lady. We actually started off our meal with the Oh No Chocolate Cake which is the best way to start off every meal. 
Second visit was early evening. We had a larger party and I felt that the timing of when items came out took longer than it really should have. The restaurant was empty and most of us ordered breakfast items. The Belgian waffle is good and comes with butter and syrup. If you want to add fruit, chocolate chips or pecans- be prepared to fork up $1 EACH!   I also had the creamy mashed potatoes which are excellent and a highly recommended side item. They make them with red potatoes and they came out piping hot.

Service was a little so so on both visits. The first time , it took awhile for someone to approach our table to take our order. Luckily, once we flagged someone she was pretty attentive but took awhile to get our checks to us. The recent visit  was ok- our server wasn't as friendly and was sort of going through the motions?   Overall, service isn't consistent so you never know how your experience will be.   

I would probably check them out for dessert on a future visit or when I'm craving breakfast. It's a fun option for the Downtown crowd though and being open 24/7 will definitely work in its favor.

Input: Decided to come here last night on a whim to get a Tex-mex fix. We've never been to this location but have been to Chuy's in Texas.

There's plenty of parking as the restaurant has its own parking lot. 

On a Friday night, the restaurant was probably only one third full, so there was no wait. The first thing I noticed upon walking in was the dirty floors (silverware, napkins, chips, etc). Lots of dirty tables too.. with minimal staff in sight.

Salsa is suuuuper fresh tasting and delicious. I didn't care for their jalapeño ranch sauce (honestly tastes like a dressing to me) or for the boom boom sauce which is highly reviewed. I will say my husband really likes the boom boom sauce. 

I ordered a skinny margarita which was OK - definitely tasted the sour mix. If I ever go back, I may try the sangria.

Got the Friday special for my meal- chicken enchiladas with green chili avocado sauce. The chicken was extremely tender. The enchiladas were decent. 

Everyone else in our party got the boom boom enchiladas. We all thought the enchiladas were extremely spicy. Much spicier than expected and we eat spicy food all the time!

Got the tres leches cake for dessert. It was decadent, rich, and delicious. Split between 4 people and we had trouble finishing it. The slice is HUGE.

Not sure if I will be back considering I was turned off by how dirty the restaurant felt, mediocre service, and OK food.

If I ever find myself here again, I will probably just fill up on chips and salsa... and dessert!

Overall, we enjoyed Chuy's in Texas more.

Input: For such high prices, I was a little disappointed. 

We ordered:
Involtini di Melanzane: it tasted ok and had nice presentation, but it was quite small for a $10.50 appetizer. It was three very thin slices of eggplant wrapped around cheese, with marina sauce drizzled around and garnished with arugula. Tasted good, but nothing out of this world.

Polenta al forno: This was the best tasting dish of the night. The polenta was moist and delicate. I think it could have used more Gorgonzola for flavor. I felt like they skimped on it. 

Rigatoni al ragu: Pretty good, nice sauce. Worth $19.50, though? Probably more like $15. 

Trota alla grigla: Had some issues...the biggest being the fish did not taste very fresh. The menu said it was rainbow trout. Usually rainbow trout has a delicate, almost sweet flavor. This one had a fishy, unctuous flavor, and the texture was dense and kind of unpleasant. The sauce was OK, but why were there so many onions in the dish--sautéed with the side of asparagus in addition to diced raw on top of the fish? Seemed like onion overkill.

Overall, I thought the food was expensive and just average. 

A note about the bread: I've traveled through Italy, and the bread they serve is not authentic, my friend. Correct me if I'm wrong, but squishy soft bread is more of an American preference. Don't get me wrong, I devoured it. But it ain't Eye-talian. I might expect a crusty bread or maybe focaccia in a fine authentic Italian joint. 

For better food for the same or lower prices, try Olive and June or Enoteca. The ambience at those places is much more interesting as well.

Input: I had a one-night business stay here. It's a decent choice in that area. 

Good things:
* Location - very close to Disney 
* Pool area - great resort feel with lots of fun things to do; beautiful to look at, too
* The pantry food area - way more offerings than the typical Marriott pantry (including some premade items in a refrigerated section)
* Breakfast buffet - lots of diversity on the buffet including a delicious cous cous salad, eggs benedict, tomato/mozzarella salad, etc. Very good service, too. Wilson was fabulous. 
* Room had a balcony (but a warning: there were a lot of wasps out there during the day)
* A full Starbucks in the lobby
* Elevators were pretty fast and available in spite of it being such a huge hotel 

Bad things:
* No M Club
* Stayed in a room that hadn't been renovated yet -- it was just OK and looked a little worn out. But renovated rooms are happening in waves there. 
* My room's AC was really struggling and wasn't cooling the room or taking the humidity out. If I had been staying there longer I would have had to move or get it fixed. 
* The parking options are self-park and valet, but the self park option is pricey ($24) and involves parking in a garage that is far enough away from the hotel that a shuttle runs you back and forth. You need to allow for time for the shuttle to get to you and then run you there and back. Valet is $35 a night. It's probably worth it just to valet. 
* Had to pay for the $30 a night resort fee even though I didn't use any of the pools or anything resort-like at all (as I was there for work). I did get "free" internet but I would have had that anyway with Titanium status 

If I stayed again in the area, I might stay here again if the price was right but I also would consider trying another Marriott property in the area.

Input: Really tried hard to love the food esp. after reading all the 4 and 5 star reviews from my favorite Yelpers - but couldn't. However the service was top notch, and I loved the ambiance. 

We had a party of 5, and shared 2 apps and 5 entrees - just the right amount of food. Everyone cleaned their plates :) Yes we did family-style dining at a restaurant where the food isn't designed for that - we just said we're going to share our food, and next thing you know, they brought all 5 entrees to the center of our table, and set 5 empty plates for each of us. Extra bonus points for portioning out some of the dishes, plus adding a few extra corn on the cob to equal 5 :) That's service! 

I so wanted to give 5 stars b/c of the great service but the food didn't live up to the hype. Part of me wonders if I should blame the ok food b/c we came on a Monday. Anthony Bourdain's "Kitchen Confidential" said Mondays aren't a good day to eat out at restaurants. 

COMPLIMENTARY CHIPS & SALSA
Love the blue chips and I liked that the salsa was spicy.

GUACAMOLE & CHIPS - $7 (full order)
Nothing special, and a full order is not really all that big ... good size for 5 people though.

GUAJILLO MUSSELS - $10.50
Mussels were small & fishy, and while the red chili citrus wine broth was tasty, I wish it were thicker. The flour tortilla seemed random ... I guess crusty bread wouldn't fit the southwestern theme. 

CHILI SEARED JUMBO DIVER SEA SCALLOPS - $19.50
Menu description set too high expectations :( Pan seared scallops in signature herb & chili rub, served w/ fire roasted tomato & serrano stone ground grits (salty) and honey cider collard greens (good & sweet). Just ok.

AGAVE FAMOUS CAYENNE FRIED CHICKEN - $15
Jumbo size boneless chicken breast but didn't get any cayenne flavor. Buttermilk marinated & fried (not crispy). Yukon Gold mashed potatoes were good, and grilled corn was too buttery for me and I couldn't taste the Poblano drizzle at all.

STUFFED MOUNTAIN TROUT TOMATILLO - $17.50
Just ok. Liked the stuffing more than the actual trout. Idaho trout was stuffed w/ crawfish, mushrooms, onions, and basil over Spanish rice w/ roasted tomatillo sauce and freshly cut cilantro (but I don't remember tasting any cilantro). 

SPICY TEQUILA ANEJO SHRIMP - $18.75
Biggest disappointment b/c this dish got the most positive reviews. Again menu description set very high expectations. Fresh gulf shrimp grilled & sauteed in fresh lime & tequila cream sauce (not spicy at all), and served a/ jalapeno & cheddar ground grits cake (good but mostly cheddar flavor and very salty), and grilled asparagus. The asparagus was probably my favorite item of the evening. 

TENDERLOIN MEDALLIONS - $23
Meat was pretty tender and one of the better dishes. Tenderloin pan seared over roasted tomato, garlic, and chile tequila puree, and served w/ Yukon Gold mashed potatoes (yum), fried cayenne onion rings (not spicy), and grilled zucchini. 

Overall, I thought the sides were better than the entrees. Also, couldn't taste all the flavors described in the menu. Other than the salsa, nothing was spicy. However like I said before, service was outstanding ... and maybe we just came on a bad day. I definitely want to try their drinks next time - almost every table around us had margaritas :)

FYI - complimentary valet parking is available but if you're lucky, you might be able to find nearby street parking on Carroll Street. Also join their VIP club to get 20% off your entire check Sun-Thur, or get $10 entrees if you come between 5-6pm any night of the week! Sign up now!

Input: This evening a couple of my lady friends and I decided to play tourist in our own back yard.  So we went to TGIFridays to watch the bats while enjoying some beverages and snacks.  

My three star rating is an 'average' for the chain restaurant experience.  The food was up to standard and consistency of the well know brand.  I have no gripe there what so ever...   And to be honest,  I have to say that is hard to find decent chicken wings... TGIFridays never disappoints!  For maintaining their brand standards I give them a 4 star.

I give our server a 1.  After waiting SEVERAL minutes a server who clearly came over from another section asked us is we had been helped.  His name was Andrew and he was VERY friendly.   If we had been able to keep him as a server I think that our experience would have been ideal.  However, it was not his section and he was just being a team player.  Our server is nameless because he never introduced himself.  Of course they all wear name tags, and a name is usually on the guest check... however I was so unsettled from our bad experience that I had actually forgotten to put his name to memory.  Our server was constantly absent,  and it took him forever to bring items we may have requested.  We had to ask for water THREE times.  It took over five minutes to process our check.  

If you read my blog and my reviews here, you know that I am NOT accustomed to write about my negative experiences.  Therefor I guess that I just could not be bothered to put his name to memory.  Fitting I suspect, as he just could not be bothered to do his job!

The service was not up to standard for any establishment.   As a fellow server, I am embarrassed to have someone like this in my profession.  This kind of service gives the rest of us a bad rap, and he should be ashamed.

After a while, they did move up to three cashiers and things moved much more quickly after that. There is an express line if you just want concretes, shakes, or other drinks. If you want food, though, you have to wait in the longer line.

Placing our order was easy. There's a limited menu, which makes it easier to figure out what you'll eat (less indecisiveness there!). We got two ShackBurgers and added pickles and onion for free--for whatever reason, they just come with lettuce and tomato unless you specify. We split one order of regular fries (they also offer cheese fries) and then each got a shake: peanut butter for me, caramel for my husband. I like that Shake Shack puts the calorie count next to their food items although it's just a range for things like shakes (it will say "Shakes, 640-930 calories," for example, instead of saying "Peanut butter shake, X # of calories" ... I'm pretty sure mine was the 930 calories one).

They give you a pager device and you wait for your food. Ketchup, mustard, mayo in packets, etc. is nearby. It took a while to get our food and in the short time that we waited, the place got PACKED. Like, no more tables inside packed; we had to go outside. It wasn't too hot yet but we did have to move our table out of the sun. Bonus: There is a pretty view of the lake. There's also a ping-pong table out there.

People kept having a hard time getting out to the patio and then back in to get their food because there's only one door that's unlocked so you can move in and out. There were supposed to be two but the second one kept getting re-locked. Some servers came over to prop it open finally but that lets out their air conditioning ...

Our food was good. I would say Burger Fi serves up a better all-around burger and Burger 21 does better shakes. But Shake Shack would be good for a quick bite if you're in the area. The burgers were pretty standard, tasty, on a soft bun and with "shack sauce," which appeared to be something like ketchup, mayo, and chopped pickles. Our shakes were disappointing. If I didn't know mine was peanut butter and his was caramel, I'd think we both got vanilla. Maybe the frozen custard base flavor is just overwhelming, but I didn't find the shakes to be worth the calories for me personally. Again, I'd rather have a Burger 21 shake, which is much more flavorful. The fries were good: They're crinkle-cut, which is a rarity at burger places, and they were hot and fluffy. Nothing out of this world, but they were good alongside the burger.

Our food was nearly $25. Would I go again? Probably not any time soon, but if I'm nearby and hungry, I'd definitely get a burger and fries again. I don't think I'll bother with another shake. Maybe I'll try one of their concretes instead--they have a rotating menu of daily flavors that they told me changes every month, and there were some good ones.

By the way, if you have dogs with you, you could sit on the porch and get them some dog biscuits or the Pooch-ini, which has dog biscuits, peanut butter sauce, and custard. Cute!

Oh yeah, there's only one bathroom for each gender as other reviews have said. If you're waiting for the bathroom, you have to stand in a small hallway where cooking staff often need to walk down, or you end up going into the dining area as overflow. Terrible idea to only have two bathrooms totals! Also, come here early if you want some food and to be able to get parking!

Input: I've been coming here for years. It's close to work, and it's cheap -- for $9, you get all the pizza and salad you can eat, and all the refills on soda or tea you can drink.

I used to call it "Dirty Daves" because, as with a lot of buffet places, the plate and utensil cleaning was spotty at best. I still get the occasional unidentifiable crusty thing on a fork or knife, but it is what it is -- a pizza buffet.

You know what you are getting at a place like this -- dodgy lettuce, miscellaneous veggies of questionable freshness, pepperoni rolls that range from all dough to a perfect ratio of dough to pepperoni. Greasy pizza and cheese sticks. Nothing surprising, nothing culinary adventurous. You can't knock a pizza buffet place for being a pizza buffet place.

For me, this is not a destination place other than an infrequent lunch spot when I feel the need to carbo-load. When I eat here and I walk out full, it isn't because I just had good pizza, it's because I wanted carbs.

You know Gatti's -- good salad bar, bad pizza. DD's is the opposite -- bad salad bar, adequate pizza. Not the best pizza, not the worst pizza. Again, it is what it is, nothing more, nothing less.

I almost made this a 2-star review but truth be told, I DO keep coming back, and barely-adequate lunchtime buffet pizza is still better than no pizza at all.

Input: I'll start with the positives. I love the grand ballroom space with huge windows overlooking the water. The "check-in" counter upstairs with Italian stewardesses that guide you down to the main dining room themed to a retro airport terminal sets a promising start.

I also had great service. We were there at 5:30pm on weeknight, and there was more wait staff than actual guests so I know that helped, but after reading a few reviews of slow service that was definitely not the case. 

We ordered a glass of pinot grigio and the "summer" sangria that was the the lovechild of a sangria and a pina colada. Nice. Bread came, along with olive oil poured on the bread plates. Ok. The bread was a bit stale, but I'm not going to look gift dough in the mouth. 

Our first course was arancini, and it was great. Cripsy on the outside, moist on the inside. The pricing -- $14 for two golf ball-sized fried risotto balls -- seemed extreme, but on to the next course.

My wife ordered the spaghetti with meatballs. I went with chicken parm. Both were surprisingly ho-hum. The chicken parm comes with no accompaniments. I thought I had read that it came served with a side of penne, but I later discovered that I was eyeing the brunch menu online where it's served that way. I was surprised that the waiter didn't ask if I wanted a pasta side, since just eating chicken parm -- $29 chicken parm, at that -- by itself seems incomplete. My wife passed over some of the spaghetti -- thicker than usual noodles cooked al dente -- and it was fine, but both entrees were closer to Olive Garden quality than the high-end Italian joints that this place aspires to be. 

The brunch menu seems far more interesting/inviting, and maybe we'll check that out in the future. However, for an actual lunch or dinner meal there are at least six other places I'd rather go in Disney Springs, and if I'm craving Italian on property this is no Il Mulino.

 But when we first ordered drinks, my friend got a black velvet and I got a jack d'or. 

 When the bartender brought them, she went to give us each the opposite drink, and we just laughed but corrected her and she apologized (not a big deal in any way, but relevant to the story). 

 So a little while later my friend has ordered another beer and then I order another beer. The bartender brings me a black velvet (what my friend ordered the first time) and I look over and realize that when she served my friend her second drink she'd given her a Jack D'or (my first drink). My friend likes both so hadn't said anything, but we (in visible sight of the waitress) switched drinks so we could each have the beer we actually wanted/ordered. 

 Finally it gets hilarious, because when we ordered a third round, the bartender just brought us two black velvets. What? At no time in the night did we order the same drink. It was like she'd forgotten whatever the other beer was we'd at some point ordered and so just brought two of the one she knew someone was drinking. 

 Anyway no harm done, it's St. Paddy's Day Weekend and we should all drink a little Guiness I suppose.

Input: First off, the decor is not to my taste for a tea house. The stark, modern, all light color felt cold. Plus the blank, concrete walls echo people's voices all over the place. I was trying to have a private conversation and the two other couples in the shop were talking in normal volume, yet it was so loud in there you'd think it was packed. 
On to the tea. The menu is not very informative. Only the recommended tea lattes have ingredients listed. This meant my diabetic companion had to ask what was sugar free. The counter person didn't really know how to lead us through sugar free options. We had to ask about each item my friend was interested in. I know that many of the lattes here are premixed (something I do not care for) and therefore can't be made sugar free. At least the coconut milk and almond milk was unsweetened. I got the cardamom chia latte. It was nicely spiced but a too sweet for my taste. My companion got a London Fog latte with coconut milk. It tasted more of lavender than Earl Gray. He only finished half of it. 
At 6:30pm, the worker started putting everything away in preparation for closing. She even cleared away the water, napkins, pastries, and stir-ins well before 7pm, meaning the people who walked in about 20 minutes to closing weren't able to access these things. Ten minutes to closing she had brought in the outside sign, tables, and chairs. I've worked service management before, for years. I understand doing pre-closing but a half hour before closing to remove the water, stir-ins, and pastry case just tells your clientele "Get out" and "I'm not interested in serving you." 
Overall, it wasn't horrible but it wasn't great either. I have a meeting set there this weekend and I really wish Townshend's on Alberta was open from its remodel. I'd rather go there.

Input: After finally clarifying what exactly differentiated Hannah Montana from Miley Cyrus, my 6 year old cousin steered our post Thanksgiving Dinner conversation to Disney princesses:

"Which one do you like?" she asked. 

"Aurora from Sleeping Beauty" I replied. Easily my choice for as long as I can remember, heck my prom dress was the same sweet, soft, sleepy blue.  And although my cousin argued that the Little Mermaid was far superior, we agreed that in both cases their entourage and accessories definitely helped make them the characters they were.  

But of course this is the case with many young ladies.  So many stores push the little pieces that complete the look they are selling, and at Urban Outfitters it becomes an adventure to track them down.  Hidden around displays and near registers, sometimes it feels like you're cutting through a hipster forest to get to the little things that are actually worth picking up here. 

One such day found me standing in front of a table of fall scarves.  I was having one of those "Hmm... do I really want this?" moments, and my sister walked over:

"Which one do you like?" she asked.

I pointed out a pretty plaid merlot and after some deliberation decided that I could spring for it.  At $20, it was a little on the expensive side, but I'm a major sucker for winter accessories and this was exactly my kind of weakness. Though I almost left without it, as the challenge of finding someone from whom I could actually buy the thing proved a little much... Be wary of the folks who inhabit this place, sometime they are as sweet as fluttery fairies, pointing you in the right direction.  Other times very unresponsive, as if put under some sort of magical sleeping spell.   

Though generally speaking, there's a significantly lower percentage of witchy mistresses of evil that turn into fire breathing dragons.

So they've got that going for them.

Madrid does offer shrimp tacos on soft shells . . . so, here's an idea - give me the option of ordering the soft shells on my fish tacos!

The "fish mixture" on top of the won-ton consisted of the fish, some jicama mint slaw, candied jalepenos and salsa.  Did I say fish?  Oh yeah, you kind of had to dig for it to find the protein (cut up in small pieces and not a lot of it).  My friend had the shrimp tacos and appeared to enjoy more protein than I did.

The prices aren't bad, but the taco portions are small.  Acceptable food for lunch in downtown Columbus, but nothing spectacular to draw me back repeatedly.  Larger portions and more fish on the fish tacos (two birds with one stone really) may have made me a repeat customer.
