Input: A little trip down memory lane:

Remember the original Mc & Schmick's? $2 happy hour, downtown PDX.?  Ahh, the food was fantastic, even for HH.   Dinners were top notch and it was a great Portland destination.  Ok, I am showing my age a bit as well as remembering via grandparents comments 20++ years back.

Well, M&S grill is an off-shoot of the original but don't be fooled pretty one's.............. it's not the same.  Nor is the original!!!  As soon as they became chain-ised (aka incorporated) their food quality took a big FAT dive.  Now, while it's less chain-like than those horrible other places in Bridgeport, it's still looking for a large file to escape it's prison.  I don't think there's any saving this place.  

Food: lunch is better than dinner and far more affordable.  Their menu is too large, so they can't possibly have 50 amazing dishes (this is a big obvious button for me).  Fish is fresh (just make sure you order "fresh").  
And the Brit likes the fish & chips gives it the "ok".  Plus lot of micro-brews on tap to wash it down.  Wine list is over-priced and I stick with cocktails here. 

Service can be patchy, but usually efficient and experienced.  I love seafood, but cookie cutter places are the norm-this one is just a cut above that.  For goodness sakes, we live 1 hour from the Pacific OCEAN!  I expect better.   Sorry you went corporate MS.

Input: I go to other BSC locations: usually Wellington and Woburn.  This review is for BSC South Station.

Let's do some Rating Math.  Starting at zero, they get:

(+ 2) Two stars for being right next door to my office and for friendly staff.  

(+ 3) Three stars for some pretty great instructors.  Love the Tuesday 1:15 and Wednesday 12:15 spin classes.  (I'm so bad with names. Sorry.)  But BSC spin instructors in general are good.  When I joined BSC, I'd been spinning for a couple of years at another gym.  I didn't realize how easy I'd had it.  My first few spin classes at a BSC were a wake-up call!  These guys know how to make you work AND they are very good at describing what your body should be feeling in terms of perceived exertion and what muscles should be working.  Makes for a great workout.  I've learned a lot and I'm in better shape.  

However: 

(-2) Minus two stars for a less-than-ideal spin studio.  It is small. Fine, ok -- it's downtown Boston, space is at a premium.  I can do small.  BUT.  The bikes are so often broken.  If you get to class early enough and can test the bikes, you're fine.  (But if you can get to class 10 minutes early in the middle of a work day or right after work, I want your job.)  If you can't, you might end up on a bike with a wonky pedal or worse. That gets in the way of a good workout.  

They typically do not overbook their classes.  That is: they seem to account for the broken bikes when letting (or not letting) people sign up.  But still.  I'm not giving back a point for that when they could just fix the bikes.

Input: I came here once before several years ago but I don't remember much of the visit. I got invited last night and decided to give it a go again. I left with mixed feelings.

The food was excellent! I absolutely have nothing negative to say about the food. Everything came out delicious and fresh. We got the calamari for an appetizer and it was great. The salad and cheese bread came out next and they were delicious as well! While waiting for our main courses, a manager came over with a sample of their ahi tuna nachos. I'm not much of a tuna fan, but I gave it a try and loved it. It was spicy and crunchy; the fish definitely tasted fresh.

I ordered the prime rib which was probably one of the best I've ever had. It was cooked perfectly and just melted in your mouth. The garlic whipped potatoes were delicious. I ended up ordering a side to go for my left overs (which I had a lot of!). I appreciated that the prime rib was anti-biotic and hormone free, it's one of the reasons I ordered it. Lastly, we finished off the meal with the chocolate grand marnier cake and it was out of this world. First off, the slice of cake was huge. Between three people we barely made a dent. The cake itself was rich and moist. The orange flavor really came through and mixed well with the chocolate.

The downfall was the service. Our server was friendly and pleasant; he was knowledgeable regarding the menu so all of that was good and well. It was just at times he was pretty nonexistent. Now I'm not a huge fan of an overly attentive server, I like my meal time peace!  But it took too long for refills, waiting for our check took over 30 minutes and when he was there he seemed rushed. We were seated at a booth tucked away all the way back of the restaurant and it seemed like he was serving the opposite side so maybe management just needs to better evaluate the flow of service. 

Like I said, the food was excellent and the place is beautiful. Our server was friendly, but it seemed like he had too much going on. I'd definitely return, but not anytime in the near future.

Input: First time here. Been wanting to try out their breakfast for a while now. (Warning: pricing is different than what is listed on the website!)

Was seated right away. Great. Ordered a breakfast burrito and enchiladas. Server asked if we wanted red, green or Christmas chili. I asked which one was more spicy. Green was. Friend opted for red chili and I did the same, but asked for a side of green chili to taste. At the end of the bill we were charged $3 for a side of chili. First of all, we were NOT informed that there was additional charge for getting two chili. Since "Christmas" was offered, I figured there was no additional charge. Brought it up to my server's attention.

For those who are first timer- she suggested you say: I want CHRISTMAS, but have the green chili on the side. I did not know you have to say those "key words". Seriously? Would have been nice if you spent 30 seconds to explain to us our options, then we wouldn't have had this awkward conversation. Went on to explaining the chili is imported from New Mexico, spendy, that's why they charge extra, etc, etc., so specific lingo is important. Anyways, she took cared of charge for us. But another reason why they did not receive full stars on our books was that we were NOT informed they had a daily special nor unlimited mimosas on weekends. We only overhead this conversation through another server who sat a couple next to us (this happened AFTER we placed our order). Uhm.. what? THERE WAS A DAILY SPECIAL? What did I missed out? wow. just wow. Btw, my friend didn't even receive any water. He ordered horchata with his meal and that's all he got. Would have been nice to have a glass of water with his meal too. 

Anyways, food wise 5 stars!. We love both our food, was super delicious! Received one complimentary sopapilla (woohoo). I am hesitant to go back, would go back if I get a different server. SO go try it at your own risk of not having attentive/awesome service. ha. Good Luck!

The mashed sweet potatoes were good, I enjoyed the pecans on top, but it needed a little more sweet like brown sugar to balance out from the salt of the pecans. 

Overall, I would eat here again. I will stick to sausage only next time. I still want to try their fried okra and dessert. On the plus, we did get a free beer here tonight. A distributer was there and giving out full samples. I just felt that for the price, some of the food left us underwhelmed.

Input: I finally got the opportunity to get to Agave for dinner.  The atmosphere is lively and the restaurant got very loud.  It was a fun place to have dinner.

I'm a fan and it will probably be the one thing that gets me back to Agave.  Also, the drinks were superb.  I had the Peachtree Margarita and it was perfect. I also have to give it to them on the salsa that comes with the chips.  It was some of the best I've had.  I loved the blue chips too.  Loved the corn on the cob too. It was grilled and I tore it the hell up.  

On the flip side, the other items that I ate did not impress me.  The short ribs were very bland tasting, although very tender.  They failed to live up to what I was looking for and I was mad at them. Also, I had some spring rolls that were so incredibly spicy until I couldn't taste anything else.  It was obvious that too much of something was put in those.  The quesadillas were pretty good, but not anything special.  

I'm going to have to add that I felt that the entrees were overpriced. Just saying.  

The service was outstanding. Everything flowed like clockwork. A+ for service here.   

Parking here is plentiful with free valet.

Input: I stopped into Gunshow over the weekend. For those that don't know, Gunshow is Kevin Gillespie's latest fine dining meets dim sum concept in Glenwood Park. The environment is extremely loud, cavernous and feels exactly like a pop-up, not a full-fledged restaurant. The food was good, service friendly and helpful, but in short, the only part of the equation that felt fine dining was the price.

Getting a reservation at Gunshow seemed difficult. They only had 9:30 slots open on Friday and Saturday. However, we were able to walk in at 8 PM and get a table for two with no problem.

Small plates - I love the concept. Getting to try many items that can show a kitchen's range and ability is always ideal. I'm not going to tell you how Gunshow operates (you can read that on every review of the place so far), but if you want to try the whole menu somewhere, Gunshow is a great place (so long as you brought your billfold). We ate a majority of the menu and really, that's not too difficult - the servings are small.

The reason for the dim sum/cart concept, as explained by Gillespie, is to keep things completely fresh from the kitchen. Nothing is supposedly precooked like many restaurants must do - parboiled rice for risotto was the example given in an early interview. I thought to myself, "OK that makes some sense." And I thought that until the first dish, Cuban chicken with black beans and rice, was delivered to our table - cold. 

Now, that Cuban chicken was mighty tasty. Well cooked, well seasoned and nice cumin flavored rice. However, there were no twists. It was a very straight-forward rendition of Cuban food. And the serving was a single chicken thigh over just enough rice and beans to provide a pedestal for a chicken thigh. Price - $14. This is about a $5 serving at any Cuban restaurant in the city and there just wasn't anything special about the dish that warranted the price. Even if you consider the fact that everything at Gunshow is local, you just can't hit that price point. And the chicken was cold.

Then came what Gunshow calls "Assorted Savory, Spicy, Crispy and Crunchy Snacks. This was delivered in two forms. 1. Some cubed melon with duck pastrami (smart combo) and 2. a Hopping John type of fritter. The Hopping John fritter was completely comforting and delicious. It was approximately the size of a golf ball. Price - $5. That's flat out criminal anyway you look at it. If there were three balls on the plate, maybe they should be able to charge $5. OK, I'll stop harping on the price now.

A "Closed on Sunday" chicken sandwich was a take on the Chick-fil-a sandwich. Again, delicious with a pillowy soft sweet roll bun (they called it a biscuit?), but extremely simple and straightforward.

There were three savory dishes that standout in my mind as excellent. A smoked lamb leg with field peas. The lamb was exceptionally tender, flavorful and the field pea ragout cut through the unctuous lamb with acidic precision. 

The country breakfast consisted of grits with chicken and bacon gravy, some pickled tomatoes and a poached egg on top. This combination is delicious but the yolk of the egg was gelatinized and overcooked, not runny. Again, not exactly fine dining execution.

Lastly, a wild mushroom tart was obnoxiously delicious. The entire top portion, which included figs and cheese, had a sweet and sour finishes that cut through the fatty cheese and butter crust much like the lamb dish.

If you didn't notice by now, vegetables are extremely underrepresented at Gunshow. The color green is often used as a garnish, not an accompaniment. Plan on a meat-centric meal. 

Dessert we had a peanut butter and chocolate dish that was simple and kind of a throwaway. The sticky toffee pudding, however was phenomenal. They used fig instead of dates to cut the fat again (seeing a theme yet?) and it was finished with some bacon and Morreli's Salted Caramel ice cream. I know that bacon and salted caramel are buzzwords and easy sells, but the dish would have probably been better with plain, ol' vanilla.

Did I like the food at Gunshow? Absolutely. Did I enjoy the experience? Yup. Am I being hyper critical? Yessir. But the bottom line is both the pricing and execution need serious tweaking. A $50 meal should not only be delicious and close to perfect, it should also be moderately filling. I applaud Gillespie's concept - local food prepared as freshly as possible and sold to you by cooks, not servers. I also love trying new items and the option of an ever-changing menu. Ultimately, Gunshow comes off as a pop-up, not a destination fine-dining restaurant.  I know the ingredients are expensive and the preparation is time consuming, but the overall experience at Gunshow doesn't equal the cost.

Input: I was so excited about this place when many many months back I got to sample some of their food while on a foodie bicycle tour. Everything was so delicious that when my friend suggested we go while on the East Austin Studio Tour, I said hell yeah!

First off, I absolutely love sweet potato fries. Theirs are really great. EXCEPT that they put some sort of sickly sweet sauce on it that is not mentioned in the menu. When I had sampled these before they were perfectly fried and dusted with a cinnamon spice mix that was a perfect balance. The sauce is too much and I would've 86'd it had I known about it.

I ordered the Willie Nelson burger because I love me some bacon, cheese, and fried onion rings. This burger was so huge, I almost couldn't get my mouth around it. And that's my biggest complaint. I love a good burger, but maybe my mouth is extra small (which is weird because I often am called a big-mouth). I just could barely eat this burger. Plus, it was MESSY! The cheese spilled out, the sauce ran everywhere and a lot of it ended up in the basket and not my mouth. Which is too bad because it was very tasty otherwise.

On the plus side, they have Mexican coke and some really great fried pickles and veggies. The staff is really hilarious and fun and it's very Austin. I'll try this place again, but will be real careful when I order. Wish they offered a smaller sized burger for those of us with tiny mouths.
